# ART Development guide

Link to ART: <https://ripplelearning.github.io/ART/>

ART Repository: <https://github.com/ripplelearning/ART>

## Introduction

The Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART) is a comprehensive accessibility
evaluation workspace that empowers accessibility professionals to plan,
manage, document, and communicate accessibility evaluations through an
intuitive, fully accessible, and standards-driven platform. By
streamlining audit workflows, producing professional reports, and
supporting continuous accessibility improvement, ART enables
organizations to deliver more inclusive digital experiences with greater
efficiency, consistency, and confidence.

## Vision Statement

ART exists to become the industry's leading accessibility evaluation and
reporting workspace—a platform that supports every stage of the
accessibility assessment lifecycle, from planning and evaluation through
reporting, collaboration, metrics, and continuous accessibility
improvement.

## Mission Statement

The Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART) exists to empower accessibility
professionals with a comprehensive, accessible, and standards-driven
platform for planning, conducting, documenting, managing, and
communicating accessibility evaluations. ART streamlines the evaluation
lifecycle by providing intuitive workflows, professional reporting
capabilities, and flexible project management tools that improve
efficiency, consistency, accuracy, and collaboration while promoting the
creation of more inclusive digital experiences.

## Core Principles

### Accessibility First

ART shall demonstrate the same commitment to accessibility that it
promotes. Every feature, workflow, and user interface shall be designed
to meet or exceed applicable accessibility standards and provide an
equitable experience for all users.

### Standards-Driven

ART shall support industry-recognized accessibility standards and best
practices, including WCAG, Section 508, EN 301 549, WAI-ARIA, PDF/UA,
and other applicable accessibility guidance, while remaining adaptable
to future revisions.

### Human-Centered Evaluation

ART is designed to support professional accessibility evaluators. It
complements human expertise by providing tools that improve efficiency,
organization, documentation, and reporting without replacing
professional judgment.

### Accuracy and Consistency

ART shall promote consistent evaluation methodologies, standardized
reporting practices, and repeatable workflows that improve the quality
and reliability of accessibility evaluations.

### Flexibility

Organizations and individual consultants shall be able to configure ART
to support their preferred evaluation methodologies, report formats,
templates, workflows, and organizational requirements.

### Local-First

ART is designed as a desktop-first application that prioritizes user
ownership of data. Reports, templates, and supporting artifacts shall be
stored on user-selected local or network-accessible storage without
requiring cloud services for core functionality.

### Productivity Through Simplicity

Complex accessibility evaluations should not require complex software.
ART shall simplify routine tasks, reduce repetitive work, and allow
evaluators to focus on analysis rather than document management.

### Professional Quality

ART shall produce polished, professional, and accessible deliverables
suitable for consultants, government agencies, educational institutions,
and enterprise organizations.

### Extensibility

ART shall be designed to evolve as accessibility standards,
technologies, and organizational needs change without requiring
significant redesign of the application.

## Target Users

ART is intended for professionals and organizations responsible for
evaluating, documenting, managing, or improving digital accessibility,
including:

- Accessibility Consultants
- Accessibility Specialists
- Digital Accessibility Analysts
- Quality Assurance Analysts
- UX Researchers
- Usability Professionals
- Web Developers
- Software Engineers
- Designers
- Project Managers
- Product Owners
- Government Agencies
- Educational Institutions
- Enterprise Organizations
- Internal Accessibility Programs
- Digital Compliance Teams
- Independent Accessibility Auditors

## Product Goals

The primary goals of ART are to:

- Provide a comprehensive workspace for managing the complete
  accessibility evaluation lifecycle.
- Reduce the administrative effort required to produce professional
  accessibility reports.
- Improve consistency across accessibility evaluations.
- Support manual accessibility testing and expert analysis.
- Produce accessible, standards-compliant reports and documentation
  aligned with applicable accessibility standards and organizational
  requirements.
- Streamline report authoring through reusable templates and
  configurable workflows.
- Support accessibility evaluations across websites, web applications,
  mobile applications, desktop applications, electronic documents, and
  other digital content.
- Support reporting aligned with WCAG, Section 508, EN 301 549, PDF/UA,
  WAI-ARIA, and other applicable accessibility standards and guidelines.
- Provide comprehensive progress tracking throughout accessibility
  evaluations.
- Improve communication between evaluators, stakeholders, developers,
  and clients.
- Support both individual consultants and enterprise accessibility
  teams.
- Enable organizations to measure accessibility trends and continuous
  improvement over time.
- Maintain compatibility with evolving accessibility standards and
  technologies.
- Deliver an intuitive user experience without compromising
  functionality or flexibility.

## Non-Goals

ART is not intended to:

- Replace professional accessibility expertise or human judgment.
- Function as a fully automated accessibility testing tool.
- Automatically determine accessibility conformance.
- Replace assistive technology testing or usability testing.
- Generate accessibility findings without evaluator review.
- Require cloud services for core application functionality.
- Lock organizations into proprietary report formats or storage
  locations.
- Serve as a general-purpose project management application.
- Replace issue tracking systems such as Azure DevOps or Jira.
- Replace document management systems.
- Limit organizations to a single accessibility methodology.
- Restrict evaluators to predefined reporting workflows.

## Product Roadmap

\###Phase 1 – Accessibility Foundation (In Progress)

Objective: Establish ART as an exemplary accessible desktop application
by implementing comprehensive accessibility features, user preferences,
and inclusive interaction patterns that support users with a wide range
of disabilities and accessibility needs.

### Primary Objectives

- Implement application-wide accessibility preferences. (Planned)
- Provide visual accessibility customization options. (Planned)
- Provide keyboard accessibility enhancements. (Completed)
- Support screen reader optimization. (Completed)
- Support users with low vision, color vision deficiencies, mobility
  impairments, cognitive disabilities, hearing impairments, and other
  accessibility needs. (Planned)

#### Potential Features

Visual Accessibility

- High Contrast Mode (Planned)
- Light Theme (Planned)
- Dark Theme (Planned)
- User-defined color themes (Planned)
- Adjustable font size (Planned)
- Adjustable UI scaling (Planned)
- Zoom controls (Planned)
- Increased spacing options (Planned)
- Adjustable line spacing (Planned)
- Adjustable letter spacing (Planned)
- Reduced motion (Planned)
- Animation controls (Planned)
- Focus indicator customization (Planned)
- Caret visibility options (Planned)
- Color-independent status indicators (Planned)
- Custom accent colors (Planned)
- Support for Windows high contrast themes (Planned)

Keyboard Accessibility

- Fully keyboard-operable interface (Complete)
- Configurable keyboard shortcuts (Complete)
- Keyboard shortcut reference (Complete)
- Skip navigation options where appropriate (Complete)
- Focus management improvements (Planned)
- Customizable tab behavior (Planned)
- Command palette (Planned)

Screen Reader Support

- Improved accessible names (Complete)
- Live region management (Complete)
- Landmark support where applicable (Complete)
- Logical navigation order (Complete)
- Consistent announcements (Planned)
- Status notifications (Planned)

User Preferences

- Accessibility Preferences dialog (Planned)
- Import/export preferences (Planned)
- Reset accessibility settings (Planned)
- Application-wide preference persistence (Planned)

### Phase 2 – Foundation (Completed)

Establish the core architecture and foundational capabilities of ART,
including report creation, report management, template support,
accessible user interface requirements, dashboard functionality, and
professional report generation.

### Phase 3 – Evaluation Management (Completed)

Expand ART into a comprehensive accessibility evaluation workspace
through the introduction of structured audit workflows, evaluation
management, Progress Logs, report customization, and improved user
productivity.

### Phase 4 – Reporting Enhancements (Planned)

Enhance reporting capabilities through additional report types, expanded
report customization, improved export options, enhanced template
management, and advanced document generation.

### Phase 5 – Organizational Insights (Planned)

Provide organizations with meaningful accessibility metrics, dashboards,
historical reporting, trend analysis, and organization-wide reporting to
support continuous accessibility improvement.

### Phase 6 – Collaboration (Planned)

Introduce multi-user workflows, report review processes, shared
evaluations, role-based collaboration, report merging, and controlled
editing while maintaining data integrity and accessibility.

### Phase 7 – Enterprise Capabilities (Future)

Expand ART with enterprise-focused capabilities including project
management, organization administration, configurable workflows,
extensibility, integrations, advanced analytics, and optional
cloud-connected services while preserving the application's local-first
architecture.

## Epic 6A — Report Viewer Controls and Navigation

Objective

Implement the Report Viewer controls that allow users to export, modify
report configuration, and continue editing report content while
preserving accessibility, focus management, and the current report
state.

1.  Report Viewer Export Options Button

In the Report Viewer, create an accessible button labeled:

Export Options...

When activated:

Open an accessible export dialog.\
The dialog should allow users to configure export settings before
saving.\
Maintain keyboard focus management.\
When the dialog opens:\
Move programmatic keyboard focus to the first meaningful control in the
dialog.\
Ensure screen readers announce the dialog correctly.\
When the dialog closes:\
Return focus to the Export Options button.

The export dialog should contain:

File Name

A textbox labeled:

File Name

Automatically populate the textbox with the current Report Name.\
Allow the user to modify the file name before exporting.\
Format Selection

Create an accessible format picker containing:

Microsoft Word (.docx)\
PDF\
HTML\
Markdown\
Plain Text\
RTF\
Actions

Include:

Save button\
Cancel button\
2. Change Report Configuration Button

In the Report Viewer, add a button:

Change Report Configuration

When activated:

Open the Report Builder.\
Load the current report configuration.\
Do not create a new report.\
Preserve the current report identity.\
Preserve existing report data.\
Populate:\
Report Metadata\
Report Type\
Report Layout\
Template selection\
Report Fields configuration

Move programmatic keyboard focus to:

Report Builder h2 heading

When the user finishes editing the configuration:

Return to the existing report.\
Preserve all report content.\
3. Edit Report Button

In the Report Viewer, add a button:

Edit Report

When activated:

Open the Report Editor.\
Load the current report.\
Allow the user to continue editing report field values.\
Preserve existing report content.

Move programmatic keyboard focus to:

Report Editor h2 heading

Accessibility Requirements

For all Report Viewer controls:

Use semantic HTML.\
Ensure all buttons have accessible names.\
Maintain logical keyboard navigation.\
Do not unexpectedly move focus after actions.\
Ensure focus only moves automatically when explicitly required.\
Ensure dialogs are announced correctly by screen readers.

## Epic 6b — Report Layout Rendering Engine

Objective

Implement the report rendering engine that displays reports differently
depending on the selected Report Type and Report Layout.

The selected Report Layout determines only the presentation format of
the report data.

It must not change:

Report metadata\
Configured report fields\
Field order\
Report values

The existing Template functionality is complete and must not be
modified.

Available Report Layout Options\
Audit Log Report Type

Available layouts:

Paragraphs\
Tabular\
Template (already implemented — do not modify)\
Executive Summary Report Type

Available layouts:

Paragraphs\
Bullets\
Template (already implemented — do not modify)\
General Rendering Requirements

For all non-template layouts:

Display the Report Name as the first element.\
Display the Report Name as a heading.\
Display metadata immediately after the Report Name.\
Preserve heading hierarchy.\
Preserve keyboard accessibility.\
Preserve screen reader accessibility.\
Hide empty fields.\
Preserve field order.\
Do not duplicate data.\
Audit Log — Paragraph Layout

Render the report as a narrative document.

Requirements:

Report Name appears first as a heading.\
Metadata appears below the heading.\
Each configured report field should display:\
Field Name\
Field Value\
Use readable paragraph formatting.\
Do not use tables.\
Use semantic HTML.

Example:

Accessibility Audit Report

Audit Date

July 13, 2026

Finding

Missing alternative text was identified on several images.

Recommendation

Add descriptive alternative text.

Audit Log — Tabular Layout

Render the report as a structured data table.

Requirements:

Report Name appears first as a heading.\
Metadata appears above the table.\
Use:

<table>
<thead>
<tbody>
<th>
<td>
Column headers contain configured Field Names.
Each row represents one report entry.
Each row contains corresponding field values.

Accessibility requirements:

Each <th> must be programmatically associated with its data cells.

Use appropriate attributes such as:

scope="col"

If many columns exist, ensure screen reader users can efficiently
navigate the table.\
Long values should wrap inside cells.

Example:

Issue WCAG Criterion Severity Description Recommendation\
Missing image alternative text 1.1.1 Critical Images lack meaningful
alternative text Add descriptive alt text\
Executive Summary — Paragraph Layout

Requirements:

Report Name appears first as a heading.\
Metadata follows.\
Render content as readable narrative sections.\
Use headings where appropriate.\
Hide empty fields.\
Executive Summary — Bullet Layout

Requirements:

Report Name appears first as a heading.\
Metadata follows.

Render fields using:

<ul> and <li>

Use nested lists for multiple entries.\
Preserve field order.\
Ensure screen readers announce lists correctly.\
Testing Requirements

Verify:

Audit Log + Paragraphs\
Audit Log + Tabular\
Executive Summary + Paragraphs\
Executive Summary + Bullets

Verify:

Template layouts continue working unchanged.\
Keyboard navigation works.\
Screen reader output is logical.

Objective

Implement the report export system, including export file generation,
ZIP packaging, and ART-compatible JSON export.

Export Workflow

When the user selects Export Options and activates Save:

Create a ZIP file containing exactly two files:

1.  Human-readable Report Export

The exported report should use the format selected by the user:

Supported formats:

DOCX\
PDF\
HTML\
Markdown\
Plain Text\
RTF\
2. ART JSON File

Create:

\[Report Name\]\_ART.json

Requirements:

Contains the complete report data model.\
Contains all information required to reopen and edit the report in ART.\
Must preserve:\
Metadata\
Report Type\
Report Layout\
Template information\
Report Fields\
Report Values

The JSON should include:

{\
"artVersion": "1.0",\
"\_warning": "Warning: Do not edit. This file is used for importing your
report back into ART and will not work if modified."\
}

Do not use comments because JSON does not support comments.

Export Testing

Verify:

Each format generates successfully.\
ZIP contains exactly two files.\
JSON contains complete report information.\
Exported report can reconstruct the original report.\
Invalid or modified JSON files can be detected during future import
development.\
Accessibility Requirements

Ensure:

Export workflow is keyboard accessible.\
Dialogs are screen-reader accessible.\
Focus behavior is predictable.

## Epic 7 — WCAG Success Criteria Integration

Objective

Enhance the Report Builder, Report Editor, Report Viewer, WCAG Lookup
Tool, and export system to support structured WCAG Success Criterion
references.

This feature should allow report authors to quickly select official WCAG
Success Criteria while authoring reports, while allowing report readers
to easily access the official W3C documentation for any referenced
Success Criterion.

Part 1 — New Field Type

In the Report Builder, add a new Field Type named:

WCAG Success Criterion

This field type should appear alongside the existing field types (Text,
Text Area, Dropdown, etc.).

Part 2 — Populate Success Criteria from ART Data

When the report author configures a report field whose Field Type is
WCAG Success Criterion, the available Success Criterion options shall be
populated dynamically from the existing wcag_data.js file.

The list of available Success Criteria shall be determined by the
Accessibility Standard/Version selected in the Report Builder metadata.

For example:

WCAG 2.1\
WCAG 2.2

Do not hard-code Success Criterion data anywhere else in the
application.

If additional metadata is needed, extend wcag_data.js rather than
duplicating the same information in multiple locations.

The implementation shall automatically support future Accessibility
Standards or WCAG versions that are added to wcag_data.js without
requiring changes to the application logic.

Part 3 — Report Editor

When a WCAG Success Criterion field appears in the Report Editor:

Display an accessible searchable combobox containing every Success
Criterion available for the selected Accessibility Standard.

Each option shall display:

Success Criterion Number\
Official Success Criterion Title

Example:

1.1.1 Non-text Content\
1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)\
1.3.1 Info and Relationships\
1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)

The combobox must:

support keyboard navigation\
support screen readers\
support type-ahead searching\
allow searching by Success Criterion number\
allow searching by Success Criterion title\
announce expanded/collapsed state correctly\
preserve standard keyboard interaction\
expose the correct accessible name, role, and value

Store the selected value as structured data, not merely display text.

At a minimum, store:

Accessibility Standard/Version\
Success Criterion Identifier\
Success Criterion Number\
Success Criterion Title\
Conformance Level (A, AA, or AAA)

The stored identifier should remain stable even if a future WCAG
revision updates the display title.

Part 4 — WCAG Lookup Tool Synchronization

Whenever the Accessibility Standard/Version changes in the Report
Builder metadata:

Automatically update the WCAG Lookup Tool Version filter to match the
selected Accessibility Standard.\
Do not reset any other Lookup Tool filters unless necessary.\
Ensure the Lookup Tool immediately displays the Success Criteria for the
selected Accessibility Standard.

This synchronization should occur automatically whenever the
Accessibility Standard changes.

Part 5 — Report Viewer

When a report is viewed inside ART:

Display every referenced Success Criterion as an accessible hyperlink.

Example:

1.3.1 Info and Relationships

The hyperlink shall:

be keyboard accessible\
have a visible focus indicator\
include descriptive accessible link text\
preserve normal browser link behavior\
clearly indicate that official W3C documentation is available

Activating the hyperlink shall open the WCAG Documentation dialog.

The destination URL shall be obtained from the structured data in
wcag_data.js.

Part 6 — WCAG Documentation Dialog

When a Success Criterion hyperlink is activated from within ART:

Attempt to display the official W3C Understanding page for the selected
Success Criterion inside an accessible modal dialog.

Implementation requirements:

Obtain the exact Understanding page URL from wcag_data.js.\
Dynamically generate the destination URL using the stored Success
Criterion data.\
Do not hard-code W3C URLs throughout the application.\
Display the page inside an iframe if the W3C page permits embedding.

If the browser prevents the W3C page from being displayed inside an
iframe (for example because of security restrictions), automatically
open the official W3C Understanding page in a new browser tab instead.

This fallback shall occur automatically without displaying an error to
the user.

Accessibility requirements:

The dialog shall:

use semantic dialog markup\
expose an accessible name\
expose an accessible description when appropriate\
automatically move programmatic keyboard focus into the dialog when it
opens\
trap keyboard focus while open\
restore focus to the hyperlink that opened the dialog when it closes\
close when:\
Escape is pressed\
the Close button is activated\
be announced correctly by screen readers

The Close button shall be the first interactive control within the
dialog.

The embedded documentation shall:

provide a descriptive iframe title\
be keyboard accessible\
allow screen reader users to browse and read the W3C documentation using
normal browser commands\
not interfere with normal interaction inside the embedded page\
Part 7 — Export Behavior

When reports are exported:

Do not embed the documentation dialog.

Instead, render every referenced Success Criterion as a standard
hyperlink pointing directly to the official W3C Understanding page.

This behavior shall apply to:

HTML\
Markdown\
Microsoft Word\
PDF\
RTF

For Plain Text exports:

Display the Success Criterion followed by its complete W3C URL.

Example:

1.3.1 Info and Relationships

<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html>

Part 8 — Future-proof Architecture

Use wcag_data.js as the application's single source of truth for WCAG
Success Criterion information.

The catalog should contain (or be extended to contain):

Accessibility Standard/Version\
Success Criterion Identifier\
Success Criterion Number\
Success Criterion Title\
Conformance Level\
Official Understanding URL\
Official Recommendation URL (optional for future use)\
Any additional metadata already maintained by wcag_data.js

All comboboxes, hyperlinks, exported reports, documentation dialogs, and
Lookup Tool synchronization shall retrieve their information from this
centralized catalog.

The implementation should support future Accessibility Standards or WCAG
versions by updating wcag_data.js without requiring changes elsewhere in
the application.

Part 9 — Testing

Verify:

Each supported Accessibility Standard displays the correct Success
Criteria.\
The combobox filters correctly by Success Criterion number.\
The combobox filters correctly by Success Criterion title.\
Keyboard navigation functions correctly.\
Screen readers correctly announce the combobox.\
Selected values are stored correctly.\
The stable Success Criterion Identifier is preserved.\
Changing the Accessibility Standard immediately updates:\
the WCAG Success Criterion combobox\
the WCAG Lookup Tool Version filter\
generated documentation links\
Report Viewer displays accessible hyperlinks.\
The documentation dialog is fully keyboard accessible.\
Screen readers announce the dialog correctly.\
Escape closes the dialog.\
Focus returns to the hyperlink that opened the dialog.\
If iframe embedding is blocked by the browser or W3C website, the
Understanding page automatically opens in a new browser tab.\
Exported reports contain correct hyperlinks to the official W3C
Understanding pages.\
Existing report field types continue to work without regression.

Finally, summarize:

Files modified\
Data model changes\
Changes made to wcag_data.js\
Accessibility features implemented\
Testing performed

## Epic 8 — Report Management, Multi-Entry Editing, and Application Usability

Objective

Enhance ART by implementing comprehensive report management, support for
multi-entry audit reports, improved editing workflows, robust keyboard
accessibility, and application-wide usability improvements.

Before making changes:

1.  Review the existing application architecture and state management.
2.  Reuse existing patterns wherever possible.
3.  Do not introduce duplicate data models.
4.  Preserve all existing functionality, accessibility features,
    templates, exports, and report rendering.
5.  Maintain compatibility with existing reports stored in Local
    Storage.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 1 — Recent Reports Dashboard

Replace the existing Recent Reports area with an accessible report
selection control.

The Dashboard shall contain:

- Recent Reports selection box (combobox or listbox)
- Configure Report button
- Edit Report button
- View Report button
- Delete Report button

#### Configure Report

Loads the selected report into the Report Builder.

The Report Builder shall be populated with:

- Report metadata
- Report Type
- Report Layout
- Configure Report Fields
- Report field order
- Template information (if applicable)

Move programmatic keyboard focus to the Report Builder h2 heading.

##### Edit Report

Loads the selected report into the Report Editor.

Move programmatic keyboard focus to the Report Editor h2 heading.

#### View Report

Loads the selected report into the Report Viewer.

Move programmatic keyboard focus to the Report Viewer h2 heading.

#### Delete Report

Display an accessible confirmation dialog.

Example:

> Are you sure you want to delete **\[Report Name\]**?
>
> This action cannot be undone.

Buttons:

- Delete
- Cancel

Accessibility requirements:

- Focus moves into the dialog.
- Escape closes the dialog (same as Cancel).
- Cancel returns focus to the Delete Report button.
- Delete removes the report and returns focus to the Recent Reports
  selection control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 2 — Multi-Entry Audit Log Support

Audit Log reports shall support an unlimited number of report entries.

Add an **Add Entry** button to the Report Editor.

Activating Add Entry shall:

- Create a new blank audit entry.
- Use the current Report Field configuration.
- Preserve field order.
- Initialize every field to its default/blank value.
- Append the new entry to the report.
- Move keyboard focus to the first editable field in the new entry.

Users shall be able to create as many audit entries as needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 3 — Audit Log Table Editor

Display Audit Log entries in a semantic HTML table.

Use:

- `<table>`
- `<thead>`
- `<tbody>`
- `<th scope="col">`
- `<td>`

#### Table structure

Each configured report field becomes a column.

Each audit entry becomes one table row.

The final column shall be:

**Actions**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Edit Entry

Each row shall contain:

> Edit \[Entry Name\]

where **\[Entry Name\]** is replaced with the identifying field for that
row.

The Edit button shall:

- expose `aria-expanded`
- expose `aria-controls`
- update `aria-expanded` when expanded/collapsed

Expanding the Edit button shall reveal:

- Move Up
- Move Down
- Delete Entry

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Move Up

Move the selected row one position earlier.

Update both:

- the table
- the underlying report data

Announce:

> Moved before \[Entry Name\]

using an `aria-live="polite"` region.

Disable Move Up on the first row.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Move Down

Move the selected row one position later.

Update both:

- the table
- the underlying report data

Announce:

> Moved after \[Entry Name\]

using an `aria-live="polite"` region.

Disable Move Down on the final row.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Delete Entry

Display an accessible confirmation dialog.

Example:

> Are you sure you want to delete the **\[Entry Name\]** entry?
>
> This action cannot be undone.

Buttons:

- Confirm
- Cancel

Confirm:

- deletes the entry from both the report and the table
- closes the dialog
- moves focus to the Delete button for the next entry (or previous entry
  if the last row was deleted)

Cancel:

- closes the dialog
- restores focus to the Delete button that opened it

Escape shall perform the same action as Cancel.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 4 — Import Conflict Protection

When importing a report whose name already exists:

Display:

> A report named **Accessibility Audit – July 2026** already exists.

Options:

- Replace existing report
- Create a copy
- Cancel

Replace:

- overwrite the existing report

Create a copy:

- preserve the existing report
- import the new report as a separate report

Cancel:

- cancel the import
- restore focus to the Import button

### Part 5 — Dashboard Metrics

Display report metrics for the currently selected report.

Include:

- Total Issues
- Pages Tested (unique page names)

- Number of WCAG Success Criteria referenced

The metrics shall update automatically whenever the report changes.

Implement application-wide Undo and Redo.

Keyboard shortcuts:

- Ctrl+Z — Undo
- Ctrl+Shift+Z — Redo

Before implementation:

Identify the existing state management approach.

Implement Undo/Redo using the existing architecture rather than
introducing a separate state model.

Undo/Redo shall support:

- report metadata
- report fields
- audit entries
- templates
- report layouts
- report type
- report content

Requirements:

- restore complete report state
- preserve keyboard accessibility
- never lose user data
- maintain programmatic focus whenever practical

Announce actions using an `aria-live="polite"` region.

Example announcements:

- Undo: Deleted report field Severity.
- Redo: Restored report field Severity.
- Undo: Moved WCAG Criterion before Recommendation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 7 — Landmark Navigation

Restore landmark navigation using:

- Ctrl+F6
- Ctrl+Shift+F6

The shortcuts shall cycle through:

1.  Navigation tablist
2.  Dashboard
3.  Active Report panel (**Welcome, Builder, Editor, or Viewer**,
    depending on which panel is currently displayed)
4.  WCAG Lookup Tool

Then return to the Navigation tablist.

Reverse order shall be supported using Ctrl+Shift+F6.

When focus moves:

- Screen readers should announce the first visible heading within the
  destination region whenever possible.
- If no heading is available, announce the accessible name of the
  destination region or landmark (for example, "Navigation",
  "Dashboard", "Welcome", "Report Builder", "Report Editor", "Report
  Viewer", or "WCAG Lookup Tool").
- Do not produce duplicate announcements for the same navigation action.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 8 — Additional Keyboard Shortcuts

Add application shortcuts that do not conflict with standard browser
shortcuts.

| Shortcut    | Action                                                |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Alt+Shift+N | Move to the Navigation tablist                        |
| Alt+Shift+S | Move to the Dashboard                                 |
| Alt+Shift+U | Open the Report Builder and move focus to its heading |

| Alt+Shift+F | Activate the Add Field button in the Report Builder   |
| Alt+Shift+O | Activate the Done button in the Report Builder        |

### Part 9 — Focus Management

Review all interactive controls throughout ART.

Except where a previous Epic explicitly requires focus to move
elsewhere:

- Activating a button shall not move focus unexpectedly.
- Selecting an item from a combobox shall not move focus.
- Selecting a dropdown value shall not move focus.
- Editing report content shall not move focus.
- Dialogs shall restore focus to the control that opened them.
- Programmatic focus shall never jump to the beginning of the page.

Maintain a predictable keyboard experience throughout the application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Accessibility Requirements

All new functionality shall:

- Use semantic HTML.
- Preserve logical heading hierarchy.
- Preserve logical tab order.
- Support keyboard-only operation.
- Support screen readers.
- Use ARIA only when native HTML semantics are insufficient.
- Preserve visible keyboard focus indicators.
- Provide appropriate `aria-live` announcements where state changes
  occur.
- Correctly manage focus for dialogs, region navigation, and application
  keyboard shortcuts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Testing

Verify:

- Configure Report workflow
- Edit Report workflow
- View Report workflow
- Delete Report workflow
- Multiple audit entries
- Add Entry functionality
- Audit Log table rendering
- Entry editing

- Ctrl+F6 and Ctrl+Shift+F6 landmark navigation
- All new keyboard shortcuts

## Epic 9 — Report Maintenance and Metadata Editing

Objective

Improve the report editing workflow by allowing users to:

- Clear report data without accidentally losing report configuration.
- Edit report metadata directly from the Report Editor.
- Preserve accessibility, keyboard usability, and predictable focus
  management throughout both workflows.

Before implementation:

1.  Review the existing report state management.
2.  Reuse the existing dialog component and accessibility patterns where

3.  Do not introduce duplicate metadata models.
4.  Preserve compatibility with existing reports, templates, exports,
    and Local Storage.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part 1 — Clear Report Data

Add a **Clear Report Data...** button to the Report Editor.

The button should appear after the Audit Entries section and before the
final report action buttons.

Activating **Clear Report Data...** shall open an accessible
confirmation dialog.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Clear Report Dialog

Dialog title:

**Clear Report**

Dialog text:

**What would you like to clear?**

Radio button options:

**Clear report content only (recommended)**

Description:

- Removes all audit entries and entered field values.
- Preserves report metadata.
- Preserves report fields.
- Preserves Report Type.
- Preserves Report Layout.
- Preserves template selection and configuration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Clear everything**

Description:

- Removes report metadata.
- Removes configured report fields.
- Removes report content.
- Removes Report Type and Report Layout selections.
- Returns the report to a blank report ready for configuration.

Buttons:

- Clear
- Cancel

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Clear Report Behavior

Clear report content only

When the user activates **Clear**:

- Remove every audit entry.

- Clear every entered field value.

- Preserve:

  - Report metadata
  - Report fields
  - Report Type
  - Report Layout
  - Template information

- Save the updated report.

- Close the dialog.

- Move programmatic keyboard focus to the first editable field in the
  Report Editor.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Clear everything

When the user activates **Clear**:

- Remove all report metadata.
- Remove all configured report fields.
- Remove all report content.
- Reset Report Type and Report Layout to their default selections.
- Preserve the report object itself so the user remains in the same
  editing session.
- Save the updated report.
- Close the dialog.
- Open the Report Builder.
- Move programmatic keyboard focus to the Report Builder h2 heading.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cancel

When the user activates **Cancel**:

- Close the dialog.
- Make no changes.
- Return focus to the **Clear Report Data...** button.

Pressing the **Escape** key shall perform the same action as **Cancel**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Accessibility Requirements

The dialog shall:

- Use semantic dialog markup.
- Have an accessible name.
- Have an accessible description.
- Automatically receive programmatic keyboard focus when opened.
- Trap keyboard focus while open.
- Restore focus correctly when closed.
- Support keyboard-only users.
- Support screen readers.
- Announce itself appropriately.
- Clearly communicate the consequences of each option.

Part 2 — Edit Metadata

Add an **Edit Metadata...** button immediately after the displayed
metadata section and before the Audit Entries heading within the Report
Editor.

This button allows users to update report metadata without returning to

This feature edits only report metadata.

Edit Metadata Dialog

- Website

- Audit Date

- Scope
- Description
- Header information
- Logo or branding metadata

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dialog Buttons

Buttons:

- Confirm
- Cancel

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Confirm

When activated:

- Update the report metadata.
- Update the Report Builder metadata model.
- Update the metadata displayed within the Report Editor.
- Update the metadata displayed within the Report Viewer.
- Update any exported report generated afterward.
- Save the report.
- Close the dialog.

Cancel

- Preserve template compatibility.

Testing

## Epic 10 — Accessibility, Focus Management, and Editor Stability

Objective

Resolve remaining accessibility regressions and focus-management issues
throughout ART. Ensure programmatic keyboard focus is predictable,
screen reader announcements are appropriate, and keyboard users can
navigate the application without unexpected focus movement.

Before implementation:

1.  Review the application's current focus-management logic.
2.  Identify the underlying cause(s) of focus unexpectedly moving to the
    beginning of the page.
3.  Correct the underlying focus-management implementation rather than
    adding individual workarounds for specific controls.
4.  Preserve all existing accessibility features, keyboard shortcuts,
    templates, report rendering, and exports.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 1 — Suppress WCAG Lookup Tool Announcements Outside the Lookup Tool

Temporarily suppress all `aria-live` announcements originating from the
WCAG Lookup Tool whenever the user is interacting with controls in the
Report Builder or Report Editor.

The Lookup Tool's announcements should only occur while the user is
actively interacting with the WCAG Lookup Tool itself.

Restore normal `aria-live` behavior immediately when focus returns to
the WCAG Lookup Tool.

Do not suppress any other application announcements.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 2 — Correct Focus Management

Investigate and correct the underlying cause of programmatic keyboard
focus returning to the beginning of the page.

This issue currently occurs after interacting with:

- Accessibility Standard
- Report Type
- Report Layout
- Template selection
- Enable Branding
- Configure Report Fields
- Hide Field Configuration
- Editing an existing template

Correct the underlying focus-management logic rather than implementing
individual fixes for each control.

Unless another Epic explicitly requires focus movement, activating
controls or confirming selections shall leave programmatic keyboard
focus on the control that initiated the interaction.

This shall include:

- Comboboxes
- Checkboxes
- Buttons
- Expand/collapse controls

Tab order shall remain continuous and predictable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 3 — Template Selection

When:

Report Layout → Template

Template Option → Choose Template

Populate the Choose Template combobox using exactly the same template
collection displayed in the Dashboard's Template Selection control.

Include:

- Built-in templates
- User-created templates

Do not maintain duplicate template collections.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 4 — Builder to Editor Transition

After the user activates:

Apply

followed by:

Done

Display the Report Editor.

Before moving keyboard focus:

Announce using an `aria-live="polite"` region:

> Report moved to Editor.

Immediately after the announcement begins:

Move programmatic keyboard focus to the Report Title heading (h2).

Do not produce duplicate announcements.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 5 — Report Editor Instructions

Remove the text:

> Use Up and Down arrow keys to review options, then Enter to confirm.

Replace it with concise instructions such as:

> Fill in the audit report fields in the table.
>
> Use the Add Entry button to create another audit entry.
>
> Use Edit Entry to expand options for moving or deleting entries.

The instructions should be concise, readable, and useful for both
keyboard and screen reader users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 6 — Accessible Field Associations

Every editable field within the Audit Entries table shall expose an
`aria-labelledby` attribute referencing its column header.

Example:

If the column header is:

``` html
<th id="page">Page</th>
```

every editable field within that column shall include:

``` html
aria-labelledby="page"
```

Apply this dynamically to every row.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 7 — Dynamic Accessible Names

The value contained in the first column of each audit entry shall be
treated as the entry's display name.

Whenever that value changes, immediately update the accessible names for
the associated controls.

Examples:

- Edit Homepage
- Edit Contact Us
- Edit Location

Likewise, update:

- Move Homepage Up
- Move Homepage Down
- Delete Homepage

These accessible names shall update dynamically whenever the identifying
field changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Requirements

All fixes shall:

- Preserve semantic HTML.
- Preserve heading hierarchy.
- Preserve logical tab order.
- Preserve keyboard accessibility.
- Preserve screen reader usability.
- Avoid duplicate announcements.
- Use ARIA only where native HTML semantics are insufficient.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Testing

Verify:

- WCAG Lookup announcements occur only while interacting with the Lookup
  Tool.
- Focus no longer jumps to the beginning of the page.
- Template selection displays every available template.
- Report Builder → Editor transition announces correctly.
- Updated instructions display correctly.
- Every Audit Entry field references its column header using
  `aria-labelledby`.
- Accessible names update dynamically.
- Keyboard navigation remains logical.
- Screen readers announce all controls correctly.

Finally, summarize:

- Files modified
- Accessibility fixes implemented
- Focus-management improvements
- Testing performed

## Epic 11 — Report Editor Workflow Enhancements

Objective

Enhance the Report Editor by adding additional report management
actions, validation tools, statistics, and navigation features that
improve usability while preserving accessibility.

Before implementation:

1.  Review the existing Report Editor architecture.
2.  Reuse existing dialogs and application patterns where possible.
3.  Preserve compatibility with templates, exports, Local Storage,
    Undo/Redo, and existing report rendering.

### Part 1 — Move Add Entry Button

Move the Add Entry button.

Instead of appearing before the Audit Entries table, it shall appear
immediately after the Audit Entries table.

Part 1.5 — Keyboard Shortcut for Add Entry

Assign the keyboard shortcut:

Alt+Shift+A

to activate the Add Entry button from anywhere within the application.

Requirements\
The shortcut shall not conflict with standard browser, operating system,
or existing ART keyboard shortcuts.\
When Alt+Shift+A is pressed:\
If the current report supports multiple audit entries, activate the Add
Entry functionality.\
Create a new blank audit entry using the current report's configured
field structure.\
Append the new entry to the end of the Audit Entries table.\
Move programmatic keyboard focus to the first editable field in the
newly created row.\
Announce the action using an aria-live="polite" region.\
The Add Entry button shall continue to function normally when activated
using the mouse, touch, keyboard (Tab + Enter/Space), or any other
supported input method.\
Regardless of how the action is invoked (button activation or keyboard
shortcut), the same focus management and announcement behavior shall be
used.\
Announcement

The announcement shall include the newly created audit entry number.

The audit entry number shall always be calculated as:

(Total number of rows in the Audit Entries table) − 1

Subtract one to account for the table's header row (<thead>), which is
not an audit entry.

Examples:

Total Table Rows Audit Entry Number Announced\
2 Added audit entry 1.\
3 Added audit entry 2.\
5 Added audit entry 4.\
16 Added audit entry 15.

The announcement shall accurately reflect the new audit entry's position
in the table immediately after it has been added.

Accessible Tooltip

The Add Entry button shall expose an accessible tooltip that identifies
its keyboard shortcut.

Example tooltip text:

Alt+Shift+A

Requirements:

The tooltip shall be available to mouse, keyboard, and screen reader
users.\
Keyboard users shall be able to discover the tooltip when the button
receives keyboard focus.\
The tooltip shall use semantic, accessible markup and be
programmatically associated with the button (for example, using
aria-describedby when appropriate).\
The tooltip shall not interfere with keyboard navigation or screen
reader announcements.\
The tooltip shall display only the keyboard shortcut, since the button's
accessible name already identifies its purpose.\
The tooltip text shall also be included wherever the application
documents available keyboard shortcuts, including the Keyboard Shortcuts
Manager.

If the active report type does not support multiple entries, the
shortcut shall have no effect or provide a polite announcement
indicating that the command is unavailable for the current report type.

The shortcut shall be included in:

The application's Keyboard Shortcuts Help.\
The Keyboard Shortcuts Manager (once implemented).

## Epic 12 — Application Identity, Landmark Accessibility, and Template Management

Objective

Improve ART's usability, accessibility, and template management by:

- Keeping the browser window title synchronized with the active report
  and application panel.
- Improving landmark identification for assistive technology users
  through proper semantic region labeling.
- Allowing users to import and export report templates from the
  Dashboard.
- Ensuring imported templates are validated and handled safely.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 1 — Dynamic Window Title

Keep the browser window title synchronized with the current application
state.

The window title shall update whenever:

- The active application panel changes.
- The active report changes.
- The report title changes.
- A report is opened.
- A report is closed.
- A new report is created.
- The user switches between the Welcome, Dashboard, Report Builder,
  Report Editor, Report Viewer, WCAG Lookup Tool, or Settings (if
  implemented).

#### Window Title Format

When a report is open:

``` text
<Report Name> – <Current Panel> | ART
```

Examples:

``` text
Accessibility Audit – Dashboard | ART

Accessibility Audit – Report Builder | ART

Accessibility Audit – Report Editor | ART

Accessibility Audit – Report Viewer | ART

Accessibility Audit – WCAG Lookup Tool | ART
```

When no report is open:

``` text
Welcome | ART

Dashboard | ART
```

##### Requirements

- Update immediately whenever the active report or active panel changes.
- Do not require refreshing the page.
- Keep the browser tab title synchronized with the application state.
- Avoid unnecessary title updates when neither the report nor active
  panel has changed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 2 — Import Template

Add an **Import Template...** action to the **Dashboard** alongside the
existing template management controls.

#### Requirements

- Accept ART Template JSON files.

- Validate the template before importing.

- Display accessible error messages if the file is invalid.

- Add successfully imported templates to the existing Template Library.

- Preserve:

  - report metadata definitions
  - configured report fields
  - report layouts
  - branding configuration
  - report type
  - validation settings
  - template metadata

- Support future template schema versions through version metadata.

- Reject malformed or unsupported template files without affecting
  existing templates.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 3 — Template Conflict Resolution

If an imported template has the same name as an existing template,
display an accessible confirmation dialog.

Example:

``` text
Template already exists

A template named:

Accessibility Audit Template

already exists.

What would you like to do?

○ Replace existing template

○ Create a copy

○ Cancel
```

#### Requirements

- Fully keyboard accessible.
- Fully screen reader accessible.
- Take programmatic keyboard focus when opened.
- Escape performs Cancel.
- Confirm performs the selected action.
- Restore focus to the Import Template button if cancelled.
- After successful import, move focus to the newly imported template
  within the Template Selection list.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 4 — Export Template

Add an **Export Template...** action to the **Dashboard** alongside the
existing template management controls.

#### Requirements

Export only reusable template information.

Do **not** include:

- report content
- audit entries
- completed field values

Preserve:

- report metadata definitions
- configured report fields
- branding configuration
- report layouts
- report type
- validation rules
- template metadata

Export as ART Template JSON.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 5 — Landmark Naming and Region Identification

Improve identification of ART's major application regions by ensuring
each landmark has a programmatically associated accessible name.

#### Requirements

Every major application region shall expose an accessible name using its
first visible heading.

This includes:

- Welcome
- Dashboard
- Report Builder
- Report Editor
- Report Viewer
- WCAG Lookup Tool
- Settings (if implemented)

The navigation tablist shall continue to be contained within the
existing `<nav>` landmark and shall retain its current accessible name.

Each application region shall:

- Use the appropriate semantic landmark element (`<main>`, `<section>`,
  `<aside>`, etc.) according to its purpose.
- Contain a visible heading as its first child element.
- Reference that heading using `aria-labelledby`.
- Ensure the heading's `id` is unique within the document.
- Avoid duplicate or conflicting accessible names.
- Preserve the existing heading hierarchy.

Example:

``` html
<section
    id="reportBuilderRegion"
    aria-labelledby="reportBuilderHeading">

    <h2 id="reportBuilderHeading">
        Report Builder
    </h2>

    ...
</section>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 6 — Screen Reader Region Identification

Improve contextual awareness when users move between major application
regions.

The implementation shall improve the likelihood that screen readers
announce entry into a new application region when navigating using:

- Tab
- Shift+Tab
- Headings
- Form controls
- Buttons
- Tables
- Lists
- Links
- Other standard screen reader navigation commands

Do **not** use `aria-live` announcements solely to announce entry into a
region.

Instead:

- Rely on semantic HTML landmarks.
- Use correctly associated headings through `aria-labelledby`.
- Allow assistive technologies to naturally announce region names
  without creating duplicate or unnecessary speech.
- Do not interfere with existing focus management or keyboard
  navigation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Part 7 — Testing

Verify:

#### Dynamic Window Title

- Opening a report updates the title.
- Closing a report updates the title.
- Renaming a report immediately updates the title.
- Switching between Welcome, Dashboard, Builder, Editor, Viewer, Lookup
  Tool, and Settings updates the title.
- Browser refresh preserves the correct title.

#### Template Import

- Valid templates import successfully.
- Invalid templates are rejected.
- Malformed JSON is handled gracefully.
- Existing templates remain unaffected after failed imports.

#### Template Conflict Resolution

- Replace existing template works correctly.
- Create copy works correctly.
- Cancel leaves existing templates unchanged.
- Keyboard navigation works.
- Screen readers announce the dialog correctly.
- Focus management behaves correctly.

#### Template Export

- Exported templates contain configuration only.
- No report content is exported.
- Exported templates can be imported successfully.

#### Landmark Accessibility

Verify using keyboard navigation and at least JAWS and NVDA that:

- Every application region exposes the correct accessible name.
- The accessible name is derived from the first visible heading.
- The `<nav>` landmark continues to expose the correct accessible name.
- Duplicate announcements are not introduced.
- Screen readers naturally announce region names when supported by the
  browser and assistive technology.
- Existing keyboard navigation continues to function correctly.
- Existing focus management is not affected.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Before Implementation

1.  Review the existing template management implementation.
2.  Identify where templates are stored in local storage.
3.  Identify the current template JSON schema.
4.  Reuse existing import/export logic wherever practical.
5.  Ensure imported templates remain compatible with future schema
    versions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### After Implementation

Summarize:

- Files modified
- Changes to the template data model
- Import functionality added
- Export functionality added
- Window title management implementation
- Landmark accessibility improvements
- Testing performed
- Accessibility considerations implemented

## Epic 13 — Application Settings and User Preferences

Objective

Create an accessible Application Settings modal that allows users to
manage ART configuration, customize keyboard shortcuts, manage imported
accessibility standards, and perform application maintenance tasks.

The settings system should provide a centralized location for
user-controlled application behavior while maintaining ART's
accessibility-first design principles.

Part 1 — Application Settings Access

Add an Application Settings button to the ART interface.

Recommended location:

Dashboard near other application-level actions.

Activating the button shall open an accessible modal dialog.

The dialog shall:

Use semantic dialog markup.\
Have an accessible name.\
Move programmatic focus into the dialog when opened.\
Place initial focus on the first interactive control.\
Trap keyboard focus while open.\
Close with:\
Escape key.\
Close button.\
Restore focus to the Application Settings button when closed.

The dialog should contain clearly labeled sections.

Part 2 — Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Create a Keyboard Shortcut Manager section.

The shortcut manager shall:

Display all currently assigned ART keyboard shortcuts.\
Display the associated action/function.\
Allow users to customize existing shortcuts.\
Allow users to assign shortcuts to actions that do not currently have
shortcuts.\
Detect shortcut conflicts.\
Prevent duplicate shortcut assignments unless explicitly confirmed.\
Allow users to restore default shortcuts.

The shortcut manager shall support existing ART shortcuts, including:

Examples:

Ctrl+F6 / Ctrl+Shift+F6 — Navigate application regions.\
Alt+Shift+N — Navigation tablist.\
Alt+Shift+S — Dashboard.\
Alt+Shift+U — Report Builder.\
Alt+Shift+E — Report Editor.\
Alt+Shift+L — WCAG Lookup Tool.\
Alt+Shift+F — Add Field.\
Alt+Shift+O — Done.\
Alt+Shift+A — Add Entry.\
Ctrl+O — Open/Import Report.\
Ctrl+Shift+S — Export Report.\
Ctrl+N — New Report.\
Ctrl+Shift+N — New Report from Template.

The shortcut manager should:

Provide an accessible table/list of shortcuts.\
Allow keyboard-only editing.\
Announce shortcut changes through aria-live.\
Clearly identify conflicts.

Example announcement:

"Shortcut changed. Alt Shift A is now assigned to Add Entry."

Part 3 — Accessibility Standards Management

Add an Accessibility Standards section.

Users shall be able to:

View currently available accessibility standards.\
Import additional accessibility standard data files.\
Manage imported standards.

Imported accessibility standards shall:

Use a structured JSON format.\
Be validated before import.\
Be stored safely.\
Not overwrite existing standards without confirmation.

After a new accessibility standard is successfully imported, ART shall
prompt the user to provide a display name for the imported standard.

The application shall display an accessible dialog or prompt containing:

Accessibility Standard Name

Textbox:

\[User enters name\]

Buttons:

Save\
Cancel

Requirements:

The textbox shall receive programmatic focus when the naming prompt
opens.\
The prompt shall clearly explain that this name will be used throughout
ART.\
The entered name shall become the user-facing display name for the
imported accessibility standard.

The user-provided accessibility standard name shall be displayed in:

The Accessibility Standard selection box in the Report Builder.\
The Version selection box in the WCAG Lookup Tool.\
Any other user-facing location where ART displays available
accessibility standards.

The imported standard's internal metadata shall preserve:

Original imported identifier (if available).\
User-provided display name.\
Version information.\
Source information.\
Structured success criteria data.

The system should:

Extend the existing wcag_data.js architecture.\
Maintain a centralized accessibility standard catalog.\
Support future accessibility standards without requiring application
code changes.\
Part 4 — Reset Application Data

Add an application reset option.

Button:

Reset ART Application Data

Because this action can remove significant user data, activating it
shall open an accessible confirmation dialog.

Dialog text:

Reset ART Application Data

"What would you like to reset?"

Options:

○ Reset user preferences only

Removes customized settings.\
Restores default keyboard shortcuts.\
Keeps reports and templates.

○ Reset all application data

Removes reports.\
Removes templates.\
Removes imported accessibility standards.\
Clears local storage.\
Returns ART to its default installation state.

Buttons:

Reset\
Cancel

Accessibility requirements:

The dialog shall:

Receive programmatic focus when opened.\
Clearly explain consequences.\
Support keyboard navigation.\
Close with Escape.\
Return focus to the reset button if canceled.

After completion:

Announce the result using aria-live.

Example:

"Application settings restored."

or

"ART has been reset to its default state."

Part 5 — Application Information

Add an About section.

Display:

ART application name.\
Version number.\
Build date (if available).\
Data schema version.\
Imported accessibility standards.\
Link to documentation/help.\
Part 6 — Settings Persistence

Settings changes shall:

Persist using the existing local storage architecture.\
Survive application restart.\
Be included in application backup/export where appropriate.

The implementation should:

Use existing state management.\
Avoid creating a separate settings data model.\
Part 7 — Accessibility Testing

Verify:

Settings modal opens correctly.\
Focus management works correctly.\
Keyboard-only users can operate all settings.\
Screen readers announce sections correctly.\
Shortcut customization works.\
Shortcut conflicts are detected.\
Reset confirmation works.\
Local storage updates correctly.\
Imported accessibility standards appear correctly.\
User-provided accessibility standard names appear in:\
Report Builder Accessibility Standard selection.\
WCAG Lookup Tool Version selection.\
Imported accessibility standards do not affect existing reports or
templates.\
Existing ART functionality is not affected.\
Final Summary

Provide:

Files modified.\
New settings architecture.\
Keyboard shortcut changes.\
Accessibility standard import changes.\
Data model changes.\
Accessibility improvements.\
Testing performed.

## Epic 14 – Spell Checking, Editing Productivity, Excel Export, Keyboard Enhancements, and Accessibility Remediation

Objective

Improve report authoring, editing efficiency, keyboard customization,
export capabilities, and overall accessibility of the Accessibility
Reporting Tool (ART).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Spell Check

Implement an integrated spell checker for the Report Editor.

##### Requirements

- Default shortcut: **F7**.
- Attempt to intercept/override browser F7 behavior where technically
  possible.
- If browser restrictions prevent this, provide the closest possible
  implementation while preserving F7 where supported.
- Add Spell Check to the Welcome screen shortcut list.
- Add Spell Check to the Help documentation.
- Add Spell Check to the Keyboard Manager so the shortcut can be
  reassigned.

#### Spell Check Dialog

Open Spell Check in a fully accessible modal dialog modeled after the
familiar workflow of modern desktop word processors.

Requirements:

- Accessible modal using native `<dialog>` where practical.
- Focus trapped within dialog.
- Restore focus to editor on close.
- ESC closes dialog.
- Enter activates default action.
- Underlying editor remains inaccessible while dialog is open.
- Maintain visible focus at all times.

Display:

- Current misspelled word.
- Sentence/paragraph context.
- Suggested replacements.
- Editable **Replace With** textbox for manually entering corrections.
- Remaining spelling issue count.

Selecting a suggestion automatically populates the Replace With textbox.

The textbox allows users to manually correct technical terms, acronyms,
product names, and specialized vocabulary not present in the spelling
dictionary.

While dialog is open:

- Highlight current misspelled word in editor.
- Scroll current word into view.
- Keep keyboard focus inside dialog.

##### Commands

- Replace
- Replace All
- Ignore
- Ignore All
- Undo Last Correction
- Cancel

##### Keyboard Accelerators

Default accelerators:

- Alt+R — Replace
- Alt+A — Replace All
- Alt+I — Ignore
- Alt+G — Ignore All
- Alt+U — Undo Last Correction
- Alt+C — Cancel

These accelerators shall be configurable within the Keyboard Manager and
behave like any other customizable ART shortcut.

##### Undo

Replace Add to Dictionary with Undo Last Correction.

Requirements:

- Ctrl+Z performs Undo Last Correction while Spell Check is active.
- Undo only affects the most recent spelling replacement within the
  current spell-check session.
- Restore original word.
- Restore original context.
- Return to corrected spelling issue.
- Announce undo to assistive technologies.

##### Completion

When finished:

Display:

- "No spelling issues were found."

or

- "Spell checking is complete."

Provide Close button returning focus to editor.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Excel Export

Add Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) as a report export format.

Requirements:

- Preserve report structure.
- Include meaningful worksheet names.
- Include descriptive column headers.
- Maintain readable formatting.
- Export all report information currently supported by existing export
  formats.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Manager Enhancements

Expand shortcut customization.

Add assignable shortcuts for:

- Spell Check
- Replace
- Replace All
- Ignore
- Ignore All
- Undo Last Correction
- Copy Entry
- Copy Name
- Copy Description
- Copy Failures
- Copy Fixes
- Copy Link

Existing functionality shall continue supporting:

- Shortcut reassignment
- Conflict detection
- Reserved shortcut detection
- Duplicate warnings
- Restore Defaults

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Audit and Remediation

Perform a complete accessibility audit of the entire ART application.

Review and remediate all accessibility issues discovered.

Verify every:

- View
- Panel
- Dialog
- Menu
- Toolbar
- Form
- Workflow
- Keyboard shortcut
- Dynamic update
- Editor
- Report workflow
- Import/Export workflow
- WCAG Lookup Tool
- Template workflow
- Help system
- Settings page

Correct all issues necessary to achieve WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.

Requirements:

- Prefer semantic HTML.
- Remove unnecessary ARIA.
- Correct invalid ARIA.
- Ensure meaningful accessible names.
- Verify logical reading order.
- Verify logical focus order.
- Maintain visible focus indicators.
- Support keyboard-only operation.
- Support NVDA, JAWS, Narrator, and VoiceOver.
- Verify operation at 200%, 300%, and 400% zoom.
- Verify Windows High Contrast / forced-colors compatibility.
- Respect Reduced Motion preferences.
- Prevent accessibility regressions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Documentation

Update:

- Welcome screen shortcuts.
- Help documentation.
- Keyboard shortcut reference.
- Settings documentation.
- Release notes.

Document:

- Spell Check workflow.
- Manual correction textbox.
- Keyboard accelerators.
- Customizable accelerators.
- Excel export.
- New copy shortcuts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Acceptance Criteria

Epic 14 is complete when:

- F7 launches Spell Check.
- Spell Check is fully keyboard accessible.
- Spell Check uses an accessible modal dialog.
- Users may choose a suggestion or manually enter a replacement.
- Ctrl+Z performs Undo Last Correction.
- Default accelerators function correctly.
- Spell Check accelerators are user-configurable.
- Spell Check shortcut is user-configurable.
- Excel (.xlsx) export functions correctly.
- Keyboard Manager supports all newly added commands.
- Documentation has been updated.
- A full accessibility audit has been completed.
- Accessibility issues identified during the audit have been remediated.
- ART conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA without introducing regressions.

## Epic 15– ART Integrated Help and Documentation System

Objective

Create a complete, accessible Help and Documentation system for the
Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART).

The Help system shall provide users with a reliable reference for
understanding ART, learning workflows, discovering features, and
accessing assistance without requiring external documentation.

The Help system shall be designed for long-term maintainability and
should automatically evolve as ART functionality expands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Help System Requirements

Implement an integrated Help system accessible from within ART.

Requirements:

- Provide a dedicated Help experience.
- Support opening Help through the ART Help command.
- Support F1 Help access where technically possible.
- Allow Help to open independently from the main application workflow.
- Preserve the user's place in ART while Help is open.
- Provide clear navigation throughout documentation.
- Allow users to quickly locate information through headings, links, and
  search/browser find functionality.

The Help system architecture should allow future migration to a desktop
Help window when ART is packaged as an Electron or Tauri application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Documentation Structure

Create a structured documentation system with:

- Semantic HTML.
- Properly nested heading hierarchy.
- Logical document organization.
- Accessible Table of Contents.
- Internal section links.
- Bookmarkable sections.
- Consistent navigation.

The documentation should be organized into logical sections such as:

- Getting Started
- ART Overview
- User Interface
- Navigation
- Features and Workflows
- Settings and Configuration
- Accessibility
- Keyboard Shortcuts
- Import and Export
- Templates
- Reports
- WCAG Lookup Tool
- Frequently Asked Questions
- About ART
- Credits
- Open Source Information
- Future Development

The exact organization may be refined during implementation to provide
the best user experience.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Documentation Content Requirements

Document all ART functionality, including:

- Application purpose and intended users.
- What ART does and does not do.
- User interface structure.
- Navigation methods.
- Panels, regions, landmarks, and major application areas.
- Features and workflows.
- Settings and configuration options.
- Import/export behavior.
- Templates.
- Reports and layouts.
- Accessibility features and limitations.
- Help system usage.

Documentation should describe both:

- What a feature does.
- How users interact with it.

Avoid duplicating implementation details already defined in other ART
development epics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

User Interface Documentation

Document the ART interface in a way that helps both new and experienced
users understand:

- Application layout.
- Major regions and landmarks.
- Navigation model.
- Relationship between panels.
- Keyboard and screen reader navigation approaches.
- Available commands within each area.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Keyboard Shortcut Documentation

Provide a complete keyboard shortcut reference.

Requirements:

- Include all ART keyboard shortcuts.
- Include both default and user-customized shortcuts.
- Display shortcuts using this format:

**Command Name: Keyboard Shortcut**

Examples:

- Add entry in Report Editor: **Alt+Shift+A**
- Help: **F1**
- Spell Check: **F7**

Requirements:

- Sort all shortcut listings alphabetically by command name.
- Do not sort by shortcut key.
- Display the current shortcut assignment, not only the default value.
- Reflect user-customized shortcut mappings.
- Keep shortcut references synchronized with the Keyboard Manager.

Display shortcut references consistently in:

- Help documentation.
- Welcome panel.
- Keyboard Manager.
- Settings.

Shortcut documentation shall include:

- Command purpose.
- Current shortcut assignment.
- Whether the shortcut can be customized.
- Any limitations or reserved combinations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### About ART Section

Create an About ART section containing:

- Project background.
- Origins of ART.
- Purpose and motivation.
- Reason for the ART name.
- Project philosophy.
- Vision and goals.
- Accessibility-first principles.
