## Epic 16: Accessibility Standards Engine, Import, and Management

Objective

Expand ART's existing Accessibility Standards Engine and Accessibility
Lookup Tool into a standards-agnostic accessibility knowledge system
capable of supporting multiple accessibility standards while preserving
existing WCAG functionality and ART's accessibility knowledge
enhancements.

The system shall support official accessibility standards,
organization-specific standards, user-created standards, and future
standards (including WCAG 3) through a flexible, extensible architecture
without requiring major application redesigns.

Standards Engine Expansion

Enhance the Accessibility Standards Engine to support:

Multiple installed accessibility standards.\
Multiple versions of the same accessibility standard when applicable.\
Future WCAG 3 support.\
Organization-specific accessibility standards.\
User-created accessibility standards.\
Flexible standards-agnostic architecture.\
Independent updates to standards without requiring ART application
updates.

Maintain a clear separation between:

ART-provided default accessibility standards.\
User-installed, imported, and modified accessibility standards.\
ART accessibility knowledge metadata.\
Default and User Standards Storage

Rename the existing built-in standards file:

wcag_data.js

to:

defaultStandards.js

Update all repository references, imports, and code references
accordingly.

defaultStandards.js shall contain only ART-provided default
accessibility standards and shall be treated as read-only system data.

Built-in standards shall:

Not be modified or deleted by users.\
Remain separate from user-created or imported standards.\
Continue functioning after ART updates.\
Be replaceable or updated through future ART releases without affecting
user content.

Create:

userStandards.json

as the persistent repository for all user-managed standards data.

userStandards.json shall store:

Imported standards.\
Organization-specific standards.\
User-created standards.\
User-added accessibility metadata.\
Custom fields.\
Additional categories.\
Additional tags.\
Additional disabilities.\
Additional failures.\
Additional fixes.\
Additional references.\
User modifications/enrichments to built-in standards.

User modifications to built-in standards shall store only the user-added
or changed information rather than duplicating the entire built-in
standard.

The Standards Engine shall load:

defaultStandards.js\
userStandards.json

and merge them into a unified standards collection used throughout ART.

Accessibility Standard Import

Expand standard import capabilities beyond the current JSON-only
implementation.

Support importing accessibility standards from:

JSON.\
CSV.\
Excel (.xlsx).\
URL.\
Google Sheets (when Google Workspace integration is available).\
Pasted tables.

The "Paste Table" import option shall allow users to copy and paste
tabular accessibility requirements from sources such as:

Excel.\
Google Sheets.\
Word.\
Google Docs.\
HTML tables.\
Other tabular sources.

All import methods shall use the same accessible workflow.

Unified Import Pipeline

All supported import formats shall follow the same process:

Import Source

↓

Source Parser

↓

Normalized Data

↓

Field Mapping

↓

Validation

↓

Import Preview

↓

ART Accessibility Requirement Data Model

↓

userStandards.json

↓

Standards Engine

Regardless of the original import format, ART shall convert imported
information into its internal standards data model before storage and
use.

Import Workflow

Provide an accessible import workflow that allows users to:

Select an import source.\
Map imported fields to ART fields.\
Validate required information.\
Review imported data before activation.\
Identify and edit missing optional enrichment information.\
Update existing standards.

Before completing an import, display an accessible validation summary
identifying:

Missing required fields.\
Duplicate Requirement IDs.\
Duplicate Standard Names and Versions when applicable.\
Invalid URLs.\
Unmapped fields.\
Ignored fields.\
Newly created custom fields.\
Warnings or non-blocking issues.

Users shall be able to return to previous import steps to resolve issues
before completing the import.

Field Mapping and Custom Field Configuration

During field mapping:

Present all imported source fields.\
Allow users to map each imported field to an existing ART field.\
Allow users to create custom fields for imported information that does
not match existing ART fields.\
Allow users to rename custom field display labels.\
Allow users to ignore unwanted fields.\
Preserve custom fields in userStandards.json.\
Remember previous field mappings and configurations for the same source
or standard.

For each custom field, provide accessible configuration options:

Display Label (editable text field).\
Display in Accessibility Lookup Tool (checkbox).\
Include in search indexing (checkbox).\
Generate individual Copy action (checkbox).\
Include in Copy Full Entry (checkbox).\
Display Order.

Use semantic controls appropriate for each setting.

Boolean options shall use accessible checkboxes.

Built-In ART Fields

Built-in ART fields shall remain protected and shall not be renamed
internally.

Built-in fields include:

Standard Name.\
Standard Version (when applicable).\
Requirement ID.\
Requirement Name.\
Description.\
Categories.\
Disabilities.\
Tags.\
Failures.\
Fixes.\
References.\
Accessibility Requirement Data Model

Create a flexible requirement structure supporting multiple
accessibility standards.

Required Fields\
Standard Name.\
Requirement ID.\
Requirement Name/Title.\
Description.\
Optional Fields\
Standard Version.\
Publisher/Organization.\
Release Date.\
Categories.\
Conformance Level/Rating.\
Disabilities.\
Tags.\
Failures.\
Fixes.\
Techniques.\
References.\
Additional Guidance.\
User-defined custom fields.

Standard Name shall be used throughout ART to identify installed
standards within:

Accessibility Lookup Tool.\
Project Metadata.\
Report Builder.\
Report Editor.\
Report Viewer.\
Templates.\
Export formats.\
Future integrations.

Standard Version shall be displayed wherever applicable.

Standards without formal versions shall remain fully supported.

Standards Management

Create a Standards Management interface allowing users to:

View installed accessibility standards.\
View standard metadata.\
Identify whether standards are ART-provided or user-installed.\
Enable or disable standards.\
Update existing user standards.\
Import standards.\
Export user standards.\
Duplicate standards.\
Delete user-installed standards.\
View active standards.

Built-in ART standards shall not be deletable or directly editable.

ART Accessibility Knowledge Layer

Preserve and expand ART's accessibility knowledge enhancements.

Support:

Categories.\
Disabilities.\
Tags.\
Failure examples.\
Fix recommendations.\
Techniques.\
Additional guidance.\
References.

Allow imported standards to be enriched over time without modifying
original source data.

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Rename the WCAG Lookup Tool to:

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Update the tool to support multiple installed accessibility standards.

Maintain a simple, efficient user experience.

Support accessibility for:

Screen readers.\
Screen magnifiers.\
Speech recognition/dictation.\
Keyboard navigation.

Primary search and filter controls shall remain limited to:

Search.\
Standard.\
Categories.\
Level/Rating when supported.

Avoid unnecessary filtering options that increase complexity without
improving usability.

Lookup Tool Search

Search shall include:

Requirement ID.\
Requirement Name.\
Description.\
Categories.\
Disabilities.\
Tags.\
Related keywords.\
Aliases/synonyms when provided.

Tags and aliases shall improve search relevance and discoverability.

Lookup Entry Display

Display requirements dynamically using the existing accessible heading
structure.

Each requirement shall be represented by an expandable control labeled
with:

Requirement ID.\
Requirement Name.

When expanded, display available information including:

Requirement Name.\
Description.\
Categories.\
Disabilities.\
Tags.\
Failures.\
Fixes.\
Techniques.\
References.\
User-defined custom fields configured for display.

Display only fields containing data.

Use the same formatting and styling patterns as existing WCAG Lookup
Tool entries.

References Rename

Rename the existing "Link" field throughout ART to:

References

Update:

Data fields.\
UI labels.\
Copy actions.\
Documentation.\
Related functionality.

value by migrating it into References.

Dynamic Copy Actions

Preserve existing ART copy functionality while making copy actions
data-driven.

Existing built-in actions:

Copy Full Entry.\
Copy Name.\
Copy Description.\
Copy Failures.\
Copy Fixes.\
Copy References.

Generate additional copy actions dynamically for custom fields

Examples:

Fields not configured for copying.

Copied content shall remain suitable for:

Reports.\
Issue trackers.\
Documentation.\
Email.\
External workflows.\
Integration Throughout ART

Imported and managed standards shall become available throughout ART
including:

Accessibility Lookup Tool.\
Project Metadata.\
Report Builder.\
Report Editor.\
Dashboard.\
Report Viewer.\
Templates.\
Validation.\
Import functionality.\
Export functionality.\
Future integrations.

Projects shall retain the accessibility standard used during evaluation.

Accessibility Requirements

Maintain ART's accessibility-first design.

Ensure:

Semantic HTML is used wherever possible.\
Native HTML controls are preferred over unnecessary ARIA.\
Full keyboard accessibility.\
Proper focus management.\
Logical reading order.\
Meaningful labels.\
Screen reader compatibility.\
Compatibility with user-defined keyboard shortcuts.\
High Contrast Mode support.\
Reduced Motion support.\
Correct operation at 200%, 300%, and 400% browser zoom.\
Future Considerations

Design the architecture to support:

WCAG 3.\
Additional accessibility standards.\
Organization-specific standards.\
Community-created standards packages.\
Standards sharing.\
Plugin-based standards providers.\
Future standards management enhancements.\
Success Criteria

ART shall support importing, managing, searching, displaying, and using

The Standards Engine shall provide a future-proof foundation for

## Epic 18: Google Workspace Integration

Objective

Integrate ART with Google Workspace services to support accessible
import, export, collaboration, reporting, template management, and
document workflows while maintaining ART's accessibility-first design
principles and existing functionality.

The integration shall support:

Google Drive.\
Google Docs.\
Google Sheets.

The implementation shall provide a flexible foundation for future cloud
storage and productivity platform integrations.

Google Workspace functionality shall extend existing ART workflows
rather than create separate workflows or duplicate functionality.

Google Workspace Authentication and Connection

Implement a secure Google Workspace connection workflow.

Users shall be able to:

Connect ART to their Google account.\
Authorize required Google Workspace permissions.\
Disconnect their Google account.\
View connection status.\
Reconnect when authorization expires.

Requirements:

Request only the minimum permissions required.\
Clearly communicate requested permissions.\
Provide accessible authentication workflows.\
Handle connection failures gracefully.\
Never require Google Workspace access for core ART functionality.\
Google Drive Integration

Support Google Drive integration for ART files and workflows.

Users shall be able to:

Select files for import.\
Export ART files and reports to Google Drive.\
Save templates and project files to Google Drive when supported.\
Open supported ART files from Google Drive.

Maintain:

Existing ART file handling behavior.\
Clear file type identification.\
Accessible file selection workflows.\
Google Sheets Integration

Accessibility standards.\

Project data where applicable.\
Other supported tabular data.

Validate required information.\
Review imported data.\
Activate imported content.

Export

## Epic 18 Amendment: Refine Google Workspace Integration for MVP

Objective

Refine the Google Workspace integration to provide a simple, secure,
privacy-first user experience that aligns with ART's Global Security,
Privacy, and Data Integrity Framework (Epic 19).

The Google Workspace integration shall focus on explicit, user-initiated
import and export workflows while following the principle of least
privilege.

This amendment supersedes any previous implementation requiring end
users to manually configure OAuth credentials or exposing developer
configuration within the user interface.

End User Experience

Users shall not be required to enter or configure:

OAuth Client IDs\
OAuth Client Secrets\
API keys\
Redirect URIs\
OAuth scopes\
Google Cloud project information\
Any other developer-specific authentication configuration

Instead, Application Settings shall provide an Integrations section
containing a Google Workspace connection panel.

Example:

Google Workspace

Status:\
Not Connected

Connect your Google account to import and export reports, templates, and
accessibility standards.

\[Connect Google Workspace\]

Selecting Connect Google Workspace shall initiate Google's standard
OAuth authorization flow.

After successful authorization, ART shall display:

Connected account email address.\
Connection status.\
Disconnect option.\
Developer Configuration

Any developer-specific OAuth configuration required for official ART
builds shall be removed from the normal user interface.

Developer configuration shall be isolated from user-facing settings and
documented separately for developers building custom versions of ART.

Least Privilege

Google Workspace integration shall request only the minimum OAuth
permissions required for currently implemented functionality.

Current implementation shall be designed around minimal scopes,
including:

User email address.\
Access only to files explicitly created or selected for use with ART.

Avoid requesting broader Google permissions unless a future feature
requires them.

User-Initiated Operations

All Google Workspace operations shall require explicit user initiation.

Supported MVP workflows include:

Connect Google Workspace account.\
Disconnect Google Workspace account.\
Import supported files from Google Drive.\
Export ART reports to Google Drive.\
Export Executive Summary reports.\
Export report templates.\
Import accessibility standards from supported Google Sheets.\
Export accessibility standards where supported.

ART shall not automatically synchronize, monitor, or update external
files.

Non-Destructive Operation

Google Workspace integration shall follow ART's non-destructive
philosophy.

ART shall never automatically:

Delete Google Drive files.\
Rename Google Drive files.\
Move Google Drive files.\
Modify files without explicit user action.\
Synchronize changes automatically.

All modifications to Google Workspace content shall occur only after
explicit user approval.

Remove Automatic Merge Behavior

Remove any implementation that assumes automatic synchronization or
merge operations with Google Docs or Google Sheets.

The MVP shall instead follow a simple import/edit/export workflow:

Import document or spreadsheet

↓

Edit within ART

↓

User explicitly chooses Export

↓

ART creates or updates the selected destination

Future synchronization or merge capabilities may be implemented in a
later epic.

### Privacy Mode Integration

Google Workspace shall fully respect Privacy Mode.

When Privacy Mode is enabled:

Google Workspace connections shall be disabled.\
Existing connections shall remain stored but inactive.\
No network communication shall occur until Privacy Mode is disabled and
the user initiates a new operation.\
Accessibility Requirements

All Google Workspace connection workflows shall:

Be fully keyboard accessible.\
Be screen reader compatible.\
Use semantic HTML wherever possible.\
Maintain logical focus order.\
Support High Contrast Mode.\
Support Reduced Motion preferences.\
Operate correctly at 200%, 300%, and 400% browser zoom.\
Help Documentation

Update the Help documentation to reflect the revised integration
workflow.

Documentation shall explain:

How to connect a Google account.\
How to disconnect a Google account.\
What permissions ART requests.\
Why those permissions are required.\
ART's non-destructive behavior.\
Privacy Mode interaction with Google Workspace.

Maintain existing Help formatting, terminology, accessibility, and Table
of Contents structure.

Success Criteria

The Google Workspace integration shall provide a streamlined, secure,
and accessible experience that:

Requires no developer knowledge from end users.\
Requests only the minimum Google permissions necessary.\
Follows ART's Privacy by Default and Non-Destructive principles.\
Supports explicit user-controlled import and export workflows.\
Integrates cleanly with ART's security architecture established in Epic
19.

## Epic 19: Global Security, Privacy, and Data Integrity Framework

Objective

Establish ART's global security, privacy, and data integrity framework
to ensure that all current and future features protect user data,
preserve user control, and follow secure, non-destructive operating
principles.

This framework shall guide all future development, including:

Cloud integrations.\
Issue tracker integrations.\
Desktop packaging.\
Plugin architecture.\
External services.\
Data import/export workflows.

ART shall be designed around the following guiding principles:

Accessibility First.\
Privacy by Default.\
User Control.\
Non-Destructive Operation.\
Open Development.\
Data Ownership and Integrity.\
ART Security and Privacy Standards Documentation

Create and maintain a dedicated security standards document:

docs/ART-Security-and-Privacy-Standards.md

This document shall define ART's security and privacy requirements and
serve as the source of truth for future development.

Document:

Data ownership principles.\
Privacy requirements.\
External communication rules.\
Permission requirements.\
Backup and recovery principles.\
Integration security requirements.\
Non-destructive operation requirements.\
Enterprise security considerations.\
Help Documentation Updates

Add security and privacy documentation to the ART Help system.

Create a Security and Privacy section covering:

ART's security philosophy.\
Privacy by Default.\
Non-destructive operation.\
Data ownership.\
External integrations.\
Privacy Mode.\
Backups and restore.\
Network activity indicator.\
Data transmission policies.\
What ART stores.\
What ART does not transmit.\
Enterprise security considerations.

Add the following statement to the Development Standards section of
Help:

ART is a non-destructive application. It is designed to assist users in
creating, managing, and exporting accessibility information while
preserving the integrity of user data and external files.

Maintain existing Help formatting, structure, terminology, accessibility
requirements, and Table of Contents organization.

User Data Ownership

ART shall follow a user-owned data model.

Requirements:

Users retain ownership of all data created, imported, exported, or
managed within ART.\
ART shall not claim ownership of user content.\
ART shall not transmit or share user content without explicit user
authorization.\
ART shall clearly identify all operations that involve external data
transfer.\
Explicit User Consent

ART shall never transmit, upload, synchronize, or share user data
automatically.

Before any information leaves ART, the user shall be informed of:

What information will be transmitted.\
Where the information will be sent.\
Which account/service will receive it.\
Why the transmission is occurring.\
What action will be performed.

The user must explicitly approve the operation.

Non-Destructive Operation

ART shall operate as a non-destructive application.

ART shall never automatically:

Delete external files.\
Rename external files.\
Move external files.\
Replace external files.\
Overwrite existing files without confirmation.\
Modify files the user has not explicitly selected.

This applies to:

Local storage.\
Network locations.\
Google Drive.\
Cloud storage providers.\
Future integrations.

Only ART-managed application data may be deleted.

ART-managed data includes:

Reports.\
Templates.\
Executive Summary Reports.\
User standards.\
Settings.\
Audit logs.\
Other ART-owned application data.

Deletion shall:

Require explicit confirmation.\
Clearly identify affected data.\
Never impact external files.\
Privacy Mode

Implement a user-controlled Privacy Mode.

Privacy Mode shall:

Disable external integrations.\
Disable cloud connections.\
Disable background synchronization.\
Disable automatic network communication.\
Disable telemetry if implemented.\
Disable automatic update checks if implemented.\
Disable plugin network access if implemented.

Only user-initiated operations such as imports and exports shall be
allowed.

Display Privacy Mode status clearly.

Network Activity Indicator

Add a Network Activity indicator.

Current application:

Display the indicator at the bottom of the Dashboard.

Future desktop application:

Display the indicator in the application status bar.

The indicator shall:

Clearly communicate connection status.\
Not rely on color alone.\
Provide accessible text labels.\
Be available to assistive technologies.

Example statuses:

Offline.\
Privacy Mode Enabled.\
Connected to Google Workspace.\
Connected to Jira.\
Authorization Required.\
Connection Failed.\
Integrations

Create an Integrations section within Application Settings.

Do not place connected services inside Administrator Tools.

Integrations shall support:

Google Workspace.\
Jira.\
GitHub Issues.\
Azure DevOps.\
Future integrations.

Users shall be able to:

Connect services.\
Disconnect services.\
View connection status.\
Manage authorization.

ART shall request only the minimum permissions necessary.

Administrator Tools

Create an accessible collapsed Administrator Tools region at the bottom
of Application Settings.

The region shall be:

Collapsed by default.\
Keyboard accessible.\
Screen reader accessible.\
Implemented using semantic controls where possible.

Administrator Tools shall contain:

Backup and Recovery\
Data Management\
Diagnostics\
Reset\
ART Backup and Recovery System

Implement an ART backup and recovery system.

ART backups shall include ART-managed data:

Reports.\
Executive Summary Reports.\
Templates.\
User standards.\
Settings.\
Keyboard shortcut mappings.\
Report layouts.\
Branding.\
Project metadata.\
Audit logs.\
Custom dictionaries.\
Other ART-managed data.

ART backups shall never include external files unless explicitly
imported into ART.

Backup Requirements

Support:

Automatic backups.\
Manual backups.\
Restore points.\
Full ART backups.

Users shall configure:

Backup frequency.\
Backup location.\
Backup retention.\
Included data.

Backups shall:

Never upload automatically.\
Never synchronize automatically.\
Never share automatically.\
Remain under user control.\
Restore and Recovery

Provide:

Restore Backup workflow.\
Restore point selection.\
Backup information including date, time, and project.

Restoration shall:

Require confirmation.\
Clearly identify affected ART data.\
Preserve user control.\
Secure External Integrations

All integrations shall follow:

Least privilege.\
Explicit authorization.\
User-controlled data transfer.\
Non-destructive operation.

ART shall not:

Access unrelated user files.\
Delete external content.\
Modify unauthorized content.\
Share data with third parties without permission.\
Data Security Requirements

ART shall:

Protect authentication credentials.\
Never store secrets in plain text.\
Avoid unnecessary data collection.\
Avoid unnecessary network communication.\
Maintain secure handling of tokens and credentials.\
Preserve data integrity.

Security-sensitive actions should be recorded in the ART Audit Log,
including:

External connections.\
Imports.\
Exports.\
Merge operations.

Logs shall never contain passwords, tokens, or secrets.

Accessibility of Security Features

All security and privacy features shall meet ART accessibility
requirements.

Ensure:

Semantic HTML.\
Native controls where possible.\
Keyboard accessibility.\
Screen reader compatibility.\
Proper focus management.\
Logical reading order.\
High Contrast Mode support.\
Reduced Motion support.\
Correct operation at 200%, 300%, and 400% zoom.\
Keyboard Shortcut and Help Requirements

Follow ART Feature Completion Requirements.

For all new security, backup, integration, and administrative controls:

Review shortcut eligibility.\
Add shortcuts where appropriate.\
Register shortcuts in Keyboard Shortcut Manager.\
Update Welcome shortcut display.\
Update Help documentation.\
Update Help Table of Contents.\
Update accessible tooltips.\
Success Criteria

ART shall provide a secure, privacy-focused, non-destructive
architecture that protects user data, provides transparent control over
external communication, supports enterprise confidence, and establishes
a foundation for future integrations and desktop deployment.

ART shall preserve the integrity of user data while enabling users to
securely manage, export, back up, and collaborate on accessibility
information.

Permission Request and Incremental Authorization\
User Permission Transparency

Before redirecting users to any third-party authentication or
authorization provider, ART shall clearly explain:

Which service the user is connecting.\
Why the connection is needed.\
What permissions ART is requesting.\
How those permissions will be used.\
That users remain in control of granting or denying access.

Permission explanations shall:

Use clear, non-technical language.\
Avoid unnecessary jargon.\
Be concise while providing sufficient information for informed consent.\
Follow ART's accessibility-first design principles.\
Incremental Authorization

ART shall follow the Principle of Least Privilege.

External integrations shall request only the minimum permissions
necessary for the user's current action.

Permissions shall be requested incrementally as additional functionality
is used.

Examples:

Initial Google Workspace Connection

The initial connection shall request only the permissions necessary to
establish the connection and perform basic ART-managed file operations.

Additional permissions shall not be requested until required.

Examples include:

Importing accessibility standards from Google Sheets.\
Exporting reports to Google Docs.\
Future Google Workspace features.

Users shall never be prompted to approve permissions for features they
have not chosen to use.

Permission Explanation Dialog

Before redirecting users to a third-party authorization page, ART shall
present an accessible confirmation dialog explaining the requested
permissions.

Example: Connect Google Workspace

ART is requesting permission to:

Connect to your Google account.\
Create and update Google Drive files that you create or select using
ART.\
Access Google Sheets only when you choose to import spreadsheet data.\
Access Google Docs only when you choose to export reports to Google
Docs.

ART will not:

Access files you have not selected or chosen to use with ART.\
Delete files from your Google Drive.\
Modify files outside of the operations you explicitly initiate.\
Share your data with third parties.\
Transmit your information without your explicit permission.

All changes made to Google Workspace files shall result only from
actions that you intentionally initiate within ART.

Users shall be able to:

Continue to the provider's authorization page.\
Cancel the connection.\
Learn more about ART's Security and Privacy Policy.\
Connection Status and Management

ART shall clearly display the current connection status for each
supported third-party integration.

For connected services, ART shall display:

The connected account's email address or user identifier (when
permission has been granted to retrieve it).\
The current connection status.\
The date and time the connection was last successfully authenticated or
refreshed, when available.\
The permissions currently granted to ART.\
Whether additional permissions may be requested when new functionality
is used.

Users shall be able to:

Connect a service.\
Disconnect a service at any time.\
Reconnect a service.\
Review the permissions currently granted.\
Reauthorize the connection if permissions have expired or changed.

When no account is connected, ART shall clearly indicate that no
connection exists and shall provide an accessible Connect action.

Disconnecting a service shall:

Revoke ART's ability to access the service until the user reconnects.\
Preserve locally stored ART-managed data unless the user explicitly
chooses to remove it.\
Never delete or modify data stored within the third-party service.\
Integration Consistency

All current and future third-party integrations shall follow this
permission model, including but not limited to:

Google Workspace\
Jira\
GitHub Issues\
Azure DevOps\
Microsoft 365\
Future supported integrations

Each integration shall:

Request permissions incrementally.\
Clearly explain each requested permission.\
Request only the minimum permissions necessary for the user's selected
action.\
Allow users to revoke or disconnect the integration at any time.\
Accessibility Requirements

Permission dialogs and integration management interfaces shall:

Be fully keyboard accessible.\
Support screen readers.\
Use semantic HTML wherever possible.\
Maintain logical focus order.\
Clearly identify the purpose of each permission request and control.\
Provide accessible status messages for successful connections,
disconnections, permission changes, and authentication errors.\
Avoid relying solely on the third-party provider's authorization screen
to explain requested permissions.

## Epic 20: ART Project File Format, Persistence, and Portability

Objective

Create a portable, standards-based ART project file system that allows
users to save, recover, share, archive, and continue editing
accessibility projects outside of ART-managed local storage.

ART shall introduce an open, human-readable project format that
preserves user ownership, portability, transparency, and long-term
compatibility while maintaining ART's accessibility-first design
principles.

The project persistence system shall allow users to:

Save projects as portable ART files.\
Reopen previously saved projects.\
Recover work after unexpected interruptions.\
Export reports in industry-standard formats.\
Share editable ART projects with other ART users.\
Preserve project metadata, standards references, report configurations,
templates, branding, and accessibility findings.\
ART Project File Format\
.art Project Files

ART shall introduce the .art file extension as the official editable ART
project format.

.art files shall represent complete ART projects and contain the
information necessary to continue editing a project.

A .art project may include:

Project metadata.\
Report information.\
Accessibility findings.\
Audit logs.\
Executive Summary data.\
Selected accessibility standards and versions.\
Report layouts.\
Report configuration settings.\
Branding information.\
Templates used.\
References.\
Supporting project information.\
Other ART-managed project data.\
Open Format Requirements

.art files shall:

Use an open, human-readable data format.\
Be based on JSON.\
Avoid proprietary binary storage formats.\
Avoid encryption or unnecessary obfuscation.\
Remain inspectable by advanced users.\
Support future migration and compatibility improvements.

ART shall prioritize transparency and avoid unnecessary vendor lock-in.

ART Project Schema

ART shall define and maintain an official project schema.

The schema shall:

Define the structure of .art files.\
Identify required and optional fields.\
Support validation.\
Support future version migration.\
Be maintained independently from application code.

The schema shall be published within the repository.

Example:

art-project.schema.json

Documentation shall explain the schema structure and organization of
.art files.

Project Metadata and Versioning

Each .art file shall contain metadata identifying:

ART format version.\
Schema version.\
ART application version used to create the file.\
ART application version used for the last save.\
Creation date.\
Last modification date.

Example:

{\
"formatVersion": "1.0",\
"schemaVersion": "1.0",\
"createdWith": "ART 1.0",\
"lastSavedWith": "ART 1.0"\
}

This information shall support:

Troubleshooting.\
Compatibility checks.\
Future migration.\
User support.\
ART Template Format\
.artx Template Files

ART shall introduce .artx as the official ART template file format.

The .artx extension shall be used instead of .artt to improve
accessibility and distinguishability for screen reader users.

ART templates may include:

Report layouts.\
Branding.\
Metadata defaults.\
Accessibility standard selections.\
Report configuration defaults.\
Template-specific settings.

Opening an .artx file shall allow users to create a new ART project
based on the template.

Project Persistence Model

ART shall use a dual persistence model.

ART Local Storage

ART shall continue using local storage as an automatic recovery
mechanism.

Local storage shall:

Preserve active user work automatically.\
Protect against unexpected interruptions.\
Recover unsaved work after:\
Browser crashes.\
Device shutdown.\
Application failures.\
Unexpected interruptions.

Local storage shall not replace user-controlled saving.

User-Controlled .art Files

Users shall be able to save .art files anywhere they choose.

Users shall be able to:

Save projects locally.\
Back up projects.\
Move projects between systems.\
Share projects.\
Reopen projects later.

ART shall never require users to store .art files only within
ART-managed storage.

Save Workflow\
Save Command

Default keyboard shortcut:

Ctrl+S

The Save command shall behave as follows:

Existing .art Project

If the project already has an associated .art file:

Save changes to that file.\
Update local recovery storage.\
Preserve schema information.\
New Project

If the project has never been saved as an .art file:

Activating Save or pressing Ctrl+S shall open the Save As dialog.\
The user shall select the filename and location.\
The project shall be saved as an .art file.\
Save As

Default keyboard shortcut:

Ctrl+Shift+S

Save As shall:

Use the operating system's standard accessible save dialog when
available.\
Allow users to choose the destination.\
Allow users to choose the filename.\
Apply the .art extension automatically.\
Save the complete ART project structure.

After Save As:

The new file becomes the active project.\
Future Save actions update that file.\
Local recovery continues.\
Open ART Projects

Default keyboard shortcut:

Ctrl+O

The Open command shall:

Open .art project files.\
Use the operating system's standard accessible file selection dialog
when available.\

## Epic 21: Accessibility Evaluation Progress Tracker and Audit Workflow Management

Overview

ART shall provide an Accessibility Evaluation Progress Tracker to
support the planning, execution, and management of accessibility
evaluations.

The Progress Log shall allow users to define evaluation targets, monitor
testing progress, maintain internal audit workflow information, and
improve efficiency when creating accessibility reports.

The Progress Log shall enhance ART's audit workflow capabilities while
maintaining separation between internal evaluation management
information and report content.

The Progress Log is an optional feature. Users shall not be required to
use the Progress Log to create Audit Logs or accessibility reports.

Accessibility Evaluation Progress Log

ART shall provide an Accessibility Evaluation Progress Log for managing
accessibility evaluation activities.

The Progress Log shall allow users to define evaluation targets,
including:

Web pages.\
Application screens.\
User flows.\
Components.\
Documents.\
Other accessibility evaluation targets.

Each Progress Log entry shall support the following fields:

Field Description\
Evaluation Item Name Name of the page, screen, component, flow,
document, or evaluation target\
Type Page, Screen, Component, Flow, Document, or user-defined type\
URL/Location Optional URL, file location, application location, or
reference location\
Status Current evaluation state\
Notes Additional evaluator information\
Findings Count Number of linked findings, when applicable\
Assigned Tester Optional evaluator assignment\
Date Started Automatically recorded when evaluation begins\
Date Completed Automatically recorded when evaluation is completed

Internally, ART shall refer to Progress Log entries as Evaluation Items
because evaluations may include more than pages.

Evaluation Status Values

The Progress Log shall support the following statuses:

Not Started\
In Progress\
On Hold\
Blocked\
Needs Review\
Retest Required\
Not Applicable\
Complete\
Status Definitions\
Not Started

The evaluation target has been created but testing has not begun.

In Progress

Testing is actively occurring.

On Hold

Testing has temporarily stopped due to an external dependency, decision,
or other reason.

Examples:

Waiting for developer response.\
Environment unavailable.\
Requirement clarification needed.\
Access credentials unavailable.\
Blocked

Testing cannot continue until a blocking issue has been resolved.

Examples:

Missing access.\
Missing required information.\
Unavailable environment.\
Needs Review

Testing has been completed but requires review or confirmation.

Retest Required

Previously completed testing requires additional evaluation.

Not Applicable

The evaluation target does not apply to the current audit scope.

Complete

Testing has been completed.

The Progress Log data model shall support future additional statuses.

Progress Log Notes

Each Progress Log entry shall provide a multiline Notes field.

Notes may contain:

Testing observations.\
Evaluation notes.\
Blockers.\
Follow-up actions.\
Environment details.\
Testing credential references.\
Instructions for accessing protected areas.

Users should avoid storing sensitive passwords, secrets, or
authentication tokens directly within ART notes unless they explicitly
accept the associated security implications.

Notes shall:

Be preserved when saving ART files.\
Be included in ART backups.\
Maintain accessibility requirements.\
URL/Location Support

Each Progress Log entry shall support an optional URL/Location field.

When a valid URL is provided:

The Evaluation Item Name shall become a hyperlink.\
The provided URL shall become the hyperlink destination.\
The hyperlink shall open in a new browser tab/window using
target="\_blank".\
The behavior shall be communicated accessibly.

Example:

Homepage

becomes:

Homepage (opens in new tab)

The hyperlink shall:

Preserve meaningful link text.\
Avoid requiring users to read raw URLs.\
Follow ART accessibility standards.\
Progress Log User Interface

The Progress Log shall be displayed as an accessible table inside an
accessible modal dialog.

The modal shall include:

A descriptive accessible name.\
A Close button.\
Escape key functionality.\
Proper focus management.

When opened:

Focus shall move into the Progress Log modal.\
Users shall be informed that the Progress Log is available.

When closed:

Focus shall return to the control that opened the Progress Log.\
All data and selections shall be preserved.\
The Progress Log shall be ready for later reopening.

The Progress Log shall remain accessible from:

The Editor.\
The Viewer.

Users shall have:

An accessible on-screen mechanism to open the Progress Log.\
A keyboard shortcut to open the Progress Log.

The keyboard shortcut shall:

Be configurable through ART keyboard shortcut settings.\
Appear in keyboard shortcut documentation.\
Follow ART shortcut conflict rules.\
Progress Log Edit Mode

Once created, static Progress Log information shall be protected from
accidental modification.

By default:

Evaluation Item Name shall be static text.\
Type shall be static text.\
URL/Location shall be static text.\
Notes shall be static text.\
Assigned Tester information shall be static text.

Status selection controls shall remain available for updating.

Enable Edit Mode

Users may activate an Edit Mode option to modify static Progress Log
information.

When Edit Mode is enabled:

Static fields become editable.\
Status controls shall become unavailable.\
ART shall announce that Edit Mode is active.

Example announcement:

"Edit mode enabled. Evaluation item information can now be modified."

Done Editing

When the user activates Done Editing:

Changes shall be saved.\
Static fields shall return to their protected state.\
Status controls shall become available again.\
Focus shall return to the Progress Log.\
ART shall announce:

"Editing complete. Evaluation statuses are available."

User Choice and Workflow Flexibility

The Progress Log shall remain optional.

Users may:

Use the Progress Log to manage evaluation scope and progress.\
Manually enter page/screen/component names directly into Audit Log
fields.\
Use both workflows simultaneously.

ART shall never require users to use the Progress Log.

Report Builder Integration\
Audit Log Report Type Integration

When the Report Builder report type is set to:

Audit Log

ART shall display an:

Enable Progress Log

checkbox.

Requirements:

The checkbox shall be checked by default.\
Users may disable the Progress Log.\
The setting shall be stored with the report configuration.\
Progress Log Configuration Region

When Enable Progress Log is checked:

ART shall display a:

Progress Log Configuration

region.

The region shall appear:

After the Configure Fields region.\
Before the Done button.

The configuration interface shall follow existing ART Builder patterns:

Accessible headings.\
Keyboard accessibility.\
Existing styling conventions.\
Enabling Progress Log After Report Creation

The Enable Progress Log option shall remain available for Audit Log
reports regardless of report state.

Users may enable Progress Log when:

Creating a report.\
Opening a report.\
Importing a report.\
Continuing work in the Editor.

Enabling Progress Log shall:

Preserve existing report data.\
Preserve existing Audit Log entries.\
Preserve existing fields.\
Never require report recreation.\
Never delete or modify existing data.\
Progress Log and Audit Log Separation

Progress Log data shall remain separate from Audit Log content.

The following Progress Log information shall not automatically appear in
the Audit Log:

URL/Location.\
Notes.\
Testing instructions.\
Assigned Tester.\
Status.\
Dates.\
Internal workflow information.

The Progress Log shall only provide Evaluation Item names as optional
data sources for specialized Editor components.

Evaluation Item Selection Box Integration

ART shall provide support for a specially formatted Audit Log Editor
component:

Evaluation Item Selection Box

When inserted into an Audit Log template, the component shall populate
available selections from the current Progress Log.

Example:

Progress Log:

Homepage\
Login Screen\
Navigation Menu

Audit Log Editor:

Page/Screen/Component:\
\[Homepage ▼\]

The component shall:

Reduce duplicate data entry.\
Preserve user choice.\
Remain optional.\
Not expose Progress Log metadata.

URL, notes, status, and other Progress Log metadata shall remain
available only within the Progress Log.

Progress Log Appendix Generation

When Progress Log is enabled, ART shall include Progress Log reference
information as an Appendix in saved and exported Audit Reports.

The Appendix may include:

Evaluation Item Name.\
URL/Location information.\
Links.\
Testing instructions.\
Other user-designated appendix information.

The Appendix shall:

Appear after the primary audit report content.\
Remain separate from Audit Log findings.\
Preserve the separation between workflow management and report content.\
Appendix Visibility Configuration

ART shall provide configuration options for controlling Progress Log
Appendix inclusion.

Options shall include:

Include Progress Log Appendix.\
Exclude Progress Log Appendix.

Default behavior:

Include Progress Log Appendix when Progress Log is enabled.

The setting shall:

Persist with the report configuration.\
Apply to saved and exported reports.\
Support future extension.

Future options may include:

Include all Progress Log information.\
Include only completed evaluation items.\
Include selected evaluation items.\
Exclude internal evaluation information.\
Appendix Viewing Rules

Within ART:

Appendix information shall be viewable in the Report Viewer.\
Appendix information shall not appear during normal Editor workflows.\
Editor users shall have an accessible option to open the Report Viewer
and review Appendix information.

Exported reports:

Appendix content shall appear after audit report content.\
Appendix shall use a semantic heading.\
Export formats shall preserve accessibility structure.

Examples:

HTML semantic headings.\
Word heading styles.\
Tagged PDF headings where supported.\
Clearly identified spreadsheet sections.\
Progress Status Privacy

Progress Log Status values shall remain internal to ART.

Status values shall not appear in:

Report Viewer audit report content.\
Exported reports.\
Saved presentation formats.

Status shall only be viewed and modified within the Progress Log.

Dashboard Progress Metrics Integration

When an Audit Log report has an associated Progress Log, ART shall
display additional metrics in the Dashboard Report Metrics area.

Progress metrics shall:

Be dynamically calculated from the Progress Log.\
Update automatically when Progress Log data changes.\
Use the Progress Log as the source of truth.

Progress metrics shall not generate ARIA live announcements during
routine updates.

Progress Metric Placement and Separation

Progress Log metrics shall supplement, not replace, modify, or overwrite
existing ART Dashboard metrics.

Requirements:

Default ART Dashboard metrics shall always remain visible if ART metrics
exist.\
If ART metrics exist, Progress Log metrics shall appear beneath the
existing ART Dashboard metrics.\
If no ART metrics exist, ART shall maintain existing behavior and
display:

"There are no open reports to show metrics for."

Progress Log metrics shall not alter:

Existing metric labels.\
Existing calculations.\
Existing ordering.\
Existing Dashboard behavior.\
Required Progress Metrics

When a Progress Log exists, ART shall display:

Total Evaluation Items

Example:

Total Evaluation Items: 120

Completed

Example:

Completed: 65

Testing Completion

Example:

Testing Completion: 54% (65/120)

Calculation:

Completed Items ÷ Total Evaluation Items × 100

Conditional Status Metrics

Status-specific metrics shall only appear when their value is greater
than zero.

ART shall display:

In Progress.\
On Hold.\
Blocked.\
Needs Review.\
Retest Required.\
Not Applicable.

Zero-value metrics shall be hidden.

Example:

Display:

Total Evaluation Items: 120

Completed: 65

Testing Completion: 54% (65/120)

In Progress: 18

Do not display:

On Hold: 0

Blocked: 0

Needs Review: 0

Dashboard Accessibility

Progress metrics shall:

Use semantic structure.\
Maintain logical reading order.\
Be keyboard accessible.\
Follow existing ART Dashboard patterns.

Routine metric changes shall not trigger ARIA live announcements.

Future Extensibility

The Progress Log architecture should support future capabilities,
including:

Importing evaluation plans from CSV/Excel/Google Sheets.\
Exporting progress summaries.\
Multi-user assignments.\
Audit timelines.\
Review workflows.\
Project management integrations.\
Enterprise audit history features.

## Git Source Control – Create ART Version 1.0 Release Branch and Begin Version 2.0 Development

Objective

The implementation of ART Version 1.0 has been completed, validated,
committed, and pushed to the main branch.

The purpose of this task is to preserve the completed Version 1.0
release by creating a permanent release branch while leaving the main
branch available for continued development of ART Version 2.0.

This task performs Git source control operations only.

Do not modify any application source code, documentation, configuration
files, project files, assets, or dependencies.

Current State

Push the current ART-1.0 release to the main branch.\
The current main branch now contains the completed ART Version 1.0
release.

All Version 1.0 work has already been:

Implemented\
Validated\
Committed\
Pushed to GitHub

No application changes are required.

Required Tasks

1.  Verify Repository Status

Verify that:

The working tree is clean.\
There are no uncommitted changes.\
There are no staged files awaiting commit.

If uncommitted changes exist, stop and report them.

Do not continue until the repository is clean.

2.  Verify Current Branch

Verify that the current branch is:

main

If the current branch is not main, stop and report the current branch.

3.  Synchronize with Remote

Fetch the latest changes from the remote repository.

Verify that the local main branch is synchronized with the remote main
branch.

Do not modify history.

Do not rebase.

Do not perform a force push.

4.  Create the ART 1.0 Release Branch

Create a new branch named:

art-1.0

The new branch shall point to the current commit on main.

Do not clone the repository.

Do not duplicate files.

Create a normal Git branch.

5.  Push the Release Branch

Push the new branch to the remote repository.

Configure the upstream tracking branch.

Verify that the remote branch:

art-1.0

has been created successfully.

6.  Create the Version 1.0 Release Tag

Create an annotated Git tag named:

v1.0.0

Use the tag message:

ART Version 1.0 Release

Verify that the tag references the current Version 1.0 release commit.

Push the tag to the remote repository.

Do not modify any commits.

7.  Return to Main

After the release branch and tag have been created successfully:

Switch back to:

main

Verify that the current branch is once again:

main

No additional branches shall remain checked out.

8.  Prepare Main for ART Version 2.0

Do not implement any Version 2.0 features.

Do not create any commits.

Do not modify any files.

Leave the repository on the main branch so that development of ART
Version 2.0 can begin with the next implementation epic.

Validation

Verify that:

The repository remains clean.\
No application files were modified.\
The new branch art-1.0 exists locally.\
The new branch art-1.0 exists remotely.\
The annotated tag v1.0.0 exists locally.\
The annotated tag v1.0.0 exists remotely.\
Both the art-1.0 branch and the v1.0.0 tag reference the same commit as
the completed Version 1.0 release.\
The current checked-out branch is main.\
No merge commits were created.\
No force pushes were performed.\
No Git history was rewritten.\
Reporting

After all tasks have completed successfully, report:

The current branch name.\
The name of the newly created release branch.\
Confirmation that the remote release branch was created successfully.\
The Git tag name.\
The commit hash referenced by the release branch.\
The commit hash referenced by the tag.\
Confirmation that both references point to the same Version 1.0 release
commit.\
Confirmation that the repository has been returned to the main branch.\
Confirmation that main is now ready for ART Version 2.0 development.

Do not make any application code changes as part of this task.

## Epic 23 — Application Command Framework

Version: ART 2.0

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Read Epic-23-Application-Command-Framework.md completely. Analyze the
current codebase and produce an implementation plan that maps each
implementation phase to the files that will be created or modified,
identifies existing features that can be reused, highlights any
architectural risks, and estimates the scope of each phase. Do not
modify any code yet.

### Implementation Strategy

Read Epic-23-Application-Command-Framework.md completely. Analyze the
current codebase and produce an implementation plan that maps each
implementation phase to the files that will be created or modified,
identifies existing features that can be reused, highlights any
architectural risks, and estimates the scope of each phase. Do not
modify any code yet.

### Overview

This epic establishes the architectural foundation for ART Version 2.0.

Unlike previous implementation epics, this epic is primarily an
architectural\
refactoring effort rather than the implementation of new end-user
features.

The objective is to introduce a centralized Application Command
Framework while\
preserving the complete functionality, accessibility, and user
experience\
established in ART Version 1.0.

Existing business logic shall be reused whenever practical.

Existing application features shall continue to function exactly as they
do\
today unless explicitly modified by this specification.

The implementation shall prioritize stability, maintainability, and
incremental\
progress over large-scale rewrites.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement this epic incrementally.

Do not rewrite mature application features unless required to integrate
them\
with the Command Framework.

Do not redesign the user interface.

Do not remove existing functionality.

Do not introduce unnecessary architectural changes outside the scope of
this\
epic.

The objective is to centralize execution while preserving existing
behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Existing Functionality Preservation

The following application areas already exist and shall be preserved.

Dashboard

Report Builder

Report Viewer

Progress Log

Executive Summary

Usability Report

Application Settings

Help Documentation

User Guide

README

Existing Accessibility Features

Existing Keyboard Shortcuts

Existing Screen Reader Support

Existing Focus Management

Existing Modal Dialog Behavior

Existing Validation Logic

Existing business logic shall be integrated into the Command Framework
rather\
than rewritten whenever practical.

### Implementation Success Criteria

This epic shall be considered complete only when:
