## Epic 25 – Visual Accessibility & Personalization

### Part 1 – Overview, Objectives & Implementation Strategy

### Overview

This epic introduces comprehensive Visual Accessibility and
Personalization\
features for ART Version 2.0.

The objective is to allow every user to customize the visual
presentation of\
ART according to their individual accessibility preferences while
preserving\
ART's keyboard-first and screen reader-first design philosophy.

Visual accessibility settings shall apply consistently throughout the
entire\
application.

The implementation shall establish a centralized Theme and
Personalization\
Engine that serves as the single authoritative source for all visual\
accessibility settings.

Future user interface components shall automatically inherit these
settings\
without requiring feature-specific implementation wherever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Objective

Implement a centralized Visual Accessibility and Personalization system
that:

- Improves usability for users with low vision and other visual
  accessibility\
  needs.

- Provides consistent appearance throughout the application.

- Supports both keyboard users and screen reader users.

- Allows users to immediately preview accessibility settings before
  saving.

- Automatically applies user preferences throughout ART.

- Establishes a scalable architecture for future personalization
  features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Relationship to Previous Epics

Epic 23 introduced the centralized Application Command Framework.

Epic 24 introduced the Command Palette.

Epic 25 shall build upon those architectural foundations.

The Visual Accessibility and Personalization system shall integrate
with\
existing ART functionality without modifying business logic.

Visual settings shall affect presentation only.

No report content or user data shall be modified by this epic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Preserve all existing application functionality.

Preserve all existing report workflows.

Preserve all existing keyboard accessibility.

Preserve all existing screen reader accessibility.

Do not redesign unrelated user interface components.

Do not duplicate existing configuration management logic.

Reuse the existing Application Settings infrastructure wherever
practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Centralized Theme & Personalization Engine

Implement a centralized Theme and Personalization Engine.

The Theme Engine shall become the single authoritative source for all
visual\
accessibility settings.

All user interface components shall obtain appearance settings from the
Theme\
Engine.

Individual components shall not maintain their own appearance settings.

The Theme Engine shall support future expansion without requiring
redesign of\
existing user interface components.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Global Application Settings

Visual accessibility settings shall be global application settings.

Settings shall automatically apply throughout the application.

This includes existing and future functionality.

Wherever practical, newly implemented user interface components shall
inherit\
the currently selected visual accessibility settings automatically.

Feature-specific implementation shall only be required when technically\
necessary.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Scope

This epic includes:

Theme Engine

Application appearance settings

Zoom

Font size

High contrast themes

System theme support

Enhanced focus indicators

Reduced motion

Live Preview

Application Settings integration

Documentation updates

Validation

Regression testing

Source control

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Out of Scope

This epic does not include:

Menu Bar implementation

Dashboard redesign

Project Management

Desktop application implementation

Plug-in system

Jira integration

Custom user-created themes

Color-blind simulation

Magnification tools

These features may build upon the Theme Engine introduced by this epic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Existing Functionality Preservation

The implementation shall not modify:

Dashboard functionality

Report Builder

Report Viewer

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Template Management

Import

Export

Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Command Framework

Command Palette functionality

Report Validation

Help

User Guide

Application Settings functionality unrelated to visual accessibility

Existing report data

Existing project data

Existing templates

Existing accessibility features unrelated to appearance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Application-Wide Integration

Visual accessibility settings shall automatically apply to:

Dashboard

Welcome screen

Report Builder

Report Viewer

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Application Settings

Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Command Palette

Future Menu Bar

Future Project Management features

Dialogs

Modal windows

Confirmation dialogs

Validation dialogs

Tooltips

Accessible tooltips

Status messages

Notifications

Tables

Forms

Buttons

Menus

Future desktop user interface components

Future plug-ins

Future Jira integration

Any future user interface component introduced into ART.

Application developers shall not be required to implement visual
accessibility\
settings independently for each new feature wherever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The Theme Engine shall be designed to support future enhancements
including:

Additional themes

Custom themes

Organization themes

User-defined color palettes

Desktop-specific appearance settings

Plug-in appearance extensions

Additional accessibility options

Future visual accessibility technologies

The implementation shall prioritize extensibility while maintaining
simplicity\
for Version 2.0.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Implementation Strategy

Implement this epic incrementally.

Proceed to the next implementation phase only after successfully
completing the\
current phase.

#### Phase 1

Implement the centralized Theme Engine.

Integrate the Theme Engine with the existing Application Settings\
infrastructure.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 2

Implement the initial visual accessibility settings.

Apply settings throughout the application.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 3

Implement Live Preview.

Verify settings update dynamically.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 4

Apply the Theme Engine consistently to all existing application
components.

Verify that the Command Palette automatically inherits visual
accessibility\
settings without requiring feature-specific implementation.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 5

Update documentation.

Update:

README.md

ARCHITECTURE.md

CHANGELOG.md

User Guide

Help documentation

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 6

Perform validation.

Run regression testing.

Resolve all identified issues.

Proceed to Source Control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Success Criteria

This epic shall be considered complete only when:

The centralized Theme Engine has been implemented.

Visual accessibility settings are applied consistently throughout ART.

The Command Palette automatically inherits all visual accessibility
settings.

Existing application functionality remains unchanged.

Accessibility has been preserved or improved.

The application builds successfully.

Documentation has been updated.

The implementation is ready for Epic 26 – Menu Bar.

### Part 2 – Visual Accessibility Features & Personalization Options

### Overview

The Theme and Personalization Engine shall provide a centralized
collection of\
visual accessibility settings that improve usability while maintaining
a\
consistent appearance throughout ART.

All settings shall be configurable from the existing Application
Settings\
dialog.

Unless otherwise specified, changes shall affect the entire application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Theme Selection

Implement the following built-in application themes.

Light Theme (Default)

Dark Theme

High Contrast Light

High Contrast Dark

Follow System Theme

When Follow System Theme is selected, ART shall automatically adopt the\
operating system's preferred light or dark appearance whenever
practical.

Future themes shall be able to register with the Theme Engine without
requiring\
modifications to existing application components.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Application Zoom

Provide an application-wide zoom setting.

The zoom setting shall enlarge or reduce the user interface without
affecting\
application functionality.

Zoom shall apply consistently throughout the application.

Zoom shall affect:

Dashboard

Welcome Screen

Report Builder

Report Viewer

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Application Settings

Command Palette

Future Menu Bar

Dialogs

Tables

Forms

Buttons

Tooltips

Status messages

Notifications

Future user interface components

The zoom setting shall not alter report content or exported documents.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### User Interface Font Size

Provide an independent user interface font size setting.

Font size shall affect only the application's user interface.

Report content shall not be modified.

Font size changes shall apply consistently throughout the application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Enhanced Focus Indicators

Provide an option to enable enhanced keyboard focus indicators.

When enabled:

Focus indicators shall become more visually prominent.

Focus indicators shall satisfy applicable WCAG 2.2 Level AA
requirements.

Focus indicators shall remain visible regardless of the selected theme.

Future components shall automatically inherit enhanced focus indicators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Reduced Motion

Provide an option to reduce non-essential animations.

When enabled:

Visual transitions shall be minimized.

Animation timing shall be reduced where practical.

Functionality shall remain unchanged.

Future animations shall respect this setting automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### User Interface Density

Provide an option to control interface density.

Supported options shall include:

Standard

Comfortable

Compact

Density settings shall adjust spacing between user interface elements
without\
changing functionality.

Future components shall inherit the selected density automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Border Visibility

Provide an option to enhance visual separation of interface components.

When enabled:

Borders surrounding controls and content regions shall become more
visually\
distinct.

Tables shall remain clearly delineated.

Dialogs shall remain visually identifiable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Color Independence

Visual customization shall never become the sole means of conveying\
information.

Changing themes or colors shall not remove visible status indicators.

Application functionality shall remain understandable regardless of the\
selected theme.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Live Preview

All visual accessibility settings shall support Live Preview.

As settings are modified:

The application shall immediately reflect the pending changes.

Users shall be able to evaluate appearance before saving.

If the user selects Cancel:

All previewed changes shall be discarded.

The previous settings shall be restored.

If the user selects Apply or OK:

The new settings shall become the active application settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Preview Panel

Add an Accessibility Preview Panel to the Application Settings dialog.

The preview panel shall contain representative user interface
components.

Examples include:

Headings

Paragraph text

Buttons

Links

Checkboxes

Radio buttons

Textboxes

Dropdown lists

Tables

Dialogs

Status messages

Tooltips

Keyboard focus indicators

The preview panel shall immediately reflect changes made during Live
Preview.

The preview panel shall not modify application data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Persistence

Visual accessibility settings shall be saved as part of the existing\
application settings.

Settings shall automatically be restored whenever ART is reopened.

Settings shall remain independent of reports, templates, and future
projects.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Theme Engine Integration

All visual accessibility settings shall be provided through the
centralized\
Theme Engine.

Individual components shall not implement independent appearance
settings.

New components introduced in future epics shall automatically inherit
the\
currently active visual accessibility settings without requiring
feature-\
specific implementation wherever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Command Palette Integration

The Command Palette implemented in Epic 24 shall automatically inherit
all\
visual accessibility settings.

This includes:

Theme

Zoom

Font size

Enhanced focus indicators

Reduced motion

Interface density

Border visibility

Future visual accessibility settings

No Command Palette-specific implementation shall be required unless\
technically necessary.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Extensibility

The Theme Engine architecture shall support future additions including:

Custom user-created themes

Organization-specific themes

Custom color palettes

Additional high contrast themes

Additional accessibility preferences

Desktop-specific appearance options

Plug-in supplied themes

Future personalization features

Version 2.0 shall implement only the functionality described within this
epic.

The architecture shall ensure that future visual accessibility
enhancements may\
be added without redesigning the existing Theme Engine.\

But architect it so a future version could support:

### Live Preview

The Theme Engine shall support Live Preview.

As users modify settings:

The application shall immediately reflect pending changes.

No application restart shall be required.

Users shall be able to continue evaluating settings until they choose
one of\
the following actions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Apply

Selecting Apply shall:

Save the current settings.

Continue displaying the Application Settings dialog.

Leave Live Preview enabled.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### OK

Selecting OK shall:

Save the current settings.

Close the Application Settings dialog.

Retain all selected appearance settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Cancel

Selecting Cancel shall:

Discard all unsaved appearance changes.

Restore the appearance that existed when the dialog was opened.

Close the Application Settings dialog.

No partial changes shall remain.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Restore Defaults

Provide a Restore Defaults button.

Selecting Restore Defaults shall restore the default visual
accessibility\
configuration.

The restored configuration shall immediately appear in Live Preview.

Users shall still be able to select Cancel to abandon the restored
defaults.

Defaults shall not be permanently saved until Apply or OK is selected.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Theme Propagation

Whenever visual accessibility settings change:

The Theme Engine shall notify all registered application components.

Application components shall immediately update their appearance.

Components shall not require individual refresh logic wherever
practical.

Appearance changes shall remain centralized.

## Epic 26 – Menu Bar & Command Search

### Part 1 – Overview, Objectives & Implementation Strategy

### Overview

This epic introduces a fully accessible, keyboard-first Menu Bar and\
application-wide Command Search for ART Version 2.0.

The Menu Bar shall provide a familiar desktop-style application menu
structure\
while building upon the centralized Application Command Framework
implemented\
in Epic 23, the Command Palette implemented in Epic 24, and the Theme &\
Personalization Engine implemented in Epic 25.

The Menu Bar shall not introduce duplicate command implementations.

Instead, it shall present commands already registered within the
centralized\
Application Command Registry and execute them through the centralized
Command\
Execution Service.

This epic also introduces a Menu Bar Command Search inspired by the
Microsoft\
Office "Tell Me" experience.

The Command Search shall provide rapid access to application commands
from\
anywhere within ART without requiring users to navigate menus.

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall become additional user interfaces
for\
discovering and executing Application Commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Objective

Implement an accessible Menu Bar and global Command Search that:

- Presents all registered Application Commands using traditional
  application\
  menus.

- Provides rapid command discovery using an inline Menu Bar Command
  Search.

- Executes commands through the centralized Command Execution Service.

- Displays current keyboard shortcuts obtained dynamically from the
  Keyboard\
  Shortcut Manager.

- Automatically reflects future command additions without requiring Menu
  Bar-\
  specific implementations.

- Integrates with the Theme & Personalization Engine.

- Supports both the current web application and the future desktop\
  application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Relationship to Previous Epics

Epic 23 introduced the centralized Application Command Framework.

Epic 24 introduced the Command Palette.

Epic 25 introduced the Theme & Personalization Engine.

Epic 26 shall build upon all three architectural foundations.

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall consume these services rather
than\
duplicate their functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Preserve all existing application functionality.

Preserve all keyboard accessibility.

Preserve all screen reader accessibility.

Preserve all existing report workflows.

Do not duplicate command execution logic.

Do not duplicate keyboard shortcut management.

Do not duplicate appearance management.

Reuse existing architecture wherever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Architectural Principles

The Menu Bar shall remain a presentation layer.

The Menu Bar shall not contain business logic.

The Menu Bar shall:

Display commands.

Display command categories.

Display current keyboard shortcuts.

Display command availability.

Provide inline Command Search.

Execute commands.

The centralized Application Command Framework shall remain responsible
for:

Command registration.

Command execution.

Command searching.

Keyboard shortcut resolution.

Command availability.

The Menu Bar shall consume these services rather than implement them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Centralized Integration

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall integrate with:

Application Command Registry

Command Execution Service

Centralized Command Search Engine

Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Theme & Personalization Engine

Application Settings

Future Project Management

Future Plug-ins

Future Jira integration

Future Desktop Application

Future command providers

No duplicate command definitions shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Global Keyboard Access

Because browser-reserved keyboard shortcuts prevent implementation of\
traditional desktop menu behavior within the web application, ART shall
provide\
web-friendly keyboard alternatives.

The following global shortcuts shall be supported.

F10

Moves keyboard focus to the Menu Bar.

Alt+/

Alternative shortcut that moves keyboard focus to the Menu Bar.

Alt+Q

Global shortcut that moves keyboard focus directly to the Menu Bar
Command\
Search from anywhere within the application.

Users shall not be required to first focus the Menu Bar before using
Command\
Search.

Ctrl+Shift+P

Opens the Command Palette.

The Menu Bar Command Search and the Command Palette shall both use the
same\
centralized Command Search Engine.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Web Application Behavior

Within the web application:

F10 shall move keyboard focus to the Menu Bar.

Alt+/ shall provide an alternative method for focusing the Menu Bar.

Alt+Q shall immediately move keyboard focus to the Menu Bar Command
Search.

Traditional browser-reserved Alt behavior shall not be overridden.

The implementation shall avoid conflicts with browser keyboard
shortcuts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Desktop Compatibility

The architecture shall support native desktop menu behavior.

When ART is implemented as a desktop application, the Menu Bar shall
support\
traditional desktop keyboard interaction including:

Alt

Alt+F

Alt+E

Alt+V

Alt+T

Alt+H

and other platform-specific menu behaviors where appropriate.

No redesign of the Menu Bar architecture shall be required.

Platform-specific keyboard behavior shall remain isolated from Menu Bar\
implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Theme Integration

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall automatically inherit all visual\
accessibility settings from the Theme & Personalization Engine.

This includes:

Theme

Zoom

Font Size

Interface Density

Enhanced Focus Indicators

Reduced Motion

Border Visibility

Future personalization settings

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall not maintain independent
appearance\
settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Shortcut Integration

All displayed keyboard shortcuts shall be retrieved dynamically from
the\
Keyboard Shortcut Manager.

No shortcut text shall be hard-coded.

Whenever a keyboard shortcut assignment changes, the Menu Bar, Command
Search,\
and Command Palette shall immediately display the updated shortcut.

All user interface components that display commands shall remain
synchronized,\
including:

Menu Bar

Command Search

Command Palette

Help documentation

Welcome Screen

Accessible tooltips

Future user interface components

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Scope

This epic includes:

Menu Bar

Application menus

Menu navigation

Menu accessibility

Global Command Search

Keyboard interaction

Screen reader accessibility

Dynamic command display

Dynamic keyboard shortcut display

Theme Engine integration

Documentation updates

Validation

Regression testing

Source control

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Out of Scope

This epic does not include:

Dashboard redesign

Project Management

Desktop implementation

Ribbon interface

Toolbar

Context menus

Plug-in implementation

Jira implementation

These features may integrate with the Menu Bar and Command Search in
future\
epics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Implementation Strategy

Implement this epic incrementally.

Proceed to the next implementation phase only after successfully
completing the\
current phase.

#### Phase 1

Implement the Menu Bar framework.

Integrate with the centralized Command Framework.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 2

Implement keyboard navigation.

Implement web-specific keyboard behavior.

Implement global Menu Bar focus.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 3

Implement the Menu Bar Command Search.

Integrate with the centralized Command Search Engine.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 4

Implement dynamic menus.

Implement dynamic keyboard shortcut display.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 5

Integrate the Theme & Personalization Engine.

Verify appearance inheritance.

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 6

Update documentation.

Update:

README.md

ARCHITECTURE.md

COMMANDS.md

CHANGELOG.md

User Guide

Help documentation

Verify successful application build.

Create a checkpoint commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 7

Perform validation.

Perform accessibility testing.

Perform regression testing.

Proceed to Source Control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Success Criteria

This epic shall be considered complete only when:

A fully accessible Menu Bar has been implemented.

Global Command Search has been implemented.

The Menu Bar and Command Search execute commands through the
centralized\
Application Command Framework.

Current keyboard shortcuts are dynamically displayed.

The Menu Bar and Command Search automatically inherit all Theme Engine\
settings.

Existing functionality remains unchanged.

Accessibility has been preserved or improved.

The application builds successfully.

Documentation has been updated.

The implementation is ready for Epic 27 – Dashboard Simplification.

### Part 2 – Menu Structure & Command Organization

### Overview

Implement a fully accessible Menu Bar that dynamically presents
Application\
Commands organized into logical menus.

The Menu Bar shall be generated from the centralized Application
Command\
Registry.

Menu definitions shall not be hard-coded throughout the application.

Instead, the Menu Bar shall construct itself using registered command
metadata.

Future features shall be able to contribute menus and menu items
without\
modifying existing Menu Bar implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Standard Menu Structure

Version 2.0 shall include the following top-level menus.

File

Edit

View

Report

Tools

Templates

Window

Help

Future menus may be automatically added by registered command providers.

Examples include:

Projects

Plugins

Jira

Desktop

Cloud

Developer

Experimental

These menus shall only appear when one or more registered commands
belong to\
that category.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### File Menu

The File menu shall contain commands including, but not limited to:

New Report

Open Report

Open Project (future)

Close Report

Save

Save As

Import

Export

Print (future)

Exit (desktop)

Commands shall be displayed only when applicable.

Unavailable commands shall be disabled rather than removed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Edit Menu

The Edit menu shall contain editing commands including:

Undo

Redo

Cut

Copy

Paste

Find

Replace

Application Settings

Future editing commands

The Menu Bar shall obtain keyboard shortcuts dynamically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### View Menu

The View menu shall contain presentation-related commands.

Examples include:

Welcome Screen

Dashboard

Command Palette

Toggle Status Bar (future)

Zoom In

Zoom Out

Reset Zoom

Theme Selection

Future visual accessibility commands

View commands shall integrate with the Theme Engine.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Report Menu

The Report menu shall contain report-related commands.

Examples include:

Configure Report

Edit Report

View Report

Validate Report

Report Statistics

Generate Executive Summary

Generate Audit Log

Generate Usability Report

Progress Log

Future report commands

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Tools Menu

The Tools menu shall contain application tools.

Examples include:

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Template Manager

Future Plug-in Manager

Future Jira Integration

Future Desktop Synchronization

Future Diagnostics

Future utilities

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Templates Menu

The Templates menu shall contain template-related commands.

Examples include:

Use Template

View Template

Edit Template

Delete Template

Import Template

Export Template

Template Settings

Future template commands

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Window Menu

The Window menu shall manage application windows and dialogs.

Version 2.0 may initially contain only:

Bring Welcome Screen to Front

Close Current Dialog

Future desktop implementations may expand this menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Help Menu

The Help menu shall contain:

User Guide

Keyboard Shortcut Reference

Help Topics

Release Notes

Version Information

Report an Issue

About ART

Future documentation commands

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Menu Generation

The Menu Bar shall not hard-code menu contents.

Instead:

Each registered command shall expose:

Menu Category

Menu Order

Command Order

Command Name

Command Identifier

Current Keyboard Shortcut

Command Availability

Visibility Rules

The Menu Bar shall construct menus dynamically from this information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Command Availability

Commands shall automatically update based on application state.

Examples:

Save shall be disabled when no report is open.

Validate Report shall be disabled until appropriate.

Export commands shall be disabled when unavailable.

Users shall receive appropriate accessibility feedback.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Keyboard Shortcuts

Displayed keyboard shortcuts shall always reflect current assignments
from the\
Keyboard Shortcut Manager.

No shortcut text shall be hard-coded.

Whenever a shortcut changes:

The Menu Bar

Command Search

Command Palette

Help

Welcome Screen

Accessible tooltips

shall immediately reflect the new assignment.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Menu Providers

The architecture shall allow future components to register additional
menus.

Examples include:

Projects

Plugins

Jira

Desktop

Cloud

Developer

Experimental

No modifications to the Menu Bar implementation shall be required.

Menus shall appear automatically when registered.

Menus shall disappear automatically when no registered commands remain.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Requirements

Every menu shall expose:

Appropriate semantic roles.

Accessible names.

Accessible states.

Accessible expanded/collapsed status.

Accessible disabled state.

Accessible shortcut information where appropriate.

Screen readers shall announce:

Menu names.

Current item.

Shortcut.

Disabled state.

Expanded state.

Checked state where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Theme Integration

Menus shall automatically inherit:

Theme

Zoom

Font Size

Interface Density

Enhanced Focus Indicators

Reduced Motion

Border Visibility

Future Theme Engine settings.

Menus shall not maintain independent appearance settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The menu architecture shall support:

Desktop native menus

Context menus

Ribbon interfaces (if ever desired)

Plug-in supplied menus

Jira menus

Cloud menus

Organization-specific menus

Developer menus

Version 2.0 shall implement only the menus described in this epic.

The architecture shall support future expansion without redesign.

### Part 3 – Keyboard Interaction, Command Search & Accessibility

### Overview

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall provide a fully
keyboard-accessible\
experience that complements the Command Palette while remaining
optimized for\
both the current web application and the future desktop application.\
The menu bar and menus shall use the accessible design pattern described
at
<https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/examples/menubar-navigation/>.

Better... But we can improve it. When programmatic focus is in the
menubar, pressing down arrow should also open the focused menu the same
way that enter and spacebar already open focused menus. When a menu is
open and programmatic/keyboard focus is inside the menu, pressing left
arrow should move focus into the previous menu to the left, while
pressing right arrow should move focus into the next menu to the right.
If focus is in the last menu in the menu bar, and user presses right
arrow, focus should move into the first menu. If focus is in the first
menu and user presses left arrow, focus should move into the last menu
on the menubar. All other menu functionality should be maintained. Note,
if a menu item has a sub menu and user presses right arrow, the sub menu
shall open and focus shall move into the first item in the submenu;
pressing left arrow or escape closes the submenu and returns focus to
the menu item containing the submenu. If focus is inside a menu and user
presses escape, focus shall return to the top-level menubar items,
pressing escape once more exits the menubar and returns focus to the
location where user was before envoking the menubar. Regarding the
menubar command search, search results shall begin to display directly
beneath the search box as the user types. Pressing the down arrow key
shall move focus directly into the list of search results, pressing
escape while in the search results list shall move focus back into the
search box with the current search term selected.\

open and programmatic/keyboard focus is inside the menu, pressing left

If focus is in the last menu in the menu bar, and user presses right

escape while in the search results list shall move focus back into the
search box with the current search term selected.

The Menu Bar shall function as an alternative interface for browsing
commands.

The Command Search shall function as a rapid command discovery tool.

Both interfaces shall use the centralized Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Menu Bar Keyboard Interaction

The Menu Bar shall support the following keyboard interactions.

#### Focus Menu Bar

F10

Moves keyboard focus to the first enabled top-level menu.

Alt+/

Provides an alternative method of focusing the Menu Bar within the web\
application.

These shortcuts shall function from anywhere within the application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigate Top-Level Menus

Right Arrow

Moves to the next top-level menu.

Left Arrow

Moves to the previous top-level menu.

Home

Moves to the first top-level menu.

End

Moves to the final top-level menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Open Menus

Enter

Opens the currently focused menu.

Down Arrow

Opens the currently focused menu and moves to the first enabled menu
item.

Space

Opens the currently focused menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigate Menu Items

Up Arrow

Moves to the previous enabled menu item.

Down Arrow

Moves to the next enabled menu item.

Home

Moves to the first enabled menu item.

End

Moves to the final enabled menu item.

Typing printable characters shall move focus to the next menu item whose
name\
begins with the typed character whenever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Execute Commands

Enter

Executes the currently selected command.

Space

Executes the currently selected command where appropriate.

Immediately after execution:

Menus shall close.

Keyboard focus shall move appropriately based upon the executed command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Close Menus

Escape

Closes the currently open menu.

If no menus remain open:

Keyboard focus shall remain on the corresponding top-level menu.

Pressing Escape again shall return focus to the previously focused
application\
control whenever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Global Command Search

Implement an inline Command Search within the Menu Bar.

The Command Search shall be globally accessible.

Users shall not be required to first focus the Menu Bar.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Access

Alt+Q

Moves keyboard focus directly to the Menu Bar Command Search from
anywhere\
within ART.

If Command Search already contains text:

All existing text shall be selected.

Users may immediately begin typing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Behavior

Command Search shall search the centralized Application Command
Registry.

Searching shall occur dynamically as users type.

The implementation shall:

Ignore capitalization.

Ignore leading and trailing whitespace.

Return matching commands immediately.

Sort results by relevance.

Avoid duplicate results.

Automatically include future registered commands.

No search indexing shall be duplicated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Results

Each result shall display:

Command Name

Current Keyboard Shortcut

Menu Category

Optional brief description

Example:

Export Report Ctrl+Shift+E File

Validate Report Ctrl+Shift+V Report

Application Settings Ctrl+, Edit

Keyboard Shortcut Manager Ctrl+Alt+K Tools

Displayed keyboard shortcuts shall always reflect the current
assignments from\
the Keyboard Shortcut Manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Interaction Within Command Search

Up Arrow

Moves to the previous search result.

Down Arrow

Moves to the next search result.

Page Up

Moves up through larger result sets.

Page Down

Moves down through larger result sets.

Enter

Executes the selected command.

Escape

If search text exists:

Clear the current search.

If the search box is already empty:

Return keyboard focus to the Menu Bar.

Tab

Move according to the normal application tab order.

Shift+Tab

Move according to the reverse tab order.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Relationship to the Command Palette

The Menu Bar Command Search and the Command Palette shall both use the
same\
centralized Command Search Engine.

The search engine shall be implemented only once.

The Menu Bar Command Search shall provide:

A lightweight inline search experience integrated into the Menu Bar.

The Command Palette shall provide:

A dedicated modal interface optimized for keyboard-first workflows.

Both interfaces shall:

Search the same registered commands.

Display current keyboard shortcuts.

Execute commands through the centralized Command Execution Service.

Automatically reflect future registered commands.

Automatically reflect keyboard shortcut changes.

Automatically inherit Theme, Zoom, Text Size, Display Spacing, Enhanced
Focus\
Indicators, Border Visibility, Reduced Motion, and future Theme Engine\
settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Requirements

The Menu Bar and Command Search shall fully support:

Keyboard-only operation.

JAWS.

NVDA.

VoiceOver.

TalkBack.

Other assistive technologies.

The Command Search edit field shall expose:

An accessible name.

An accessible description.

An appropriate role.

Accessible autocomplete behavior where applicable.

Search results shall expose:

Accessible names.

Accessible roles.

Accessible selection state.

Accessible shortcut information.

Accessible menu category information.

Appropriate result count announcements.

Keyboard focus shall always remain visible.

No keyboard traps shall be introduced.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The Command Search architecture shall support future searching of:

Application Commands

Projects

Reports

Templates

Recent Reports

Recent Projects

Help Topics

User Guide

Documentation

Plug-ins

Jira Commands

Desktop Commands

Cloud Commands

Future searchable metadata

Version 2.0 shall implement searching of registered Application Commands
only.

The architecture shall support future expansion without redesign.

### Part 4 – Menu Behavior, Accessibility & Dynamic Command Integration

### Overview

The Menu Bar shall dynamically present commands registered with the
centralized\
Application Command Framework.

The Menu Bar shall automatically update whenever commands become
available,\
unavailable, visible, hidden, added, or removed.

The Menu Bar shall remain synchronized with the:

Application Command Registry

Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Theme & Personalization Engine

Command Search

Command Palette

No duplicate command definitions shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Remember Last Active Menu

The Menu Bar shall remember the last top-level menu that had keyboard
focus.

When the user presses:

F10

keyboard focus shall return to the previously focused top-level menu
whenever\
practical.

If the user has not previously used the Menu Bar during the current
session,\
focus shall move to:

File

The remembered menu shall remain valid only for the current application\
session.

The remembered menu shall not be persisted between application launches.

Home shall always move focus to the first visible top-level menu.

End shall always move focus to the final visible top-level menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Command Integration

The Menu Bar shall automatically display commands registered with the\
Application Command Registry.

Menu items shall not be hard-coded.

Each registered command shall provide metadata including:

Command Name

Unique Command Identifier

Menu Category

Display Order

Current Keyboard Shortcut

Command Availability

Visibility

Enabled State

Checked State (where applicable)

Future command metadata

The Menu Bar shall construct itself dynamically from this metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Menu Visibility

Menus shall only appear when they contain one or more registered
commands.

Examples include future menus such as:

Projects

Plugins

Jira

Desktop

Cloud

Developer

Experimental

If no registered commands belong to one of these categories, that menu
shall\
not be displayed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Disabled Commands

Commands that are temporarily unavailable shall remain visible.

Unavailable commands shall:

Appear disabled.

Remain in their expected location.

Expose the appropriate disabled state to assistive technologies.

Disabled commands shall not receive keyboard focus.

Examples include:

Save

Close Report

Export

Validate Report

Generate Executive Summary

Open Project

Future commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Checked Menu Items

Commands representing toggleable application state shall display a
checkmark.

Examples include:

Enhanced Focus Indicators

Border Visibility

Reduced Motion

Word Wrap (future)

Status Bar (future)

Other toggle commands

The checked state shall be synchronized with the underlying application
state.

Screen readers shall announce checked and unchecked states
appropriately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Submenus

The Menu Bar shall support nested submenus.

Examples include:

View

Zoom

Theme

Display Spacing

Text Size

Visual Accessibility

Help

Documentation

Tutorials

Keyboard Reference

Future nested menus shall be supported without architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Submenu Keyboard Interaction

Right Arrow

When positioned on a submenu:

Expand the submenu.

Move keyboard focus to the first enabled submenu item.

Left Arrow

Close the current submenu.

Return focus to the parent menu item.

Escape

Close the current submenu.

Return focus to the parent menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Mnemonic Support

Each top-level menu shall expose an application mnemonic.

Examples:

File

Edit

View

Report

Tools

Templates

Window

Help

Within the web application:

Browser-reserved Alt combinations shall not be overridden.

Future desktop implementations may enable traditional mnemonic behavior.

The Menu Bar architecture shall support mnemonics without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Keyboard Shortcuts

Every displayed keyboard shortcut shall be obtained from the Keyboard
Shortcut\
Manager.

Whenever shortcut assignments change:

Menu Bar

Command Search

Command Palette

Help

Welcome Screen

Accessible Tooltips

Future UI components

shall immediately display the updated shortcut.

No restart shall be required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessible Tooltips

Every interactive Menu Bar command shall expose an accessible tooltip.

Tooltips shall include:

Command Name

Current Keyboard Shortcut

Brief command description

Example:

Validate Report

Ctrl+Shift+V

Checks the current report for completeness and potential issues.

Accessible tooltips shall automatically reflect updated keyboard
shortcuts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Theme Integration

The Menu Bar shall inherit all appearance settings from the Theme &\
Personalization Engine.

This includes:

Theme

Zoom

Text Size

Display Spacing

Enhanced Focus Indicators

Border Visibility

Reduced Motion

Future appearance settings

No Menu Bar-specific appearance settings shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Screen Reader Accessibility

Every menu shall expose:

Accessible Name

Accessible Role

Accessible State

Expanded State

Collapsed State

Disabled State

## Epic 27 – Dashboard Widget Framework

### Part 1 – Overview, Objectives & Architectural Foundation

### Overview

This epic introduces the Dashboard Widget Framework for ART Version 2.0.

The Dashboard shall evolve from a fixed collection of controls into a\
fully configurable, accessibility-first workspace composed of
independent,\
reusable dashboard widgets.

Rather than hard-coding dashboard functionality, the Dashboard Widget
Framework\
shall dynamically discover, display, and manage registered dashboard
widgets.

Widgets may be supplied by:

- Core ART functionality
- Projects
- Future integrations
- Future plugins
- Future desktop features
- Future cloud services

The Dashboard Widget Framework shall provide users with complete control
over\
which widgets are displayed, how they are organized, and how they are
arranged\
within supported dashboard layouts.

The Dashboard shall prioritize information and workflow over command
execution.

Application commands shall continue to be accessed through:

- Menu Bar
- Command Search
- Command Palette
- Keyboard Shortcuts
- Context Menus

The Dashboard shall become the user's personalized workspace.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Objectives

Implement an extensible Dashboard Widget Framework that:

- Supports reusable dashboard widgets.

- Supports multiple dashboard layouts.

- Allows users to customize their dashboard.

- Supports future integrations and plugins.

- Supports dashboard analytics.

- Supports project-specific widgets.

- Supports report-specific widgets.

- Supports workspace-wide metrics.

- Preserves accessibility-first design.

- Requires no architectural redesign as ART evolves.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Preserve all existing report functionality.

Preserve all existing project functionality.

Preserve all existing accessibility features.

Preserve keyboard accessibility.

Preserve screen reader accessibility.

Preserve voice navigation accessibility.

Preserve speech dictation accessibility.

Preserve switch device accessibility.

Preserve compatibility with other assistive technologies.

Do not duplicate Application Command Framework functionality.

Do not duplicate Theme Engine functionality.

Do not duplicate Menu Bar functionality.

Reuse existing architecture wherever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Architectural Principles

The Dashboard shall function as a presentation layer.

The Dashboard shall not contain business logic.

The Dashboard shall consume:

Application Command Framework

Theme & Personalization Framework

Menu Bar

Command Search

Command Palette

Future Global Context Menu Framework

Widgets shall expose data.

Widgets shall expose commands.

Widgets shall not implement duplicate command execution logic.

Every widget command shall execute through the centralized Application
Command\
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Widget Framework

The Dashboard shall dynamically discover registered widgets.

The Dashboard shall not hard-code widget implementations.

Every widget shall register itself with the Dashboard Widget Framework.

Future plugins and integrations shall be able to register widgets
without\
modifying Dashboard code.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Widget Metadata

Every registered widget shall provide metadata including:

Widget Name

Unique Widget Identifier

Widget Description

Widget Category

Widget Priority

Widget Heading

Widget Region Label

Refresh Policy

Visibility Rules

Configuration Options

Supported Commands

Help Topic

Minimum ART Version

Future metadata as required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Widget Accessibility

Every widget shall:

Begin with a level 3 heading.

Be rendered as an independent landmark region.

Expose appropriate accessible names.

Expose appropriate accessible descriptions where applicable.

Be fully operable using:

Keyboard

Screen readers

Voice navigation

Speech dictation

Switch devices

Other assistive technologies

Every widget heading shall function as the widget's Collapse/Expand
control.

The widget heading shall be operable using:

Mouse

Touch

Enter

Space

Whenever a widget is expanded or collapsed:

The updated state shall be programmatically exposed.

Screen readers shall announce:

- Heading level 3
- Expanded

or

- Heading level 3
- Collapsed

The expanded or collapsed state of each widget shall persist between\
application sessions.

Widget headings shall use stable, descriptive names to ensure reliable\
operation with voice navigation and speech recognition software.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dashboard Philosophy

The Dashboard shall answer three primary questions:

What should I work on?

What is the current status of my work?

What insights can ART provide?

The Dashboard shall prioritize information over commands.

The Dashboard shall remain clean, organized, and user-configurable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Default Dashboard

ART Version 2.0 shall provide a default dashboard containing:

Quick Actions

Continue Working

Current Project

Current Report

Report Metrics

Recent Activity

Notifications

Users may customize this dashboard at any time.

Future versions of ART may expand the default configuration without
requiring\
architectural redesign.

### Part 2 – Built-in Widgets, Dashboard Layouts & Dashboard Configuration

### Built-in Widget Library

ART Version 2.0 shall include a library of built-in dashboard widgets.

Widgets shall be grouped into logical categories within the Dashboard
Framework.

Widgets shall automatically determine whether they are applicable based
on the\
current application state.

Widgets that are not applicable shall either:

- Be hidden, or
- Display an appropriate informational message indicating why no data
  is\
  currently available.

The Dashboard shall never display empty or confusing widgets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Workspace Widgets

Workspace widgets provide information about the user's overall ART
workspace.

Examples include:

- Continue Working
- Recent Activity
- Notifications
- Workspace Summary
- Frequently Used Commands
- Frequently Referenced Accessibility Standards
- Frequently Referenced Success Criteria
- Frequently Used Issue Types
- Recently Used Templates
- Recently Referenced Accessibility Standards

Workspace widgets shall summarize activity across all reports and
projects.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Widgets

Project widgets shall become available whenever a project is open.

Examples include:

- Current Project
- Project Health
- Project Progress
- Project Reports
- Project Timeline
- Project Statistics
- Project Validation Status
- Project Export History

Future project widgets may be added without modifying the Dashboard
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Report Widgets

Report widgets shall become available whenever a report is open.

Examples include:

- Current Report
- Report Metrics
- Report Validation
- Report Statistics
- Evaluation Progress
- Referenced Accessibility Standards
- Referenced Success Criteria
- Referenced Issue Types
- Export History

The existing Report Metrics functionality shall be preserved and
incorporated as\
a Report Metrics widget.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Analytics Widgets

Analytics widgets shall summarize information across the entire ART
workspace.

Examples include:

Framework.

Plugins may register one or more dashboard widgets.

Plugins may also register:

Commands

Help topics

Analytics

Context menu commands

Future metadata

### Dashboard Layouts

The Dashboard Framework shall support multiple layouts.

Version 2.0 shall implement:

Dashboard Tabs

Compact Dashboard

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dashboard Cards Layout

Dashboard Cards shall be the default layout.

Each selected widget shall appear as an independent dashboard card.

Cards shall appear in user-configurable order.

Each card shall begin with a level 3 heading.

Each card shall function as an independent landmark region.

Practices Guide\
(APG) Tabs pattern.

### Custom Widgets

### Widget Import & Export

practical.

### Widget Layout Persistence

The Dashboard shall automatically remember:

### Future Compatibility

### Part 3 – Widget Behavior, Commands & Interaction

### Widget Behavior

Each dashboard widget shall function as an independent, reusable
component.

Widgets shall operate independently of one another.

Failure of one widget shall not affect the operation of other dashboard
widgets.

Widgets shall automatically update when their underlying data changes.

Widgets shall not require users to manually refresh the Dashboard unless
a\
widget has been explicitly configured for manual refresh.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Widget Headings

Every dashboard widget shall begin with a level 3 heading.

The widget heading shall function as the widget's Collapse/Expand
control.

Separate Expand or Collapse buttons shall not be displayed.

Users shall be able to toggle the widget by:

- Mouse
- Touch
- Enter
- Space
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation

Whenever practical, users shall also be able to activate widgets using
their\
displayed heading text.

Example voice commands include:

"Click Current Report"

"Expand Project Health"

"Collapse Notifications"

Widget headings shall use stable, descriptive names that remain suitable
for\
voice navigation software.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Expanded and Collapsed States

All dashboard widgets shall be expanded by default.

Each widget shall maintain its own expanded or collapsed state.

Collapsing one widget shall not affect any other widget.

Expanded and collapsed states shall persist between application
sessions.

The expanded state shall be programmatically exposed using appropriate\
accessibility semantics.

Screen readers shall announce whether a widget is:

Expanded

or

Collapsed

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Widget Refresh

Widgets shall automatically refresh whenever practical.

Widgets may support one or more refresh policies.

Supported refresh policies include:

Automatic

Manual

Timed Refresh

Future refresh policies

Widget authors shall determine the default refresh behavior appropriate
for\
their widget.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Widget Commands

Every widget shall expose commands through the centralized Application
Command\
Framework.

Widgets shall never implement independent command execution logic.

Standard widget commands include:

Refresh Widget

Configure Widget

Collapse Widget

Expand Widget

Hide Widget

Move Widget Up

Move Widget Down

Reset Widget

Optional widget commands include:

Duplicate Widget

Export Widget

Delete Widget

Individual widgets may register additional commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Jira

#### GitHub

View Repository

Future integrations may register additional commands without modifying
the\
Dashboard Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Command Framework Integration

All widget commands shall execute through the centralized Application
Command\
Framework.

Widget commands shall automatically become available through:

Menu Bar

Command Search

Command Palette

Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Help Documentation

Welcome Screen

Future Global Context Menu Framework

Future command surfaces

No duplicate command implementations shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

commands.

introduced.

### Accessibility Requirements

Screen readers

Switch devices

Other assistive technologies

Every interactive control shall expose:

Appropriate properties

Interactive controls shall use stable and descriptive names suitable for
both\
screen readers and voice navigation software.

Widget headings shall support:

No keyboard traps shall be introduced.

### Future Compatibility

## Epic 28 – Project Workspace Framework

### Part 1 – Overview, Objectives & Architectural Foundation

### Overview

This epic introduces the Project Workspace Framework for ART Version
2.0.

The Project Workspace Framework shall allow users to organize multiple
reports,\
templates, project resources, and future integrations into a single,\
persistent accessibility project.

Rather than treating reports as isolated files, ART shall treat them as\
components of a Project Workspace.

A Project Workspace shall preserve both project information and the
user's\
working environment so that users may resume work exactly where they
left off.

The Project Workspace Framework shall build upon the architecture
established\
by:

- Application Command Framework
- Command Palette
- Theme & Personalization Framework
- Menu Bar
- Dashboard Widget Framework
- Future Global Context Menu Framework

The Project Workspace Framework shall become the foundation for future:

- Jira integration
- Azure DevOps integration
- GitHub integration
- Plugin support
- Cloud synchronization
- Desktop application functionality
- Team collaboration
- Organization-level reporting

No architectural redesign shall be required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Objectives

Implement a Project Workspace Framework that:

- Organizes related reports into a single project.

- Preserves the user's working environment.

- Supports multiple report types.

- Supports future integrations.

- Supports future plugins.

- Supports project analytics.

- Supports project-level commands.

- Supports project-level validation.

- Supports project import and export.

- Supports future synchronization.

- Preserves ART's accessibility-first philosophy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Preserve all existing report functionality.

Preserve all existing Dashboard functionality.

Preserve all existing accessibility features.

Preserve keyboard accessibility.

Preserve screen reader accessibility.

Preserve voice navigation accessibility.

Preserve speech dictation accessibility.

Preserve switch device accessibility.

Preserve compatibility with other assistive technologies.

Reuse existing Application Frameworks whenever practical.

Do not duplicate existing framework functionality.

The Project Workspace Framework shall consume existing ART frameworks
rather\
than implementing duplicate functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Workspace Philosophy

A Project Workspace shall represent an accessibility project rather than
a\
single document.

A Project Workspace shall contain one or more reports and associated
project\
resources.

Opening a Project Workspace shall restore the user's working environment
rather\
than merely opening files.

Users shall be able to leave ART and later resume work from the exact
location\
where they stopped.

The Continue Working dashboard widget shall use the Project Workspace\
Framework to restore the user's previous workspace.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Workspace Components

A Project Workspace may contain:

Accessibility reports

Executive summaries

Audit logs

Progress logs

Usability reports

Templates

Project notes (future)

Project attachments (future)

Integration metadata

Plugin data

Future project resources

The framework shall allow additional project resource types without
requiring\
architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Workspace Metadata

Every Project Workspace shall maintain metadata including:

Project Name

Unique Project Identifier

Project Description

Project Owner

Date Created

Last Modified

Current Status

Project Version

Associated Templates

Associated Reports

Project Statistics

Future metadata

The metadata model shall be extensible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Workspace Lifecycle

Users shall be able to:

Create Project Workspace

Open Project Workspace

Close Project Workspace

Save Project Workspace

Save Project Workspace As

Rename Project Workspace

Duplicate Project Workspace

Import Project Workspace

Export Project Workspace

Delete Project Workspace

Archive Project Workspace (future)

Restore Archived Project Workspace (future)

All project lifecycle commands shall execute through the Application
Command\
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Workspace State Restoration

Opening a Project Workspace shall restore the user's previous working\
environment whenever practical.

The restored workspace shall include:

Previously open reports.

Previously active report.

Previously selected evaluation item.

Cursor position.

Expanded or collapsed sections.

Search and filter settings.

Dashboard state.

Dashboard widgets.

Current dashboard layout.

Project-specific widget configuration.

Future workspace state information.

Workspace restoration shall be transparent to the user.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Accessibility Requirements

The Project Workspace Framework shall fully support:

Keyboard-only operation.

Screen readers.

Voice navigation.

Speech dictation.

Switch devices.

Screen magnification.

High contrast themes.

Reduced motion.

All ART personalization settings.

All Project Workspace functionality shall expose appropriate accessible
names,\
roles, states, and properties where applicable.

Interactive controls shall expose stable, descriptive names suitable for
both\
screen readers and voice navigation software.

No Project Workspace functionality shall introduce keyboard traps or\
accessibility regressions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Architectural Principles

The Project Workspace Framework shall function as a centralized project\
management layer.

Project Workspaces shall consume existing ART frameworks.

Project Workspaces shall not duplicate:

Application Commands

Theme settings

Dashboard functionality

Menu functionality

Context menu functionality

Widget functionality

Future frameworks

Future integrations shall extend the Project Workspace Framework
through\
well-defined registration mechanisms rather than modifying the
framework\
directly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The Project Workspace Framework shall support future integration with:

Jira

Azure DevOps

GitHub

Desktop Application

Cloud Services

Organization Extensions

Plugins

Developer Extensions

Experimental Features

No architectural redesign shall be required.

### Part 2 – Project Storage, File Organization & Resource Management

### Project Workspace Storage

Every Project Workspace shall be stored as a dedicated folder on the
user's\
computer.

The Project Workspace folder shall be named using the Project Name.

Example:

My Website Accessibility Audit/

Users shall interact with ordinary folders and files rather than hidden\
databases.

The Project Workspace folder shall remain portable and suitable for
backup,\
copying, synchronization, and archival.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Workspace File

Every Project Workspace shall contain a Project.artproj file.

The Project.artproj file shall store:

Project Name

Unique Project Identifier (GUID)

Project Description

Project Owner

Organization

Creation Date

Last Modified Date

Project Version

Current Status

Workspace Configuration

Dashboard Configuration

Project Relationships

Registered Resources

Plugin Metadata

Integration Metadata

Workspace State

Future metadata

The Project.artproj file shall function as the authoritative description
of\
the Project Workspace.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Folder Structure

When a Project Workspace is created, ART shall automatically create the\
standard Project Workspace folder structure.

Example:

My Website Accessibility Audit/

    Project.artproj

    Reports/

    Audit Logs/

    Progress Logs/

    Templates/

    Project Assets/

        Planning/

        Requirements/

        Timeline/

        Documentation/

        Credentials/

        Designs/

        Meeting Notes/

        Images/

        Other/

    Attachments/

    Exports/

    Backups/

    .art/

Additional folders may be introduced in future versions without
requiring\
architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Automatic Organization

Users shall not be required to manually organize project resources.

Whenever project resources are created, imported, or added, ART shall\
automatically store them in the appropriate Project Workspace folder.

Examples include:

Reports

Progress Logs

Templates

Project Assets

Attachments

Exports

Backups

### Resource Independence

All reports shall continue functioning as independent files.

Delete reports

Project Workspaces shall provide organization without removing the
ability to\
work with individual reports.

### Workspace Portability

### Creating a Project Workspace

### Saving Project Workspaces

Users shall determine where Project Workspaces are stored.

ART shall never automatically choose the location where a Project
Workspace is\

### Opening Project Workspaces

Restore workspace state.

Restore project relationships.

Restore future project settings.

Closing a Project Workspace shall:

### Future Compatibility

The Project Workspace Framework shall support future:

Cloud synchronization

Shared workspaces

Project permissions

Collaboration

Organization workspaces

Desktop application features

Plugin extensions

Developer extensions

No architectural redesign shall be required.\
One recommendation

I would make one more architectural addition while we're here.

Right now, a user can have one Project Workspace open at a time. I think
that's the right decision for Version 2.0 because it keeps the interface
focused and avoids unnecessary complexity.

However, I'd specify that the framework must not assume this limitation
is permanent. Internally, it should be designed so that supporting
multiple open Project Workspaces in a future version is an enhancement
rather than a redesign. That gives us flexibility if, years down the
road, ART evolves into a desktop application where users can compare or
work across projects side by side. For Version 2.0, though, one active
Project Workspace keeps the user experience simple and predictable.

### Part 5 – Workspace Experience, Persistence & Navigation

### Workspace Experience

The Project Workspace shall provide a unified working environment for
all\
resources associated with an accessibility project.

Rather than opening isolated documents, users shall work within a
Project\
Workspace that preserves project organization, workspace state, and
user\
context.

One Project Workspace shall be active at a time.

Future versions may support multiple simultaneously open Project
Workspaces\
without requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Workspace State Persistence

The Project Workspace shall automatically preserve the user's working\
environment.

Examples include:

Previously open reports

Previously active report

Selected report section

Cursor location

Keyboard focus location

Expanded and collapsed sections

Search and filter settings

Sort order

Dashboard layout

Dashboard widget configuration

Current dashboard widget states

Workspace panel sizes

Open dialogs (where practical)

Future workspace settings

Users shall be able to leave ART and later resume work from the same
location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Automatic Workspace Restoration

Opening a Project Workspace shall automatically restore the previously
saved\
workspace state whenever practical.

Restoration shall include:

Previously open reports

Previously active report

Current editing location

Dashboard configuration

Dashboard layout

Resource Navigator state

Expanded and collapsed navigation groups

Future workspace state

The restoration process shall be automatic and require no user
intervention.

The Resource Navigator shall provide organized navigation throughout the
active\
Project Workspace.

The Resource Navigator shall replace traditional tree-view navigation.

than\

Attachments

Exports

Backups

Future resource categories

landmark\
navigation, keyboard shortcuts, and voice commands.
