## Epic 29 – Universal Search Framework

### Part 1 – Overview, Objectives & Architectural Foundation

### Overview

Implement the Universal Search Framework for ART Version 2.0.

The Universal Search Framework shall provide a centralized, extensible,\
accessibility-first search architecture capable of locating information\
throughout the ART application.

Rather than requiring users to remember where information is stored,
the\
Universal Search Framework shall allow users to search by concept,
keyword,\
metadata, command, accessibility standard, project resource, or future\
integration.

The Universal Search Framework shall become a core application framework
and\
shall build upon:

- Application Command Framework
- Command Palette
- Theme & Personalization Framework
- Menu Bar
- Dashboard Widget Framework
- Project Workspace Framework
- Future Global Context Menu Framework

Future frameworks and plugins shall consume the Universal Search
Framework\
rather than implementing their own independent search functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Objectives

Implement a Universal Search Framework that:

- Provides a centralized search architecture.

- Supports context-aware searching.

- Supports full-text searching.

- Supports metadata searching.

- Supports accessibility-aware searching.

- Supports navigation directly to search results.

- Supports extensibility through Search Providers.

- Supports future integrations.

- Supports future plugins.

- Preserves ART's accessibility-first philosophy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Philosophy

Searching within ART shall focus on helping users locate information
rather\
than requiring them to locate files.

Users shall be able to search using concepts, keywords, accessibility\
terminology, commands, metadata, and other searchable information.

The Universal Search Framework shall determine the most appropriate
search\
scope based upon the user's current context unless the user specifies\
otherwise.

Searching shall always prioritize helping users continue their work with
the\
fewest possible interactions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Universal Search Principles

The Universal Search Framework shall be:

Context-aware

Accessibility-first

Keyboard-first

Voice navigation friendly

Speech dictation friendly

Screen reader friendly

Braille display friendly

Extensible

Plugin-aware

Integration-ready

Future AI-ready

Future cloud-ready

Future desktop-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context-Aware Search

The Universal Search Framework shall automatically determine the
appropriate\
default search scope.

Examples include:

Current Report

Current Project Workspace

Entire ART Workspace

Help Documentation

Accessibility Standards

Commands

Templates

Project Assets

Future search scopes

Users shall always be able to override the default search scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Provider Architecture

The Universal Search Framework shall not search application resources\
directly.

Instead, searchable resources shall register Search Providers.

Examples include:

Report Search Provider

Audit Log Search Provider

Progress Log Search Provider

Template Search Provider

Project Asset Search Provider

Command Search Provider

Help Search Provider

Accessibility Standards Search Provider

Dashboard Search Provider

Plugin Search Providers

Future Integration Search Providers

The Universal Search Framework shall query registered Search Providers
rather\
than implementing duplicate search logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Provider Responsibilities

Each Search Provider shall be responsible for:

Searching its own content.

Providing search result metadata.

Providing stable navigation targets.

Providing result previews.

Providing result ranking information.

Supporting future filtering.

Supporting future indexing.

Supporting future metadata.

The Universal Search Framework shall aggregate and present results from
all\
participating Search Providers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Categories

The Universal Search Framework shall support searching:

Reports

Executive Summaries

Audit Logs

Progress Logs

Templates

Project Assets

Commands

Keyboard Shortcuts

Help Documentation

User Guide

Accessibility Standards

Dashboard Widgets

Project Metadata

Future Plugins

Future Integrations

Future Collaboration Resources

Future Cloud Resources

Additional search categories shall be added through Search Providers
without\
architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Navigation

Every search result shall represent a stable navigation target.

Activating a search result shall navigate directly to the exact
matching\
location whenever practical.

Search navigation shall be consistent regardless of activation method.

Supported activation methods include:

Keyboard

Mouse

Touch

Voice Navigation

Speech Dictation

Screen Readers

Braille Displays

Switch Devices

Future input methods

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Requirements

The Universal Search Framework shall fully support:

Keyboard-only operation

Screen readers

Braille displays

Voice navigation

Speech dictation

Switch devices

High contrast themes

Reduced motion

ART personalization settings

All search functionality shall expose appropriate accessible names,
roles,\
states, and properties where applicable.

No search functionality shall introduce accessibility regressions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Architectural Principles

The Universal Search Framework shall function as a centralized
application\
service.

Application components shall register searchable content rather than\
implementing independent search systems.

Search Providers shall extend the framework through standardized
registration\
mechanisms.

Future integrations shall consume the Universal Search Framework
without\
requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The Universal Search Framework shall support future integration with:

Global Context Menu Framework

Collaboration Framework

Desktop Application

Cloud Synchronization

Jira

Azure DevOps

GitHub

Plugin Marketplace

Artificial Intelligence features

Organization Management

Developer Extensions

No architectural redesign shall be required.

### Part 2 – Search Scope, Context Awareness & Search Sources

### Search Scope Overview

The Universal Search Framework shall automatically determine the
appropriate\
search scope based upon the user's current location within ART.

Users shall not be required to manually select a search scope for
routine\
searches.

The default search scope shall always be the most relevant scope for
the\
user's current context.

Users may override the default search scope at any time.

### Part 3 – Search Query Language, Search Intelligence & Query Processing

### Overview

Implement a comprehensive Search Query Language for the Universal
Search\
Framework.

The Search Query Language shall support both simple keyword searching
and\
advanced query expressions.

Users shall never be required to learn advanced syntax to perform
effective\
searches.

Natural-language searches and advanced queries shall coexist.

The Universal Search Framework shall automatically determine the most\
appropriate interpretation of each search query.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Query Processing

Every search query shall pass through a standardized query processing
pipeline.

The pipeline shall:

Normalize text.

Ignore unnecessary whitespace.

Handle capitalization consistently.

Recognize accessibility terminology.

Expand supported synonyms.

Interpret Boolean expressions.

Interpret field-specific searches.

Recognize Accessibility Standard references.

Recognize WCAG Success Criterion identifiers.

Recognize resource identifiers where applicable.

Prepare the query for execution by registered Search Providers.

Future query processors shall integrate without architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Natural Language Search

Users shall be able to perform searches using ordinary language.

Examples include:

keyboard trap

button label

heading structure

missing alt text

Mark W

executive summary

color contrast

open findings

The Universal Search Framework shall interpret natural-language queries
without\
requiring special syntax.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Exact Phrase Searching

Users shall be able to search for exact phrases.

Examples include:

"Keyboard Trap"

"Product Owner"

"Accessible Name"

Exact phrase searches shall prioritize exact matches over partial
matches.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Boolean Logic

Implement Boolean query support.

Supported operators shall include:

AND

OR

NOT

Symbolic equivalents shall also be supported.

Examples include:

Accessibility AND Forms

1.3.1 AND "Mark W."

Keyboard AND Trap

Heading OR Structure

Keyboard NOT Homepage

1.3.1 & "Mark W."

Keyboard Trap\* -Homepage

Users shall not be required to capitalize Boolean operators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Grouped Expressions

Users shall be able to group expressions.

Examples include:

(Forms OR Inputs) AND Label

(Project OR Workspace) AND Export

("Accessible Name" OR aria-label) AND Button

Nested grouped expressions shall be supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Wildcards

Support wildcard searching.

Examples include:

label\*

head\*

access\*

keyboard\*

trap\*

Support:

Multiple-character wildcard (\*)

Single-character wildcard (?)

Wildcard behavior shall remain consistent throughout the Universal
Search\
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Field-Specific Searching

Users shall be able to search specific metadata fields.

Examples include:

owner:"Mark W."

project:"Yakima"

status:Open

type:Report

tag:Critical

created:\>=2026-01-01

modified:\<2026-06-01

future custom fields

Field searches shall be extensible through Search Providers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility-Aware Search

The Universal Search Framework shall understand common accessibility\
terminology.

Searches shall automatically include recognized synonymous terminology
where\
appropriate.

Examples include:

Alt Text

Alternative Text

Text Alternative

Image Description

Accessible Name

Label

Form Label

aria-label

aria-labelledby

Keyboard Trap

Focus Trap

Trapped Focus

Heading

Heading Level

Heading Structure

H1

H2

H3

Additional accessibility terminology may be introduced without
requiring\
architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Standards Intelligence

### Part 4 – Search Indexing, Search Providers & Result Generation

### Overview

Implement the Search Indexing Framework.

The Search Indexing Framework shall maintain searchable indexes for all\
registered Search Providers.

The Universal Search Framework shall retrieve search results from
indexed\
content whenever practical.

Indexes shall remain transparent to users and shall automatically
remain\
synchronized with Project Workspace resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Index Architecture

The Universal Search Framework shall maintain one or more searchable
indexes.

Indexes shall support:

Full-text content

Metadata

Accessibility Standards

Commands

Relationships

Tags

Keywords

Document properties

Future searchable content

Indexes shall remain extensible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Incremental Indexing

Search indexes shall update automatically whenever searchable content
changes.

Examples include:

Report created

Report modified

Report deleted

Project Asset added

Project Asset modified

Project Asset removed

Template updated

Help documentation updated

Accessibility Standards updated

Plugin resources added

Future searchable resources

Only affected resources shall be re-indexed whenever practical.

Full index rebuilds shall not be required for routine edits.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Background Indexing

Index updates shall occur in the background.

Background indexing shall:

Avoid interrupting user workflows.

Avoid blocking the user interface.

Minimize unnecessary resource usage.

Remain responsive while indexing.

Background indexing progress shall be available to users when
appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Providers

Every searchable subsystem shall register a Search Provider.

Examples include:

Plugin Search Providers

Future Integration Search Providers

or\
plugin initialization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

using a\
standardized registration mechanism.

Registration shall expose:

Provider Name

Provider Description

Supported Search Categories

Supported Search Scopes

Supported Metadata

Supported Query Features

Supported Navigation

Supported Preview Types

Supported Capabilities

Future provider metadata

Duplicate registrations shall be prevented.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Provider Capabilities

Capabilities may include:

Full-text Search

Metadata Search

Boolean Search

Wildcard Search

Phrase Search

Accessibility Metadata

Result Preview

Exact Navigation

Filtering

Ranking Hints

Future capabilities

capabilities.

within the active search scope.

Providers.

### Part 5 – Unified Search Results Framework, Navigation & Accessibility

### Overview

Implement a reusable Search Results Framework for the Universal Search\

developed for the Menu Bar Command Search.

### Unified Search Results Framework

The Search Results Framework shall be the single reusable search
results\

Command Palette

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Help Documentation

User Guide

Current Report Search

Current Project Workspace Search

Project Asset Search

Dashboard Search

Future Plugin Search Providers

Future Integration Search Providers

Future Desktop Application

Any future search experience introduced within ART

All search experiences shall share identical interaction patterns,\
accessibility behavior, and navigation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Implementation Requirements

Do not implement a separate search results component.

Identify the existing Search Results Framework implemented for the Menu
Bar\
Command Search.

Refactor the implementation where necessary so that every search
experience\
consumes the same reusable Search Results Framework.

Extend the framework rather than duplicating functionality.

Future enhancements shall automatically benefit every search experience.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Result Presentation

Search results shall be presented in a consistent format.

Each result shall display, where applicable:

Result Title

Result Type

opened.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

highlighted.

The destination resource shall open automatically.

Keyboard focus shall move directly to the first matching occurrence.

The active occurrence shall remain highlighted.

Users shall be able to navigate among additional matches.

Highlighting shall remain visible until:

A new search begins.

The user clears highlighting.

### Bidirectional Navigation

The Search Results Framework shall support bidirectional navigation.

Users shall be able to:

Return to the original search results.

Move to the next search result.

Move to the previous search result.

Move to the next occurrence.

Move to the previous occurrence.

Resume searching without losing context.

The user's search query shall remain available throughout the search
session.

## Epic 30 – Global Context Menu Framework

### Part 1 – Overview, Objectives & Architecture

### Overview

Implement a reusable Global Context Menu Framework for ART.

The Global Context Menu Framework shall provide a single, consistent,\
accessible, extensible, and context-aware mechanism for presenting\
context-specific commands throughout the application.

The framework shall replace all hard-coded context menus.

Every context menu in ART shall consume the Global Context Menu
Framework.

Future plugins, integrations, desktop editions, and application modules
shall\
reuse this framework without requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application functionality.

Preserve all existing keyboard accessibility.

Preserve all existing screen reader support.

Preserve all existing voice navigation support.

Preserve all existing speech dictation support.

Preserve all existing Application Command Framework functionality.

Preserve all existing Keyboard Shortcut Manager functionality.

Preserve all existing Command Palette functionality.

Preserve all existing Menu Bar functionality.

Preserve all existing Menu Bar Command Search functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Framework Objectives

The Global Context Menu Framework shall:

Provide context-sensitive commands.

Present commands consistently throughout ART.

Consume the Application Command Framework.

Determine available commands using Context Providers.

Support keyboard, mouse, touch, voice, braille, and switch device users.

Remain fully accessible.

Remain fully extensible.

Remain implementation-independent.

Support future plugins and integrations.

Support future desktop editions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Global Context Menu Framework

Implement a reusable Global Context Menu Framework.

The framework shall:

Determine the current application context.

Retrieve available commands.

Organize commands logically.

Generate context menus dynamically.

Present context menus consistently.

Execute commands through the Application Command Framework.

Future application features shall consume this framework rather than
creating\
independent context menu implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Implementation Requirements

Do not hard-code context menu contents.

Do not duplicate Application Command implementations.

Do not duplicate command logic.

Do not duplicate accessibility implementations.

Do not create multiple context menu frameworks.

All context menus shall consume the reusable Global Context Menu
Framework.

Future enhancements to the framework shall automatically benefit every
context\
menu throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Application Command Framework Integration

Every context menu command shall be an Application Command.

Context menus shall never directly execute application logic.

Instead:

The Global Context Menu Framework shall invoke the corresponding
registered\
Application Command.

The Application Command Framework shall determine:

Command availability

Command enabled state

Command execution

Keyboard shortcuts

Voice activation

Future integrations

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context Awareness

The Global Context Menu Framework shall determine the user's current\
programmatic context before generating a context menu.

Examples include:

Dashboard

Dashboard Widget

Current Report

Report Builder

Report Viewer

Editor

Progress Log

Project Workspace

Project Asset

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Search Results

Help Documentation

User Guide

Application Settings

Welcome Screen

Future plugins

Future integrations

Future desktop components

Commands shall appear only when applicable to the active context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context Providers

Implement Context Providers.

Context Providers shall determine which Application Commands are
available for\
the current context.

Examples include:

Dashboard Context Provider

Dashboard Widget Context Provider

Project Workspace Context Provider

Report Builder Context Provider

Editor Context Provider

Report Viewer Context Provider

Progress Log Context Provider

Accessibility Lookup Context Provider

Help Context Provider

Search Results Context Provider

Settings Context Provider

Plugin Context Providers

Future Context Providers

Context Providers shall register automatically during application
startup or\
plugin initialization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Menu Generation

Context menus shall be generated dynamically.

Menu contents shall be determined by:

Current context

Current selection

Current keyboard focus

Current application state

Command availability

Command enabled state

Plugin contributions

Future integration contributions

Users shall never encounter irrelevant commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Supported Invocation Methods

The Global Context Menu Framework shall support:

Mouse right-click

Shift+F10

Applications/Menu key

Touch and hold

Voice navigation

Speech dictation

Windows Voice Access

Dragon NaturallySpeaking

Apple Voice Control

Screen reader context menu commands

Braille display commands

Switch devices

Future platform-specific invocation methods

Every invocation method shall produce the same context menu for the
same\
application context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Requirements

The Global Context Menu Framework shall fully support:

Keyboard-only operation

JAWS

NVDA

VoiceOver

TalkBack

Braille displays

Voice navigation

Speech dictation

Switch devices

High contrast themes

Reduced motion

ART personalization settings

Every context menu shall expose appropriate accessible names, roles,
states,\
and properties where applicable.

Context menus shall never introduce keyboard traps.

Focus shall remain predictable before, during, and after menu
interaction.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Voice Interaction

Every context menu command shall expose a stable, descriptive accessible
name\
suitable for voice activation.

Voice users shall be able to:

Open context menus.

Navigate menu items.

Expand submenus.

Collapse submenus.

Activate commands.

Dismiss menus.

Future voice technologies shall integrate without architectural
redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The Global Context Menu Framework shall support future:

Plugin-defined context menus

Integration-defined context menus

Organization-specific commands

Desktop application menus

Artificial Intelligence features

Developer extensions

Cloud integrations

Additional interaction methods

No architectural redesign shall be required.

### Part 2 – Context Providers, Command Registration, Command Groups & Menu Generation

### Overview

Implement the Context Provider Framework.

Context Providers shall determine which Application Commands are
available for\
the current application context.

The Global Context Menu Framework shall consume Context Providers to
generate\
context-sensitive menus dynamically.

Context Providers shall never execute application logic directly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context Provider Responsibilities

Every Context Provider shall:

Identify the current application context.

Determine the current selection.

Determine the current keyboard focus.

Determine the current application state.

Determine which Application Commands are applicable.

Determine command availability.

Determine command enabled state.

Provide command grouping information.

Provide command ordering information.

Provide submenu information.

Provide future metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context Provider Registration

Every Context Provider shall register with the Global Context Menu
Framework.

Registration shall expose:

Provider Name

Provider Description

Supported Context

Supported Commands

Supported Command Groups

Supported Submenus

Supported Priorities

Supported Selection Types

Future capabilities

Duplicate registrations shall not be permitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Built-in Context Providers

Implement Context Providers for:

Dashboard

Dashboard Widget

Project Workspace

Project Assets

Report Builder

Field Configuration

Editor

Report Viewer

Progress Log

Accessibility Lookup Tool

Search Results

Help Documentation

User Guide

Welcome Screen

Application Settings

Menu Bar

Command Palette

Menu Bar Command Search

Future application modules

Future plugins

Future integrations

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Application Command Registration

Every context menu item shall be a registered Application Command.

Context menu items shall never execute application logic directly.

Commands shall execute exclusively through the Application Command
Framework.

No duplicate command implementations shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Command Availability

Commands shall appear only when:

The current context supports the command.

The command has been registered.

The command is currently available.

The current selection supports the command.

The current application state supports the command.

The current user workflow permits the command.

Commands that are unavailable shall not be displayed unless
intentionally\
presented in a disabled state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Enabled and Disabled Commands

The Global Context Menu Framework shall determine whether each command
is:

Enabled

Disabled

Hidden

Unavailable

Disabled commands shall remain accessible to assistive technologies.

Disabled commands shall clearly communicate why they are unavailable
whenever\
practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Command Groups

Commands shall be organized into logical Command Groups.

Examples include:

Workspace

Project

Reports

Editor

Progress Log

Validation

Accessibility

Export

Import

Clipboard

Navigation

Search

Dashboard

Templates

View

Tools

Settings

Help

Future plugin groups

Future integration groups

Additional Command Groups may be registered without architectural
redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Automatic Menu Organization

The Global Context Menu Framework shall automatically organize commands
into\
their appropriate Command Groups.

Application developers shall not manually construct context menus.

The framework shall:

Create group headings where appropriate.

Insert separators automatically.

Maintain consistent ordering.

Maintain consistent spacing.

Maintain consistent accessibility behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Command Priorities

Every Application Command shall expose a priority.

Examples include:

Critical

Primary

Secondary

Advanced

Administrative

Future priorities

Priority shall influence command placement within each Command Group.

Commands shall remain consistently ordered throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Submenu Registration

Commands may optionally register within submenus.

Examples include:

Export \>

Import \>

Open Recent \>

Templates \>

Reports \>

Accessibility Standards \>

Project Assets \>

Dashboard \>

View \>

Developer Tools \>

Future plugin menus \>

Submenus shall remain optional.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dynamic Menu Generation

The Global Context Menu Framework shall dynamically generate menus
using:

Registered Context Providers

Registered Application Commands

Current application context

Current keyboard focus

Current selection

Current application state

Registered plugins

Future integrations

Menus shall never contain hard-coded command lists.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Selection Awareness

Context Providers shall understand the current selection.

Examples include:

No selection

Single selection

Multiple selection

Text selection

Report selection

Project selection

Dashboard Widget selection

Search Result selection

Project Asset selection

Future selection types

Menu contents shall adapt appropriately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Focus Awareness

Context Providers shall determine the current programmatic focus.

Examples include:

Focused control

Focused widget

Focused editor

Focused report

Focused search result

Focused Project Asset

Focused dashboard card

Future controls

Focus shall determine which context menu is presented.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### State Awareness

Context Providers shall consider current application state.

Examples include:

Read-only

Edit mode

Preview mode

Validation mode

Progress Log editing enabled

Workspace loaded

Workspace not loaded

Report open

No report open

Future application states

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context Menu Lifecycle

Every context menu shall follow a standardized lifecycle.

Determine context.

Determine selection.

Determine focus.

Retrieve applicable Context Provider.

Retrieve registered commands.

Evaluate availability.

Evaluate priorities.

Organize Command Groups.

Generate submenus.

Generate accessibility information.

Display menu.

Execute selected command.

Dismiss menu.

Restore focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility

Context Providers shall generate identical context menus regardless of
the\
invocation method.

Right-click

Shift+F10

Applications/Menu key

Touch and hold

Voice navigation

Speech dictation

Screen reader commands

Braille display commands

Switch devices

Future interaction methods

Every invocation method shall expose identical commands, ordering, and\
accessibility behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The Context Provider Framework shall support future:

Plugin-defined Context Providers

Integration-defined Context Providers

Organization-specific Context Providers

Desktop application Context Providers

Artificial Intelligence Context Providers

Developer extensions

Additional interaction methods

No architectural redesign shall be required.

### Part 4 – Menu Interaction, Keyboard Navigation, Focus Management & Accessibility

### Overview

Implement a standardized interaction model for the Global Context Menu\
Framework.

Every context menu shall behave consistently regardless of where or how
it is\
invoked.

The interaction model shall remain predictable, accessible, and
compatible\
with standard operating system conventions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Menu Invocation

The Global Context Menu Framework shall support invocation using:

Mouse right-click

Shift+F10

Applications/Menu key

Touch and hold

Voice navigation

Speech dictation

Windows Voice Access

Dragon NaturallySpeaking

Apple Voice Control

Screen reader context menu commands

Braille display commands

Switch devices

Future platform-specific interaction methods

Regardless of the invocation method, the same context menu shall be
displayed\
for the same application context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Menu Positioning

The context menu shall appear adjacent to the location where it was
invoked.

When practical:

Mouse invocation shall position the menu near the pointer.

Keyboard invocation shall position the menu adjacent to the focused
control or\
selection.

Touch invocation shall position the menu adjacent to the touch location.

Voice invocation shall position the menu adjacent to the
programmatically\
focused element.

The menu shall never appear partially off-screen.

If necessary, the framework shall automatically reposition the menu to
ensure\
that it remains fully visible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Navigation

Every context menu shall support:

Up Arrow

Down Arrow

Left Arrow

Right Arrow

Home

End

Enter

Space

Escape

Applications/Menu key

Shift+F10

Type-ahead navigation

Future standard keyboard navigation

Keyboard behavior shall remain consistent throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Behavior

Up Arrow

Move to the previous menu item.

Down Arrow

Move to the next menu item.

Home

Move to the first enabled menu item.

End

Move to the last enabled menu item.

Right Arrow

Open the currently selected submenu.

If no submenu exists, no action shall occur.

Left Arrow

Close the current submenu.

If already within the top-level menu, no action shall occur.

Enter

Execute the currently selected Application Command.

Space

Execute the currently selected Application Command when appropriate.

Escape

Dismiss the currently open context menu regardless of how it was
invoked.

Escape shall behave consistently throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Type-Ahead Navigation

While a context menu is open:

Typing printable characters shall move focus to the next menu item
whose\
visible text begins with the typed characters.

Repeated typing shall continue cycling through matching menu items.

Type-ahead searching shall remain fully accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Submenu Behavior

Submenus shall:

Open using the Right Arrow key.

Close using the Left Arrow key.

Open using pointer interaction.

Remain open while navigating within the submenu.

Close automatically when focus returns to the parent menu.

Nested submenus shall behave consistently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Menu Dismissal

The Global Context Menu shall always be dismissed by:

Escape

Selecting a command

Pointer activation outside the menu

Touch interaction outside the menu

Voice dismissal command

Future platform-standard dismissal methods

Menu dismissal shall never leave keyboard focus undefined.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Focus Management

Before opening a context menu, ART shall preserve the current
programmatic\
focus.

After the context menu is dismissed without executing a command:

Focus shall return to the element that had focus immediately before the
menu\
was opened.

After executing a command:

Focus shall move according to the behavior of the executed Application
Command.

Focus movement shall remain logical, sequential, and predictable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Context Preservation

Opening a context menu shall not change:

The active project.

The active report.

The active widget.

The active selection.

The active search session.

The active editing state.

Future application state.

Only execution of an Application Command may change application state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessible Semantics

Every context menu shall expose appropriate semantics.

Where applicable, menus shall expose:

menu

menuitem

menuitemcheckbox

menuitemradio

separator

group

submenu

Appropriate accessible names, roles, states, and properties shall be
exposed\
for every menu element.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessible Names

Every menu item shall expose:

A stable accessible name.

A meaningful accessible description where appropriate.

The associated keyboard shortcut, when one exists.

The current enabled or disabled state.

The current checked state, where applicable.

The current expanded or collapsed state for submenu items.

Accessible names shall be suitable for both screen reader users and
voice\
control users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Live Region Announcements

Where appropriate, assistive technologies shall be notified when:

A context menu opens.

A submenu opens.

A submenu closes.

A command becomes unavailable.

A command becomes available.

A command executes successfully.

Future significant menu events occur.

Announcements shall be concise and shall not overwhelm users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Screen Reader Compatibility

The Global Context Menu Framework shall fully support:

JAWS

NVDA

VoiceOver

TalkBack

Future screen readers

Screen reader users shall receive equivalent information regardless of
the\
context in which the menu is invoked.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Voice Navigation

Context menus shall support:

Voice navigation.

Speech dictation.

Windows Voice Access.

Dragon NaturallySpeaking.

Apple Voice Control.

Future voice technologies.

Voice users shall be able to:

Open context menus.

Navigate menu items.

Expand submenus.

Collapse submenus.

Execute commands.

Dismiss menus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Braille Display Support

Context menus shall fully support refreshable braille displays.

Braille users shall be able to:

Open menus.

Navigate menu items.

Expand submenus.

Collapse submenus.

Execute commands.

Dismiss menus.

Braille output shall accurately reflect the current menu state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Touch Support

Touch users shall be able to:

Open context menus using touch-and-hold.

Navigate menus.

Open submenus.

Activate commands.

Dismiss menus.

Touch interaction shall remain consistent with platform conventions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### High Contrast & Personalization

Context menus shall fully support:

High contrast themes.

Reduced motion.

Display Spacing preferences.

Theme personalization.

Future accessibility personalization settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Error Prevention

The Global Context Menu Framework shall prevent:

Duplicate menu items.

Duplicate separators.

Empty submenus.

Empty command groups.

Orphaned submenus.

Inaccessible menu items.

Keyboard traps.

Unexpected focus movement.

Future menu inconsistencies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Compatibility

The interaction model shall support future:

Plugin-defined menus.

Integration-defined menus.

Desktop application menus.

Organization-specific commands.

Artificial Intelligence interactions.

Developer extensions.

Additional input technologies.

No architectural redesign shall be required.

### Part 5 – Customization, Extensibility & Framework Integration

### Overview

Implement customization and extensibility support for the Global Context
Menu\
Framework.

The framework shall allow ART, future plugins, future integrations, and
future\
desktop editions to contribute commands without modifying existing
context menu\
implementations.

The framework shall remain reusable, configurable, and implementation\
independent.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### User Customization

The architecture shall support future user customization of context
menus.

Future customization options may include:

Show or hide individual commands.

Show or hide command groups.

Pin frequently used commands.

Reorder command groups.

Restore default layouts.

Future personalization options.

User customization is outside the scope of Version 2.0.

### Part 7 – Menu Navigation, Command Search & Universal Menu Behavior

### Overview

Implement standardized navigation behavior for every menu throughout
ART.

This includes:

Menu Bar

Menus

Submenus

Global Context Menus

Future desktop menus

Future plugin menus

Future integration menus

All menus shall exhibit identical keyboard interaction, search
behavior,\
accessibility behavior, and focus management.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Universal Menu Navigation

Every menu shall support continuous keyboard navigation.

Pressing:

Down Arrow on the final menu item shall move focus to the first menu
item.

Up Arrow on the first menu item shall move focus to the final menu item.

For horizontal menus, including the Menu Bar:

Right Arrow on the final top-level menu shall move focus to the first\
top-level menu.

Left Arrow on the first top-level menu shall move focus to the final\
top-level menu.

Menus shall never contain keyboard dead ends.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Incremental Type Navigation

Every menu shall support Incremental Type Navigation.

Typing one or more printable characters shall move focus to the next
menu item\
whose visible text begins with the typed character sequence.

Examples:

Typing:

S

May move focus to:

Save Report

Typing:

S

again shall move focus to:

Save Report As…

Typing:

SP

shall move focus to:

Spell Check

Typing:

ST

shall move focus to:

Statistics

Typing characters shall never execute commands.

Commands shall execute only through explicit user activation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Search Commands

Every context menu shall include a **Search Commands…** command
positioned at\
the bottom of the menu, separated from the preceding commands by a
separator.

Selecting **Search Commands…** shall invoke the existing Menu Bar
Command\
Search or the user's configured command search interface.

The search interface shall automatically be scoped to the current
application\
context.

Examples include:

Dashboard commands.

Editor commands.

Report Viewer commands.

Report Builder commands.

Project Workspace commands.

Progress Log commands.

Accessibility Lookup Tool commands.

Plugin commands.

Future contexts.

The **Search Commands…** command shall consume the existing Universal
Search\
Framework and Application Command Framework.

No separate command search implementation shall exist.

Current context.

interface.

## Modification To Epic 30 Context Menu

Modify epic 30. In the global context menu (in all contexts of the ART
interface), the last item in every context menu shall be the Menu Bar
Command Search labeled as "Command Search". The Command Search textbox
shall have all of the same roles, states, properties,and functionality
as the Menu Bar Command Search.

When user invokes the global context menu, user should be able to use
the up and down arrow keys to navigate the options and categories in the
menu. If the context menu is displaying 9 options, then the tenth option
shall be the Command Search textbox. As previously specified, the
Commands Search textbox and functionality shall be the same as the Menu
Bar Command Search textbox and functionality. The global context menu
shall always contain the Commands Search textbox at the bottom of the
context menu and the Commands Search textbox shall not replace any
commands/options/categories in the context menu; the commands search
shall be in addition to the commands/options/categories already
displayed in the context menu. The Commands Search textbox shall not be
located inside a sub menu; it must always be the last item at the bottom
of the parent-level of the global context menu. And, the Commands Search
textbox shall provide users the ability to search for, locate, and
activate commands that may or may not already be available in the global
context menu. This modification shall be available in all areas/contexts
of the ART application interface, both present and future. And, the
Commands Search textbox shall also work with Future commands registered
in the existing Application Command Framework. The embedded Context Menu
Search component defined here shall be available within every present
and future context menus. The Commands Search component in the global
context menu shall support future plugins and future integrations.
