#### Overview

Implement an optional **Explorer Framework** that provides a structured,
accessible, and context-aware navigation experience throughout ART.

The Explorer Framework shall serve as an alternative navigation
interface for users who prefer browsing resources using a hierarchical
view similar to professional desktop applications.

The Explorer shall complement the Dashboard rather than replace it.

The Dashboard shall remain the default workspace view.

The Explorer shall remain completely optional.

Users shall never be required to use the Explorer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Philosophy

The Explorer Framework is intended to provide an efficient navigation
experience for users working with:

- Individual reports

- Project Workspaces

- Progress Logs

- Templates

- Project Assets

- Future plugin resources

- Future integration resources

Unlike traditional file explorers, the Explorer Framework shall present
**resources**, not merely files and folders.

Every item displayed within the Explorer shall represent an ART
Resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Primary Objectives

The Explorer Framework shall:

- Provide a structured navigation experience.

- Complement the Dashboard.

- Adapt automatically to the user's current working context.

- Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

- Remain intuitive for new users.

- Increase productivity for experienced users.

- Never duplicate existing navigation functionality.

- Never require users to organize work using Project Workspaces.

- Scale naturally as ART continues to grow.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Remains the Default

The Dashboard shall remain the default workspace view.

The Dashboard shall continue providing:

- Quick Actions

- Continue Working

- Current Project

- Current Report

- Report Metrics

- Dashboard Widgets

- Notifications

- Recent Activity

- Workspace Summary

- Future Dashboard Widgets

Nothing within this epic shall replace or diminish the Dashboard
experience.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer is Optional

The Explorer shall function as an alternative workspace view.

Users may:

- Use only the Dashboard.

- Use only the Explorer.

- Switch between both as desired.

Users shall never be required to interact with the Explorer.

All ART functionality shall remain available regardless of the currently
selected workspace view.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Workspace Views

ART shall support two primary workspace views.

- Dashboard

- Explorer

Only one workspace view shall be active at any time.

Changing workspace views shall not:

- Modify report data.

- Modify project data.

- Modify user settings.

- Modify report presentation.

- Modify report order.

Changing workspace views shall only affect how navigation information is
presented.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### View Switching

Users shall be able to switch between Dashboard and Explorer using:

- View menu

- Global Context Menu

- Command Palette

- Menu Bar Command Search

- Voice commands

- Optional keyboard shortcut

- Future interaction methods

All view switching shall consume the Application Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Commands

The following Application Commands shall be registered.

- Show Dashboard

- Show Explorer

- Toggle Workspace View

Future workspace views shall register additional Application Commands
using the same framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Settings

Application Settings shall include a new category.

##### Workspace View

Users shall be able to configure:

###### Default Workspace View

Options:

- Dashboard (Default)

- Explorer

------------------------------------------------------------------------

###### Remember Last Workspace View

When enabled:

ART shall restore the previously active workspace view during startup.

When disabled:

ART shall always open using the configured Default Workspace View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### View Menu

The View menu shall include:

Workspace View \>

    ● Dashboard

    ○ Explorer

Dashboard and Explorer shall be implemented as accessible radio menu
items.

Exactly one workspace view shall always be selected.

Changing the selected radio item shall immediately switch workspace
views.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Global Context Menu

The Global Context Menu shall include:

Workspace View \>

    ● Dashboard

    ○ Explorer

The submenu shall:

- Display the active workspace view.

- Display an accessible and visible check indicator.

- Consume the Application Command Framework.

- Consume the Global Context Menu Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcuts

Workspace View commands shall be exposed through:

Keyboard Shortcut Manager.

No default keyboard shortcut shall be assigned.

Users may optionally assign keyboard shortcuts.

Keyboard shortcuts shall automatically appear within:

- Menus

- Context Menus

- Command Palette

- Menu Bar Command Search

- Help documentation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Navigation

Workspace view commands shall support:

Voice Access.

Dragon NaturallySpeaking.

Apple Voice Control.

Future voice navigation systems.

Examples include:

> 

Show Dashboard

> 

Show Explorer

> 

Switch Workspace View

Voice navigation shall consume the Application Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Integration

The Explorer Framework shall consume the existing Window Title
Framework.

The Explorer shall not implement an independent window title
implementation.

Window titles shall continue following the standardized ART window title
format already defined by previous epics.

Future Report Views, including Working Views, shall inherit this same
Window Title Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Architecture

The Explorer Framework shall consume:

- Application Command Framework

- Universal Search Framework

- Keyboard Shortcut Manager

- Window Title Framework

- Dashboard Widget Framework

- Project Workspace Framework

- Global Context Menu Framework

- Accessibility Framework

- Future Report Views Framework

- Future Plugin Framework

- Future Integration Framework

The Explorer shall never duplicate functionality already provided by
these frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Architecture Principles

The Explorer Framework shall be:

- Context-aware

- Resource-based

- Framework-driven

- Extensible

- Accessible

- Keyboard-first

- Voice-friendly

- Screen reader friendly

- Braille friendly

- Modular

- Plugin-ready

- Integration-ready

- Future-proof

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing functionality.

Preserve all existing keyboard accessibility.

Preserve all existing screen reader accessibility.

Preserve all existing voice navigation support.

Preserve all existing refreshable braille support.

Preserve all existing personalization settings.

Preserve all existing Dashboard functionality.

Preserve all existing Project Workspace functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not create duplicate implementations of existing functionality.

The Explorer Framework shall become the reusable navigation foundation
for future ART features while remaining completely optional for users
who prefer the Dashboard.

### Part 2 – Resource Model, Context Awareness & Explorer Organization

#### Overview

The Explorer Framework shall organize information using a
**resource-based architecture** rather than a traditional file and
folder model.

Every item displayed within the Explorer shall represent an ART
Resource.

The Explorer shall automatically adapt its contents according to the
user's current working context.

The Explorer shall never display unnecessary, irrelevant, or empty
resource groups.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource-Based Architecture

The Explorer shall operate using Resources.

A Resource is any navigable object managed by ART.

Examples include:

- Project Workspace
- Report
- Executive Summary
- Audit Log
- Progress Log
- Project Asset
- Template
- Saved Search
- Dashboard Layout
- Report Configuration
- Export Configuration
- Plugin Resource
- Integration Resource
- Future Resource Types

Future Resource Types shall be able to register with the Explorer
without requiring modifications to the Explorer Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Metadata

Every Resource shall expose metadata appropriate to its Resource Type.

Examples include:

- Resource Name
- Resource Description
- Resource Type
- Date Created
- Last Modified
- Author (if available)
- Current Status
- Associated Project Workspace
- Associated Report
- Associated Progress Log
- Associated Template
- Associated Plugin
- Associated Integration
- Future metadata

Explorer shall consume existing metadata rather than maintaining
duplicate information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Awareness

The Explorer shall automatically adapt according to the user's current
working context.

Users shall never be required to manually switch Explorer modes.

Explorer shall determine its contents automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Context

When no Project Workspace or report is open, the Explorer shall display
application-level resources.

Examples include:

``` text
Explorer

Recent Reports

Recent Project Workspaces

Templates

Favorites

Saved Searches

Recent Project Assets

Recently Imported Resources

Recently Exported Resources
```

The application context shall provide quick access to commonly used
resources without requiring users to first open a Project Workspace.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Context

When a report is open without an associated Project Workspace, the
Explorer shall display only resources associated with that report.

Example:

``` text
Explorer

AuditLog.ARTAudit

├── Report Metadata
├── Findings
├── Attachments
├── Linked Accessibility Standards
├── Report Configuration
├── Export Options
└── Report Properties
```

The Explorer shall not display Project Workspace resources when no
Project Workspace is open.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Project Workspace Context

When a Project Workspace is open, the Explorer shall automatically
transition into Project Workspace mode.

Example:

``` text
Explorer

City of Yakima Audit

├── Reports
├── Progress Logs
├── Project Assets
├── Templates
├── Saved Searches
├── Dashboard Layouts
└── Favorites
```

The Project Workspace context shall replace the application context
automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Progress Log Context

When a Progress Log is the active resource, the Explorer shall display
resources associated with that Progress Log.

Examples include:

- Progress Log Metadata
- Evaluation Items
- Attachments
- Linked Reports
- Associated Project Workspace
- Export Options
- Properties

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Template Context

When editing or viewing a template, the Explorer shall display resources
associated with that template.

Examples include:

- Template Metadata
- Associated Reports
- Template Properties
- Version History
- Export Options

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Project Asset Context

When a Project Asset is active, the Explorer shall display resources
associated with that asset.

Examples include:

- Asset Information
- Associated Project Workspace
- Linked Reports
- Read-only Preview
- Properties

Project Assets shall remain read-only within ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Results Context

When Explorer Search or Universal Search displays search results, the
Explorer shall temporarily adapt to display the matching resources.

The search results shall become the active navigation context.

Clearing the search shall automatically restore the previous Explorer
context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Contexts

The Explorer Framework shall support additional contexts including:

- Plugin Resources
- Integration Resources
- Collaboration Resources
- Review Resources
- Assignment Resources
- AI-generated Resources
- Future application contexts

No architectural redesign shall be required to support future contexts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dynamic Organization

Explorer shall display only resource groups relevant to the current
context.

Empty resource groups shall not be displayed.

Examples:

If no Project Assets exist:

The **Project Assets** section shall not appear.

If no Templates exist:

The **Templates** section shall not appear.

If no Saved Searches exist:

The **Saved Searches** section shall not appear.

Explorer shall remain concise and relevant.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Empty States

When no resources exist within a supported category, Explorer shall
provide meaningful guidance instead of displaying an empty hierarchy.

Example:

``` text
Project Assets

No Project Assets have been added.

Use Add Project Asset to attach planning documents,
contracts, timelines, credentials, screenshots,
or other supporting documentation.
```

Explorer shall never display meaningless placeholder nodes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Hierarchy

Explorer shall present resources using a logical hierarchy.

Example:

``` text
Project Workspace

├── Reports
├── Progress Logs
├── Project Assets
├── Templates
├── Saved Searches
├── Dashboard Layouts
└── Favorites
```

Each Resource shall appear only once within its parent hierarchy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Status

Explorer may display optional status indicators.

Examples include:

- Validation Complete
- Validation Required
- Modified
- Read-only
- Imported
- Export Pending
- Needs Review
- Missing Attachment
- Future status indicators

Status indicators shall supplement, not replace, accessible text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Badges

Explorer may display optional informational badges.

Examples include:

Audit Log

``` text
143 Findings
```

Progress Log

``` text
12 Evaluation Items
```

Project Workspace

``` text
8 Reports
```

Project Assets

``` text
17 Assets
```

Badges shall be exposed programmatically to assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Properties

Every Resource shall expose a Properties command.

Examples include:

- Workspace Properties
- Report Properties
- Progress Log Properties
- Project Asset Properties
- Template Properties
- Plugin Resource Properties
- Integration Resource Properties
- Future Resource Properties

Properties shall consume the Application Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites

Users shall be able to designate Resources as Favorites.

Favorites shall remain available regardless of the current Explorer
context.

Removing a Favorite shall never delete the underlying Resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recent Resources

Explorer shall maintain lists of recently accessed Resources.

Examples include:

- Recent Reports
- Recent Project Workspaces
- Recent Project Assets
- Recent Templates
- Recent Saved Searches

Recent Resources shall automatically update as users work within ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Explorer shall expose:

- Appropriate accessible names
- Appropriate accessible descriptions
- Appropriate roles
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties

The Resource hierarchy shall be communicated correctly to assistive
technologies.

Status indicators and badges shall be available to screen readers and
refreshable braille displays.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing accessibility.

Preserve all existing keyboard navigation.

Preserve all existing voice navigation.

Preserve all existing refreshable braille support.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate existing metadata or business logic.

The Explorer Framework shall provide a clean, context-aware navigation
experience while remaining simple for users who choose to enable it.

### Part 3 – Explorer User Interface, Navigation & Resource Activation

#### Explorer User Interface

The Explorer shall present resources using a clean, hierarchical
navigation interface that remains simple for new users while scaling to
support complex Project Workspaces.

The Explorer shall consume the existing ART visual design system.

The Explorer shall support all application themes, personalization
settings, Display Spacing settings, and future appearance options.

The Explorer shall not duplicate functionality already provided by other
ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Layout

The Explorer shall display a hierarchical resource tree.

Resources may contain child resources.

Parent resources shall expose Expand and Collapse functionality.

Child resources shall appear visually nested beneath their parent
resource.

The Explorer shall automatically size itself according to the selected
application layout.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Headings

Each major resource grouping shall include a visible heading.

Examples include:

- Reports
- Progress Logs
- Project Assets
- Templates
- Saved Searches
- Dashboard Layouts
- Favorites

Heading levels shall remain logically nested within the Explorer.

The Explorer shall never skip heading levels.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Expand and Collapse

Resources containing child resources shall expose an Expand/Collapse
control.

Users shall be able to:

- Expand a resource.
- Collapse a resource.
- Expand all child resources (where applicable).
- Collapse all child resources (where applicable).

Expand/Collapse state shall be exposed programmatically to assistive
technologies.

The Expand/Collapse control shall not activate the resource itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Navigation

Users shall be able to navigate the Explorer using:

- Keyboard
- Mouse
- Touch
- Refreshable braille displays
- Screen readers
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Future interaction methods

Explorer navigation shall remain consistent with navigation throughout
ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Navigation

The Explorer shall support:

- Up Arrow
- Down Arrow
- Left Arrow
- Right Arrow
- Home
- End
- Page Up
- Page Down
- Enter
- Space
- Applications key
- Shift+F10
- Escape
- First-letter navigation

Navigation shall consume the same keyboard interaction model used
throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### First-Letter Navigation

Typing one or more letters while the Explorer has keyboard focus shall
move focus to the next visible resource whose name begins with the typed
characters.

Typing the same letter repeatedly shall cycle through matching
resources.

Typing shall never activate a resource.

Users shall activate resources explicitly using Enter, Space, mouse,
touch, voice, or another supported activation method.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Circular Navigation

Explorer navigation shall wrap continuously.

When keyboard focus reaches the final visible resource:

Pressing Down Arrow shall move focus to the first visible resource.

When keyboard focus reaches the first visible resource:

Pressing Up Arrow shall move focus to the final visible resource.

This behavior shall remain consistent with ART's Menu Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Selection

Selecting a resource shall not automatically activate it.

Selection and activation shall remain separate actions.

Selection shall expose the currently selected resource to assistive
technologies.

Only one resource shall be selected at a time unless future
functionality explicitly supports multi-selection.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Activation

Resources may be activated using:

- Enter
- Double-click
- Touch
- Voice command
- Braille display routing keys
- Switch device
- Future interaction methods

Activation shall invoke the appropriate Application Command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Actions

Depending on the selected resource type, activation may:

- Open the resource.
- Preview the resource.
- Navigate to the resource.
- Display Properties.
- Launch the associated editor.
- Launch the associated viewer.
- Invoke another ART framework.

Explorer shall never contain resource-specific business logic.

All actions shall consume the Application Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Preview Support

Where supported, resources may expose a Preview action.

Preview shall allow users to inspect a resource without fully opening
it.

Preview shall consume the existing Viewer Framework whenever possible.

Project Assets shall remain read-only when previewed within ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Management

When a resource is activated:

Keyboard focus shall move directly to the primary interactive element
associated with the activated resource.

Examples include:

- First editable field
- First finding
- Report heading
- Viewer heading
- Properties dialog
- Preview pane

Focus shall never be lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Returning Focus

When the user closes an activated resource:

Keyboard focus shall return to the originating resource within the
Explorer whenever possible.

If the originating resource no longer exists:

Focus shall move to the nearest logical resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Icons

Each Resource Type may display an icon.

Icons shall supplement, not replace, accessible text.

Icons shall never convey information that is unavailable through
accessible names or descriptions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Badges

Resources may display optional badges indicating information such as:

- Number of findings
- Number of evaluation items
- Number of child resources
- Validation status
- Modified status
- Read-only status
- Future resource metadata

Badges shall be exposed programmatically to assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Explorer shall expose:

- Appropriate roles
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties
- Accessible names
- Accessible descriptions

Parent resources shall expose their expanded or collapsed state.

Selected resources shall expose their selected state.

Keyboard focus shall remain clearly visible.

Screen readers shall announce resource hierarchy correctly.

Refreshable braille displays shall expose the same structural
information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve existing keyboard accessibility.

Preserve existing screen reader accessibility.

Preserve existing voice navigation support.

Preserve existing refreshable braille support.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate existing navigation functionality.

The Explorer shall provide a predictable, efficient, and fully
accessible navigation experience for every supported interaction method.

### Part 4 – Workspace Views, View Switching & Explorer Personalization

#### Workspace Views

ART shall support two primary workspace views:

- Dashboard
- Explorer

Exactly one workspace view shall be active at any time.

Switching between workspace views shall affect only the navigation
interface.

Switching workspace views shall never:

- Modify report content.
- Modify Project Workspace content.
- Modify report presentation.
- Modify report ordering.
- Modify report settings.
- Modify user data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard View

Dashboard shall remain the default workspace view.

Dashboard View shall continue providing:

- Continue Working
- Quick Actions
- Current Project
- Current Report
- Report Metrics
- Dashboard Widgets
- Notifications
- Recent Activity
- Workspace Summary
- Future Dashboard Widgets

Nothing in this epic shall replace or reduce Dashboard functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer View

Explorer View shall provide an alternative navigation experience.

Explorer shall present resources relevant to the user's current working
context.

Explorer shall never replace the Dashboard.

Explorer shall remain completely optional.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Switching Workspace Views

Users shall be able to switch between Dashboard and Explorer using:

- View menu
- Global Context Menu
- Command Palette
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Voice commands
- Optional keyboard shortcut
- Future interaction methods

All methods shall invoke the same underlying Application Commands.

Separate implementations shall not be created.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Commands

The following Application Commands shall be registered:

- Show Dashboard
- Show Explorer
- Toggle Workspace View

Future workspace views shall register additional Application Commands
using the same framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### View Menu

The View menu shall contain:

``` text
Workspace View >

    ● Dashboard

    ○ Explorer
```

Dashboard and Explorer shall be implemented as accessible radio menu
items.

Exactly one workspace view shall always be selected.

The selected workspace view shall expose the appropriate accessible
checked state.

Changing the selected workspace view shall immediately update the
application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Global Context Menu

The Global Context Menu shall include:

``` text
Workspace View >

    ● Dashboard

    ○ Explorer
```

The submenu shall:

- Display the current workspace view.
- Display a visible check indicator.
- Expose the checked state programmatically.
- Consume the Global Context Menu Framework.
- Consume the Application Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

Users shall be able to execute:

- Show Dashboard
- Show Explorer
- Toggle Workspace View

from the Command Palette.

Command names shall remain consistent throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Command Search Integration

Workspace View commands shall be discoverable using Menu Bar Command
Search.

Examples include:

- Dashboard
- Explorer
- Show Dashboard
- Show Explorer
- Workspace View

Search results shall invoke the same Application Commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcut Manager

Workspace View commands shall appear within Keyboard Shortcut Manager.

No default keyboard shortcuts shall be assigned.

Users may optionally assign custom keyboard shortcuts.

Assigned shortcuts shall automatically appear within:

- Menus
- Context Menus
- Tooltips
- Command Palette
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Help documentation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Navigation

Workspace View commands shall support:

- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Future voice navigation technologies

Example commands include:

- Show Dashboard
- Show Explorer
- Switch Workspace View

Voice commands shall invoke the same Application Commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Settings

Application Settings shall include:

##### Workspace View

Users shall be able to configure:

###### Default Workspace View

Options:

- Dashboard (Default)
- Explorer

------------------------------------------------------------------------

###### Remember Last Workspace View

Options:

- Enabled
- Disabled

When enabled:

ART shall restore the last active workspace view during startup.

When disabled:

ART shall always start using the configured Default Workspace View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Personalization

Users shall be able to personalize Explorer without affecting Dashboard.

Explorer settings may include:

- Show resource icons
- Show resource badges
- Show recent resources
- Show Favorites
- Show Saved Searches
- Automatically expand parent resources
- Restore previous expansion state
- Future Explorer personalization settings

Explorer personalization shall not modify application data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Expansion State

Explorer shall remember the expanded and collapsed state of resources
within the current session.

If the user enables:

**Restore Explorer State**

ART shall restore the previous expansion state when reopening the same
Project Workspace or report.

If disabled:

Explorer shall use its default expansion behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Default Expansion Behavior

Explorer shall intelligently determine which resources should initially
be expanded.

Examples:

Application context:

Only top-level resource groups shall be expanded.

Project Workspace context:

The active resource and its immediate parent hierarchy shall be
expanded.

Report context:

The active report shall be expanded.

Explorer shall avoid overwhelming users with unnecessarily expanded
trees.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Width

Users shall be able to resize the Explorer.

The selected width shall persist between sessions.

Explorer width shall not affect report content or Dashboard layout.

Minimum and maximum widths shall be defined to preserve usability and
accessibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Responsive Layout

Explorer shall adapt to different application sizes.

When horizontal space becomes limited:

Explorer shall remain usable without obscuring report content.

The responsive layout shall preserve:

- Keyboard accessibility
- Screen reader accessibility
- Voice navigation
- Refreshable braille support

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Framework

Explorer shall consume the existing Window Title Framework.

Explorer shall not implement independent window title behavior.

Future Report Views, including Working Views, shall inherit the same
Window Title Framework rather than introducing a separate
implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Workspace View selection shall expose:

- Appropriate roles
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties
- Accessible names
- Accessible descriptions

Radio menu items shall expose their checked state.

Voice navigation shall announce the selected workspace view correctly.

Keyboard focus shall remain predictable when switching views.

Focus shall move to the primary landmark of the newly selected workspace
view.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Dashboard functionality.

Preserve all existing accessibility.

Preserve all existing keyboard navigation.

Preserve all existing voice navigation.

Preserve all existing refreshable braille support.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate Application Command implementations.

Workspace Views shall provide users with two equally capable navigation
experiences while allowing every user to choose the workflow that best
fits their needs.

### Part 5 – Explorer Search & Framework Integration

#### Overview

The Explorer shall include an embedded search component that enables
users to quickly locate Resources within the current Explorer context.

The Explorer shall **not** implement its own search engine.

Instead, Explorer Search shall consume the existing Universal Search
Framework defined in **Epic 29**.

Explorer Search shall function as a context-aware entry point into the
Universal Search Framework while preserving all search capabilities,
accessibility, and extensibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Principles

Explorer Search shall:

- Consume the Universal Search Framework.
- Respect the current Explorer context.
- Produce consistent search results regardless of how search is
  initiated.
- Never duplicate search indexing or search logic.
- Support all existing and future Universal Search features.
- Remain fully accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Component

The Explorer shall include a Search box positioned at the top of the
Explorer.

The Search box shall include:

- Visible label
- Accessible label
- Placeholder text
- Clear Search button
- Search options (when applicable)

The Search box shall consume the existing ART Search Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Scope

Explorer Search shall automatically determine its search scope based on
the current working context.

Examples include:

##### Application Context

When no Project Workspace or report is open:

Search shall include all searchable resources managed by ART.

Examples include:

- Reports
- Project Workspaces
- Templates
- Saved Searches
- Project Assets
- Dashboard Layouts
- Future resources

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Project Workspace Context

When a Project Workspace is open:

Explorer Search shall search only resources belonging to that Project
Workspace.

Examples include:

- Reports
- Progress Logs
- Project Assets
- Templates
- Saved Searches
- Dashboard Layouts
- Future Project Workspace resources

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Report Context

When a report is open outside of a Project Workspace:

Explorer Search shall search only resources associated with that report.

Examples include:

- Findings
- Metadata
- Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Report Configuration
- Export Configuration
- Future report resources

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Future Contexts

Future contexts shall automatically inherit this behavior.

Examples include:

- Plugin Resources
- Integration Resources
- Collaboration Resources
- AI Resources
- Future ART resource types

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Search Features

Explorer Search shall automatically support every capability provided by
the Universal Search Framework.

Including:

- Plain text search
- Phrase search
- Boolean search
- Wildcards
- Prefix matching
- Incremental search
- Fuzzy matching
- Search history
- Saved searches
- Search suggestions
- Future search capabilities

No duplicate implementations shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Boolean Search

Explorer Search shall support Boolean operators defined by the Universal
Search Framework.

Examples include:

``` text
1.3.1 AND Table
```

``` text
Keyboard* NOT Homepage
```

``` text
"Product Owner"
```

``` text
Severity:Critical AND WCAG:1.4.3
```

Explorer Search shall never implement Boolean parsing independently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Incremental Search

Explorer Search shall update results as users type.

Results shall update without requiring the user to activate a Search
button.

Incremental searching shall remain responsive regardless of Project
Workspace size.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Results

Matching Resources shall be displayed within the Explorer hierarchy.

Non-matching Resources may be temporarily hidden.

Search results shall remain clearly distinguishable from the normal
Explorer hierarchy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Highlighting

Matching search terms shall be visually highlighted.

Highlighting shall satisfy all ART accessibility requirements.

Highlighting shall never become the sole means of identifying matching
Resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Activation

Activating a search result shall invoke the appropriate Application
Command.

Examples include:

- Open Report
- Open Project Workspace
- Open Template
- Open Project Asset
- Open Progress Log
- Open Properties
- Future resource actions

Explorer shall never directly implement resource activation logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bidirectional Integration

Explorer Search and Universal Search shall remain fully synchronized.

Searches initiated from Explorer shall produce identical results to
equivalent searches initiated through Universal Search.

Resources opened from Explorer Search shall update:

- Recent Resources
- Search History
- Favorites (where applicable)
- Future search integrations

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search History

Explorer Search shall consume the Universal Search History.

Users shall see the same search history regardless of where searches
were initiated.

Search history shall never be duplicated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Searches

Explorer Search shall provide access to Saved Searches created through
the Universal Search Framework.

Saved Searches shall remain available throughout ART.

Explorer shall not implement an independent Saved Search system.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Commands

Explorer Search shall expose the standard Search Commands context menu.

Examples include:

- Clear Search
- Advanced Search
- Search Options
- Save Search
- Recent Searches
- Search Help

Search Commands shall consume the Application Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Navigation

Users shall be able to:

- Tab to the Search box.
- Type search text.
- Navigate results using Arrow keys.
- Activate results using Enter.
- Open context menus using the Applications key or Shift+F10.
- Exit Search using Escape according to the global Escape behavior.

Explorer Search shall remain fully keyboard accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Navigation

Explorer Search shall support:

- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Future speech technologies

Examples include:

> Focus Explorer Search

> Search for keyboard trap

> Clear Search

> Open first result

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Explorer Search shall expose:

- Appropriate accessible name
- Appropriate accessible description
- Appropriate role
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties

Search results shall expose:

- Position within result set
- Current selection
- Resource type
- Available actions

Screen readers shall announce search result updates appropriately.

Refreshable braille displays shall expose equivalent information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Integration

Explorer Search shall consume:

- Universal Search Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Accessibility Framework
- Future Plugin Framework
- Future Integration Framework

Explorer Search shall never duplicate functionality already implemented
by these frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Explorer Search consumes the Universal Search Framework.
- Search scope adapts correctly to context.
- Boolean searching functions correctly.
- Wildcards function correctly.
- Phrase searching functions correctly.
- Incremental search functions correctly.
- Search highlighting functions correctly.
- Resource activation invokes Application Commands.
- Search history is shared with Universal Search.
- Saved Searches function correctly.
- Keyboard navigation functions correctly.
- Voice navigation functions correctly.
- Screen reader support remains intact.
- Refreshable braille support remains intact.
- No duplicate search implementations exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Universal Search functionality.

Preserve all existing accessibility.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate search indexing, search history, search parsing, or
search result management.

Explorer Search shall function as a context-aware extension of the
Universal Search Framework, providing a consistent and fully accessible
search experience throughout ART.

### Part 6 – Context Menus, Accessibility & Personalization

#### Overview

The Explorer Framework shall fully consume the Global Context Menu
Framework, Accessibility Framework, Application Command Framework,
Personalization Framework, and future Plugin and Integration Frameworks.

The Explorer shall not implement independent context menus,
accessibility behavior, personalization logic, or command
implementations.

Explorer shall remain fully accessible using keyboard, mouse, touch,
screen readers, refreshable braille displays, voice navigation, speech
dictation, switch devices, eye tracking, and future assistive
technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Context Menus

Every Explorer Resource shall expose a context menu.

Context menus shall be invoked using:

- Right-click
- Applications key
- Shift+F10
- Voice command
- Touch and hold (where supported)
- Future interaction methods

Explorer shall consume the Global Context Menu Framework.

Explorer shall never implement independent context menu behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context-Aware Commands

Explorer context menus shall automatically expose commands appropriate
for the selected Resource.

Examples include:

##### Project Workspace

- Open Workspace
- Save Workspace
- Save Workspace As...
- Export Workspace...
- Close Workspace
- Add Project Asset...
- New Report
- Import...
- Project Properties
- Create Template
- Import Template
- Configure Dashboard
- Application Settings
- Help

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Report

- Open Report
- Edit Report
- View Report
- Configure Report
- Validate Report
- Report Statistics
- Export Report...
- Print Preview
- Close Report
- Report Properties

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Progress Log

- Open Progress Log
- Enable Edit Mode
- Add Evaluation Item
- Export Progress Log...
- Progress Log Properties

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Project Asset

- Open
- Preview
- Reveal in Explorer
- Copy Path
- Properties

Project Assets shall remain read-only within ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Template

- Open Template
- Duplicate Template
- Export Template
- Template Properties

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Plugin Resources

Plugins may contribute Resource-specific commands.

Examples include:

- Create Ticket
- View Related Tickets
- Synchronize
- Plugin Settings
- Future plugin commands

Plugins shall consume the Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Integration Resources

Integrations may contribute Resource-specific commands.

Examples include:

- Create New Ticket
- View Related Tickets
- Synchronize
- Refresh Status
- Integration Options
- Future integration commands

Integrations shall consume the Integration Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Standard Editing Commands

Where applicable, context menus shall include standard editing commands.

Examples include:

- Undo
- Redo
- Cut
- Copy
- Paste
- Delete
- Rename
- Select All

Unavailable commands shall be disabled rather than removed.

Disabled commands shall expose their unavailable state programmatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menu Organization

Context menus shall remain concise and logically organized.

Related commands shall be grouped together.

Where appropriate, submenus shall be used to organize large collections
of related commands.

Examples include:

``` text
Export >

Properties >

Open With >

Workspace View >

Plugin Commands >

Integration Commands >
```

Explorer shall follow the same menu organization standards used
throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Commands

Every Explorer context menu shall include the embedded Search Commands
component defined by the Global Context Menu Framework.

The Search Commands component shall allow users to quickly locate
commands within the current context menu.

The Search Commands component shall consume the existing Menu Search
Framework.

Explorer shall not implement an independent command search
implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Navigation

Explorer context menus shall support:

- Up Arrow
- Down Arrow
- Left Arrow
- Right Arrow
- Home
- End
- Enter
- Space
- Escape
- First-letter navigation

Keyboard navigation shall consume the existing ART Menu Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Circular Navigation

Explorer context menus shall support continuous navigation.

Pressing Down Arrow on the final menu item shall move focus to the first
menu item.

Pressing Up Arrow on the first menu item shall move focus to the final
menu item.

Circular navigation shall remain consistent with every menu throughout
ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### First-Letter Navigation

Typing one or more letters while a context menu has focus shall move
focus to the next menu item whose visible text begins with the typed
characters.

Typing shall never automatically activate a command.

Activation shall require Enter, Space, mouse, touch, or another
supported activation method.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Escape Behavior

Explorer shall consume the global Escape behavior defined throughout
ART.

When Explorer has focus:

1.  If a modal dialog is open, Escape shall close the dialog when
    permitted.
2.  Else if a context menu is open, Escape shall close the context menu.
3.  Else if the Menu Bar is active or any menu or submenu is open,
    Escape shall close the menu and exit Menu Bar navigation.
4.  Else if a search box currently has keyboard focus, Escape shall
    follow the standardized Search Framework behavior.
5.  Otherwise, Escape shall perform no Explorer-specific action.

Explorer shall not override the global Escape behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Explorer shall fully support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- JAWS
- NVDA
- VoiceOver
- TalkBack
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Eye tracking systems
- Switch devices
- Future assistive technologies

Accessibility shall consume the ART Accessibility Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Names

Every interactive control shall expose a meaningful accessible name.

Examples include:

- Reports
- Progress Logs
- Project Assets
- Templates
- Favorites
- Saved Searches

Accessible names shall accurately describe the purpose of each control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Roles, States and Properties

Explorer shall expose the appropriate ARIA roles, states, and properties
where required.

Examples include:

- Tree
- Tree Item
- Group
- Button
- Menu
- Menu Item
- Radio Menu Item
- Checkbox Menu Item

Examples of states and properties include:

- Expanded
- Collapsed
- Selected
- Checked
- Disabled
- Current
- Level
- Position in Set
- Set Size

ARIA shall supplement native semantics rather than replace them whenever
native HTML provides equivalent behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Announcements

Screen readers shall announce:

- Resource name
- Resource type
- Expanded/Collapsed state
- Selected state
- Number of child resources (when applicable)
- Position within hierarchy
- Status indicators
- Badges
- Future metadata

Announcements shall remain concise and meaningful.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Refreshable Braille Displays

Explorer shall expose equivalent structural information to refreshable
braille displays.

Braille users shall receive the same hierarchy, selection, and state
information available to screen reader users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Navigation

Explorer controls shall be addressable using visible labels.

Users shall be able to activate controls using natural voice commands.

Explorer shall avoid duplicate visible labels that could create
ambiguity for speech recognition software.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Personalization

Explorer shall respect all applicable personalization settings.

Examples include:

- Appearance
- Accent color
- Display Spacing
- High Contrast
- Reduced Motion
- Font scaling
- Zoom
- Future personalization settings

Explorer shall never override user accessibility preferences.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Extensibility

Plugins shall be able to contribute:

- Resource Types
- Context menu commands
- Icons
- Badges
- Status indicators
- Properties pages
- Future Explorer extensions

Plugins shall register extensions using the Plugin Framework.

Explorer shall not require modification to support new plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Integration Extensibility

Integrations shall be able to contribute:

- Resource Types
- Context menu commands
- Status indicators
- Properties
- Synchronization commands
- Future integration functionality

Explorer shall consume the Integration Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing accessibility.

Preserve all existing keyboard navigation.

Preserve all existing voice navigation.

Preserve all existing refreshable braille support.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate menu logic, accessibility implementations,
personalization settings, plugin architecture, or integration
architecture.

The Explorer Framework shall provide a fully accessible, extensible, and
context-aware navigation experience that remains consistent with every
other framework throughout ART.
