### Part 8 – Explorer Framework Enhancements

#### Overview

This part extends the Explorer Framework with additional accessibility,
navigation, integration, and extensibility requirements.

These enhancements further establish the Explorer as the central
navigation framework for ART while remaining completely optional for
users who prefer the Dashboard.

The Explorer shall continue consuming existing ART frameworks and shall
not duplicate existing functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Landmarks

The Explorer shall be implemented as a dedicated navigation landmark.

The primary Explorer container shall expose an accessible landmark
labeled:

> **Explorer Navigation**

This landmark shall allow assistive technology users to quickly locate
the Explorer using landmark navigation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Section Landmarks

Each major Explorer section shall be implemented as an independently
labeled region.

Examples include:

- Reports
- Progress Logs
- Project Assets
- Templates
- Favorites
- Saved Searches
- Dashboard Layouts
- Future Explorer sections

Each region shall derive its accessible name from its visible heading.

Example:

``` text
Explorer Navigation

Reports
(region)

Progress Logs
(region)

Project Assets
(region)
```

These regions shall support quick navigation using screen reader
landmark navigation commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Heading Hierarchy

Explorer headings shall follow the standardized ART heading hierarchy.

The Explorer itself shall expose a visible Heading Level 2.

Each primary Explorer section shall expose a visible Heading Level 3.

Examples include:

``` text
Explorer
(H2)

Reports
(H3)

Progress Logs
(H3)

Project Assets
(H3)

Templates
(H3)

Favorites
(H3)
```

Nested Resources shall **not** be implemented as headings.

Nested Resources shall instead expose the appropriate tree item
semantics.

Heading levels shall never be skipped.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Focus Landmark

When users switch to Explorer View, keyboard focus shall move to the
Explorer Navigation landmark.

Explorer shall then restore the previously selected Resource whenever
possible.

If no previous Resource exists, focus shall move to the first available
Resource within the Explorer.

Focus shall never be lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep Linking

The Explorer Framework shall support deep linking.

Other ART frameworks shall be able to request that the Explorer
automatically reveal a specific Resource.

Examples include:

- Universal Search
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Dashboard Widgets
- Report Viewer
- Report Builder
- Project Workspace
- Plugin Framework
- Integration Framework
- Future ART frameworks

When a deep link request is received, Explorer shall:

1.  Activate Explorer View if necessary.
2.  Expand parent Resources as needed.
3.  Reveal the requested Resource.
4.  Scroll the Resource into view.
5.  Select the Resource.
6.  Move keyboard focus to the Resource.

Explorer shall perform these actions automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Service API

The Explorer Framework shall expose reusable navigation services for use
by other ART frameworks.

The following services shall be provided:

- Show Explorer
- Hide Explorer
- Reveal Resource
- Select Resource
- Open Resource
- Expand Resource
- Collapse Resource
- Expand Ancestors
- Refresh Resource
- Refresh Explorer
- Get Selected Resource
- Get Current Context
- Get Explorer State

Future services may be added without requiring architectural redesign.

Other frameworks shall consume these services rather than directly
manipulating the Explorer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Integration

The Explorer Service API shall be consumed by:

- Application Command Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Dashboard Widget Framework
- Project Workspace Framework
- Report Builder
- Report Viewer
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Plugin Framework
- Integration Framework
- Future ART frameworks

Explorer shall remain the single authoritative navigation framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer State Restoration

Explorer shall automatically preserve and restore its navigation state.

State restoration shall include:

- Selected Resource
- Expanded Resources
- Collapsed Resources
- Keyboard focus
- Scroll position
- Active Explorer context

When reopening the same Project Workspace or report, Explorer shall
restore its previous navigation state whenever possible.

If the previously selected Resource no longer exists, Explorer shall
move focus to the nearest logical Resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Personalization

Application Settings shall allow users to configure Explorer state
restoration.

Options shall include:

- Restore expanded Resources
- Restore selected Resource
- Restore keyboard focus
- Restore scroll position
- Restore Explorer context

Users may enable or disable these options independently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Counts

Explorer shall display summary counts for parent Resources when
applicable.

Examples include:

``` text
Reports (7)

Progress Logs (2)

Project Assets (18)

Templates (4)
```

Resource counts shall automatically update as Resources are created,
modified, imported, exported, or removed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Resource Counts

Resource counts shall be exposed programmatically to assistive
technologies.

Examples include:

> Reports, 7 items

> Project Assets, 18 items

> Progress Logs, 2 items

Counts shall remain synchronized with the visible interface.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dynamic Updates

Explorer shall automatically refresh Resource counts when:

- Resources are added.
- Resources are removed.
- Resources are imported.
- Resources are exported.
- Resources are renamed.
- Project Workspaces are opened or closed.
- Reports are created or deleted.
- Future Resource Types are registered.

Users shall not be required to manually refresh the Explorer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The enhancements described within this part shall fully support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Mouse
- Touch
- Refreshable braille displays
- Screen readers
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

Explorer landmarks, headings, Resource counts, and deep linking shall
all expose appropriate accessible names, roles, states, and properties.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Explorer exposes the Explorer Navigation landmark.
- Every Explorer section exposes a correctly labeled region.
- Heading hierarchy is correct.
- Heading levels are never skipped.
- Deep linking correctly reveals Resources.
- Parent Resources automatically expand during deep linking.
- Keyboard focus moves to the revealed Resource.
- Explorer Service API functions correctly.
- Other frameworks consume the Explorer Service API.
- Explorer state restoration functions correctly.
- Selected Resource restoration functions correctly.
- Scroll position restoration functions correctly.
- Keyboard focus restoration functions correctly.
- Resource counts update automatically.
- Resource counts are exposed correctly to assistive technologies.
- Screen readers announce Explorer landmarks, headings, and Resource
  counts correctly.
- Refreshable braille displays expose equivalent information.
- No regressions are introduced.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing accessibility.

Preserve all existing keyboard navigation.

Preserve all existing voice navigation.

Preserve all existing refreshable braille support.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate navigation services or framework implementations.

The Explorer Framework shall remain the single, extensible, accessible,
and authoritative navigation framework for ART while providing seamless
integration with every current and future application framework.

## Epic 32 – Report Views Framework

### Part 1 – Framework Overview, Architecture & Objectives

#### Overview

Implement a comprehensive **Report Views Framework** that allows users
to temporarily organize, analyze, review, and navigate report data
without modifying the underlying report unless the user explicitly
chooses to apply changes.

The Report Views Framework shall provide temporary analytical views of
report data while preserving the integrity of the original report.

The framework shall support sorting, filtering, grouping, searching,
highlighting, working views, saved view presets, and future report
analysis capabilities.

The Report Views Framework shall consume existing ART frameworks
whenever possible and shall not duplicate existing functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Philosophy

The Report Views Framework is intended to help accessibility
professionals answer questions such as:

- Show all Table issues.
- Group findings by WCAG Success Criterion.
- Show Critical findings only.
- Group findings by Page.
- Show unresolved issues.
- Show findings assigned to a particular reviewer.
- Review only Keyboard issues.
- Analyze findings without permanently modifying the report.

Users shall be able to explore report data freely while knowing the
original report remains unchanged unless they explicitly apply changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Primary Objectives

The Report Views Framework shall:

- Preserve the original report.
- Support temporary analytical views.
- Improve navigation of large reports.
- Reduce time spent locating related findings.
- Support accessibility-focused review workflows.
- Integrate with Universal Search.
- Integrate with Explorer.
- Integrate with Dashboard.
- Integrate with Report Builder.
- Integrate with Report Viewer.
- Support future analytics features.
- Support future plugins.
- Support future integrations.
- Remain completely accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Philosophy

A **Working View** represents a temporary representation of report data.

Unless the user explicitly chooses **Apply Working View**, the Working
View shall never modify:

- Report content
- Report ordering
- Report metadata
- Report configuration
- Report statistics
- Report history

Users shall be able to experiment freely without risk of accidentally
changing their reports.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Scope

The Report Views Framework shall support:

- Audit Logs
- Executive Summaries
- Progress Logs (where applicable)
- Future report types

The framework shall remain extensible to support additional report types
without requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Architecture

The Report Views Framework shall consume:

- Application Command Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Window Title Framework
- Accessibility Framework
- Report Builder Framework
- Report Viewer Framework
- Project Workspace Framework
- Future Plugin Framework
- Future Integration Framework

The Report Views Framework shall not duplicate functionality already
provided by these frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working Views

Working Views shall provide temporary report representations.

Examples include:

- Tables
- Forms
- Images
- Keyboard
- Color Contrast
- WCAG Success Criterion
- Accessibility Standard
- Severity
- Assigned Reviewer
- Custom Tags
- Future analytical views

Working Views shall never modify the report unless explicitly applied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Integrity

The Report Views Framework shall preserve report integrity.

Users shall always have access to the original report.

Temporary Working Views shall never overwrite report data.

Users shall always be able to return to the original report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Principles

The Report Views Framework shall be:

- Temporary
- Non-destructive
- Context-aware
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Voice-friendly
- Screen reader friendly
- Refreshable braille friendly
- Extensible
- Framework-driven
- Plugin-ready
- Integration-ready
- Future-proof

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Commands

The following Application Commands shall be registered:

- Open Working View
- Exit Working View
- Apply Working View
- Save Working View
- Load Working View
- Delete Working View
- Refresh Working View

Future Report View commands shall register using the same Application
Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Framework

The Report Views Framework shall consume the existing Window Title
Framework.

Working Views shall not implement independent window title logic.

Window titles shall continue following the standardized ART window title
format.

When a Working View is active, the window title shall clearly indicate
that the user is working within a temporary analytical view.

Example:

``` text
AuditLog.ARTAudit — Working View – Tables (Temporary) — Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART)
```

This title shall be generated using the existing Window Title Framework
rather than a separate implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Philosophy

The Report Views Framework shall remain fully usable using:

- Keyboard
- Mouse
- Touch
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

No functionality shall require a pointing device.

Every feature shall expose appropriate accessible names, roles, states,
and properties where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve existing Report Builder functionality.

Preserve existing Report Viewer functionality.

Preserve existing Project Workspace functionality.

Preserve all accessibility features.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate existing functionality.

The Report Views Framework shall become the reusable analytical
framework for all current and future report types while preserving the
integrity of users' reports.

### Part 2 – Working Views Framework

#### Overview

The Working Views Framework shall provide temporary analytical views of
report data that allow users to reorganize, filter, group, sort, and
review findings without modifying the underlying report unless the user
explicitly chooses to apply the changes.

Working Views shall be temporary by default.

Users shall always have a clear understanding of whether they are
viewing the original report or a temporary Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

Working Views shall allow users to:

- Analyze related findings.
- Review subsets of findings.
- Temporarily reorganize reports.
- Locate patterns.
- Prepare reports for review.
- Validate report completeness.
- Improve navigation of large reports.
- Experiment with different report organizations without risk.

Working Views shall never automatically modify the underlying report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Opening a Working View

Working Views may be opened from:

- Report Builder
- Report Viewer
- Explorer
- Universal Search
- Dashboard
- Global Context Menu
- Menu Bar
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Command Palette
- Future plugins
- Future integrations

All methods shall invoke the same underlying Application Command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Configuration

Before a Working View is created, ART shall display a **Working View
Configuration** modal dialog.

The dialog shall allow users to configure:

- Sorting
- Filtering
- Grouping
- Search criteria
- Highlighting options
- Display options
- Saved View Presets
- Future Working View options

The configuration dialog shall be fully keyboard accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Creating a Working View

Selecting **Create Working View** shall:

1.  Preserve the original report.
2.  Apply the selected Working View options.
3.  Generate a temporary representation of the report.
4.  Open the Working View.
5.  Move keyboard focus to the Working View heading.

The original report shall remain unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Identification

Users shall always be able to determine that they are viewing a
temporary Working View.

The Working View shall clearly indicate:

- Working View name.
- Temporary status.
- Original report name.

The application shall never allow users to confuse a Working View with
the underlying report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title

The Working View shall consume the existing Window Title Framework.

Example:

``` text
AuditLog.ARTAudit — Working View – Tables (Temporary) — Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART)
```

Window titles shall update automatically whenever the Working View
changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Heading

Every Working View shall begin with a visible Heading Level 1.

Example:

``` text
Working View – Tables
```

Immediately beneath the heading, explanatory text shall indicate that
the current view is temporary.

Example:

> You are viewing a temporary Working View. The underlying report has
> not been modified.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Exit Working View Button

Every Working View shall provide an **Exit Working View** button.

The button shall appear near the beginning of the Working View.

The button shall:

- Close the Working View.
- Return to the original report.
- Restore keyboard focus to approximately the same location from which
  the Working View was opened.

The Exit Working View button shall be the preferred method for leaving
the Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Escape Key Behavior

The Working View shall consume the standardized ART Escape behavior.

When the Working View has focus:

1.  If a modal dialog is open, Escape shall close the dialog when
    permitted.
2.  Else if a menu, submenu, or context menu is open, Escape shall close
    the menu.
3.  Else if a search box currently has keyboard focus, Escape shall
    follow the standardized Search Framework behavior.
4.  Else if keyboard focus is within the Working View, Escape shall
    close the Working View and return to the original report.

Escape shall never discard report data because the Working View contains
only temporary state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Returning to the Report

Closing a Working View shall:

- Restore the original report.
- Restore the original report order.
- Restore the original report presentation.
- Restore keyboard focus to approximately the corresponding finding or
  location represented by the user's current Working View position.
- Restore scroll position whenever possible.

Users shall never lose their place unnecessarily.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Editing Within a Working View

Working Views shall permit editing of report content.

When a user edits a finding while inside a Working View:

- The edit shall be applied immediately to the underlying report.
- The Working View shall automatically refresh as needed.
- Sorting, filtering, and grouping shall remain active.
- The user's current context shall be preserved whenever possible.

Working Views shall function as alternative presentations of the same
report rather than editable copies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Status

Working Views shall expose their temporary status programmatically.

Assistive technologies shall be informed that:

- A Working View is active.
- The Working View is temporary.
- The underlying report remains unchanged unless explicitly reordered.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Opening Multiple Working Views

Only one Working View shall be active for a report at any given time.

Opening a different Working View for the same report shall replace the
existing Working View.

Different reports may each have their own Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Lifetime

A Working View shall remain available until:

- The user exits the Working View.
- The report is closed.
- The report is replaced.
- The Project Workspace is closed.
- ART is closed.
- Another Working View replaces it.

Future enhancements may allow persistent Working Views without requiring
architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Working Views shall fully support:

- Keyboard-only operation.
- Screen readers.
- Refreshable braille displays.
- Voice navigation.
- Speech dictation.
- Switch devices.
- Eye tracking.
- Future assistive technologies.

Every control shall expose:

- Appropriate accessible names.
- Appropriate descriptions.
- Appropriate roles.
- Appropriate states.
- Appropriate properties.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Working Views are temporary.
- Original reports remain unchanged.
- Working View Configuration opens correctly.
- Window titles update correctly.
- Working View headings display correctly.
- Exit Working View functions correctly.
- Escape closes the Working View when appropriate.
- Focus returns to approximately the correct report location.
- Scroll position is restored whenever possible.
- Editing updates the underlying report.
- Working View refreshes appropriately after edits.
- Screen readers announce Working View status.
- Refreshable braille displays expose equivalent information.
- Voice navigation functions correctly.
- No report data is lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing report editing functionality.

Preserve all accessibility features.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate window title logic, search functionality, navigation
behavior, or accessibility implementations.

The Working Views Framework shall provide a safe, temporary, and fully
accessible environment for analyzing and editing report data while
preserving the integrity and organization of the original report.

### Part 3 – Sorting, Filtering & Grouping Framework

#### Overview

The Report Views Framework shall provide a comprehensive Sorting,
Filtering, and Grouping Framework that enables users to temporarily
organize report data for analysis without modifying the underlying
report unless the user explicitly chooses to apply the resulting
organization.

Sorting, filtering, and grouping may be used individually or in any
combination.

All operations shall be temporary by default.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Principles

Sorting, filtering, and grouping shall:

- Be non-destructive.
- Be reversible.
- Be independently configurable.
- Work together seamlessly.
- Update the Working View immediately.
- Preserve report integrity.
- Support future report types.
- Support future custom fields.
- Support future plugins.
- Support future integrations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sorting

Users shall be able to sort findings using one or more sort criteria.

Supported sort fields shall include:

- Finding Number
- Severity
- Priority
- WCAG Version
- WCAG Success Criterion
- Accessibility Standard
- Rule Identifier
- Finding Type
- Component
- Page Title
- Page URL
- Screen Name
- Technology
- Browser
- Platform
- Assigned Reviewer
- Status
- Resolution Status
- Date Created
- Date Modified
- Date Verified
- Category
- Tags
- Custom Fields
- Future fields

Future Resource Types shall be able to register additional sortable
fields.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sort Order

Each sort criterion shall support:

- Ascending
- Descending

The selected sort direction shall be clearly indicated visually and
programmatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multi-Level Sorting

Users shall be able to define multiple sort levels.

Example:

1.  Severity
2.  WCAG Success Criterion
3.  Page Title
4.  Finding Number

Each level shall be evaluated in sequence.

Users shall be able to reorder sort levels.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stable Sorting

Sorting shall be stable.

When two findings contain identical values for the active sort field,
their relative order shall remain unchanged unless additional sort
levels are specified.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filtering

Users shall be able to filter findings using one or more criteria.

Supported filters shall include:

- Severity
- Priority
- WCAG Version
- WCAG Success Criterion
- Accessibility Standard
- Rule Identifier
- Finding Type
- Component
- Page
- URL
- Screen
- Technology
- Browser
- Platform
- Assigned Reviewer
- Status
- Resolution Status
- Tags
- Category
- Custom Fields
- Future fields

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multiple Filters

Users shall be able to combine multiple filters.

Examples include:

- Critical findings assigned to Mark W.
- Open issues affecting Tables.
- WCAG 2.2 AA findings.
- Findings tagged Forms.
- Findings requiring review.

Multiple filters shall update the Working View immediately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Grouping

Users shall be able to group findings by one or more fields.

Supported grouping fields shall include:

- Severity
- Priority
- WCAG Success Criterion
- Accessibility Standard
- Page
- URL
- Screen
- Component
- Technology
- Assigned Reviewer
- Status
- Resolution Status
- Tags
- Category
- Custom Fields
- Future fields

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Nested Grouping

Grouping shall support multiple hierarchical levels.

Example:

``` text
Severity

    Critical

        WCAG 1.3.1

            Homepage

            Checkout

        WCAG 2.4.7

            Search

    Serious

        WCAG 4.1.2
```

Users shall be able to reorder grouping levels.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Expand and Collapse

Grouped findings shall support:

- Expand
- Collapse
- Expand All
- Collapse All

Expand/Collapse state shall be preserved while the Working View remains
open.

Expand/Collapse state shall be exposed programmatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Group Counts

Every group shall display the number of findings it contains.

Example:

``` text
Critical (12)

Serious (34)

Moderate (18)
```

Counts shall automatically update whenever sorting, filtering, or
editing changes the contents of a group.

Counts shall be exposed to assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Empty Groups

Groups containing no findings shall not be displayed.

The Working View shall never display empty groups.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Combined Operations

Users shall be able to combine:

- Sorting
- Filtering
- Grouping
- Search
- Highlighting

Example:

Filter:

``` text
Severity = Critical
```

Group by:

``` text
WCAG Success Criterion
```

Sort by:

``` text
Page Title
```

The resulting Working View shall update immediately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Live Updates

The Working View shall automatically refresh whenever:

- A finding is edited.
- A finding is deleted.
- A finding is added.
- Metadata changes.
- Tags change.
- Status changes.
- Reviewer changes.
- Custom fields change.

Users shall not be required to manually refresh the Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Summary

Each Working View shall provide a summary describing the current
organization.

Example:

``` text
Grouped by:

• Severity

Then by:

• WCAG Success Criterion

Sorted by:

• Page Title (Ascending)

Filtered by:

• Status = Open

Showing:

64 of 173 findings
```

This summary shall be visible and programmatically exposed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Breadcrumb

The Working View shall display the active analytical path.

Example:

``` text
Working View

Grouped by Severity

Filtered by Status: Open

Sorted by Page Title
```

The breadcrumb shall update dynamically whenever the Working View
configuration changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Reset Options

Users shall be able to independently:

- Clear Sorting
- Clear Filtering
- Clear Grouping
- Reset Working View

Resetting one option shall not automatically clear the others.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Sorting, filtering, and grouping controls shall expose:

- Appropriate accessible names
- Appropriate descriptions
- Appropriate roles
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties

Grouped findings shall expose:

- Expanded state
- Collapsed state
- Level within hierarchy
- Position within set
- Number of child findings

Screen readers and refreshable braille displays shall communicate
equivalent structural information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Single-field sorting functions correctly.
- Multi-level sorting functions correctly.
- Sorting remains stable.
- Filtering functions correctly.
- Multiple filters function correctly.
- Grouping functions correctly.
- Nested grouping functions correctly.
- Expand and Collapse function correctly.
- Group counts update automatically.
- Empty groups are not displayed.
- Combined sorting, filtering, grouping, and searching function
  correctly.
- Working View summaries update correctly.
- Breadcrumbs update correctly.
- Reset options function independently.
- Live updates refresh the Working View correctly.
- Accessibility information is exposed correctly.
- No underlying report data is modified unless explicitly applied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing report editing functionality.

Preserve all accessibility features.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate search functionality, Application Commands, or
accessibility implementations.

The Sorting, Filtering, and Grouping Framework shall provide users with
powerful analytical capabilities while preserving the integrity of the
original report.

### Part 4 – Applying Working Views, Saved View Presets & View Management

#### Overview

The Report Views Framework shall allow users to save, reuse, apply,
duplicate, rename, export, import, and delete Working View
configurations.

A Working View configuration shall define **how a report is presented**,
not the report data itself.

Working View configurations shall remain independent of report content
and shall not contain copies of findings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Configurations

A Working View configuration may contain:

- Sorting criteria
- Filtering criteria
- Grouping criteria
- Search criteria
- Highlighting options
- Expanded and collapsed group state (optional)
- Display options
- Future Working View settings

Working View configurations shall never contain report findings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Temporary Working Views

By default, every Working View shall remain temporary.

Closing the Working View shall return the user to the original report
without modifying:

- Finding order
- Report structure
- Report layout
- Report metadata

Temporary Working Views shall not require users to save changes before
exiting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Applying a Working View

Users may choose to permanently apply a Working View to the current
report.

Applying a Working View shall permanently update the report organization
according to the active:

- Sorting
- Grouping
- Filtering (where applicable)
- Display options supported by the report format

The user shall explicitly initiate this action.

The application shall never automatically apply a Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Apply Working View Command

The Report Views Framework shall expose an **Apply Working View**
command.

The command shall be available from:

- Working View
- Report Viewer
- Report Builder
- Global Context Menu
- Menu Bar
- Command Palette
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Future frameworks

All entry points shall invoke the same Application Command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Apply Working View Confirmation

Before applying a Working View, ART shall display a confirmation dialog.

The dialog shall explain:

- The current Working View is temporary.
- Applying the Working View will permanently reorganize the current
  report.
- Report content will not change.
- Only the organization of findings will change.

The dialog shall provide:

- Apply
- Cancel

Optionally:

- Do not show again

The dialog shall be fully accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Applying Sorting

When applied, sorting shall permanently reorder findings within the
report.

Only the ordering shall change.

Finding content shall remain unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Applying Grouping

When supported by the report type, grouping may become the default
organization of the report.

If a report format does not support grouping, ART shall preserve
grouping only within future Working Views.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Applying Filtering

Filtering shall not permanently delete or remove findings.

Instead, ART shall allow supported report types to persist filter
settings as the default report presentation.

Hidden findings shall remain part of the report.

Users shall always be able to clear filters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Presets

Users shall be able to save Working View configurations as reusable
presets.

Examples include:

- Tables Review
- Keyboard Accessibility
- Color Contrast
- Critical Issues
- WCAG 2.2 AA
- Needs Review
- Forms Analysis
- Custom Presets

Presets shall remain independent of any specific report unless
explicitly saved as report-specific.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Preset Types

ART shall support:

##### Global Presets

Available throughout ART.

##### Project Presets

Available only within the current Project Workspace.

##### Report Presets

Available only for the associated report.

Future preset scopes may be added.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Creating Presets

Users shall be able to create presets from the current Working View.

Users shall provide:

- Preset name
- Optional description
- Preset scope
- Optional category

Duplicate preset names within the same scope shall not be permitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Managing Presets

Users shall be able to:

- Open
- Apply
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Export
- Import
- Share (future)
- Convert scope (where applicable)

Preset management shall be fully keyboard accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Default Presets

ART shall include optional built-in presets.

Examples include:

- Critical Findings
- Serious Findings
- Tables
- Forms
- Keyboard
- Images
- WCAG 2.1
- WCAG 2.2
- Open Findings
- Closed Findings

Users may duplicate built-in presets but shall not modify the originals.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Importing Presets

Users shall be able to import previously exported Working View presets.

Imported presets shall be validated before being added.

Invalid presets shall not be imported.

The import process shall preserve existing presets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Exporting Presets

Users shall be able to export one or more Working View presets.

Exported presets shall contain:

- Configuration information
- Metadata
- Version information
- Future-compatible extension data

Exported presets shall not include report findings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Preset Compatibility

When opening an older preset:

ART shall attempt to migrate the preset automatically.

If migration cannot be completed safely:

The user shall receive an accessible explanation.

The preset shall remain unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recent Working Views

ART may maintain a history of recently used Working Views.

Examples include:

- Tables Review
- Critical Findings
- Keyboard Review
- Forms Review

Recent Working Views shall allow users to quickly reopen frequently used
analytical views.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Integration

Working View presets shall integrate with:

- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Universal Search
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Command Palette
- Global Context Menu
- Future Plugin Framework
- Future Integration Framework

The same preset shall be available regardless of how it is opened.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Working View preset management shall fully support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

All preset controls shall expose:

- Appropriate accessible names
- Appropriate descriptions
- Appropriate roles
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Temporary Working Views remain non-destructive.
- Apply Working View permanently updates report organization only when
  explicitly requested.
- Confirmation dialog functions correctly.
- Sorting is correctly applied.
- Grouping is correctly applied where supported.
- Filtering behaves correctly.
- Working View presets can be created.
- Presets can be renamed.
- Presets can be duplicated.
- Presets can be deleted.
- Presets can be exported.
- Presets can be imported.
- Presets remain compatible across versions.
- Built-in presets remain read-only.
- Recent Working Views function correctly.
- Keyboard accessibility functions correctly.
- Screen reader accessibility functions correctly.
- Refreshable braille support functions correctly.
- Voice navigation functions correctly.
- No report findings are lost or modified unintentionally.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing report editing functionality.

Preserve all accessibility features.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate Application Commands, accessibility implementations, or
configuration management logic.

The Report Views Framework shall provide users with a powerful,
reusable, and fully accessible system for creating, managing, and
applying analytical report views while preserving the integrity of
report data.

### Part 5 – Working View Search, Navigation & Deep Integration

#### Overview

The Report Views Framework shall fully integrate with the Universal
Search Framework, Explorer Framework, Global Context Menu Framework,
Application Command Framework, Keyboard Shortcut Manager, and Window
Title Framework.

Working Views shall provide powerful navigation and search capabilities
while maintaining synchronization with the underlying report.

Working Views shall not implement independent search, navigation, or
command frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Framework Integration

Working Views shall consume the Universal Search Framework.

All search functionality within a Working View shall invoke the existing
Universal Search Framework.

Working Views shall not implement an independent search engine, search
parser, search index, search history, or search result manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Scope

When search is initiated within a Working View, the default search scope
shall be the active Working View.

Search results shall include only findings currently visible within the
Working View.

Hidden findings excluded by active filters shall not appear unless the
user explicitly expands the search scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Expanding Search Scope

Users shall be able to expand the search scope beyond the current
Working View.

Available search scopes shall include:

- Current Working View (Default)
- Current Report
- Current Project Workspace
- Entire ART Repository

The selected search scope shall remain in effect until changed or until
the Working View is closed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Boolean Search

Working Views shall support every search capability provided by the
Universal Search Framework.

Examples include:

``` text
Table AND Critical
```

``` text
"Keyboard Trap"
```

``` text
Forms* NOT Closed
```

``` text
Severity:Critical AND WCAG:2.1.1
```

Working Views shall consume the existing Boolean search parser.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Highlighting

Matching findings shall be highlighted.

Highlighting shall satisfy ART accessibility requirements.

Highlighting shall never be the sole method of identifying search
results.

Users shall be able to disable highlighting through Application
Settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Counts

Working Views shall display the total number of matching findings.

Example:

``` text
Showing 12 matching findings

Viewing 12 of 247 findings
```

Counts shall automatically update whenever:

- Search changes
- Filters change
- Grouping changes
- Sorting changes
- Findings change

Counts shall be exposed programmatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Navigation

Working Views shall support sequential navigation through search
results.

Users shall be able to:

- Move to the next result.
- Move to the previous result.
- Jump directly to a selected result.
- View the current result position.

Example:

``` text
Result 4 of 12
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Navigation

Working Views shall consume the Universal Search keyboard model.

Default keyboard shortcuts shall include:

- F3 — Next Search Result
- Shift+F3 — Previous Search Result

These shortcuts shall:

- Be configurable through Keyboard Shortcut Manager.
- Appear in Keyboard Manager.
- Appear within Help documentation.
- Appear wherever keyboard shortcuts are displayed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Navigation

Users shall be able to navigate Working Views using:

- Keyboard
- Mouse
- Touch
- Refreshable braille displays
- Screen readers
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future interaction methods

Navigation shall remain consistent with the rest of ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Group Navigation

When findings are grouped:

Users shall be able to navigate:

- Next Group
- Previous Group
- Expand Group
- Collapse Group
- Expand All Groups
- Collapse All Groups

Group navigation commands shall consume the Application Command
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Navigation

Working Views shall provide commands for navigating:

- Next Finding
- Previous Finding
- Next Filtered Finding
- Previous Filtered Finding
- Next Group
- Previous Group
- First Finding
- Last Finding

Future navigation commands may be registered without architectural
redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Navigation

Working Views shall display a breadcrumb describing the current
analytical path.

Example:

``` text
Working View

Grouped by Severity

Critical

WCAG 1.3.1

Page: Homepage

Finding 3 of 12
```

Breadcrumbs shall update automatically as navigation changes.

Breadcrumbs shall be programmatically exposed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep Integration with Explorer

Explorer shall consume the Explorer Service API defined in Epic 31.

When a user activates an analytical category from Explorer, the
corresponding Working View shall be created automatically.

Example:

``` text
Explorer

Tables (17 Findings)
```

Activating **Tables** shall:

1.  Open the associated report if necessary.
2.  Create or activate a Working View configured for Table findings.
3.  Group, sort, and filter findings according to the selected Explorer
    resource.
4.  Move keyboard focus to the first matching finding.
5.  Update the application window title.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep Linking

Working Views shall support deep linking.

Other ART frameworks shall be able to request:

- Reveal Finding
- Reveal Group
- Reveal Category
- Reveal Page
- Reveal WCAG Success Criterion

When a deep link is received:

The Working View shall:

1.  Open if necessary.
2.  Expand required groups.
3.  Scroll the target finding into view.
4.  Select the target finding.
5.  Move keyboard focus to the target finding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bidirectional Synchronization

Working Views and Explorer shall remain synchronized.

Examples include:

Selecting a finding in Explorer shall update the Working View.

Selecting a finding in the Working View shall update Explorer.

Changing groups shall update Explorer.

Changing filters shall update Explorer.

Changing Working Views shall update Explorer.

Synchronization shall not create duplicate state management.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menus

Working Views shall consume the Global Context Menu Framework.

Context menus shall provide commands appropriate to the selected finding
or group.

Examples include:

- Edit Finding
- Copy
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Reveal in Explorer
- Reveal in Report
- Expand Group
- Collapse Group
- Apply Working View
- Exit Working View
- Working View Properties

The embedded Context Menu Search component defined in Epic 30 shall be
available within every Working View context menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Commands

The Report Views Framework shall register additional commands including:

- Next Finding
- Previous Finding
- Next Group
- Previous Group
- Reveal in Explorer
- Reveal in Report
- Expand All Groups
- Collapse All Groups
- Refresh Working View
- Reset Working View

Future commands shall register using the existing Application Command
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Working Views shall expose:

- Appropriate accessible names
- Appropriate descriptions
- Appropriate roles
- Appropriate states
- Appropriate properties

Grouped findings shall expose:

- Hierarchical level
- Expanded state
- Collapsed state
- Position within set
- Number of findings within group

Search results shall expose:

- Current result
- Total results
- Result position
- Current Working View scope

Equivalent information shall be available through refreshable braille
displays.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Working Views consume the Universal Search Framework.
- Boolean searching functions correctly.
- Search scopes function correctly.
- Search highlighting functions correctly.
- Result counts update automatically.
- F3 and Shift+F3 navigate search results.
- Keyboard shortcuts appear in Keyboard Shortcut Manager.
- Breadcrumbs update correctly.
- Explorer automatically creates Working Views from analytical
  resources.
- Deep linking functions correctly.
- Explorer and Working Views remain synchronized.
- Context menus consume the Global Context Menu Framework.
- Voice navigation functions correctly.
- Screen readers announce navigation correctly.
- Refreshable braille displays expose equivalent information.
- No duplicate navigation or search implementations exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing report editing functionality.

Preserve all accessibility features.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate search, navigation, command, or synchronization logic.

The Working Views Framework shall provide a seamless, searchable,
navigable, and fully integrated analytical environment that works
consistently with every major framework throughout ART.

### Part 6 – Working View Editing, Batch Operations & Bulk Actions

#### Overview

The Report Views Framework shall support editing individual findings and
performing batch operations on multiple findings while preserving the
integrity of the underlying report.

Working Views shall function as alternative presentations of report data
rather than independent copies.

All edits performed within a Working View shall update the underlying
report immediately unless the user is performing a batch operation that
requires confirmation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Editing Findings

Users shall be able to edit findings directly from a Working View.

Supported editing operations shall include:

- Finding Title
- Finding Description
- Steps to Reproduce
- Expected Result
- Actual Result
- Recommendation
- Severity
- Priority
- Status
- Assigned Reviewer
- Tags
- Custom Fields
- Attachments
- Metadata
- Future editable fields

Editing shall consume the existing Report Builder Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Editing Behavior

Editing a finding within a Working View shall:

- Update the underlying report.
- Preserve the current Working View.
- Maintain active sorting.
- Maintain active grouping.
- Maintain active filtering.
- Maintain the current search.
- Refresh the Working View automatically.

Users shall not be required to recreate the Working View after editing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Automatic Repositioning

When an edited value affects sorting, grouping, or filtering:

The finding shall automatically move to its correct location within the
Working View.

Example:

A finding grouped under:

``` text
Status

Open
```

is changed to:

``` text
Closed
```

The finding shall automatically move to:

``` text
Status

Closed
```

The movement shall occur immediately after the edit is committed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Maintaining User Context

When a finding automatically moves because of sorting or grouping
changes:

ART shall attempt to preserve the user's workflow.

The application shall:

- Announce that the finding has moved.
- Automatically move focus to the finding in its new location.
- Scroll the finding into view.
- Preserve keyboard interaction whenever possible.

If the finding is filtered out as a result of the edit, ART shall notify
the user and move focus to the next logical finding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Batch Selection

Working Views shall support selecting multiple findings.

Users shall be able to select findings using:

- Keyboard
- Mouse
- Touch
- Voice navigation
- Switch devices
- Future interaction methods

Selection shall remain fully accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Selection Commands

The following Application Commands shall be registered:

- Select Finding
- Deselect Finding
- Select All Visible Findings
- Clear Selection
- Invert Selection
- Select Current Group

Future selection commands may be registered without architectural
redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bulk Editing

Users shall be able to modify selected findings simultaneously.

Supported bulk operations shall include:

- Change Severity
- Change Priority
- Change Status
- Assign Reviewer
- Add Tags
- Remove Tags
- Add Custom Field Values
- Remove Custom Field Values
- Future bulk operations

Bulk operations shall update every selected finding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bulk Delete

Users shall be able to delete multiple findings simultaneously.

Before deletion:

ART shall display an accessible confirmation dialog.

The dialog shall indicate:

- Number of findings affected.
- Whether the action can be undone.
- Consequences of deletion.

Deletion shall not occur until confirmed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bulk Duplicate

Users shall be able to duplicate one or more findings.

Duplicated findings shall receive:

- New identifiers.
- New creation timestamps.
- Appropriate metadata.

Duplicated findings shall appear according to the active Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bulk Export

Users shall be able to export selected findings.

Supported export formats shall be identical to those supported elsewhere
in ART.

Export shall include only the selected findings.

The underlying report shall remain unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bulk Print

Users shall be able to print:

- Selected findings.
- Current group.
- Entire Working View.

Printing shall consume the existing Print Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Batch Operations Context Menu

When multiple findings are selected, the context menu shall expose
commands appropriate to the current selection.

Examples include:

- Edit Selected
- Delete Selected
- Export Selected
- Print Selected
- Change Severity
- Change Status
- Assign Reviewer
- Add Tags
- Remove Tags
- Copy
- Select All
- Clear Selection

Commands unavailable for the current selection shall be disabled rather
than removed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Batch Operations Toolbar

When one or more findings are selected, ART may display a contextual
Batch Operations toolbar.

The toolbar shall provide quick access to frequently used operations.

Users shall be able to dismiss the toolbar without affecting the current
selection.

The toolbar shall be fully keyboard accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Undo and Redo

All edits and batch operations shall integrate with the existing
Undo/Redo Framework.

Users shall be able to undo:

- Individual edits.
- Bulk edits.
- Bulk deletion.
- Bulk duplication.
- Tag changes.
- Status changes.
- Future supported operations.

Undo shall restore the Working View automatically.

Redo shall reapply the operation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Conflict Detection

If the underlying report changes while a Working View is open:

ART shall automatically refresh the Working View.

If automatic refresh cannot safely preserve the user's current context:

ART shall notify the user and provide options to:

- Refresh Now
- Continue Reviewing
- Save Current Selection (where applicable)

Users shall never lose report data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Batch editing shall fully support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

Selection state shall be exposed programmatically.

Selected findings shall communicate:

- Selected state
- Position within selection
- Total selected findings

Equivalent information shall be available to refreshable braille
displays.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Individual finding editing functions correctly.
- Working Views refresh automatically after edits.
- Findings automatically reposition when required.
- Focus follows moved findings appropriately.
- Users are notified when findings become filtered out.
- Batch selection functions correctly.
- Bulk editing functions correctly.
- Bulk deletion functions correctly.
- Bulk duplication functions correctly.
- Bulk export functions correctly.
- Bulk print functions correctly.
- Context menus expose appropriate commands.
- Undo and Redo function correctly.
- Automatic refresh functions correctly.
- Keyboard accessibility remains intact.
- Screen reader accessibility remains intact.
- Refreshable braille support remains intact.
- Voice navigation remains intact.
- No report data is unintentionally lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Report Builder functionality.

Preserve all existing accessibility.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate editing, printing, exporting, or Undo/Redo
implementations.

The Working Views Framework shall provide a powerful, efficient, and
fully accessible editing environment that allows users to review and
update findings individually or in bulk while maintaining
synchronization with the underlying report.

### Part 7 – Report View Modes, Presentation & Accessibility

#### Overview

The Report Views Framework shall support multiple report presentation
modes that allow users to analyze report data using different visual and
structural layouts without modifying the underlying report.

A Report View Mode affects **only how report information is presented**.

Changing a Report View Mode shall never modify:

- Report data
- Report findings
- Report metadata
- Report history
- Project Workspace data

Report View Modes shall consume the existing Working Views Framework and
shall not implement independent presentation logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Report View Modes

The Report Views Framework shall support:

- Standard Report View (Default)
- Working View
- Grouped View
- Outline View
- Compact View
- Expanded View
- Reading View
- Review View
- Future View Modes

Future view modes shall be able to register with the framework without
requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Standard Report View

Standard Report View shall display the report exactly as authored.

This view shall represent the canonical report.

Unless a Working View is active, users shall always be viewing the
Standard Report View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View

Working View shall remain the primary analytical view defined in
previous parts of this epic.

Working View shall consume:

- Sorting
- Filtering
- Grouping
- Search
- Highlighting

Working View shall remain temporary unless explicitly applied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Grouped View

Grouped View shall emphasize hierarchical organization.

Examples include grouping by:

- WCAG Success Criterion
- Severity
- Page
- Component
- Technology
- Assigned Reviewer
- Status
- Tags
- Future grouping criteria

Grouped View shall consume the existing Grouping Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Outline View

Outline View shall emphasize report structure.

Examples include:

``` text
Audit Log

Report Metadata

Executive Summary

Findings

    WCAG 1.1.1

        Finding 1

        Finding 2

    WCAG 1.3.1

        Finding 3

Recommendations

Appendices
```

Outline View shall improve navigation for large reports.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Compact View

Compact View shall minimize whitespace while preserving readability.

Compact View shall allow users to review more findings simultaneously.

Compact View shall not remove information.

Only presentation shall change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Expanded View

Expanded View shall maximize readability.

Examples include:

- Increased spacing
- Larger finding separation
- Expanded metadata
- Increased readability

Expanded View shall be especially beneficial for users with cognitive
disabilities and low vision.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Reading View

Reading View shall optimize the report for uninterrupted reading.

Reading View shall:

- Reduce visual distractions.
- Emphasize report content.
- Preserve accessibility.
- Maintain semantic structure.

Reading View shall not modify report content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Review View

Review View shall emphasize reviewer workflow.

Examples include displaying:

- Status
- Assigned Reviewer
- Resolution State
- Comments
- Review Notes
- Outstanding Actions

Review View shall assist peer reviews and quality assurance.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### View Mode Switching

Users shall be able to change Report View Modes from:

- Menu Bar
- View menu
- Working View
- Global Context Menu
- Command Palette
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Future interaction methods

All methods shall invoke the same Application Command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### View Menu

The View menu shall contain:

``` text
Report View >

    ● Standard

    ○ Working

    ○ Outline

    ○ Compact

    ○ Expanded

    ○ Reading

    ○ Review
```

Exactly one Report View Mode shall be active at a time.

The selected view shall expose an accessible checked state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcuts

Users may assign keyboard shortcuts for:

- Standard View
- Working View
- Outline View
- Compact View
- Expanded View
- Reading View
- Review View
- Toggle Report View

No default shortcuts shall be assigned unless defined elsewhere in ART.

All assigned shortcuts shall appear within:

- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Menus
- Tooltips
- Help documentation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Framework

Report View Modes shall consume the existing Window Title Framework.

Examples include:

``` text
AuditLog.ARTAudit — Standard View — Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART)
```

``` text
AuditLog.ARTAudit — Working View – Tables (Temporary) — Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART)
```

``` text
AuditLog.ARTAudit — Outline View — Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART)
```

The existing Window Title Framework shall generate all titles.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Preserving User Context

Changing Report View Modes shall preserve:

- Current finding
- Keyboard focus
- Scroll position
- Search results
- Selection
- Expanded groups (when applicable)

Whenever possible, focus shall remain on the equivalent finding in the
newly selected view.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Presentation Preferences

Users shall be able to configure presentation preferences.

Examples include:

- Default Report View
- Default Compact spacing
- Default Expanded spacing
- Remember last Report View
- Automatically restore previous Working View

Presentation preferences shall not modify report content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Every Report View Mode shall preserve:

- Heading hierarchy
- Landmark structure
- Keyboard navigation
- Screen reader compatibility
- Refreshable braille compatibility
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch device compatibility
- Eye tracking compatibility

Changing Report View Modes shall never reduce accessibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Semantic Structure

Regardless of the selected Report View Mode:

The underlying document semantics shall remain correct.

Examples include:

- Proper heading levels
- Lists
- Tables
- Regions
- Landmarks
- Tree structures
- Form controls

Presentation changes shall never replace semantic structure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Management

Changing Report View Modes shall:

- Preserve keyboard focus whenever possible.
- Restore focus to the equivalent finding.
- Avoid unnecessary focus movement.
- Never trap keyboard focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Standard Report View functions correctly.
- Working View functions correctly.
- Outline View functions correctly.
- Compact View functions correctly.
- Expanded View functions correctly.
- Reading View functions correctly.
- Review View functions correctly.
- View switching functions correctly.
- Keyboard focus is preserved.
- Scroll position is preserved.
- Search remains active.
- Window titles update correctly.
- Keyboard shortcuts function correctly.
- Screen reader accessibility remains intact.
- Refreshable braille support remains intact.
- Voice navigation remains intact.
- Underlying report semantics remain correct.
- Report data is never modified by changing view modes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing report editing functionality.

Preserve all accessibility features.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate presentation logic or accessibility implementations.

The Report Views Framework shall provide flexible, accessible, and
consistent presentation modes that enable users to analyze report data
using the layout that best supports their current task while preserving
the integrity of the underlying report.
