## Addition To Working Views Framework

### Description

Add another report view mode to Working View called "Table". In the
Table Working View, each column should be a field from the report and
each row is an entry. Each column header should be a menu button that
opens an accessible menu containing sorting and filtering options that
can be applied to that specific column. For example, user could choose
to sort the Page Name column in descending order, group the Success
Criteria column by conformance level, and/or Filter the Tester column by
values containing "David G.". The options for sorting, grouping, and
filtering should contain both generic options, dynamic options (based on
the column data), and customizable (with an accessible text entry field
that allows users to type a custom value for filtering based on values
present in the data).\
If the Table view mode is being used for the Working View, all of the
same options in the Working View Configuration shall be available. And,
in the actual working view, if Table is selected as the working view
mode, then the actual working view shall display the data in a dynamic,
configurable table as described above, with the same applicable
options/actions as the other existing view modes, with the primary
differences being the table layout and the sorting, filtering, and
grouping options in the table columns being present in the actual
working view instead of on the working view configuration screen.

## Epic 33 – Resource Framework

### Part 1 – Resource Framework Overview, Architecture & Design Principles

#### Overview

Implement a centralized **Resource Framework** that provides a
consistent architecture for identifying, managing, storing, searching,
opening, editing, importing, exporting, and extending every
user-manageable object within ART.

The Resource Framework shall provide a single, reusable abstraction for
all supported resource types throughout the application.

All existing ART frameworks shall consume the Resource Framework rather
than implementing resource-specific management logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The Resource Framework shall provide:

- A consistent object model.
- A standardized resource lifecycle.
- Consistent resource identification.
- Consistent metadata.
- Consistent storage.
- Consistent import and export behavior.
- Consistent search integration.
- Consistent Explorer integration.
- Consistent Dashboard integration.
- Consistent context menu integration.
- Consistent Application Command integration.
- Consistent accessibility support.
- Extensibility for future resource types.

The framework shall become the authoritative source for managing every
user-manageable object in ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Definition

Within ART, a **Resource** is an object that can be independently:

- Created
- Opened
- Saved
- Saved As
- Imported
- Exported
- Renamed
- Deleted
- Searched
- Indexed
- Referenced
- Managed
- Extended

Objects that do not meet these criteria shall remain part of their
parent resource rather than becoming independent resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Principles

The Resource Framework shall be:

- Consistent
- Extensible
- Local-first
- Framework-driven
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Searchable
- Explorer-aware
- Workspace-aware
- Plugin-ready
- Integration-ready
- Future-proof

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Ownership

Every resource shall have exactly one logical owner.

Examples include:

- A Project Workspace owns Reports.
- A Report owns its Report Attachments.
- The application owns Global Templates.
- The application owns Global Saved Searches.
- The application owns Global Working View Presets.

Ownership defines organization and lifecycle but shall not restrict
future sharing or collaboration features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Resource Types

The Resource Framework shall initially support the following resource
types.

##### Project Resources

- Project Workspace
- Project Asset

##### Report Resources

- Audit Log
- Executive Summary
- Progress Log
- Future Report Types

##### Report Attachment Resources

The existing Report Attachment implementation shall be migrated to
consume the Resource Framework without changing existing functionality
or user workflows.

Supported attachment resources shall include:

- Images
- Documents
- PDFs
- Word documents
- HTML files
- Markdown files
- Plain text files
- Audio files
- Video files
- Spreadsheets
- Presentations
- Future supported attachment types

##### Configuration Resources

- Report Template
- Working View Preset
- Saved Search
- Dashboard Layout
- Keyboard Shortcut Profile
- Accessibility Profile
- Future configuration resources

##### Plugin Resources

- Plugin
- Plugin Configuration
- Plugin Data

##### Integration Resources

- Integration Configuration
- External Connection
- Future integration resources

Future resource types shall be registerable without architectural
redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Non-Resources

The following objects shall remain components of their parent resource
and shall **not** be treated as independent resources.

Examples include:

- Findings
- Report Metadata
- Recommendations
- Evaluation Items
- Report Statistics
- Validation Results
- Report Sections
- Future report content

These objects shall continue to be managed by their respective
frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Relationships

Resources may contain child resources.

Example hierarchy:

``` text
Project Workspace
│
├── Audit Log
│   └── Report Attachments
│
├── Executive Summary
│   └── Report Attachments
│
├── Progress Log
│   └── Report Attachments
│
├── Project Assets
│
├── Templates
│
├── Saved Searches
│
├── Working View Presets
│
└── Dashboard Layouts
```

The Resource Framework shall support additional parent-child
relationships in future releases.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Existing Framework Integration

The Resource Framework shall be consumed by:

- Project Workspace Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Window Title Framework
- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Accessibility Framework
- Future Plugin Framework
- Future Integration Framework

Existing frameworks shall not implement duplicate resource management
logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Identity

Every resource shall have a unique identity.

The Resource Framework shall assign every resource:

- Resource Identifier
- Resource Type
- Display Name
- Parent Resource (when applicable)

Resource identifiers shall remain stable for the lifetime of the
resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Lifecycle

Every resource shall support a standardized lifecycle.

Examples include:

- Create
- Open
- Close
- Save
- Save As
- Rename
- Delete
- Import
- Export
- Duplicate
- Refresh

Individual resource types may disable unsupported operations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Every resource shall expose sufficient information for assistive
technologies.

The Resource Framework shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

Accessibility behavior shall remain consistent across all resource
types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Report Attachment functionality.

Preserve all existing Project Workspace functionality.

Preserve all existing Report functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource management logic within individual frameworks.

The Resource Framework shall become the centralized foundation for
managing every user-manageable object throughout ART while preserving
existing functionality and providing a consistent architecture for
future expansion.

### Part 2 – Resource Metadata, Identification & Relationships

#### Overview

The Resource Framework shall provide a standardized metadata model for
every resource managed by ART.

Every supported resource type shall expose a consistent set of metadata
properties while allowing individual resource types to define additional
type-specific properties.

The Resource Framework shall become the authoritative source for
resource identity, metadata, ownership, and relationships.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The metadata model shall be:

- Consistent
- Extensible
- Human-readable
- Machine-readable
- Searchable
- Accessible
- Versionable
- Local-first
- Plugin-extensible
- Integration-ready

Individual frameworks shall consume this metadata rather than
maintaining duplicate implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Required Resource Metadata

Every resource shall expose the following metadata.

##### Identity

- Resource Identifier
- Resource Type
- Display Name

The Resource Identifier shall remain stable throughout the lifetime of
the resource.

Display Names may be changed by the user without affecting the Resource
Identifier.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Ownership

Every resource shall expose:

- Parent Resource (if applicable)
- Owning Project Workspace (if applicable)

Resources that are globally available shall not require a parent
resource.

Examples include:

- Global Templates
- Global Saved Searches
- Global Dashboard Layouts
- Global Keyboard Shortcut Profiles

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Lifecycle Information

Every resource shall expose:

- Date Created
- Date Modified
- Last Opened (optional)
- Last Saved
- Resource Version

These values shall be maintained automatically by the Resource
Framework.

Users shall not edit lifecycle metadata directly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Descriptive Metadata

Resources may include:

- Description
- Notes
- Tags
- Category
- Keywords

These fields shall support searching through the Universal Search
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Resource Status

Resources may expose status information appropriate to their type.

Examples include:

- Draft
- Final
- Archived
- Read-only
- Imported
- Template
- Future resource-specific states

Status values shall be extensible by future resource types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Resource Size Information

Where appropriate, the framework shall expose:

- Resource Size
- Attachment Count
- Child Resource Count

Examples:

``` text
Project Workspace

12 Reports

43 Assets

18 Templates
```

``` text
Audit Log

5 Report Attachments
```

Resource counts shall update automatically as resources are added or
removed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Type-Specific Metadata

Individual resource types may define additional metadata.

Examples include:

##### Audit Log

- Audit Scope
- Audit Date
- Organization
- Auditor
- WCAG Version

##### Executive Summary

- Summary Type
- Audience

##### Progress Log

- Completion Status
- Last Evaluation Date

##### Report Attachment

- File Name
- File Extension
- MIME Type
- Original File Size
- Imported Date

##### Project Asset

- Asset Category
- Asset Type

Future resource types may register additional metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Custom Metadata

The Resource Framework shall support custom metadata.

Plugins and future integrations shall be able to register additional
metadata fields without modifying existing resource definitions.

Custom metadata shall:

- Participate in Universal Search.
- Be available to Explorer.
- Be available to Report Views where applicable.
- Be exportable.
- Be importable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Relationships

Resources may define relationships with other resources.

Supported relationship types shall include:

- Parent
- Child
- Related
- Depends On
- References
- Derived From
- Template Of
- Created From
- Future relationship types

Relationships shall be directional.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Parent-Child Relationships

Examples include:

``` text
Project Workspace

└── Audit Log
```

``` text
Audit Log

└── Report Attachment
```

``` text
Project Workspace

└── Project Asset
```

Deleting a parent resource shall invoke the Resource Lifecycle rules
defined in a later part of this epic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Related Resources

Resources may reference other resources without ownership.

Examples include:

- A Report Template related to multiple Audit Logs.
- A Saved Search used by multiple Project Workspaces.
- A Dashboard Layout used across projects.

Related resources shall not imply ownership.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource References

The Resource Framework shall provide stable references between
resources.

References shall continue functioning when:

- Resource names change.
- Display names change.
- Parent display names change.

References shall rely on Resource Identifiers rather than visible names.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Counts

The framework shall automatically maintain resource counts.

Examples include:

``` text
Project Workspace

Reports (6)

Assets (14)

Templates (8)
```

``` text
Audit Log

Attachments (3)
```

Counts shall update immediately whenever resources change.

Counts shall be available to:

- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Universal Search
- Context Menus
- Future frameworks

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metadata Accessibility

Metadata shall be exposed programmatically.

Examples include:

- Resource name
- Resource type
- Parent resource
- Resource description
- Tags
- Status
- Resource counts

Equivalent information shall be available to:

- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation systems

Metadata shall never rely solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metadata Editing

Users shall be able to edit resource metadata where appropriate.

Examples include:

- Display Name
- Description
- Notes
- Tags
- Category

System-generated metadata shall remain read-only.

Examples include:

- Resource Identifier
- Date Created
- Last Saved
- Resource Version

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Every resource receives a unique Resource Identifier.
- Resource Identifiers remain stable.
- Display Names can be changed without affecting references.
- Lifecycle metadata updates automatically.
- Descriptive metadata participates in Universal Search.
- Type-specific metadata functions correctly.
- Custom metadata functions correctly.
- Parent-child relationships function correctly.
- Related resources function correctly.
- Resource references remain valid after renaming.
- Resource counts update automatically.
- Metadata editing functions correctly.
- Read-only metadata cannot be modified.
- Metadata is fully exposed to assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing resource functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate metadata implementations within individual frameworks.

The Resource Metadata Framework shall provide a consistent, extensible,
and accessible foundation for identifying, describing, organizing, and
relating every resource managed by ART.

### Part 3 – Resource Lifecycle, Storage, Import & Export

#### Overview

The Resource Framework shall provide a standardized lifecycle for every
resource managed by ART.

Every supported resource type shall consume the Resource Lifecycle
Framework rather than implementing its own lifecycle behavior.

The framework shall ensure that resources behave consistently regardless
of their type.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Lifecycle Framework shall be:

- Consistent
- Predictable
- Recoverable
- Non-destructive
- Local-first
- Extensible
- Accessible
- Plugin-ready
- Integration-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Standard Resource Lifecycle

Every resource shall participate in the following lifecycle, as
applicable:

- Create
- Open
- Close
- Save
- Save As
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Move
- Copy
- Import
- Export
- Archive (future)
- Restore (future)
- Delete

Individual resource types may disable unsupported operations.

Example:

A **Project Workspace** supports all lifecycle operations.

A **Dashboard Layout** may support Create, Save, Rename, Duplicate,
Import, Export, and Delete, but not Open in the traditional sense.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Creation

Users shall be able to create resources using appropriate entry points,
including:

- Menu Bar
- Global Context Menu
- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Command Palette
- Menu Bar Command Search
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Future entry points

All creation commands shall invoke the same Application Command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Opening

Resources shall open using the Resource Framework.

The framework shall determine:

- Which editor or viewer to use.
- Whether the resource is already open.
- Whether the resource supports multiple open instances.
- Whether unsaved changes require user interaction.

Opening behavior shall remain consistent across all resource types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Closing

Resources shall close consistently.

Before closing, ART shall determine whether:

- The resource has unsaved changes.
- Child resources require attention.
- Background operations are in progress.

If confirmation is required, an accessible dialog shall be displayed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Save

Saving shall update the existing resource.

Users shall not be prompted for a new location unless required by the
resource type.

The existing save behavior defined by previous epics shall remain
unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Save As

Resources supporting **Save As** shall allow users to:

- Specify a new name.
- Select a destination.
- Create a copy of the resource.

The original resource shall remain unchanged.

The copied resource shall receive a new Resource Identifier.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User-Selected Storage Locations

For resources that are stored as files, ART shall allow users to choose
where resources are saved.

During:

- Initial Save
- Save As
- Export

Users shall be able to choose:

- Local folders
- External drives
- Network locations
- Future supported storage providers

The Resource Framework shall not impose a fixed storage location.

This requirement shall remain consistent with the Project Workspace
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Duplication

Users shall be able to duplicate supported resources.

Duplicated resources shall receive:

- A new Resource Identifier.
- New lifecycle metadata.
- A copied configuration.
- A copied content structure, where applicable.

Relationships shall be updated appropriately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Renaming

Renaming a resource shall modify only its Display Name.

Resource Identifiers shall remain unchanged.

Relationships and references shall continue to function.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Movement

Where supported, users shall be able to move resources between Project
Workspaces or logical containers.

Moving a resource shall preserve:

- Resource Identifier
- Metadata
- Relationships
- History (where applicable)

Moving shall not duplicate the resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Copying

Copying shall create an independent resource.

The copied resource shall receive:

- A new Resource Identifier.
- Independent lifecycle metadata.

The copied resource shall no longer depend on the original.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Import

Supported resource types shall participate in the Resource Import
Framework.

Import shall:

- Validate the incoming resource.
- Preserve supported metadata.
- Preserve supported relationships.
- Assign new Resource Identifiers when required.
- Report import warnings or errors accessibly.

Existing import behavior defined by previous epics shall remain
unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Export

Supported resource types shall participate in the Resource Export
Framework.

Export shall preserve:

- Metadata
- Relationships
- Configuration
- Version information
- Future-compatible extension data

Export shall not modify the source resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Attachments

The existing Report Attachment implementation shall participate in the
Resource Lifecycle Framework.

Report Attachments shall support, where applicable:

- Add Attachment
- Open Attachment
- Rename Attachment
- Replace Attachment
- Remove Attachment
- Export Attachment
- Import Attachment

Existing attachment behavior shall be preserved.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Importing and Exporting Project Workspaces

Project Workspace import and export shall consume the Resource
Framework.

Workspace export shall include:

- Reports
- Report Attachments
- Project Assets
- Templates
- Saved Searches
- Working View Presets
- Dashboard Layouts
- Future supported resources

Workspace import shall restore those resources and their relationships.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Export Format Selection

When exporting a Project Workspace, users shall be able to choose the
file format used for individual exported resources where multiple
formats are supported.

Examples include report exports such as:

- Microsoft Word (.docx)
- PDF
- HTML
- Markdown
- Plain Text
- Future supported report formats

Available export formats shall remain consistent with the Report Export
Framework.

The Resource Framework shall consume the existing export infrastructure
rather than duplicating it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deletion

Deleting a resource shall invoke standardized deletion behavior.

Before deletion, ART shall determine:

- Whether child resources exist.
- Whether related resources exist.
- Whether the operation can be undone.

Users shall receive an accessible confirmation dialog.

Deletion shall not occur until confirmed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Undo and Recovery

Lifecycle operations shall integrate with the existing Undo/Redo
Framework where supported.

Future recovery features (Recycle Bin, Restore, Version History) shall
consume the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Every lifecycle operation shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

Confirmation dialogs shall:

- Receive focus appropriately.
- Expose meaningful accessible names.
- Provide descriptive explanations.
- Return focus logically after completion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Resources can be created.
- Resources can be opened.
- Resources can be closed.
- Save functions correctly.
- Save As functions correctly.
- User-selected storage locations function correctly.
- Resource duplication functions correctly.
- Resource renaming functions correctly.
- Resource movement functions correctly.
- Resource copying functions correctly.
- Import functions correctly.
- Export functions correctly.
- Project Workspace import and export preserve all supported resources
  and relationships.
- Export format selection functions correctly.
- Report Attachments participate in the Resource Lifecycle Framework.
- Deletion confirmation functions correctly.
- Undo integration functions correctly.
- Accessibility remains fully functional.
- No duplicate lifecycle implementations exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Project Workspace, Report Attachment, Import,
Export, and Report Export functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate lifecycle, storage, import, or export implementations.

The Resource Lifecycle Framework shall provide a single, consistent,
extensible, and accessible mechanism for managing every supported
resource throughout its lifetime while preserving existing ART
functionality and supporting future expansion.

### Part 4 – Resource Explorer, Search, Commands & Framework Integration

#### Overview

The Resource Framework shall integrate seamlessly with every major ART
framework.

Resources shall become the common objects consumed by Explorer,
Universal Search, Dashboard, Context Menus, Working Views, Project
Workspaces, Application Commands, and future frameworks.

Individual frameworks shall not implement independent resource discovery
or management logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Framework shall provide:

- A unified resource model.
- Consistent resource discovery.
- Consistent resource navigation.
- Consistent resource activation.
- Consistent resource management.
- Consistent accessibility.
- Extensible framework integration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Integration

The Explorer Framework shall consume the Resource Framework.

Explorer shall discover resources dynamically through the Resource
Framework rather than maintaining independent collections.

Explorer shall automatically display supported resources based on:

- Resource Type
- Parent Resource
- Resource Relationships
- User Preferences
- Current Project Workspace
- Current View

Future resource types shall automatically become available to Explorer
when registered with the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Organization

Explorer shall organize resources logically.

Example:

``` text
Project Workspace

    Reports

        Audit Log

        Executive Summary

        Progress Log

    Report Attachments

    Project Assets

    Templates

    Saved Searches

    Working View Presets

    Dashboard Layouts
```

The exact visual organization may evolve, but it shall always be derived
from the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Activation

Activating a resource from Explorer shall invoke the Resource Framework.

The framework shall determine:

- Whether the resource is already open.
- The appropriate editor or viewer.
- Whether focus should move to an existing instance.
- Whether the resource should open in a new view.

Explorer shall not implement independent activation logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Universal Search Integration

The Universal Search Framework shall consume the Resource Framework.

Search shall index:

- Resource metadata
- Resource names
- Resource descriptions
- Resource tags
- Resource keywords
- Supported resource content
- Future searchable metadata

Search shall continue to support location-aware scopes defined in
previous epics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Search Results

Search results shall identify:

- Resource Name
- Resource Type
- Parent Resource
- Matching Property
- Search Scope

Example:

``` text
Accessibility Audit

Audit Log

Project Workspace: WA.gov Audit

Matched:

Description
```

Search results shall expose equivalent information programmatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Opening Search Results

Activating a search result shall:

1.  Open the containing Project Workspace if necessary.
2.  Open the appropriate resource.
3.  Restore any required parent views.
4.  Move keyboard focus to the matching location.
5.  Highlight the matched content when appropriate.

This behavior shall consume the existing Universal Search Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Integration

Dashboard cards shall consume the Resource Framework.

Examples include:

- Recent Resources
- Favorite Resources
- Recently Modified Resources
- Recently Opened Resources
- Templates
- Saved Searches
- Working View Presets

Future Dashboard cards shall obtain resource information through the
Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Global Context Menu Integration

The Global Context Menu Framework shall consume the Resource Framework.

Context menus shall be generated based on:

- Resource Type
- Current State
- Current Selection
- Supported Operations
- Registered Commands

Resource types shall not implement independent context menu systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Standard Resource Commands

Supported resources shall automatically expose applicable commands.

Examples include:

- Open
- Open With…
- Save
- Save As…
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Import
- Export
- Properties

Unavailable commands shall appear disabled rather than removed, where
appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Properties

Every supported resource shall provide a **Properties** command.

The Properties dialog shall display:

- Display Name
- Resource Type
- Description
- Parent Resource
- Creation Date
- Last Modified
- Resource Version
- Resource Identifier (read-only)
- Type-specific metadata

Properties shall be presented consistently across resource types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Command Framework Integration

The Resource Framework shall consume the existing Application Command
Framework.

Standard commands shall include:

- Open Resource
- Close Resource
- Save Resource
- Save Resource As
- Rename Resource
- Duplicate Resource
- Delete Resource
- Import Resource
- Export Resource
- Open Properties

Future commands shall register without requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Integration

The Menu Bar shall consume the Resource Framework.

Menus shall expose only commands appropriate to the selected resource.

Examples include:

**File**

- New
- Open
- Save
- Save As
- Export

**Edit**

- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete

**View**

- Explorer
- Dashboard

The Resource Framework shall determine command availability.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Command Search Integration

Menu Bar Command Search shall index:

- Resource commands
- Resource operations
- Resource Properties
- Resource-specific actions

Command execution shall invoke the same Application Commands regardless
of entry point.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep Linking

The Resource Framework shall provide standardized deep linking.

Any framework may request:

- Open Resource
- Reveal Resource
- Reveal Parent Resource
- Open Properties
- Reveal in Explorer

The Resource Framework shall resolve these requests consistently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Registration

Every supported resource type shall register itself with the Resource
Framework.

Registration shall include:

- Resource Type
- Display Name
- Supported Operations
- Supported Commands
- Default Icon
- Parent Relationships
- Metadata Provider
- Search Provider
- Future extension points

Registration shall occur automatically during application startup or
plugin initialization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Every framework consuming the Resource Framework shall expose consistent
accessibility information.

Resource information shall include:

- Accessible Name
- Resource Type
- Parent Resource
- Current State
- Supported Operations

Equivalent information shall be available through:

- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation

Accessibility shall remain consistent regardless of the framework
through which the resource is accessed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Explorer consumes the Resource Framework.
- Universal Search consumes the Resource Framework.
- Dashboard consumes the Resource Framework.
- Global Context Menus consume the Resource Framework.
- Application Commands consume the Resource Framework.
- Menu Bar integration functions correctly.
- Menu Bar Command Search functions correctly.
- Resource activation functions correctly.
- Resource search results function correctly.
- Resource Properties function correctly.
- Deep linking functions correctly.
- Resource registration functions correctly.
- Accessibility information remains consistent across frameworks.
- No duplicate resource discovery or management implementations exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Explorer, Universal Search, Dashboard, Context
Menu, and Application Command functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource discovery, activation, navigation, or command
implementations.

The Resource Framework shall serve as the single authoritative source
for resource discovery, activation, management, and integration across
every current and future ART framework.

### Part 5 – Resource Service API, Registration & Extensibility

#### Overview

The Resource Framework shall provide a centralized **Resource Service
API** that serves as the authoritative interface for discovering,
creating, opening, modifying, querying, and managing resources
throughout ART.

All ART frameworks, plugins, and future integrations shall interact with
resources exclusively through the Resource Service API.

Direct access to resource storage or resource implementations shall be
prohibited except within the Resource Framework itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Service API shall be:

- Centralized
- Framework-independent
- Extensible
- Strongly typed
- Event-driven
- Local-first
- Plugin-ready
- Integration-ready
- Accessible
- Versionable

The API shall hide implementation details from consuming frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Service Responsibilities

The Resource Service API shall provide:

- Resource registration
- Resource discovery
- Resource lookup
- Resource creation
- Resource opening
- Resource lifecycle management
- Resource relationship management
- Resource metadata access
- Resource querying
- Resource event notification
- Resource validation
- Future resource services

Individual frameworks shall consume these services rather than
implementing duplicate logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Registration

Every supported resource type shall register itself with the Resource
Framework during application initialization.

Registration shall include:

- Resource Type
- Display Name
- Default Icon
- Parent Resource Types
- Supported Lifecycle Operations
- Metadata Provider
- Search Provider
- Properties Provider
- Context Menu Provider
- Default Editor or Viewer
- Supported Import Formats
- Supported Export Formats
- Accessibility Provider
- Future extension points

Registration shall occur automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Providers

Each resource type shall provide standardized providers.

Examples include:

##### Metadata Provider

Returns resource metadata.

##### Search Provider

Indexes searchable content.

##### Properties Provider

Supplies information for the Properties dialog.

##### Editor Provider

Opens the appropriate editor or viewer.

##### Export Provider

Supports exporting the resource.

##### Import Provider

Supports importing the resource.

##### Accessibility Provider

Supplies accessibility metadata and behaviors.

Future providers shall be registerable without modifying the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Discovery

Frameworks shall be able to discover resources by requesting:

- All Resources
- Resource Type
- Parent Resource
- Project Workspace
- Current Report
- Resource Identifier
- Tag
- Category
- Metadata
- Future query criteria

Discovery shall remain consistent regardless of resource type.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Queries

The Resource Service API shall support structured queries.

Examples include:

- All Audit Logs
- All Report Attachments
- All Templates
- Resources modified today
- Resources containing a specific tag
- Resources belonging to the active Project Workspace
- Future query types

The Universal Search Framework shall consume these query capabilities
where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Events

The Resource Framework shall publish standardized events.

Examples include:

- Resource Created
- Resource Opened
- Resource Closed
- Resource Modified
- Resource Saved
- Resource Renamed
- Resource Deleted
- Resource Imported
- Resource Exported
- Resource Relationship Changed
- Resource Metadata Changed

Future events shall be supported without architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Event Subscribers

Frameworks may subscribe to Resource Framework events.

Examples include:

- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Universal Search
- Working Views
- Project Workspace Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Future plugins
- Future integrations

Subscribers shall update automatically when resources change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Event Consistency

Every resource event shall include:

- Resource Identifier
- Resource Type
- Event Type
- Timestamp
- Parent Resource (if applicable)

Additional resource-specific information may also be included.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Validation

The Resource Framework shall validate resources before performing
lifecycle operations.

Validation shall include:

- Required metadata
- Resource relationships
- Parent resource validity
- Import compatibility
- Export compatibility
- Resource integrity
- Future validation rules

Validation failures shall be communicated accessibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Type Extensions

Future plugins shall be able to register entirely new resource types.

Example:

``` text
Accessibility Checklist
```

After registration:

- Explorer shall display it.
- Universal Search shall index it.
- Dashboard shall recognize it.
- Context Menus shall support it.
- Properties shall display correctly.
- Application Commands shall function correctly.

No existing framework shall require modification.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Capabilities

Rather than hardcoding behavior by resource type, frameworks shall
determine supported operations through declared capabilities.

Examples include:

- Can Open
- Can Save
- Can Save As
- Can Duplicate
- Can Rename
- Can Delete
- Can Import
- Can Export
- Has Properties
- Supports Search
- Supports Attachments
- Supports Child Resources

Frameworks shall enable or disable commands based on capabilities rather
than resource type.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Versioning

The Resource Service API shall expose a framework version.

Plugins and future integrations shall verify compatibility before
registering new resource types.

Version negotiation shall support future backward compatibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Error Handling

The Resource Service API shall provide consistent error handling.

Examples include:

- Resource not found
- Invalid metadata
- Unsupported operation
- Invalid relationship
- Import failure
- Export failure
- Validation failure

Errors shall be:

- Accessible
- Human-readable
- Loggable
- Recoverable where possible

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Resource Service API shall expose sufficient accessibility
information for every registered resource type.

Registered providers shall support:

- Accessible Names
- Accessible Descriptions
- Roles
- States
- Properties

Accessibility shall remain consistent across all resource types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Resource registration functions correctly.
- Providers register correctly.
- Resource discovery functions correctly.
- Structured queries function correctly.
- Resource events are published correctly.
- Framework subscriptions update automatically.
- Validation occurs before lifecycle operations.
- Resource capabilities determine command availability.
- New resource types can be registered without modifying existing
  frameworks.
- Error handling functions correctly.
- Accessibility providers expose appropriate information.
- No framework bypasses the Resource Service API.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource registration, discovery, querying, validation,
or event logic.

The Resource Service API shall become the single authoritative interface
through which every current and future ART framework, plugin, and
integration discovers, manages, validates, and interacts with resources.

### Part 6 – Resource Integrity, Recovery, Versioning & Future Collaboration Support

#### Overview

The Resource Framework shall provide mechanisms that preserve the
integrity, reliability, recoverability, and future extensibility of
resources throughout their lifecycle.

This part defines:

- Resource integrity
- Relationship integrity
- Recovery
- Versioning
- Backup
- Conflict detection
- Future collaboration support

These features shall build upon the existing local-first architecture
while preparing ART for future collaboration, synchronization, and
integration features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Integrity Framework shall be:

- Reliable
- Recoverable
- Non-destructive
- Local-first
- Extensible
- Version-aware
- Collaboration-ready
- Accessible

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Integrity

The Resource Framework shall maintain resource integrity at all times.

Integrity includes:

- Resource identity
- Metadata
- Parent-child relationships
- Related resource references
- Attachments
- Imported resources
- Exported resources
- Future relationships

Resources shall never become orphaned without explicit user action.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Integrity

When resources are moved, renamed, imported, exported, duplicated, or
restored:

Relationships shall remain valid whenever possible.

Examples include:

``` text
Project Workspace

    Audit Log

        Report Attachments
```

Renaming:

``` text
Accessibility Audit
```

to:

``` text
WA.gov Accessibility Audit
```

shall not break:

- Report Attachments
- Saved Searches
- Working View Presets
- Dashboard references
- Explorer references

Relationships shall rely on Resource Identifiers rather than display
names.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Integrity Validation

The Resource Framework shall periodically validate:

- Resource identity
- Parent resources
- Child resources
- Related resources
- Attachments
- Metadata
- Import integrity
- Export integrity

Validation may occur:

- During startup
- During import
- During export
- During save
- During recovery
- On demand

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Integrity Repair

Where possible, ART shall automatically repair:

- Missing references
- Invalid parent relationships
- Duplicate identifiers
- Metadata inconsistencies

If automatic repair is not possible:

Users shall receive an accessible explanation and options to resolve the
issue.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Versioning

Every resource shall maintain a version number.

Version information shall support:

- Import compatibility
- Export compatibility
- Migration
- Plugin compatibility
- Future collaboration

Versioning shall not be visible unless needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Migration

When opening older resources:

ART shall:

- Detect the resource version.
- Determine compatibility.
- Apply migrations where appropriate.

Migration shall preserve:

- Content
- Metadata
- Relationships
- Attachments
- Configuration

Migration failures shall be reported accessibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Automatic Backup

ART may maintain automatic backups of selected resources.

Examples include:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Templates
- Dashboard Layouts
- Saved Searches
- Working View Presets

Backup behavior shall be configurable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Backup Options

Users may configure:

- Backup frequency
- Backup location
- Backup retention
- Backup type

Users shall be able to select:

- Local storage
- External drives
- Network locations
- Future storage providers

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recovery

Users shall be able to recover:

- Deleted resources (future)
- Damaged resources
- Backup versions
- Previous versions (future)

Recovery shall preserve:

- Metadata
- Relationships
- Attachments
- Resource identifiers where appropriate

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Recycle Bin

The Resource Framework shall support a future Recycle Bin feature.

Deleted resources may be:

- Restorable
- Permanently deleted
- Automatically removed after a retention period

This feature shall not require architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Conflict Detection

Future synchronization and collaboration features may create conflicts.

The Resource Framework shall prepare for:

- Duplicate resources
- Simultaneous edits
- Imported conflicts
- Synchronization conflicts

Conflict information shall include:

- Resource
- Version
- Timestamp
- Change source

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Collaboration Support

Although ART is currently local-first, the Resource Framework shall
support future collaboration features.

Examples include:

- Shared Project Workspaces
- Shared Templates
- Shared Saved Searches
- Shared Dashboard Layouts
- Shared Working View Presets
- Shared Attachments

Collaboration shall consume the Resource Framework rather than replacing
it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Locking (Future)

Future collaboration features may require:

- Resource locks
- Edit notifications
- Shared ownership
- Conflict resolution

The Resource Framework shall support these features without
architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future History Support

Resources may support future history features.

Examples include:

- Previous versions
- Change history
- Restore points
- Audit history

The Resource Framework shall support these capabilities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Logging

The Resource Framework shall generate structured logs for:

- Create
- Open
- Save
- Rename
- Import
- Export
- Delete
- Recovery
- Migration

Logs shall support:

- Troubleshooting
- Diagnostics
- Future audit capabilities

Logging shall respect privacy requirements.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Integrity, migration, backup, recovery, and conflict dialogs shall:

- Be keyboard accessible.
- Be screen reader accessible.
- Support refreshable braille displays.
- Support voice navigation.
- Support speech dictation.

Messages shall be:

- Clear
- Concise
- Actionable

Errors shall never rely solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Resource relationships remain intact.
- Renaming does not break references.
- Moving resources preserves relationships.
- Import preserves metadata.
- Export preserves metadata.
- Version information functions correctly.
- Migration functions correctly.
- Backups function correctly.
- Recovery functions correctly.
- Integrity validation functions correctly.
- Automatic repair functions correctly.
- Logging functions correctly.
- Future collaboration requirements are supported.
- Accessibility remains intact.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing resource functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate integrity, migration, backup, recovery, or versioning
logic.

The Resource Framework shall provide a reliable, recoverable, and
future-ready foundation that preserves resource integrity while
preparing ART for future collaboration, synchronization, and enterprise
features.

## Epic 34 – Plugin Framework

### Part 1 – Plugin Framework Overview, Architecture & Design Principles

#### Overview

Implement a centralized **Plugin Framework** that enables ART to be
extended through installable plugins without requiring modifications to
the core application.

The Plugin Framework shall provide a standardized architecture for
discovering, loading, registering, configuring, enabling, disabling,
updating, and removing plugins.

Plugins shall integrate with existing ART frameworks through
well-defined extension points rather than modifying core application
behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The Plugin Framework shall enable developers to extend ART by adding:

- Resource Types
- Report Types
- Import Providers
- Export Providers
- Dashboard Cards
- Explorer Nodes
- Context Menu Commands
- Application Commands
- Menu Items
- Toolbars
- Keyboard Shortcuts
- Search Providers
- Working View Providers
- Validation Rules
- Accessibility Standards
- WCAG Extensions
- Section 508 Extensions
- EN 301 549 Extensions
- Custom Accessibility Standards
- AI Providers
- Integration Providers
- Future extension types

The framework shall allow ART to evolve without requiring changes to its
core architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Design Goals

The Plugin Framework shall be:

- Modular
- Extensible
- Secure
- Discoverable
- Local-first
- Accessible
- Version-aware
- Resource-aware
- Framework-driven
- Integration-ready
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Core Principles

Plugins shall:

- Extend ART rather than replace it.
- Consume existing ART frameworks.
- Register capabilities instead of modifying application code.
- Respect accessibility requirements.
- Participate in centralized command, search, explorer, and resource
  systems.

No plugin shall bypass established ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Definition

Within ART, a **Plugin** is a packaged extension that registers one or
more capabilities with the application through the Plugin Framework.

Plugins may provide:

- New functionality
- New resource types
- New commands
- New reports
- New validation rules
- New import/export formats
- New accessibility standards
- New integrations

Plugins shall not require modification of existing ART source code.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Architecture

The Plugin Framework shall serve as a coordination layer between plugins
and existing ART frameworks.

Plugins shall integrate through existing frameworks, including:

- Resource Framework
- Project Workspace Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Window Title Framework
- Accessibility Framework
- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Future Integration Framework

Plugins shall never implement duplicate framework functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Lifecycle

Every plugin shall participate in a standardized lifecycle.

Supported lifecycle operations shall include:

- Discover
- Validate
- Install
- Register
- Load
- Initialize
- Enable
- Disable
- Update
- Unload
- Uninstall

The Plugin Framework shall manage the lifecycle consistently for all
plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Built-in vs External Plugins

The framework shall support two categories of plugins.

### Built-in Plugins

Built-in plugins are shipped with ART.

Examples may include:

- WCAG Standards
- Section 508 Standards
- EN 301 549 Standards
- Default Report Templates
- Built-in Export Providers

Built-in plugins shall use the same Plugin Framework as external
plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### External Plugins

External plugins may be installed by users or organizations.

Examples include:

- Organization-specific report templates
- Custom accessibility standards
- Proprietary integrations
- AI providers
- Industry-specific reporting extensions

External plugins shall behave consistently with built-in plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Independence

Each plugin shall remain independent.

A failure in one plugin shall not prevent:

- ART from starting.
- Other plugins from loading.
- Existing projects from opening.
- Core application functionality from operating.

Plugin failures shall be isolated and reported accessibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Metadata

Every plugin shall provide standardized metadata, including:

- Plugin Identifier
- Display Name
- Description
- Version
- Author
- Publisher
- License
- Homepage (optional)
- Documentation URL (optional)
- Supported ART Version
- Plugin Dependencies (optional)

The Plugin Framework shall validate metadata during installation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Framework Integration

Plugins shall register capabilities through the appropriate framework.

Examples include:

| Capability              | Framework                     |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Resource Types          | Resource Framework            |
| Commands                | Application Command Framework |
| Search Providers        | Universal Search Framework    |
| Explorer Nodes          | Explorer Framework            |
| Dashboard Cards         | Dashboard Framework           |
| Context Menu Items      | Global Context Menu Framework |
| Keyboard Shortcuts      | Keyboard Shortcut Manager     |
| Report Types            | Resource Framework            |
| Import/Export Providers | Resource Framework            |
| Working Views           | Report Views Framework        |

Plugins shall never modify framework implementations directly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility

The Plugin Framework shall require all plugins to comply with ART
accessibility requirements.

Plugins shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

Plugins shall consume the existing Accessibility Framework rather than
implementing independent accessibility behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate framework implementations.

The Plugin Framework shall provide a secure, extensible, and accessible
foundation for extending ART while preserving the consistency,
reliability, and accessibility of the core application.

### Part 2 – Plugin & Package Registration, Existing Workflow Integration & Extension Points

### Overview

The Plugin Framework shall provide a standardized registration system
that enables plugins and packages to extend ART while consuming existing
ART frameworks and workflows.

The Plugin Framework shall serve as the central registration,
validation, lifecycle, compatibility, and discovery service for
executable plugins and non-executable packages.

The Plugin Framework shall **not** duplicate existing user workflows for
importing, exporting, connecting, configuring, or managing supported
extension types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Design Goals

The Plugin Framework shall be:

- Modular
- Extensible
- Accessible
- Local-first
- Secure
- Discoverable
- Version-aware
- Resource-aware
- Framework-driven
- Integration-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugins vs. Packages

### Plugins

Plugins extend application behavior.

Examples include:

- AI Providers
- Import Providers
- Export Providers
- Validation Providers
- Search Providers
- Dashboard Providers
- Explorer Providers
- Report View Providers
- Integration Providers
- Future executable extensions

Plugins may execute application code.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Packages

Packages provide reusable content without executing application code.

Examples include:

- Accessibility Standards
- Report Templates
- Dashboard Layouts
- Keyboard Shortcut Profiles
- Working View Presets
- Saved Searches
- Sample Projects
- Icon Sets
- AI Prompt Libraries
- Documentation Packages
- Future content packages

Packages shall be treated as Resources by the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Existing ART Workflows

The Plugin Framework shall consume existing ART workflows wherever
possible.

The Plugin Framework shall **not** replace or duplicate existing
user-facing workflows.

Instead, it shall provide:

- Registration
- Validation
- Compatibility checking
- Metadata management
- Lifecycle management
- Discovery
- Version management

after the existing workflow completes successfully.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Standards

ART already provides an **Import Accessibility Standard** workflow.

The Plugin Framework shall **not** create another workflow for importing
accessibility standards.

Instead, after an accessibility standard is imported, the Plugin
Framework shall:

- Validate the package.
- Register the package.
- Register the accessibility standard with the Resource Framework.
- Register searchable content with Universal Search.
- Register report compatibility.
- Register Accessibility Lookup Tool compatibility.
- Register Report Viewer compatibility.
- Register Report Builder compatibility.
- Register Report Export compatibility.
- Register Explorer compatibility.
- Register Dashboard compatibility.

The existing Import Accessibility Standard workflow shall remain the
authoritative user interface.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Integrations

ART already provides a **Connect Integrations** workflow.

The Plugin Framework shall not duplicate this workflow.

After an integration has been configured, the Plugin Framework shall:

- Register the integration provider.
- Register supported commands.
- Register Resource Providers.
- Register Search Providers.
- Register synchronization providers.
- Register metadata.

The existing Connect Integrations workflow shall remain unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Report Templates

The existing Template import workflow shall remain the authoritative
method for importing templates.

After a template has been imported, the Plugin Framework shall:

- Validate the template.
- Register the template.
- Register template metadata.
- Register searchable metadata.
- Register template resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Keyboard Shortcut Profiles

Keyboard shortcut profiles shall continue to be managed through the
existing Keyboard Manager.

The Plugin Framework shall register imported profiles after they have
been imported.

The Plugin Framework shall not introduce a second keyboard profile
manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Working View Presets

Working View Presets shall continue to use the Working View Framework.

The Plugin Framework shall register imported presets after they have
been created or imported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dashboard Layouts

Dashboard Layouts shall continue to use the existing Dashboard
Framework.

The Plugin Framework shall register layouts and metadata.

Dashboard management shall remain within the Dashboard Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Project Workspaces

Project Workspace import and export shall continue to use the Project
Workspace Framework.

The Plugin Framework shall register resources after the workspace has
been opened or imported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Repository Structure

The ART repository shall include a dedicated packages directory.

Example:

``` text
/packages

    /accessibility-standards

    /report-templates

    /dashboard-layouts

    /keyboard-profiles

    /working-view-presets

    /saved-searches

    /sample-data

    /future-package-types
```

Future package categories shall be addable without modifying the Plugin
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility Standards Packages

Copilot shall create complete JSON packages for:

- WCAG 2.0 (if not already present)
- Section 508
- EN 301 549
- European Accessibility Act (EAA)

These packages shall:

- Use the same schema as the built-in WCAG standards.
- Use the same metadata model.
- Use the same validation rules.
- Use the same identifier format.
- Use the same resource model.
- Use the same report compatibility model.
- Use the same Lookup Tool compatibility model.

Copilot shall carefully verify every Success Criterion, requirement,
reference, and metadata field for completeness and correctness before
committing these packages.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Extension Points

The Plugin Framework shall expose standardized extension points for:

- Resource Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Context Menu Framework
- Accessibility Framework
- Import Framework
- Export Framework
- Future frameworks

Plugins shall register through extension points rather than modifying
framework implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Registration

Executable plugins shall register:

- Commands
- Providers
- Resource Types
- Search Providers
- Dashboard Providers
- Explorer Providers
- Context Menu Providers
- Validation Providers
- AI Providers
- Future providers

Registration shall occur automatically during plugin initialization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Package Registration

Packages shall register:

- Metadata
- Resource Types (where applicable)
- Searchable Content
- Templates
- Accessibility Standards
- Dashboard Layouts
- Working View Presets
- Keyboard Profiles
- Future content types

Registration shall occur automatically after successful import through
the appropriate ART workflow.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Documentation

Copilot shall update:

- README.md
- HELP.md
- USER-GUIDE.md
- ARCHITECTURE.md

to clearly explain:

### Plugins

- What plugins are.
- How plugins differ from packages.
- How plugins are installed.
- How plugins register with ART.
- How plugins are updated.
- Plugin lifecycle.

### Packages

- What packages are.
- Supported package types.
- Repository organization.
- Existing import workflows.
- Package lifecycle.
- Compatibility.

The documentation shall explicitly explain that most package types are
imported through their existing ART workflows rather than through the
Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Package Authoring Guide

Copilot shall create:

**PACKAGE-AUTHORING-GUIDE.md**

The guide shall include:

- Package architecture
- JSON schema
- Required fields
- Optional fields
- Metadata
- Versioning
- Validation
- Accessibility requirements
- Best practices
- Complete sample packages

Including complete, annotated JSON examples.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Developer Guide

Copilot shall create:

**PLUGIN-DEVELOPER-GUIDE.md**

The guide shall include:

- Plugin architecture
- Registration
- Lifecycle
- Providers
- Extension Points
- Resource Framework integration
- Accessibility requirements
- Versioning
- Best practices
- Complete sample plugins

Including commented code examples.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Validation

Verify that:

- Existing Import Accessibility Standard workflow remains unchanged.
- Existing Connect Integrations workflow remains unchanged.
- Existing Template import workflow remains unchanged.
- Existing Dashboard workflow remains unchanged.
- Existing Keyboard Manager remains unchanged.
- Existing Working View workflow remains unchanged.
- Plugins register correctly.
- Packages register correctly.
- Accessibility standards function correctly throughout ART.
- Documentation accurately describes plugins, packages, and existing
  workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART workflows.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate:

- Import workflows
- Export workflows
- Integration workflows
- Dashboard workflows
- Working View workflows
- Keyboard management workflows

The Plugin Framework shall provide centralized registration, lifecycle
management, validation, compatibility checking, and discovery for
plugins and packages while preserving the existing user workflows that
already exist throughout ART.

### Part 3 – Plugin & Package Manager, Lifecycle Management & Extension Administration

### Overview

The Plugin Framework shall provide a centralized **Plugin & Package
Manager** for managing installed plugins and packages throughout ART.

The Plugin & Package Manager shall provide lifecycle management,
validation, compatibility checking, configuration, diagnostics, and
documentation for extensions.

The Plugin & Package Manager **shall not duplicate existing ART
workflows** for importing accessibility standards, connecting
integrations, importing templates, managing keyboard profiles, or
managing other resource-specific content.

Instead, it shall act as the centralized administration console for all
installed extensions after they have been added through their existing
workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Design Goals

The Plugin & Package Manager shall be:

- Accessible
- Easy to use
- Discoverable
- Keyboard-first
- Local-first
- Safe
- Extensible
- Self-documenting
- Consistent with existing ART architecture

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Location

The Plugin & Package Manager shall be available from:

**Application Settings → Developer & Administrator → Plugin & Package
Manager**

Organizations may optionally expose a simplified **Extensions** page for
general users.

All extension management interfaces shall consume the same Plugin
Framework services.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Responsibilities

The Plugin & Package Manager shall provide centralized management for:

- Installed Plugins
- Installed Packages
- Package Metadata
- Plugin Metadata
- Extension Registration
- Version Information
- Compatibility Information
- Diagnostics
- Validation
- Dependencies
- Configuration
- Future Extension Types

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Responsibilities Specifically Excluded

The Plugin & Package Manager shall **not** replace or duplicate existing
workflows including, but not limited to:

- Import Accessibility Standard
- Connect Integrations
- Import Report Template
- Keyboard Profile Management
- Dashboard Layout Management
- Working View Preset Management
- Project Workspace Import/Export

Those workflows shall remain the authoritative user interfaces for their

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Plugin Management

The Plugin & Package Manager shall allow users to:

### Compatibility Checking

### Validation

Users shall be able to validate any installed extension.

Validation shall include:

- Registration

- Accessibility Requirements
- Version Compatibility
- Schema Validation
- Integrity Checks

Validation results shall be human-readable and programmatically exposed.

### Import and Export of Extension Configuration

Users shall be able to export:

- Package Configuration

Users shall be able to restore those configurations on another ART

This feature shall export configuration information only.

It shall **not** replace existing import/export workflows for individual
resources.

## Plugin & Package Manager

The Plugin & Package Manager and Plugin Installation Wizard shall

Verify that:

- Plugins uninstall correctly.

- Packages are automatically registered after import.
- Existing Accessibility Standard import workflow remains unchanged.
- Existing Connect Integrations workflow remains unchanged.
- Existing Template import workflow remains unchanged.

- Compatibility checking functions correctly.
- Validation functions correctly.

  workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Preserve all existing import, export, and integration workflows.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate:

- Import workflows
- Export workflows
- Integration workflows
- Dashboard workflows
- Working View workflows
- Keyboard management workflows
- Accessibility Standard management workflows

The Plugin & Package Manager shall provide a centralized, accessible,
and user-friendly administrative interface for managing plugins and
packages while preserving the existing ART workflows that users already
rely upon. It shall serve as the authoritative interface for extension
lifecycle management, validation, compatibility, diagnostics, and
configuration without replacing the specialized workflows implemented
elsewhere in ART.

### Part 4 – Plugin Discovery, Loading, Dependencies & Security

#### Overview

The Plugin Framework shall provide a secure, reliable, and extensible
mechanism for discovering, validating, loading, initializing, and
unloading plugins during application startup and throughout the
application's lifetime.

Plugins shall be isolated from one another and from the core application
wherever practical. A failure in one plugin shall not prevent ART or
other plugins from functioning.

The Plugin Framework shall also provide dependency management, version
compatibility checking, and security validation before allowing a plugin
to execute.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Plugin Framework shall be:

- Secure
- Reliable
- Predictable
- Isolated
- Recoverable
- Extensible
- Version-aware
- Accessible
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Discovery

During application startup, the Plugin Framework shall automatically
discover installed plugins.

Discovery shall include:

- Built-in plugins
- User-installed plugins
- Organization-managed plugins
- Future plugin repositories

Plugin discovery shall occur before plugin initialization.

Packages imported through existing ART workflows shall not participate
in executable plugin discovery.

Instead, packages shall be discovered through the Resource Framework
after successful registration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Discovery Order

Plugin discovery shall occur in the following order:

1.  Built-in Plugins
2.  Organization-managed Plugins
3.  User-installed Plugins

If duplicate plugin identifiers are encountered:

- The duplicate shall not be loaded.
- An accessible error shall be presented.
- The conflict shall be recorded in the application log.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Validation

Before loading a plugin, the Plugin Framework shall validate:

- Plugin Identifier
- Version
- Manifest
- Metadata
- Dependencies
- ART version compatibility
- Duplicate registrations
- Required providers
- Required permissions
- Package integrity

Plugins that fail validation shall not be loaded.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Manifest

Every executable plugin shall include a manifest describing the plugin.

The manifest shall contain, at minimum:

- Plugin Identifier
- Display Name
- Version
- Description
- Author
- Publisher
- License
- Supported ART Version
- Required Dependencies
- Optional Dependencies
- Registered Providers
- Registered Commands
- Registered Resources
- Requested Permissions
- Minimum Plugin Framework Version

The Plugin Framework shall validate the manifest before loading the
plugin.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Initialization

After successful validation:

The Plugin Framework shall:

1.  Load the plugin.
2.  Initialize the plugin.
3.  Register providers.
4.  Register commands.
5.  Register resources.
6.  Register search providers.
7.  Register dashboard providers.
8.  Register Explorer providers.
9.  Register context menu providers.
10. Publish a Plugin Loaded event.

Initialization failures shall not prevent ART from starting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dependency Management

Plugins may declare:

##### Required Dependencies

The plugin cannot load unless these dependencies are available.

##### Optional Dependencies

The plugin shall continue to function without these dependencies but may
disable certain features.

Dependency failures shall be communicated accessibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dependency Resolution

The Plugin Framework shall:

- Detect missing dependencies.
- Detect incompatible versions.
- Detect circular dependencies.
- Detect duplicate providers.
- Detect incompatible registrations.

Dependency resolution shall occur before plugin initialization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Permissions
