Plugins shall explicitly declare the application capabilities they
require.

Examples include:

- Register Commands
- Register Resources
- Register Search Providers
- Register Dashboard Cards
- Register Explorer Nodes
- Register Context Menu Items
- Read Project Resources
- Modify Project Resources
- Export Reports
- Import Resources
- Connect to External Services
- Future capabilities

Users and administrators shall be able to review these permissions
before installation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Security Principles

Plugins shall operate using the principle of least privilege.

A plugin shall only receive the permissions explicitly granted through
the Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not bypass ART frameworks to obtain additional
capabilities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Isolation

Where practical, plugins shall execute independently.

A failure in one plugin shall not:

- Crash ART.
- Prevent other plugins from loading.
- Prevent reports from opening.
- Prevent Project Workspaces from loading.
- Corrupt Resource Framework data.

Plugin failures shall be isolated and recoverable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Events

The Plugin Framework shall publish standardized lifecycle events,
including:

- Plugin Discovered
- Plugin Validated
- Plugin Loaded
- Plugin Enabled
- Plugin Disabled
- Plugin Updated
- Plugin Unloaded
- Plugin Uninstalled
- Plugin Validation Failed
- Plugin Dependency Failed

Other ART frameworks may subscribe to these events.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Registration

Plugins shall register with existing ART frameworks only through
approved extension points.

Examples include:

- Resource Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Accessibility Framework

Direct modification of framework implementations shall not be permitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Diagnostics

The Plugin Framework shall maintain diagnostic information for each
plugin.

Diagnostic information may include:

- Load time
- Initialization time
- Version
- Dependencies
- Registered providers
- Registered commands
- Validation status
- Error history

Diagnostic information shall be viewable through the Plugin & Package
Manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Logging

The Plugin Framework shall log:

- Discovery
- Validation
- Initialization
- Registration
- Enable
- Disable
- Update
- Unload
- Uninstall
- Errors
- Warnings

Logs shall support troubleshooting while respecting ART's privacy and
local-first principles.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Plugin loading, validation, dependency, and security information shall
be fully accessible.

Status information shall be available to:

- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Keyboard-only users

Errors and warnings shall never rely solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Built-in plugins are discovered correctly.
- User-installed plugins are discovered correctly.
- Plugin manifests validate correctly.
- Invalid plugins are rejected.
- Dependency resolution functions correctly.
- Required permissions are validated.
- Plugin initialization functions correctly.
- Plugin failures do not affect ART stability.
- Framework registration functions correctly.
- Lifecycle events are published correctly.
- Diagnostic information is available.
- Logging functions correctly.
- Accessibility information is exposed correctly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource registration, command registration, search
registration, or existing import and integration workflows.

The Plugin Framework shall provide a secure, robust, and extensible
foundation for executable plugins by managing discovery, validation,
loading, dependency resolution, permissions, and lifecycle events while
preserving the stability, accessibility, and integrity of the core ART
application.

### Part 5 – Plugin Communication, Services, APIs & Framework Integration

#### Overview

The Plugin Framework shall provide a standardized communication model
that allows plugins to safely interact with ART and with other plugins
through well-defined services and extension points.

Plugins shall never communicate by directly accessing another plugin's
implementation or internal state.

Instead, all communication shall occur through registered services,
providers, events, and framework APIs.

This architecture shall preserve loose coupling, maintainability,
extensibility, and long-term compatibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The communication architecture shall be:

- Framework-driven
- Service-oriented
- Loosely coupled
- Extensible
- Version-aware
- Secure
- Accessible
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework-First Integration

Plugins shall integrate with ART through existing framework APIs.

Examples include:

- Resource Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Accessibility Framework
- Window Title Framework
- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Future frameworks

Plugins shall not directly modify framework implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Services

Plugins may register reusable services.

Examples include:

- AI Services
- Translation Services
- Report Analysis Services
- Import Services
- Export Services
- Validation Services
- Synchronization Services
- Notification Services
- Future services

Services shall be discoverable through the Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Service Registration

Each service shall register:

- Service Identifier
- Display Name
- Plugin Owner
- Service Version
- Description
- Supported Interfaces
- Dependencies
- Required Permissions

The Plugin Framework shall validate service registrations before making
them available.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Service Discovery

Plugins shall be able to discover registered services through the Plugin
Framework.

Discovery may be performed using:

- Service Identifier
- Service Type
- Service Category
- Registered Interface
- Plugin Identifier

Direct references to plugin implementations shall not be permitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Service Versioning

Every service shall expose version information.

The Plugin Framework shall verify compatibility before allowing one
plugin to consume another plugin's service.

Version incompatibilities shall prevent service registration while
allowing ART and unrelated plugins to continue operating.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Events

Plugins may publish events through the Plugin Framework.

Examples include:

- Analysis Completed
- Validation Completed
- Import Completed
- Export Completed
- AI Response Generated
- Synchronization Completed
- Resource Processed
- Future events

Events shall use a standardized event model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Event Subscriptions

Plugins may subscribe to:

- Framework events
- Resource events
- Plugin lifecycle events
- Application events
- User-defined plugin events

Subscriptions shall be managed by the Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not subscribe directly to another plugin.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Registration

Plugins may register Application Commands.

Registered commands shall automatically participate in:

- Menu Bar Command Search
- Keyboard Manager
- Global Context Menus
- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Future command consumers

Registered commands shall consume the existing Application Command
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcut Registration

Plugins may register optional keyboard shortcuts.

Registered shortcuts shall:

- Appear in Keyboard Manager.
- Be configurable.
- Be removable.
- Support user customization.
- Participate in keyboard conflict detection.

Plugins shall not hardcode keyboard shortcuts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Universal Search Integration

Plugins may contribute searchable content through the Universal Search
Framework.

Examples include:

- Resources
- Commands
- Templates
- AI Prompts
- Documentation
- Validation Rules
- Accessibility Standards
- Future searchable content

Plugins shall register searchable content through Search Providers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Integration

Plugins may register Explorer Providers.

Examples include:

- New Resource Types
- Virtual Nodes
- Resource Categories
- Organization Views

Explorer shall consume registered providers automatically.

Plugins shall not directly modify Explorer navigation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Dashboard Cards
- Dashboard Widgets
- Dashboard Metrics
- Dashboard Commands

Dashboard providers shall register through the Dashboard Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menu Integration

Plugins may contribute context-sensitive commands.

Commands shall appear only when applicable.

Examples include:

- Analyze Report with AI
- Translate Report
- Export to Organization Format
- Run Organization Validation Rules

Plugins shall register context menu providers through the Global Context
Menu Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Framework Integration

Plugins shall register:

- Resource Types
- Resource Providers
- Metadata Providers
- Property Providers
- Search Providers

The Resource Framework shall remain the authoritative source for
resource discovery and management.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report View Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Working Views
- Filters
- Groupings
- Analysis Views
- Visualization Providers

The Report Views Framework shall remain the authoritative framework for
report presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Requirements

Every plugin service shall expose sufficient accessibility information.

Where applicable, services shall provide:

- Accessible Names
- Accessible Descriptions
- Status messages
- Progress notifications
- Error information

Plugins shall consume ART's Accessibility Framework rather than
implementing independent accessibility behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Error Isolation

If a plugin service fails:

- The service shall fail independently.
- Other services shall continue functioning.
- ART shall remain operational.
- Users shall receive an accessible error message.
- The failure shall be logged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Plugin services register correctly.
- Services can be discovered correctly.
- Service versioning functions correctly.
- Commands register correctly.
- Keyboard shortcuts register correctly.
- Search Providers function correctly.
- Explorer Providers function correctly.
- Dashboard Providers function correctly.
- Context Menu Providers function correctly.
- Resource Providers function correctly.
- Report View Providers function correctly.
- Plugin events function correctly.
- Event subscriptions function correctly.
- Accessibility information is exposed correctly.
- Service failures do not affect unrelated plugins.
- ART remains stable when plugins fail.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate framework APIs or communication mechanisms.

Plugins shall communicate exclusively through standardized framework
APIs, registered services, providers, and events. The Plugin Framework
shall provide the single authoritative mechanism for plugin discovery,
service registration, inter-plugin communication, and framework
integration while preserving the modularity, stability, accessibility,
and long-term maintainability of ART.

### Part 6 – Plugin Configuration, Settings, Permissions & Administrative Policies

#### Overview

The Plugin Framework shall provide a centralized configuration system
that allows plugins to expose configurable settings while maintaining a
consistent user experience throughout ART.

Plugin configuration shall integrate with the existing **Application
Settings** architecture and shall not introduce separate or inconsistent
settings interfaces.

The framework shall also provide administrative policy controls,
permission management, compatibility enforcement, and organization-wide
defaults.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Plugin configuration architecture shall be:

- Consistent
- Accessible
- Discoverable
- Secure
- Local-first
- Policy-driven
- Extensible
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Settings Integration

Plugins that expose configurable settings shall register those settings
with the existing **Application Settings Framework**.

Plugins shall not create independent settings windows or dialogs.

Plugin settings shall appear within:

**Application Settings → Developer & Administrator → Plugins**

Each plugin may expose one or more settings pages.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Package Configuration

Packages may expose configurable metadata when appropriate.

Examples include:

- Default report templates
- Dashboard defaults
- Working View defaults
- AI prompt libraries
- Organization-specific terminology
- Accessibility Standards metadata
- Future package configuration

Package configuration shall also be managed through the existing
Application Settings framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Configuration Registration

Each plugin shall register:

- Configuration Pages
- Configuration Categories
- Setting Definitions
- Default Values
- Validation Rules
- Accessibility Metadata
- Help Documentation References

Configuration registration shall occur during plugin initialization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Setting Types

The Plugin Framework shall support standardized setting types including:

- Checkbox
- Switch
- Radio Button
- Combo Box
- List Box
- Text Box
- Numeric Input
- Password Field
- File Picker
- Folder Picker
- Color Picker (future)
- Keyboard Shortcut Selector
- Future standardized controls

Plugins shall use existing ART controls whenever possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Configuration Validation

Every configurable setting shall support validation.

Validation may include:

- Required values
- Numeric ranges
- String length
- Regular expressions
- Existing resources
- Existing commands
- Existing providers
- Version compatibility

Validation messages shall be accessible and consistent with ART
validation behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Default Values

Every configurable setting shall define:

- Default value
- Default behavior
- Reset behavior

Users shall be able to restore:

- Individual settings
- Plugin defaults
- Package defaults

using standardized controls.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Administrative Policies

Organizations may define administrative policies controlling plugins.

Policies may include:

- Approved Plugins
- Blocked Plugins
- Required Plugins
- Approved Package Types
- Approved Accessibility Standards
- Approved AI Providers
- Approved Integrations
- Future policy types

Policies shall override user configuration where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Management

Administrators shall be able to review granted plugin permissions.

Examples include:

- Resource Access
- Project Workspace Access
- Import Resources
- Export Resources
- Register Commands
- Register Search Providers
- Register Dashboard Cards
- Register Explorer Nodes
- External Network Access
- AI Service Access
- Future permissions

Permissions shall be visible within the Plugin & Package Manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Trust Levels

The Plugin Framework shall support configurable trust levels.

Examples include:

##### Built-in

Plugins distributed with ART.

##### Organization Approved

Plugins approved by an organization.

##### User Installed

Plugins installed by individual users.

##### Development

Unsigned or developer plugins.

Trust levels may affect:

- Installation
- Permissions
- Warning messages
- Administrative approval

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Compatibility Policies

Administrators may configure:

- Minimum supported Plugin Framework version
- Allowed plugin versions
- Allowed package versions
- Blocked versions
- Automatic compatibility enforcement

The Plugin Framework shall prevent incompatible plugins from loading.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Configuration Import and Export

Users shall be able to export:

- Plugin configuration
- Package configuration
- Administrative policies (administrator only)

Users shall be able to import previously exported configuration.

Configuration export shall not replace existing resource export
workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation Integration

Plugins shall register documentation links with ART.

Documentation may include:

- User Guide
- Administrator Guide
- Developer Guide
- Online Documentation
- Release Notes
- Troubleshooting Guide

Documentation shall be accessible through:

- Plugin Details
- Help menus
- Context-sensitive help
- Application documentation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Localization

Plugin configuration shall support localization.

Plugins shall provide localized:

- Setting names
- Descriptions
- Error messages
- Help text
- Validation messages

Localization shall integrate with ART's existing localization framework
when implemented.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Plugin configuration shall comply with all ART accessibility
requirements.

Configuration pages shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Logical heading hierarchy
- Proper label associations
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Plugins shall use ART's existing accessibility components rather than
implementing custom controls.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Plugin settings register correctly.
- Package settings register correctly.
- Configuration validation functions correctly.
- Default values function correctly.
- Reset functionality functions correctly.
- Administrative policies function correctly.
- Permission management functions correctly.
- Trust levels function correctly.
- Compatibility policies function correctly.
- Configuration import and export function correctly.
- Documentation links function correctly.
- Localization support functions correctly.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume the existing Application Settings framework whenever possible.

Do not create independent settings dialogs or duplicate configuration
mechanisms.

The Plugin Framework shall provide a centralized, accessible, and
policy-driven configuration system that integrates seamlessly with ART's
existing Application Settings architecture while supporting both
individual users and enterprise administrators.

### Part 7 – Plugin Accessibility Requirements, Quality Assurance, Validation & Documentation

#### Overview

Every plugin and package installed in ART shall meet the same
accessibility, quality, architectural, and documentation standards
required of the core application.

The Plugin Framework shall provide standardized validation mechanisms to
ensure that third-party extensions integrate consistently, remain fully
accessible, and do not compromise the stability, usability, or
maintainability of ART.

No plugin or package shall be considered production-ready until it has
successfully completed all required validation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The validation framework shall be:

- Accessible
- Consistent
- Automated where practical
- Repeatable
- Extensible
- Transparent
- Developer-friendly
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Requirements

Every plugin shall comply with all accessibility requirements
implemented throughout ART.

Plugins shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Mouse
- Touch
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking
- Future assistive technologies

Plugins shall not reduce or override the accessibility of ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Accessibility Requirements

Plugins shall consume existing ART accessibility infrastructure.

Plugins shall use:

- Accessibility Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Resource Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Global Context Menu Framework
- Keyboard Shortcut Manager
- Window Title Framework
- Existing accessible controls
- Existing accessibility utilities

Plugins shall not implement independent accessibility frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User Interface Requirements

Any user interface provided by a plugin shall:

- Follow ART visual design guidelines.
- Follow ART interaction patterns.
- Follow ART keyboard behavior.
- Follow ART focus management.
- Follow ART heading hierarchy.
- Follow ART menu behavior.
- Follow ART dialog behavior.
- Follow ART status messaging.
- Follow ART error presentation.

Plugin user interfaces shall appear as a natural part of ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Accessibility

Plugin functionality shall support:

- Sequential keyboard navigation
- Logical focus order
- Standard keyboard shortcuts
- User-configurable shortcuts
- Arrow key navigation
- First-letter navigation where applicable
- Escape behavior consistent with ART
- Focus restoration after dialogs close

Plugins shall not introduce inconsistent keyboard behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Requirements

Plugin interfaces shall expose:

- Accessible Names
- Accessible Descriptions
- Accessible Roles
- Accessible States
- Accessible Properties
- Status Messages
- Error Messages
- Progress Information

Screen readers shall receive information equivalent to sighted users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Refreshable Braille Requirements

Plugins shall expose sufficient semantic information for refreshable
braille displays.

Braille users shall receive:

- Labels
- Values
- Status
- Errors
- Progress
- Selection state
- Expanded/collapsed state
- Required field indicators

Equivalent information shall be available regardless of output modality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Navigation Requirements

Plugin interfaces shall support:

- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control

Visible labels shall uniquely identify interactive controls whenever
practical.

Plugin commands shall participate in ART's Application Command Framework
to ensure discoverability.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation Framework

The Plugin Framework shall validate plugins before installation and
during ongoing lifecycle operations.

Validation shall include:

- Manifest validation
- Metadata validation
- Version validation
- Dependency validation
- Permission validation
- Registration validation
- Resource validation
- Command validation
- Search Provider validation
- Explorer Provider validation
- Dashboard Provider validation
- Accessibility validation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Package Validation

Packages shall be validated for:

- JSON syntax
- Schema compliance
- Metadata
- Resource registration
- Duplicate identifiers
- Version compatibility
- Required fields
- Accessibility Standard integrity (where applicable)

Invalid packages shall not be registered.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Standards Validation

Accessibility Standards packages shall be validated for:

- Standard metadata
- Version information
- Criterion identifiers
- References
- Categories
- Lookup Tool compatibility
- Report compatibility
- Export compatibility
- Resource registration
- Search registration

The Plugin Framework shall ensure imported standards function
consistently with built-in standards.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Testing

Every plugin shall be tested to verify that it does not introduce
regressions affecting:

- Resource Framework
- Universal Search
- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Report Views
- Application Commands
- Keyboard Manager
- Context Menus
- Accessibility Framework
- Report Builder
- Report Viewer
- Import workflows
- Export workflows
- Project Workspaces
- Existing plugins
- Existing packages

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Validation

Plugins shall be evaluated for:

- Startup performance
- Initialization time
- Resource usage
- Search performance
- Explorer performance
- Command execution
- Memory usage
- Responsiveness

Plugins shall not significantly degrade ART performance.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Diagnostic Reporting

The Plugin Framework shall generate diagnostic information including:

- Validation status
- Registration status
- Dependency status
- Compatibility status
- Accessibility validation results
- Performance metrics
- Warnings
- Errors

Diagnostic information shall be available through the Plugin & Package
Manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation Requirements

Every plugin shall include documentation appropriate to its
functionality.

Documentation may include:

- Overview
- Features
- Installation
- Configuration
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Commands
- Accessibility notes
- Troubleshooting
- Known limitations
- Version history

Documentation shall integrate with ART's Help system where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Package Documentation

Every package type shall include documentation describing:

- Purpose
- Contents
- Compatibility
- Import workflow
- Version information
- Resource registration
- Future updates

Documentation shall explain how the package integrates with existing ART
workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Developer Documentation

Copilot shall update:

- PLUGIN-DEVELOPER-GUIDE.md
- PACKAGE-AUTHORING-GUIDE.md

to include:

- Validation requirements
- Accessibility requirements
- Quality expectations
- Performance expectations
- Testing recommendations
- Sample validation workflows
- Common implementation mistakes
- Troubleshooting guidance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Plugin accessibility requirements are enforced.
- Package validation functions correctly.
- Accessibility Standards packages validate correctly.
- Existing ART workflows remain unchanged.
- Plugin diagnostics function correctly.
- Performance validation functions correctly.
- Documentation requirements are satisfied.
- Regression testing passes.
- Plugins integrate seamlessly with existing ART frameworks.
- Plugins cannot reduce the accessibility or stability of ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate accessibility, validation, testing, documentation, or
import workflows.

The Plugin Framework shall ensure that every plugin and package meets
the same architectural, accessibility, usability, documentation, and
quality standards as the core ART application while preserving
consistency across the entire platform.

### Part 8 – Final Validation, Acceptance Criteria, Future Extensibility & Completion Requirements

#### Overview

This part defines the final acceptance criteria for the Plugin Framework
and establishes the long-term architectural requirements that shall
govern future plugins, packages, and extension types.

The Plugin Framework shall become the authoritative infrastructure for
extending ART while preserving the application's accessibility-first,
local-first, framework-driven architecture.

Future development shall extend the Plugin Framework rather than
introducing competing extension mechanisms.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The completed Plugin Framework shall be:

- Complete
- Accessible
- Extensible
- Stable
- Maintainable
- Discoverable
- Framework-driven
- Local-first
- Enterprise-ready
- Future-proof

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Architectural Principles

Future plugins and packages shall adhere to the following principles.

##### Consume Existing Frameworks

Plugins and packages shall consume existing ART frameworks whenever
possible.

New frameworks shall not duplicate:

- Resource management
- Search
- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Context menus
- Commands
- Accessibility
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Working Views
- Window title management
- Existing import/export workflows

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Single Responsibility

Each framework shall have one clearly defined responsibility.

Examples include:

| Framework                     | Responsibility                       |
|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Resource Framework            | Resource registration and management |
| Plugin Framework              | Extension registration and lifecycle |
| Universal Search              | Search                               |
| Explorer                      | Resource navigation                  |
| Dashboard                     | Workspace overview                   |
| Report Views                  | Temporary report organization        |
| Accessibility Framework       | Accessibility behavior               |
| Application Command Framework | Commands                             |
| Keyboard Manager              | Keyboard shortcut configuration      |

Future enhancements shall extend these frameworks rather than replacing
them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Local-First Operation

The Plugin Framework shall preserve ART's local-first philosophy.

Plugins shall not require:

- Internet connectivity
- Cloud services
- User accounts
- Authentication

unless explicitly required by the plugin itself.

Core ART functionality shall continue operating offline.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Accessibility-First Design

Accessibility shall remain a foundational requirement.

Plugins shall never reduce:

- Keyboard accessibility
- Screen reader accessibility
- Braille accessibility
- Voice accessibility
- Focus management
- Semantic information

Plugins shall inherit ART accessibility behavior whenever possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Plugin Types

The Plugin Framework shall support future extension categories without
architectural redesign.

Examples may include:

- AI Models
- AI Agents
- Industry-specific standards
- Organization policies
- Workflow automation
- Script providers
- Collaboration providers
- Cloud synchronization providers
- Third-party reporting engines
- Visualization providers
- Analytics providers
- Future extension types

These extensions shall register through existing Plugin Framework
extension points.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Package Types

The Package Framework shall support future package categories,
including:

- Accessibility Standards
- Report Templates
- Dashboard Layouts
- Keyboard Profiles
- Working View Presets
- AI Prompt Libraries
- Saved Searches
- Documentation
- Organization Policies
- Sample Projects
- Sample Reports
- Training Content
- Future package types

New package types shall not require changes to the Plugin Framework
architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Enterprise Readiness

The Plugin Framework shall support future enterprise features including:

- Organization-managed plugins
- Organization-managed packages
- Centralized deployment
- Administrative approval workflows
- Version pinning
- Enterprise policy enforcement
- Trusted publisher management
- Digital signature verification (future)
- Centralized repositories (future)

These capabilities shall be additive and shall not require redesign of
the Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation Completion

Copilot shall ensure that all plugin- and package-related documentation
is complete, internally consistent, and cross-referenced.

Documentation shall include, at a minimum:

- README.md
- USER-GUIDE.md
- HELP.md
- ARCHITECTURE.md
- PLUGIN-DEVELOPER-GUIDE.md
- PACKAGE-AUTHORING-GUIDE.md

Where appropriate, documentation shall reference existing ART workflows
rather than describing duplicate procedures.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User Guide Updates

The User Guide shall include dedicated sections covering:

- Plugins
- Packages
- Plugin & Package Manager
- Installing plugins
- Managing installed plugins
- Existing package import workflows
- Optional Accessibility Standards packages
- Plugin troubleshooting
- Package troubleshooting
- Frequently Asked Questions

Step-by-step examples shall be included where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Developer Documentation

Developer documentation shall include:

- Plugin architecture
- Package architecture
- Extension points
- Registration
- Lifecycle
- Validation
- Accessibility requirements
- Versioning
- Best practices
- Sample plugins
- Sample packages

Documentation shall encourage reuse of existing ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Source Code Requirements

Copilot shall:

- Reuse existing framework implementations whenever possible.
- Eliminate duplicated logic.
- Remove obsolete code introduced during development.
- Maintain consistent naming conventions.
- Maintain consistent coding standards.
- Preserve backward compatibility where practical.

All new code shall follow the existing ART project structure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Testing

Before completion, Copilot shall verify that the Plugin Framework does
not introduce regressions affecting:

- Resource Framework
- Universal Search
- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Report Views
- Global Context Menus
- Application Commands
- Keyboard Manager
- Accessibility Lookup Tool
- Report Builder
- Report Viewer
- Project Workspaces
- Existing import workflows
- Existing export workflows
- Existing integrations
- Existing accessibility standards
- Existing report templates
- Existing keyboard shortcuts

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Acceptance Criteria

The Plugin Framework shall be considered complete when all of the
following are true:

- Executable plugins can be discovered, validated, loaded, configured,
  updated, disabled, enabled, and uninstalled.
- Packages participate in the Plugin Framework after being imported
  through their existing ART workflows.
- Existing workflows, including Import Accessibility Standard and
  Connect Integrations, remain unchanged.
- Plugins integrate exclusively through approved ART frameworks.
- Packages are automatically registered and discoverable after import.
- Plugin and package metadata is available through the Plugin & Package
  Manager.
- Validation, diagnostics, and compatibility checking function
  correctly.
- Documentation is complete and accurate.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied throughout the framework.
- Existing ART functionality continues to operate without regression.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Verification

Verify that:

- All parts of this epic have been implemented.
- All documentation has been updated.
- All accessibility requirements have been met.
- All existing workflows remain intact.
- All plugin and package lifecycle operations function correctly.
- Framework integration is complete.
- No duplicated workflows or framework implementations have been
  introduced.
- Existing projects continue to function correctly.
- Existing reports remain compatible.
- Existing user settings remain compatible.
- Existing ART architecture has been preserved.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Preserve all existing user workflows.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not introduce duplicate workflows, duplicate framework
implementations, or competing extension mechanisms.

The completed Plugin Framework shall provide a secure, accessible,
extensible, and maintainable foundation for all future ART extensions
while preserving the architectural principles established throughout
previous epics.

## Epic 35 – Resource Relationships & Cross-References

### Part 1 – Resource Relationship Framework Architecture

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall provide a standardized,
application-wide mechanism for defining, discovering, managing, and
navigating relationships between resources within ART.

The framework shall enable resources to reference one another without
duplicating information and shall provide the foundation for Explorer
navigation, Universal Search, Properties dialogs, impact analysis, safe
deletion, dependency validation, and future reporting features.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall extend the existing Resource
Framework introduced in Epic 33 and shall not replace or duplicate
existing resource management functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Relationship Framework shall be:

- Resource-centric
- Relationship-aware
- Extensible
- Discoverable
- Accessible
- Local-first
- Framework-driven
- Scalable
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The framework shall allow ART to answer questions such as:

- Which reports use this template?
- Which reports reference this attachment?
- Which accessibility standard is this report using?
- Which workspaces contain this report?
- Which resources depend on this resource?
- Can this resource be safely deleted?
- What will be affected if this resource changes?

The framework shall maintain these relationships automatically whenever
possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Model

Every relationship shall consist of:

- Source Resource
- Relationship Type
- Target Resource
- Relationship Metadata (optional)

Relationships shall be directional but may optionally support
bidirectional navigation.

Example:

``` text
Report
    Uses
        Accessibility Standard

Accessibility Standard
    Used By
        Report
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Relationship Types

The framework shall support, at minimum, the following relationship
types:

##### Contains

A parent resource contains another resource.

Examples:

- Workspace contains Report
- Report contains Attachment

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Uses

A resource uses another resource.

Examples:

- Report uses Template
- Report uses Accessibility Standard

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### References

A resource references another resource.

Examples:

- Report references Attachment
- Report references Project Asset

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Depends On

A resource requires another resource.

Examples:

- Plugin depends on Plugin
- Package depends on Package

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Shared With

A resource is shared among multiple resources.

Examples:

- Attachment shared across Reports
- Template shared across Workspaces

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Generated From

A resource originated from another resource.

Examples:

- Export generated from Report
- Summary generated from Audit Log

Future relationship types shall be supported without redesigning the
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Registration

Relationships shall be registered automatically whenever possible.

Examples include:

- Opening a Workspace
- Importing a Report
- Importing a Template
- Importing an Accessibility Standard
- Adding an Attachment
- Creating a Report
- Creating an Export

Plugins may register additional relationships through the existing
Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Integration

The Resource Relationship Framework shall integrate with:

- Resource Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Plugin Framework
- Package Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Dashboard Framework

The framework shall consume existing services rather than duplicating
them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Storage

Relationship data shall be stored independently from the resources
themselves whenever practical.

The framework shall not require modifications to existing resource file
formats solely to support relationships.

Relationship storage shall support:

- Efficient lookup
- Incremental updates
- Validation
- Future synchronization
- Future export

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Automatic Maintenance

Relationships shall automatically update when:

- Resources are renamed.
- Resources are moved.
- Resources are imported.
- Resources are deleted.
- Resources are copied.
- Resources are duplicated.
- Resources are restored.

The framework shall ensure relationship integrity throughout the
application lifecycle.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The framework shall expose relationship information to assistive
technologies through the user interfaces that consume it.

Relationship information shall never rely solely on visual presentation.

Explorer, Properties dialogs, Universal Search, and future consumers
shall present relationship information in an accessible and consistent
manner.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Relationships can be registered.
- Relationship types are validated.
- Bidirectional navigation functions correctly.
- Automatic relationship maintenance functions correctly.
- Existing Resource Framework functionality remains unchanged.
- Plugins can register additional relationships.
- Relationship information is available to all consuming frameworks.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource management functionality.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall become the authoritative
mechanism for defining, maintaining, and exposing relationships between
resources throughout ART while preserving the existing architecture
established in previous epics.

### Part 2 – Relationship Discovery, Explorer Integration & Navigation

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall integrate with the Explorer
Framework to enable users to discover, navigate, and understand
relationships between resources without leaving the Explorer.

Explorer shall become the primary interface for browsing resource
relationships while preserving its existing role as the hierarchical
navigator for Project Workspaces and individual reports.

Relationship information shall complement—not replace—the existing
Explorer hierarchy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

Explorer relationship integration shall be:

- Discoverable
- Intuitive
- Non-destructive
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Performance-oriented
- Extensible
- Consistent

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Navigation

Users shall be able to navigate from any resource to its related
resources.

Examples include:

- Report → Accessibility Standard
- Report → Template
- Report → Attachments
- Report → Project Assets
- Attachment → Reports Using Attachment
- Template → Reports Using Template
- Accessibility Standard → Reports Using Standard
- Workspace → Shared Resources

Navigation shall occur without modifying the underlying resource
structure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Relationship Nodes

The Explorer shall support virtual relationship nodes.

Virtual relationship nodes represent relationships maintained by the
Resource Relationship Framework rather than physical resources.

Examples include:

``` text
Report

    Attachments

    Uses

        WCAG 2.2

        Standard Web Audit Template

    Referenced Assets

    Related Reports

    Generated Reports
```

Virtual nodes shall be generated dynamically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Relationship Categories

Where applicable, related resources shall be grouped into logical
categories.

Examples include:

- Uses
- Used By
- References
- Referenced By
- Contains
- Contained In
- Depends On
- Required By
- Shared With
- Generated From
- Generated Outputs

Future categories shall be supported without architectural changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Expand and Collapse Behavior

Relationship nodes shall support the same interaction model as existing
Explorer nodes.

Users shall be able to:

- Expand
- Collapse
- Expand All
- Collapse All

Keyboard shortcuts and context menu commands shall remain consistent
with existing Explorer behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Lazy Loading

Relationship information shall be loaded only when needed.

The framework shall avoid eagerly loading every relationship during
Explorer initialization.

Relationship nodes shall populate when:

- Expanded
- Requested by search
- Requested by navigation
- Requested by a consuming framework

This shall improve startup and Explorer performance.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Behavior

Activating a related resource shall move focus to that resource within
Explorer.

If the resource is not currently visible:

- Explorer shall automatically expand the required hierarchy.
- Focus shall move to the destination resource.
- The destination shall become the current selection.

Navigation shall never create duplicate Explorer nodes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multiple Relationship Paths

A resource may participate in multiple relationships simultaneously.

Example:

``` text
Login Screenshot

Referenced By

    Login Report

Shared With

    Executive Summary

Contained In

    Project Assets
```

Explorer shall present each relationship independently while maintaining
a single underlying resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menus

Relationship nodes shall participate in the Global Context Menu
Framework.

Examples include:

- Open
- Go To Resource
- Show Properties
- Show Relationships
- Show Dependents
- Show References
- Copy Resource Path
- Reveal in Explorer
- Future commands

Commands shall appear only when applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Badges

Explorer may optionally display visual indicators that summarize
relationship information.

Examples include:

- Shared
- Referenced
- Dependency
- Generated
- Organization Resource

Badges shall supplement—not replace—textual information.

Equivalent information shall always be exposed programmatically to
assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Integration

Explorer search shall include relationship metadata.

Examples:

Searching for:

``` text
WCAG 2.2
```

may return:

- Accessibility Standard
- Reports using WCAG 2.2
- Templates using WCAG 2.2

Searching for:

``` text
Login Screenshot
```

may return:

- Attachment
- Reports referencing the attachment
- Project Assets containing the attachment

Relationship-aware searching shall consume the existing Universal Search
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

Explorer shall:

- Cache relationship lookups where practical.
- Refresh only affected relationship nodes.
- Avoid unnecessary rebuilding of the Explorer tree.
- Maintain responsiveness regardless of workspace size.

Relationship updates shall be incremental whenever possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Relationship navigation shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Relationship nodes shall expose:

- Accessible Name
- Accessible Role
- Expanded/Collapsed State
- Position within hierarchy
- Relationship type where appropriate

Navigation shall follow the existing Explorer accessibility model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Relationship nodes appear correctly.
- Virtual nodes function correctly.
- Lazy loading functions correctly.
- Navigation moves focus correctly.
- Explorer expands automatically when necessary.
- Duplicate nodes are not created.
- Context menus function correctly.
- Search returns related resources.
- Performance remains acceptable for large workspaces.
- Accessibility information is exposed correctly.
- Existing Explorer functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Explorer functionality.

Consume the existing Explorer Framework, Resource Framework, Universal
Search Framework, and Global Context Menu Framework.

Do not duplicate resource navigation or search functionality.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall extend Explorer with rich,
accessible, and efficient relationship navigation while preserving the
familiar Explorer experience established in previous epics.

### Part 3 – Properties Dialog, Relationship Details & Impact Analysis

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall integrate with the existing
Properties dialogs to provide users with a comprehensive view of how a
resource is related to other resources throughout ART.

The Properties dialog shall become the primary interface for inspecting
a resource's metadata, relationships, dependencies, usage, and impact
without modifying the resource.

Relationship information presented in the Properties dialog shall be
read-only unless explicitly stated otherwise.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Properties dialog shall be:

- Informative
- Discoverable
- Accessible
- Read-only by default
- Relationship-aware
- Keyboard-first
- Extensible
- Consistent

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Tab

Every resource type that participates in the Resource Relationship
Framework shall include a **Relationships** tab within its Properties
dialog.

The Relationships tab shall summarize how the selected resource
participates within the current Project Workspace and throughout ART
where applicable.

Examples include:

- Uses
- Used By
- References
- Referenced By
- Contains
- Contained In
- Shared With
- Depends On
- Required By
- Generated From
- Generated Outputs

Future relationship categories shall automatically appear when
registered.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Summary

The top of the Relationships tab shall present a concise summary.

Example:

``` text
Relationship Summary

Uses:
    2 Accessibility Standards
    1 Report Template
    4 Attachments

Referenced By:
    Executive Summary
    Audit Log

Contained In:
    Accessibility Audit Workspace

Shared With:
    3 Reports
```

The summary shall update automatically when relationships change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Details

Each relationship category shall be expandable.

Expanding a category shall reveal the related resources.

Example:

``` text
Attachments

▼ Login Screenshot.png

▼ Keyboard Testing.mp4

▼ Forms.pdf
```

Selecting a related resource shall not automatically navigate away from
the current Properties dialog.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Commands

The Relationships tab shall provide commands including:

- Open
- Go To Resource
- Show Properties
- Reveal in Explorer
- Copy Resource Name
- Copy Resource Path
- Copy Relationship Information

Commands shall participate in the existing Application Command Framework
and Global Context Menu Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Counts

Where appropriate, relationship categories shall display counts.

Example:

``` text
Referenced By (7)

Uses (4)

Contains (18)

Shared With (3)
```

Counts shall update dynamically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Impact Analysis

The Properties dialog shall include an **Impact Analysis** section.

Impact Analysis shall summarize the effects of modifying or deleting the
selected resource.

Examples include:

``` text
Changing this template will affect:

12 Reports

3 Saved Working Views

2 Dashboard Cards
```

or

``` text
Deleting this attachment will affect:

4 Reports

1 Executive Summary

2 Project Assets
```

Impact Analysis shall be informational only.

No changes shall occur automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Safe Deletion Preview

Where applicable, the Relationships tab shall support a **Preview
Deletion Impact** command.

The preview shall identify:

- Resources that reference the selected resource.
- Resources that depend on the selected resource.
- Resources that will lose functionality.
- Resources that may become incomplete.

The preview shall not delete any resources.

Actual deletion behavior shall be defined in a later part of this epic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Usage

The Properties dialog shall summarize resource usage.

Examples include:

For a Template:

``` text
Currently used by:

18 Reports

2 Report Templates

1 Organization Default
```

For an Accessibility Standard:

``` text
Currently used by:

42 Reports

6 Templates
```

For an Attachment:

``` text
Referenced by:

Audit Log

Executive Summary

Usability Report
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dependency Information

Where applicable, the Relationships tab shall distinguish between:

- Optional relationships
- Required relationships

Example:

``` text
Required Dependencies

WCAG 2.2

Organization Template

Optional Resources

Project Logo

Sample Screenshots
```

This distinction shall assist users in understanding potential impacts
before modifying resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Filtering

Users shall be able to filter relationship information within the
Relationships tab.

Examples include:

- Uses
- Used By
- References
- Shared
- Dependencies
- Generated Resources
- Current Workspace Only
- All Registered Resources

Filtering shall not modify the underlying relationship data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Search

The Relationships tab shall include an accessible search box.

Users shall be able to search within the displayed relationships.

Searching shall filter only the current Properties dialog.

It shall not invoke Universal Search.

The search box shall:

- Support keyboard-only operation.
- Support first-letter navigation.
- Support standard text editing commands.
- Clear using **Escape** when focus is within the search box and the
  search contains text.
- Close the Properties dialog only if the search box is empty and focus
  has already returned to the dialog, consistent with ART's standard
  Escape behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Relationship Types

The Properties dialog shall automatically display future relationship
types registered through the Resource Relationship Framework.

No dialog redesign shall be required when new relationship categories
are introduced.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Relationships tab shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Logical heading hierarchy
- Logical tab order
- Arrow key navigation where appropriate
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Relationship information shall be fully programmatically exposed.

Counts, dependency status, and impact information shall never rely
solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Every supported resource includes a Relationships tab.
- Relationship summaries display correctly.
- Relationship counts update automatically.
- Related resources are displayed correctly.
- Navigation commands function correctly.
- Impact Analysis reflects current relationships.
- Deletion previews identify affected resources.
- Resource usage summaries are accurate.
- Relationship filtering functions correctly.
- Relationship search functions correctly.
- Future relationship types appear automatically.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing Properties dialog functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Properties dialog functionality.

Consume the existing Resource Framework, Resource Relationship
Framework, Explorer Framework, Application Command Framework, and Global
Context Menu Framework.

Do not duplicate navigation, search, or resource management
functionality.

The Properties dialog shall become the authoritative interface for
inspecting resource relationships, usage, dependencies, and impact while
preserving ART's accessibility-first, framework-driven architecture.

### Part 4 – Safe Deletion, Relationship Integrity & Automatic Maintenance

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall preserve relationship
integrity throughout the lifecycle of every resource managed by ART.

Before any resource is modified, moved, duplicated, exported, imported,
archived, or deleted, the framework shall evaluate all registered
relationships and ensure that no operation leaves ART in an inconsistent
state.

Users shall always be informed of the potential impact of destructive
operations before changes are committed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

Relationship integrity shall be:

- Automatic
- Reliable
- Predictable
- Accessible
- Recoverable
- Non-destructive
- Extensible
- Framework-driven

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Integrity

The Resource Relationship Framework shall maintain valid relationships
at all times.

Relationship integrity shall be preserved when:

- Creating resources
- Renaming resources
- Moving resources
- Copying resources
- Duplicating resources
- Importing resources
- Exporting resources
- Deleting resources
- Restoring resources
- Closing workspaces
- Opening workspaces

Relationship maintenance shall occur automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Safe Deletion

Before deleting any resource, ART shall evaluate every relationship
involving that resource.

Deletion shall never occur without first determining:

- What resources reference the selected resource.
- What resources depend upon the selected resource.
- Whether deletion would leave invalid references.
- Whether deletion would affect generated reports.
- Whether deletion would affect exported artifacts.
- Whether deletion would affect templates.
- Whether deletion would affect Project Workspaces.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deletion Analysis Dialog

If relationships are detected, ART shall display an accessible
**Deletion Analysis** dialog.

The dialog shall summarize:

- Selected resource
- Relationship count
- Dependent resources
- Referencing resources
- Potential consequences
- Available actions

Example:

``` text
Delete Resource

The selected attachment is referenced by:

• Audit Log
• Executive Summary
• Report A
• Report B

Deleting this attachment will remove those references.

What would you like to do?
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Deletion Actions

Depending on the resource type, users may be offered one or more of the
following actions:

- Cancel
- Delete
- Delete and Remove References
- Delete and Replace Resource…
- Open Relationships
- Open Impact Analysis
- Reveal in Explorer

Available actions shall be determined by the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Validation

The Resource Relationship Framework shall prevent invalid relationship
states.

Examples include:

- References to deleted resources
- Circular containment
- Duplicate identifiers
- Invalid dependency chains
- Broken generated-resource links

Relationship validation shall occur automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Automatic Relationship Updates

Relationships shall automatically update when resources are:

##### Renamed

Relationship references shall continue to point to the renamed resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Moved

Relationships shall remain intact regardless of the resource's location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Copied

The Resource Framework shall determine whether relationships are:

- Copied
- Recreated
- Shared
- Removed

based upon resource type.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Duplicated

Duplicated resources shall receive new unique identifiers.

Relationships shall be recreated according to the Resource Framework's
duplication policy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Restored

Restored resources shall automatically reconnect to valid relationships
whenever possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Broken Relationships

If ART detects a broken relationship, the framework shall:

- Record the issue.
- Notify the user.
- Prevent application instability.
- Offer repair options where possible.

Broken relationships shall never cause ART to crash.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Repair

Where practical, users shall be able to repair broken relationships.

Repair options may include:

- Locate Missing Resource…
- Replace Resource…
- Remove Invalid Relationship
- Ignore
- Cancel

Repair workflows shall be fully accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Duplicate Detection

The framework shall detect duplicate resources where applicable.

Examples include:

- Duplicate attachments
- Duplicate templates
- Duplicate accessibility standards
- Duplicate project assets

Detection shall be informational only unless explicitly configured
otherwise.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Consistency

Relationship updates shall remain consistent across:

- Explorer
- Properties dialogs
- Universal Search
- Dashboard
- Report Views
- Plugin Framework
- Resource Framework

No framework shall maintain independent relationship data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Transaction Safety

Relationship updates shall participate in the same transaction as the
underlying resource operation whenever practical.

If an operation fails:

- Resource changes shall be rolled back where supported.
- Relationship changes shall also be rolled back.
- Partial relationship updates shall not occur.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Logging

The framework shall log significant relationship operations including:

- Relationship creation
- Relationship removal
- Relationship repair
- Resource deletion
- Dependency failures
- Broken relationship detection

Logs shall support diagnostics and troubleshooting while respecting
ART's local-first architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

All relationship integrity workflows shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Voice navigation
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Deletion warnings, validation messages, and repair options shall be
fully programmatically exposed.

No warning shall rely solely on color, icons, or other visual
indicators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Relationships remain valid after renaming resources.
- Relationships remain valid after moving resources.
- Relationships remain valid after copying resources.
- Relationships remain valid after duplicating resources.
- Relationships remain valid after restoring resources.
- Deletion Analysis accurately identifies affected resources.
- Broken relationships are detected.
- Relationship repair functions correctly.
- Duplicate detection functions correctly.
- Relationship updates are transactional where supported.
- Logging functions correctly.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing Resource Framework functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework functionality.

Consume the existing Resource Framework, Resource Relationship
Framework, Explorer Framework, and Properties Framework.

Do not duplicate resource validation, transaction management, or logging
functionality.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall ensure that all resource
relationships remain accurate, consistent, and recoverable throughout
the lifecycle of every resource while providing users with clear,
accessible information before any operation that could affect related
resources.

### Part 5 – Universal Search, Relationship Queries & Cross-Resource Discovery

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall integrate with the Universal
Search Framework to enable users to discover resources not only by their
own properties, but also by their relationships to other resources.

Relationship-aware searching shall allow users to answer questions such
as:

- Which reports use this template?
- Which reports use WCAG 2.2?
- Which reports reference this attachment?
- Which workspaces contain this report?
- Which resources depend on this plugin?
- Which templates are organization defaults?

The Universal Search Framework shall remain the authoritative search
engine for ART.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall contribute additional
searchable relationship metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

Relationship-aware searching shall be:

- Fast
- Discoverable
- Accessible
- Relationship-aware
- Resource-aware
- Extensible
- Keyboard-first
- Local-first

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Search

Universal Search shall index registered relationships.

Relationship information shall become searchable without requiring users
to understand the underlying relationship model.

Example searches may include:

``` text
Reports using WCAG 2.2

Reports using Standard Web Audit Template

Reports referencing Login Screenshot

Reports sharing Project Logo

Templates using EN 301 549

Reports generated from Template X
```

Search queries shall return matching resources together with the
relationship that produced the match.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Searchable Relationship Types

The Resource Relationship Framework shall expose searchable metadata for
relationship types including:

- Uses
- Used By
- References
- Referenced By
- Contains
- Contained In
- Shared With
- Depends On
- Required By
- Generated From
- Generated Outputs

Future relationship types shall automatically become searchable after
registration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Presentation

Search results shall clearly distinguish between:

- Direct matches
- Relationship matches

Example:

``` text
Report

Accessibility Audit – City Website

Relationship Match

Uses:

WCAG 2.2
```

or

``` text
Attachment

Login Screenshot.png

Relationship Match

Referenced By:

Executive Summary
```

Users shall understand why a result appeared.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Preview

Each relationship-based search result shall include a concise
relationship summary.

Examples include:

``` text
Uses

WCAG 2.2

Standard Web Audit Template

3 Attachments
```

or

``` text
Referenced By

Executive Summary

Audit Log

Report A
```

The summary shall be expandable where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Filters

Users shall be able to filter relationship-aware search results.

Examples include:

##### Resource Type

- Reports
- Templates
- Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Project Assets
- Plugins
- Packages

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Relationship Type

- Uses
- References
- Shared With
- Depends On
- Generated From

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Workspace Scope

- Current Workspace
- Open Workspaces
- All Registered Resources

Future filters shall be supported without redesigning the search
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Facets

Universal Search may expose relationship facets.

Examples include:

``` text
Relationship Type

Uses (18)

Referenced By (7)

Shared (4)
```

Selecting a facet shall filter the current search results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep Linking

Relationship-based search results shall support direct navigation.

Users shall be able to:

- Open Resource
- Reveal in Explorer
- Open Properties
- View Relationships
- Show Impact Analysis
- Copy Resource Path

Navigation shall use existing ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Ranking

Relationship-aware search results shall participate in the existing
Universal Search ranking algorithm.

Exact resource matches shall generally rank above relationship matches
unless the user explicitly searches for a relationship.

Relationship metadata shall improve relevance without overwhelming
direct search results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Search Suggestions

Universal Search may provide intelligent suggestions based on registered
relationship types.

Examples include:

``` text
Reports using…

Templates used by…

Attachments referenced by…

Resources shared with…

Reports generated from…
```

Suggestions shall be generated dynamically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may register additional searchable relationship metadata through
the existing Universal Search Framework.

Plugins shall not modify search behavior directly.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall remain responsible for
relationship registration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

Relationship-aware searching shall:

- Index relationship metadata incrementally.
- Avoid rebuilding the entire search index unnecessarily.
- Update automatically when relationships change.
- Scale to large workspaces.
- Maintain acceptable search performance.

Relationship indexing shall consume the existing Universal Search
indexing infrastructure whenever possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Relationship-aware searching shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Search results shall expose:

- Resource name
- Resource type
- Relationship type
- Relationship summary
- Available actions

Relationship information shall be fully programmatically exposed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Relationship metadata is indexed correctly.
- Relationship searches return accurate results.
- Relationship summaries display correctly.
- Filters function correctly.
- Facets function correctly.
- Deep linking functions correctly.
- Search ranking remains appropriate.
- Relationship suggestions function correctly.
- Plugins can register searchable relationship metadata.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing Universal Search functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Universal Search functionality.

Consume the existing Universal Search Framework, Resource Framework,
Resource Relationship Framework, Explorer Framework, and Properties
Framework.

Do not duplicate search indexing or search infrastructure.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall extend Universal Search with
rich, relationship-aware discovery capabilities while preserving the
speed, accessibility, and consistency of ART's existing search
