experience.

### Part 6 – Relationship Visualization, Working Views & Report Analysis

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall integrate with the Report
Views Framework to provide relationship-based analysis without modifying
the underlying report or Project Workspace.

Relationship analysis shall be presented through temporary **Working
Views**, allowing users to better understand how report content,
resources, and supporting artifacts relate to one another.

Working Views shall remain temporary unless the user explicitly applies
supported organizational changes to the report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

Relationship-based Working Views shall be:

- Temporary
- Non-destructive
- Analytical
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Resource-aware
- Extensible
- Consistent

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Working Views

Users shall be able to generate Working Views based upon resource
relationships.

Examples include:

- Findings using the same Accessibility Standard
- Findings sharing the same Attachment
- Findings using the same Screenshot
- Findings using the same Project Asset
- Findings generated from the same Template
- Findings grouped by related resource
- Findings grouped by shared evidence

Working Views shall consume the existing Report Views Framework
introduced in Epic 32.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship-Based Grouping

Working Views may temporarily group report content using relationship
metadata.

Examples include:

``` text
Using WCAG 2.2

    Finding 1

    Finding 8

    Finding 12

Using EN 301 549

    Finding 3

    Finding 6
```

or

``` text
Using Login Screenshot

    Finding 2

    Finding 5

    Finding 9
```

Grouping shall not permanently reorder report content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship-Based Sorting

Working Views may temporarily sort report content according to
relationship information.

Examples include:

- Accessibility Standard
- Attachment
- Template
- Project Asset
- Shared Evidence
- Resource Type
- Related Report

Sorting shall remain temporary unless explicitly applied through
existing Working View functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship-Based Filtering

Users shall be able to temporarily filter report content using
relationship criteria.

Examples include:

- Show findings using this attachment
- Show findings using this template
- Show findings referencing this project asset
- Show findings using WCAG 2.2
- Show findings using Section 508
- Show findings generated from imported resources

Filtering shall not modify report data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Analysis

Working Views shall summarize relationship information.

Examples include:

``` text
Working View

Grouped by Attachment

Login Screenshot

7 Findings

Keyboard Testing.mp4

3 Findings

Forms.pdf

5 Findings
```

or

``` text
Grouped by Accessibility Standard

WCAG 2.2

18 Findings

EN 301 549

7 Findings
```

Summaries shall update dynamically while the Working View remains open.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation

Users shall be able to navigate relationship groups using:

- Keyboard
- Mouse
- Touch
- Voice

Selecting a relationship group shall move focus to the first
corresponding finding.

Remaining findings within the group shall appear consecutively within
the temporary Working View.

This behavior shall remain consistent with the Working View architecture
established in Epic 32.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Statistics

Working Views may display summary statistics including:

- Number of related findings
- Number of referenced attachments
- Number of shared resources
- Number of accessibility standards
- Number of templates
- Number of related reports

Statistics shall be informational only.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Commands

Relationship Working Views shall support existing Working View commands,
including:

- Exit Working View
- Apply Supported Sort
- Apply Supported Filter
- Reveal in Explorer
- Open Properties
- Copy Resource Name
- Copy Relationship Information

Commands shall integrate with the existing Application Command
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Integration

Relationship Working Views shall participate in ART's existing Window
Title Framework.

Examples include:

``` text
Accessibility Reporting Tool

Report Viewer

Working View – Grouped by Attachment (Temporary)
```

or

``` text
Accessibility Reporting Tool

Report Viewer

Working View – Using WCAG 2.2 (Temporary)
```

Working Views shall inherit all existing window title requirements
established elsewhere in ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Escape Behavior

Relationship Working Views shall inherit the standard Escape behavior
defined in previous epics.

When:

- The Working View is active,
- No menus are open,
- No context menu is active,
- No search box currently owns focus,

pressing **Escape** shall:

- Exit the Working View.
- Restore the report's original presentation.
- Restore focus to approximately the same finding the user was viewing
  within the Working View.

No report data shall be modified.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Visualization Providers

Plugins may contribute additional relationship visualization providers.

Examples include:

- Timeline View
- Dependency View
- Evidence View
- Standards View
- Organization View

Visualization providers shall consume the existing Report Views
Framework.

Plugins shall not replace existing Working View behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Relationship Working Views shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Relationship summaries, statistics, grouping information, and temporary
ordering shall all be fully programmatically exposed.

No relationship information shall rely solely upon visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Relationship Working Views generate correctly.
- Relationship grouping functions correctly.
- Relationship sorting functions correctly.
- Relationship filtering functions correctly.
- Relationship summaries are accurate.
- Relationship statistics are accurate.
- Window titles update correctly.
- Escape exits the Working View and restores focus appropriately.
- Existing Working View functionality remains unchanged.
- Plugin visualization providers integrate correctly.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Report Views functionality.

Consume the existing Report Views Framework, Resource Framework,
Resource Relationship Framework, Window Title Framework, Application
Command Framework, and Explorer Framework.

Do not duplicate report sorting, filtering, grouping, or navigation
functionality.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall enrich the existing Working
View experience by enabling temporary, relationship-based analysis and
visualization while preserving ART's accessibility-first,
framework-driven, and non-destructive design principles.

### Part 7 – Relationship Framework API, Plugin Integration & Extensibility

#### Overview

The Resource Relationship Framework shall provide a standardized API
that allows ART and approved plugins to create, discover, query,
validate, and maintain relationships between resources.

The framework shall serve as the single authoritative source for
relationship information throughout ART.

Plugins shall interact exclusively through this framework and shall not
directly manipulate another resource's internal relationship data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Relationship Framework API shall be:

- Framework-driven
- Consistent
- Extensible
- Secure
- Accessible
- Discoverable
- Version-aware
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Authoritative Relationship Service

The Resource Relationship Framework shall expose a centralized
**Relationship Service**.

The Relationship Service shall become the authoritative source for:

- Relationship registration
- Relationship discovery
- Relationship queries
- Relationship validation
- Relationship updates
- Relationship removal
- Relationship diagnostics

No other ART framework shall maintain an independent relationship store.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Registration API

The framework shall provide standardized APIs for registering
relationships.

Examples include:

- RegisterRelationship()
- UpdateRelationship()
- RemoveRelationship()
- RelationshipExists()
- ValidateRelationship()

Actual implementation details may vary, provided the functionality
remains consistent with this specification.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Query API

ART and approved plugins shall be able to query relationships.

Examples include:

- GetRelationships(resource)
- GetUses(resource)
- GetReferencedBy(resource)
- GetDependencies(resource)
- GetSharedResources(resource)
- GetContainingResources(resource)

The framework shall optimize queries internally.

Consumers shall not need to understand the underlying storage
implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Metadata

Each registered relationship may expose metadata.

Examples include:

- Relationship Type
- Creation Date
- Last Updated
- Source Plugin
- Workspace Scope
- Visibility
- Priority
- User-defined Metadata

Future metadata fields shall be supported without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Providers

Plugins may register Relationship Providers.

Relationship Providers may contribute:

- New relationship types
- Computed relationships
- Virtual relationships
- Organization-specific relationships

Relationship Providers shall register through the existing Plugin
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Validators

Plugins may register Relationship Validators.

Validators may enforce:

- Organizational rules
- Industry-specific requirements
- Plugin-specific constraints
- Dependency rules
- Resource compatibility

Validators shall supplement, not replace, the framework's built-in
validation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship Events

The Relationship Framework shall publish standardized events.

Examples include:

- Relationship Created
- Relationship Updated
- Relationship Removed
- Relationship Repaired
- Relationship Validation Failed
- Relationship Query Completed

Events shall integrate with the Plugin Framework's event model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Event Subscribers

Approved plugins may subscribe to relationship events.

Examples include:

- Dashboard refresh
- Explorer refresh
- Search index update
- Report View refresh
- Organization analytics
- Future integrations

Subscribers shall never directly modify framework state during event
processing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Compatibility

Relationship Providers shall declare compatibility with:

- ART version
- Resource Framework version
- Plugin Framework version
- Relationship Framework version

The Plugin Framework shall prevent incompatible providers from loading.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Security

Plugins shall only access relationship information they are authorized
to consume.

The framework shall enforce permissions consistently with the Plugin
Framework.

Relationship Providers shall not bypass ART permission policies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The Relationship Framework API shall:

- Cache frequently used queries where appropriate.
- Support incremental updates.
- Minimize redundant relationship lookups.
- Scale efficiently to large workspaces.
- Avoid blocking the user interface during long-running operations.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Diagnostics

The framework shall expose diagnostic information including:

- Registered relationship types
- Registered providers
- Registered validators
- Validation failures
- Broken relationships
- Query statistics
- Cache statistics (where applicable)

Diagnostics shall integrate with the existing Plugin & Package Manager
where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Extensibility

The Relationship Framework shall support future capabilities including:

- Organization-defined relationship types
- AI-generated relationships
- Workflow relationships
- Version history relationships
- External system references
- Cloud synchronization relationships (future)
- Future resource categories

New relationship types shall not require modifications to the core
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Relationship APIs shall expose sufficient semantic information so that
consuming user interfaces can present relationships accessibly.

Framework APIs shall support:

- Accessible names
- Relationship descriptions
- Relationship categories
- Relationship counts
- Relationship status

Accessibility information shall remain centralized within ART's
Accessibility Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Relationship registration functions correctly.
- Relationship queries return accurate results.
- Relationship metadata is maintained correctly.
- Relationship Providers register successfully.
- Relationship Validators function correctly.
- Relationship events are published correctly.
- Event subscribers function correctly.
- Version compatibility is enforced.
- Permission enforcement functions correctly.
- Diagnostics are accurate.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing framework functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework and Plugin Framework
functionality.

Consume the existing Resource Framework, Plugin Framework, Accessibility
Framework, Universal Search Framework, Explorer Framework, and Report
Views Framework.

Do not duplicate relationship storage, validation, event handling, or
permission management functionality.

The Resource Relationship Framework shall provide the single
authoritative API for relationship management throughout ART while
enabling future expansion through standardized providers, validators,
events, and framework extension points.

### Part 8 – Final Validation, Acceptance Criteria, Documentation & Completion Requirements

#### Overview

This part defines the final acceptance criteria for the Resource
Relationship Framework and establishes the architectural principles that
shall govern future relationship-aware features throughout ART.

Upon completion of this epic, the Resource Relationship Framework shall
become the authoritative mechanism for creating, maintaining, querying,
and exposing relationships between resources.

Future functionality shall consume this framework rather than
implementing independent relationship models.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The completed Resource Relationship Framework shall be:

- Complete
- Accessible
- Consistent
- Extensible
- Framework-driven
- Local-first
- High-performance
- Maintainable
- Enterprise-ready
- Future-proof

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Architectural Principles

The Resource Relationship Framework shall adhere to the following
principles.

##### Single Source of Truth

Relationship information shall exist in one authoritative location.

Explorer, Universal Search, Working Views, Properties dialogs,
Dashboard, plugins, and future consumers shall retrieve relationship
information from the Resource Relationship Framework.

Relationship data shall never be duplicated across multiple frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Framework Reuse

The Resource Relationship Framework shall consume existing ART
frameworks whenever possible.

Examples include:

- Resource Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Accessibility Framework
- Plugin Framework
- Package Framework
- Window Title Framework

Future functionality shall extend these frameworks rather than
duplicating them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Non-Destructive Operation

Relationship discovery, navigation, visualization, grouping, filtering,
and analysis shall never modify resources unless the user explicitly
performs an action that changes the underlying data.

Relationship inspection shall remain read-only by default.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Local-First Architecture

Relationship information shall remain fully functional while ART is
operating offline.

The framework shall not require:

- Cloud services
- User accounts
- Internet connectivity
- Remote databases

unless explicitly required by a future plugin or integration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Accessibility-First Design

Relationship functionality shall comply with all existing ART
accessibility requirements.

Every relationship-aware interface shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Accessibility shall never be optional.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Resource Types

Upon completion of this epic, the framework shall support relationship
management for all applicable ART resource types, including:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Report Templates
- Report Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Project Assets
- Dashboard resources
- Explorer resources
- Plugins
- Packages

Future resource types shall integrate through the existing Resource
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Relationship Types

The framework shall support future relationship categories without
requiring architectural redesign.

Examples include:

- Organization ownership
- Version history
- Workflow dependencies
- AI-generated relationships
- Review assignments
- Approval chains
- External repository references
- Cloud synchronization relationships
- Future relationship categories

Relationship categories shall be extensible through the existing Plugin
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation Requirements

Copilot shall update all relevant documentation to reflect the completed
Resource Relationship Framework.

Documentation shall include:

- Framework overview
- Relationship concepts
- Explorer integration
- Universal Search integration
- Working View integration
- Properties dialog integration
- Safe deletion behavior
- Relationship diagnostics
- Plugin integration
- Developer guidance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User Guide Updates

The User Guide shall include documentation describing:

- What resource relationships are
- How relationships appear in Explorer
- How to navigate related resources
- Understanding the Relationships tab
- Impact Analysis
- Safe Deletion
- Relationship-aware searching
- Relationship-based Working Views

Examples shall demonstrate common relationship workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Developer Documentation

Developer documentation shall include:

- Relationship Framework architecture
- Relationship registration
- Relationship Providers
- Relationship Validators
- Relationship events
- API usage
- Best practices
- Performance recommendations
- Accessibility requirements
- Sample implementations

Documentation shall emphasize reuse of existing ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Source Code Requirements

Copilot shall:

- Eliminate duplicate relationship logic.
- Reuse existing framework implementations.
- Maintain consistent naming conventions.
- Preserve backward compatibility where practical.
- Follow existing ART architectural patterns.
- Keep relationship management centralized.

No framework shall independently manage relationships outside of the
Resource Relationship Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Testing

Before completion, Copilot shall verify that no regressions have been
introduced affecting:

- Resource Framework
- Explorer
- Universal Search
- Dashboard
- Working Views
- Report Viewer
- Report Builder
- Project Workspaces
- Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Templates
- Plugins
- Packages
- Existing import workflows
- Existing export workflows
- Existing keyboard navigation
- Existing context menus
- Existing accessibility functionality

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Acceptance Criteria

The Resource Relationship Framework shall be considered complete when:

- Relationships are automatically maintained throughout the resource
  lifecycle.
- Explorer exposes relationship navigation.
- Properties dialogs display relationship information.
- Universal Search supports relationship-aware searching.
- Working Views support relationship-based analysis.
- Safe Deletion accurately identifies affected resources.
- Plugins can register relationship providers and validators.
- Relationship APIs function correctly.
- Documentation is complete.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality continues to operate without regression.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Verification

Verify that:

- Relationship integrity is maintained throughout ART.
- Existing Resource Framework functionality remains unchanged.
- Relationship navigation functions correctly.
- Relationship-aware searching functions correctly.
- Working Views consume relationship information correctly.
- Safe Deletion behaves correctly.
- Relationship APIs are stable.
- Documentation is complete.

- No duplicate relationship systems have been introduced.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not introduce duplicate relationship models, navigation systems,
search mechanisms, validation logic, or resource management
functionality.

The completed Resource Relationship Framework shall provide the single
