## Epic 36 – Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views

### Part 1 – Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework Architecture

#### Overview

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall provide a
standardized, application-wide mechanism for organizing, classifying,
and quickly accessing resources without modifying the underlying
Resource Framework or Resource Relationship Framework.

This framework shall enable users to create multiple logical
organizations of the same resources through user-defined tags,
collections, and saved views while preserving the integrity of the
original resources and their relationships.

Tags, collections, and saved views shall function as organizational
metadata and shall never duplicate or replace the underlying resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The framework shall be:

- Resource-centric
- Non-destructive
- User-configurable
- Accessible
- Discoverable
- Extensible
- Framework-driven
- Local-first
- High-performance
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The framework shall allow users to organize resources in multiple ways
simultaneously without changing where resources are stored.

Examples include:

- Group reports by client.
- Group reports by release.
- Group reports by sprint.
- Group reports by audit status.
- Mark resources for follow-up.
- Save frequently used Working Views.
- Create temporary or permanent organizational groupings.

The framework shall improve navigation and productivity while preserving
the underlying resource hierarchy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Components

The framework shall consist of three primary organizational mechanisms:

##### Resource Tags

User-defined labels that classify one or more resources.

Examples include:

- Critical
- Needs Review
- Ready for Client
- Mobile
- Desktop
- Training
- Sample
- Archived

Tags shall not imply ownership, hierarchy, or resource location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Collections

Named groups containing references to resources.

Collections shall behave similarly to playlists or saved groups.

A resource may belong to:

- Zero collections
- One collection
- Multiple collections

Collections shall contain references to resources rather than copies of
resources.

Deleting a collection shall never delete the underlying resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Saved Views

Persistent definitions of Working View configurations.

A Saved View shall preserve:

- Grouping
- Sorting
- Filtering
- Visible columns
- Display preferences
- Relationship-based organization where applicable

Opening a Saved View shall recreate a temporary Working View using the
stored configuration.

Saved Views shall not permanently modify reports unless the user
explicitly applies supported changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship to Existing Frameworks

This framework shall extend and consume existing ART frameworks.

It shall integrate with:

- Resource Framework
- Resource Relationship Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Plugin Framework
- Package Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Keyboard Manager
- Window Title Framework

Existing frameworks shall remain authoritative within their respective
responsibilities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Independence

Tags, collections, and saved views shall remain independent of resource
storage.

Resources shall continue to exist only once.

Examples include:

- A report may belong to multiple collections.
- A report may have multiple tags.
- A report may appear in multiple Saved Views.
- A report shall continue to have only one underlying resource.

The framework shall avoid duplication of resource data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Workspace Scope

The framework shall support both workspace-scoped and application-scoped
organizational metadata.

Examples include:

##### Workspace Scope

- Sprint collections
- Current audit tags
- Temporary Saved Views

##### Application Scope

- Personal tags
- Frequently used Saved Views
- Organization collections
- Training collections

Future scope types shall be supported without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metadata Storage

Organizational metadata shall be stored separately from resource content
whenever practical.

Metadata shall include:

- Unique identifier
- Name
- Description
- Creation date
- Last modified date
- Scope
- Owner (future)
- Plugin source (where applicable)

Resources shall not require modification solely to support this
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Responsibilities

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall be
responsible for:

- Registering tags
- Registering collections
- Registering Saved Views
- Maintaining metadata
- Resource associations
- Validation
- Lifecycle management
- Framework integration

The framework shall not duplicate responsibilities already assigned to
other ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Default tags
- Default collections
- Organization collections
- Smart collections (future)
- Saved View templates
- Tag providers
- Collection providers

Plugins shall register through the existing Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The framework shall ensure that organizational metadata is available
through all consuming user interfaces.

Tags, collections, and saved views shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Organizational information shall never rely solely on visual
presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Tags can be registered.
- Collections can be registered.
- Saved Views can be registered.
- Resources participate in multiple collections.
- Resources support multiple tags.
- Saved Views recreate Working Views correctly.
- Organizational metadata remains separate from resource data.
- Plugins register organizational metadata correctly.
- Existing ART frameworks remain unchanged.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, Resource Relationship
Framework, Explorer Framework, Universal Search Framework, and Report
Views Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource storage, relationship management, report
organization, or Working View functionality.

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall provide the
authoritative, non-destructive mechanism for organizing and classifying
resources throughout ART while preserving the framework-driven
architecture established in previous epics.

### Part 2 – Tag Management Framework & Resource Classification

#### Overview

The Resource Tags Framework shall provide a consistent, application-wide
mechanism for creating, managing, assigning, and organizing user-defined
tags.

Tags shall enable users to classify resources according to their own
workflows without affecting the underlying Resource Framework, Resource
Relationship Framework, or resource hierarchy.

A tag shall represent descriptive metadata rather than ownership,
containment, or dependency.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Tags Framework shall be:

- User-defined
- Flexible
- Non-destructive
- Searchable
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Extensible
- Framework-driven

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Characteristics

A tag shall consist of metadata only.

Each tag shall include, at a minimum:

- Unique identifier
- Name
- Optional description
- Scope
- Creation date
- Last modified date
- Color (optional, visual only)
- Plugin source (if applicable)
- Reserved status (system or user-defined)

Future metadata fields shall be supported without redesigning the
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Scope

Tags shall support multiple scopes.

##### Resource-Specific

Available only within a single resource where appropriate.

##### Workspace

Available to all resources within the current Project Workspace.

Examples include:

- Sprint 12
- Client Review
- Regression Testing

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Application

Available throughout ART.

Examples include:

- Training
- Sample
- Archived
- Critical
- Needs Review

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Organization (Future)

Available through future enterprise features or plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Assignment

Users shall be able to assign zero or more tags to any supported
resource.

Examples include:

A report may contain:

- Critical
- Mobile
- Client Review

A template may contain:

- Organization Standard
- Approved

An attachment may contain:

- Screenshot
- Evidence
- Login

Assigning a tag shall not modify the underlying resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multiple Tags

Resources may have multiple tags simultaneously.

Example:

``` text
Homepage Accessibility Report

Tags

• Critical

• WCAG 2.2

• Client Review

• Sprint 5
```

The framework shall impose no arbitrary limit on the number of assigned
tags.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### System Tags

ART may provide built-in system tags.

Examples include:

- Archived
- Sample
- Imported
- Shared
- Organization Default
- Read Only

System tags shall be clearly distinguished from user-created tags.

Users shall not be able to modify protected system tags.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User-Defined Tags

Users shall be able to:

- Create tags
- Rename tags
- Modify descriptions
- Delete unused tags
- Merge tags
- Assign tags
- Remove tags

These operations shall not affect the underlying resources except for
tag assignments.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Manager

ART shall provide a centralized **Tag Manager**.

The Tag Manager shall support:

- Browse tags
- Create tags
- Edit tags
- Delete tags
- Merge tags
- Search tags
- Sort tags
- View usage counts

The Tag Manager shall integrate with the existing Application Settings
architecture where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Assignment Interface

Resources shall expose a consistent mechanism for assigning tags.

Where appropriate, users shall be able to:

- Add existing tags
- Create new tags during assignment
- Remove assigned tags
- Search available tags

Tag assignment shall support keyboard-only workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Usage Counts

The framework shall maintain usage statistics.

Examples include:

``` text
Critical

Used by:

18 Reports

2 Templates

6 Attachments
```

Usage counts shall update automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Merging

Users shall be able to merge tags.

Example:

``` text
Needs Review

Merge Into

Client Review
```

After merging:

- Resource assignments shall transfer automatically.
- Duplicate assignments shall not be created.
- The obsolete tag may be removed.

The operation shall be reversible through ART's existing Undo framework
if supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Reserved Tag Names

The framework may reserve certain tag names for ART.

Examples include:

- System
- Imported
- Archived

Plugins may register additional reserved names.

Reserved tags shall not conflict with user-defined tags.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Default tags
- Organization tags
- Protected tags
- Tag templates
- Tag validation rules

Plugins shall register tags through the existing Plugin Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Integration

Explorer shall expose a **Tags** node.

Example:

``` text
Tags

    Critical

        Homepage Report

        Checkout Report

    Mobile

        Login Report

        Forms Report

    Client Review

        Executive Summary

        Homepage Report
```

Resources shall remain in their original locations.

The Tags node shall provide alternate navigation only.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Universal Search Integration

Universal Search shall support searching by tag.

Examples include:

``` text
tag:critical

tag:"Client Review"

tag:mobile
```

Tag searches shall consume the existing Universal Search Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Resource Tags Framework shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Tag names, descriptions, usage counts, and assignment status shall be
fully programmatically exposed.

Color shall never be the sole method of conveying tag information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Tags can be created.
- Tags can be edited.
- Tags can be deleted.
- Tags can be merged.
- Resources support multiple tags.
- Usage counts update correctly.
- Explorer displays tags correctly.
- Universal Search supports tag queries.
- Plugins register tags correctly.
- Reserved tags function correctly.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, Resource Relationship
Framework, Explorer Framework, Universal Search Framework, and
Application Settings functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource management, search indexing, or Explorer
navigation functionality.

The Resource Tags Framework shall provide the authoritative mechanism
for classifying resources through flexible, user-defined metadata while
preserving ART's accessibility-first and framework-driven architecture.

### Part 3 – Collections Framework & Resource Organization

#### Overview

The Collections Framework shall provide a standardized mechanism for
organizing resources into user-defined groups without changing the
resources' physical location, ownership, relationships, or hierarchy.

Collections shall contain references to resources rather than copies of
resources.

A single resource may belong to any number of collections while
continuing to exist as a single resource within the Resource Framework.

Collections shall complement, not replace:

- Explorer hierarchy
- Resource relationships
- Tags
- Saved Views
- Project Workspaces

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Collections Framework shall be:

- Non-destructive
- User-defined
- Flexible
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Searchable
- Extensible
- Framework-driven

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Characteristics

Each collection shall include, at a minimum:

- Unique identifier
- Name
- Optional description
- Scope
- Creation date
- Last modified date
- Owner (future)
- Collection type
- Plugin source (if applicable)

Future metadata fields shall be supported without redesigning the
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Scope

Collections shall support multiple scopes.

##### Workspace Collections

Collections available only within the current Project Workspace.

Examples include:

- Sprint 6
- Client Deliverables
- Regression Testing
- Phase 1 Review

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Application Collections

Collections available throughout ART.

Examples include:

- Favorite Reports
- Training Examples
- Demonstrations
- Reusable Templates

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Organization Collections (Future)

Collections provided by enterprise features or plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Resource Types

Collections may contain any supported ART resource type, including:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Report Templates
- Report Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Project Assets
- Plugins
- Packages
- Saved Views

Future resource types shall automatically participate through the
Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Membership

A resource may belong to:

- No collections
- One collection
- Multiple collections

Membership shall not affect:

- Resource ownership
- Resource location
- Resource identifiers
- Resource relationships

Removing a resource from a collection shall not delete the resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Manager

ART shall provide a centralized **Collection Manager**.

The Collection Manager shall support:

- Create collection
- Rename collection
- Edit description
- Delete collection
- Duplicate collection
- Search collections
- Sort collections
- View resource counts

Collection management shall integrate with the existing Application
Settings architecture where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Membership

Users shall be able to:

- Add resources to collections
- Remove resources from collections
- Move resources between collections
- Copy resources into additional collections

Adding a resource to a collection shall create only a reference.

No duplicate resources shall be created.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Nested Collections

Collections shall support optional nested collections.

Example:

``` text
Client Deliverables

    Phase 1

    Phase 2

    Executive Reports

Regression Testing

    Sprint 4

    Sprint 5
```

Nested collections shall organize collections only.

Resources shall remain independently referenced.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Resource Counts

Collections shall display resource counts.

Example:

``` text
Client Deliverables

18 Resources

Regression Testing

42 Resources
```

Counts shall update automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Sorting

Users shall be able to sort collection contents.

Examples include:

- Name
- Resource Type
- Date Created
- Date Modified
- Tag
- Accessibility Standard
- Report Status

Sorting shall affect only the current collection view.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Filtering

Collections shall support filtering.

Examples include:

- Reports only
- Attachments only
- Templates only
- Tagged Critical
- Tagged Mobile
- Current Workspace

Filtering shall not modify collection membership.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Integration

Explorer shall expose a dedicated **Collections** node.

Example:

``` text
Collections

    Client Deliverables

        Homepage Report

        Executive Summary

        Final PDF

    Regression Testing

        Login Report

        Checkout Report

    Training Examples

        Sample Audit

        Demo Workspace
```

Collection nodes shall provide alternate navigation only.

Resources shall continue to exist in their original Explorer locations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Universal Search Integration

Universal Search shall support collection-aware searching.

Examples include:

``` text
collection:"Client Deliverables"

collection:Training

collection:Regression
```

Collection membership shall participate in the existing Universal Search
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Context Menus

Collections shall participate in the Global Context Menu Framework.

Examples include:

- Open
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Show Properties
- Reveal in Explorer
- Add Resources…
- Remove Selected Resource
- Sort
- Filter

Commands shall appear only when applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Default collections
- Organization collections
- Collection templates
- Collection validation
- Future smart collections

Plugins shall register collections through the existing Plugin
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Collections Framework shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Collection names, descriptions, resource counts, and membership shall be
fully programmatically exposed.

Collection membership shall never rely solely upon visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Collections can be created.
- Collections can be renamed.
- Collections can be duplicated.
- Collections can be deleted.
- Resources participate in multiple collections.
- Nested collections function correctly.
- Resource counts update automatically.
- Explorer displays collections correctly.
- Universal Search supports collection queries.
- Context menus function correctly.
- Plugins register collections correctly.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, Resource Relationship
Framework, Explorer Framework, Universal Search Framework, and
Application Settings functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource storage, resource relationships, Explorer
hierarchy, or search indexing functionality.

The Collections Framework shall provide the authoritative mechanism for
organizing resources into reusable, non-destructive user-defined groups
while preserving ART's accessibility-first, framework-driven
architecture.

### Part 4 – Saved Views Framework & Persistent Working Views

#### Overview

The Saved Views Framework shall provide a standardized mechanism for
saving, organizing, managing, and reopening frequently used Working View
configurations.

A Saved View shall preserve the configuration of a Working View without
permanently modifying the underlying report, Project Workspace, or
resources.

Opening a Saved View shall recreate a temporary Working View using the
saved configuration while preserving the non-destructive behavior
established in Epic 32.

Saved Views shall describe **how information is presented**, not **what
information exists**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Saved Views Framework shall be:

- Non-destructive
- Reusable
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Resource-aware
- Relationship-aware
- Extensible
- Framework-driven

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

Saved Views shall eliminate the need for users to repeatedly recreate
the same Working Views.

Examples include:

- Critical Findings
- WCAG 2.2 Review
- Keyboard Accessibility Review
- Color Contrast Review
- Mobile Accessibility Review
- Client Deliverables
- Open Findings
- Findings Requiring Screenshots
- Executive Summary Preparation

Saved Views shall increase productivity while preserving the integrity
of the underlying report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved View Definition

Each Saved View shall include, at a minimum:

- Unique identifier
- Name
- Optional description
- Scope
- Creation date
- Last modified date
- Resource type
- Plugin source (if applicable)

Future metadata fields shall be supported without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Configuration

A Saved View may preserve:

- Sorting
- Filtering
- Grouping
- Expanded or collapsed groups
- Visible columns
- Column order
- Column widths
- Relationship-based grouping
- Navigation preferences
- Explorer synchronization preferences (future)

Saved Views shall not permanently reorder report content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Scope

Saved Views shall support multiple scopes.

##### Report

Available only for a specific report.

##### Workspace

Available throughout the current Project Workspace.

##### Application

Available throughout ART.

##### Organization (Future)

Available through future enterprise features or plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Creating a Saved View

Users shall be able to create a Saved View from the currently active
Working View.

The saved configuration shall reflect the current presentation only.

The report data itself shall not be modified.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Opening a Saved View

Opening a Saved View shall:

- Create a temporary Working View.
- Apply the stored configuration.
- Update the application window title using ART's existing Window Title
  Framework.
- Move focus to the first visible item within the Working View.
- Preserve the underlying report.

Saved Views shall inherit all Working View behavior established in Epic
32.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Updating a Saved View

Users shall be able to:

- Save changes to the current Saved View.
- Save As New Saved View.
- Rename Saved View.
- Edit description.

Updating a Saved View shall never modify report data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved View Manager

ART shall provide a centralized **Saved View Manager**.

The Saved View Manager shall support:

- Browse Saved Views
- Search Saved Views
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Export
- Import
- View properties

Management shall integrate with existing ART framework patterns.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Integration

Explorer shall expose a dedicated **Saved Views** node.

Example:

``` text
Saved Views

    Critical Findings

    WCAG 2.2 Review

    Keyboard Accessibility

    Mobile Review

    Executive Summary
```

Selecting a Saved View shall recreate the corresponding temporary
Working View.

Saved Views shall not duplicate reports.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Integration

The Dashboard Framework may display:

- Recently Used Saved Views
- Favorite Saved Views
- Recommended Saved Views (future)

Dashboard cards shall consume the existing Dashboard Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Universal Search Integration

Universal Search shall support Saved View queries.

Examples include:

``` text
view:"Critical Findings"

view:Keyboard

view:Executive
```

Search results shall identify matching Saved Views separately from
reports and other resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menus

Saved Views shall participate in the Global Context Menu Framework.

Examples include:

- Open
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Show Properties
- Reveal in Explorer
- Export
- Copy Name

Commands shall appear only when applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Integration

Saved Views shall inherit all existing Window Title Framework
requirements.

Examples include:

``` text
Accessibility Reporting Tool

Report Viewer

Working View – Critical Findings (Temporary)
```

or

``` text
Accessibility Reporting Tool

Report Viewer

Working View – Keyboard Accessibility Review (Temporary)
```

The window title shall clearly indicate that the user is viewing a
temporary Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Exit Behavior

Saved Views shall inherit the existing Working View exit behavior.

Users may exit the Working View by:

- Activating **Exit Working View**
- Pressing **Escape**, when no menu, search box, dialog, or other
  higher-priority UI element currently owns Escape behavior

Exiting shall:

- Close the temporary Working View.
- Restore the report's original presentation.
- Restore focus to approximately the same report item viewed within the
  Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Default Saved Views
- Organization Saved Views
- Saved View templates
- Specialized report perspectives
- Future Saved View providers

Plugins shall register Saved Views through the existing Plugin
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Saved Views Framework shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Saved View names, descriptions, scope, and configuration summaries shall
be fully programmatically exposed.

The temporary nature of Working Views recreated from Saved Views shall
be clearly communicated to assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Saved Views can be created.
- Saved Views can be opened.
- Saved Views recreate Working Views accurately.
- Saved Views can be renamed.
- Saved Views can be duplicated.
- Saved Views can be deleted.
- Saved Views can be imported and exported.
- Explorer displays Saved Views correctly.
- Dashboard integration functions correctly.
- Universal Search supports Saved View queries.
- Window titles update correctly.
- Escape exits the temporary Working View correctly.
- Plugin-provided Saved Views function correctly.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing Working View functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Report Views Framework, Explorer Framework,
Dashboard Framework, Universal Search Framework, Window Title Framework,
and Resource Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate Working View functionality or report organization
logic.

The Saved Views Framework shall provide the authoritative mechanism for
persisting and reopening Working View configurations while preserving
ART's accessibility-first, framework-driven, and non-destructive
architecture.

### Part 5 – Explorer, Dashboard & Navigation Integration

#### Overview

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall integrate
with the Explorer Framework and Dashboard Framework to provide
consistent, accessible, and efficient navigation to organizational
metadata throughout ART.

Explorer shall remain the primary navigation interface for resources
while providing alternate, non-destructive organizational views based on
tags, collections, and saved views.

Dashboard shall provide quick access to commonly used organizational
resources without replacing Explorer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

Navigation integration shall be:

- Discoverable
- Consistent
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Non-destructive
- Resource-aware
- Extensible
- Framework-driven

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Organization

Explorer shall expose dedicated top-level nodes for organizational
metadata.

Example:

``` text
Project Workspace

    Reports

    Templates

    Attachments

    Accessibility Standards

Collections

Tags

Saved Views
```

These nodes shall represent alternate organizational perspectives.

They shall not replace the underlying resource hierarchy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collections Node

The **Collections** node shall display user-defined collections.

Example:

``` text
Collections

    Client Deliverables

    Regression Testing

    Sprint 6

    Training
```

Expanding a collection shall display references to its resources.

Resources shall continue to exist only once within the Resource
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tags Node

The **Tags** node shall organize resources by assigned tags.

Example:

``` text
Tags

    Critical

        Homepage Report

        Login Report

    Client Review

        Executive Summary

        Checkout Report

    Mobile

        Forms Report
```

Selecting a tagged resource shall navigate to the underlying resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Views Node

The **Saved Views** node shall display available Saved Views.

Example:

``` text
Saved Views

    Critical Findings

    WCAG 2.2 Review

    Executive Summary

    Mobile Accessibility
```

Activating a Saved View shall recreate its corresponding temporary
Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Behavior

Selecting a resource through:

- Collections
- Tags
- Saved Views

shall navigate to the underlying resource without creating duplicate
resources.

Explorer shall automatically:

- Expand required hierarchy.
- Select the destination resource.
- Move keyboard focus appropriately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Cross-Navigation

Users shall be able to move seamlessly between:

- Resource hierarchy
- Collections
- Tags
- Saved Views
- Relationship nodes

Navigation shall remain consistent regardless of entry point.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Synchronization

Explorer shall synchronize selection across organizational views where
appropriate.

Example:

If a user selects:

``` text
Collections

    Client Deliverables

        Homepage Report
```

the underlying report shall become the active resource throughout ART.

Other frameworks shall recognize the same active resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Integration

Dashboard may provide dedicated cards for:

- Recent Collections
- Favorite Collections
- Frequently Used Tags
- Recently Used Saved Views
- Favorite Saved Views

Dashboard cards shall consume existing Dashboard Framework services.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Actions

Dashboard cards may support:

- Open
- Pin
- Remove from Favorites
- Show Properties
- Reveal in Explorer

Dashboard actions shall integrate with the Application Command
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites

Users may designate:

- Tags
- Collections
- Saved Views

as Favorites.

Favorites shall appear:

- On the Dashboard
- Within Explorer (optional)
- Within Universal Search ranking where appropriate

Favorite status shall not affect resource behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recently Used

ART shall maintain recently used lists for:

- Collections
- Saved Views

Recently used information shall support quick navigation.

The framework shall avoid maintaining unnecessary history for individual
tag assignments.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menus

Collections, Tags, and Saved Views shall participate in the Global
Context Menu Framework.

Examples include:

##### Collections

- Open
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Add Resources
- Show Properties

##### Tags

- Assign
- Remove
- Rename
- Merge
- Show Usage
- Show Properties

##### Saved Views

- Open
- Rename
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Export
- Show Properties

Commands shall appear only when applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Integration

When navigating organizational metadata, ART shall continue to follow
the existing Window Title Framework.

Explorer navigation alone shall not modify the application window title.

Only opening a report, dialog, Working View, Saved View, or other
window-title-aware component shall update the title.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Explorer organizational nodes
- Dashboard cards
- Collection categories
- Tag categories
- Saved View categories
- Organization favorites

Plugins shall consume the existing Explorer and Dashboard Frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

Explorer and Dashboard integration shall:

- Load organizational metadata incrementally.
- Avoid duplicate resource loading.
- Cache organizational structures where practical.
- Refresh only affected nodes.
- Maintain acceptable responsiveness for large workspaces.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Explorer and Dashboard integration shall support:

- Keyboard-only navigation
- Arrow-key navigation
- Continuous menu and tree navigation as defined in previous epics
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Collections, Tags, and Saved Views shall expose:

- Accessible Name
- Accessible Role
- Expanded/Collapsed State
- Position within hierarchy
- Resource counts where applicable

Equivalent information shall be available regardless of presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Explorer displays Collections correctly.
- Explorer displays Tags correctly.
- Explorer displays Saved Views correctly.
- Navigation always resolves to the correct underlying resource.
- Dashboard cards function correctly.
- Favorites function correctly.
- Recently Used lists function correctly.
- Context menus function correctly.
- Window titles remain consistent with ART requirements.
- Plugin contributions integrate correctly.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing Explorer and Dashboard functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Explorer Framework, Dashboard Framework, Window
Title Framework, Application Command Framework, and Resource Framework
functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate Explorer navigation, Dashboard functionality, or
resource management logic.

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall extend
Explorer and Dashboard with rich, accessible organizational navigation
while preserving the existing resource hierarchy and ART's
framework-driven architecture.

### Part 6 – Universal Search, Smart Queries & Organizational Discovery

#### Overview

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall integrate
with the Universal Search Framework to provide comprehensive discovery
of resources through organizational metadata.

Users shall be able to locate resources by searching for:

- Tags
- Collections
- Saved Views
- Resource names
- Resource metadata
- Relationship metadata
- Combined search criteria

The Universal Search Framework shall remain the authoritative search
engine for ART.

The Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall contribute
additional searchable metadata without duplicating search functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

Organizational searching shall be:

- Fast
- Discoverable
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Resource-aware
- Context-aware
- Extensible
- Framework-driven

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Searchable Metadata

Universal Search shall index organizational metadata including:

##### Tags

- Tag names
- Tag descriptions
- Reserved tags
- Plugin-defined tags

##### Collections

- Collection names
- Collection descriptions
- Collection membership

##### Saved Views

- Saved View names
- Saved View descriptions
- Saved View scope
- Saved View configuration metadata

Future organizational metadata shall automatically become searchable
after registration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Syntax

Universal Search shall support structured organizational queries.

Examples include:

``` text
tag:critical

tag:"Needs Review"

collection:"Client Deliverables"

collection:Training

view:"WCAG 2.2 Review"

view:Keyboard

tag:critical collection:"Sprint 6"

tag:mobile view:"Accessibility Review"
```

Structured queries shall integrate seamlessly with standard free-text
searching.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Combined Queries

Users shall be able to combine organizational metadata with existing
search capabilities.

Examples include:

``` text
tag:critical WCAG 2.2

collection:"Client Review" attachment

view:"Executive Summary" contrast

tag:mobile relationship:"Uses WCAG 2.2"
```

Search criteria shall be evaluated together.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Suggestions

Universal Search shall provide intelligent suggestions while users type.

Examples include:

``` text
Tags

Critical

Client Review

Collections

Training

Regression Testing

Saved Views

Executive Summary

Keyboard Accessibility
```

Suggestions shall be generated dynamically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Presentation

Search results shall distinguish between:

- Resource matches
- Tag matches
- Collection matches
- Saved View matches
- Relationship matches

Each result shall clearly indicate why it was returned.

Example:

``` text
Homepage Report

Matched By

Tag

Critical
```

or

``` text
Executive Summary

Matched By

Collection

Client Deliverables
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organizational Filters

Universal Search shall support filtering by organizational metadata.

Examples include:

##### Tags

- Critical
- Client Review
- Mobile

##### Collections

- Training
- Current Sprint
- Deliverables

##### Saved Views

- Executive Summary
- WCAG Review

Filters shall refine search results without modifying the underlying
metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organizational Facets

Search results may display facets including:

``` text
Tags

Critical (18)

Needs Review (7)

Collections

Client Deliverables (12)

Regression Testing (21)

Saved Views

Keyboard Review (1)

Executive Summary (2)
```

Selecting a facet shall filter the current search results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep Linking

Search results shall support direct navigation.

Users shall be able to:

- Open Resource
- Reveal in Explorer
- Open Properties
- Open Collection
- Open Saved View
- Show Assigned Tags
- Show Relationships

Navigation shall consume existing ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Ranking

Search ranking shall prioritize:

1.  Exact resource matches
2.  Exact tag matches
3.  Exact collection matches
4.  Exact Saved View matches
5.  Relationship matches
6.  Partial matches

The ranking algorithm shall continue using the existing Universal Search
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search History

Universal Search may maintain recently used organizational searches.

Examples include:

``` text
tag:critical

collection:"Client Deliverables"

view:"Executive Summary"
```

History shall remain local to the user's device.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Organizational search providers
- Custom search suggestions
- Organization-specific filters
- Additional searchable metadata

Plugins shall register through the existing Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not replace the Universal Search Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

Organizational searching shall:

- Index metadata incrementally.
- Update automatically when metadata changes.
- Avoid rebuilding the complete search index.
- Scale efficiently to large workspaces.
- Maintain existing Universal Search responsiveness.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Universal Search shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Search results shall expose:

- Resource name
- Match type
- Matching tag
- Matching collection
- Matching Saved View
- Available actions

All organizational metadata shall be fully programmatically exposed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Tags are searchable.
- Collections are searchable.
- Saved Views are searchable.
- Combined queries function correctly.
- Search suggestions function correctly.
- Organizational filters function correctly.
- Organizational facets function correctly.
- Deep linking functions correctly.
- Search ranking remains appropriate.
- Search history functions correctly.
- Plugin contributions integrate correctly.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing Universal Search functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Universal Search Framework functionality.

Consume the existing Universal Search Framework, Resource Framework,
Resource Relationship Framework, Explorer Framework, and Application
Command Framework.

Do not duplicate search indexing, search ranking, or query processing
functionality.

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall extend
Universal Search with rich organizational discovery capabilities while
preserving ART's accessibility-first, high-performance, and
framework-driven architecture.

### Part 7 – Framework API, Plugin Integration, Import/Export & Lifecycle Management

#### Overview

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall provide a
standardized API for creating, managing, querying, importing, exporting,
and maintaining organizational metadata throughout ART.

The framework shall serve as the authoritative source for tags,
collections, and saved views.

Plugins and future ART components shall consume this framework rather
than implementing independent organizational systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The framework API shall be:

- Centralized
- Extensible
- Accessible
- Framework-driven
- Version-aware
- Local-first
- High-performance
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organizational Services

The framework shall expose centralized services including:

- Tag Service
- Collection Service
- Saved View Service

These services shall provide a consistent programming model for ART and
approved plugins.

No other framework shall maintain independent implementations of these
organizational concepts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tag Service

The Tag Service shall support operations including:

- Create Tag
- Update Tag
- Delete Tag
- Merge Tags
- Assign Tag
- Remove Tag
- Query Tags
- Retrieve Usage Counts
- Validate Tag

The internal implementation may vary provided equivalent functionality
is maintained.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collection Service

The Collection Service shall support operations including:

- Create Collection
- Rename Collection
- Delete Collection
- Duplicate Collection
- Add Resource
- Remove Resource
- Query Membership
- Validate Collection

Collections shall store references to resources rather than duplicate
resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved View Service

The Saved View Service shall support operations including:

- Create Saved View
- Update Saved View
- Rename Saved View
- Delete Saved View
- Duplicate Saved View
- Open Saved View
- Validate Saved View

Opening a Saved View shall recreate a temporary Working View using the
existing Report Views Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organizational Events

The framework shall publish standardized events including:

##### Tags

- Tag Created
- Tag Updated
- Tag Deleted
- Tag Assigned
- Tag Removed
- Tags Merged

##### Collections

- Collection Created
- Collection Updated
- Collection Deleted
- Resource Added
- Resource Removed

##### Saved Views

- Saved View Created
- Saved View Updated
- Saved View Deleted
- Saved View Opened

Events shall integrate with the existing Plugin Framework event model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Event Subscribers

Approved plugins may subscribe to organizational events.

Examples include:

- Explorer refresh
- Dashboard refresh
- Universal Search index update
- Resource metadata update
- Future analytics
- Future enterprise integrations

Subscribers shall not directly manipulate framework state during event
processing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Import & Export

The framework shall support importing and exporting organizational
metadata independently of the underlying resources.

Supported organizational data includes:

- Tags
- Collections
- Saved Views

Importing organizational metadata shall not duplicate existing
resources.

Exporting organizational metadata shall preserve references whenever
practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Existing ART Workflows

The framework shall integrate with ART's existing import and export
workflows.

Copilot shall **not** create new import or export workflows for tags,
collections, or saved views if equivalent workflows already exist.

Instead, the existing workflows shall be extended to support
organizational metadata where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Import Validation

During import, the framework shall validate:

- Unique identifiers
- Collection membership
- Saved View compatibility
- Tag definitions
- Version compatibility
- Missing resources
- Duplicate organizational metadata

Import validation shall not modify existing resources until validation
succeeds.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Missing Resources

If imported organizational metadata references resources that are
unavailable, the framework shall:

- Preserve the organizational metadata.
- Mark unresolved references.
- Notify the user.
- Allow later resolution where practical.

Import shall not fail solely because referenced resources are
unavailable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Lifecycle Management

The framework shall automatically maintain organizational metadata when
resources are:

- Created
- Renamed
- Moved
- Copied
- Duplicated
- Deleted
- Restored
- Imported
- Exported

Resource lifecycle events shall automatically update tags, collections,
and saved views where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- Default tags
- Default collections
- Default Saved Views
- Organizational templates
- Organizational validators
- Organizational metadata providers

Plugins shall register these components through the existing Plugin
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Compatibility

Plugins contributing organizational metadata shall declare compatibility
with:

- ART version
- Resource Framework version
- Plugin Framework version
- Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework version

The Plugin Framework shall prevent incompatible plugins from loading.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Diagnostics

The framework shall expose diagnostic information including:

- Registered tags
- Registered collections
- Registered Saved Views
- Usage statistics
- Validation failures
- Import warnings
- Export warnings
- Plugin providers

Diagnostics shall integrate with ART's existing diagnostics and Plugin &
Package Manager where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The framework shall:

- Cache organizational metadata where practical.
- Update metadata incrementally.
- Avoid unnecessary rebuilding of indexes.
- Scale efficiently to large workspaces.
- Maintain responsiveness throughout ART.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The framework shall expose sufficient semantic information so that
consuming user interfaces present organizational metadata accessibly.

Framework APIs shall support:

- Accessible names
- Descriptions
- Counts
- Assignment status
- Scope
- Category
- Validation status

Accessibility information shall remain centralized within ART's
Accessibility Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Tag services function correctly.
- Collection services function correctly.
- Saved View services function correctly.
- Organizational events are published correctly.
- Event subscribers function correctly.
- Organizational metadata imports correctly.
- Organizational metadata exports correctly.
- Missing resource references are handled correctly.
- Lifecycle management functions correctly.
- Plugin integration functions correctly.
- Diagnostics are accurate.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, Plugin Framework,
Import/Export workflows, and Report Views Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate organizational metadata management, import/export
workflows, event handling, or lifecycle management functionality.

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall provide the
single authoritative API for managing organizational metadata throughout
ART while supporting future expansion through standardized services,
providers, validators, and framework extension points.

### Part 8 – Final Validation, Acceptance Criteria, Documentation & Completion Requirements

#### Overview

This part defines the final acceptance criteria for the Resource Tags,
Collections & Saved Views Framework and establishes the architectural
principles that shall govern future organizational features throughout
ART.

Upon completion of this epic, the framework shall become the
authoritative mechanism for organizing, classifying, and presenting
resources without modifying the underlying Resource Framework or
Resource Relationship Framework.

Future organizational features shall consume this framework rather than
introducing independent implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The completed framework shall be:

- Accessible
- Consistent
- Extensible
- Framework-driven
- High-performance
- Local-first
- Maintainable
- Non-destructive
- Scalable
- Future-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Architectural Principles

The framework shall adhere to the following principles.

##### Single Source of Truth

Tags, collections, and saved views shall each have a single
authoritative implementation.

Explorer, Dashboard, Universal Search, Working Views, plugins, and
future consumers shall retrieve organizational metadata from this
framework.

Organizational metadata shall never be duplicated across multiple
frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Separation of Responsibilities

The framework shall preserve clear responsibilities throughout ART.

##### Resource Framework

Owns the resources.

##### Resource Relationship Framework

Defines relationships between resources.

##### Tags Framework

Classifies resources.

##### Collections Framework

Organizes resources into reusable user-defined groups.

##### Saved Views Framework

Persists temporary report presentation configurations.

No framework shall assume responsibilities assigned to another
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Non-Destructive Operation

Tags, collections, and saved views shall never modify the underlying
resources unless the user explicitly performs an operation that changes
resource data.

Organizational metadata shall remain independent of resource content.

Deleting organizational metadata shall not delete the associated
resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Local-First Architecture

The framework shall operate entirely offline.

Tags, collections, and saved views shall not require:

- Cloud services
- User accounts
- Internet connectivity
- Remote databases

unless explicitly required by a future plugin or integration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Accessibility-First Design

Every organizational feature shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Accessibility shall never depend upon color or visual presentation
alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation Requirements

Copilot shall update all relevant documentation describing the completed
framework.

Documentation shall include:

- Framework overview
- Tags
- Collections
- Saved Views
- Explorer integration
- Dashboard integration
- Universal Search integration
- Plugin integration
- Import/Export behavior
- Developer guidance

Documentation shall remain consistent with previous framework epics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User Guide Updates

The User Guide shall include guidance describing:

##### Tags

- Creating tags
- Assigning tags
- Removing tags
- Merging tags
- Searching by tags

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Collections

- Creating collections
- Managing collections
- Adding resources
- Removing resources
- Nested collections
- Collection navigation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Saved Views

- Creating Saved Views
- Opening Saved Views
- Updating Saved Views
- Deleting Saved Views
- Relationship to Working Views

Examples shall illustrate common workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Developer Documentation

Developer documentation shall include:

- Framework architecture
- Framework services
- Plugin integration
- Organizational providers
- Organizational events
- Import/Export integration
- Accessibility guidance
- Performance recommendations
- Sample implementations
- Best practices

Documentation shall emphasize reuse of existing ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Source Code Requirements

Copilot shall:

- Eliminate duplicate organizational logic.
- Reuse existing framework implementations.
- Maintain consistent naming conventions.
- Preserve backward compatibility where practical.
- Follow established ART architectural patterns.
- Centralize organizational metadata management.

No independent organizational implementations shall remain elsewhere
within ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Testing

Before completion, Copilot shall verify that no regressions have been
introduced affecting:

- Resource Framework
- Resource Relationship Framework
- Explorer
- Dashboard
- Universal Search
- Working Views
- Report Viewer
- Report Builder
- Project Workspaces
- Attachments
- Templates
- Accessibility Standards
- Plugins
- Packages
- Existing import workflows
- Existing export workflows
- Existing keyboard navigation
- Existing context menus
- Existing accessibility functionality

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Acceptance Criteria

The Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall be
considered complete when:

- Tags function correctly throughout ART.
- Collections organize resources without duplication.
- Saved Views accurately recreate Working Views.
- Explorer exposes organizational metadata correctly.
- Dashboard integrates organizational shortcuts correctly.
- Universal Search supports organizational queries.
- Organizational metadata imports and exports correctly using existing
  ART workflows.
- Plugins integrate successfully.
- Documentation is complete.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality continues to operate without regression.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Extensibility

The framework shall support future capabilities without architectural
redesign, including:

- Smart Collections
- Dynamic Collections
- Rule-based Tags
- Automatic Tag Assignment
- Shared Team Collections
- Organization-wide Saved Views
- AI-assisted Tag Suggestions
- AI-assisted Collection Recommendations
- Future enterprise organizational features

These capabilities shall extend the framework rather than replacing it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Verification

Verify that:

- All parts of this epic have been implemented.
- Organizational metadata remains independent of resource data.
- Resources participate correctly in multiple tags and collections.
- Saved Views recreate Working Views accurately.
- Explorer integration functions correctly.
- Dashboard integration functions correctly.
- Universal Search integration functions correctly.
- Plugin integration functions correctly.
- Documentation is complete.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not introduce duplicate implementations for tags, collections, saved
views, navigation, search indexing, import/export, or organizational
metadata management.

The completed Resource Tags, Collections & Saved Views Framework shall
provide the single authoritative, accessible, extensible, and
maintainable foundation for organizing and presenting resources
throughout ART while preserving the framework-driven architecture
established by previous epics.

## Epic 37 – History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework

### Part 1 – History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework Architecture

#### Overview

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall provide a
centralized, application-wide mechanism for recording, reviewing,
undoing, redoing, comparing, restoring, and managing changes made
throughout ART.

Rather than allowing individual components to implement independent
history mechanisms, every participating framework shall consume the
shared History Framework.

The History Framework shall become the authoritative source for:

- Undo
- Redo
- Change history
- Resource version history
- Transaction history
- Restore operations
- Change comparison
- Version navigation
- History queries

Future ART functionality shall consume this framework rather than
implementing separate history systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The History Framework shall be:

- Centralized
- Non-destructive
- Accessible
- Framework-driven
- Extensible
- Local-first
- High-performance
- Predictable
- Recoverable
- Enterprise-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The framework shall allow users to:

- Undo mistakes.
- Redo previously undone operations.
- Review previous changes.
- Compare resource versions.
- Restore earlier versions.
- Recover deleted resources where supported.
- Review workspace activity.
- Safely experiment without fear of losing work.

The framework shall improve user confidence while preserving ART's
local-first architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship to Existing Frameworks

The History Framework shall integrate with and consume existing ART
frameworks, including:

- Resource Framework
- Resource Relationship Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Report Views Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Plugin Framework
- Package Framework
- Window Title Framework
- Application Command Framework
- Keyboard Manager

Existing frameworks shall remain responsible for their own domain logic.

The History Framework shall only record and manage change history.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### History Scope

The framework shall support history for all versionable ART resources,
including:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Report Templates
- Report Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Project Assets
- Collections
- Saved Views
- Plugins
- Packages

Where appropriate, additional metadata such as tag assignments and
relationship changes shall also participate in history tracking.

Future resource types shall integrate through the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Versionable Operations

Examples of operations that may participate in history include:

- Create
- Rename
- Edit
- Move
- Copy
- Duplicate
- Delete
- Restore
- Import
- Export
- Assign Tag
- Remove Tag
- Collection membership changes
- Relationship changes
- Accessibility Standard updates
- Template modifications

The framework shall determine whether an operation is undoable,
versionable, or informational.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### History Entries

Each recorded history entry shall include, at a minimum:

- Unique identifier
- Timestamp
- Operation type
- Resource type
- Resource identifier
- Resource name (at the time of the operation)
- Brief description
- Undo availability
- Redo availability
- Transaction identifier (where applicable)
- Plugin source (if applicable)

Future metadata fields shall be supported without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Independence

History shall describe changes to resources without replacing or
duplicating the underlying resources.

Resources shall continue to be managed exclusively by the Resource
Framework.

The History Framework shall reference resources rather than storing
duplicate resource data whenever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### History Lifetime

The framework shall support configurable retention policies.

Examples include:

- Current session
- Current workspace
- Application lifetime
- User-defined retention period
- Unlimited (subject to storage constraints)

Retention settings shall be configurable through Application Settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User Interface Integration

The History Framework shall avoid introducing persistent interface
elements that increase visual clutter.

Instead, history functionality shall integrate with existing ART
navigation mechanisms.

Primary access shall be provided through:

##### Menu Bar

History commands shall be available from the **Edit** menu, within a
History sub menu.

Example commands that may be included within the History sub menu
include:

- Undo
- Redo
- History…
- Compare Versions…
- Restore Previous Version…
- Clear History…

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Command Palette

The existing Command Palette shall expose history commands.

Examples include:

- History
- Undo
- Redo
- Compare Versions
- Restore Previous Version
- Clear History

History commands shall participate in the existing Command Palette
search and ranking behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Menu Bar Search

The existing Menu Bar Search feature shall index history-related
commands.

Users shall be able to locate commands by searching for terms such as:

- History
- Undo
- Redo
- Compare Versions
- Restore Version
- Clear History

History commands shall appear alongside all other searchable application
commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Context Menus

Where appropriate, resource context menus may expose:

- History…
- Compare Versions…
- Restore Previous Version…

These commands shall appear only when supported by the selected
resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deliberately Excluded

To preserve a clean user interface:

The framework shall **not** introduce:

- A permanent History pane
- A permanent History toolbar
- A History node in Explorer
- A mandatory Dashboard History widget

Future Dashboard widgets showing recent activity may be implemented as
optional dashboard components.

Explorer shall remain focused on current resources rather than
historical events.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The History Framework shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

History metadata shall be fully programmatically exposed.

Time, operation type, resource name, and available actions shall never
rely solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- History entries are recorded correctly.
- Versionable resources participate correctly.
- Menu Bar commands are available.
- Command Palette exposes history commands.
- Menu Bar Search locates history commands.
- Context menus display supported history actions.
- Explorer remains free of permanent history nodes.
- Dashboard remains uncluttered by default.
- History metadata remains independent of resource data.
- Existing ART frameworks remain unchanged.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, Explorer Framework, Dashboard
Framework, Universal Search Framework, Application Command Framework,
Command Palette, Menu Bar Search, Window Title Framework, and Keyboard
Manager functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource management, version tracking, command routing,
or navigation functionality.

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall provide the
authoritative, centralized, and accessible foundation for recording and
managing changes throughout ART while preserving the clean, professional
desktop interface established by previous epics.

### Part 2 – Undo/Redo Framework & Transaction Management

#### Overview

The Undo/Redo Framework shall provide a centralized mechanism for
reversing and reapplying supported operations throughout ART.

Rather than each feature implementing its own undo logic, all undoable
operations shall register with the shared History Framework.

The Undo/Redo Framework shall ensure that changes are applied
consistently, predictably, and safely across all participating ART
frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Undo/Redo Framework shall be:

- Centralized
- Predictable
- Transaction-based
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Non-destructive
- Framework-driven
- Extensible

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Operations

Undo and Redo shall support all eligible operations performed within
participating frameworks.

Examples include:

- Create resource
- Rename resource
- Edit resource properties
- Delete resource
- Restore resource
- Move resource
- Copy resource
- Duplicate resource
- Import resource
- Assign tag
- Remove tag
- Create collection
- Modify collection membership
- Create Saved View
- Modify Saved View
- Relationship changes
- Plugin installation and removal (where supported)
- Accessibility Standard imports

Operations that cannot safely be undone shall be recorded as
informational history entries only.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Undo Stack

The framework shall maintain an ordered Undo stack.

Each successful undoable operation shall be added to the top of the
stack.

Undo operations shall be performed in reverse chronological order.

The framework shall automatically maintain stack integrity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Redo Stack

Whenever an undo operation is performed, the corresponding transaction
shall be placed on the Redo stack.

Performing a new undoable operation shall clear the Redo stack in
accordance with standard desktop application behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Transaction-Based Architecture

Undo and Redo shall operate on transactions rather than individual
implementation details.

A transaction may represent:

- A single operation
- A grouped operation
- A batch operation
- A plugin-defined operation

The framework shall determine transaction boundaries.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Atomic Operations

Each undoable transaction shall either:

- Complete successfully, or
- Roll back completely.

Partial undo states shall not be permitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multi-Step Operations

Some user actions may involve multiple internal operations.

Examples include:

- Importing an Accessibility Standard
- Installing a plugin
- Duplicating a report
- Creating a Project Workspace

These operations shall appear as a single undoable transaction whenever
practical.

Example:

``` text
Undo

Import WCAG 2.2 Package
```

rather than displaying dozens of internal implementation steps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User-Facing Descriptions

Each undoable transaction shall provide a concise, user-friendly
description.

Examples include:

``` text
Undo Rename Report

Undo Delete Attachment

Undo Assign Tag

Undo Create Collection

Undo Import Accessibility Standard
```

Descriptions shall describe the user action rather than implementation
details.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Integration

The existing **Edit** menu shall expose Undo and Redo.

Example:

``` text
Edit

Undo Rename Report         Ctrl+Z

Redo Rename Report         Ctrl+Y
```

Menu labels shall dynamically reflect the next available action whenever
practical.

If no action is available, the command shall remain visible but
disabled.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

The existing Command Palette shall expose:

- Undo
- Redo

Dynamic descriptions may be displayed where supported.

Examples include:

``` text
Undo Rename Report

Redo Import Plugin
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Search Integration
