Menu Bar Search shall index:

- Undo
- Redo

Users searching for:

``` text
Undo

Redo

Restore
```

shall locate the corresponding commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcuts

The framework shall use existing keyboard shortcuts.

Default shortcuts include:

- **Ctrl+Z** — Undo
- **Ctrl+Y** — Redo

Support for **Ctrl+Shift+Z** as an alternate Redo shortcut may be
provided where appropriate.

All shortcuts shall remain configurable through the existing Keyboard
Manager.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menu Integration

Where appropriate, resource context menus may expose:

- Undo
- Redo

Commands shall appear only when relevant to the selected resource or
current context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Undo Confirmation

Routine undoable operations shall execute immediately without requiring
confirmation.

Examples include:

- Rename
- Move
- Tag assignment
- Collection membership changes

Operations that may result in data loss beyond the undo history or
affect multiple unrelated resources may require confirmation.

The framework shall determine when confirmation is appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Transaction History

Each undo and redo operation shall itself be recorded in the History
Framework.

History entries shall indicate:

- Original operation
- Undo
- Redo
- Timestamp

This shall provide a complete chronological record of user activity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute undoable operations.

Plugins shall register undo handlers through the existing Plugin
Framework.

Plugin-defined operations shall:

- Participate in the global Undo stack.
- Participate in the global Redo stack.
- Follow transaction rules.
- Provide user-friendly descriptions.

Plugins shall not maintain independent undo systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Failure Handling

If an undo or redo operation cannot be completed safely, the framework
shall:

- Preserve application stability.
- Leave resources in a consistent state.
- Notify the user with an accessible error message.
- Record the failure in diagnostics where appropriate.

Partial transaction completion shall not occur.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The Undo/Redo Framework shall:

- Execute operations efficiently.
- Avoid unnecessary duplication of resource data.
- Scale to large transactions.
- Support incremental recording.
- Minimize memory usage where practical.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Undo and Redo shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Dynamic menu labels and command descriptions shall be fully
programmatically exposed.

Disabled commands shall communicate their unavailable state to assistive
technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Undo operates correctly.
- Redo operates correctly.
- Undo and Redo stacks are maintained correctly.
- Transaction grouping functions correctly.
- Multi-step operations appear as single transactions where appropriate.
- Menu labels update correctly.
- Command Palette integration functions correctly.
- Menu Bar Search locates Undo and Redo commands.
- Keyboard shortcuts function correctly.
- Context menus display supported commands.
- Plugin-defined undo operations integrate correctly.
- Failure handling preserves application consistency.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Application Command Framework, Keyboard Manager,
Command Palette, Menu Bar Search, Resource Framework, Plugin Framework,
and History Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate transaction management, command routing, or resource
management functionality.

The Undo/Redo Framework shall provide the authoritative,
transaction-based mechanism for reversing and reapplying supported
operations throughout ART while maintaining consistency, accessibility,
and a professional desktop application experience.

### Part 3 – Resource Version History & Version Management

#### Overview

The Resource Version History Framework shall provide a standardized
mechanism for recording, viewing, comparing, restoring, and managing
historical versions of versionable resources throughout ART.

Version History shall allow users to review how a resource has changed
over time without permanently affecting the current version.

The Version History Framework shall extend the History Framework by
preserving meaningful snapshots of resource state rather than simply
recording individual user actions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Resource Version History Framework shall be:

- Non-destructive
- Resource-aware
- Accessible
- Version-controlled
- Local-first
- Framework-driven
- Extensible
- High-performance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The framework shall allow users to:

- Review previous versions of resources.
- Restore earlier versions.
- Compare versions.
- Recover accidentally overwritten information.
- Track resource evolution over time.
- Audit changes made to important resources.

The framework shall preserve user confidence while maintaining ART's
local-first architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Resource Types

Version history shall be supported for all versionable resources,
including:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Report Templates
- Report Attachments
- Accessibility Standards
- Project Assets
- Collections
- Saved Views
- Plugin configuration data
- Package configuration data

Future resource types shall participate automatically through the
Resource Framework where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Creation

A new version may be created when:

- A resource is created.
- A resource is modified.
- A resource is renamed.
- Resource metadata changes.
- An import updates a resource.
- A restore operation completes.
- A plugin performs a versionable operation.

The framework may intelligently consolidate multiple closely related
edits into a single version when appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Metadata

Each version shall include, at a minimum:

- Version identifier
- Resource identifier
- Version number
- Timestamp
- Operation that created the version
- User-friendly description
- Resource type
- Plugin source (if applicable)

Future metadata fields shall be supported without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Numbering

Version numbers shall be automatically managed.

Example:

``` text
Homepage Report

Version 1

Version 2

Version 3

Current Version
```

Users shall not manually assign version numbers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Browser

Selecting **Edit → History → Version History...** or the equivalent
resource context menu command shall open an accessible **Version
History** window.

Example:

``` text
Homepage Report

Current Version

Version 8

Today

Updated Executive Summary

Version 7

Yesterday

Added Screenshot

Version 6

Yesterday

Corrected WCAG References

Version 5

Last Week

Initial Draft
```

The Version History window shall support keyboard-only navigation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Viewing a Version

Users shall be able to inspect any previous version.

Viewing a historical version shall:

- Open in a read-only mode.
- Preserve the current version.
- Clearly indicate that the displayed version is historical.

Viewing shall not restore or overwrite the current version.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Restoring a Version

Users shall be able to restore any previous version.

Restoring shall:

- Create a new current version.
- Preserve all previous versions.
- Record the restore operation in the History Framework.

The restored version shall not replace historical versions.

Example:

``` text
Version 8

Current

Version 7

Version 6

Restore Version 4

↓

Version 9

(Current)

Restored from Version 4
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Retention

Application Settings shall allow users to configure version retention
policies.

Examples include:

- Keep all versions
- Keep the most recent N versions
- Retain versions for a specified time period
- Workspace-specific retention
- Resource-specific retention (future)

The framework shall automatically apply the configured policy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Read-Only Historical Versions

Historical versions shall be immutable.

Users shall not directly edit historical versions.

To modify historical content, users shall restore the desired version,
which creates a new current version.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Properties

Each version shall expose properties including:

- Version number
- Creation date
- Resource type
- Operation performed
- Description
- Resource size (where applicable)
- Plugin source (if applicable)

Properties shall integrate with ART's existing Properties dialog
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Integration

History-related version commands shall be available from the **Edit**
menu.

Examples include:

``` text
Edit

History ▶

    Version History...

    Compare Versions...

    Restore Previous Version...
```

These commands shall remain disabled when unsupported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menu Integration

Where appropriate, version-related commands shall appear within resource
context menus.

Examples include:

- Version History...
- Compare Versions...
- Restore Previous Version...

Commands shall appear only for versionable resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

The existing Command Palette shall expose version-related commands.

Examples include:

- Version History
- Compare Versions
- Restore Previous Version

Command names shall participate in normal command search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Search Integration

Menu Bar Search shall index:

- Version History
- Compare Versions
- Restore Previous Version

Users shall be able to locate these commands through the existing Menu
Bar Search feature.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may:

- Register versionable resources.
- Provide version serializers.
- Supply version descriptions.
- Participate in restore operations.

Plugins shall consume the existing Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not implement independent version history systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The framework shall:

- Store versions efficiently.
- Avoid unnecessary duplication where practical.
- Support incremental version storage.
- Scale to large resources.
- Maintain acceptable application responsiveness.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Version history shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Version metadata shall be fully programmatically exposed.

Historical status, current status, restore availability, and version
descriptions shall never rely solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Versions are created correctly.
- Version numbering is maintained correctly.
- Historical versions are read-only.
- Version History displays correctly.
- Restoring a version creates a new current version.
- Previous versions remain preserved.
- Version Properties display correctly.
- Menu Bar integration functions correctly.
- Context menu integration functions correctly.
- Command Palette integration functions correctly.
- Menu Bar Search locates version commands.
- Plugin-defined resources participate correctly.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, History Framework, Application
Command Framework, Command Palette, Menu Bar Search, Plugin Framework,
and Properties dialog functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate resource storage, version management, or history
functionality.

The Resource Version History Framework shall provide the authoritative,
centralized, and accessible mechanism for preserving, reviewing,
restoring, and managing historical versions of versionable resources
throughout ART while maintaining its framework-driven architecture and
local-first design.

### Part 4 – Change Comparison & Diff Viewer Framework

#### Overview

The Change Comparison & Diff Viewer Framework shall provide a
standardized mechanism for comparing two versions of a versionable
resource and presenting the differences in an accessible, structured,
and understandable manner.

The framework shall support semantic comparison rather than relying
solely on line-by-line textual differences.

All comparison functionality shall consume the existing Resource Version
History Framework.

The Diff Viewer shall be read-only and shall never modify either version
being compared.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Change Comparison & Diff Viewer Framework shall be:

- Read-only
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Resource-aware
- Semantic
- Framework-driven
- Extensible
- High-performance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The framework shall allow users to:

- Compare two versions of a resource.
- Understand what changed.
- Review edits before restoring a version.
- Audit modifications.
- Verify imported changes.
- Compare plugin updates.
- Compare Accessibility Standard revisions.
- Review report revisions before delivery.

The framework shall improve transparency while reducing the risk of
unintended changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Supported Resource Types

Comparison shall be supported for all versionable resources, including:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Report Templates
- Report Attachments (where comparison is meaningful)
- Accessibility Standards
- Project Assets
- Collections
- Saved Views
- Plugin configuration data
- Package configuration data

Future resource types shall integrate through the Resource Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Comparison Sources

Users shall be able to compare:

- Current version vs. previous version
- Current version vs. any historical version
- Two historical versions
- Imported version vs. existing version
- Plugin-provided version vs. installed version
- Package version vs. existing package

The framework shall determine compatibility before performing the
comparison.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Comparison Window

Comparisons shall open in a dedicated, read-only **Compare Versions**
window.

The window shall be accessible, resizable, and keyboard navigable.

Example:

``` text
Compare Versions

Homepage Report

Version 9 (Current)

↓

Version 6

----------------------------------------

Differences

• Executive Summary modified

• 3 findings added

• 1 finding removed

• Attachment updated

• WCAG reference corrected

----------------------------------------

Previous Difference

Next Difference

Export Comparison

Close
```

The window shall not allow editing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Semantic Comparison

Whenever practical, the framework shall compare resources semantically
rather than by raw text.

Examples include:

Reports

- Findings added
- Findings removed
- Severity changed
- Recommendation updated
- Status changed

Collections

- Resources added
- Resources removed

Saved Views

- Sorting changed
- Filtering changed
- Columns changed

Accessibility Standards

- Success Criterion added
- Description modified
- Reference updated

Semantic comparisons shall produce meaningful summaries for users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Change Categories

Differences shall be categorized where appropriate.

Examples include:

- Added
- Removed
- Modified
- Renamed
- Moved
- Reordered
- Metadata Changed
- Relationship Changed

Categories shall remain consistent throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Difference Navigation

The Diff Viewer shall provide commands including:

- Previous Difference
- Next Difference
- First Difference
- Last Difference

Users shall be able to navigate efficiently using both keyboard and
assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Difference Summary

The framework shall generate an accessible summary.

Example:

``` text
Comparison Summary

7 Differences Found

3 Added

2 Modified

2 Removed
```

The summary shall appear before detailed differences.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Difference Details

Each reported difference shall include:

- Resource element
- Change type
- Previous value
- Current value
- Version identifiers

Presentation shall remain consistent across resource types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filtering Differences

Users shall be able to filter displayed differences.

Examples include:

- Added only
- Removed only
- Modified only
- Metadata only
- Content only
- Relationships only

Filtering shall affect presentation only.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search

The Diff Viewer shall support searching within comparison results.

Users shall be able to locate:

- Resource names
- Findings
- Tags
- Relationships
- Accessibility Standards
- Textual changes

Search shall integrate with ART's existing search framework where
appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Export Comparison

Users shall be able to export comparison results.

Supported export formats shall consume ART's existing export
infrastructure.

Examples include:

- HTML
- PDF
- Microsoft Word
- Plain text (where appropriate)

Copilot shall not create duplicate export workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Integration

The **Edit** menu shall expose:

``` text
History ▶

    Compare Versions...
```

The command shall remain disabled when comparison is unavailable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

The existing Command Palette shall expose:

- Compare Versions

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Search Integration

Menu Bar Search shall locate:

- Compare Versions

Users shall not need to know where the command resides.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menu Integration

Versionable resources may expose:

- Compare Versions...

through existing context menus.

Commands shall appear only when supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may:

- Register comparison providers
- Provide semantic comparison logic
- Supply comparison summaries
- Extend comparison categories

Plugins shall consume the existing Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not implement independent comparison systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The framework shall:

- Compare versions efficiently.
- Scale to large reports.
- Compare incrementally where practical.
- Avoid unnecessary duplication of resource data.
- Maintain acceptable responsiveness.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Diff Viewer shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Every reported difference shall expose:

- Difference category
- Previous value
- Current value
- Position within results
- Total number of differences

Color shall never be the sole method of conveying differences.

The framework shall not rely on visual side-by-side highlighting alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Version comparisons function correctly.
- Semantic comparisons are generated where supported.
- Difference summaries are accurate.
- Difference navigation functions correctly.
- Filtering functions correctly.
- Search functions correctly.
- Export uses existing ART export infrastructure.
- Menu Bar integration functions correctly.
- Command Palette integration functions correctly.
- Menu Bar Search locates comparison commands.
- Context menus function correctly.
- Plugin comparison providers integrate correctly.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Version History Framework, Export
Framework, Application Command Framework, Command Palette, Menu Bar
Search, Plugin Framework, and Search Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate version management, export workflows, or comparison
logic.

The Change Comparison & Diff Viewer Framework shall provide the
authoritative, accessible, and semantic mechanism for comparing
historical resource versions throughout ART while preserving its
framework-driven architecture and local-first philosophy.

### Part 5 – Transaction Groups, Batch Operations & Recovery Framework

#### Overview

The Transaction Groups, Batch Operations & Recovery Framework shall
provide a standardized mechanism for grouping related operations into a
single logical transaction for history, undo, redo, recovery, and
version management.

Users shall perceive complex operations as one meaningful action rather
than a series of low-level implementation steps.

This framework shall build upon the History Framework and Undo/Redo
Framework by ensuring consistency, atomicity, and recoverability for
multi-step operations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The framework shall be:

- Transaction-based
- Atomic
- Recoverable
- Predictable
- Accessible
- Framework-driven
- Extensible
- High-performance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Purpose

The framework shall allow ART to treat multiple related operations as a
single user action.

Examples include:

- Importing an Accessibility Standard package
- Installing a plugin
- Importing a Project Workspace
- Restoring a resource version
- Duplicating a report
- Moving multiple resources
- Applying batch tag assignments
- Adding multiple resources to a collection
- Deleting multiple resources
- Bulk renaming resources

Users shall be able to undo or redo these operations with a single
command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Transaction Groups

A transaction group shall represent one logical user action, regardless
of how many internal operations are required.

Example:

``` text
Undo

Import WCAG 2.2 Accessibility Standard Package
```

instead of:

``` text
Undo Create Standard

Undo Create Success Criterion

Undo Create Technique

Undo Create Mapping

Undo Register Lookup Index

Undo Register Relationships
```

Implementation details shall remain hidden from users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Atomic Transactions

Each transaction group shall be atomic.

A transaction shall either:

- Complete successfully, or
- Roll back completely.

Partial completion shall not be permitted.

Resources shall never remain in an inconsistent state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Nested Transactions

The framework shall support nested transactions where appropriate.

Example:

``` text
Import Workspace

    Import Reports

    Import Templates

    Import Attachments

    Register Relationships
```

Nested transactions shall remain invisible to users unless diagnostic
tools explicitly expose them.

Undo and Redo shall operate on the parent transaction.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Batch Operations

Batch operations shall be treated as a single transaction whenever
initiated as one user action.

Examples include:

- Delete 25 reports
- Assign "Client Review" tag to 18 reports
- Move 12 reports into another Project Workspace
- Remove 10 attachments
- Add multiple resources to a collection

The framework shall record one history entry describing the overall
operation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recovery Framework

If a transaction cannot be completed successfully, the Recovery
Framework shall:

- Roll back completed steps where possible.
- Restore application consistency.
- Preserve resource integrity.
- Notify the user with an accessible error message.
- Record diagnostic information.

Recovery shall occur automatically whenever practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Failure Classification

Failures may be categorized for diagnostic purposes.

Examples include:

- Validation failure
- Resource conflict
- Version conflict
- Plugin failure
- Import failure
- Storage failure
- Permission failure (future)
- Unknown failure

Failure categories shall support diagnostics without exposing
unnecessary technical details to end users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recovery Notifications

Recovery notifications shall clearly communicate:

- What operation failed.
- Whether recovery succeeded.
- Whether any manual action is required.

Example:

``` text
Import Workspace

The import could not be completed.

All changes have been rolled back successfully.

No resources were modified.
```

Messages shall avoid exposing internal implementation details.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### History Integration

Completed transaction groups shall appear as single history entries.

Example:

``` text
Today

Imported Accessibility Standard Package

Assigned Client Review tag to 24 Reports

Moved 18 Reports into Sprint 5
```

History shall not display every internal operation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Undo/Redo Integration

Undo and Redo shall operate on complete transaction groups.

Users shall never be required to undo individual internal implementation
steps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version History Integration

When a transaction modifies versionable resources, Version History shall
record the resulting changes as part of the overall transaction.

The Version History Framework shall continue to determine when new
versions are created.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Progress Reporting

Long-running transactions shall provide accessible progress feedback.

Examples include:

``` text
Importing Workspace

45%

Importing Reports

Importing Attachments

Registering Relationships
```

Progress reporting shall integrate with ART's existing progress dialog
infrastructure where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Cancellation

Where practical, long-running operations shall support cancellation.

If cancellation occurs:

- Completed work shall be rolled back where possible.
- Resources shall remain consistent.
- Partial transactions shall not become permanent unless explicitly
  supported.

The framework shall determine which operations safely support
cancellation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Integration

The Transaction Framework shall not introduce new permanent menu items.

Existing history commands shall automatically operate on transaction
groups.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

The existing Command Palette shall expose transaction-aware commands
through existing history commands.

No separate transaction management commands shall be required for
ordinary users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may:

- Register transaction groups.
- Participate in transaction execution.
- Participate in rollback.
- Provide recovery handlers.
- Report transaction progress.

Plugins shall consume the existing Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not implement independent transaction managers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Diagnostics

ART's diagnostics may expose transaction information including:

- Transaction identifier
- Duration
- Completion status
- Recovery status
- Failure category
- Plugin participants

Diagnostic information shall support troubleshooting without affecting
normal application workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The framework shall:

- Execute transaction groups efficiently.
- Minimize unnecessary resource duplication.
- Support large batch operations.
- Scale to enterprise-sized workspaces.
- Maintain acceptable responsiveness.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Transaction Groups, Batch Operations & Recovery Framework shall
support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Progress indicators, recovery messages, and transaction summaries shall
be fully programmatically exposed.

Status changes shall be announced appropriately to assistive
technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Transaction groups execute correctly.
- Batch operations are grouped into single transactions.
- Atomic transactions complete or roll back successfully.
- Nested transactions function correctly.
- Recovery restores application consistency.
- Failure notifications are accurate.
- History records transaction groups correctly.
- Undo and Redo operate on transaction groups.
- Version History integrates correctly.
- Progress reporting functions correctly.
- Cancellation behaves safely.
- Plugin-defined transactions integrate correctly.
- Diagnostics report transaction information accurately.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing History Framework, Undo/Redo Framework, Resource
Version History Framework, Plugin Framework, and Progress Dialog
functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate transaction management, rollback logic, progress
reporting, or recovery mechanisms.

The Transaction Groups, Batch Operations & Recovery Framework shall
provide the authoritative mechanism for executing, recovering, and
managing complex user operations while preserving ART's
accessibility-first, framework-driven, and local-first architecture.

### Part 6 – Explorer, Dashboard, Properties & History Navigation Integration

#### Overview

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall integrate
seamlessly with the Explorer Framework, Dashboard Framework, Properties
Framework, Universal Search Framework, and Application Command
Framework.

History functionality shall be discoverable without introducing
permanent interface clutter.

The framework shall leverage existing ART navigation patterns while
preserving Explorer as the authoritative navigator for current
resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

History integration shall be:

- Discoverable
- Non-intrusive
- Accessible
- Keyboard-first
- Context-sensitive
- Framework-driven
- Consistent
- Extensible

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Integration

Explorer shall remain focused exclusively on current resources.

History records shall **not** appear as permanent Explorer nodes.

Examples of prohibited additions include:

``` text
Explorer

History

Recent Changes

Version History
```

These nodes shall **not** be added.

Explorer shall continue to represent only current resources and their
organization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Context Menus

Versionable resources may expose history-related commands through their
existing context menus.

Examples include:

``` text
Open

Rename

Properties

──────────────

Version History…

Compare Versions…

Restore Previous Version…

──────────────

Delete
```

Commands shall appear only when applicable to the selected resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Explorer Selection Synchronization

When a user selects:

- Version History…
- Compare Versions…
- Restore Previous Version…

the selected Explorer resource shall become the context for the
requested operation.

The framework shall avoid requiring duplicate resource selection.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Integration

Dashboard shall not display a permanent History panel.

Instead, Dashboard may optionally provide configurable widgets.

Examples include:

- Recent Activity
- Recently Modified Resources
- Recently Restored Resources
- Recent Imports
- Recent Plugin Activity

These widgets shall be disabled by default.

Users may enable them through Dashboard customization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Widget Behavior

Dashboard history widgets shall:

- Display concise summaries.
- Open the associated resource.
- Open Version History.
- Reveal the resource in Explorer.

Widgets shall consume the existing Dashboard Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Properties Dialog Integration

Versionable resources shall expose history-related information within
the existing Properties dialog.

Examples include:

``` text
Properties

General

History

Relationships

Attachments

Security (Future)
```

The History section may display:

- Current version
- Creation date
- Last modified date
- Number of stored versions
- Most recent modification
- Version retention policy
- Available history commands

The Properties dialog shall not duplicate the Version History window.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Navigation

History-related windows shall support direct navigation back to the
current resource.

Examples include:

- Reveal in Explorer
- Open Resource
- Open Properties

Navigation shall consume the existing Explorer Framework and Application
Command Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Window Title Integration

History-related windows shall participate in the existing Window Title
Framework.

Examples include:

``` text
Accessibility Reporting Tool

Version History

Homepage Report
```

``` text
Accessibility Reporting Tool

Compare Versions

Homepage Report
```

Window titles shall remain consistent with previously established ART
conventions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Routing

History commands shall consume the existing Application Command
Framework.

Examples include:

- Undo
- Redo
- Version History
- Compare Versions
- Restore Previous Version

Command routing shall remain centralized.

History windows shall not implement independent command dispatching.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

The existing Command Palette shall expose:

- Version History
- Compare Versions
- Restore Previous Version
- History

Commands shall automatically operate on the currently active resource
whenever appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Search Integration

Menu Bar Search shall locate:

- History
- Version History
- Compare Versions
- Restore Previous Version
- Undo
- Redo

Search shall return history commands using the same ranking behavior as
other ART commands.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Universal Search Integration

Universal Search shall continue searching current resources.

History entries shall **not** become part of ordinary Universal Search
results.

Instead, History windows shall provide their own dedicated search
capability.

This separation shall preserve search relevance while avoiding confusion
between:

- Current resources
- Historical versions

Future enterprise search extensions may optionally search historical
content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Integration

Working Views shall remain temporary report presentations.

Entering or exiting a Working View shall not automatically create
resource versions.

Only operations that modify underlying resources shall participate in
Version History.

History windows opened from within a Working View shall continue
operating on the underlying resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute:

- History context menu commands
- Dashboard history widgets
- Properties pages
- Version navigation providers
- History viewers

Plugins shall consume existing ART frameworks.

Plugins shall not introduce separate navigation systems for history.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

History navigation shall:

- Open quickly.
- Load history incrementally.
- Cache metadata where practical.
- Avoid unnecessary resource loading.
- Scale efficiently for large workspaces.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

History navigation shall support:

- Keyboard-only navigation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

All history commands shall expose:

- Accessible name
- Accessible description
- Enabled/disabled state
- Associated resource where applicable

History windows shall maintain logical heading hierarchy, predictable
focus management, and full keyboard operability.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Explorer remains free of permanent history nodes.
- Context menus expose appropriate history commands.
- Explorer selection is synchronized correctly.
- Dashboard widgets function correctly when enabled.
- Dashboard remains uncluttered by default.
- Properties dialog displays history information correctly.
- Reveal in Explorer functions correctly.
- Window titles conform to the Window Title Framework.
- Application Command Framework routes history commands correctly.
- Command Palette integration functions correctly.
- Menu Bar Search locates history commands.
- Universal Search remains limited to current resources.
- Working Views integrate correctly with history.
- Plugin contributions function correctly.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Explorer Framework, Dashboard Framework,
Properties Framework, Universal Search Framework, Application Command
Framework, Window Title Framework, Command Palette, Menu Bar Search, and
Working View Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate navigation systems, command routing, dashboard
infrastructure, or search functionality.

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall integrate
naturally with ART's existing navigation architecture while preserving a
clean, uncluttered user experience and maintaining the framework-driven
design established by previous epics.

### Part 7 – Framework API, Plugin Integration, Persistence & Lifecycle Management

#### Overview

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall expose a
centralized API for recording history, creating versions, grouping
transactions, performing undo and redo operations, restoring previous
versions, querying history, and participating in lifecycle events.

The framework shall become the single authoritative source for change
tracking throughout ART.

No ART component or plugin shall implement an independent history,
undo/redo, transaction, or versioning system.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The framework API shall be:

- Centralized
- Transaction-based
- Accessible
- Framework-driven
- Extensible
- Local-first
- Version-aware
- High-performance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Services

The History Framework shall expose centralized services including:

- History Service
- Undo/Redo Service
- Version History Service
- Transaction Service
- Recovery Service
- Comparison Service

These services shall provide a consistent programming model for all ART
frameworks and approved plugins.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### History Service

The History Service shall support operations including:

- Record History Entry
- Query History
- Retrieve History
- Clear History
- Filter History
- Search History
- Retrieve Resource History

The internal implementation may vary provided equivalent functionality
is maintained.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Undo/Redo Service

The Undo/Redo Service shall support operations including:

- Undo
- Redo
- CanUndo
- CanRedo
- Retrieve Undo Description
- Retrieve Redo Description
- Clear Redo Stack
- Retrieve Transaction Stack

Undo and Redo behavior shall remain consistent throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version History Service

The Version History Service shall support operations including:

- Create Version
- Retrieve Version
- Retrieve Version History
- Restore Version
- Delete Historical Versions (subject to retention policy)
- Compare Versions
- Retrieve Version Metadata

Version creation policies shall remain configurable through Application
Settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Transaction Service

The Transaction Service shall support operations including:

- Begin Transaction
- Commit Transaction
- Roll Back Transaction
- Create Nested Transaction
- Register Transaction Participant
- Retrieve Transaction Metadata

Only the Transaction Service shall manage transaction boundaries.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recovery Service

The Recovery Service shall support operations including:

- Register Recovery Handler
- Recover Transaction
- Report Recovery Failure
- Query Recovery Status
- Retrieve Recovery Diagnostics

Recovery logic shall remain centralized.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Comparison Service

The Comparison Service shall support operations including:

- Compare Versions
- Generate Semantic Differences
- Generate Difference Summary
- Export Comparison
- Query Comparison Results

The Diff Viewer shall consume this service.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Framework Events

The framework shall publish standardized events.

Examples include:

##### History

- History Entry Recorded
- History Cleared

##### Undo/Redo

- Undo Completed
- Redo Completed
- Undo Failed
- Redo Failed

##### Version History

- Version Created
- Version Restored
- Version Deleted
- Version Compared

##### Transactions

- Transaction Started
- Transaction Committed
- Transaction Rolled Back
- Recovery Completed

Events shall integrate with the existing Plugin Framework event model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Event Subscribers

ART frameworks and approved plugins may subscribe to history events.

Examples include:

- Explorer refresh
- Dashboard refresh
- Properties updates
- Universal Search metadata updates (where appropriate)
- Diagnostics
- Future enterprise integrations

Subscribers shall not modify framework state during event processing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Persistence

History and version metadata shall be persisted locally using ART's
existing local storage architecture.

Persistence shall preserve:

- History entries
- Undo stack (where appropriate)
- Version metadata
- Transaction metadata
- Retention settings

Persistence shall not require cloud services or user accounts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Session Management

Application Settings shall allow users to configure session behavior.

Examples include:

- Preserve history between sessions
- Clear history on exit
- Retain only current session
- Workspace-specific history

The framework shall apply the configured policy automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Lifecycle Integration

The framework shall automatically respond to resource lifecycle events
including:

- Resource created
- Resource renamed
- Resource modified
- Resource deleted
- Resource restored
- Resource imported
- Resource exported
- Plugin installed
- Plugin removed
- Package imported
- Package updated

Resource lifecycle management shall remain the responsibility of the
Resource Framework.

The History Framework shall record the resulting activity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may:

- Register versionable resources.
- Register transaction participants.
- Register comparison providers.
- Register recovery handlers.
- Publish history entries.
- Subscribe to framework events.

Plugins shall consume the existing Plugin Framework.

Plugins shall not create independent history or versioning
implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Version Compatibility

Plugins participating in the History Framework shall declare
compatibility with:

- ART version
- Resource Framework version
- Plugin Framework version
- History Framework version

The Plugin Framework shall prevent incompatible plugins from
participating.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Diagnostics

The framework shall expose diagnostic information including:

- History statistics
- Version statistics
- Undo stack state
- Redo stack state
- Transaction statistics
- Recovery statistics
- Plugin participants
- Event subscribers
- Retention policy status

Diagnostics shall integrate with ART's existing diagnostics
infrastructure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance Requirements

The framework shall:

- Record history incrementally.
- Cache metadata where practical.
- Minimize unnecessary serialization.
- Support large workspaces.
- Scale efficiently to thousands of history entries.
- Maintain acceptable application responsiveness.

Performance optimizations shall remain internal to the framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

Framework APIs shall expose sufficient semantic information for
accessible user interface presentation.

Accessible metadata shall include:

- Operation description
- Resource name
- Timestamp
- Transaction description
- Version description
- Recovery status
- Comparison availability

Accessibility information shall remain centralized within ART's
Accessibility Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- History services function correctly.
- Undo/Redo services function correctly.
- Version History services function correctly.
- Transaction services function correctly.
- Recovery services function correctly.
- Comparison services function correctly.
- Framework events are published correctly.
- Event subscribers function correctly.
- Persistence functions correctly.
- Session policies function correctly.
- Lifecycle integration functions correctly.
- Plugin integration functions correctly.
- Diagnostics report accurate information.
- Performance remains acceptable.
- Accessibility requirements are satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this part.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Resource Framework, Plugin Framework, Diagnostics
Framework, Local Storage Framework, Application Settings Framework, and
Accessibility Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate persistence, event management, lifecycle management,
transaction management, or diagnostics functionality.

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall provide the
single authoritative API for recording, managing, restoring, and
querying resource history throughout ART while supporting future
expansion through standardized services, providers, and framework
extension points.

### Part 8 – Final Validation, Acceptance Criteria, Documentation & Completion Requirements

#### Overview

This part defines the final acceptance criteria for the History,
Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework and establishes the
architectural principles that shall govern change tracking, version
management, and recovery throughout ART.

Upon completion of this epic, the History Framework shall become the
authoritative mechanism for recording and managing user actions,
resource versions, transaction groups, and recovery operations.

Future ART features shall consume this framework rather than
implementing independent history, undo/redo, or versioning systems.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Design Goals

The completed framework shall be:

- Accessible
- Consistent
- Extensible
- Framework-driven
- High-performance
- Local-first
- Maintainable
- Recoverable
- Predictable
- Future-ready

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Architectural Principles

The framework shall adhere to the following principles.

#### Single Source of Truth

History, Undo/Redo, Version History, Transaction Management, Recovery,
and Version Comparison shall each have a single authoritative
implementation.

Explorer, Dashboard, Resource Framework, Working Views, Plugins,
Packages, and future ART components shall consume these services rather
than implementing independent solutions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Separation of Responsibilities

The framework shall preserve clear responsibilities throughout ART.

### Resource Framework

Owns resources.

### History Framework

Records operations performed on resources.

### Version History Framework

Maintains historical versions of versionable resources.

### Undo/Redo Framework

Reverses or reapplies completed transactions.

### Transaction Framework

Groups related operations into atomic units.

### Recovery Framework

Restores application consistency after failed transactions.

### Comparison Framework

Generates semantic differences between resource versions.

No framework shall assume responsibilities assigned to another
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Local-First Architecture

All history information shall remain local unless the user explicitly
exports data through existing ART export workflows or a future plugin
provides synchronization.

The framework shall not require:

- Cloud services
- Internet connectivity
- User accounts
- Remote databases

for normal operation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Non-Destructive Design

History shall never overwrite existing resources.

Restoring a version shall create a new current version.

Comparisons shall remain read-only.

Undo operations shall preserve application consistency.

Historical versions shall remain immutable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility-First Design

Every history feature shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Accessibility shall never rely solely on color, animation, or visual
comparison.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Documentation Requirements

Copilot shall update all relevant ART documentation to describe the
completed History Framework.

Documentation shall include:

- Framework overview
- History
- Undo/Redo
- Version History
- Version Comparison
- Transaction Groups
- Recovery
- Explorer integration
- Dashboard integration
- Plugin integration
- Lifecycle integration
- Framework APIs

Documentation shall remain consistent with previous framework epics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### User Guide Updates

The User Guide shall include instructions describing:

## History

- Viewing history
- Searching history
- Filtering history
- Clearing history

### Undo and Redo

- Using Undo
- Using Redo
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Transaction behavior

### Version History

- Viewing previous versions
- Restoring versions
- Understanding version numbers
- Version retention

### Compare Versions

- Opening comparisons
- Understanding semantic differences
- Navigating differences
- Exporting comparison results

Examples shall illustrate common workflows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Developer Documentation

Developer documentation shall include:

- Framework architecture
- Framework services
- Transaction model
- Recovery model
- Version providers
- Comparison providers
- Plugin integration
- Event model
- Accessibility guidance
- Performance recommendations
- Sample implementations
- Best practices

Documentation shall emphasize reuse of existing ART frameworks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Source Code Requirements

Copilot shall:

- Eliminate duplicate history logic.
- Eliminate duplicate versioning logic.
- Eliminate duplicate undo/redo implementations.
- Eliminate duplicate comparison logic.
- Eliminate duplicate recovery logic.
- Maintain consistent naming conventions.
- Preserve backward compatibility where practical.
- Centralize all history-related behavior.

No independent history or versioning systems shall remain elsewhere
within ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Regression Testing

Before completion, Copilot shall verify that no regressions have been
introduced affecting:

- Resource Framework
- Resource Relationship Framework
- Explorer Framework
- Dashboard Framework
- Working Views Framework
- Universal Search Framework
- Properties Framework
- Plugin Framework
- Package Framework
- Accessibility Standards
- Report Viewer
- Report Builder
- Templates
- Report Attachments
- Collections
- Saved Views
- Existing import workflows
- Existing export workflows
- Existing keyboard navigation
- Existing context menus
- Existing accessibility functionality

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Acceptance Criteria

The History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall be
considered complete when:

- History entries are recorded correctly.
- Undo functions correctly.
- Redo functions correctly.
- Transaction groups behave atomically.
- Recovery preserves application consistency.
- Version History records meaningful resource versions.
- Historical versions remain immutable.
- Version restoration creates new current versions.
- Semantic version comparisons function correctly.
- Explorer integration functions correctly.
- Dashboard integration functions correctly.
- Properties integration functions correctly.
- Command Palette integration functions correctly.
- Menu Bar Search locates all history-related commands.
- Plugin integration functions correctly.
- Documentation is complete.
- Accessibility requirements are fully satisfied.
- Existing ART functionality continues to operate without regression.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Future Extensibility

The framework shall support future enhancements without architectural
redesign, including:

- Named restore points
- Automatic checkpoint versions
- Scheduled snapshots
- Cross-workspace comparison
- Selective transaction rollback
- Collaborative version history (future)
- Digital signatures for version verification
- Enterprise audit history
- Cloud synchronization through optional plugins
- AI-assisted change summaries
- AI-assisted version comparison explanations

These capabilities shall extend the framework rather than replacing it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Final Verification

Verify that:

- All parts of this epic have been implemented.
- Every versionable resource participates correctly.
- Undo and Redo remain consistent throughout ART.
- Transaction groups execute atomically.
- Recovery preserves application stability.
- Version History remains accurate.
- Version Comparison produces meaningful semantic results.
- History integrates correctly with Explorer, Dashboard, Properties,
  Command Palette, and Menu Bar Search.
- Plugin contributions function correctly.
- Documentation is complete.
- Accessibility requirements are fully satisfied.
- No duplicate history, undo/redo, recovery, or versioning systems have
  been introduced.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described within this epic.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing ART functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not introduce duplicate implementations for history recording,
version management, undo/redo, transaction grouping, recovery,
comparison, persistence, or navigation.

The completed History, Undo/Redo & Resource Versioning Framework shall
provide the single authoritative, accessible, extensible, and
maintainable foundation for tracking, managing, comparing, restoring,
and recovering changes throughout ART while preserving the clean,
professional desktop application architecture established by previous
epics.

## Focus & Keyboard Accessibility Improvements

#### Overview

Investigate and correct the focus management issues described below.

These issues all relate to preserving the user's logical keyboard
workflow after commands are executed or dialogs are closed.

Implement a consistent focus restoration strategy throughout ART rather
than creating individual, one-off solutions for each issue.

Consume existing focus management, keyboard navigation, modal dialog,
and menu frameworks whenever possible.

Do not introduce duplicate focus restoration logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

The application shall:

- Preserve logical keyboard workflow.
- Preserve predictable focus movement.
- Preserve screen reader usability.
- Never move keyboard focus to the top of the page unless explicitly
  required.
- Restore focus to the invoking control whenever appropriate.
- Maintain existing keyboard shortcuts.
- Maintain existing menu behavior.
- Maintain existing modal dialog behavior.
- Preserve all existing functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 1 – Menu Bar Escape Key Focus Restoration

#### Current Behavior

While interacting with the Menu Bar or one of its menus using the
keyboard, pressing **Escape** exits the menu system but incorrectly
moves keyboard focus to the top of the page.

This disrupts keyboard and screen reader workflows.

#### Required Fix

When the user presses **Escape** while interacting with the Menu Bar or
an open menu:

- Close the active menu.
- Exit direct interaction with the Menu Bar.
- Restore focus to the Menu Bar item that had focus immediately before
  direct menu interaction began.
- Do not move focus to the document root or top of the page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 2 – Report Builder Add Field Focus Restoration

#### Current Behavior

Within the **Report Builder → Report Fields** section, invoking **Add
Field** (regardless of how the command is invoked) successfully creates
a new field but incorrectly moves keyboard focus to the top of the page.

#### Required Fix

After a field is successfully added:

- Move keyboard focus directly to the empty **Field Name** textbox for
  the newly created field.
- Ensure this behavior is identical regardless of whether Add Field is
  invoked using:
  - Mouse
  - Keyboard shortcut
  - Context menu
  - Toolbar
  - Command Palette
  - Any future command routing

The Add Field command shall expose a single implementation that performs
all field creation and focus restoration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 3 – Move Up / Move Down Focus Preservation

#### Current Behavior

Within the **Report Builder → Report Fields** section:

Activating either:

- Move Up
- Move Down

successfully reorders the field but incorrectly moves keyboard focus to
the top of the page.

#### Required Fix

After either command completes:

- Focus shall remain on the same Move Up or Move Down button that
  initiated the action.
- Keyboard users shall be able to continue reordering fields without
  manually relocating focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 4 – User Guide Focus Restoration

#### Current Behavior

When the **Help/User Guide** is opened, closing it using either:

- the Close button, or
- the Escape key

does not consistently restore focus to the control that originally
opened the User Guide.

#### Required Fix

Whenever the User Guide is closed:

- Restore keyboard focus to the control that opened the User Guide.
- Preserve the user's original workflow.
- Do not move focus elsewhere.
- Continue supporting both Close button and Escape key.

This behavior shall consume the existing modal dialog framework rather
than introducing separate focus restoration logic.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Requirements

All fixes shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Focus changes shall be programmatically determinable and predictable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Escape restores Menu Bar focus correctly.
- Add Field moves focus to the new Field Name textbox.
- Move Up preserves focus.
- Move Down preserves focus.
- Closing the User Guide restores focus to the invoking control.
- Existing keyboard shortcuts continue functioning.
- Existing menu behavior remains unchanged.
- Existing modal dialog behavior remains unchanged.
- Screen readers correctly announce the focused controls.
- No regressions have been introduced elsewhere in ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described above.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Menu Bar, Keyboard Navigation, Command Routing,
Modal Dialog, and Focus Management functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate focus restoration logic.

The completed implementation shall provide a consistent, accessible, and
predictable focus management experience throughout ART.

``` text
2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA)

3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (Level AA)
```

Continue sorting by Success Criterion number.

Continue using the existing Accessibility Standards Framework.

Do not duplicate WCAG metadata.

#### Accessibility Requirements

The complete displayed value shall also be exposed to assistive
technologies.

Users shall be able to distinguish Success Criteria sharing similar

- Criterion number
- Criterion title
- Conformance level

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

## Epic 38 Dashboard Analytics Framework

#### Overview

Implement a reusable **Analytics Framework** for ART by expanding the
existing **Analytics** tab within the Dashboard.

The Analytics Framework shall provide dynamic accessibility analytics
for the currently active Project Workspace and Working View.

Do **not** create separate Workspace Statistics or Report Statistics
dialogs.

Instead, utilize and expand the existing **Dashboard → Analytics** tab
to present all analytics.

The Analytics Framework shall serve as the authoritative mechanism for
presenting accessibility metrics, summaries, trends, and future
analytics throughout ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

The implementation shall:

- Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.
- Avoid duplicate statistics calculations.
- Generate analytics dynamically.
- Remain fully accessible.
- Support future expansion.
- Preserve all existing Dashboard functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Integration

Continue using the existing **Analytics** tab on the Dashboard.

Do not create additional Dashboard tabs.

The Analytics tab shall automatically adapt to the current application
context.

Examples include:

#### No Project Workspace Open

Display an informative empty state.

Example:

> No Project Workspace is currently open.
>
> Open or create a Project Workspace to begin viewing accessibility
> analytics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Project Workspace Open

Display analytics aggregated across every report contained within the
active Project Workspace.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Active

Display analytics for:

- Current Report
- Entire Project Workspace

Provide an accessible mechanism allowing users to switch between these
views without leaving the Analytics tab.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Sections

Organize the Analytics tab into collapsible accordion sections.

Each section shall:

- Be collapsed by default.
- Support keyboard navigation.
- Support Enter and Space to expand or collapse.
- Expose expanded/collapsed state programmatically.
- Preserve state while the Analytics tab remains open.
- Minimize visual clutter.

Example:

``` text
▶ Coverage

▶ Findings Summary

▶ Severity Breakdown

▶ Accessibility Standards

▶ Issue Types

▶ Page / Screen / Component Analysis

▶ Trends

▶ Charts

▶ Custom Analytics
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Coverage

Display coverage information including, where applicable:

- Number of Pages Tested
- Number of Screens Tested
- Number of Components Tested

Future coverage metrics shall integrate automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Findings Summary

Display:

- Total Findings
- Passed Findings *(only when the selected report(s) contain Passed
  findings)*
- Failed Findings *(only when the selected report(s) contain Failed
  findings)*
- Manual Review Findings *(only when the selected report(s) contain
  Manual Review findings)*
- Not Tested Findings *(only when the selected report(s) contain Not
  Tested findings)*

The framework shall not assume these finding categories exist.

Unavailable metrics shall be omitted automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Severity Breakdown

Display findings grouped by the report's configured severity values.

Examples:

- Critical
- Serious
- Moderate
- Minor
- Informational

Severity values shall be generated dynamically from the report
configuration rather than being hardcoded.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Standards

Display findings grouped by:

- Accessibility Standard
- Conformance Level (when applicable)

Examples:

WCAG 2.2

- Level A
- Level AA
- Level AAA

Future accessibility standards (including optional packages such as
Section 508, EN 301 549, and the European Accessibility Act) shall
automatically participate without modifying the Analytics Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Issue Types

Display:

- Number of Findings by Issue Type
- Most Frequent Issue Types

Issue Type refers to the individual test criterion defined within an
Accessibility Standard.

Examples include:

- Missing Alternative Text
- Color Contrast
- Missing Form Labels
- Keyboard Accessibility
- Focus Indicators
- Duplicate IDs

Issue Types shall be generated dynamically from installed Accessibility
Standards.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Page / Screen / Component Analysis

Display:

- Number of Findings by Page
- Number of Findings by Screen
- Number of Findings by Component

Additionally display:

- Most Frequent Issue Types by Page
- Most Frequent Issue Types by Screen
- Most Frequent Issue Types by Component

Example:

Homepage

- Missing Alternative Text (14)
- Color Contrast (9)

Checkout Page

- Missing Labels (8)
- Keyboard Trap (3)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Trends

The framework shall provide a Trends section for future expansion.

Initial implementations may include:

- Findings by Report
- Findings by Accessibility Standard
- Findings by Severity
- Findings by Date

The architecture shall support future analytics without redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Charts

The Analytics Framework shall support future accessible visualizations.

Examples include:

- Bar Charts
- Pie Charts
- Line Charts
- Trend Charts

Every visual chart shall always provide:

- Accessible textual summary
- Accessible data table
- Keyboard accessibility
- Screen reader accessibility

Charts shall never be the sole presentation of information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dynamic Analytics

Analytics shall be generated dynamically from the fields and data
present within the selected report(s).

The framework shall **not** assume that any specific report field
exists.

Analytics that cannot be computed because the necessary fields are
unavailable shall automatically be omitted.

This shall allow custom report templates to participate without
modifying the Analytics Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Settings

Add a new **Analytics** page to Application Settings.

Allow users to configure:

#### Default Expanded Sections

Users may choose which accordion sections are expanded by default.

Examples:

- Coverage
- Findings Summary
- Severity Breakdown
- Accessibility Standards
- Issue Types
- Page Analysis
- Trends
- Charts

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Display Options

Allow users to configure:

- Hide unavailable analytics
- Show percentages
- Show totals
- Show charts
- Show data tables
- Expand all sections by default
- Restore previous Analytics layout

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Options

Allow users to configure:

- Always display textual summaries
- Prefer tables over charts
- Announce updated analytics automatically
- Reduce animations

These settings shall integrate with existing Accessibility Settings
where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Customize Analytics

Within the Analytics tab, provide a command:

``` text
Customize Analytics…
```

Selecting this command shall open the Analytics page within Application
Settings.

This command shall provide convenient access to Analytics preferences
without duplicating settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Plugin Integration

Plugins may contribute additional Analytics sections.

Examples include:

- WCAG Analytics
- Section 508 Analytics
- EN 301 549 Analytics
- European Accessibility Act Analytics
- Usability Analytics
- AI Recommendations

Plugins shall register analytics through the existing Plugin Framework.

The Analytics Framework shall not require modification to support
plugin-provided analytics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance

Analytics shall:

- Consume existing ART framework data.
- Avoid duplicate calculations.
- Cache reusable calculations where appropriate.
- Refresh automatically after report changes.
- Scale efficiently for large Project Workspaces.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The Analytics Framework shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Accordion controls shall expose expanded and collapsed states
programmatically.

Analytics shall be fully navigable using headings and landmarks.

Charts shall always provide accessible textual alternatives.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Analytics appear within the existing Dashboard Analytics tab.
- Analytics adapt correctly to the current context.
- Workspace analytics aggregate correctly.
- Report analytics summarize correctly.
- Accordion sections operate correctly.
- Analytics update automatically after report changes.
- Application Settings correctly configure Analytics behavior.
- Customize Analytics opens the appropriate settings page.
- Plugin-provided analytics integrate correctly.
- Keyboard accessibility remains fully functional.
- Screen readers announce analytics correctly.
- Existing Dashboard functionality remains unchanged.
- No regressions have been introduced elsewhere in ART.
