#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described above.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Dashboard, Resource Framework, Working View
Framework, Accessibility Standards Framework, Plugin Framework,
Application Settings Framework, and Accessibility Framework
functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate analytics calculations or maintain independent
statistical data.

The completed Analytics Framework shall provide the single
authoritative, accessible, extensible, and future-ready mechanism for
presenting accessibility analytics throughout ART while preserving the
clean, framework-driven architecture established by previous epics.

### Accessibility Lookup Tool & Smart Data Entry Improvements

#### Overview

Implement the Accessibility Lookup Tool and Smart Data Entry
improvements described below.

These enhancements shall improve accessibility, reduce repetitive data
entry, and increase report authoring efficiency while preserving ART's
accessibility-first architecture.

Implement only the functionality described within this prompt.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

The implementation shall:

- Preserve existing Report Builder functionality.
- Preserve existing Report Editor functionality.
- Preserve existing Accessibility Lookup Tool functionality.
- Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.
- Remain fully accessible.
- Avoid introducing duplicate implementations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 1 – Accessibility Lookup Tool Accessible Name

#### Current Behavior

When the Accessibility Lookup Tool search field receives focus, JAWS
currently announces:

> Search and filter criteria **Control**. Shortcut: Alt+Shift+L.

The additional word **"Control"** is unnecessary and results in an
inconsistent user experience.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Required Fix

Update the accessible name of the search field so that assistive
technologies announce:

> Search and filter criteria. Shortcut: Alt+Shift+L.

#### Requirements

- Remove the unnecessary word **"Control"**.
- Preserve the existing keyboard shortcut announcement.
- Preserve all existing search functionality.
- Preserve all existing keyboard shortcuts.
- Preserve all existing labels and visible text.
- Continue exposing the correct programmatic name.

The implementation shall improve only the accessible name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 2 – Smart Data Entry (Autocomplete)

#### Overview

Implement an accessible autocomplete system within the Report Editor to
reduce repetitive typing while preserving complete keyboard
accessibility.

The autocomplete system shall allow users to efficiently reuse
previously entered values while remaining unobtrusive and never
interrupting the user's typing workflow.

The implementation shall serve as the foundation for future Smart Data
Entry capabilities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Scope

The initial implementation shall operate only within the currently open
report.

Do **not** search:

- Other reports
- Report templates
- Project Workspaces
- Imported reports
- External data sources

Future versions may expand the available data sources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Matching Rules

Autocomplete suggestions shall be generated only from values previously
entered into the **same report field**.

Example:

If previous rows contain:

``` text
Missing Alternative Text

Missing Form Label

Keyboard Trap
```

Typing:

``` text
Mis
```

shall generate:

``` text
Missing Alternative Text

Missing Form Label
```

Typing:

``` text
Key
```

shall generate:

``` text
Keyboard Trap
```

Values from different report fields shall never be suggested.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Suggestion Behavior

Suggestions shall:

- Match typed prefixes.
- Ignore letter case.
- Remove duplicate values.
- Prefer the most recently used matching value.
- Update automatically while the user types.
- Never interrupt typing.
- Never steal keyboard focus.
- Never require the user to stop typing.

Suggestions shall disappear automatically when:

- No matching suggestions remain.
- The text field loses focus.
- The suggestion list is dismissed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Interaction

Autocomplete shall support efficient keyboard-only operation while
preserving uninterrupted text entry.

##### While Typing

As the user types:

- Suggestions shall be generated automatically.
- Suggestions shall update automatically.
- Suggestions shall update silently.
- Keyboard focus shall remain within the text field.
- The suggestion list shall remain hidden until explicitly requested by
  the user.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Opening Suggestions

Users may display available suggestions by pressing either:

- Down Arrow
- Alt+Down Arrow

When the suggestion list opens:

- Keyboard focus shall move to the first suggestion.
- The suggestion list shall become fully keyboard accessible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Navigating Suggestions

Users shall be able to navigate suggestions using:

- Down Arrow
- Up Arrow
- Home
- End

Keyboard focus shall move normally through the suggestion list.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Accepting Suggestions

Pressing **Enter** on the currently focused suggestion shall:

- Insert the selected suggestion into the text field at the user's
  current insertion point.
- Return keyboard focus to the text field.
- Position the text insertion point immediately after the inserted
  suggestion.
- Allow the user to immediately continue typing.

Suggestions shall remain completely editable after insertion.

Autocomplete shall never lock or protect inserted content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Dismissing Suggestions

Pressing **Escape** shall:

- Close the suggestion list.
- Return focus to the text field.
- Preserve the user's existing text.
- Make no modifications to the report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Behavior

Autocomplete shall be designed to minimize interruptions while users are
typing.

##### Suggestion Availability

When suggestions first become available during a typing sequence:

Screen readers shall announce:

> Suggestions available.

This announcement shall occur **only once** while the user continues
typing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Silent Updates

As suggestions continue changing while the user types:

Screen readers shall **not** repeatedly announce:

- Updated suggestions
- New suggestions
- Removed suggestions
- Suggestion counts

Suggestions shall update automatically and quietly.

Users shall remain free to continue typing without interruption.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Reviewing Suggestions

When the user explicitly opens the suggestion list:

- Keyboard focus shall move to the first suggestion.
- Each suggestion shall receive programmatic keyboard focus.
- Screen readers shall announce the complete text of each suggestion as
  it receives focus.
- Users shall review suggestions using normal keyboard navigation.

No hidden or inaccessible suggestions shall exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Accepting Suggestions

After the user presses **Enter** on a suggestion:

- The selected suggestion shall be inserted into the text field.
- Focus shall immediately return to the text field.
- The insertion point shall be positioned at the end of the inserted
  suggestion.
- Users shall immediately be able to continue typing or edit the
  inserted text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Requirements

Autocomplete shall fully support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

The implementation shall prioritize uninterrupted typing while ensuring
every suggestion remains fully accessible once the user chooses to
review available suggestions.

The suggestion list shall expose appropriate accessibility roles,
states, and relationships consistent with WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance

Autocomplete shall:

- Operate efficiently on large reports.
- Search only the active report field.
- Avoid duplicate calculations.
- Update suggestions immediately while typing.
- Remain responsive even in large reports.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Future Extensibility

Architect the autocomplete implementation to support future enhancements
without redesign.

Future capabilities may include:

- Cross-report suggestions
- Report template suggestions
- Workspace-wide suggestions
- Frequently used phrases
- Favorite phrases
- Phrase expansion
- AI-assisted suggestions
- Plugin-provided suggestion providers
- Organization-wide suggestion providers

The initial implementation shall **not** implement these features but
shall allow them to integrate naturally in the future.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

#### Accessibility Lookup Tool

- The corrected accessible name is announced.
- Existing search functionality remains unchanged.
- Existing keyboard shortcuts remain unchanged.

#### Smart Data Entry

- Suggestions are generated correctly.
- Suggestions are limited to the same report field.
- Suggestions update automatically while typing.
- Suggestions remain hidden until requested.
- "Suggestions available." is announced only once during a typing
  sequence.
- Suggestions update silently thereafter.
- Suggestions become fully accessible once opened.
- Every suggestion is announced correctly when it receives keyboard
  focus.
- Enter inserts the selected suggestion correctly.
- Focus returns to the text field.
- The insertion point is positioned at the end of the inserted
  suggestion.
- Users can immediately continue typing.
- Escape dismisses the suggestion list without modifying the field.
- Existing Report Editor functionality remains unchanged.
- No regressions have been introduced elsewhere in ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described above.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

Preserve all existing Accessibility Lookup Tool, Report Builder, Report
Editor, Keyboard Navigation, Accessibility Framework, Application
Command Framework, and Report Framework functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate search logic or introduce independent autocomplete
systems.

The completed implementation shall improve both accessibility and report
authoring efficiency while preserving ART's framework-driven,
accessibility-first architecture and providing the foundation for future
Smart Data Entry enhancements.

#### Report Branding Improvements

#### Overview

Improve the Report Branding functionality within the Report Builder to
support rich, professional report branding while preserving
accessibility and existing report generation behavior.

The implementation shall enhance report branding without introducing a
separate report designer.

Implement only the functionality described within this prompt.

Do not modify unrelated application behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

The implementation shall:

- Preserve existing report templates.
- Preserve existing export formats.
- Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.
- Remain fully accessible.
- Maintain compatibility with all supported export formats.
- Preserve existing accessibility semantics throughout the report
  generation pipeline.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Unless otherwise specified, the requirements in this document apply to:

- Report previews

Requirements that are explicitly identified as applying only to Project

### Issue 1 – Rich Report Header

#### Overview

Replace the existing plain-text report header implementation with a rich
content editor.

The header editor shall support creating, editing, and pasting rich
content, including one or more images, while preserving formatting,
document structure, and accessibility information.---

#### Supported Content

Users shall be able to paste content from:

- Microsoft Word
- Microsoft Outlook
- Google Docs
- Web browsers
- Markdown-rendered documents
- Existing ART reports
- Other rich text editors

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Preserve

Where supported, preserve:

- Paragraphs

- Tables
- Hyperlinks
- Images
- Bold
- Italics
- Underline
- Font family
- Font size
- Text color
- Background color

- Indentation
- Accessible semantics

### Issue 2 – Rich Report Footer

Provide identical functionality for report footers.

Headers and footers shall consume the same editor implementation.

### Issue 3 – Accessible Rich Content

Headers and footers shall preserve accessibility semantics.

This includes, where applicable:

- Heading hierarchy
- Alternative text
- Accessible hyperlinks
- Lists
- Tables
- Reading order
- Language attributes
- Semantic HTML

Generated reports shall preserve these semantics whenever supported by

### Issue 4 – Branding Preview

Provide a live preview showing how the current branding will appear in
generated reports.

The Branding Preview shall function identically for both standalone
reports and reports contained within Project Workspaces.

The preview shall:

- Update automatically as branding changes.
- Reflect page margins.
- Display headers.
- Display footers.
- Display images.
- Display page numbering where applicable.
- Preserve the same visual layout that will appear in generated reports.

The preview shall supplement—not replace—the existing report preview
functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 5 – Header and Footer Image Management

Allow users to insert, manage, and arrange one or more images within
report headers and footers. Images may be used for purposes including,
but not limited to: - Organization logos - Client logos - Certification
badges - Partner logos - Program icons - Decorative graphics - Other
branding elements

Image management shall function identically for standalone reports and
reports contained within Project Workspaces.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Image Management Users shall be able to: - Insert one or more images. - Replace individual images. - Remove individual images. - Reorder images. - Resize images. - Specify image alignment. - Specify image spacing. - Preserve image aspect ratio. - Specify maximum display size. The Report Branding editor shall support any reasonable number of images that can be accommodated within the available header or footer layout. Supported image formats shall include:

- PNG
- JPG
- SVG (where supported)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Image Layout

Images shall participate naturally within the rich content editor. Users
shall be able to position images: - Before text - After text - Between
paragraphs - Within tables (where supported) - Inline with text (where
supported) Images shall preserve the surrounding document structure and
accessibility semantics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Image Ordering

Users shall be able to reorder images using both mouse and keyboard.
\### Mouse Users shall be able to drag and drop images to a new location
within the header or footer. Visual drop indicators shall clearly
identify the destination before the image is moved.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard

Provide keyboard-accessible image reordering. Users shall be able to
move the currently selected image:

- Earlier within the content

- Later within the content Keyboard reordering shall:

- Preserve keyboard focus.

- Announce successful movement.

- Update the preview automatically.

- Preserve accessibility semantics.

Do not rely solely on drag-and-drop.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Required Alternative Text

Every image inserted into a report header or footer shall require
alternative text. Provide a required **Alternative Text** field for each
image. The Alternative Text field shall:

- Be required before the report, report template, or branding
  configuration can be saved.
- Clearly indicate that it provides the image's alternative text.
- Support editing at any time.
- Preserve the entered value whenever the image is copied, imported,
  exported, inherited, or reused. The value entered into

the Alternative Text field shall become the image's accessible
alternative text throughout ART. Specifically, the value shall be used
as the image's **`alt`** attribute (or the equivalent accessibility
property required by the destination format) in:

- Header previews
- Footer previews
- Saved reports
- Report templates
- Saved branding configurations
- Workspace branding
- HTML exports
- Microsoft Word (.docx) exports
- PDF exports (where supported by the export technology)
- Any other report formats generated by ART that support image
  alternative text

Alternative text shall remain synchronized with its associated image
throughout the image's lifecycle. If an image is replaced, the existing
Alternative Text shall remain editable and may be updated before saving.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The image management interface shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Windows Voice Access
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking
- Apple Voice Control
- Speech dictation
- Switch devices
- Eye tracking

Alternative Text fields shall expose:

- Accessible labels
- Required\
  -field indicators
- Validation messages
- Appropriate programmatic relationships

Users shall not be permitted to save a report, report template, or
branding configuration containing an image that does not have
Alternative Text. Image reordering shall be fully operable without
requiring a mouse. All drag-and-drop functionality shall have an
equivalent keyboard-accessible method.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Multiple images may be inserted into headers and footers.
- Images may be reordered using both mouse and keyboard.
- Drag-and-drop preserves accessibility.
- Keyboard reordering preserves keyboard focus.
- Every image requires Alternative Text.
- Alternative Text is correctly propagated to previews, reports,
  templates, workspace branding, and exports.
- Image layout is preserved across all supported report formats.
- Existing report generation remains unchanged.
- No regressions have been introduced elsewhere in ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Issue 6 – Project Workspace Only: Workspace Branding Inheritance

#### Applicability

This issue applies only to reports that belong to a Project Workspace.

Standalone reports shall not display the workspace branding option and
shall not participate in workspace branding inheritance.

Allow Active Project Workspaces to maintain a default branding
configuration that is automatically applied to newly created reports.

When editing branding for a report that belongs to a Active Project
Workspace, provide the following option immediately below the Report
Branding editor:

``` text
☐ Make this the default branding for new reports in this Active Project Workspace.
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Behavior

When the checkbox is selected and the report is saved:

- The current report's complete branding configuration shall become the
  default branding configuration for the active Active Project
  Workspace.
- Existing reports within the Active Project Workspace shall remain
  unchanged.
- Newly created reports within the Active Project Workspace shall
  automatically inherit the workspace's default branding.

When the checkbox is not selected:

- The current report shall continue using its own branding.
- The Active Project Workspace's default branding shall remain
  unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Workspace Branding

The Active Project Workspace's default branding shall include all
branding information, including but not limited to:

- Header
- Footer
- Images
- Alternative Text for every image
- Fonts
- Colors
- Branding layout
- Branding metadata
- Future branding properties

Future branding properties shall automatically participate in workspace
branding inheritance without requiring modifications to the inheritance
framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Existing Reports

Changing the Active Project Workspace's default branding shall **not**
automatically modify branding in existing reports.

Existing reports shall retain their current branding unless the user
explicitly chooses to replace it with the current Active Project
Workspace branding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### New Reports

Whenever a new report is created within the Active Project Workspace:

- The Active Project Workspace's default branding shall automatically be
  copied into the new report.
- The copied branding shall become part of the report.
- Users may customize the report's branding independently.
- Subsequent modifications to the report's branding shall not modify the
  Active Project Workspace's default branding unless the user explicitly
  selects:

``` text
☐ Make this the default branding for new reports in this Active Project Workspace.
```

again and saves the report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility

The checkbox shall:

- Be fully keyboard accessible.
- Have an accessible programmatic label matching its visible text.
- Expose its checked state programmatically.
- Be correctly announced by assistive technologies.
- Participate in the normal keyboard tab order.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Selecting the checkbox updates the Active Project Workspace's default
  branding.
- Existing reports remain unchanged.
- Newly created reports inherit the Active Project Workspace's default
  branding.
- Individual reports may override inherited branding.
- Alternative Text for images is preserved throughout the inheritance

## Epic 39 – Collaboration Framework

### Part 1 – Collaboration Architecture and Resource Ownership

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Overview

Implement the foundational Collaboration Framework for ART.

The Collaboration Framework shall enable users to work independently or
collaboratively while preserving ART's local-first philosophy.

The framework shall support collaboration across Project Workspaces,
Reports, and other collaborative resources without requiring
architectural redesign as future collaboration capabilities are
introduced.

The initial implementation is **not** required to support simultaneous
character-level collaborative editing.

Instead, the framework shall establish the architecture necessary to
support future real-time collaboration similar to applications such as
Google Docs and Google Sheets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Design Goals

The Collaboration Framework shall:

- Preserve ART's local-first architecture.
- Operate without requiring an Internet connection.
- Support future cloud-based collaboration.
- Support future enterprise deployments.
- Support future real-time collaboration.
- Support future synchronization providers.
- Support future collaboration providers.
- Remain storage independent.
- Remain transport independent.
- Remain authentication independent.
- Remain extensible through ART's existing framework architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration Modes

The Collaboration Framework shall support multiple collaboration modes.

These include:

- Independent work
- Shared Project Workspaces
- Asynchronous collaboration
- Synchronous collaboration (future)
- Real-time collaborative editing (future)

The initial implementation shall fully support independent work and
asynchronous collaboration.

The architecture shall support future synchronous collaboration without
requiring redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Ownership Model

Every user-created resource within ART shall support ownership.

Ownership shall be independent of storage location.

Each resource shall have:

- Owner
- Visibility
- Permission assignments
- Sharing information
- Audit history

Ownership shall remain associated with the resource regardless of
whether it is stored:

- Locally
- Within a Project Workspace
- On a shared drive
- Using a future Collaboration Provider

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Visibility

Resources shall support one of the following visibility levels.

##### Private

The resource is visible only to its owner.

##### Shared

The resource is visible only to explicitly authorized users.

##### Workspace

The resource is available to users who have permission to access the
active Project Workspace.

##### Organization

The resource is available throughout the organization.

##### Public (Future)

The architecture shall support publicly shared resources without
requiring redesign.

The initial implementation is not required to implement Public
visibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Types

The Collaboration Framework shall support ownership and sharing for
resources including, but not limited to:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Working Views
- Report Templates
- Branding configurations
- Analytics layouts
- Dashboard layouts
- Export profiles
- Accessibility Standard packages
- Plugins
- Resource collections
- Future user-created resource types

Future resource types shall automatically participate in the
Collaboration Framework without requiring architectural redesign.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Personal vs Shared Resources

Unless explicitly designated otherwise by the user, newly created
resources shall be private.

Users may choose to publish supported resources according to their
permissions.

For example:

- Personal plugins may remain private.
- A user may choose to share a plugin with specific collaborators.
- A team lead may publish a plugin to an entire Project Workspace.
- An organization administrator may publish a plugin organization-wide.

The same behavior shall apply to:

- Accessibility Standard packages
- Working Views
- Templates
- Branding configurations
- Analytics layouts
- Other supported resource types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working Views

Working Views shall be personal by default.

Each user may create, modify, organize, and delete personal Working
Views without affecting other users.

Users viewing the same report may each maintain completely different
Working Views.

Working Views shall support optional sharing.

Authorized users may publish Working Views for:

- Specific users
- Project Workspaces
- Organizations

Users receiving a shared Working View may:

- Use it directly.
- Copy it.
- Customize their personal copy independently.

Modifying a copied Working View shall never modify the original shared
Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described above.

Do not implement real-time collaborative editing in this phase.

Preserve all existing Report Builder, Project Workspace, Working View,
Plugin Framework, Accessibility Standards Framework, Branding Framework,
Analytics Framework, Export Framework, and Resource Framework
functionality.

Consume existing ART frameworks whenever possible.

Do not duplicate ownership, sharing, or permission logic.

The completed implementation shall establish a flexible, extensible
Collaboration Framework capable of supporting future enterprise
collaboration while preserving ART's local-first philosophy.

### Part 2 – Collaboration Commands, Navigation, and Optional Toolbar

#### Collaboration Command Architecture

All commands and actions introduced by the Collaboration Framework shall
use ART's existing command/action architecture whenever possible.

Do not create duplicate command implementations for different UI
surfaces.

A single underlying command/action shall be capable of being exposed
through multiple supported interfaces, including:

Menu bar menus\
Command Search\
Command Palette\
Global context menu\
Optional Collaboration toolbar

The same command shall produce the same behavior, validation,
permissions checking, and results regardless of how the user invokes it.

Do not duplicate collaboration functionality merely to support different
invocation methods.

#### Minimize UI Clutter

The Collaboration Framework shall not introduce persistent buttons,
panels, cards, dialogs, widgets, or other controls throughout the ART
interface merely to expose collaboration functionality.

ART already contains substantial functionality and information on
screen.

Collaboration commands shall therefore be discoverable without
unnecessarily increasing visual or cognitive clutter.

Do not add collaboration controls directly to:

Report Builder\
Report Viewer\
Working View\
Dashboard\
Workspace content areas\
Other primary application interfaces

unless a future requirement explicitly identifies a specific contextual
control as necessary.

#### Menu Bar

When Collaboration is enabled in Application Settings, add a
Collaboration menu to the ART menu bar.

The Collaboration menu shall contain the collaboration commands and
actions available to the current user based on:

Current application state\
Active Project Workspace\
Active Report\
Active Working View\
User permissions\
Resource ownership\
Collaboration provider availability\
Collaboration feature availability

Commands that are not applicable to the current context shall be:

Hidden when appropriate, or\
Disabled with an accessible explanation when the command's presence
provides useful discoverability.

Do not display commands that the current user is not authorized to
perform.

The Collaboration menu shall follow the same keyboard navigation, focus
management, menu semantics, and accessibility behavior as ART's existing
menus.

#### Command Search

All applicable Collaboration commands shall be available through ART's
existing Command Search functionality.

Do not create a separate Collaboration command-search interface.

Command Search results shall:

Expose the command's accessible name.\
Clearly communicate what the command does.\
Respect user permissions.\
Respect the current application context.\
Indicate when a command is unavailable, where appropriate.\
Invoke the same underlying command used by the menu bar and Command
Palette.

#### Command Palette

All applicable Collaboration commands shall also be available through
ART's existing Command Palette.

Do not create a separate Collaboration command palette.

The Collaboration commands exposed through the Command Palette shall use
the same underlying command definitions used by:

Collaboration menu\
Command Search\
Global context menu\
Collaboration toolbar

The Command Palette shall respect all permission and contextual
restrictions.

#### Global Context Menu

When Collaboration is enabled in Application Settings, applicable
Collaboration commands shall be available through ART's existing global
context menu.

Do not create a separate Collaboration context-menu system.

The global context menu shall dynamically expose commands appropriate to
the current context.

For example, when the user is working with:

A Project Workspace\
A Report\
A Working View\
A shared plugin\
A shared Accessibility Standard package\
Another collaboration-enabled resource

the context menu may expose relevant collaboration actions.

Only actions applicable to the selected resource and current user
permissions shall be presented.

#### Collaboration Toolbar

Provide an optional Collaboration Toolbar for users who prefer a
visible, mouse-accessible collection of collaboration commands.

The toolbar shall not be enabled by default.

Users shall be able to enable or disable the Collaboration Toolbar
through Application Settings.

Provide an Application Settings option such as:

Show Collaboration Toolbar

The setting shall clearly communicate that the toolbar is optional.

#### Toolbar Placement

When enabled, the Collaboration Toolbar shall be movable.

Users shall be able to drag and drop the toolbar to their preferred
supported location within the ART application window.

The toolbar shall provide an accessible alternative to mouse-based
drag-and-drop positioning.

Users who cannot or do not wish to use drag-and-drop shall still be able
to reposition the toolbar using the keyboard and/or accessible toolbar
positioning controls.

The user's toolbar location shall persist according to ART's existing
settings persistence architecture.

#### Toolbar Accessibility

The Collaboration Toolbar shall be fully accessible.

It shall support:

Keyboard-only operation\
Screen readers\
Refreshable braille displays\
Speech recognition\
Voice control\
Switch access\
Other supported assistive technologies

The toolbar shall:

Have an appropriate accessible name.\
Expose its toolbar role programmatically.\
Provide accessible names for every command.\
Expose command states where applicable.\
Maintain a logical keyboard navigation order.\
Preserve visible focus.\
Support standard keyboard interaction patterns.\
Avoid trapping keyboard focus.\
Provide an accessible method for repositioning the toolbar.\
Provide an accessible method for enabling/disabling the toolbar.

Toolbar buttons shall not be the only way to invoke any Collaboration
command.

#### Toolbar Commands

The Collaboration Toolbar shall display only commands applicable to the
current context and user permissions.

The toolbar shall not attempt to expose every Collaboration command
simultaneously.

The implementation may provide a configurable set of commonly used
Collaboration commands while retaining access to all other commands
through:

Collaboration menu\
Command Search\
Command Palette\
Global context menu

The toolbar shall not become an alternative navigation system that
duplicates the entire Collaboration menu.

#### Collaboration Feature Setting

Provide an Application Settings option to enable or disable
Collaboration functionality.

When Collaboration is disabled:

The Collaboration menu shall not be displayed in the menu bar.\
Collaboration commands shall not appear in Command Search.\
Collaboration commands shall not appear in the Command Palette.\
Collaboration commands shall not appear in the global context menu.\
The Collaboration Toolbar shall not be displayed.\
Collaboration-specific UI shall not clutter the application.

When Collaboration is enabled:

The Collaboration menu shall be added to the menu bar.\
Applicable Collaboration commands shall become available through Command
Search.\
Applicable Collaboration commands shall become available through the
Command Palette.\
Applicable Collaboration commands shall become available through the
global context menu.\
Users may optionally enable the Collaboration Toolbar through
Application Settings.

Disabling Collaboration shall not delete or modify existing
collaboration data, resources, permissions, or configurations.

Re-enabling Collaboration shall restore access to previously configured
collaboration functionality.

#### Context Awareness

Collaboration commands shall be context-aware.

For example, the commands available while the user is:

Outside a Project Workspace\
Inside a Project Workspace\
Viewing a Report\
Editing a Report\
Viewing a Working View\
Editing a personal Working View\
Viewing a shared Working View\
Managing a shared resource

may differ.

The command system shall determine availability based on the current
context rather than presenting a large collection of irrelevant
commands.

#### Permissions

Every Collaboration command shall perform permission validation before
executing.

A command shall never rely solely on whether the command is visible or
enabled in the UI to enforce authorization.

Permission validation shall occur in the underlying command/action
implementation.

This ensures that Collaboration commands remain secure and consistent
regardless of whether they are invoked through:

Menu bar\
Command Search\
Command Palette\
Global context menu\
Collaboration Toolbar\
Future collaboration interfaces

#### Keyboard Accessibility

All Collaboration commands shall support ART's existing keyboard command
architecture.

Where ART supports customizable keyboard shortcuts, Collaboration
commands shall be compatible with that system.

Do not introduce Collaboration-specific keyboard shortcut mechanisms
that duplicate the existing shortcut architecture.

Keyboard shortcuts shall:

Be discoverable.\
Respect existing shortcut customization.\
Avoid conflicting with existing shortcuts.\
Preserve focus appropriately.\
Respect user permissions and context.

#### Focus Management

Collaboration commands shall follow ART's existing focus-management
patterns.

Opening a Collaboration command, menu, dialog, or other interface shall
not unexpectedly move focus to the top of the page.

When a Collaboration interface is closed, focus shall return to the
logical element that invoked it whenever appropriate.

This requirement applies to:

Collaboration menus\
Collaboration dialogs\
Sharing interfaces\
Permission interfaces\
Collaboration notifications\
Collaboration resource-management interfaces\
Other Collaboration Framework interfaces

#### Validation

Verify that:

Collaboration commands do not unnecessarily clutter the primary ART
interface.\
The Collaboration menu appears only when Collaboration is enabled.\
Collaboration commands are available through Command Search.\
Collaboration commands are available through the Command Palette.\
Applicable Collaboration commands are available through the global
context menu when Collaboration is enabled.\
The Collaboration Toolbar is disabled by default.\
Users can enable and disable the Collaboration Toolbar through
Application Settings.\
The toolbar is fully keyboard and screen-reader accessible.\
The toolbar can be repositioned using mouse and accessible non-mouse
methods.\
Toolbar position persists appropriately.\
Commands remain context-sensitive.\
Unauthorized commands cannot be executed even if invoked through another
interface.\
Existing menu, Command Search, Command Palette, context-menu, and
keyboard-shortcut functionality is not disrupted.\
Collaboration functionality does not introduce unnecessary persistent UI
clutter.\
Focus is preserved and restored appropriately throughout Collaboration
interactions.\
Disabling Collaboration removes Collaboration-specific UI and command
discovery surfaces without deleting collaboration data or
configurations.\
Re-enabling Collaboration restores the user's previously configured
Collaboration functionality.

#### Implementation Requirements

Use ART's existing:

Menu Framework\
Command Framework\
Command Search\
Command Palette\
Context Menu Framework\
Keyboard Shortcut Framework\
Application Settings Framework\
Focus Management Framework\
Accessibility Framework

Do not create duplicate implementations of these systems.

The Collaboration Framework shall integrate with these existing
frameworks rather than creating parallel UI, command, keyboard,
settings, or accessibility systems.

The completed implementation shall provide a low-clutter, discoverable,
fully accessible command architecture that allows users to access
Collaboration functionality through existing ART navigation mechanisms
while providing an optional visible toolbar for users who prefer
mouse-oriented interaction.

### Part 3 – Collaboration Permissions and Modular Access Control

#### Permission Architecture

Implement a modular, resource-based permission system for the
Collaboration Framework.

Permissions shall be assigned independently of the user's role or title.

Do not rely exclusively on fixed roles such as:

Owner\
Administrator\
Contributor\
Reviewer\
Viewer

Instead, roles and permission profiles shall be collections of
individual permissions that can be assigned to users, groups, or other
supported principals.

The underlying authorization system shall evaluate individual
permissions.

#### Permission-Based Actions

Permissions shall represent specific actions that a user may perform.

The initial permission model shall support, where applicable:

Read\
Create\
Edit\
Rename\
Delete\
Comment\
Resolve Comments\
Share\
Export\
Publish\
Assign Reviewers\
Manage Permissions\
Manage Workspace Settings\
Manage Branding\
Manage Templates\
Manage Accessibility Standards\
Manage Plugins\
Run Analytics\
Manage Analytics\
Create Working Views\
Manage Personal Working Views\
Share Working Views\
Manage Shared Working Views

The permission framework shall be extensible so additional permissions
can be introduced later without redesigning the authorization
architecture.

#### Resource-Level Permissions

Permissions shall be assignable at the resource level.

Supported resources shall include, where applicable:

Project Workspaces\
Reports\
Working Views\
Report Templates\
Branding configurations\
Accessibility Standard packages\
Plugins\
Analytics configurations\
Other collaboration-enabled resources

A user may therefore have different permissions for different resources.

For example, a user may:

Have full administrative permissions for one Project Workspace.\
Have Contributor permissions for another Project Workspace.\
Have Edit permission for one specific report.\
Have Read-only permission for another report.\
Have no access to a third report.\
Own a private plugin that is not shared with anyone else.

#### Permissions Outside Project Workspaces

Permissions shall not be limited to Project Workspaces.

A user shall be able to receive permissions to individual supported
resources that exist outside a Project Workspace.

For example, a user may be granted:

Read access to a standalone report.\
Edit access to a specific standalone report.\
Comment access to a specific report.\
Permission to use a specific shared plugin.\
Permission to use a specific Accessibility Standard package.

The user shall not automatically receive access to unrelated resources
merely because they have access to one resource.

#### Project Workspace Permissions

Project Workspaces shall support comprehensive permission management.

A user with appropriate administrative permissions may be able to
manage:

Workspace members\
Workspace permissions\
Workspace resources\
Reports\
Working Views\
Templates\
Branding\
Accessibility Standards\
Plugins\
Analytics\
Comments\
Sharing\
Exports\
Other supported workspace resources

The exact permissions available to each user shall be determined by the
permission assignments for that user.

#### Example: Workspace Administrator

A Workspace Administrator may be assigned permissions allowing them to:

Read workspace contents.\
Create resources.\
Edit resources.\
Rename resources.\
Delete resources.\
Comment.\
Resolve comments.\
Share resources.\
Export reports.\
Publish reports.\
Manage workspace settings.\
Manage members.\
Manage permissions.\
Manage workspace plugins.\
Manage workspace Accessibility Standard packages.\
Manage workspace templates.\
Manage workspace branding.\
Manage workspace analytics.

These permissions shall be represented as individual permissions rather
than being hard-coded solely to an "Administrator" role.

#### Example: Workspace Contributor

A Contributor may be assigned permissions allowing them to:

Read workspace contents.\
Create reports.\
Edit reports.\
Rename permitted resources.\
Delete permitted resources.\
Comment.\
Resolve comments where authorized.\
Share permitted resources.\
Export permitted reports.

A Contributor shall not automatically receive administrative permissions
simply because they are a Contributor.

Their actual capabilities shall be determined by their assigned
permission set.

#### Example: Viewer

A Viewer may have:

Read permission for reports.\
Read permission for workspace resources.\
Permission to create personal Working Views.\
Permission to manage their own personal Working Views.

A Viewer shall not need Edit permission on a report merely to create a
personal Working View.

Creating or modifying a personal Working View shall not modify the
underlying report data.

A Viewer shall not be able to:

Edit report content.\
Delete report content.\
Modify shared resources.\
Modify workspace settings.\
Manage workspace permissions.

unless those permissions are explicitly granted.

#### Personal Resource Permissions

Personal resources shall remain under the owner's control by default.

Examples include:

Personal Working Views\
Personal plugins\
Personal Accessibility Standard packages\
Personal analytics configurations\
Other user-created resources

The owner shall be able to manage the resource according to their
permissions.

Personal resources shall not automatically become visible or available
to other users.

#### Sharing Personal Resources

A user may choose to share a personal resource if the user has the
required Share permission.

For example:

A user creates a report-view plugin that they find useful.

The plugin remains private unless the user chooses to share it.

The user may then be able to share it with:

A specific user.\
A group.\
A Project Workspace.\
An organization.

Sharing shall not automatically transfer ownership unless explicitly
supported by a separate ownership-transfer operation.

#### Shared Plugins

Plugins shall support the same ownership and permission model as other
collaboration-enabled resources.

A plugin may be:

Personal/private.\
Shared with specific users.\
Shared with a Project Workspace.\
Shared organization-wide.

For example:

A team lead may create a report-view plugin and make it available to
everyone within a Project Workspace.

Individual users may use the shared plugin without becoming its owner.

The plugin owner or authorized administrator may update or withdraw the
shared plugin according to its permissions.

#### Accessibility Standard Packages

Accessibility Standard packages shall use the same ownership,
visibility, and permission architecture as plugins.

A package may be:

Personal/private.\
Shared with specific users.\
Shared with a Project Workspace.\
Shared organization-wide.

For example:

An accessibility specialist may create a custom Accessibility Standard
package for personal use.

A team lead may create a package and share it with the entire team.

An organization administrator may publish an approved package for
organization-wide use.

Do not create a separate sharing or permission system for Accessibility
Standard packages.

#### Permission Profiles

Provide reusable Permission Profiles to make permission management
easier for administrators.

ART may provide default profiles such as:

Owner\
Administrator\
Contributor\
Reviewer\
Viewer

However, these shall be permission profiles, not hard-coded
authorization roles.

Each profile shall represent a configurable collection of individual
permissions.

#### Custom Permission Profiles

Authorized administrators shall be able to create and manage custom
Permission Profiles.

For example:

Accessibility Reviewer

Read\
Comment\
Resolve Comments\
Run Analytics\
Export

Report Author

Read\
Create\
Edit\
Rename\
Comment\
Export

Report Publisher

Read\
Review\
Export\
Publish

The framework shall allow organizations to define profiles appropriate
to their workflows.

#### Permission Inheritance

Where appropriate, permissions shall support inheritance.

For example:

Project Workspace\
↓\
Report\
↓\
Working View

A user who has Read permission at the Workspace level may inherit Read
access to reports within that workspace.

More specific resource-level permissions may override inherited
permissions where authorized.

The implementation shall clearly distinguish between:

Inherited permissions\
Direct permissions\
Explicit permission overrides

Users with permission-management authority shall be able to understand
where a permission originated.

#### Permission Precedence

The framework shall establish deterministic rules for resolving
conflicting permissions.

For example, if a user receives:

Read permission through a Workspace.\
Edit permission directly on a Report.

the user shall receive the resulting effective permissions according to
the framework's defined precedence rules.

Do not implement ambiguous or unpredictable permission behavior.

Permission evaluation shall be centralized so all ART features use the
same authorization result.

#### Authorization Enforcement

Permission checks shall occur in the underlying command, action,
service, or resource operation.

Do not rely solely on UI visibility or disabled controls for security.

A user must not be able to bypass authorization by:

Using Command Search.\
Using the Command Palette.\
Using a context menu.\
Using a keyboard shortcut.\
Using the Collaboration Toolbar.\
Opening a direct resource URL.\
Importing a resource.\
Using another ART interface.\
Invoking an underlying command through another supported mechanism.

All supported access paths shall use the same authorization framework.

#### Permission-Aware UI

The UI shall reflect the user's effective permissions.

Where appropriate:

Unauthorized commands shall be hidden.\
Contextually unavailable commands may be disabled.\
Accessible explanations may be provided when a disabled command is
useful for discoverability.\
Permission-dependent controls shall expose their current state
programmatically.

The UI shall never be considered the authoritative security boundary.

#### Permission Management Accessibility

Permission management interfaces shall support:

Keyboard-only operation.\
Screen readers.\
Refreshable braille displays.\
Speech recognition.\
Voice control.\
Switch access.\
Other supported assistive technologies.

Permission information shall be presented in a clear, understandable
structure.

Users shall be able to determine:

Who has access.\
What permissions they have.\
Whether permissions are inherited.\
Whether permissions are directly assigned.\
What resource the permission applies to.

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  Permissions are modular and independently assignable.
2.  Users can have different permissions for different resources.
3.  Permissions can apply to resources outside Project Workspaces.
4.  Workspace permissions can be inherited by resources where
    appropriate.
5.  Resource-level permissions can override inherited permissions
    according to defined rules.
6.  Personal Working Views can be created by users who have permission
    to read the underlying report, even when those users cannot edit the
    report.
7.  Personal plugins can remain private.
8.  Plugins can be shared without automatically transferring ownership.
9.  Accessibility Standard packages use the same permission architecture
    as plugins.
10. Administrators can use configurable Permission Profiles.
11. Custom Permission Profiles can be created where authorized.
12. Authorization is enforced independently of UI visibility.
13. All command invocation methods use the same authorization framework.
14. Permission evaluation is consistent throughout ART.
15. Existing report, workspace, Working View, plugin, package,
    analytics, and resource functionality is not broken by the new
    permission architecture.
16. Screen readers and keyboard users can fully manage permissions.
17. No user can gain unauthorized access by using an alternate ART
    interface.
18. Permission behavior is deterministic, documented, and extensible.

### Part 4 – Collaboration Providers, Storage, Authentication, and Synchronization Architecture

#### Collaboration Provider Architecture

Implement the Collaboration Framework using a provider-based
architecture.

The core Collaboration Framework shall not depend on a single:

Server\
Database\
Cloud provider\
Storage system\
Authentication provider\
Networking protocol\
Synchronization technology

The framework shall define common interfaces that allow different
collaboration providers to be added without modifying the core
Collaboration Framework.

#### Initial Provider Strategy

The Collaboration Framework shall support the following provider
categories:

Local storage provider\
Shared-folder provider\
Network storage provider\
Cloud storage provider\
Collaboration server provider\
Future custom providers

The initial implementation does not need to implement every provider.

The architecture shall make it possible to add providers incrementally.

#### Local-First Operation

ART shall remain fully functional when no Collaboration Provider is
configured.

Users shall be able to:

Create reports.\
Edit reports.\
Create Project Workspaces.\
Create Working Views.\
Create plugins.\
Create Accessibility Standard packages.\
Export reports.\
Perform other supported ART operations.

without requiring:

An Internet connection.\
A remote server.\
A user account.\
A cloud provider.

Enabling Collaboration shall extend ART's capabilities rather than make
existing local functionality dependent upon a network connection.

#### Provider Independence

The core Collaboration Framework shall not contain provider-specific
business logic.

For example, the core framework shall not contain logic that assumes:

Google Drive is the storage system.\
Microsoft SharePoint is the collaboration system.\
GitHub is the synchronization system.\
A particular database is being used.\
A particular authentication service is being used.

Provider-specific behavior shall be isolated behind provider interfaces.

#### Storage Independence

The Collaboration Framework shall remain independent of the underlying
storage technology.

A collaboration-enabled resource may ultimately be stored in:

Local browser storage.\
Local files.\
Network folders.\
Shared drives.\
Cloud storage.\
Databases.\
Collaboration servers.\
Other supported storage systems.

The resource model shall not need to change merely because the storage
provider changes.

#### Transport Independence

The Collaboration Framework shall not require a specific communication
technology.

The architecture shall be capable of supporting future providers using
technologies such as:

HTTP/REST\
WebSockets\
Server-Sent Events\
WebRTC\
GraphQL\
Other suitable transport technologies

Do not select or hard-code one transport technology solely for the
purpose of this epic.

The transport implementation shall remain a provider-level concern.

#### Authentication Independence

The Collaboration Framework shall support pluggable authentication.

The framework shall not assume that all ART users have an online
account.

Future authentication providers may include:

Local ART identity.\
Organization-managed identity.\
Microsoft Entra ID.\
Google identity.\
GitHub identity.\
LDAP/Active Directory.\
Custom identity providers.\
Future ART-managed accounts.

Authentication and authorization shall remain separate concerns.

A user being authenticated does not automatically grant permission to a
resource.

Identity

The Collaboration Framework shall provide an abstract identity model.

A collaboration identity shall support, where available:

Stable unique identifier.\
Display name.\
Optional email address.\
Optional organization.\
Optional avatar/profile information.\
Authentication-provider identifier.

The framework shall not require email addresses to identify users.

The identity model shall allow the same person to be associated with
different providers without creating duplicate collaboration identities
where provider mapping is supported.

Synchronization Architecture

Implement synchronization as an independent framework service.

The synchronization architecture shall support:

Uploading local changes.\
Downloading remote changes.\
Detecting changes.\
Detecting conflicts.\
Resolving conflicts.\
Tracking synchronization state.\
Tracking synchronization errors.\
Retrying failed synchronization operations.

Synchronization shall not be tightly coupled to any specific storage
provider.

Synchronization States

Resources shall expose an understandable synchronization state.

Possible states shall include:

Local Only\
Synced\
Synchronizing\
Changes Pending\
Conflict Detected\
Synchronization Error\
Offline\
Provider Unavailable

The exact terminology may be refined during implementation, but the
underlying state model shall be explicit and extensible.

Synchronization state shall be available programmatically to assistive
technologies.

Offline Operation

ART shall continue operating when a collaboration provider becomes
temporarily unavailable.

Users shall be able to continue working locally when:

The Internet connection is unavailable.\
A collaboration server is unavailable.\
A cloud provider is unavailable.\
A network share is temporarily unavailable.

Changes made while offline shall be retained locally.

When connectivity is restored, the Synchronization Framework shall
determine whether the changes can be synchronized automatically or
require conflict resolution.

Synchronization Does Not Equal Real-Time Collaboration

Do not assume that synchronization requires real-time collaboration.

The initial Collaboration Framework may synchronize changes
asynchronously.

The architecture shall nevertheless support future real-time
collaboration.

For example:

Local Change\
↓\
Synchronization Provider\
↓\
Remote Resource

Future real-time collaboration may extend this architecture:

User A\
↕\
Real-Time Collaboration Service\
↕\
User B

without requiring the underlying resource model to be redesigned.

#### Future Real-Time Collaboration

The Collaboration Framework shall be architected to support future
synchronous, real-time editing similar to Google Docs and Google Sheets.

The framework shall not hard-code a particular real-time synchronization
algorithm.

Future implementations may use technologies or algorithms such as:

Operational Transformation (OT)\
Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs)\
Other suitable collaborative editing technologies

The selection of a real-time synchronization algorithm is outside the
scope of this initial implementation.

#### Collaboration Session

The framework shall introduce an abstract Collaboration Session concept.

A Collaboration Session represents a user's active participation in a
collaborative resource.

A session may eventually track:

Connected users.\
User presence.\
Active resource.\
Active Report.\
Active Working View.\
Synchronization state.\
Active edits.\
Comments.\
Notifications.\
Collaboration events.\
Future real-time cursor/presence information.

The initial implementation does not need to provide real-time cursors or
simultaneous editing.

The session architecture shall exist so these capabilities can be added
later without redesigning the Collaboration Framework.

#### Resource Synchronization

Synchronization shall operate at an appropriate resource level rather
than blindly synchronizing the entire application state.

For example, the framework should be capable of independently
synchronizing:

A Project Workspace.\
A Report.\
A Report Template.\
A Plugin.\
An Accessibility Standard package.\
A shared Working View.\
A Branding configuration.

Personal resources shall not be synchronized or shared with other users
unless the user explicitly chooses to do so and the applicable provider
supports it.

#### Resource Version Information

Collaboration-enabled resources shall maintain sufficient metadata to
determine whether changes have occurred.

Where appropriate, metadata may include:

Resource identifier.\
Owner identifier.\
Revision identifier.\
Parent revision.\
Last modified timestamp.\
Last modified user.\
Provider identifier.\
Synchronization state.

Do not rely solely on timestamps to determine whether two resources have
conflicting changes.

The architecture shall support stronger revision/change identifiers.

#### Provider Capabilities

Each Collaboration Provider shall expose its supported capabilities.

Capabilities may include:

Read\
Create\
Edit\
Delete\
Rename\
Share\
Permission management\
Synchronization\
Offline synchronization\
Version history\
Comments\
Presence\
Real-time collaboration\
File locking\
Conflict detection\
Conflict resolution\
Resource discovery

The Collaboration Framework shall determine available functionality
based on provider capabilities rather than assuming every provider
supports every feature.

#### Provider Availability

If a provider does not support a particular capability, ART shall:

Hide unsupported commands where appropriate, or\
Clearly communicate that the capability is unavailable.

ART shall not present a command that cannot work with the currently
selected provider unless there is a meaningful explanation for why it is
unavailable.

#### Provider Configuration

Provider configuration shall be managed through the existing Application
Settings framework.

Do not add persistent provider configuration controls to the primary ART
interface.

Users shall be able to:

View configured providers.\
Add supported providers.\
Remove providers.\
Enable or disable providers.\
Configure provider-specific settings.\
Test provider connectivity where supported.

Provider-specific configuration interfaces shall remain isolated from
the core Collaboration Framework.

#### Collaboration Provider Extensibility

The architecture shall allow future providers to be added without
modifying existing resource models.

A future provider could support:

OneDrive.\
SharePoint.\
Google Drive.\
Dropbox.\
GitHub.\
SMB/network shares.\
An ART collaboration server.\
A custom organizational service.

The addition of a provider shall not require rewriting:

Reports.\
Project Workspaces.\
Working Views.\
Plugins.\
Accessibility Standard packages.\
Permissions.\
Branding.\
Analytics.

#### Server Requirements

Do not require the user to have an ART collaboration server for the
initial implementation.

Do not assume that a server already exists.

Do not require a specific server language or technology.

The Collaboration Framework shall be designed so a future server-based
provider can be implemented without changing the core framework.

The eventual ART collaboration server may use any appropriate
technology.

The selection of technologies such as:

Node.js\
Python\
.NET\
Java\
Go\
Rust\
Other server technologies

is outside the scope of this epic.

#### Security

Provider communication shall use secure transport and authentication
mechanisms appropriate to the provider.

Do not store authentication credentials in ordinary report or workspace
data.

Sensitive authentication information shall be managed using appropriate
secure storage mechanisms available to the platform.

The Collaboration Framework shall not expose credentials through:

Reports.\
Templates.\
Plugins.\
Accessibility Standard packages.\
Exported files.\
Workspace files.

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  ART continues to function normally without Collaboration being
    configured.
2.  The Collaboration Framework does not require a server.
3.  The Collaboration Framework does not require an Internet connection
    for normal local ART functionality.
4.  Collaboration providers are isolated behind provider interfaces.
5.  Storage technology is not hard-coded into the core framework.
6.  Communication technology is not hard-coded into the core framework.
7.  Authentication is independent from authorization.
8.  Users can continue working while a provider is temporarily
    unavailable.
9.  Offline changes can be retained for later synchronization.
10. Synchronization state is accurately represented.
11. Provider capabilities determine which collaboration features are
    available.
12. Unsupported provider capabilities are handled gracefully.
13. Resource revisions can be tracked without relying solely on
    timestamps.
14. The framework can support future real-time collaboration.
15. The framework does not require selecting OT, CRDT, or another
    real-time synchronization algorithm at this stage.
16. Personal resources remain private unless explicitly shared.
17. Collaboration providers can be added without redesigning existing
    ART resources.
18. Provider configuration is accessible through Application Settings.
19. Authentication credentials are not stored in report or workspace
    data.
20. No provider-specific implementation leaks into the core
    Collaboration Framework.
21. Existing ART functionality remains fully operational when
    Collaboration is disabled.
22. No unnecessary collaboration UI is introduced as part of provider or
    synchronization functionality.
23. All provider, synchronization, and collaboration-state interfaces
    remain fully accessible.
24. No implementation decision in this part unnecessarily restricts
    future enterprise or real-time collaboration.

### Part 5: Synchronization, Versioning, and Conflict Resolution

#### Overview

Implement the synchronization, versioning, and conflict-resolution
foundation for the ART Collaboration Framework.

The framework shall allow users to work independently while offline and
synchronize changes when collaboration is available.

The initial implementation shall prioritize reliable asynchronous
collaboration.

The architecture shall also support future synchronous, real-time
collaboration without requiring the underlying resource model to be
redesigned.

#### Synchronization Principles

The Collaboration Framework shall follow these principles:

- Local work shall never depend on continuous network connectivity.
- Local changes shall be preserved when synchronization is unavailable.
- Synchronization shall not silently overwrite another user's changes.
- Conflicts shall be detected deterministically.
- Users shall be informed when their changes conflict with another
  user's changes.
- Conflict resolution shall preserve sufficient information for users to
  make informed decisions.
- Synchronization shall be provider-independent.
- Synchronization shall be resource-aware.
- Synchronization shall be extensible to support future real-time
  collaboration.

#### Resource Revisions

Each collaboration-enabled resource shall support revision tracking.

A revision shall include, where applicable:

- Resource identifier
- Revision identifier
- Parent revision identifier
- Resource owner
- Date and time of modification
- User who made the modification
- Collaboration provider
- Synchronization status
- Change metadata

Revision identifiers shall be sufficiently reliable to determine whether
two versions of a resource share a common history.

Do not rely solely on modification timestamps to determine whether a
conflict exists.

#### Change Tracking

The Collaboration Framework shall be capable of determining what changed
between resource revisions.

Where technically appropriate, changes may be tracked at different
levels of granularity.

Examples include:

- Resource level
- Report level
- Section level
- Finding level
- Field level
- Comment level
- Workspace metadata level

The framework shall not require every resource type to use identical
change-tracking granularity.

Each resource type may define the smallest meaningful unit that can be
synchronized and merged.

#### Synchronization Queue

When synchronization is unavailable, ART shall maintain a local queue of
pending synchronization operations.

The queue shall support:

- Pending changes
- Successful changes
- Failed changes
- Retryable changes
- Conflicted changes
- Cancelled changes

Pending changes shall remain available until they are successfully
synchronized or explicitly resolved.

ART shall not silently discard unsynchronized user work.

#### Synchronization Operations

The synchronization engine shall support operations such as:

- Create
- Update
- Rename
- Delete
- Share
- Unshare
- Permission change
- Resource metadata change

Provider capabilities shall determine which operations are supported.

The synchronization engine shall not assume that every provider supports
every operation.

#### Concurrent Changes

The Collaboration Framework shall detect when two users have modified
the same resource or meaningful portion of a resource since a common
revision.

For example:

``` text
Revision A
   |
   +---- User 1 → Revision B
   |
   +---- User 2 → Revision C
```

Revision B and Revision C shall be recognized as divergent revisions.

The framework shall not automatically assume that either revision should
replace the other.

#### Conflict Detection

A conflict shall occur when changes cannot safely be synchronized
without potentially discarding or altering another user's work.

Conflict detection shall consider:

- Revision history
- Resource identity
- Parent revision
- Change scope
- Resource-specific merge capabilities
- Provider capabilities

The framework shall distinguish between:

- Automatically mergeable changes
- Non-conflicting concurrent changes
- Conflicting changes
- Changes requiring user review

#### Automatic Merging

Where changes can be safely merged, ART may automatically merge them.

Examples may include:

- Two users editing different reports within the same workspace.
- Two users adding different findings.
- Two users creating separate Working Views.
- Two users adding independent comments.
- Changes to unrelated workspace metadata.

Automatic merging shall not silently discard either user's work.

#### Resource-Specific Merging

Different resource types may require different merge strategies.

For example:

#### Project Workspace

May merge independent resource additions or metadata changes.

#### Report

May merge changes to independent findings or report fields where
technically safe.

#### Working View

Personal Working Views should normally not require conflict resolution
because they are user-owned.

Shared Working Views may require conflict detection.

#### Plugin

Plugin metadata and package contents may require replacement, version
comparison, or explicit conflict resolution rather than attempting to
merge arbitrary plugin code.

#### Accessibility Standard Package

Structured standard data may be mergeable when the package format
supports it.

The framework shall allow each resource type to define its supported
merge behavior.

#### Conflict Resolution Interface

When a conflict cannot be automatically resolved, ART shall provide an
accessible Conflict Resolution interface.

The interface shall clearly communicate:

- The affected resource
- The user's version
- The other version
- The common ancestor revision, when available
- Who made each change
- When each change was made
- What portions of the resource differ
- Available resolution options

Users shall not be expected to understand technical revision identifiers
to resolve a conflict.

#### Conflict Resolution Options

Where appropriate, users may be offered options such as:

- Keep My Changes
- Keep Other Changes
- Merge Changes
- Review Changes
- Save Both Versions
- Cancel Resolution

Only options that are technically valid for the affected resource shall
be presented.

The terminology may be refined to match the specific resource being
resolved.

#### Preserve Both Versions

When automatic or manual merging could result in loss of information,
ART shall provide an option to preserve both versions.

The preserved version shall remain identifiable and recoverable.

Users shall not lose work merely because they were unable to resolve a
conflict immediately.

#### Conflict Notifications

Users shall be informed when one of their resources enters a conflict
state.

Notifications shall:

- Clearly identify the affected resource.
- Explain that synchronization requires attention.
- Provide an accessible method for opening the conflict-resolution
  interface.
- Avoid interrupting the user's current work unnecessarily.

Conflict notifications shall not repeatedly interrupt users while they
are actively working.

#### Synchronization Status

Users shall be able to determine the synchronization status of the
current resource.

Status information may include:

- Synced
- Saving locally
- Synchronizing
- Changes pending
- Offline
- Conflict detected
- Synchronization failed
- Provider unavailable

The synchronization state shall be exposed programmatically to assistive
technologies.

#### User-Initiated Synchronization

Where supported by the provider, users shall be able to manually
initiate synchronization.

The command shall be available through the existing Collaboration
command architecture, including:

- Collaboration menu
- Command Search
- Command Palette
- Global context menu
- Optional Collaboration Toolbar

Do not create a separate synchronization interface solely for manual
synchronization.

#### Automatic Synchronization

Providers that support automatic synchronization may synchronize changes
automatically.

Automatic synchronization shall:

- Preserve local changes.
- Detect conflicts.
- Respect permissions.
- Respect provider capabilities.
- Provide understandable status information.

Users shall not be required to manually save or synchronize every change
simply to prevent data loss.

#### Synchronization Errors

When synchronization fails, ART shall provide a meaningful explanation.

The error should identify, where possible:

- The affected resource
- The failed operation
- Whether the operation will be retried
- Whether the user needs to take action
- Whether the resource remains safely stored locally

Technical provider errors shall not be presented as the only explanation
to users.

Where technical details are useful, provide them as additional
information rather than replacing the user-facing explanation.

#### Retry Behavior

Retryable synchronization failures may be retried automatically.

The synchronization engine shall avoid creating an uncontrolled retry
loop.

Users shall be able to determine when synchronization remains
unsuccessful.

Where appropriate, users shall be able to manually retry
synchronization.

#### Deletions

Deletion synchronization shall receive special handling.

ART shall not silently delete a local resource merely because another
user deleted a remote version.

Where a deletion conflict exists, the framework shall preserve
sufficient information to allow the user to:

- Accept the deletion
- Restore the resource
- Preserve a local copy
- Resolve the conflict

Deletion behavior shall respect the user's permissions.

#### Offline Deletion

If a user deletes a resource while offline, the deletion shall be
retained as a pending synchronization operation.

ART shall not silently recreate the resource merely because
synchronization was temporarily unavailable.

If another user modified the resource while the first user was offline,
the framework shall detect the resulting conflict before permanently
applying the deletion.

#### Version History

Collaboration-enabled resources shall support version history where the
provider supports it.

Version history shall allow authorized users to determine:

- What revisions exist
- When they were created
- Who created them
- Which revision is currently active
- Whether a revision was synchronized
- Whether a revision is associated with a conflict

#### Restore Previous Version

Where supported, authorized users shall be able to restore a previous
revision.

Restoring a previous version shall not silently destroy the current
version.

Instead, restoration should create a new revision based on the selected
historical revision.

For example:

``` text
Revision 1
Revision 2
Revision 3  ← Current
        ↓
Restore Revision 1
        ↓
Revision 4  ← New current revision based on Revision 1
```

The previous revisions shall remain available in history.

#### Auditability

Synchronization and conflict-resolution operations shall be recorded in
the Collaboration Framework's audit history where appropriate.

Events may include:

- Resource created
- Resource modified
- Resource renamed
- Resource deleted
- Resource shared
- Permission changed
- Synchronization completed
- Synchronization failed
- Conflict detected
- Conflict resolved
- Previous revision restored

Audit records shall identify:

- User
- Action
- Resource
- Date and time
- Result

#### Personal Resources

Personal resources shall not participate in collaborative
synchronization merely because Collaboration is enabled.

For example:

- Personal Working Views
- Personal plugins
- Personal Accessibility Standard packages
- Personal analytics configurations

shall remain local/private unless the user explicitly chooses to share
them.

#### Shared Resource Changes

When a shared resource is modified, the Collaboration Framework shall
synchronize the change according to the resource's synchronization
capabilities.

The owner of a shared resource shall not automatically receive
unrestricted control over other users' copies or derived resources.

For example, if a user copies a shared Working View into their personal
Working Views, changes to the original shared Working View shall not
overwrite the user's personal copy.

#### Future Real-Time Collaboration

The synchronization architecture shall provide a foundation for future
real-time collaboration.

Future functionality may include:

- Live user presence
- Live editing
- Remote cursor positions
- Selection indicators
- Real-time comments
- Typing indicators
- Instant change propagation
- Collaborative undo/redo
- Real-time conflict prevention

These capabilities shall be implemented later without replacing the core
resource, revision, permission, and synchronization architecture defined
here.

#### Accessibility Requirements

All synchronization and conflict-resolution functionality shall be fully
accessible.

The implementation shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation
- Screen readers
- Refreshable braille displays
- Speech recognition
- Voice control
- Switch access
- Other supported assistive technologies
