Status changes shall not continuously interrupt screen reader users.

Synchronization updates shall generally be communicated through
appropriate status information rather than repeated intrusive
announcements.

Critical errors and conflicts shall be announced appropriately without
overwhelming the user with repeated notifications.

Conflict-resolution interfaces shall provide:

- Clear headings
- Logical focus order
- Programmatic relationships
- Accessible names
- Accessible descriptions
- Keyboard-accessible controls
- Meaningful status information
- Appropriate focus restoration when the interface is closed

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  Local work is preserved when synchronization is unavailable.
2.  Pending changes are not silently discarded.
3.  Resource revisions are tracked reliably.
4.  Concurrent changes are detected.
5.  Non-conflicting changes can be merged where supported.
6.  Conflicting changes are clearly identified.
7.  Users can resolve conflicts without losing work.
8.  Both versions can be preserved when necessary.
9.  Deleted resources are handled safely.
10. Version history accurately represents resource changes.
11. Restoring a previous version creates a new revision rather than
    destroying revision history.
12. Synchronization errors provide meaningful user-facing information.
13. Retry behavior does not create uncontrolled synchronization loops.
14. Personal resources remain private unless explicitly shared.
15. Shared Working Views can be copied without creating unwanted
    synchronization between the original and personal copy.
16. Synchronization state is accessible to screen reader users.
17. Synchronization updates do not repeatedly interrupt users while they
    work.
18. Conflict notifications are accessible without becoming excessively
    disruptive.
19. Conflict-resolution interfaces preserve keyboard focus
    appropriately.
20. All synchronization commands use the existing Collaboration command
    architecture.
21. Permissions are enforced during synchronization and conflict
    resolution.
22. Resource-specific merge behavior can be extended without redesigning
    the Collaboration Framework.
23. The architecture remains capable of supporting future real-time
    collaboration.
24. Existing local-only ART functionality continues to work when
    Collaboration is disabled.
25. No synchronization or versioning functionality introduces
    unnecessary persistent UI clutter.

### Part 6: Collaboration Sessions, Presence, and Shared Activity

#### Overview

Implement the foundation for Collaboration Sessions and shared user
presence within ART.

The Collaboration Framework shall allow users to understand when they
are participating in collaborative work and, when supported by the
active Collaboration Provider, which other users are currently
participating in the same collaborative context.

The initial implementation shall support collaboration-session
architecture and provider capability detection without requiring
real-time collaborative editing.

Future implementations shall be able to extend this foundation to
support real-time presence and editing similar to Google Docs and Google
Sheets.

#### Collaboration Session Model

A Collaboration Session shall represent a user's active participation in
a collaboration-enabled resource or context.

A session may be associated with:

- Project Workspace
- Report
- Working View
- Shared resource
- Collaboration provider

A session shall have a unique identifier and sufficient metadata to
determine:

- Current user
- Active resource
- Session state
- Provider
- Connection state
- Session start
- Last activity
- Other supported session information

The session model shall remain independent of any particular provider or
communication technology.

#### Session States

The Collaboration Framework shall support explicit session states, such
as:

- Inactive
- Starting
- Active
- Reconnecting
- Offline
- Disconnected
- Ending
- Ended
- Error

The exact terminology may be refined during implementation.

Session state shall be exposed programmatically and shall be available
to assistive technologies where the state is presented to users.

#### Collaboration Context

The framework shall distinguish between the user's current application
context and their collaboration context.

For example, a user may be:

- Working locally without collaboration.
- Viewing a shared Project Workspace.
- Editing a shared Report.
- Viewing a shared Working View.
- Using a shared plugin.
- Working with a shared Accessibility Standard package.

The collaboration session shall identify the applicable collaborative
context without changing the user's personal Working View or other
personal preferences.

#### Personal Working Views and Sessions

Working Views shall remain personal by default.

Opening or using a shared Report shall not automatically make a user's
Working View collaborative.

For example:

- User A may use a personal Working View.
- User B may use a different personal Working View.
- Both users may be viewing the same Report.
- Neither user's personal Working View shall be modified by the other
  user.

A shared Working View shall be treated as a shared resource.

A user may choose to use a shared Working View without making their
subsequent personal modifications visible to other users.

#### Shared Working View Usage

When a user opens a shared Working View, ART shall distinguish between:

- Using the original shared Working View.
- Creating a personal copy of the shared Working View.

If the user creates a personal copy:

- The user becomes the owner of the copy.
- Changes to the copy shall not modify the original.
- Changes to the original shall not silently overwrite the copy.
- The copy shall follow the user's personal Working View permissions.

#### User Presence

The Collaboration Framework shall support future user-presence
information.

When the active Collaboration Provider supports presence, ART may expose
information such as:

- User name
- Display name
- Avatar, when available
- Current collaborative resource
- Current report
- Current Working View
- Presence state
- Last active time

Possible presence states include:

- Active
- Idle
- Away
- Offline

The provider shall determine which presence capabilities are available.

Do not assume that every Collaboration Provider supports real-time
presence.

#### Presence Capability

Collaboration Providers shall expose whether they support:

- User presence
- Presence updates
- Active-resource information
- Real-time presence
- Last-active information

ART shall use provider capabilities to determine which presence features
are available.

Unsupported presence capabilities shall not cause errors or unnecessary
UI elements.

#### Presence Privacy

Users shall have control over supported presence information where
applicable.

The framework shall support future Application Settings options for
controlling whether a user's presence information is shared.

Possible settings may include:

- Show me as active
- Show my current collaborative resource
- Show my last active time

The exact settings may be refined during implementation.

Presence information shall not be exposed more broadly than permitted by
the user's collaboration settings and applicable resource permissions.

#### No Mandatory Presence

Users shall not be required to expose their presence simply because
Collaboration is enabled.

A user may work independently without participating in live presence
functionality.

If the configured Collaboration Provider does not support presence, ART
shall continue to operate normally without displaying unavailable
presence controls.

#### Active Collaborators

When supported, users with appropriate access may be able to view other
users participating in the same collaborative context.

For example:

``` text
Project Workspace: Accessibility Audit

Active Collaborators:
- Alex
- Jordan
- Morgan
```

#### Resource-Specific Presence

Presence should be scoped appropriately.

A user working in one Project Workspace should not automatically appear
as active in unrelated Project Workspaces.

Likewise, users viewing one Report should not automatically appear as
active in every Report they have permission to access.

The Collaboration Framework shall use the smallest appropriate
collaborative scope supported by the provider.

#### Report Presence

When supported, users viewing or editing the same Report may be
identified as active collaborators.

The initial implementation does not need to provide:

- Live cursors

- Selection indicators

- Typing indicators

- Character-level editing presence

Those capabilities shall remain future extensions.

#### Future Real-Time Editing

The Collaboration Session model shall provide a foundation for future
real-time editing.

Future implementations may expose:

- User cursors

- Text selections

- Current field

- Current finding

- Active section

- Typing indicators

- Live edits

- Real-time comments

The current implementation shall not require these capabilities.

#### Shared Activity

The Collaboration Framework shall support future shared activity
information.

Examples include:

- User created a report.

- User edited a finding.

- User added a comment.

- User resolved a comment.

- User shared a resource.

- User created a Working View.

- User published a plugin.

- User updated a shared Accessibility Standard package.

Shared activity shall be separate from audit history.

Audit history records authoritative resource events.

Shared activity is intended to help users understand what is happening
within their collaborative context.

#### Activity Privacy

Shared activity shall respect:

- Resource permissions

- User privacy settings

- Organization policies

- Collaboration provider capabilities

Do not expose activity from resources that the current user cannot
access.

Do not expose sensitive information unnecessarily.

#### Activity Notifications

Collaboration activity may eventually produce notifications.

Examples include:

- A user mentioned another user in a comment.

- A user was assigned a review.

- A shared resource changed.

- A user's permission changed.

- A conflict requires attention.

Notifications shall use ART's existing notification architecture.

Do not create a separate Collaboration notification system.

#### Notification Non-Interruption

Collaboration notifications shall not unnecessarily interrupt users.

In particular:

- Routine synchronization updates should not repeatedly interrupt
  screen-reader users.

- Presence changes should not generate continuous announcements.

- Users joining or leaving a collaborative resource should not
  automatically generate disruptive announcements unless the user has
  requested that behavior.

- Shared activity updates should generally be available through an
  accessible status or activity interface rather than being announced
  continuously.

Critical events may receive appropriate announcements according to their
importance and the user's settings.

#### Screen Reader Behavior

Collaboration presence and activity information shall be accessible to
screen-reader users without creating excessive speech interruptions.

Dynamic updates shall use appropriate accessible status mechanisms.

Do not repeatedly announce every presence change.

For example, if multiple users join or leave a Report while a user is
typing, ART shall not repeatedly interrupt the user's typing with
announcements such as:

> 

Alex joined.

> 

Jordan joined.

> 

Morgan left.

Instead, the user should be able to access the current collaborator
information when they choose to review it.

#### Keyboard Accessibility

All collaboration-session and presence functionality shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation

- Logical focus order

- Visible focus

- Screen readers

- Refreshable braille

- Speech recognition

- Voice control

- Switch access

Opening a collaborator or activity interface shall not move focus
unexpectedly.

When such an interface is closed, focus shall return to the invoking
control or the most logical previous location.

#### Collaboration Activity Interface

If a dedicated activity interface is implemented, it shall use existing
ART UI patterns and shall not create persistent screen clutter.

The interface may be exposed through:

- Collaboration menu

- Command Search

- Command Palette

- Global context menu

- Optional Collaboration Toolbar

Do not add a permanently visible collaborator panel by default.

#### Optional Collaboration Toolbar Integration

If the Collaboration Toolbar is enabled, it may expose commands such as:

- View Collaborators

- View Activity

- View Session Status

- Synchronize

- Resolve Conflicts

The toolbar shall not be required to access any collaboration-session
functionality.

All functionality shall remain available through the other Collaboration
command surfaces.

#### Connection State

The Collaboration Session shall expose connection state independently
from resource synchronization state.

For example:

- Connected

- Connecting

- Reconnecting

- Offline

- Provider unavailable

Connection state shall not automatically imply that a resource has
unsynchronized changes.

A user may be:

- Connected with no pending changes.

- Connected with pending changes.

- Offline with no pending changes.

- Offline with pending changes.

- Connected while a synchronization conflict exists.

These states shall remain independently representable.

#### Session Recovery

If a collaboration session is interrupted, ART shall attempt to recover
the session when supported.

Examples include:

- Temporary network interruption.

- Browser reconnection.

- Collaboration provider restart.

- Temporary authentication interruption.

Session recovery shall not discard local work.

If recovery cannot occur automatically, ART shall provide an accessible
explanation and appropriate next steps.

#### Session Termination

When the user closes or leaves a collaboration-enabled resource, the
Collaboration Session shall be ended or suspended according to the
provider's capabilities.

Ending a session shall not:

- Delete the resource.

- Remove the user's permissions.

- Delete personal Working Views.

- Delete pending local changes.

- Revoke sharing.

Session termination shall only affect the user's active participation in
the collaboration context.

#### Multiple Sessions

The framework shall support a user being active in multiple
collaboration contexts when the platform permits it.

For example, a user may have:

- One Report open in one browser tab.

- Another Report open in another browser tab.

- A Project Workspace open in another supported application context.

The framework shall distinguish these sessions without corrupting
resource state.

#### Session Identity

A session shall not be treated as the user's identity.

A user may have multiple sessions.

A single collaboration identity may therefore have:

User\
├── Session A\
├── Session B\
└── Session C

The Collaboration Framework shall prevent multiple sessions belonging to
the same user from being incorrectly represented as multiple users.

#### Future Multi-User Editing

The session architecture shall support future simultaneous editing by
multiple users.

Future real-time editing may associate collaborators with:

- Report fields

- Findings

- Text selections

- Comments

- Report sections

- Working View elements

The current implementation shall not require these associations.

#### Provider Independence

Collaboration Sessions and presence shall not depend on a particular:

- Server

- Database

- Network protocol

- Authentication provider

- Cloud provider

- Real-time collaboration technology

Provider-specific session and presence implementations shall be isolated
behind the Collaboration Provider architecture established in earlier
parts of this epic.

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  Collaboration Sessions have explicit, identifiable states.

2.  Session state is independent from synchronization state.

3.  Users can work without participating in a collaboration session.

4.  Personal Working Views remain personal even when the underlying
    Report is shared.

5.  Shared Working Views remain distinguishable from personal Working
    Views.

6.  Copying a shared Working View creates an independent personal
    resource.

7.  Presence is provider-capability dependent.

8.  Presence is scoped to the appropriate collaborative context.

9.  Users cannot see presence information for resources they cannot
    access.

10. Users are not required to expose presence simply because
    Collaboration is enabled.

11. Presence updates do not continuously interrupt screen-reader users.

12. Shared activity does not unnecessarily interrupt users.

13. Collaboration notifications use the existing notification
    architecture.

14. Session interruption does not cause loss of local work.

15. Session recovery does not create duplicate users or duplicate
    resource changes.

16. Multiple sessions belonging to the same user are correctly
    represented.

17. Session termination does not alter resource ownership or
    permissions.

18. Collaboration-session functionality is accessible using keyboard and
    assistive technologies.

19. Focus is preserved when collaboration interfaces are opened and
    closed.

20. No persistent collaborator panel or other unnecessary UI clutter is
    introduced.

21. Collaboration commands remain available through the established
    command surfaces.

22. The architecture supports future real-time presence and simultaneous
    editing without requiring a redesign.

23. Existing local-only ART functionality remains unaffected when
    Collaboration is disabled.

### Part 7: Comments, Mentions, Reviews, and Collaborative Discussion

#### Overview

Implement the collaborative commenting and discussion foundation for
ART.

Users shall be able to communicate about reports, findings, workspaces,
and other supported collaboration resources without requiring them to
modify the underlying content.

The commenting framework shall support asynchronous collaboration
initially while providing an architecture that can later support
real-time discussion.

Comments shall respect the Collaboration Framework's existing
permissions, resource ownership, synchronization, identity, and
accessibility models.

#### Commentable Resources

Comments shall be supported on appropriate collaboration-enabled
resources, including:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Findings
- Report sections
- Report fields
- Working Views where supported
- Templates where supported
- Plugins where supported
- Accessibility Standard packages where supported

Not every resource type must support every comment feature.

Each resource type shall define where comments can be attached.

#### Comment Types

The framework shall support, where appropriate:

- General comments
- Resource-level comments
- Finding-level comments
- Field-level comments
- Section-level comments
- Replies
- Mentions
- Review comments

Comments shall remain separate from the actual report content unless a
specific feature explicitly converts a comment into report content.

#### Comment Ownership

Each comment shall have an identifiable author.

Comment metadata shall include, where applicable:

- Comment identifier
- Author
- Creation date and time
- Last modified date and time
- Resource identifier
- Parent comment or thread
- Comment status
- Revision information

A user shall only be able to modify or delete a comment when permitted
by the applicable permissions.

#### Comment Permissions

Comment functionality shall use the existing modular permission
architecture.

Do not create a separate authorization system specifically for comments.

Relevant permissions may include:

- Comment
- Edit Comment
- Delete Comment
- Reply
- Resolve Comments
- Reopen Comments
- Mention Users
- Manage Comments

A user may have permission to comment without having permission to edit
the underlying resource.

For example:

A reviewer may have permission to comment on a report while having no
permission to modify the report itself.

#### Comment Threads

Related comments shall be grouped into accessible discussion threads.

A thread may contain:

- Original comment
- Replies
- Mentions
- Resolution state
- Activity history

Users shall be able to determine which comments belong to the same
thread.

#### Replies

Users with appropriate permissions shall be able to reply to an existing
comment.

Replies shall remain associated with the parent comment.

The interface shall clearly communicate:

- Which comment is being replied to.
- Who authored the original comment.
- The relationship between the reply and the original comment.

#### Comment Resolution

Comments shall support a resolved/unresolved state where appropriate.

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Resolve a comment.
- Reopen a resolved comment.
- View resolved comments.
- Hide resolved comments from the default view where appropriate.

Resolving a comment shall not delete it.

The comment and its history shall remain available according to the
resource's retention and permission rules.

#### Review Workflow

The commenting framework shall support future review workflows.

A review process may allow users to:

- Add comments.
- Reply to comments.
- Resolve comments.
- Reopen comments.
- Assign comments.
- Mention other users.
- Review outstanding comments.

The initial implementation does not need to implement a complete formal
approval workflow.

The architecture shall allow review and approval functionality to be
added later.

#### Mentions

Users shall be able to mention another user when the applicable resource
and permissions support mentions.

For example:

``` text
@Alex Please review the contrast finding on this page.
```

A mention shall identify the intended user programmatically.

The mention shall not depend solely on visually displaying the user's
name.

#### Mention Suggestions

When a user types a mention trigger such as `@`, ART may provide a list
of users who can be mentioned.

The mention suggestion interface shall:

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Be accessible to screen readers.

- 

Support programmatic focus.

- 

Clearly identify each available user.

- 

Respect resource permissions.

- 

Avoid exposing users who cannot legitimately be mentioned.

Screen readers shall not be repeatedly interrupted while the mention
list is being updated.

#### Mention Notifications

When a user is mentioned, ART may notify that user according to the
existing notification framework.

Mention notifications shall:

- 

Identify the author.

- 

Identify the resource.

- 

Identify the relevant comment.

- 

Provide an accessible way to navigate to the comment.

Notifications shall respect the user's notification settings.

#### No Notification Spam

ART shall not generate excessive notifications for collaborative
activity.

For example, if a user is mentioned multiple times in the same thread
within a short period, the notification system should avoid
unnecessarily generating a separate disruptive notification for every
event where appropriate.

Users shall have control over notification preferences where supported.

#### Comment Editing

Users with appropriate permissions shall be able to edit their comments.

When a comment is edited, ART shall preserve appropriate metadata
indicating that the comment was modified.

Where version history is supported, previous versions of the comment may
be retained.

Editing a comment shall not change the author.

#### Comment Deletion

Users with appropriate permissions may delete comments.

Where deletion is supported, ART should preserve sufficient audit
information to indicate that a comment was deleted without unnecessarily
retaining deleted comment content when retention policies do not permit
it.

Deleting a comment shall not silently delete replies or unrelated
comments.

If a parent comment is deleted while replies exist, ART shall preserve
the thread structure appropriately.

#### Comment Search

The Collaboration Framework shall support future searching and filtering
of comments.

Possible filters include:

- 

Author

- 

Date

- 

Resource

- 

Report

- 

Finding

- 

Unresolved

- 

Resolved

- 

Mentioned user

- 

Assigned user

The initial implementation may provide a smaller subset of these
capabilities.

The architecture shall not prevent additional comment-search
functionality from being added later.

#### Comment Navigation

Users shall be able to navigate directly to a comment's associated
resource.

For example, activating a comment associated with a finding should take
the user to the appropriate finding.

Activating a comment associated with a report field should take the user
to the appropriate report field when possible.

The destination shall preserve the user's context where appropriate.

#### Focus Management

Opening a comment interface shall preserve logical focus.

When a user:

1.  

Opens a comment interface.

2.  

Reads or writes a comment.

3.  

Closes the interface.

focus shall return to the control or location from which the comment
interface was invoked.

The interface shall not unexpectedly move focus to the top of the page.

This requirement applies to:

- 

Comment dialogs

- 

Comment panels

- 

Reply controls

- 

Mention interfaces

- 

Comment notifications

- 

Comment navigation

#### Keyboard Accessibility

All comment functionality shall support keyboard-only operation.

Users shall be able to:

- 

Open comments.

- 

Create comments.

- 

Edit comments.

- 

Delete comments when authorized.

- 

Reply.

- 

Resolve comments.

- 

Reopen comments.

- 

Navigate between comments.

- 

Navigate between comment threads.

- 

Mention users.

- 

Close comment interfaces.

All controls shall have logical keyboard navigation order.

#### Screen Reader Accessibility

Comment functionality shall provide meaningful information to screen
readers.

A screen reader user shall be able to determine:

- 

That a comment exists.

- 

Who authored it.

- 

When it was created or modified.

- 

What resource it applies to.

- 

Whether it is resolved.

- 

Whether it has replies.

- 

Whether the user has been mentioned.

- 

What actions are available.

The semantic relationship between a comment and its associated resource
shall be programmatically determinable.

#### Dynamic Comment Updates

When another user adds or modifies a comment, ART shall not continuously
interrupt the current user's work.

Dynamic comment updates should generally be available through:

- 

Accessible status information.

- 

Notification indicators.

- 

Comment counts.

- 

Activity views.

Do not announce every remote comment change through a screen reader
automatically.

Critical notifications may be announced when appropriate and according
to user settings.

#### Comment Counts

Where comments are represented in the interface, ART may display comment
counts.

For example:

    Finding 3
    Comments: 4

The comment count shall be programmatically associated with the
resource.

A changed comment count shall not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader
users.

#### Comment Indicators

Comment indicators shall not rely solely on color, icons, or visual
styling.

If an icon or visual marker indicates that a resource has comments, the
same information shall be available programmatically.

For example:

- 

Accessible name

- 

Accessible description

- 

Textual status

- 

Screen-reader accessible information

#### Resolved Comment Indicators

Resolved comments shall be distinguishable from unresolved comments
without relying solely on color.

Users shall be able to determine programmatically whether a comment
thread is:

- 

Unresolved

- 

Resolved

#### Comments and Working Views

Comments associated with a report shall remain associated with the
underlying report resource rather than being duplicated separately for
every personal Working View.

A user's personal Working View may filter or display comments according
to the user's preferences and permissions.

Changing a personal Working View shall not modify the underlying
comments.

Shared Working Views may optionally define comment-related filtering or
display behavior when supported.

#### Comments and Report Revisions

Where comments are associated with specific report content, ART shall
retain enough information to determine what the comment originally
referred to.

If the associated content changes significantly, the comment should
remain understandable and traceable to the appropriate resource or
revision.

The framework shall avoid silently attaching a comment to unrelated
content after significant report changes.

#### Comments and Synchronization

Comments shall participate in the existing Collaboration synchronization
architecture.

The commenting system shall support:

- 

Offline comments

- 

Pending comment synchronization

- 

Comment synchronization errors

- 

Concurrent replies

- 

Conflict detection where necessary

Independent comments and replies should be automatically synchronized
when they do not conflict.

#### Concurrent Comments

If two users add separate comments to the same resource, both comments
shall be preserved.

For example:

    Finding 12
    ├── Comment by Alex
    └── Comment by Jordan

ART shall not treat independent comments as conflicting merely because
they reference the same resource.

#### Concurrent Comment Editing

If two users edit the same comment concurrently and the changes cannot
be safely merged, ART shall use the existing synchronization and
conflict-resolution framework.

The system shall not silently overwrite one user's changes.

#### Comment Audit History

Where collaboration audit history is enabled, ART shall record
appropriate comment events.

Possible events include:

- 

Comment created

- 

Comment edited

- 

Comment deleted

- 

Reply added

- 

Comment resolved

- 

Comment reopened

- 

User mentioned

- 

Comment assigned

Audit information shall respect applicable permissions and privacy
requirements.

#### Comment Privacy

Comments shall inherit the access restrictions of their associated
resource unless a more restrictive permission model is explicitly
defined.

A user who cannot access a report shall not gain access to its comments
merely because they were mentioned elsewhere.

Comments shall not expose restricted report information to unauthorized
users.

#### Comment Sharing

Sharing a report or workspace shall not automatically expose comments to
users who do not have permission to access the associated resource.

When a resource is shared, its comments shall become available according
to the resource's effective permissions and comment permissions.

#### Comment Notifications and Shared Resources

If a user receives a notification about a comment on a shared resource,
opening the notification shall verify that the user still has access to
the resource.

If access has been revoked, ART shall not expose restricted comment or
report content.

The user shall receive an appropriate explanation that the resource is
no longer available to them.

#### UI Placement

Comment commands and actions shall not unnecessarily clutter the ART
interface.

Use the existing collaboration command architecture.

Comment-related commands should be available through:

- 

Collaboration menu

- 

Context menus

- 

Command Search

- 

Command Palette

- 

Global context menu when Collaboration is enabled

- 

Optional Collaboration Toolbar

Do not create a permanently visible comment toolbar or panel by default.

#### Optional Comment Panel

If ART provides a comment panel, it shall be optional.

Users should be able to open and close the panel when needed.

The panel shall:

- 

Be fully keyboard accessible.

- 

Have an accessible name.

- 

Have a logical heading structure.

- 

Preserve focus when opened and closed.

- 

Support screen readers.

- 

Avoid obscuring important report content unnecessarily.

#### Comment Dialogs

If comments are implemented using dialogs:

- 

The dialog shall have an accessible name.

- 

Focus shall move into the dialog when opened.

- 

Focus shall remain appropriately contained while the dialog is modal.

- 

Escape shall close the dialog when appropriate.

- 

Closing the dialog shall restore focus to the invoking control.

- 

The dialog shall not move focus to the top of the page.

#### Comment Text Input

Comment text fields shall have:

- 

Visible labels.

- 

Programmatic accessible names.

- 

Appropriate descriptions or instructions where needed.

- 

Correct keyboard behavior.

- 

Appropriate input semantics.

Do not rely solely on placeholder text as the accessible name.

#### Comment Drafts

If technically appropriate, ART may preserve an unsent comment draft.

If a user accidentally closes a comment interface while composing a
comment, the framework may preserve the draft locally.

A draft shall not become visible to other collaborators until the user
explicitly submits it.

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  

Users can create comments when they have the appropriate permission.

2.  

Users can comment without necessarily having permission to edit the
underlying report.

3.  

Comments are associated with the correct resource.

4.  

Comment threads are accessible.

5.  

Replies remain associated with the correct parent comment.

6.  

Comments can be resolved and reopened where authorized.

7.  

Resolved comments are not deleted.

8.  

Mentions identify the intended user programmatically.

9.  

Mention suggestions are fully keyboard and screen-reader accessible.

10. 

Users cannot mention unauthorized users.

11. 

Mention notifications use the existing notification architecture.

12. 

Comment updates do not continuously interrupt screen-reader users.

13. 

Comment counts and indicators are accessible without relying solely on
visual styling.

14. 

Opening and closing comment interfaces preserves logical focus.

15. 

Comments remain synchronized according to the existing Collaboration
Framework.

16. 

Independent concurrent comments are preserved.

17. 

Concurrent comment edits do not silently overwrite another user's
changes.

18. 

Comments respect resource permissions.

19. 

Users cannot access comments belonging to resources they cannot access.

20. 

Personal Working Views do not alter the underlying comments.

21. 

Shared Working Views can display or filter comments without changing the
underlying comment data.

22. 

Comment-related commands are available through the established
Collaboration command surfaces.

23. 

Comment functionality does not introduce unnecessary persistent UI
clutter.

24. 

All comment functionality works with keyboard-only navigation and
assistive technologies.

25. 

Existing local-only ART functionality continues to work when
Collaboration is disabled.

26. 

The commenting architecture remains extensible for future review
workflows and real-time collaborative discussion.

### Part 8: Collaboration Sharing, Invitations, and Resource Discovery

#### Overview

Implement the sharing, invitation, and resource-discovery foundation for
the ART Collaboration Framework.

Users shall be able to share supported ART resources with other users
while maintaining the modular permission model established in earlier
parts of this epic.

Sharing shall be available for both:

- Standalone resources.
- Resources contained within Project Workspaces.

The implementation shall clearly distinguish between sharing a resource
and transferring ownership.

#### Shareable Resources

The Collaboration Framework shall support sharing, where applicable,
for:

- Project Workspaces
- Reports
- Report Templates
- Working Views
- Plugins
- Accessibility Standard packages
- Branding configurations
- Other collaboration-enabled resources

Each resource type shall define:

- Whether it can be shared.
- Who may share it.
- What permissions may be granted.
- Whether sharing can be inherited.
- Whether the resource can be shared outside its parent Workspace.

#### Standalone Resource Sharing

Standalone reports and other supported standalone resources shall be
shareable independently of Project Workspaces.

For example, a user may share:

``` text
Accessibility Audit Report
    ↓
Alex — Edit
Jordan — Comment
Morgan — Read
```

Sharing a standalone report shall not automatically provide access to
unrelated reports or Project Workspaces.

#### Project Workspace Sharing

Project Workspaces shall be shareable as collaborative containers.

When a Workspace is shared, users may receive access to resources
contained within the Workspace according to the Workspace's permission
model.

Workspace administrators shall be able to determine whether individual
resources inherit Workspace permissions or have more restrictive
permissions.

#### Resource-Level Sharing Within Workspaces

A resource within a Project Workspace may be shared independently when
the user has the appropriate permissions.

For example:

    Project Workspace
    ├── Report A
    ├── Report B
    └── Report C

    Report A → Shared with Team
    Report B → Shared only with Reviewers
    Report C → Private

Sharing one resource shall not automatically expose unrelated resources.

#### Ownership

Sharing a resource shall not automatically transfer ownership.

The owner shall remain the owner unless an explicit ownership-transfer
operation is performed.

Ownership transfer shall require appropriate permissions.

When ownership is transferred:

- 

The previous owner shall no longer be represented as the owner.

- 

The new owner shall be clearly identified.

- 

Existing permissions shall be handled according to defined
ownership-transfer rules.

- 

The operation shall be recorded in collaboration history where
appropriate.

#### Sharing Permissions

The sharing interface shall use the existing modular permission
architecture.

Users shall be able to grant supported individual permissions rather
than being restricted to fixed roles.

For example:

    Alex
    - Read
    - Comment

    Jordan
    - Read
    - Edit
    - Comment
    - Export

    Morgan
    - Read

The available permissions shall depend on:

- 

Resource type.

- 

User's permissions.

- 

Provider capabilities.

- 

Applicable organization policies.

#### Permission Profiles in Sharing

The sharing interface may allow administrators to assign existing
Permission Profiles.

For example:

- 

Viewer

- 

Contributor

- 

Reviewer

- 

Custom Accessibility Reviewer

A Permission Profile shall remain a collection of individual
permissions.

Users with sufficient authority should be able to review the resulting
individual permissions before completing the share operation.

#### Sharing Restrictions

A user shall not be able to grant permissions they do not possess or are
not authorized to delegate.

For example:

A user with Read and Comment permission shall not be able to grant
another user Edit permission.

A user with Edit permission shall not automatically be able to manage
permissions unless Manage Permissions has also been granted.

#### Nested Sharing

The framework shall establish clear rules for sharing resources
contained within shared resources.

For example:

    Workspace
        ↓
    Report
        ↓
    Finding

A user with Workspace access may inherit access to the Report.

A Report may additionally be shared with another user.

ART shall calculate the effective permissions using the centralized
authorization framework.

#### Access Through Multiple Paths

A user may receive access to the same resource through multiple paths.

For example:

- 

Directly shared with the Report.

- 

Member of the Project Workspace.

- 

Member of an organization-wide group.

ART shall determine effective permissions consistently.

Removing one access path shall not remove access if another valid access
path still grants access.

#### Removing Access

Authorized users shall be able to remove a user's access to a shared
resource.

Removing access shall:

- 

Remove the applicable direct permission.

- 

Preserve other valid access paths.

- 

Immediately prevent unauthorized future access where supported.

- 

Preserve the user's existing work according to resource and
synchronization rules.

Removing a user from a Workspace shall not necessarily remove
permissions that were independently granted to standalone resources.

#### Sharing With Groups

Where supported by the provider, resources may be shared with groups.

Groups may represent:

- 

Project teams.

- 

Departments.

- 

Organizations.

- 

Custom user groups.

Group membership shall be provider-dependent.

ART shall not assume that every Collaboration Provider supports groups.

#### Organization-Wide Sharing

Where supported, authorized users may make a resource available to an
organization.

For example:

- 

Organization-wide plugin.

- 

Organization-wide Accessibility Standard package.

- 

Organization-wide template.

Organization-wide sharing shall require explicit authorization.

It shall not be available merely because a user owns the resource.

#### Invitation Model

When a resource is shared with a user who does not currently have
access, ART may create an invitation.

An invitation shall identify:

- 

Resource.

- 

Inviting user.

- 

Intended recipient.

- 

Permissions being offered.

- 

Date issued.

- 

Expiration, where applicable.

- 

Invitation status.

Possible invitation states include:

- 

Pending

- 

Accepted

- 

Declined

- 

Expired

- 

Revoked

#### Invitation Acceptance

When a user accepts an invitation:

- 

The applicable permissions shall be granted.

- 

The invitation shall become accepted.

- 

The user shall be able to access the resource.

- 

The event shall be recorded where appropriate.

Acceptance shall not grant permissions beyond those included in the
invitation.

#### Invitation Decline

Users shall be able to decline an invitation.

Declining an invitation shall not alter the resource.

The inviter may be informed that the invitation was declined according
to notification settings.

#### Invitation Expiration

Providers may support invitation expiration.

If an invitation expires:

- 

It shall no longer grant access.

- 

The resource shall remain unchanged.

- 

The authorized owner may issue a new invitation.

#### Revoking Invitations

Authorized users shall be able to revoke pending invitations.

A revoked invitation shall no longer grant access if subsequently
accepted.

#### Sharing Notifications

Sharing events may generate notifications through the existing
notification framework.

Examples include:

- 

You were invited to a Workspace.

- 

You were given access to a Report.

- 

Your permissions changed.

- 

Your access was removed.

- 

A resource was shared with you.

Notifications shall respect user settings.

#### Notification Accessibility

Sharing notifications shall:

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Be screen-reader accessible.

- 

Clearly identify the resource.

- 

Clearly identify the action.

- 

Provide an accessible method for viewing or responding to the
invitation.

Notifications shall not repeatedly interrupt users while they are
working.

#### Sharing UI

Sharing commands shall not create unnecessary persistent UI clutter.

Sharing actions shall be available through:

- 

Collaboration menu.

- 

Context menus.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Command Palette.

- 

Global context menu when Collaboration is enabled.

- 

Optional Collaboration Toolbar.

A persistent Share button shall not be added to every resource unless
there is a strong usability reason.

#### Share Dialog

If a Share dialog is implemented, it shall provide:

- 

Accessible name.

- 

Clear heading structure.

- 

Current sharing status.

- 

Current users/groups with access.

- 

Effective permissions.

- 

Controls for adding users.

- 

Controls for modifying permissions.

- 

Controls for removing access.

- 

Invitation status where applicable.

The dialog shall be fully keyboard accessible.

#### Focus Management

When a Share dialog or invitation interface opens:

- 

Focus shall move to the first meaningful control.

- 

Focus shall remain appropriately contained if modal.

- 

Escape shall close the interface where appropriate.

- 

Closing the interface shall restore focus to the invoking control.

Focus shall not move to the top of the page.

#### Sharing User Search

When users are selected for sharing, ART may provide user
search/autocomplete.

The user-search interface shall:

- 

Support keyboard navigation.

- 

Support screen readers.

- 

Clearly identify each result.

- 

Avoid exposing unauthorized user information.

- 

Handle duplicate display names appropriately.

- 

Provide sufficient information to distinguish users when necessary.

#### Sharing Search Accessibility

Dynamic user-search results shall not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader
users.

The screen reader should receive an appropriate announcement when
results become available, while individual users can be navigated using
keyboard focus.

The implementation shall follow the same non-interruptive autocomplete
principles established elsewhere in ART.

#### Resource Discovery

The Collaboration Framework shall provide a foundation for discovering
resources that the current user has permission to access.

Discovery may include:

- 

Shared with Me.

- 

My Shared Resources.

- 

Project Workspaces.

- 

Organization Resources.

- 

Recent Collaborative Resources.

- 

Pending Invitations.

The exact discovery categories may be refined during implementation.

#### Shared With Me

ART should provide a way for users to discover resources shared directly
with them.

Examples include:

- 

Reports.

- 

Workspaces.

- 

Plugins.

- 

Accessibility Standard packages.

- 

Templates.

The user shall only see resources they are authorized to discover.

#### My Shared Resources

Users should be able to identify resources they have shared with others.

For example:

    My Shared Resources

    Reports
    - Audit Report 2026

    Plugins
    - Contrast Review Plugin

    Accessibility Standards
    - Internal WCAG Extensions

The interface should provide access to sharing management where the user
has appropriate permissions.

#### Workspace Resource Discovery

When a user has access to a Project Workspace, ART shall provide an
accessible way to discover the resources available within the Workspace.

Discovery shall respect:

- 

Resource permissions.

- 

Hidden/private resources.

- 

Provider capabilities.

- 

Workspace policies.

A user shall not infer that a resource exists merely because they lack
access to it.

#### Search

The Collaboration Framework shall provide a foundation for searching
shared resources.

Search may eventually support:

- 

Resource name.

- 

Resource type.

- 

Owner.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Shared-by user.

- 

Last modified date.

- 

Permission level.

- 

Tags or metadata where supported.

The initial implementation may provide a limited search capability.

The architecture shall support expanding search later.

#### Resource Links

Where supported, ART may provide links that allow users to navigate
directly to shared resources.

A shared-resource link shall not bypass authorization.

When the user opens a resource link:

1.  

ART verifies access.

2.  

If authorized, the resource opens.

3.  

If unauthorized, ART displays an accessible explanation.

4.  

No restricted resource content is exposed.

#### Invalid or Expired Links

If a shared-resource link is no longer valid, ART shall provide a
meaningful explanation.

Possible causes include:

- 

Resource deleted.

- 

Access revoked.

- 

Invitation expired.

- 

Resource moved.

- 

Provider unavailable.

The interface shall not expose unnecessary technical information.

#### Sharing Across Providers

The framework shall not assume that a resource shared through one
provider can automatically be shared through another provider.

Provider capabilities shall determine whether cross-provider sharing is
supported.

If cross-provider sharing is unavailable, ART shall clearly communicate
the limitation.

#### Exported Resources

Sharing permissions shall not automatically be embedded into exported
report files unless the export format explicitly supports appropriate
access-control metadata.

Exporting a report shall not accidentally expose collaboration
permissions, user credentials, or private collaboration metadata.

#### Offline Sharing

If a user attempts to share a resource while offline:

- 

ART shall determine whether the provider supports queued sharing
operations.

- 

If supported, the operation may be queued.

- 

If unsupported, the user shall receive an accessible explanation.

- 

The local resource shall remain intact.

ART shall not falsely indicate that sharing has completed when the
operation has not reached the provider.

#### Sharing Audit History

Where collaboration audit history is enabled, ART shall record
appropriate sharing events.

Possible events include:

- 

Resource shared.

- 

User invited.

- 

Invitation accepted.

- 

Invitation declined.

- 

Invitation revoked.

- 

Permission granted.

- 

Permission modified.

- 

Permission removed.

- 

Ownership transferred.

- 

Resource unshared.

Audit information shall respect applicable permissions and privacy
requirements.

#### Security

Sharing functionality shall not expose:

- 

Authentication credentials.

- 

Private provider configuration.

- 

Hidden resource metadata.

- 

Unauthorized user information.

- 

Private comments.

- 

Restricted report content.

All sharing operations shall use the centralized authorization
framework.

#### Accessibility Requirements

All sharing and discovery functionality shall support:

- 

Keyboard-only operation.

- 

Screen readers.

- 

Refreshable braille.

- 

Speech recognition.

- 

Voice control.

- 

Switch access.

Users shall be able to determine:

- 

What resource is being shared.

- 

Who has access.

- 

What permissions are granted.

- 

Whether access is inherited.

- 

Whether access is direct.

- 

Who owns the resource.

- 

Whether an invitation is pending.

- 

Whether an invitation has expired.

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  

Standalone resources can be shared independently of Project Workspaces
where supported.

2.  

Project Workspaces can be shared as collaborative containers.

3.  

Individual resources within a Workspace can have separate sharing rules
where permitted.

4.  

Sharing does not automatically transfer ownership.

5.  

Ownership transfer is a separate authorized operation.

6.  

Users cannot grant permissions they are not authorized to delegate.

7.  

Direct permissions and inherited permissions are distinguishable.

8.  

Effective permissions are calculated consistently.

9.  

Removing one access path does not incorrectly remove another valid
access path.

10. 

Personal resources remain private unless explicitly shared.

11. 

Plugins can be shared without automatically transferring ownership.

12. 

Accessibility Standard packages use the same sharing architecture.

13. 

Permission Profiles can be used during sharing where appropriate.

14. 

Invitations have identifiable states.

15. 

Invitations can be accepted, declined, revoked, and expired where
supported.

16. 

Invitation acceptance grants only the permissions offered.

17. 

Sharing notifications use the existing notification framework.

18. 

Sharing notifications do not unnecessarily interrupt screen-reader
users.

19. 

Share dialogs are fully accessible.

20. 

Focus is restored correctly when sharing interfaces are closed.

21. 

User-search/autocomplete functionality is keyboard and screen-reader
accessible.

22. 

Dynamic user-search results do not continuously interrupt screen-reader
users.

23. 

Shared resources can be discovered without exposing unauthorized
resources.

24. 

Resource links never bypass authorization.

25. 

Invalid or expired links provide meaningful accessible feedback.

26. 

Offline sharing does not falsely report successful completion.

27. 

Sharing events are recorded in audit history where enabled.

28. 

Sharing commands are available through the established Collaboration
command surfaces.

29. 

Sharing functionality does not introduce unnecessary persistent UI
clutter.

30. 

Existing local-only ART functionality remains fully operational when
Collaboration is disabled.

31. 

The sharing architecture remains extensible for future organization-wide
collaboration and enterprise resource discovery.

### Part 9: Collaboration Analytics, Activity History, and Auditability

#### Overview

Implement the analytics, activity-history, and auditability foundation
for the ART Collaboration Framework.

The purpose of this functionality is to help authorized users
understand:

- What collaboration activity is occurring.
- Who is participating.
- How resources are being used.
- What changes have occurred.
- What sharing and permission changes have occurred.
- What synchronization events have occurred.
- What collaboration-related problems require attention.

This functionality shall complement ART's existing Analytics
capabilities rather than creating a separate analytics system.

#### Integration With Existing Analytics

Use ART's existing **Analytics** architecture and Analytics tab wherever
possible.

Do not create a separate permanent Collaboration Analytics dashboard if
the existing Analytics tab can accommodate the information.

Collaboration analytics shall be available as an optional Analytics
section.

Analytics shall respect:

- User permissions.
- Workspace permissions.
- Report permissions.
- Organization policies.
- Privacy settings.
- Provider capabilities.

Users shall never receive analytics about resources they are not
authorized to access.

#### Analytics Categories

Collaboration analytics may include sections such as:

- Collaboration Overview
- Workspace Activity
- Report Activity
- User Activity
- Sharing and Permissions
- Comments and Reviews
- Synchronization
- Conflicts
- Resource Usage
- Version History
- Working View Usage
- Plugin Usage
- Accessibility Standard Package Usage

The exact categories may be refined during implementation.

#### Collapsed Analytics Sections

To minimize UI clutter, collaboration analytics sections shall be
collapsed by default.

Each analytics section shall have:

- An accessible heading.
- A button or equivalent disclosure control.
- An expanded/collapsed state.
- Appropriate programmatic state information.

Users shall be able to expand only the sections they want to review.

The implementation shall not display every analytics section expanded
simultaneously by default.

#### Analytics Settings

Application Settings shall provide options allowing users or authorized
administrators to control which collaboration analytics sections are
displayed.

Settings may include options such as:

- Show Collaboration Overview.
- Show Workspace Activity.
- Show User Activity.
- Show Sharing and Permissions.
- Show Comments and Reviews.
- Show Synchronization.
- Show Conflicts.
- Show Resource Usage.
- Show Version History.

The exact settings may be refined during implementation.

Settings shall not override permissions.

A user shall never be able to enable an analytics section and thereby
gain access to information they are not authorized to see.

#### Collaboration Overview

The Collaboration Overview section may provide high-level metrics such
as:

- Number of active collaborators.
- Number of shared resources.
- Number of shared reports.
- Number of shared Workspaces.
- Number of pending invitations.
- Number of unresolved collaboration conflicts.
- Number of pending synchronization operations.
- Number of recent collaboration events.

The section should provide a concise overview rather than duplicating
every detailed metric.

#### Workspace Activity Analytics

For Project Workspaces, authorized users may view metrics such as:

- Number of active collaborators.
- Number of reports.
- Number of shared resources.
- Number of report edits.
- Number of comments.
- Number of unresolved comments.
- Number of Working Views.
- Number of shared Working Views.
- Number of plugins.
- Number of Accessibility Standard packages.
- Number of invitations.
- Number of permission changes.
- Number of synchronization events.
- Number of conflicts.

Metrics shall be calculated only from information the current user is
authorized to access.

#### Report Activity Analytics

For reports, authorized users may view metrics such as:

- Number of collaborators.
- Number of edits.
- Number of comments.
- Number of unresolved comments.
- Number of resolved comments.
- Number of revisions.
- Number of synchronization events.
- Number of conflicts.
- Number of shares.
- Number of permission changes.
- Most recent modification.
- Most recent modifying user.

Where appropriate, analytics should distinguish between local changes
and synchronized collaborative changes.

#### User Activity

Where permitted, authorized users may view collaboration activity
associated with users.

Possible metrics include:

- Number of reports edited.
- Number of comments created.
- Number of comments resolved.
- Number of resources shared.
- Number of Working Views created.
- Number of plugins created.
- Number of Accessibility Standard packages created.
- Number of synchronization events.
- Number of conflicts resolved.

User activity analytics shall not be used to expose unnecessary personal
information.

#### Sharing and Permission Analytics

Authorized users may view metrics such as:

- Number of shared resources.
- Number of users with access.
- Number of Workspace members.
- Number of direct permissions.
- Number of inherited permissions.
- Number of permission changes.
- Number of invitations.
- Number of accepted invitations.
- Number of declined invitations.
- Number of revoked invitations.
- Number of expired invitations.

Where useful, analytics may identify resources with unusually broad
sharing.

#### Comments and Review Analytics

Where commenting is enabled, analytics may include:

- Total comments.
- Unresolved comments.
- Resolved comments.
- Comments by resource.
- Comments by report.
- Comments by user.
- Average time to resolution where appropriate.
- Number of reopened comments.
- Number of active review discussions.

Do not expose comment content merely because analytics are enabled.

Analytics should provide metrics and summaries unless the user
explicitly navigates to the underlying comment.

#### Synchronization Analytics

The Synchronization section may include:

- Successful synchronization operations.
- Pending synchronization operations.
- Failed synchronization operations.
- Synchronization conflicts.
- Offline changes awaiting synchronization.
- Provider availability.
- Most recent successful synchronization.
- Most recent synchronization failure.

The interface should distinguish between:

- Temporary synchronization delays.
- Persistent synchronization errors.
- Conflicts requiring user intervention.

#### Conflict Analytics

Authorized users may view:

- Number of active conflicts.
- Number of resolved conflicts.
- Number of conflicts by resource type.
- Number of conflicts by report.
- Number of conflicts by Workspace.
- Most recent conflicts.
- Conflict resolution status.

Conflict analytics shall provide navigation to the relevant resource or
conflict-resolution interface when the user has permission to access it.

#### Version History Analytics

Where version history is supported, analytics may include:

- Number of revisions.
- Number of contributors.
- Revision frequency.
- Most recent revision.
- Number of restored revisions.
- Number of conflicting revisions.

Analytics shall not replace the detailed version-history interface.

#### Working View Analytics

Working View analytics shall respect the distinction between personal
and shared Working Views.

Metrics may include:

- Number of personal Working Views.
- Number of shared Working Views.
- Number of users using shared Working Views.
- Number of Working Views created.
- Number of Working Views modified.
- Most frequently used shared Working Views.

Personal Working View information shall not be exposed to other users
unless explicitly permitted.

#### Plugin Analytics

Where supported, plugin analytics may include:

- Number of personal plugins.
- Number of shared plugins.
- Number of Workspace plugins.
- Number of organization-wide plugins.
- Plugin usage.
- Plugin installation/use counts.
- Most frequently used shared plugins.

Do not expose private plugin information to users who do not have
permission to see it.

#### Accessibility Standard Package Analytics

Where supported, analytics may include:

- Number of personal packages.
- Number of shared packages.
- Number of Workspace packages.
- Number of organization-wide packages.
- Package usage.
- Most frequently used shared packages.

Private packages shall remain private.

#### Activity History

Provide an accessible collaboration activity history.

Activity history may include events such as:

- Workspace created.
- Report created.
- Report modified.
- Report renamed.
- Report shared.
- User invited.
- User accepted invitation.
- Permission changed.
- Comment created.
- Comment resolved.
- Working View shared.
- Plugin shared.
- Accessibility Standard package shared.
- Synchronization completed.
- Synchronization failed.
- Conflict detected.
- Conflict resolved.
- Revision restored.

Each activity event should include, where applicable:

- User.
- Action.
- Resource.
- Date and time.
- Result.

#### Activity Filtering

Where supported, users may filter activity by:

- User.
- Resource.
- Resource type.
- Date range.
- Event type.
- Workspace.
- Report.

Filters shall only expose values the user is authorized to see.

#### Activity Navigation

Where appropriate, an activity event shall provide an accessible way to
navigate to the associated resource.

For example:

``` text
Jordan edited Accessibility Audit Report
```

The user should be able to navigate to the report if they have
permission to access it.

If the resource is no longer available, ART shall provide an appropriate
explanation.

#### Activity Retention

Activity history and audit records shall use configurable retention
policies where required.

Do not assume that all collaboration activity must be retained
indefinitely.

Retention policies may be controlled by:

- Application Settings.
- Workspace administrators.
- Organization administrators.
- Collaboration provider policies.

The exact retention architecture may be implemented in a future phase if
necessary.

#### Audit Log Integration

Use ART's existing Audit Log architecture wherever possible.

Do not create a separate, disconnected collaboration audit system.

Collaboration events should use the existing audit model where
compatible.

If new event types are required, extend the existing Audit Log
architecture rather than creating an independent logging system.

#### Audit Events

The collaboration audit system shall support events such as:

- Resource created.
- Resource modified.
- Resource deleted.
- Resource renamed.
- Resource shared.
- Resource unshared.
- Permission granted.
- Permission modified.
- Permission removed.
- Ownership transferred.
- Invitation created.
- Invitation accepted.
- Invitation declined.
- Invitation revoked.
- Comment created.
- Comment edited.
- Comment deleted.
- Comment resolved.
- Comment reopened.
- Synchronization completed.
- Synchronization failed.
- Conflict detected.
- Conflict resolved.
- Revision restored.

#### Audit Integrity

Audit information shall not be editable through ordinary
resource-editing interfaces.

Users shall not be able to modify audit records merely because they have
Edit permission on the associated resource.

Authorized administrators may have permission to manage retention or
export audit information according to applicable policies.

#### Audit Accessibility

Audit information shall be fully accessible.

Users shall be able to determine:

- What happened.
- Who performed the action.
- Which resource was affected.
- When it happened.
- Whether the operation succeeded.
- What result occurred.

Do not communicate audit information solely through color, icons, or
visual styling.

#### Privacy

Analytics and activity history shall follow data-minimization
principles.

Do not collect or display more user information than is necessary for
the collaboration functionality.

For example, analytics should not expose:

- Private resources.
- Private Working Views.
- Private plugins.
- Private Accessibility Standard packages.
- Authentication credentials.
- Provider secrets.
- Unnecessary personal information.

#### Organization-Level Analytics

Where supported, organization administrators may be able to view
aggregate collaboration analytics across the organization.

Organization-level analytics shall be separate from individual user
privacy settings where required by organizational policy.

The implementation shall not assume that every deployment has an
organization-level administrator.

#### Aggregate Analytics

Where possible, analytics should support aggregate information rather
than exposing individual user activity unnecessarily.

For example:

``` text
Reports edited this month: 27
Comments created: 84
Conflicts resolved: 6
Shared Workspaces: 4
```

This may be preferable to exposing detailed user-level activity when
detailed information is not needed.

#### Analytics Accuracy

Analytics shall clearly distinguish between:

- Current values.
- Historical values.
- Cached values.
- Estimated values, if any.

Do not present stale or cached information as real-time information.

Where metrics are not immediately current, ART should communicate that
appropriately.

#### Analytics Refresh

Users may be able to refresh analytics manually.

Automatic refresh may be supported where the provider permits it.

Analytics refresh shall not unnecessarily interrupt users.

Screen readers shall not repeatedly announce every updated metric.

If the displayed analytics change while the user is reviewing the page,
appropriate status information may communicate that refreshed data is
available.

#### Analytics Export

Where permitted, authorized users may be able to export collaboration
analytics.

Exported analytics shall:

- Respect permissions.
- Avoid exposing unauthorized resources.
- Identify the date/time or period represented.
- Clearly identify the Workspace or Report to which the metrics apply.

Analytics exports shall not include authentication credentials or
provider secrets.

#### Analytics and Report Exports

Collaboration analytics shall not automatically be embedded in normal
report exports.

A report export should contain report information rather than unrelated
collaboration activity.

If collaboration analytics are specifically requested as an export, they
should be generated as a separate analytics export.

#### Command Integration

Analytics-related collaboration commands shall use the established
command architecture.

Commands should be available through:

- Analytics tab.
- Collaboration menu.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Global context menu when Collaboration is enabled.
- Optional Collaboration Toolbar.

Do not add permanent analytics controls throughout the application.

#### Accessibility Requirements

All analytics and activity interfaces shall support:

- Keyboard-only operation.
- Screen readers.
- Refreshable braille displays.
- Speech recognition.
- Voice control.
- Switch access.

Collapsed analytics sections shall expose their expanded/collapsed state
programmatically.

Dynamic analytics updates shall not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader
users.

Charts and visualizations, when used, shall provide equivalent
accessible information through text, tables, or other appropriate
mechanisms.

Do not make important analytics information available only through a
visual chart.

#### Validation

Verify that:

1.  Collaboration analytics use the existing Analytics architecture.
2.  Collaboration analytics can be displayed within the existing
    Analytics tab.
3.  Analytics sections are collapsed by default.
4.  Users can expand individual analytics sections.
5.  Application Settings can control which analytics sections are
    displayed.
6.  Settings cannot bypass permissions.
7.  Workspace analytics respect Workspace permissions.
8.  Report analytics respect Report permissions.
9.  Personal Working View analytics remain private.
10. Private plugin analytics remain private.
11. Private Accessibility Standard package analytics remain private.
12. Sharing and permission analytics accurately represent effective
    access.
13. Synchronization analytics accurately represent synchronization
    state.
14. Conflict analytics accurately represent active and resolved
    conflicts.
15. Activity history integrates with the existing Audit Log
    architecture.
16. Collaboration events are recorded appropriately.
17. Audit records cannot be modified through ordinary resource-editing
    operations.
18. Activity history can be filtered where supported.
19. Activity events provide accessible navigation to associated
    resources.
20. Analytics do not expose unauthorized resources.
21. Analytics do not expose unnecessary personal information.
22. Analytics do not expose credentials or provider secrets.
23. Analytics clearly distinguish current, historical, and cached
    information.
24. Analytics refresh does not unnecessarily interrupt users.
25. Dynamic analytics updates do not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader
    users.
26. Charts and visualizations have accessible equivalents.
27. Collaboration analytics do not automatically appear in ordinary
    report exports.
28. Authorized analytics can be exported separately where supported.
29. Analytics and activity commands use the established Collaboration
    command architecture.
30. No unnecessary persistent analytics UI clutter is introduced.
31. Existing Analytics functionality continues to operate correctly.
32. Existing local-only ART functionality remains fully operational when
    Collaboration is disabled.

### Part 10: Real-Time Collaboration, Concurrent Editing, and Conflict Resolution

#### Overview

Implement the architecture required for ART to support real-time and
near-real-time collaborative editing.

The long-term goal is to provide a collaboration experience similar to
Google Docs and Google Sheets while preserving ART's accessibility-first
design, local-first capabilities, modular permissions, personal Working
Views, and provider-independent architecture.

This part establishes the foundation for multiple authorized users to
work on the same collaborative resource asynchronously or synchronously.

The implementation shall not assume that every Collaboration Provider
supports real-time editing.

#### Collaboration Modes

The Collaboration Framework shall support the following conceptual
modes:

- **Local Mode** — The user works independently without Collaboration
  enabled.
- **Asynchronous Collaboration** — Users make changes independently and
  synchronize those changes later.
- **Synchronous Collaboration** — Multiple users can work on the same
  resource concurrently with changes synchronized in near real time.
- **Offline Collaboration** — Users can continue working locally while
  disconnected and synchronize changes when connectivity is restored.

The active mode shall depend on:

- Collaboration settings.
- Resource permissions.
- Provider capabilities.
- Network state.
- Resource configuration.

#### Provider Capabilities

The Collaboration Provider shall expose whether it supports:

- Real-time synchronization.
- Concurrent editing.
- Operational Transform (OT).
- Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs).
- Field-level synchronization.
- Character-level synchronization.
- Presence.
- Comments.
- Version history.
- Offline synchronization.
- Conflict resolution.
- Transactions.
- Resource locking.

ART shall not require a provider to implement a specific synchronization
technology.

The Collaboration Framework shall operate through provider-neutral
interfaces.

#### Local-First Editing

ART shall preserve its local-first behavior.

A user's local edits shall not be lost merely because:

- The network is unavailable.
- The Collaboration Provider is unavailable.
- Another user changes the same resource.
- A synchronization operation fails.

Local changes shall remain recoverable until they are successfully
synchronized or explicitly discarded by the user.

#### Change Tracking

The Collaboration Framework shall represent changes as discrete
operations or revisions rather than relying solely on complete-resource
replacement.

A change may represent:

- Field value changed.
- Finding added.
- Finding modified.
- Finding deleted.
- Report section modified.
- Report metadata modified.
- Comment added.
- Comment modified.
- Working View modified.
- Plugin configuration modified.
- Accessibility Standard package modified.

The exact operation model shall be determined by the implementation
architecture.

#### Resource Versioning

Collaborative resources shall maintain version information sufficient to
determine whether a local copy is:

- Current.
- Behind the shared resource.
- Ahead of the shared resource.
- Synchronizing.
- Conflicted.

Version identifiers shall be provider-independent where possible.

#### Concurrent Editing

When multiple authorized users edit the same resource simultaneously,
ART shall preserve each user's valid changes.

For example:

``` text
User A → edits Finding 1
User B → edits Finding 2

Result:
Finding 1 → User A's change
Finding 2 → User B's change
```

Independent changes shall be merged automatically whenever technically
safe.

#### Same-Field Concurrent Editing

If two users edit the same field concurrently, the Collaboration
Framework shall determine whether the changes can be merged safely.

If they cannot be merged automatically, ART shall identify a conflict
rather than silently overwriting one user's work.

For example:

    User A:
    Severity = High

    User B:
    Severity = Critical

ART shall not arbitrarily discard one value without applying an
explicitly defined conflict-resolution rule.

#### Text Editing

For text fields and textareas, the architecture should support
increasingly granular synchronization in future implementations.

Possible synchronization levels include:

- 

Whole-field.

- 

Paragraph.

- 

Text range.

- 

Character/operation level.

Where provider capabilities support true concurrent text editing, ART
should allow users to work simultaneously without unnecessarily locking
the entire field.

#### Rich Text Editing

Where ART supports rich-text editing, collaboration shall preserve:

- 

Text.

- 

Formatting.

- 

Links.

- 

Lists.

- 

Headings.

- 

Tables.

- 

Images.

- 

Semantics.

- 

Accessibility metadata.

Collaborative synchronization shall not strip or corrupt semantic or
accessibility information.

#### Report Structure Changes

The framework shall support concurrent structural changes such as:

- 

Adding a report field.

- 

Removing a report field.

- 

Reordering fields.

- 

Adding a finding.

- 

Removing a finding.

- 

Reordering findings.

- 

Adding a report section.

- 

Renaming a section.

Structural changes shall use deterministic synchronization rules.

#### Concurrent Additions

If two users add different resources at approximately the same time,
both additions shall be preserved.

For example:

    User A → adds Finding 12
    User B → adds Finding 13

    Result:
    Finding 12
    Finding 13

The system shall not treat independent additions as conflicts merely
because they occurred concurrently.

#### Concurrent Deletions

If two users delete the same resource concurrently, ART shall treat the
operation deterministically.

The framework shall avoid generating unnecessary conflicts when both
users are attempting the same logical operation.

#### Delete/Edit Conflicts

If one user deletes a resource while another user edits that resource,
ART shall identify the conflict when the operations cannot be safely
reconciled.

The user shall be given enough information to understand:

- 

What was deleted.

- 

What was changed.

- 

Who made the change.

- 

Which version contains the edit.

- 

What options are available.

#### Reordering Conflicts

If multiple users reorder the same collection concurrently, the
Collaboration Framework shall apply deterministic ordering rules.

The implementation shall avoid silently losing items.

If a deterministic merge cannot be performed safely, ART shall provide
an accessible conflict-resolution interface.

#### Synchronization Queue

Offline or temporarily disconnected changes shall be maintained in a
synchronization queue.

Each pending operation should have sufficient information to determine:

- 

Resource.

- 

Operation.

- 

Local state.

- 

Synchronization status.

- 

Error state.

- 

Retry state.

The queue shall survive appropriate application or browser lifecycle
events.

#### Synchronization States

Individual resources may have states such as:

- 

Synchronized.

- 

Saving.

- 

Synchronizing.

- 

Pending.

- 

Offline.

- 

Conflict.

- 

Error.

These states shall be distinguishable from the overall Collaboration
Session state.

#### Synchronization Indicators

If synchronization status is displayed visually, it shall also be
available programmatically.

Do not rely solely on:

- 

Color.

- 

Icons.

- 

Animation.

For example:

    Report Status: Changes saved

or:

    Report Status: Changes pending synchronization

#### Screen Reader Behavior

Synchronization updates shall not continuously interrupt users.

For example, ART should not announce:

> 

Saving.

> 

Saved.

> 

Synchronizing.

> 

Synchronized.

> 

Saving.

> 

Saved.

for every individual edit while a user is typing.

Instead, ART should use an appropriate accessible status mechanism that
provides meaningful information without disrupting the user's work.

Critical synchronization errors may be announced when appropriate.

#### Typing and Editing

Collaboration synchronization shall never interfere with keyboard input.

While the user is typing:

- 

The insertion point shall remain stable.

- 

Focus shall remain in the active field.

- 

Remote changes shall not unexpectedly steal focus.

- 

Screen readers shall not be repeatedly interrupted.

- 

Autocomplete behavior shall remain independent from collaboration
updates.

Remote synchronization shall occur without disrupting the user's local
editing experience whenever possible.

#### Remote Changes

When another user changes a resource currently being viewed, ART shall
update the local interface when technically safe.

The update shall not:

- 

Move focus unexpectedly.

- 

Move the user's insertion point unexpectedly.

- 

Scroll the page unexpectedly.

- 

Close an active dialog.

- 

Replace text the user is currently editing without an appropriate
synchronization strategy.

#### Remote Changes to the Current Field

If another user changes the same field that the current user is actively
editing, ART shall apply the provider's supported concurrent-editing
strategy.

Possible strategies include:

- 

Real-time merge.

- 

Operational transformation.

- 

CRDT-based merge.

- 

Temporary field locking.

- 

Conflict notification.

The implementation shall not silently overwrite the user's active input.
