------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Working View Bookmarks

A user shall be able to Bookmark a location within a shared Working View
if they have access.

The Bookmark remains personal unless explicitly shared.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Viewer Bookmarks

Users with Viewer permissions shall be able to create personal Bookmarks
to locations they can view.

Creating a Bookmark must not grant editing permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorite and Bookmark Relationship

A resource may be both:

- 

Favorited.

- 

Bookmarked.

These are separate concepts.

For example:

    Favorite:
    Accessibility Audit Report

    Bookmarks:
    Missing Form Label
    Keyboard Trap Finding
    Analytics — Findings by Severity

Do not automatically create a Bookmark when an item is Favorited.

Do not automatically Favorite an item when a Bookmark is created.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Open Favorites

Provide an **Open Favorites** command.

It shall provide an accessible list of the user's Favorite resources.

The list shall support:

- 

Keyboard navigation.

- 

Screen readers.

- 

Mouse.

- 

Voice input where supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Open Bookmarks

Provide an **Open Bookmarks** command.

It shall provide an accessible list of the user's Bookmarks.

The list shall support:

- 

Keyboard navigation.

- 

Screen readers.

- 

Mouse.

- 

Voice input where supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites and Bookmarks in Command Palette

The Command Palette shall be able to search for and open:

- 

Favorite resources.

- 

Bookmarks.

The Command Palette should allow users to quickly reach these items
without adding additional persistent UI.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites and Bookmarks in Menu Bar

Provide access through appropriate existing menu structures.

Do not create unnecessary top-level menus.

If a dedicated menu already exists for navigation, use the existing
structure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites and Bookmarks in Context Menus

Where contextually appropriate, provide:

    Add to Favorites
    Remove from Favorites
    Bookmark This Location
    Remove Bookmark

Do not display actions that are not applicable to the current object.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites and Bookmarks in Global Context Menu

If the Global Context Menu is enabled, appropriate Favorite and Bookmark
commands shall be available.

The commands must respect:

- 

Current context.

- 

Permissions.

- 

Object type.

- 

User preferences.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Management

Opening Favorites or Bookmarks shall follow ART's existing
focus-management requirements.

When an interface opens:

- 

Focus shall move to the first meaningful interactive control.

- 

Focus shall not move to the top of the page.

When the interface closes:

- 

Focus shall return to the control or location that opened it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Escape Behavior

Pressing Escape from Favorites or Bookmarks shall:

- 

Close the interface when appropriate.

- 

Cancel the current operation.

- 

Return focus to the originating location.

Do not move focus to the top of the page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Accessibility

Favorites and Bookmarks must be fully accessible to screen readers.

Screen readers shall be able to determine:

- 

Resource name.

- 

Resource type.

- 

Context.

- 

Favorite state.

- 

Bookmark state.

- 

Shared/personal state where applicable.

- 

Availability.

- 

Current selection.

Do not expose unnecessary implementation details.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dynamic Updates

When Favorites or Bookmarks change:

- 

Update the interface without stealing focus.

- 

Do not repeatedly announce the entire list.

- 

Announce meaningful changes when appropriate.

For example:

    Added to Favorites.

or:

    Bookmark removed.

Do not announce every list update as the user navigates.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorite/Bookmark Suggestions

Where Favorites or Bookmarks are displayed as suggestions:

- 

Suggestions may update automatically.

- 

Updates should occur quietly.

- 

Focus must not be stolen.

- 

Individual suggestions shall be announced when they receive programmatic
focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Navigation

Favorites and Bookmarks shall support predictable keyboard navigation.

At minimum:

- 

Tab moves through interactive controls.

- 

Arrow keys navigate listbox-style result collections where appropriate.

- 

Enter activates the selected item.

- 

Escape closes the interface or cancels the current interaction.

- 

Home/End may navigate to the first/last item where appropriate.

Do not create conflicting keyboard behaviors.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus After Activation

When a Favorite or Bookmark is activated:

- 

Navigate to its target.

- 

Move focus to the target when appropriate.

- 

Preserve the user's ability to determine where they landed.

Do not simply open a containing page and leave focus at an unrelated
location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Restoration After Cancellation

If the user opens Favorites or Bookmarks and cancels without selecting
anything:

- 

Close the interface.

- 

Return focus to the original location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stale Navigation Targets

If a Bookmark target becomes unavailable:

- 

Identify the Bookmark as unavailable.

- 

Explain the reason where known.

- 

Allow the user to remove it.

- 

Do not generate an application error.

- 

Do not navigate to an unrelated target.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Changes

If permissions change after a Bookmark or Favorite was created:

- 

Revalidate access when the item is opened.

- 

Prevent unauthorized navigation.

- 

Do not reveal protected content.

- 

Provide an appropriate message.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Offline Support

Personal Favorites and Bookmarks shall work with locally available
content while ART is offline.

If a target requires unavailable synchronized content:

- 

Clearly communicate that the target is unavailable offline.

- 

Preserve the Bookmark/Favorite.

- 

Allow the user to retry later.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Local-First Storage

Personal Favorites and Bookmarks should be compatible with ART's
local-first architecture.

They should not require an online account merely to use personal
Favorites or Bookmarks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration Synchronization

When Collaboration is enabled, explicitly shared Favorites or Bookmarks
may be synchronized according to the Collaboration Framework.

Personal Favorites and Bookmarks must remain personal unless the user
explicitly shares them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Backup and Export

Where ART supports project/report data export or backup, determine
whether Favorites and Bookmarks are included.

If included:

- 

Preserve stable references.

- 

Preserve personal/shared status where applicable.

- 

Do not expose private information to unauthorized users.

If not included, clearly document that Favorites and Bookmarks are
application-local navigation metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Settings

Application Settings should provide appropriate configuration options
for Favorites and Bookmarks.

Potential settings include:

- 

Enable Favorites.

- 

Enable Bookmarks.

- 

Maximum Recent/Favorite display counts where applicable.

- 

Default Favorite ordering.

- 

Default Bookmark ordering.

- 

Show Favorites in Quick Open.

- 

Show Bookmarks in Quick Open.

- 

Clear personal navigation data.

- 

Synchronization options when Collaboration is enabled.

Only expose settings that provide meaningful user control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No UI Clutter

Favorites and Bookmarks shall follow ART's existing requirement to
minimize persistent UI clutter.

Do not add large permanent Favorite or Bookmark panels to every screen.

Primary access should be through:

- 

Menu bar.

- 

Menus.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Command Palette.

- 

Context menus.

- 

Existing navigation interfaces.

Optional toolbar controls may be considered only where consistent with
ART's existing customizable toolbar architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Consistency

All Favorite and Bookmark actions shall use shared underlying
commands/actions.

For example:

    Menu → Add to Favorites
    Command Palette → Add to Favorites
    Context Menu → Add to Favorites
    Keyboard Shortcut → Add to Favorites

All must execute the same underlying operation.

Do not duplicate logic between interfaces.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Error Handling

If a Favorite or Bookmark cannot be created:

- 

Explain the problem.

- 

Preserve the current application state.

- 

Do not move focus unexpectedly.

If a Favorite or Bookmark cannot be opened:

- 

Explain why.

- 

Preserve the current application state.

- 

Keep the user's navigation location stable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Performance

Favorites and Bookmarks should remain responsive even when the user has:

- 

Hundreds of Favorites.

- 

Hundreds of Bookmarks.

- 

Large Reports.

- 

Large Workspaces.

- 

Large numbers of Findings.

Do not block the main application interface during normal Favorite or
Bookmark operations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Acceptance Criteria

Part 3 shall be considered complete when:

1.  

Favorites are implemented using the unified Search & Navigation
architecture.

2.  

Users can Favorite authorized ART resources.

3.  

Favorites are personal by default.

4.  

Personal Favorites are not automatically shared.

5.  

Favorite state is accessible to screen readers.

6.  

Users can add and remove Favorites.

7.  

Users can search Favorites.

8.  

Favorites integrate with Quick Open.

9.  

Favorites integrate with Command Search.

10. 

Favorites integrate with the Command Palette.

11. 

Favorites integrate with appropriate menu structures.

12. 

Favorites integrate with appropriate context menus.

13. 

Favorites respect permissions.

14. 

Deleted resources do not remain active Favorite targets.

15. 

Renamed resources remain valid Favorite targets.

16. 

Favorites work with Reports.

17. 

Favorites work with Project Workspaces.

18. 

Favorites work with Working Views.

19. 

Favorites work with personal Working Views.

20. 

Favorites work with shared Working Views.

21. 

Viewer users can Favorite resources without gaining additional
permissions.

22. 

Users can Favorite applicable Accessibility Standards and WCAG Success
Criteria.

23. 

WCAG Favorites preserve the criterion identifier, name, conformance
level, and applicable version.

24. 

Bookmarks are implemented separately from Favorites while using the same
underlying navigation architecture.

25. 

Users can Bookmark specific navigable locations.

26. 

Bookmarks use stable internal navigation targets.

27. 

Bookmarks remain valid when surrounding content moves.

28. 

Bookmarks resolve renamed resources correctly.

29. 

Deleted Bookmark targets are handled gracefully.

30. 

Users can name and manage Bookmarks.

31. 

Users can search Bookmarks.

32. 

Users can organize Bookmarks where supported.

33. 

Personal Bookmarks remain personal by default.

34. 

Shared Bookmarks are explicitly shared and permission-controlled.

35. 

Viewer users can create personal Bookmarks without gaining additional
permissions.

36. 

Favorites and Bookmarks remain separate concepts.

37. 

Creating a Favorite does not automatically create a Bookmark.

38. 

Creating a Bookmark does not automatically create a Favorite.

39. 

Favorites and Bookmarks are accessible to screen readers.

40. 

Favorites and Bookmarks are fully keyboard accessible.

41. 

Escape closes Favorite/Bookmark interfaces and restores focus correctly.

42. 

Activating a Favorite or Bookmark navigates to the exact intended
destination.

43. 

Focus moves to the appropriate destination after navigation.

44. 

Search/list updates do not steal focus.

45. 

Dynamic updates do not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader users.

46. 

Individual Favorite and Bookmark items are announced when they receive
programmatic keyboard focus.

47. 

Permission changes are revalidated before navigation.

48. 

Personal Favorites and Bookmarks are compatible with ART's local-first
architecture.

49. 

Collaboration synchronization does not automatically expose personal
navigation data.

50. 

Offline behavior is handled appropriately.

51. 

Favorite and Bookmark commands use the existing ART command
architecture.

52. 

Favorite and Bookmark functionality does not introduce unnecessary
persistent UI clutter.

53. 

Navigation operations preserve unsaved Report changes according to
existing ART behavior.

54. 

JAWS and keyboard-only workflows are verified.

55. 

The implementation provides the foundation for Part 4's advanced search,
filtering, sorting, and search-result refinement.

### Part 4 — Advanced Search, Filtering, Sorting, and Search Result Refinement

#### Overview

Implement the **Advanced Search, Filtering, Sorting, and Search Result
Refinement** capabilities of the Search & Navigation Framework.

These capabilities shall allow users to move beyond simple keyword
searches and efficiently locate specific ART resources, reports,
findings, accessibility standards, project content, and other searchable
information.

This part shall build on the unified Search Service, Quick Open
functionality, Favorites, Bookmarks, and saved navigation capabilities
established in Parts 1–3.

Do not create a separate search architecture for advanced search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Advanced Search

Provide an Advanced Search capability for users who need to locate
information using multiple criteria.

Advanced Search shall support applicable combinations of:

- Keywords.
- Resource type.
- Project Workspace.
- Report.
- Working View.
- Accessibility standard.
- WCAG version.
- WCAG conformance level.
- Finding status.
- Finding severity.
- Issue type.
- Page/screen/component.
- Date.
- Author/creator where applicable.
- Owner where applicable.
- Last modified date.
- Tags.
- Favorites.
- Shared/personal status.
- Other searchable ART metadata.

Only criteria applicable to the selected search scope should be
presented.

Do not overwhelm users with every possible filter by default.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Scope

Advanced Search shall clearly identify the current search scope.

Possible scopes include:

- Current Report.
- Current Working View.
- Current Project Workspace.
- My Reports.
- My Workspaces.
- Shared Reports.
- All Accessible ART Content.

The available scopes shall depend on the user's permissions and current
context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Scope Persistence

When a user performs an Advanced Search:

- Preserve the selected scope while refining the search.
- Preserve the scope when changing filters.
- Preserve the scope when changing sorting.
- Preserve the scope when navigating between result pages or result
  states.

Do not unexpectedly reset the scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Contextual Filtering

Filters shall adapt to the current context.

For example:

If the user is searching within a specific Report, filters should be
relevant to that Report.

If the user is searching within a Project Workspace, Workspace-related
filtering options should be available.

If the user is searching WCAG Success Criteria, WCAG-specific filters
should be available.

Do not display irrelevant filters merely because they exist elsewhere in
ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter Categories

Organize advanced filters into logical categories.

Potential categories include:

- Content.
- Location.
- Accessibility.
- Findings.
- Status.
- Ownership.
- Collaboration.
- Dates.
- Resource Type.

Use progressive disclosure where appropriate.

Do not display a large collection of filters expanded by default.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collapsible Filter Sections

Filter categories should be collapsible.

Each category shall:

- Have a clear heading or accessible button.
- Be collapsed by default where appropriate.
- Expand when activated.
- Preserve its expanded/collapsed state while the search remains active.
- Be keyboard accessible.
- Be accessible to screen readers.

The interface should minimize visual clutter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter Controls

Filter controls shall use appropriate native or accessible controls.

Examples include:

- Checkboxes for multiple selections.
- Radio buttons for mutually exclusive choices.
- Comboboxes for searchable selections.
- Date inputs for date ranges.
- Text fields for keyword filtering.
- Range controls where appropriate.

Do not use a custom control when a standard accessible control is
sufficient.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multiple Filter Selection

Users shall be able to combine multiple filters.

For example:

``` text
Project Workspace: City Website
Report: Accessibility Audit
Severity: High
Status: Failed
Issue Type: Missing Form Label
```

The search results shall reflect all active criteria.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter Logic

Clearly define how multiple filter values interact.

Within a single filter category, multiple selected values should
generally use **OR** logic where appropriate.

For example:

``` text
Severity:
☑ High
☑ Critical
```

means:

``` text
High OR Critical
```

Across different filter categories, filters should generally use **AND**
logic.

For example:

``` text
Severity: High
Status: Failed
```

means:

``` text
High AND Failed
```

Use behavior consistent with common search conventions unless a specific
ART requirement dictates otherwise.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Active Filters

Clearly display active filters.

For example:

``` text
Filters:
[High ×] [Failed ×] [WCAG 2.2 ×]
```

Users shall be able to remove individual filters without resetting the
entire search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Clear Filters

Provide an accessible **Clear Filters** command.

Clear Filters shall:

- Remove active filters.
- Preserve the user's search scope unless explicitly requested
  otherwise.
- Preserve the keyword search where appropriate.
- Update results immediately.

Provide a separate **Clear All** operation only if necessary.

Do not make users repeatedly remove filters individually to return to an
unfiltered search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter Changes

When a filter changes:

- Update results appropriately.
- Do not unexpectedly move focus.
- Do not steal keyboard focus.
- Preserve the user's current context.

If results update dynamically, updates should occur without interrupting
screen-reader users unnecessarily.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Behavior

Advanced Search must be fully accessible to screen readers.

Screen readers shall be able to determine:

- Search scope.
- Search query.
- Available filters.
- Selected filters.
- Number of matching results where available.
- Result position.
- Result name.
- Result type.
- Relevant context.
- Sort order.

Do not repeatedly announce the entire search interface whenever a filter
changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter Result Announcements

When filters are changed dynamically, screen readers should receive a
concise update when useful.

For example:

``` text
24 results found.
```

Do not announce every individual result as the result set changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Results

Search results shall provide enough information for users to determine
whether a result is relevant.

Each result should expose, where applicable:

- Resource name.
- Resource type.
- Workspace.
- Report.
- Working View.
- Finding status.
- Severity.
- Issue type.
- Date.
- Owner/creator.
- Shared/personal status.

Do not expose unnecessary metadata that creates noise.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Result Grouping

Results may be grouped by resource type where this improves usability.

For example:

``` text
Reports
    Accessibility Audit
    Usability Review

Findings
    Missing Form Label
    Low Contrast

Working Views
    QA Review
    Management View
```

Grouping shall be optional or contextually appropriate.

Do not create excessive nesting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Result Type Identification

Every result shall expose its resource type.

For example:

``` text
Accessibility Audit — Report
```

rather than:

``` text
Accessibility Audit
```

when the resource type is otherwise ambiguous.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Context

Where multiple objects have the same name, include additional context.

For example:

``` text
Accessibility Audit
Report
City Website Workspace
```

This information shall be available visually and programmatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Result Ranking

Search results shall be ranked according to relevance.

Ranking should consider factors such as:

- Exact name match.
- Exact phrase match.
- Keyword match.
- Resource type.
- Current scope.
- Recently accessed status.
- Favorite status.
- Search context.
- Metadata relevance.

Do not allow Favorites or Recent Items to overwhelm exact or highly
relevant matches.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Exact Match Priority

Exact matches should generally rank above partial matches.

For example, searching:

``` text
Accessibility Audit
```

should prioritize a Report named exactly:

``` text
Accessibility Audit
```

over a Report named:

``` text
City Website Accessibility Audit Results
```

unless other relevance factors clearly justify a different ranking.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Prefix and Partial Matching

Search should support partial matching where appropriate.

For example:

``` text
access
```

may match:

- Accessibility Audit.
- Accessibility Standards.
- Accessibility Findings.

Partial matching must not replace exact-match ranking.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Typo Tolerance

Where practical, support reasonable typo tolerance.

For example:

``` text
accesibility
```

may return:

``` text
Accessibility
```

Typo tolerance should improve discoverability without producing large
numbers of irrelevant results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phrase Searching

Support phrase searches where appropriate.

For example:

``` text
"missing form label"
```

should prioritize results containing that phrase.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Operators

If ART supports search operators, document and implement them
consistently.

Potential operators include:

``` text
AND
OR
NOT
"exact phrase"
```

Do not introduce complex query syntax unless it provides meaningful
value.

If operators are implemented, they must be accessible and documented.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Field-Specific Searching

Where appropriate, allow users to search specific metadata fields.

Examples:

``` text
type:report
severity:high
status:failed
workspace:"City Website"
```

Field-specific searching must remain optional.

Do not require users to learn query syntax to perform normal searches.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Search

Advanced Search shall provide appropriate filters for Findings.

Finding filters may include:

- Finding status.
- Severity.
- Issue type.
- Accessibility standard.
- Success Criterion.
- Page/screen/component.
- Report.
- Workspace.
- Assignee where applicable.
- Created date.
- Modified date.
- Reporter/creator where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Issue Type

ART uses **Issue Type** to represent the individual test criterion
within an accessibility standard.

Search and filtering interfaces shall use this terminology consistently.

For example:

``` text
Issue Type: Missing Form Label
```

Do not incorrectly interpret Issue Type as a broad category of
accessibility standards.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Standard Filtering

Allow users to filter results by Accessibility Standard.

Examples may include:

- WCAG.
- Section 508.
- ARIA.
- ATAG.
- Other supported standards.

The available standards shall be based on the standards supported by
ART.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### WCAG Version Filtering

When WCAG is selected, allow filtering by applicable WCAG version.

Examples:

- WCAG 2.0.
- WCAG 2.1.
- WCAG 2.2.
- Future supported versions.

Do not display WCAG-specific filters when WCAG is not part of the
selected scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### WCAG Conformance Level Filtering

Allow users to filter WCAG Success Criteria by:

- Level A.
- Level AA.
- Level AAA.

Where multiple levels are selected, apply the defined filter logic
consistently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Success Criterion Filtering

Users shall be able to search/filter by specific WCAG Success Criteria.

Results should preserve:

- Success Criterion ID.
- Success Criterion name.
- Conformance level.
- WCAG version.

For example:

``` text
1.1.1 Non-Text Content (Level A)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Filtering

Where reports contain status information, provide appropriate filtering
for statuses such as:

- Passed.
- Failed.
- Manual Review.
- Not Tested.
- Other report-defined statuses.

Only display status filters that apply to the selected Report or result
type.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Conditional Status Options

If a Report does not contain a particular status, that status should not
be presented as though it applies.

For example, if a Report does not support **Manual Review**, do not
present Manual Review as an active applicable filter for that Report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Severity Filtering

Where applicable, support severity filtering.

Examples may include:

- Critical.
- High.
- Medium.
- Low.
- Informational.

Use the severity model configured for the applicable Report or
Workspace.

Do not impose a new severity model on existing Reports.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Page/Screen/Component Filtering

Where Findings are associated with a page, screen, or component, allow
users to filter by that location.

This should support locating all Findings associated with a specific
location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Date Filtering

Support appropriate date filtering.

Potential options include:

- Created date.
- Modified date.
- Report date.
- Due date where applicable.

Allow users to specify:

- Exact date.
- Before.
- After.
- Between.

Use accessible date controls.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Ownership Filtering

Where ownership information exists, allow filtering by:

- Owner.
- Creator.
- Assignee.
- Contributor.

Do not expose personal information to users who do not have permission
to view it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration Filtering

When Collaboration is enabled, provide applicable filters such as:

- Personal.
- Shared.
- Workspace.
- Owned by me.
- Shared with me.

These filters must respect Collaboration Framework permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resource Type Filtering

Allow users to filter by resource type.

Potential resource types include:

- Reports.
- Project Workspaces.
- Working Views.
- Findings.
- Templates.
- Publishing Profiles.
- Themes.
- Layouts.
- Branding.
- Plugins.
- Packages.
- Accessibility Standards.
- WCAG Success Criteria.

Only show resource types that are searchable in the current scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sorting

Allow users to sort search results.

Potential sort options include:

- Relevance.
- Name.
- Date created.
- Date modified.
- Recently accessed.
- Severity.
- Status.
- Issue Type.
- Workspace.
- Report.

The available sort options should depend on the selected resource type
and scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Default Sorting

The default sort order should generally be:

``` text
Relevance
```

unless the user is viewing a context where another ordering is more
useful.

For example, Recent Items should continue to prioritize recent access
rather than search relevance.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sort Direction

Where applicable, allow users to choose:

- Ascending.
- Descending.

The current sort direction must be communicated accessibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sort Changes

Changing the sort order shall:

- Update results.
- Preserve the search query.
- Preserve active filters.
- Preserve search scope.
- Avoid stealing focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Count

Display the number of matching results where practical.

For example:

``` text
24 results found.
```

If results are paginated or virtualized, clearly communicate the visible
range where useful.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Large Result Sets

Advanced Search shall support large result sets without attempting to
render every result simultaneously.

Use appropriate:

- Pagination.
- Virtualization.
- Incremental loading.

The implementation must remain accessible to screen readers and keyboard
users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Pagination

If pagination is used, provide accessible controls for:

- First page.
- Previous page.
- Current page.
- Next page.
- Last page where appropriate.

The current page shall be programmatically identifiable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Infinite Scrolling

If infinite scrolling is used, provide an accessible alternative.

Users must not be required to continuously scroll to discover additional
results.

Keyboard and screen-reader users must be able to reach all available
results predictably.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Result Selection

Search results shall support keyboard selection.

At minimum:

- Up/Down Arrow navigation where an appropriate listbox pattern is used.
- Enter to activate.
- Escape to cancel or close the search interface.
- Tab navigation for interactive result actions where applicable.

Do not create competing keyboard models within the same search
interface.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Result Actions

Where appropriate, results may provide secondary actions such as:

- Open.
- Open in Working View.
- Add to Favorites.
- Add Bookmark.
- Copy Reference.
- Open Containing Workspace.
- Open Containing Report.

Only display actions the user is authorized to perform.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menus

Search results may provide context menus for secondary actions.

Context menus shall:

- Be keyboard accessible.
- Respect permissions.
- Use existing ART commands.
- Restore focus appropriately when dismissed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Searches

Provide the ability to save useful Advanced Search configurations.

A saved search should preserve:

- Search query.
- Search scope.
- Active filters.
- Sort order.
- Applicable result settings.

Do not save temporary UI state that has no relevance to the search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Search Naming

Users shall be able to provide a meaningful name for a Saved Search.

For example:

``` text
High-Severity Failed Findings
```

A useful default name may be generated automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Search Privacy

Saved Searches shall be personal by default.

Creating a Saved Search must not automatically share the underlying
search criteria with other users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Saved Searches

If Collaboration is enabled, users with appropriate permissions may
explicitly share Saved Searches.

Shared Saved Searches shall:

- Respect Workspace permissions.
- Identify that they are shared.
- Remain separate from personal Saved Searches.
- Revalidate permissions when executed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Search Updates

If the underlying Report, Workspace, or data structure changes:

- Reevaluate the Saved Search against current data.
- Preserve criteria that remain valid.
- Clearly identify filters that are no longer applicable.

Do not silently change a user's saved search criteria.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Invalid Saved Search Criteria

If a Saved Search contains a filter that is no longer available:

- Identify the invalid criterion.
- Explain why it is unavailable.
- Allow the user to modify the Saved Search.
- Do not silently replace it with a different criterion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Search Commands

Provide appropriate commands such as:

``` text
Save Search
Save Search As
Open Saved Search
Manage Saved Searches
Delete Saved Search
```

These commands shall use the existing ART command architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search History

Search history may be used to improve productivity.

If implemented:

- Search history should be personal.
- It should not automatically be shared.
- Users should be able to clear it.
- Search history should respect application privacy settings.

Do not confuse Search History with Recent Items.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search History Privacy

Search History must not expose private queries or resource names to
other users.

If synchronization is implemented, it must be explicitly controlled.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search History Settings

Application Settings may provide options such as:

- Enable Search History.
- Maximum history length.
- Clear Search History.
- Synchronize Search History where supported.

Do not require Search History to use Search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Suggestions

Search suggestions may include:

- Recent searches.
- Saved Searches.
- Favorites.
- Matching resource names.
- Matching criteria.

Suggestions must remain subordinate to the user's current search.

Do not allow suggestions to interfere with normal typing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Search Suggestions

Search suggestions shall follow the same non-interruptive behavior
established for autocomplete elsewhere in ART.

Specifically:

- Suggestions may update automatically.
- Screen readers must not announce every update.
- Announce **"suggestions available"** once when appropriate.
- Allow users to press Down Arrow or Alt+Down Arrow to enter the
  suggestions.
- Announce each suggestion when it receives programmatic keyboard focus.
- Enter shall activate the selected suggestion.
- Escape shall return to the search input or close the search interface
  as appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Query Editing

Users shall be able to edit their query without losing their selected
filters unless they explicitly clear them.

The cursor/insertion point shall remain where the user placed it.

Do not unexpectedly replace the user's query.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Input Autocomplete

Where search autocomplete is provided:

- Suggestions should be relevant to the current input.
- Suggestions may update quietly.
- Focus shall remain in the search input while the user types.
- The user's insertion point shall not be moved unexpectedly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Highlighting

Where appropriate, matching terms may be visually highlighted in
results.

Highlighted text must not be the only indication of a match.

Do not use color alone to communicate matching information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Result Highlighting

Screen readers should not be forced to announce decorative highlighting
markup.

The accessible result name should remain concise and meaningful.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No Results

When no results match:

Provide a clear message such as:

``` text
No results found.
```

Where useful, provide suggestions such as:

- Remove a filter.
- Broaden the search.
- Change the search scope.
- Check spelling.

Do not automatically change the user's query.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Partial Results

If the Search Service cannot complete a search because of:

- Offline limitations.
- Synchronization issues.
- Permission changes.
- Indexing delays.

Clearly communicate that the results may be incomplete.

Do not present incomplete results as definitive.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Index Status

Where indexing is necessary, provide an appropriate status mechanism.

For example:

``` text
Search index updating.
Some recently changed content may not yet appear.
```

This information should not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Reindexing

If users can manually rebuild or refresh a Search index, provide an
accessible command.

The operation shall:

- Preserve current application state.
- Not delete user data.
- Not alter Reports or Workspaces.
- Provide progress feedback where necessary.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dynamic Data Changes

When content changes while a search is active:

- Update results as appropriate.
- Do not unexpectedly reorder the result currently receiving focus.
- Do not steal focus.
- Preserve the user's current query and filters.

If a result disappears because it was deleted or no longer matches the
criteria, provide predictable behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration Changes

When Collaboration is enabled and another user changes searchable
content:

- Search should eventually reflect the updated data.
- Do not expose unauthorized content.
- Do not interrupt the current user unnecessarily.
- Preserve the current search interaction where possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission-Aware Search

Search must always be permission-aware.

The Search Service must not return content the user is not authorized to
access.

This applies to:

- Personal content.
- Workspace content.
- Shared Reports.
- Shared Working Views.
- Findings.
- Plugins.
- Packages.
- Saved Searches.
- Bookmarks.
- Other searchable resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Changes During Search

If permissions change while search results are displayed:

- Revalidate access when a result is activated.
- Remove or mark inaccessible results as appropriate.
- Never reveal protected content through result metadata.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Security

Do not rely on UI hiding alone to protect search results.

Authorization must be enforced by the underlying search/data
architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Performance

Advanced Search shall remain responsive with large datasets.

Test with:

- Large Reports.
- Large Project Workspaces.
- Large numbers of Findings.
- Many Reports.
- Many Workspaces.
- Large numbers of searchable resources.
- Large Search indexes.

Do not block the main UI while searching.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Debouncing

Search input should use appropriate debouncing or equivalent techniques
to prevent excessive search operations while the user is typing.

The implementation must not delay normal typing or move focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Cancellation

If a new query replaces an existing query while a previous search is
still running:

- Cancel or supersede the obsolete search.
- Display only results associated with the current query.
- Do not allow stale results to overwrite current results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Result Consistency

Results must correspond to the current:

- Query.
- Scope.
- Filters.
- Sort order.

Do not display stale results after the search criteria have changed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search State Restoration

If the user leaves an Advanced Search and returns:

- Preserve the query where practical.
- Preserve the scope.
- Preserve active filters.
- Preserve sort order.
- Preserve result position where practical.

Do not unnecessarily reset the search state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Restoration

When Advanced Search closes or is canceled:

- Return focus to the location that opened it.
- Do not move focus to the top of the page.
- Preserve the user's application state.

When a result is opened and the user later returns to Search:

- Restore the search state where practical.
- Restore focus to the previously selected result where possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard-Only Workflow

Verify that a user can perform the complete workflow using only the
keyboard:

1.  Open Advanced Search.
2.  Select a search scope.
3.  Enter a search query.
4.  Open filter categories.
5.  Select multiple filters.
6.  Change sorting.
7.  Navigate search results.
8.  Open a result.
9.  Return to Search.
10. Modify the search.
11. Clear individual filters.
12. Clear all filters.
13. Save a search.
14. Reopen a saved search.
15. Delete a saved search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### JAWS Testing

Test Advanced Search with JAWS.

Verify:

- Search scope announcement.
- Search input announcement.
- Filter category announcement.
- Filter state announcement.
- Search result count.
- Result name and type.
- Result context.
- Sort state.
- Selected result.
- Suggestion availability.
- Individual suggestion announcements.
- Enter activation.
- Escape behavior.
- Focus restoration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Control

Where ART supports voice-control workflows, ensure:

- Search controls have meaningful accessible names.
- Filter controls have distinguishable labels.
- Results have meaningful names.
- Commands can be identified and spoken.

Do not rely solely on icons or visual positioning.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application Settings

Application Settings should provide appropriate options for Advanced
Search behavior.

Potential options include:

- Enable Search History.
- Enable Search Suggestions.
- Show Recent Searches.
- Show Favorites in Search.
- Show Bookmarks in Search.
- Default Search Scope.
- Default Search Sort.
- Number of results displayed where appropriate.
- Synchronization options where supported.

Only expose settings that provide meaningful user control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No UI Clutter

Advanced Search should use progressive disclosure.

Do not permanently display every available filter.

Primary access should remain through:

- Search.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Menu bar.
- Existing navigation interfaces.

The interface should provide powerful functionality without creating
unnecessary visual clutter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Architecture

All Advanced Search commands shall use shared underlying
commands/actions.

For example:

``` text
Menu → Advanced Search
Command Palette → Advanced Search
Keyboard Shortcut → Advanced Search
```

All shall invoke the same underlying operation.

Do not duplicate Search functionality across interfaces.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Error Handling

If a search cannot be completed:

- Explain the problem.
- Preserve the user's query.
- Preserve active filters.
- Preserve search scope.
- Preserve the user's current location.
- Do not move focus unexpectedly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Acceptance Criteria

Part 4 shall be considered complete when:

1.  Advanced Search is implemented using the unified Search Service.
2.  Users can search using multiple criteria.
3.  Search scope is clearly identified.
4.  Search scope can be changed where permitted.
5.  Contextually relevant filters are provided.
6.  Filters are organized using progressive disclosure.
7.  Filter categories are accessible and keyboard operable.
8.  Multiple filters can be combined.
9.  Filter logic is predictable and consistent.
10. Active filters are clearly displayed.
11. Individual filters can be removed.
12. Users can clear filters.
13. Search results update without stealing focus.
14. Screen readers are not repeatedly interrupted by dynamic result
    updates.
15. Search result counts are provided where appropriate.
16. Search results identify resource type.
17. Search results provide sufficient context.
18. Exact matches receive appropriate ranking.
19. Partial matching is supported.
20. Reasonable typo tolerance is supported where practical.
21. Phrase searching is supported where appropriate.
22. Resource-type filtering is supported.
23. Report filtering is supported.
24. Workspace filtering is supported.
25. Working View filtering is supported where applicable.
26. Finding filtering is supported.
27. Issue Type filtering is supported.
28. Accessibility Standard filtering is supported.
29. WCAG version filtering is supported.
30. WCAG conformance-level filtering is supported.
31. Success Criterion filtering is supported.
32. Finding status filtering is supported where applicable.
33. Severity filtering is supported where applicable.
34. Page/screen/component filtering is supported where applicable.
35. Date filtering is supported where applicable.
36. Ownership filtering respects permissions.
37. Collaboration filtering respects permissions.
38. Search results respect user permissions.
39. Permission changes are revalidated before navigation.
40. Search results never expose unauthorized content.
41. Results can be sorted using relevant criteria.
42. Sort order is accessible.
43. Sort changes preserve the query and filters.
44. Large result sets remain usable and accessible.
45. Pagination or equivalent large-result handling is accessible.
46. Search results support predictable keyboard navigation.
47. Search result actions respect permissions.
48. Saved Searches can be created.
49. Saved Searches preserve query, scope, filters, and sort order.
50. Saved Searches are personal by default.
51. Shared Saved Searches are explicitly shared and
    permission-controlled.
52. Invalid Saved Search criteria are handled gracefully.
53. Search History is distinct from Recent Items.
54. Search History respects privacy.
55. Search suggestions update without stealing focus.
56. Screen readers do not announce every autocomplete update.
57. Screen readers announce "suggestions available" appropriately.
58. Individual suggestions are announced when they receive programmatic
    keyboard focus.
59. Search queries can be edited without losing applicable filters.
60. Search highlighting does not rely on color alone.
61. No-results states provide useful guidance.
62. Partial/incomplete results are clearly identified when applicable.
63. Search indexing status is communicated appropriately.
64. Search remains responsive with large datasets.
65. Obsolete searches cannot overwrite current search results.
66. Dynamic collaboration changes do not unexpectedly disrupt active
    searches.
67. Search state can be restored when returning to Search.
68. Focus is restored correctly when Search is closed or canceled.
69. Selecting a result navigates to the intended destination.
70. Keyboard-only workflows are fully supported.
71. JAWS workflows are verified.
72. Voice-control compatibility is preserved where applicable.
73. Search settings are configurable where appropriate.
74. Advanced Search does not introduce unnecessary persistent UI
    clutter.
75. All Search commands use the shared command architecture.
76. The implementation provides the foundation required for Part 5's
    Navigation History, Breadcrumbs, Context Preservation, and
    Back/Forward navigation.

### Part 5 — Navigation History, Breadcrumbs, Context Preservation, and Back/Forward Navigation

#### Overview

Implement the **Navigation History, Breadcrumbs, Context Preservation,
and Back/Forward Navigation** capabilities of the Search & Navigation
Framework.

These capabilities shall allow users to move through ART naturally,
understand where they are, and return to previously visited locations
without losing their current context.

This part shall build on the unified Search Service, Quick Open,
Favorites, Bookmarks, Advanced Search, and Saved Search functionality
established in Parts 1–4.

The navigation model must work consistently across:

- Standalone Reports.
- Project Workspaces.
- Working Views.
- Report Builder.
- Report Viewer.
- Findings.
- Analytics.
- Accessibility Lookup Tool.
- Settings.
- Help/User Guide.
- Other navigable ART resources.

Do not create separate navigation-history implementations for individual
features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Unified Navigation History

Implement a centralized navigation-history service for ART.

The Navigation History Service shall track meaningful navigation
locations rather than every minor UI interaction.

Navigation history should include meaningful transitions such as:

- Opening a Report.
- Opening a Project Workspace.
- Opening a Working View.
- Opening a Finding.
- Opening an Analytics section.
- Opening an Accessibility Standard.
- Opening a WCAG Success Criterion.
- Opening a Settings section.
- Opening a Help/User Guide section.
- Opening a bookmarked location.
- Opening a Favorite.
- Opening a Search result.

Do not create a history entry for every:

- Focus movement.
- Tab operation.
- Arrow-key movement within a control.
- Filter change.
- Typing operation.
- Mouse movement.
- Minor visual state change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Location

Each navigation-history entry shall represent a meaningful, restorable
location.

Where applicable, a navigation location should include:

- Resource type.
- Resource identifier.
- Workspace identifier.
- Report identifier.
- Working View identifier.
- Finding identifier.
- Section identifier.
- Subsection identifier.
- Search context.
- Relevant UI state.
- Scroll position where appropriate.
- Focus target where appropriate.

Use stable internal identifiers whenever possible.

Do not rely solely on:

- Visible names.
- DOM position.
- Row numbers.
- Screen coordinates.
- Current visual layout.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation State

Navigation history should preserve enough context to return the user to
the previous location.

For example, if the user navigates:

``` text
Project Workspace
→ Report
→ Report Viewer
→ Finding
→ Analytics
```

pressing Back should move through those meaningful locations in reverse
order.

The user should not be returned merely to the top of each containing
page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Back Navigation

Provide a **Back** navigation command.

Back shall navigate to the previous meaningful navigation location.

Back must:

- Restore the appropriate resource.
- Restore applicable context.
- Restore the appropriate Working View.
- Restore relevant search/filter state where applicable.
- Restore scroll position where practical.
- Restore focus where practical.

Do not simply reload the previous page without restoring its context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Forward Navigation

Provide a **Forward** navigation command.

Forward shall navigate to the next location in the navigation history
after the user has navigated backward.

Forward must:

- Restore the appropriate resource.
- Restore applicable context.
- Restore relevant UI state.
- Restore focus where practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Back/Forward History Model

Use a conventional browser-style navigation model.

For example:

``` text
A → B → C
```

If the user presses Back:

``` text
A ← B ← C
```

If the user then navigates from B to D:

``` text
A → B → D
```

The previous Forward history from B to C should be discarded because a
new navigation branch has been created.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation History Stack

Maintain separate conceptual:

- Back history.
- Forward history.

The implementation should avoid duplicating identical consecutive
entries.

For example:

``` text
Report A
Report A
Report A
```

should generally result in one meaningful history entry rather than
three identical entries.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Duplicate Navigation

If the user activates a navigation target that is already the current
location:

- Do not create unnecessary duplicate history entries.
- Preserve the current context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Back/Forward Availability

The Back and Forward commands shall expose their current state.

For example:

``` text
Back — unavailable
Forward — available
```

The state must be communicated programmatically to assistive
technologies.

Disabled commands must not appear actionable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Commands

Provide shared commands for:

``` text
Back
Forward
Open Navigation History
Clear Navigation History
```

Where appropriate, additional commands may include:

``` text
Back to Report
Back to Workspace
Back to Working View
```

Do not create unnecessary commands if the standard Back/Forward model
provides the required functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcuts

If ART already has navigation keyboard shortcuts, preserve them.

If new shortcuts are introduced:

- They must not conflict with existing ART shortcuts.
- They must be configurable where appropriate.
- They must work with screen readers.
- They must not interfere with browser-level commands unnecessarily.

Do not override standard browser or operating-system shortcuts without a
compelling reason.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Integration

Back and Forward shall be available through the existing:

- Menu bar.
- Menus.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Global Context Menu where enabled.

Do not add large persistent navigation controls solely to expose Back
and Forward.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Toolbar

If ART has an existing navigation toolbar, Back and Forward may be
included there.

If a new navigation toolbar is introduced:

- It must not be enabled by default unless consistent with existing ART
  UI requirements.
- It must be fully keyboard accessible.
- It must be screen-reader accessible.
- Its controls must have accessible names.
- Its location must be customizable if the toolbar is movable.
- It must not create unnecessary visual clutter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Menu Navigation

Where appropriate, context menus may provide:

``` text
Back
Forward
Open in New View
Open Containing Workspace
```

Only provide commands that are meaningful for the current context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Navigation

Implement accessible breadcrumbs for hierarchical ART resources.

Breadcrumbs should communicate the user's current location.

For example:

``` text
Project Workspace
> Accessibility Audit
> Report Viewer
> Findings
> Missing Form Label
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Hierarchy

Breadcrumbs should represent meaningful application hierarchy.

For example:

``` text
Workspace
→ Report
→ Working View
→ Finding
```

Do not include implementation-only containers that do not help users
understand their location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Links

Each breadcrumb representing a navigable ancestor shall be an accessible
link or equivalent navigation control.

The current page/location should be identified as the current item.

Do not make the current location appear to be an ordinary link if
activating it would have no meaningful effect.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Current Breadcrumb

The current breadcrumb shall expose an appropriate programmatic state
such as:

``` text
aria-current="page"
```

or another semantically appropriate mechanism.

Do not rely solely on visual styling to identify the current location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Labels

Breadcrumb labels shall use meaningful names.

For example:

``` text
City Website Project
Accessibility Audit
QA Working View
Missing Form Label
```

Do not expose internal IDs or implementation names.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Updates

Breadcrumbs shall update when the user changes navigation context.

For example:

``` text
Workspace → Report → Working View
```

may become:

``` text
Workspace → Report → Report Viewer → Finding
```

when the user opens a Finding.

Do not leave stale breadcrumb information displayed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Keyboard Accessibility

Users shall be able to navigate breadcrumbs using the keyboard.

Verify:

- Tab navigation.
- Enter activation.
- Appropriate focus indication.
- Predictable navigation order.
- Screen-reader announcements.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Screen Reader Accessibility

Screen readers shall be able to determine:

- That the control is a breadcrumb navigation region.
- The current location.
- Available ancestor navigation targets.

Use appropriate semantic structure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Landmark

Where appropriate, expose breadcrumbs as a navigation landmark with an
accessible name.

For example:

``` text
Breadcrumb
```

Do not create multiple indistinguishable navigation landmarks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumb Focus Management

When a breadcrumb is activated:

- Navigate to the selected ancestor.
- Move focus to an appropriate location.
- Preserve the user's ability to understand the new context.

Do not move focus to the top of the page unless that is genuinely the
correct destination.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context Preservation

Navigation shall preserve relevant user context whenever the destination
supports it.

Context may include:

- Current Report.
- Current Workspace.
- Current Working View.
- Selected Finding.
- Search query.
- Search filters.
- Sort order.
- Analytics section.
- Expanded/collapsed sections.
- Scroll position.
- Selected row.
- Selected field.
- Focus location.

Only restore context that remains valid.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Search Context Preservation

If a user searches for something and opens a result, returning to Search
should preserve:

- Search query.
- Search scope.
- Filters.
- Sort order.
- Selected result where practical.
- Result position where practical.

For example:

``` text
Search
→ Result
→ Back
```

should return the user to the same Search state rather than restarting
the search.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Advanced Search Preservation

Advanced Search state shall be preserved when navigating away from the
results.

The following should remain available when the user returns:

- Search query.
- Search scope.
- Active filters.
- Sort order.
- Result position where practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Favorites Preservation

If a user opens a Favorite and then navigates Back:

- Return to the location from which the Favorite was opened.
- Do not automatically navigate to the Favorites list unless that was
  the originating location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Bookmark Preservation

If a user opens a Bookmark and then navigates Back:

- Return to the originating location.
- Preserve the Bookmark's target context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Context

Working Views require special navigation handling.

A Working View may be:

- Personal.
- Shared.
- Read-only.
- Editable.
- Created by a team lead/admin.
- Created by an individual contributor.

Navigation must preserve the specific Working View context.

Do not replace a user's personal Working View with a shared Working View
merely because they navigate through the same Report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Personal Working Views

When a user navigates within a personal Working View:

- Preserve that user's Working View.
- Preserve its configuration.
- Preserve applicable filters.
- Preserve grouping/sorting.
- Preserve layout where appropriate.

Back/Forward must not unexpectedly switch to another user's Working
View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Working Views

When navigating within a shared Working View:

- Preserve the shared Working View identity.
- Preserve the user's permission level.
- Do not convert the shared Working View into a personal Working View.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Viewer Context

A Viewer may navigate through read-only content.

Back/Forward and breadcrumbs must never grant editing access.

Navigation state must respect the user's current permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Builder Context

When navigating within the Report Builder, preserve meaningful Builder
context where practical.

Examples include:

- Current Builder section.
- Selected report field.
- Selected branding section.
- Selected template.
- Current configuration dialog.

Do not lose entered data because the user navigated to another related
location unless existing unsaved-change behavior requires it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Unsaved Changes

Navigation must integrate with ART's existing unsaved-change protection.

If leaving a location would cause unsaved data to be lost:

- Preserve existing warning behavior.
- Do not bypass the warning because navigation was initiated through
  Back, Forward, Breadcrumbs, Favorites, or Bookmarks.

If the user cancels the navigation:

- Remain at the current location.
- Preserve current focus and data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Viewer Context

When navigating away from the Report Viewer and returning:

- Preserve the appropriate Report.
- Preserve the current Working View where applicable.
- Preserve relevant Finding or section context.
- Restore focus appropriately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Context

When opening a Finding:

- Preserve its containing Report.
- Preserve its Workspace where applicable.
- Preserve its Working View where applicable.
- Preserve the location within the Finding.

When returning from the Finding:

- Restore the previous result/list context where practical.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Context

If the user opens a specific Analytics section:

- Preserve the selected Analytics section.
- Preserve expanded/collapsed section state where practical.
- Preserve applicable filters.
- Preserve Report/Workspace context.

For example:

``` text
Analytics
→ Findings by Severity
```

Back should return to the previous location rather than simply reopening
the Dashboard.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Help/User Guide Context

When the Help/User Guide is opened:

- Preserve the originating location.
- When Help is closed using the Close button or Escape, return focus to
  the location that invoked Help.
- Do not move focus to the top of the page.

This must work consistently regardless of whether Help was opened from:

- Menu.
- Command Palette.
- Context menu.
- Keyboard shortcut.
- Help link.
- Other supported command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Modal Navigation

When navigation opens a modal:

- Preserve the originating focus location.
- Focus must enter the modal appropriately.
- Closing the modal must restore focus to the originating
  control/location.

Do not add modal openings to navigation history unless the modal
represents a meaningful navigable location.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dialogs vs. Navigation

Not every UI interaction should create a navigation-history entry.

Do not create history entries merely because the user opened:

- A confirmation dialog.
- A simple settings dialog.
- A context menu.
- A tooltip.
- A transient notification.

Only create history entries for meaningful navigable locations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation History Panel

Provide an **Open Navigation History** command.

The history interface should allow users to review meaningful previous
locations.

Each entry should provide:

- Resource/location name.
- Resource type.
- Workspace/Report context where applicable.
- Time information where useful.
- Current/previous state where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation History Ordering

History should be displayed in reverse chronological navigation order,
with the most recent meaningful location first.

Do not display implementation-only events.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation History Activation

Activating a history entry shall navigate directly to that location.

The user should not have to repeat the original search or navigation
sequence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation History Accessibility

The Navigation History interface shall support:

- Keyboard navigation.
- Screen readers.
- Focus management.
- Accessible names.
- Accessible state.
- Predictable Escape behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation History Search

If the history becomes large, allow users to search or filter it.

Search should use the unified Search Service where appropriate.

Do not create a separate unrelated search implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Clear Navigation History

Provide a **Clear Navigation History** command.

Clearing history shall:

- Remove navigation history entries.
- Not delete Reports.
- Not delete Workspaces.
- Not delete Favorites.
- Not delete Bookmarks.
- Not delete Search History unless explicitly requested.

Do not conflate these data types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### History Privacy

Navigation History is personal by default.

It must not automatically be shared with collaborators.

Do not expose a user's navigation history to:

- Workspace owners.
- Administrators.
- Team leads.
- Other collaborators.

unless a separate explicit feature and permission model is implemented.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration and Navigation History

Collaboration shall not automatically synchronize personal navigation
history.

A user navigating through a shared Report must not cause their personal
navigation history to become visible to other collaborators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Navigation State

If ART later supports intentionally shared navigation state, it must be
implemented separately from personal Navigation History.

It must use explicit permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Back/Forward and Collaboration

If another collaborator changes a shared resource while the user is
navigating:

- Back/Forward should continue to identify the correct resource.
- Revalidate permissions.
- Resolve changed or deleted targets appropriately.
- Do not expose unauthorized information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deleted Navigation Targets

If a navigation-history entry points to a deleted resource:

- Do not produce an application error.
- Identify that the destination is no longer available.
- Allow the user to continue navigating through other history entries.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Renamed Navigation Targets

If a resource is renamed:

- Existing history entries should display the current name.
- The navigation target should remain valid.
- Stable identifiers should be used internally.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Moved Resources

If a Report or resource moves to another Workspace or organizational
location:

- Navigation history should continue to resolve the resource when the
  user retains access.
- Breadcrumbs should update to the new hierarchy.
- Favorites and Bookmarks should continue to function where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Errors

If a navigation target cannot be resolved:

- Explain the problem.
- Preserve the current location.
- Do not move focus unexpectedly.
- Do not corrupt the Back/Forward history.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Browser Integration

ART should integrate with browser navigation behavior where practical
without breaking standard browser behavior.

If browser Back/Forward is supported:

- It should correspond logically to ART's navigation model.
- It must not create duplicate or conflicting navigation stacks.
- Browser Back must not unexpectedly exit ART when meaningful ART
  navigation history remains.

Do not override browser behavior unnecessarily.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### URL and Deep-Link Integration

Where ART uses URLs or URL-like navigation state, navigation targets
should use stable identifiers.

For example:

``` text
Workspace ID
Report ID
Working View ID
Finding ID
```

rather than relying solely on display names.

Deep links should respect permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Deep-Link Accessibility

When a user opens a valid deep link:

- Open the intended destination.
- Establish the correct breadcrumbs.
- Establish the appropriate navigation history state.
- Move focus to the appropriate destination.
- Preserve applicable context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Invalid Deep Links

If a deep link is invalid or inaccessible:

- Explain the problem.
- Do not expose protected resource information.
- Provide an appropriate fallback location.
- Preserve accessible focus behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Navigation Announcements

Screen readers should receive concise navigation announcements when the
destination changes meaningfully.

For example:

``` text
Report Viewer, Accessibility Audit.
```

or:

``` text
Finding, Missing Form Label.
```

Do not repeatedly announce every minor UI update.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Live Region Use

If live regions are used for navigation announcements:

- Keep announcements concise.
- Avoid repeated announcements.
- Do not interrupt active typing.
- Do not announce decorative UI changes.

Navigation announcements must not interfere with the user's current
task.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus After Navigation

After navigation completes:

- Move focus to the most meaningful destination control.
- Preserve focus when the destination is an inline update.
- Do not automatically move focus to the top of the page.

Examples:

**Report opened:**

Focus may move to the Report heading or first meaningful control.

**Finding opened:**

Focus may move to the Finding heading or first relevant control.

**Analytics section opened:**

Focus may move to the selected section heading or first interactive
control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Restoration After Back/Forward

When Back or Forward restores a previously visited location:

- Restore the previously focused control where possible.
- If that control no longer exists, move focus to the closest meaningful
  equivalent.
- Do not move focus to the top of the page merely because the original
  target cannot be restored.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Focus Restoration After Breadcrumb Navigation

When a breadcrumb is activated:

- Focus should move to the destination.
- The destination must be announced appropriately.
- The breadcrumb that was activated should not retain focus if it no
  longer represents the user's current context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard-Only Workflow

Verify that a user can complete the following workflow using only the
keyboard:

1.  Open a Project Workspace.
2.  Open a Report.
3.  Open a Working View.
4.  Open a Finding.
5.  Navigate Back.
6.  Navigate Back again.
7.  Navigate Forward.
8.  Navigate through breadcrumbs.
9.  Open Search.
10. Open a Search result.
11. Return using Back.
12. Open a Favorite.
13. Return using Back.
14. Open a Bookmark.
15. Return using Back.
16. Open Help.
17. Close Help with Escape.
18. Verify focus returns to the invoking location.
19. Open Navigation History.
20. Select a previous location.
21. Clear Navigation History.
22. Verify that Favorites and Bookmarks remain intact.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### JAWS Testing

Test Navigation History with JAWS.

Verify that JAWS can determine:

- Current location.
- Breadcrumb hierarchy.
- Current breadcrumb.
- Back availability.
- Forward availability.
- Navigation History entries.
- Resource type.
- Workspace/Report context.
- Navigation destination.
- Focus after navigation.
- Focus after Back.
- Focus after Forward.
- Focus after closing Help.
- Focus after closing navigation interfaces.

Verify that navigation announcements do not repeatedly interrupt users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Voice Control
