Project trends over time.

Users shall be able to select an individual Project and view its metrics
without losing the broader Organization context.

The **Workspaces** tab shall provide organization-level analytics

Number of Findings per Workspace.

Trends over time.

A user shall not be able to infer statistics about Workspaces to which

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Reports Tab

The Organization Statistics framework shall support report-level
drill-down.

Users shall be able to view the reports contributing to an
organization's statistics, subject to permissions.

For each report, where applicable, provide:

- 

Report name.

- 

Organization/Client.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report date.

- 

Tester/Tester Name.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

WCAG version.

- 

Number of findings.

- 

Findings by severity.

- 

Findings by Category.

- 

Findings by Issue Type.

- 

Findings by Success Criterion.

- 

Passed Findings.

- 

Failed Findings.

- 

Manual Review Findings.

- 

Not Tested Findings.

- 

Testing Coverage.

The report-level information shall be derived from the source report and
shall not create a second, conflicting representation of the report
data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Trends Tab

The **Trends** tab shall provide historical analysis of the
organization's accessibility testing and findings.

The user shall be able to select an applicable time period and
aggregation interval.

Supported intervals should include:

- 

Week.

- 

Month.

- 

Quarter.

- 

Year.

- 

Custom date range.

Where sufficient data exists, track trends for:

- 

Total Findings.

- 

Findings by Severity.

- 

Findings by Category.

- 

Findings by Issue Type.

- 

Findings by Accessibility Standard.

- 

Findings by WCAG Success Criterion.

- 

Passed Findings.

- 

Failed Findings.

- 

Manual Review Findings.

- 

Not Tested Findings.

- 

Reports completed.

- 

Audits completed.

- 

Projects completed.

- 

Products tested.

- 

Pages/Screens/Components tested.

- 

Unique testers.

- 

Finding recurrence.

- 

Testing coverage.

The dashboard shall clearly identify whether a trend represents:

- 

Findings discovered.

- 

Findings remaining.

- 

Findings resolved.

- 

Tests performed.

- 

Reports completed.

- 

Another explicitly defined measurement.

Do not label a trend generically as an "improvement" unless the
underlying metric and interpretation support that conclusion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Recurrence

Implement a dedicated **Finding Recurrence** analytics capability.

Finding recurrence shall identify accessibility issues that appear
repeatedly across:

- 

Reports.

- 

Audits.

- 

Projects.

- 

Workspaces.

- 

Products.

- 

Testing periods.

The objective is to identify patterns indicating that an accessibility
issue continues to occur after previous testing or appears repeatedly
across related testing activities.

The recurrence system shall distinguish between:

1.  

**Repeatedly reported findings** — the same or substantially equivalent
issue appears in multiple reports.

2.  

**Recurring issue types** — the same Issue Type repeatedly generates
findings.

3.  

**Recurring Success Criteria** — the same WCAG Success Criterion
repeatedly generates findings.

4.  

**Recurring Categories** — the same Category repeatedly generates
findings.

5.  

**Recurring products/issues** — a similar issue continues to occur
within the same Product.

6.  

**Cross-product recurrence** — a similar issue appears across multiple
Products belonging to the same Organization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Identity and Recurrence Matching

The implementation shall define a reliable mechanism for determining
when findings represent the same underlying issue.

Do not assume that two findings are identical merely because they have
the same:

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Category.

- 

WCAG Success Criterion.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

Severity.

These values may indicate a recurring **type of issue**, but not
necessarily the same specific finding.

Where ART has sufficient information to identify a finding's location or
target, recurrence matching may use information such as:

- 

Product.

- 

Page.

- 

Screen.

- 

Component.

- 

Target.

- 

Finding identifier.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Category.

- 

Success Criterion.

- 

Report date.

- 

Other stable finding metadata.

The recurrence engine shall avoid falsely identifying unrelated findings
as the same finding.

Where exact recurrence cannot be reliably established, ART should
classify the result as a recurring **issue pattern** rather than
claiming that it is the exact same finding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Categories

The Finding Recurrence analytics should distinguish at least:

- 

**Exact/Confirmed Recurrence** — ART can reliably determine that the
same finding reappeared.

- 

**Likely Recurrence** — available data strongly suggests the finding is
recurring but does not provide enough information for absolute
confirmation.

- 

**Issue-Type Recurrence** — the same Issue Type continues to generate
findings.

- 

**Category Recurrence** — the same Category continues to generate
findings.

- 

**Success Criterion Recurrence** — the same WCAG Success Criterion
continues to generate findings.

The dashboard shall clearly explain the distinction between these
categories.

Do not present inferred recurrence as confirmed recurrence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Metrics

The Finding Recurrence section shall support metrics including:

- 

Number of recurring findings.

- 

Percentage of findings that recur.

- 

Number of reports containing recurring issues.

- 

Number of Products affected.

- 

Number of Projects affected.

- 

Number of Workspaces affected.

- 

Number of recurring Issue Types.

- 

Number of recurring Categories.

- 

Number of recurring Success Criteria.

- 

Most frequently recurring issues.

- 

Most frequently recurring Issue Types.

- 

Most frequently recurring Categories.

- 

Most frequently recurring Success Criteria.

- 

Recurrence by severity.

- 

Recurrence by Product.

- 

Recurrence by Project.

- 

Recurrence by Workspace.

- 

Recurrence over time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Over Time

The dashboard shall provide a temporal view of recurring findings.

Users should be able to determine:

- 

When an issue was first identified.

- 

How many times it subsequently appeared.

- 

Which reports identified it.

- 

Which Products were affected.

- 

Which Projects or Workspaces were affected.

- 

Whether recurrence increased or decreased over time.

Where the available data permits, ART should distinguish between:

    First identified
          ↓
    Retested
          ↓
    Still present
          ↓
    Reported again
          ↓
    Resolved
          ↓
    Reappeared

The dashboard shall not imply that an issue was resolved merely because
it was absent from a later report unless the available report data
explicitly supports that conclusion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Comparisons Tab

The **Products** tab shall provide organization-level comparison of
Products.

Users shall be able to select two or more Products belonging to the same
Organization and compare available metrics.

Product comparisons shall support:

- 

Total Reports.

- 

Total Audits.

- 

Total Findings.

- 

Findings by Severity.

- 

Findings by Category.

- 

Findings by Issue Type.

- 

Findings by Accessibility Standard.

- 

Findings by WCAG Success Criterion.

- 

Passed Findings.

- 

Failed Findings.

- 

Manual Review Findings.

- 

Not Tested Findings.

- 

Testing Coverage.

- 

Pages/Screens/Components Tested.

- 

Finding Recurrence.

- 

Unique Testers.

- 

Finding trends over time.

Only metrics for which the underlying data is available shall be
included.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Comparison Context

Product comparisons shall clearly communicate the scope and methodology
of each comparison.

At minimum, the comparison view shall identify:

- 

Product name.

- 

Organization.

- 

Date range.

- 

Number of reports included.

- 

Number of Projects included.

- 

Number of Workspaces included.

- 

Testing standards represented.

- 

WCAG versions represented, where applicable.

- 

Number of findings included.

This context is important because two Products may have different
testing histories or scopes.

For example, a Product tested across ten audits should not automatically
be interpreted as less accessible than a Product tested once simply
because it has more findings.

The dashboard shall provide enough information for users to interpret
comparisons responsibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Normalized Product Comparisons

Where appropriate and where sufficient data exists, ART may provide
normalized metrics to improve comparison between Products with different
testing scopes.

Potential normalized metrics include:

- 

Findings per page tested.

- 

Findings per screen tested.

- 

Findings per component tested.

- 

Findings per report.

- 

Findings per testing criterion.

- 

Percentage of tested criteria with findings.

Normalized metrics shall clearly identify the denominator.

Do not create normalized statistics when the necessary denominator is
unavailable or unreliable.

Do not imply that a normalized metric represents an objective
accessibility score unless the calculation and methodology explicitly
support such an interpretation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Health

Implement an **Accessibility Health** analytics section.

Accessibility Health shall provide a high-level summary of measurable
accessibility indicators across the selected organization.

It shall not be presented as a definitive measure of an organization's
accessibility or legal compliance.

Instead, it should provide an evidence-based summary of available
testing data.

Potential indicators include:

- 

Total Findings.

- 

Failed Findings.

- 

High/Critical severity findings, when applicable.

- 

Testing Coverage.

- 

Percentage of tested criteria with findings.

- 

Recurring Findings.

- 

Recurring Issue Types.

- 

Findings over time.

- 

Resolution trends, when reliable resolution data exists.

- 

Products with significant recurring issues.

- 

Categories with increasing finding frequency.

- 

WCAG Success Criteria with recurring failures.

- 

Testing activity over time.

- 

Percentage of reports with complete metadata.

- 

Percentage of reports with Organization/Client populated.

- 

Percentage of reports with Product populated.

- 

Unique testers, when available.

The Health section shall clearly identify which indicators are available
and which are unavailable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Health Interpretation

Do not reduce Accessibility Health to a single unexplained numerical
score.

If ART eventually provides an overall health score, the score must:

- 

Have a documented calculation.

- 

Identify all inputs.

- 

Explain weighting.

- 

Explain limitations.

- 

Avoid implying legal compliance.

- 

Avoid implying that fewer reported findings always means better
accessibility.

- 

Account for testing coverage.

- 

Account for the possibility that missing or incomplete data affects the
result.

A dashboard containing a single number without explanatory context shall
not be considered sufficient.

The initial implementation may instead provide a collection of clearly
labeled indicators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Benchmarking

Implement an **Organization Benchmarking** analytics section.

Benchmarking shall allow authorized users to compare an organization's
metrics against appropriate reference data.

Benchmarking should support comparisons such as:

- 

Organization's current period vs. previous period.

- 

Organization's Product A vs. Product B.

- 

Organization's current testing coverage vs. historical testing coverage.

- 

Organization's current finding distribution vs. its historical
distribution.

- 

Organization's current recurrence rate vs. its previous recurrence rate.

If ART later introduces anonymized cross-organization benchmarking, that
functionality must require explicit product-level support and
appropriate privacy protections.

Do not automatically expose one organization's private metrics to
another organization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Internal Organization Benchmarking

The initial benchmarking implementation shall prioritize **internal
benchmarking**.

Examples:

    Q2 2026 vs. Q1 2026

    Findings
    Q1: 142
    Q2: 98

    Recurring Findings
    Q1: 31
    Q2: 18

    Testing Coverage
    Q1: 64%
    Q2: 82%

and:

    Product A
        2.8 findings per page tested

    Product B
        1.7 findings per page tested

    Product C
        4.1 findings per page tested

The dashboard shall make it clear that these are comparisons within the
selected organization and do not constitute industry benchmarks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Benchmarking Data Integrity

Benchmarking shall only be performed when the compared datasets are
sufficiently compatible.

Before presenting a comparison, ART should consider:

- 

Testing scope.

- 

Date range.

- 

Number of reports.

- 

Number of pages/screens/components.

- 

Accessibility standards.

- 

WCAG versions.

- 

Conformance levels.

- 

Testing methodology.

- 

Available metadata.

- 

Finding taxonomy.

If datasets are materially different, ART should provide a warning or
contextual explanation rather than presenting a potentially misleading
comparison.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Filters

Organization Statistics shall provide a consistent filtering model
across applicable tabs.

Filters should include:

- 

Organization.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report.

- 

Date range.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

WCAG version.

- 

Conformance level.

- 

Severity.

- 

Category.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Finding status.

- 

Tester, where available.

Not every filter needs to appear on every tab.

The implementation shall display only filters relevant to the selected
analytics section.

When a filter changes, all applicable metrics in the active tab shall
update consistently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter State and User Context

The dashboard shall clearly communicate the currently active filter
scope.

For example:

    Organization: Acme Corporation
    Product: Customer Portal
    Date Range: January 1 – June 30, 2026
    Severity: High + Critical

Users shall be able to determine which data is represented without
relying solely on visual styling.

Filter state shall be accessible to screen readers.

Changing filters shall not unexpectedly move keyboard focus.

The active tab and filter state should remain stable when the user
navigates between applicable analytics sections.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Data Scope

Every Organization Statistics calculation shall have a clearly defined
scope.

The implementation shall know whether a metric represents:

- 

One Report.

- 

Multiple Reports.

- 

One Workspace.

- 

Multiple Workspaces.

- 

One Project.

- 

Multiple Projects.

- 

One Product.

- 

Multiple Products.

- 

The entire selected Organization.

- 

A selected time period.

The dashboard shall not combine metrics from different scopes without
clearly identifying the resulting aggregation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No Double Counting

The metrics engine shall prevent double counting when data is aggregated
across multiple levels.

For example, if:

    Organization
     └── Product A
          ├── Project 1
          │    ├── Workspace 1
          │    └── Workspace 2
          └── Project 2
               └── Workspace 3

contains reports that are represented through multiple relationships,
the same underlying report or finding shall not be counted multiple
times merely because it is associated with both a Project and Workspace.

The metrics framework shall use stable source identifiers where
available.

If stable identifiers are unavailable, the implementation shall use the
most reliable available combination of source information and shall
document any limitations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Refresh

Organization Metrics shall update when relevant source data changes.

The implementation should support:

- 

Automatic recalculation when source report data changes.

- 

Recalculation when reports are added or removed.

- 

Recalculation when Organization/Client metadata changes.

- 

Recalculation when Product metadata changes.

- 

Recalculation when Projects or Workspaces change.

- 

Recalculation when applicable Tester information changes.

If metrics are cached for performance, the cache must be invalidated or
refreshed when the underlying data changes.

Users shall not be required to manually rebuild the entire organization
statistics dataset after ordinary report edits.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Statistics Data Quality Indicators

The dashboard shall provide data-quality information where appropriate.

Potential indicators include:

- 

Reports with missing Organization/Client.

- 

Reports with missing Product.

- 

Reports with missing Tester/Tester Name.

- 

Reports with missing dates.

- 

Reports with incompatible standards.

- 

Reports with incomplete finding status data.

- 

Reports excluded from a particular metric because required data is
unavailable.

These indicators shall help users understand why a metric may not
represent the entire organization's activity.

The dashboard should not silently exclude significant amounts of data
without providing an appropriate indication.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Accessibility Requirements

All Organization Statistics analytics shall be accessible.

This includes:

- 

Tabs.

- 

Tables.

- 

Charts.

- 

Filters.

- 

Data summaries.

- 

Expandable sections.

- 

Tooltips.

- 

Drill-down controls.

- 

Sorting controls.

- 

Pagination.

- 

Export controls.

- 

Status messages.

- 

Loading states.

- 

Error states.

Charts shall not be the sole method of communicating statistical
information.

Whenever a chart is provided, the underlying data shall also be
available in an accessible format, such as an accessible table or
equivalent textual representation.

Dynamic updates shall not cause screen readers to be repeatedly
interrupted while users interact with filters or analytics controls.

Where a metric updates dynamically, provide appropriate status
information without creating excessive or repetitive announcements.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation Requirements for Part 3

Verify that:

1.  

Projects can be analyzed at the Organization level.

2.  

Workspaces can be analyzed at the Organization level.

3.  

Reports can be identified as contributors to organization statistics.

4.  

Findings can be analyzed over time.

5.  

Finding recurrence is distinguished from simple Issue Type recurrence.

6.  

ART does not falsely identify unrelated findings as the same recurring
finding.

7.  

Product comparisons provide appropriate contextual information.

8.  

Normalized product metrics identify their denominator.

9.  

Accessibility Health does not imply legal compliance or guaranteed
accessibility.

10. 

Benchmarking does not expose private information from another
organization.

11. 

Internal benchmarking can compare current and historical organizational
data.

12. 

Analytics filters update the applicable metrics consistently.

13. 

Active filter scope is accessible and understandable.

14. 

Metrics do not double-count findings or reports.

15. 

Organization Metrics refresh when source data changes.

16. 

Missing or incomplete metadata can be identified.

17. 

Charts have accessible equivalent data representations.

18. 

Dynamic analytics updates do not unnecessarily interrupt screen-reader
users.

19. 

All analytics remain within the user's authorized permission scope.

20. 

Existing Report, Project, Workspace, and stand-alone audit functionality
continues to work without regression.

:::

### Part 4 — Advanced Metrics, Data Quality, Visualization, Export, and User Interaction

#### Remediation and Resolution Analytics

The **Remediation** section shall provide analytics related to the
disposition and resolution of accessibility findings when the underlying
report data supports those calculations.

Where reliable status or resolution data exists, track:

- 

Findings opened.

- 

Findings resolved.

- 

Findings remaining.

- 

Findings reopened.

- 

Findings closed without remediation, where applicable.

- 

Resolution rate.

- 

Reopening rate.

- 

Average time to resolution, when dates are available.

- 

Median time to resolution, when dates are available.

- 

Resolution trends over time.

- 

Resolution by Severity.

- 

Resolution by Category.

- 

Resolution by Issue Type.

- 

Resolution by Product.

- 

Resolution by Project.

- 

Resolution by Workspace.

- 

Resolution by Report.

Do not calculate resolution metrics when the source data does not
provide reliable information about resolution.

A finding disappearing from a later report shall **not automatically be
interpreted as resolved**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Resolution Rate

When sufficient data exists, ART may calculate a resolution rate.

The calculation must clearly identify:

- 

The number of findings considered.

- 

The number considered resolved.

- 

The date range.

- 

The source reports.

- 

The methodology used to determine resolution.

For example:

> 

**Resolution Rate: 72%**\
72 of 100 tracked findings were identified as resolved within the
selected reporting period.

The dashboard shall not display a resolution percentage without making
the underlying population understandable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Time-to-Resolution Analytics

When both an appropriate finding-opened date and resolution date are
available, ART shall support time-to-resolution analytics.

Provide:

- 

Average time to resolution.

- 

Median time to resolution.

- 

Minimum time to resolution.

- 

Maximum time to resolution.

- 

Time-to-resolution by Severity.

- 

Time-to-resolution by Category.

- 

Time-to-resolution by Product.

- 

Time-to-resolution by Project.

- 

Time-to-resolution by Workspace.

Where possible, allow users to identify the distribution rather than
relying exclusively on an average.

Do not infer resolution dates from unrelated report dates unless the
methodology explicitly supports that inference.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Aging

Where sufficient date information exists, provide **Finding Aging**
metrics.

Track findings that remain unresolved or otherwise active for:

- 

Less than 30 days.

- 

30–59 days.

- 

60–89 days.

- 

90–179 days.

- 

180–364 days.

- 

365 days or more.

The age ranges shall be configurable in the future.

The dashboard shall clearly identify the date from which age is
calculated.

If the source data cannot reliably establish the age of a finding, the
finding shall not be assigned an arbitrary age category.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Severity Trends

Organization Metrics shall support analysis of how finding severity
changes over time.

Users should be able to determine whether the organization is
experiencing:

- 

More high-severity findings.

- 

Fewer high-severity findings.

- 

Increasing low-severity findings.

- 

Changes in severity distribution.

- 

Changes in severity by Product.

- 

Changes in severity by Category.

- 

Changes in severity by Issue Type.

A decrease in total findings shall not automatically be interpreted as
an improvement if testing coverage also decreased.

The dashboard should provide sufficient contextual information to allow
users to interpret trends responsibly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Testing Activity Metrics

Track organizational testing activity where the required information is
available.

Potential metrics include:

- 

Number of reports created.

- 

Number of reports completed.

- 

Number of audits completed.

- 

Number of Projects tested.

- 

Number of Workspaces tested.

- 

Number of Products tested.

- 

Number of pages tested.

- 

Number of screens tested.

- 

Number of components tested.

- 

Number of accessibility criteria tested.

- 

Number of unique testers.

- 

Testing activity over time.

Testing activity should be presented separately from finding results.

This distinction is important because increased testing activity can
naturally result in an increased number of reported findings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Analytics

The **Testers** tab shall provide aggregate tester statistics when
Tester or Tester Name information is available.

Support:

- 

Total unique testers.

- 

Unique testers by Product.

- 

Unique testers by Project.

- 

Unique testers by Workspace.

- 

Unique testers by Report.

- 

Unique testers by time period.

- 

Reports per tester, where appropriate.

- 

Products tested by tester, where appropriate.

- 

Projects tested by tester, where appropriate.

Tester analytics shall be focused on understanding **testing activity
and coverage**, not evaluating individual employee performance.

The dashboard shall not create performance rankings, productivity
scores, or employee evaluations unless a separate future requirement
explicitly authorizes that functionality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Identity Matching

The unique tester calculation shall avoid counting the same tester
multiple times solely because of minor differences in how their name is
entered.

For example:

    Jane Smith
    Jane Smith

should be recognized as the same tester.

However, ART shall avoid overly aggressive matching such as assuming:

    Jane Smith
    John Smith

are the same person.

Where an explicit user identifier exists, it should be preferred over
display-name matching.

Where identity cannot be reliably resolved, ART shall preserve the
source values and avoid falsely claiming that two testers are the same
person.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Data Privacy

Tester information may contain personal information.

Organization Metrics shall therefore:

- 

Respect existing permissions.

- 

Avoid exposing tester information to unauthorized users.

- 

Prefer aggregate tester counts where individual identity is unnecessary.

- 

Avoid unnecessary personal information in charts and dashboards.

- 

Avoid creating employee-performance metrics.

- 

Respect applicable privacy requirements.

Where individual tester names are displayed, the user must have
appropriate permission to view them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metadata Completeness Metrics

Provide optional **Metadata Completeness** indicators.

The Organization Statistics Dashboard should be able to report:

- 

Percentage of reports containing Organization/Client.

- 

Percentage of reports containing Product.

- 

Percentage of reports containing Tester/Tester Name.

- 

Percentage of reports containing a valid report date.

- 

Percentage of reports containing required accessibility-standard
information.

- 

Percentage of reports with sufficient data for selected analytics.

For example:

> 

**Organization/Client Metadata Completeness: 94%**

The dashboard should allow users to understand that Organization
Statistics may be incomplete when metadata is incomplete.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Statistics Confidence and Limitations

Where appropriate, the dashboard may provide a **Data Quality** or
**Statistics Confidence** indicator.

This indicator must not imply mathematical certainty or statistical
validity beyond what the underlying data supports.

It may consider factors such as:

- 

Missing Organization/Client values.

- 

Inconsistent Organization/Client values.

- 

Missing Product values.

- 

Missing dates.

- 

Missing Tester information.

- 

Incomplete finding statuses.

- 

Inconsistent accessibility standards.

- 

Incomplete testing coverage.

The dashboard should communicate limitations in plain language.

For example:

> 

**Data Quality Notice:** 8% of reports in the selected date range do not
contain an Organization/Client value and are excluded from
organization-specific aggregation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Data Validation

Provide a mechanism for authorized users to identify potentially
inconsistent organization metadata.

Examples include:

    Acme Corporation
    ACME Corporation
    Acme Corp.
    Acme Corp

The system may identify these as **potentially related organization
values**, but shall not automatically merge them without a reliable
basis.

An authorized user may eventually be able to establish a canonical
organization identity.

The Organization Metrics architecture shall be designed to support such
a future capability.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Canonical Organization Identity

Although the initial implementation uses **Organization/Client**
metadata as the primary grouping value, the architecture should support
a future canonical organization identifier.

For example:

    Organization ID: org_12345
    Organization Name: Acme Corporation

Reports may eventually reference the canonical organization while
preserving the original Organization/Client display value.

Do not require this future organization-ID system to be implemented as
part of this epic unless it is necessary for the core Organization
Metrics architecture.

The current implementation shall remain compatible with future canonical
organization records.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Data Normalization

Organization Metrics calculations shall normalize data only where doing
so is necessary to produce accurate statistics.

Normalization shall not modify the original report data.

Examples include:

- 

Standardizing date interpretation.

- 

Normalizing internal metric identifiers.

- 

Resolving known standard identifiers.

- 

Matching tester identities where reliable identifiers exist.

- 

Mapping equivalent internal statuses where appropriate.

The original source values shall remain available and unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Source Data Preservation

Organization Metrics shall be derived from existing report and project
data without altering source records.

The metrics framework shall not:

- 

Rewrite findings.

- 

Change report metadata.

- 

Modify tester names.

- 

Modify Product names.

- 

Modify Organization/Client values.

- 

Change finding severity.

- 

Change Category values.

- 

Change Issue Types.

- 

Change Success Criteria.

- 

Change Accessibility Standards.

Any normalized or derived value shall exist in the metrics layer rather
than overwriting the original source data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Visualization Requirements

Organization Statistics should use visualizations where they improve
understanding.

Potential visualization types include:

- 

Bar charts.

- 

Stacked bar charts.

- 

Line charts.

- 

Trend charts.

- 

Tables.

- 

Summary cards.

- 

Distribution charts.

- 

Comparison charts.

Do not use visualizations merely for decoration.

Every visualization must communicate meaningful statistical information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Data Representations

Every visual chart shall have an equivalent accessible representation.

For example:

    Visual chart:
    Findings by Category

    Accessible table:
    Category | Findings | Percentage
    Keyboard | 42 | 18.4%
    Forms | 31 | 13.6%
    Contrast | 27 | 11.8%

The accessible representation shall contain the same underlying data
represented visually.

Do not require screen-reader users to interpret a visual chart without
access to its underlying data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Chart Accessibility

Charts shall:

- 

Have meaningful accessible names.

- 

Have meaningful descriptions where necessary.

- 

Expose data values to assistive technologies.

- 

Not depend solely on color.

- 

Use patterns, labels, or text where necessary to distinguish data.

- 

Provide an accessible table or equivalent.

- 

Remain keyboard accessible if interactive.

- 

Announce meaningful state changes without excessive interruption.

- 

Provide sufficient context for axes and data series.

Charts shall not use color as the only method of identifying:

- 

Severity.

- 

Category.

- 

Product.

- 

Status.

- 

Any other metric dimension.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Interactive Data Tables

Where tabular data is used, tables shall be fully accessible.

Support, where applicable:

- 

Correct table semantics.

- 

Accessible column headers.

- 

Accessible row headers where appropriate.

- 

Sortable columns.

- 

Accessible sort state.

- 

Keyboard access to sorting.

- 

Pagination or virtualization that remains accessible.

- 

Clear indication of filtered results.

- 

Accessible empty states.

- 

Accessible loading states.

- 

Accessible error states.

Sorting shall not unexpectedly move keyboard focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Drill-Down Behavior

Users shall be able to drill down from aggregate metrics to the
underlying data when authorized.

For example:

    Organization
        ↓
    Product
        ↓
    Project
        ↓
    Workspace
        ↓
    Report
        ↓
    Finding

The drill-down path shall preserve the applicable filters and context.

Users shall always be able to determine where they are within the
hierarchy.

The drill-down interface shall not expose resources outside the user's
permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Breadcrumbs and Context

Where the dashboard provides hierarchical drill-down, provide accessible
context such as:

> 

Organization: Acme Corporation → Product: Customer Portal → Project: Q2
Audit → Report: June Audit

This context shall be available visually and programmatically.

If breadcrumbs are used, they shall follow accessible navigation
semantics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Back Navigation

Users shall be able to return from a drill-down view to the previous
analytics scope without losing their filter state unnecessarily.

For example:

    Organization Statistics
        ↓
    Product Comparison
        ↓
    Product A
        ↓
    Report
        ↓
    Finding

Returning from the Finding view should restore the previous Report
context.

Returning from the Report view should restore the Product context.

The implementation should preserve:

- 

Active Organization.

- 

Active Product.

- 

Active Project.

- 

Active Workspace.

- 

Date range.

- 

Severity filters.

- 

Category filters.

- 

Issue Type filters.

- 

Other applicable filters.

- 

Previously selected tab.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Export Organization Statistics

Provide an optional mechanism for authorized users to export
Organization Statistics.

Exports should support the report formats already supported by ART where
technically appropriate.

Potential export formats include:

- 

CSV.

- 

Microsoft Excel.

- 

HTML.

- 

Microsoft Word.

- 

PDF.

- 

JSON or another structured data format where appropriate.

The export architecture should reuse the same metrics calculation layer
as the Dashboard.

Do not create separate calculations for exported statistics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Exported Metrics Integrity

Exported Organization Statistics shall contain the same underlying
metric values displayed in the Dashboard for the selected scope and
filters.

Exports shall identify:

- 

Organization.

- 

Date range.

- 

Filters.

- 

Metrics included.

- 

Data limitations.

- 

Data quality warnings, where applicable.

- 

Generation date/time, where appropriate.

If a metric is unavailable in the Dashboard, the export shall not invent
or substitute a value.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Export Accessibility

Organization Statistics exports shall preserve accessibility to the
extent supported by each format.

For example:

- 

HTML exports shall use semantic HTML.

- 

Word exports shall use appropriate heading, table, and document
structure.

- 

PDF exports shall be generated with appropriate accessibility structure
where supported by the existing ART export architecture.

- 

CSV exports shall preserve clear column headings.

- 

Structured-data exports shall preserve machine-readable metric
definitions.

Charts included in exported reports shall have accessible equivalents.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Organization Statistics Views

Authorized users should be able to save commonly used Organization
Statistics configurations as reusable views.

A saved view may include:

- 

Selected Organization.

- 

Selected Product.

- 

Selected Project.

- 

Selected Workspace.

- 

Date range.

- 

Severity.

- 

Category.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

WCAG version.

- 

Selected Dashboard tab.

- 

Selected metrics.

- 

Selected visualization/table configuration.

Saved views shall not bypass permissions.

If the user's permissions change, the saved view shall dynamically adapt
or indicate that some resources are no longer available.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Personal vs. Shared Statistics Views

If ART's collaboration framework supports shared working views,
Organization Statistics views shall follow the same general permission
architecture.

A user may create a **personal Organization Statistics view** without
sharing it.

Authorized users may optionally create a **shared Organization
Statistics view** for other users within the applicable permissions
scope.

A shared view shall not grant access to data the recipient would
otherwise be unable to access.

The saved view stores the configuration, not an authorization override.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Performance

Organization Metrics may involve substantial amounts of data.

The implementation shall be designed to remain responsive when an
organization contains:

- 

Many reports.

- 

Many findings.

- 

Multiple Products.

- 

Multiple Projects.

- 

Multiple Workspaces.

- 

Long historical periods.

- 

Many testers.

The framework should use appropriate techniques such as:

- 

Efficient aggregation.

- 

Caching.

- 

Incremental recalculation.

- 

Lazy loading.

- 

Pagination.

- 

Virtualized data tables where appropriate.

Performance optimizations shall not compromise accessibility or data
accuracy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Loading States

All asynchronous Organization Statistics operations shall provide
accessible loading states.

Loading indicators shall:

- 

Clearly communicate that data is being loaded.

- 

Be announced appropriately to assistive technologies when necessary.

- 

Not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader users.

- 

Not steal keyboard focus.

- 

Preserve the user's current interaction context.

Where possible, existing metrics should remain available while updated
data is being calculated rather than unnecessarily blanking the entire
dashboard.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Error States

Organization Statistics shall provide meaningful error states.

Errors shall explain:

- 

What failed.

- 

Which part of the Dashboard was affected.

- 

Whether existing data remains available.

- 

Whether the user can retry.

- 

Whether the problem is related to permissions, missing data, or a system
error.

Errors shall be accessible to keyboard and screen-reader users.

Do not expose technical stack traces or internal implementation details
to ordinary users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Empty States

When an organization has insufficient data for a particular metric,
provide an informative empty state.

For example:

> 

**No Product data available**\
Product-level statistics require the optional Product field to be
populated in report metadata.

or:

> 

**Tester statistics unavailable**\
No Tester/Tester Name information is available in the selected reports.

Empty states shall explain what information is missing when doing so
would help the user understand how to obtain meaningful statistics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation Requirements for Part 4

Verify that:

1.  

Remediation statistics are only calculated when reliable resolution data
exists.

2.  

ART does not infer resolution simply because a finding disappears from a
later report.

3.  

Finding aging uses reliable dates.

4.  

Tester metrics count unique testers appropriately.

5.  

Tester analytics do not become employee-performance rankings.

6.  

Organization metadata quality can be measured.

7.  

Source report data remains unchanged by metrics processing.

8.  

Derived/normalized metrics do not overwrite source values.

9.  

Charts have accessible equivalent data.

10. 

Tables expose correct headers, sorting state, and filter state.

11. 

Drill-down navigation preserves context.

12. 

Users cannot drill into unauthorized resources.

13. 

Organization Statistics can be exported without recalculating the
metrics separately.

14. 

Exported values match the Dashboard values for the same scope and
filters.

15. 

Saved views do not bypass permissions.

16. 

Shared views do not expose unauthorized organization data.

17. 

Loading states do not steal focus.

18. 

Dynamic updates do not repeatedly interrupt screen-reader users.

19. 

Error and empty states are accessible.

20. 

Organization Statistics remains usable with large datasets.

21. 

Existing report and audit functionality is unaffected.

:::

### Part 5 — Configuration, Dashboard Customization, Permissions, and Integration with ART

#### Organization Statistics Configuration

Provide an **Organization Statistics Settings** interface accessible
through the **Organization** menu when Organization Statistics is
enabled.

The configuration interface shall allow authorized users to control
which Organization Statistics features are available.

Configuration options may include:

- 

Enable/disable specific analytics sections.

- 

Configure available dashboard tabs.

- 

Configure default date ranges.

- 

Configure default filters.

- 

Configure which metrics appear in the Overview tab.

- 

Configure whether Product analytics are displayed.

- 

Configure whether Tester analytics are displayed.

- 

Configure whether Finding Recurrence analytics are displayed.

- 

Configure whether Accessibility Health is displayed.

- 

Configure whether Organization Benchmarking is displayed.

- 

Configure available export formats.

- 

Configure data-retention or aggregation behavior where applicable.

Do not place organization-specific configuration exclusively in
Application Settings when it logically belongs to the Organization
configuration model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Application-Level vs. Organization-Level Configuration

Maintain a clear distinction between:

**Application Settings**

Controls whether the Organization Metrics Framework is enabled.

**Organization Settings**

Controls organization-specific metrics, configuration, and behavior.

**Dashboard Settings**

Controls the user's personal Dashboard presentation.

For example:

    Application Settings
    └── Organization Statistics
        └── Enabled / Disabled

    Organization Menu
    └── Organization Settings
        ├── Metrics Configuration
        ├── Analytics Configuration
        └── Organization Data

    Dashboard Settings
    └── Organization Statistics
        └── Show / Hide

Do not duplicate settings unnecessarily.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Default Analytics Sections

When Organization Statistics is first enabled, the Dashboard shall
display a sensible default set of analytics sections.

At minimum, the default configuration should include:

- 

Overview.

- 

Findings.

- 

Categories.

- 

Issue Types.

- 

Accessibility Standards.

- 

Testing Coverage.

- 

Products.

- 

Testers.

- 

Trends.

- 

Recurrence.

- 

Accessibility Health.

- 

Organization Benchmarking.

The user may subsequently customize which sections are displayed,
subject to applicable permissions and organization-level configuration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Section Visibility

Users shall be able to show or hide available Organization Statistics
sections.

Hiding a section shall:

- 

Remove it from the user's Dashboard presentation.

- 

Not delete the underlying data.

- 

Not disable metrics collection.

- 

Not affect other users.

- 

Not affect saved reports.

- 

Not affect exported statistics.

- 

Not alter source reports.

Re-enabling the section shall restore access to the metrics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization-Configured Analytics

Authorized Organization administrators may configure which Organization
Statistics features are available to members of the organization.

For example, an organization administrator may choose to make:

- 

Findings Analytics available.

- 

Product Analytics available.

- 

Tester Analytics available.

- 

Recurrence Analytics available.

while disabling:

- 

Organization Benchmarking.

- 

Individual tester details.

- 

Certain export capabilities.

Organization-level configuration shall never grant a user permissions
they do not otherwise possess.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Personal Dashboard Preferences

Individual users shall be able to customize their personal Organization
Statistics Dashboard where permitted.

Personal preferences may include:

- 

Visible tabs.

- 

Selected default tab.

- 

Default filters.

- 

Default date range.

- 

Preferred chart/table representation.

- 

Saved views.

- 

Dashboard section visibility.

A user's personal preferences shall not modify the Organization's global
configuration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Organization Dashboard Views

If the collaboration framework permits shared working views, authorized
users may create shared Organization Statistics views.

A shared view may define:

- 

Selected analytics tab.

- 

Selected Organization.

- 

Selected Product.

- 

Selected Project.

- 

Selected Workspace.

- 

Date range.

- 

Filters.

- 

Visible metrics.

- 

Chart/table preferences.

A shared view shall contain configuration only.

It shall not contain embedded authorization privileges.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Administrator Permissions

Users with appropriate Organization Administrator permissions may be
allowed to:

- 

Configure Organization Statistics.

- 

Manage organization-level settings.

- 

Configure available analytics.

- 

Manage organization-level saved views.

- 

Create shared Organization Statistics views.

- 

Manage organization metadata.

- 

Access organization-level exports.

- 

View organization-wide statistics.

These capabilities shall remain subject to the application's broader
permission model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Contributor Permissions

Organization Contributors may have access to Organization Statistics
according to their assigned permissions.

A Contributor may be able to:

- 

View permitted Organization Statistics.

- 

Create personal analytics views.

- 

Apply filters.

- 

Drill into permitted Reports, Projects, Workspaces, and Products.

- 

Export permitted data.

Contributors shall not automatically receive Organization Administrator
capabilities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Viewer Permissions

Organization Viewers may have read-only access to Organization
Statistics.

A Viewer may be able to:

- 

View authorized metrics.

- 

Apply non-persistent filters.

- 

Navigate between analytics tabs.

- 

Drill into authorized read-only resources.

- 

Use personal read-only views.

A Viewer shall not be able to:

- 

Modify organization configuration.

- 

Change organization-wide analytics settings.

- 

Edit source Reports.

- 

Modify Product metadata.

- 

Modify Organization/Client metadata unless separately authorized.

- 

Create organization-wide shared configurations unless explicitly
permitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report-Level Organization Statistics Permissions

Organization Statistics shall support modular permissions.

A user may have access to:

- 

One Report.

- 

Several Reports.

- 

A Project.

- 

A Workspace.

- 

A Product.

- 

An entire Organization.

Access to one resource shall not automatically grant access to all other
resources.

Organization-level aggregation shall only include data from resources
the user is authorized to include in that metric.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Partial-Access Organizations

The dashboard shall correctly handle situations where a user has access
to only part of an organization.

For example:

    Organization
    ├── Product A ← User can access
    ├── Product B ← User can access
    └── Product C ← User cannot access

The user may see statistics based on Products A and B, but shall not
receive information about Product C.

ART shall clearly communicate when metrics represent the user's
authorized subset rather than necessarily the organization's complete
dataset.

For example:

> 

**Statistics reflect resources available to you.**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Statistics Scope Indicator

The Dashboard shall clearly indicate whether the displayed metrics
represent:

- 

The entire organization available to the user.

- 

A selected Product.

- 

A selected Project.

- 

A selected Workspace.

- 

A selected set of Reports.

- 

A filtered subset.

This indicator shall be available visually and programmatically.

Do not require users to infer the metric scope from the selected tab
alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Selection

If multiple organizations are available to the user, provide an
accessible mechanism for selecting the Organization whose statistics are
being viewed.

The Organization selector shall:

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Have a meaningful accessible name.

- 

Announce the selected organization.

- 

Support screen readers.

- 

Respect permissions.

- 

Avoid exposing unauthorized organization names or information.

- 

Clearly indicate when no Organization/Client value is available.

If only one organization is available, ART may automatically select it
without requiring unnecessary interaction.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multiple Organization Support

ART shall support users who work with multiple organizations.

For example:

    Organization A
        Reports 1–20

    Organization B
        Reports 21–35

    Organization C
        Reports 36–50

Statistics shall remain logically separated.

Changing the selected organization shall update all applicable metrics.

ART shall not combine multiple organizations into one Organization
Statistics dataset unless the user explicitly selects an aggregation
mechanism that is authorized and supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stand-Alone Reports

Stand-alone reports shall continue to function independently of
Organization Statistics.

A user may create:

    Organization/Client: [blank]
    Product: [blank]

and use ART normally.

Such reports may still use:

- 

Report Analytics.

- 

Finding Analytics.

- 

Export functionality.

- 

Templates.

- 

Other existing ART features.

They simply shall not contribute to an Organization's statistics unless
they are subsequently associated with an organization through a
supported workflow.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Assignment Changes

If an authorized user changes a report's Organization/Client value:

    Organization/Client:
    Old Organization
    ↓
    New Organization

ART shall update the applicable Organization Metrics accordingly.

The report shall be removed from the old organization's applicable
statistics and included in the new organization's applicable statistics.

If metrics are cached, the relevant caches must be invalidated.

The system shall not leave stale organization statistics after the
metadata change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Assignment Changes

The same principle shall apply when Product metadata changes.

If:

    Product:
    Product A
    ↓
    Product B

the applicable Product statistics shall be recalculated.

The report shall not continue contributing to Product A after the
change.

Historical metrics shall use the appropriate source data and documented
methodology.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Metrics and Templates

Organization Metrics shall not require Organization/Client or Product
fields to be present in every template.

However, the template system should support these fields where the
template is intended for organization-level reporting.

When a template includes Organization/Client or Product metadata, those
values shall be incorporated into Organization Metrics when the
resulting report is saved.

Template configuration shall not automatically assign a report to an
organization unless the user intentionally supplies or confirms the
organization value.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Metrics and Report Imports

When reports are imported into ART, Organization Metrics shall use the
imported report metadata.

Imported reports containing:

    Organization/Client: Acme Corporation
    Product: Customer Portal

shall become eligible for the appropriate Organization and Product
metrics after successful import.

Import processing shall not silently discard Organization/Client or
Product metadata.

If imported reports contain incomplete or inconsistent organization
metadata, ART shall preserve the source values and reflect the resulting
data-quality limitations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Metrics and Report Exports

Exporting a report shall not alter its Organization Metrics
relationships.

Where report metadata is included in an export, the Organization/Client
and Product values shall be preserved according to the existing export
format's capabilities.

Exporting a report shall not create a duplicate metric record.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Metrics and Collaboration

Organization Metrics shall integrate with ART's collaboration framework.

When collaboration is enabled:

- 

Organization permissions shall remain distinct from Report permissions.

- 

Report permissions shall remain modular.

- 

Workspace permissions shall remain modular.

- 

Organization-level permissions shall control access to organization-wide
statistics.

- 

Shared Organization Statistics views shall respect all underlying
permissions.

A user must not gain access to a Report merely because the Report
contributes to an Organization metric they are allowed to view.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Metrics and Plugins

If ART's plugin framework supports Organization Statistics integrations,
plugins may be:

- 

Personal.

- 

Shared within a Workspace.

- 

Shared within an Organization.

- 

Available globally.

A plugin shall only receive access to Organization Metrics data that the
current user and plugin permissions authorize.

Plugins shall not bypass the Organization Metrics permission model.

Organization-specific analytics plugins shall use the same metrics
definitions and data-access APIs as the built-in Dashboard where
possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Metrics API / Internal Service Layer

Implement the Organization Metrics functionality through a clearly
defined internal service or API layer.

The Dashboard should not directly calculate organization-level metrics
from raw report objects.

A conceptual architecture should be:

    Reports / Projects / Workspaces
                ↓
         Metrics Data Layer
                ↓
        Organization Metrics API
                ↓
     Dashboard / Exports / Plugins

The metrics layer should provide reusable methods for retrieving:

- 

Counts.

- 

Percentages.

- 

Trends.

- 

Aggregations.

- 

Recurrence.

- 

Product comparisons.

- 

Tester counts.

- 

Category analytics.

- 

Testing coverage.

- 

Accessibility Health indicators.

- 

Benchmarking metrics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Consistent Metric Definitions

Each metric shall have one authoritative definition.

For example:

> 

**Total Findings**

must mean the same thing wherever it appears within the Organization
Metrics framework.

Metric definitions should specify:

- 

Name.

- 

Description.

- 

Source data.

- 

Calculation.

- 

Required fields.

- 

Applicable filters.

- 

Scope.

- 

Limitations.

- 

Whether the metric supports historical calculation.

Do not create slightly different versions of the same metric for
different Dashboard tabs.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metric Metadata

The metrics framework should expose metadata describing each metric.

For example:

    Metric:
    Total Findings

    Description:
    Total number of findings within the selected scope.

    Source:
    Report findings

    Requires:
    Finding data

    Supports:
    Organization
    Product
    Project
    Workspace
    Report
    Date Range
    Severity
    Category
    Issue Type

This metadata can later support:

- 

Dashboard configuration.

- 

Documentation.

- 

Plugin development.

- 

Export generation.

- 

Accessibility descriptions.

- 

Command Palette integration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Command Palette Integration

When Organization Statistics is enabled, relevant Organization commands
shall be available through ART's existing Command Palette/Command
Search.

Potential commands include:

- 

Open Organization Statistics.

- 

Open Organization Overview.

- 

Open Organization Findings.

- 

Open Product Comparisons.

- 

Open Finding Recurrence.

- 

Open Accessibility Health.

- 

Open Organization Benchmarking.

- 

Open Organization Settings.

- 

Configure Organization Statistics.

Commands shall:

- 

Have meaningful names.

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Respect permissions.

- 

Not appear when Organization Statistics is disabled.

- 

Not expose inaccessible or unauthorized destinations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Menu Bar Integration

When Organization Statistics is enabled, add the **Organization** menu
to the menu bar.

The menu should organize commands logically rather than creating a long,
flat list.

A conceptual structure might be:

    Organization
    ├── Statistics
    │   ├── Overview
    │   ├── Findings
    │   ├── Categories
    │   ├── Products
    │   ├── Testers
    │   ├── Trends
    │   ├── Recurrence
    │   ├── Accessibility Health
    │   └── Benchmarking
    ├── Organization Settings
    └── Configure Organization Statistics

The final structure should follow ART's existing menu conventions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Global Context Menu Integration

If ART provides a global context menu for commands and actions, relevant
Organization Statistics commands may be made available there when
Organization Statistics is enabled.

Do not add unnecessary context-menu commands.

Only actions that are useful in the user's current context should be
exposed.

All context-menu commands must respect permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Keyboard Shortcuts

Keyboard shortcuts may be provided for frequently used Organization
Statistics commands.

Shortcuts shall:

- 

Follow ART's existing keyboard shortcut architecture.

- 

Avoid conflicts with existing shortcuts.

- 

Be configurable where ART supports configurable shortcuts.

- 

Be documented.

- 

Be announced appropriately to screen-reader users.

- 

Not be required for basic Organization Statistics access.

Do not introduce a large number of new global shortcuts merely to expose
every analytics function.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Optional Collaboration Toolbar

Do not enable an Organization or Collaboration toolbar by default merely
to expose these new commands.

If ART's existing collaboration architecture includes an optional
toolbar, Organization commands may be incorporated where appropriate.

The Organization menu and Command Palette shall remain the primary
command-discovery mechanisms.

This is intended to prevent Organization Statistics from unnecessarily
increasing interface clutter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### User Experience and Interface Clutter

The Organization Metrics feature shall prioritize information density
without overwhelming the user.

Do not display every metric simultaneously.

Use:

- 

Tabs.

- 

Expandable sections.

- 

Filters.

- 

Drill-downs.

- 

Summary cards.

- 

Tables.

- 

Progressive disclosure.

Avoid:

- 

Large walls of statistics.

- 

Redundant charts.

- 

Duplicate controls.

- 

Unnecessary persistent toolbars.

- 

Excessive notifications.

- 

Automatically opening multiple analytics panels.

The initial Dashboard view should provide a concise overview while
allowing users to progressively explore deeper analytics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Responsive Layout

The Organization Statistics Dashboard shall remain usable at different
viewport sizes and zoom levels.

Support:

- 

Browser zoom.

- 

Reflow.

- 

Keyboard navigation.

- 

Screen magnification.

- 

Narrow viewport layouts.

Do not rely on fixed-width charts or controls that become inaccessible
when users zoom.

Interactive controls must remain reachable and usable at high zoom
levels.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Requirements for Configuration

All Organization Statistics settings and controls shall meet ART's
accessibility requirements.

At minimum:

- 

Correct labels.

- 

Correct descriptions.

- 

Correct keyboard operation.

- 

Correct focus management.

- 

Correct screen-reader announcements.

- 

Correct state information.

- 

No keyboard traps.

- 

No inaccessible custom widgets.

- 

Sufficient focus indicators.

- 

Logical reading order.

- 

Logical tab order.

Dynamic settings changes shall not unexpectedly move focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation Requirements for Part 5

Verify that:

1.  

Organization Statistics configuration is available through the
Organization menu.

2.  

Application Settings, Organization Settings, and Dashboard Settings
remain clearly differentiated.

3.  

Users can customize which analytics sections are displayed.

4.  

Personal Dashboard preferences do not modify organization-wide settings.

5.  

Shared views respect permissions.

6.  

Organization selection respects permissions.

7.  

Multiple organizations remain statistically separated.

8.  

Stand-alone reports continue to work normally.

9.  

Changing Organization/Client metadata updates applicable metrics.

10. 

Changing Product metadata updates applicable Product metrics.

11. 

Imported reports preserve Organization/Client and Product metadata.

12. 

Exported reports preserve applicable metadata.

13. 

Organization Metrics respect collaboration permissions.

14. 

Plugins cannot bypass Organization Metrics permissions.

15. 

Metrics are exposed through a reusable service/API layer.

16. 

Metric definitions remain consistent across Dashboard sections and
exports.

17. 

Organization commands are available through the Command Palette when
enabled.

18. 

The Organization menu appears only when Organization Statistics is
enabled.

19. 

The interface does not become unnecessarily cluttered.

20. 

Organization Statistics remains accessible at high zoom and with
keyboard and screen-reader navigation.

21. 

Existing ART functionality remains unaffected when Organization
Statistics is disabled.

:::

### Part 6 — Metrics Data Model, Aggregation Engine, Historical Data, and Performance

#### Organization Metrics Data Model

Implement a dedicated internal data model for Organization Metrics.

The data model shall support relationships among:

- 

Organizations.

- 

Products.

- 

Projects.

- 

Workspaces.

- 

Reports.

- 

Audits.

- 

Findings.

- 

Categories.

- 

Issue Types.

- 

Accessibility Standards.

- 

WCAG Success Criteria.

- 

Testers.

- 

Testing targets.

- 

Dates and time periods.

The metrics model shall derive its information from existing ART data
whenever possible rather than creating duplicate authoritative records.

A conceptual relationship may be:

    Organization
        │
        ├── Products
        │     └── Reports
        │
        ├── Projects
        │     └── Workspaces
        │           └── Reports
        │
        └── Reports
              ├── Findings
              ├── Tester
              ├── Product
              ├── Category
              ├── Issue Type
              └── Accessibility Standard

The implementation may use a different internal structure provided that
the same relationships and aggregation capabilities are supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Source-of-Truth Principle

Existing ART report data shall remain the authoritative source for
report-level information.

The Organization Metrics layer shall be a **derived analytics layer**.

Do not create a second authoritative copy of:

- 

Report findings.

- 

Organization/Client values.

- 

Product values.

- 

Tester values.

- 

Category values.

- 

Issue Types.

- 

Accessibility Standards.

- 

WCAG Success Criteria.

If a derived metrics record is maintained for performance, it must be
possible to regenerate it from the underlying source data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stable Identifiers

Where ART already provides stable identifiers, the Organization Metrics
framework shall use them.

Prefer stable identifiers for:

- 

Reports.

- 

Findings.

- 

Projects.

- 

Workspaces.

- 

Products.

- 

Organizations.

- 

Testers.

- 

Templates.

Do not use display names as primary database identifiers when stable
identifiers are available.

This is particularly important when users rename:

- 

Organizations.

- 

Products.

- 

Projects.

- 

Workspaces.

- 

Reports.

A rename should not create a second logical entity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Identity

The initial implementation shall derive organization grouping from the
**Organization/Client** metadata value.

However, the metrics architecture should allow future introduction of a
canonical Organization ID.

The implementation should therefore separate:

    Organization Identity

from:

    Organization Display Name

where practical.

This will allow a future organization-management system to associate
multiple historical display-name variations with one canonical
organization without requiring a redesign of the metrics engine.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Identity

The Product field shall similarly support stable product identity in the
future.

For the initial implementation, Product may be identified by the Product
metadata value.

The architecture should allow future product records to provide:

- 

Product ID.

- 

Product Name.

- 

Organization ID.

- 

Product Status.

- 

Product Type.

- 

Product URL.

- 

Other product metadata.

Do not require all of these fields for the initial implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Dimensions

The metrics engine shall support reusable dimensions.

At minimum:

- 

Organization.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report.

- 

Date.

- 

Severity.

- 

Status.

- 

Category.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

WCAG Version.

- 

Conformance Level.

- 

Success Criterion.

- 

Tester.

- 

Testing Target.

The engine shall support combining dimensions.

For example:

    Organization
        + Product
        + Category
        + Severity
        + Date Range

may produce:

> 

Customer Portal → Keyboard Accessibility → High Severity → Q2 2026

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Measures

The metrics framework shall support reusable measures.

At minimum:

- 

Count.

- 

Percentage.

- 

Unique Count.

- 

Rate.

- 

Average.

- 

Median.

- 

Minimum.

- 

Maximum.

- 

Trend.

- 

Distribution.

Not every measure applies to every metric.

The implementation shall define which measures are valid for each
metric.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Count vs. Unique Count

The metrics engine shall distinguish between:

**Count**

The total number of records or findings.

**Unique Count**

The number of distinct entities represented by those records.

Examples:

    Findings Count:
    245

    Unique Reports:
    18

    Unique Products:
    4

    Unique Projects:
    7

    Unique Testers:
    11

Do not substitute a simple count where a unique count is required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Percentage Calculations

Percentage metrics shall clearly define their denominator.

For example:

    Category Percentage =
    Category Findings / Total Findings × 100

The denominator shall reflect the active filter and aggregation scope.

If a user filters to:

    Product: Customer Portal
    Date: Q2 2026
    Severity: High

the percentage shall be calculated against the findings remaining in
that filtered scope.

The Dashboard shall not use an organization-wide denominator when the
user is viewing a filtered subset unless this behavior is explicitly
identified.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Percentage Rounding

Percentages shall use consistent rounding across the Dashboard.

The implementation should use a sensible precision such as:

- 

Whole percentages for high-level summaries.

- 

One decimal place for detailed analytics.

For example:

> 

18.4%

rather than:

> 

18.437829%

The underlying calculation shall retain sufficient precision.

Displayed rounding must not cause totals to appear materially incorrect.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Time Dimensions

The metrics framework shall support time-based aggregation.

Where applicable, support:

- 

Day.

- 

Week.

- 

Month.

- 

Quarter.

- 

Year.

- 

Custom date range.

The date field used for each metric shall be explicitly defined.

Potential date fields include:

- 

Report creation date.

- 

Report completion date.

- 

Audit date.

- 

Finding creation date.

- 

Finding resolution date.

- 

Testing date.

Do not substitute one date for another without documenting the
calculation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Historical Metrics

Organization Metrics shall support historical analysis.

When a report's metadata or findings change, the implementation must
determine whether historical metrics should reflect:

1.  

The current state of the report.

2.  

The state at the time of the historical measurement.

The initial implementation should prioritize consistency and
transparency.

If true historical snapshots are not available, ART shall not imply that
historical metrics represent the exact state of the data at that earlier
point in time.

The User Guide shall document this limitation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Historical Organization Changes

If a report changes Organization/Client:

    Report A
    Organization: Organization A

    later changed to:

    Organization: Organization B

ART shall ensure current organization statistics reflect the current
assignment.

If historical organization-level statistics are supported using
snapshots, the historical methodology must be clearly documented.

Do not silently present current metadata as though it represented
historical organizational ownership.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Historical Product Changes

Apply the same principle to Product.

If:

    Report A
    Product: Product A

    later changed to:

    Product: Product B

current metrics should reflect Product B.

Historical metrics shall only claim to represent the previous Product
assignment if ART has sufficient historical data to support that
conclusion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Date Range Handling

All date-range filters shall define whether their boundaries are:

- 

Inclusive.

- 

Exclusive.

- 

Based on local time.

- 

Based on UTC.

Use a consistent strategy throughout Organization Statistics.

The selected date range shall be clearly communicated to users.

Avoid off-by-one-day errors caused by timezone conversions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Time Zone Handling

ART shall use a consistent timezone strategy for Organization Metrics.

Where a report contains an explicit timezone, preserve it where
appropriate.

Where no timezone is available, use ART's established application
timezone behavior.

The Dashboard shall not silently shift dates in a way that changes the
user's understanding of which reporting period a report belongs to.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Aggregation Across Hierarchies

The metrics engine shall support aggregation across organizational
hierarchies without double counting.

For example:

    Organization
     ├── Product A
     │    ├── Project 1
     │    │    └── Report 1
     │    └── Project 2
     │         └── Report 2
     │
     └── Product B
          └── Project 3
               └── Report 3

The Organization-level count of Reports must be:

> 

3

not:

> 

6

because the same reports appear in multiple related dimensions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Many-to-Many Relationships

The metrics architecture shall account for situations where
relationships are not strictly hierarchical.

For example, a report may:

- 

Belong to one Project.

- 

Reference multiple Products.

- 

Be associated with multiple Testing Standards.

- 

Contain multiple Testers.

- 

Contain findings associated with multiple Categories.

The metrics engine must define how such relationships affect counts and
percentages.

Do not assume every entity has exactly one parent.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multi-Product Reports

If a report can legitimately contain testing information for multiple
Products, the metrics engine shall support this without double counting
the underlying findings.

The Product-level metric definition shall clearly distinguish between:

- 

Findings associated with a specific Product.

- 

Findings associated with the overall Report.

If ART does not currently support multi-Product reports, the
architecture should not prevent this capability from being added later.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multi-Tester Reports

If multiple testers are associated with a report, unique tester
calculations shall count each distinct tester once within the
appropriate scope.

For example:

    Report A
    Testers:
    Jane Smith
    John Smith

    Report B
    Testers:
    Jane Smith
    Alex Smith

Organization unique testers:

> 

3

not:

> 

4

The Dashboard may separately display tester participation counts where
meaningful.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Findings With Multiple Classifications

If a finding can contain multiple:

- 

Categories.

- 

Issue Types.

- 

Success Criteria.

- 

Accessibility Standards.
