the metrics framework must define whether the finding contributes to:

- 

One classification.

- 

Multiple classifications.

- 

A primary classification plus secondary classifications.

Do not silently count the same finding multiple times without making the
aggregation methodology clear.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metric Calculation Metadata

Each derived metric should retain enough metadata to identify:

- 

Source.

- 

Scope.

- 

Calculation.

- 

Dimensions.

- 

Filters.

- 

Date range.

- 

Calculation timestamp, if relevant.

- 

Data-quality limitations.

This information will support:

- 

Dashboard transparency.

- 

Export generation.

- 

Debugging.

- 

Future plugins.

- 

Future APIs.

- 

User documentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Incremental Updates

Where practical, the metrics framework should support incremental
recalculation.

For example, when one report changes:

    Report changed
          ↓
    Identify affected metrics
          ↓
    Recalculate affected aggregates
          ↓
    Invalidate affected cached results
          ↓
    Update Dashboard

Do not unnecessarily recalculate every organization's statistics after a
change to a single report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Cache Invalidation

If Organization Metrics are cached, define explicit cache invalidation
rules.

Caches shall be invalidated when relevant source data changes,
including:

- 

Report creation.

- 

Report deletion.

- 

Report import.

- 

Report metadata changes.

- 

Organization/Client changes.

- 

Product changes.

- 

Finding changes.

- 

Finding status changes.

- 

Finding severity changes.

- 

Category changes.

- 

Issue Type changes.

- 

Tester changes.

- 

Project changes.

- 

Workspace changes.

Stale cached metrics must not remain visible after the underlying data
has changed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Large Organization Support

The metrics architecture shall be designed to support organizations
containing potentially large datasets.

The implementation should not assume that an organization contains only:

- 

A few reports.

- 

A few findings.

- 

One Product.

- 

One Project.

It should support growth to:

- 

Hundreds or thousands of reports.

- 

Large numbers of findings.

- 

Many Products.

- 

Many Projects.

- 

Many Workspaces.

- 

Large historical datasets.

Performance testing should include representative large datasets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Lazy Loading

Where a Dashboard section contains a large dataset, use lazy loading
where appropriate.

For example:

    Open Organization Statistics
            ↓
    Load Overview
            ↓
    User opens Findings
            ↓
    Load Findings Analytics
            ↓
    User opens Recurrence
            ↓
    Load Recurrence Analytics

Do not calculate every expensive analytics section simply because the
Dashboard was opened.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Progressive Data Loading

Where appropriate, display immediately available summary information
while more expensive analytics are calculated.

For example:

> 

Organization: Acme Corporation\
Reports: 245\
Findings: 1,842\
Loading detailed recurrence analysis…

The loading state shall remain accessible and shall not repeatedly
interrupt screen-reader users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Background Processing

If Organization Metrics calculations are expensive, ART may perform them
asynchronously.

Background processing shall:

- 

Not block unrelated application functionality.

- 

Provide appropriate progress/status information.

- 

Not steal focus.

- 

Not repeatedly announce incremental progress to screen readers.

- 

Allow users to continue working where technically possible.

- 

Clearly identify when metrics are stale or still calculating.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stale Data Indicators

If cached Organization Metrics are temporarily stale, ART may display an
unobtrusive status such as:

> 

**Statistics updating…**

or:

> 

**Statistics last updated 2 minutes ago.**

The status must not unnecessarily interrupt users.

If the data is materially stale, the Dashboard should make that fact
available to users before they make decisions based on the statistics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Offline and Local-First Compatibility

ART's existing local-first architecture shall be considered when
implementing Organization Metrics.

Where ART operates without a server or external backend:

- 

Organization Metrics shall operate using locally available data.

- 

The framework shall not require a cloud service solely to calculate
basic Organization Statistics.

- 

Statistics shall reflect the reports available within the user's current
local ART data set.

- 

The User Guide shall explain the scope of locally calculated
organization statistics.

Where collaboration or a future server-backed architecture is enabled,
Organization Metrics may aggregate authorized shared data according to
the collaboration architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Local Data Isolation

When ART is operating locally, Organization Metrics shall only use data
available within the current user's authorized/local dataset.

ART shall not transmit report or organization data to an external
analytics service merely to calculate Organization Statistics unless the
user explicitly enables and authorizes such functionality.

The metrics framework should be designed to work without requiring
third-party analytics services.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration Data Aggregation

When collaboration is enabled, Organization Metrics may aggregate data
from authorized shared resources.

The metrics layer shall account for:

- 

Shared Reports.

- 

Shared Projects.

- 

Shared Workspaces.

- 

Shared Products.

- 

Organization-level permissions.

- 

Report-level permissions.

- 

Workspace permissions.

- 

Contributor permissions.

- 

Viewer permissions.

The same underlying metric definitions shall be used regardless of
whether the data is local or collaboration-backed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission-Aware Aggregation

Permission filtering shall occur **before or during metric
aggregation**, not merely after calculating unrestricted results.

Conceptually:

    Source Data
        ↓
    Permission Filter
        ↓
    Authorized Dataset
        ↓
    Metrics Calculation
        ↓
    Organization Statistics

Do not calculate:

    All Organization Data
            ↓
    Hide Unauthorized Rows

because aggregate statistics could still reveal information about
unauthorized resources.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics API Security

Any internal or external API used to provide Organization Metrics shall
enforce authorization at the data-access layer.

A client shall not be able to manipulate:

- 

Organization ID.

- 

Product ID.

- 

Project ID.

- 

Workspace ID.

- 

Report ID.

to obtain statistics outside its authorized scope.

Do not rely solely on UI controls to protect Organization Metrics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Auditability

Where ART maintains an audit trail, significant Organization Metrics
configuration changes should be auditable.

Examples include:

- 

Enabling/disabling Organization Statistics.

- 

Changing Organization Statistics configuration.

- 

Creating shared Organization Statistics views.

- 

Changing organization-level metric settings.

- 

Changing organization identity or canonical organization associations.

Do not create audit records for every ordinary Dashboard filter change
unless ART's existing audit architecture requires it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Reproducibility

Where possible, Organization Metrics should be reproducible from the
same source data and filters.

A user viewing:

    Organization: Acme Corporation
    Date: Q2 2026
    Product: Customer Portal
    Category: Keyboard Accessibility

should receive the same metric result when the underlying source data
has not changed.

If results depend on a changing external source, the Dashboard shall
identify that dependency.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Versioning

The metrics framework should support internal metric-definition
versioning.

This becomes important if a future release changes how a metric is
calculated.

For example:

    Total Findings — Metric Definition v1
    Total Findings — Metric Definition v2

The user does not necessarily need to see the internal version number,
but the architecture should allow ART developers to identify which
calculation produced a historical exported result.

This will help prevent confusion when metrics definitions evolve.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Migration and Existing Data

The Organization Metrics implementation shall work with existing ART
reports.

Do not require users to recreate existing reports merely to make them
eligible for Organization Statistics.

When Organization Statistics is enabled:

1.  

ART shall identify existing reports containing Organization/Client
values.

2.  

ART shall identify existing Product values where available.

3.  

ART shall process eligible existing data.

4.  

ART shall calculate applicable metrics.

5.  

ART shall identify missing or incomplete metadata.

6.  

ART shall not modify source reports merely to prepare them for metrics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Initialization

When Organization Statistics is first enabled for an existing ART
installation, the system may need to initialize or index existing data.

This process shall:

- 

Run without modifying source reports.

- 

Provide an accessible progress state if it takes significant time.

- 

Avoid blocking unrelated functionality where possible.

- 

Avoid repeatedly interrupting screen readers.

- 

Handle errors gracefully.

- 

Allow the process to resume if interrupted.

- 

Clearly indicate when Organization Statistics is ready.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Initialization Failure

If metrics initialization fails:

- 

Existing reports shall remain intact.

- 

Existing Report Analytics shall continue functioning.

- 

ART shall clearly indicate that Organization Statistics could not be
fully initialized.

- 

The user shall have an appropriate retry/rebuild mechanism.

- 

Technical errors shall be logged appropriately without exposing
sensitive implementation details to ordinary users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Rebuild Organization Metrics

Authorized users may be provided with a **Rebuild Organization Metrics**
command when necessary.

This command shall:

- 

Recalculate derived Organization Metrics from source data.

- 

Not modify source reports.

- 

Not change metadata.

- 

Respect permissions.

- 

Provide appropriate progress/status feedback.

- 

Be available through the Organization menu and Command Palette where
appropriate.

- 

Require confirmation if rebuilding is expensive.

The command shall be considered a recovery/maintenance operation rather
than a normal workflow.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metrics Integrity Checks

Provide internal validation mechanisms to detect inconsistencies such
as:

- 

Duplicate report identifiers.

- 

Duplicate finding identifiers.

- 

Invalid Organization references.

- 

Broken Project/Workspace relationships.

- 

Missing source records.

- 

Stale metric records.

- 

Invalid date values.

- 

Invalid category references.

- 

Invalid Issue Type references.

Integrity failures should be logged and surfaced appropriately to
authorized administrators.

Do not expose raw internal diagnostic information to ordinary users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Testing Requirements for the Metrics Engine

Automated tests shall cover:

- 

Organization grouping.

- 

Product grouping.

- 

Project grouping.

- 

Workspace grouping.

- 

Report grouping.

- 

Category aggregation.

- 

Issue Type aggregation.

- 

Severity aggregation.

- 

Status aggregation.

- 

Tester unique counts.

- 

Recurrence detection.

- 

Date filtering.

- 

Percentage calculations.

- 

Permission filtering.

- 

Multi-level aggregation.

- 

Duplicate prevention.

- 

Cache invalidation.

- 

Metadata changes.

- 

Import processing.

- 

Existing-data initialization.

- 

Metrics rebuild.

- 

Large datasets.

Tests shall include both positive and negative cases.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation Requirements for Part 6

Verify that:

1.  

Organization Metrics use a dedicated reusable data model.

2.  

Existing reports remain the source of truth.

3.  

Stable identifiers are used where available.

4.  

Organization and Product identity can evolve toward future canonical
identifiers.

5.  

Counts and unique counts are correctly distinguished.

6.  

Percentage denominators respect active filters.

7.  

Date ranges are applied consistently.

8.  

Historical limitations are documented.

9.  

Many-to-many relationships do not cause unintended double counting.

10. 

Multiple testers are handled correctly.

11. 

Multiple classifications are handled consistently.

12. 

Metrics can update incrementally.

13. 

Relevant caches are invalidated after source changes.

14. 

Large datasets do not make the application unusable.

15. 

Expensive analytics can load progressively.

16. 

Local-first operation does not require unnecessary external services.

17. 

Collaboration data is aggregated only from authorized resources.

18. 

Metrics APIs enforce authorization independently of the UI.

19. 

Existing reports can be indexed without modification.

20. 

Metrics initialization can recover from failure.

21. 

Authorized users can rebuild metrics when necessary.

22. 

Automated tests cover the major aggregation and authorization scenarios.

23. 

Existing ART functionality remains unaffected by the Organization
Metrics engine.

:::

### Part 7 — Organization Benchmarking, Accessibility Health, Finding Recurrence, and Comparative Analytics

#### Organization Benchmarking

The **Organization Benchmarking** section shall provide contextual
comparisons that help users understand accessibility performance across
Products, Projects, Workspaces, Reports, and time periods.

Benchmarking shall focus on **internal organizational comparisons by
default**.

Examples include:

- 

Product-to-product comparisons.

- 

Project-to-project comparisons.

- 

Workspace-to-workspace comparisons.

- 

Report-to-report comparisons.

- 

Current period vs. previous period.

- 

Current year vs. previous year.

- 

Current audit cycle vs. previous audit cycle.

Benchmarking shall not imply that an organization's results are
objectively "good" or "bad" solely because they are above or below
another organization's results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### External Benchmarking

If ART eventually supports external benchmarking across organizations,
that functionality shall be explicitly separated from internal
Organization Benchmarking.

External benchmarking must require:

- 

Explicit user authorization.

- 

Appropriate anonymization.

- 

Appropriate aggregation.

- 

Appropriate privacy controls.

- 

Clearly documented methodology.

Do not expose one organization's identifiable data to another
organization.

The initial implementation of Epic 42 should prioritize **internal
organizational benchmarking** unless a secure external benchmarking
architecture already exists.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Benchmarking Dimensions

Organization Benchmarking shall support comparisons such as:

    Product
        Findings
        Findings per Report
        Findings by Severity
        Findings by Category
        Resolution Rate
        Testing Activity

and:

    Time Period
        Current Period
        Previous Period
        Percentage Change

Benchmarking calculations shall use the same authoritative metric
definitions used elsewhere in Organization Statistics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Benchmarking Context

Every benchmark comparison shall identify:

- 

What is being compared.

- 

The applicable date range.

- 

The population represented.

- 

The metric being compared.

- 

Any relevant filters.

- 

Whether the comparison is based on counts, percentages, rates, or
another measure.

For example:

> 

**Product A had 24% fewer findings than Product B during Q2 2026.**

should make it possible for the user to determine:

- 

How many reports were included.

- 

Which findings were included.

- 

Which date range was used.

- 

Whether the comparison is based on total findings or another measure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Testing-Coverage-Aware Benchmarking

Benchmarking shall account for differences in testing activity.

For example, comparing:

    Product A:
    10 reports
    100 findings

    Product B:
    2 reports
    40 findings

solely by total findings could be misleading.

Where meaningful, provide contextual measures such as:

- 

Findings per report.

- 

Findings per page tested.

- 

Findings per screen tested.

- 

Findings per testing target.

- 

Findings per testing hour, if reliable data exists.

- 

Reports completed.

- 

Testing coverage.

Do not present normalized metrics as universally interchangeable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Health

The **Accessibility Health** section shall provide a high-level view of
accessibility-related indicators across the selected organization scope.

Accessibility Health should consider multiple dimensions rather than
reducing accessibility to a single raw finding count.

Potential indicators include:

- 

Total active findings.

- 

High-severity findings.

- 

Critical findings, if supported.

- 

Findings by severity.

- 

Findings by Category.

- 

Findings by WCAG Level.

- 

Findings by Accessibility Standard.

- 

Recurring findings.

- 

Resolution rate.

- 

Finding aging.

- 

Testing activity.

- 

Testing coverage.

- 

Trend direction.

- 

Percentage of reports with accessibility findings.

- 

Percentage of tested Products with findings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Health Score

If ART provides a composite **Accessibility Health Score**, it must be
treated as an optional derived indicator rather than an authoritative
measurement of accessibility quality.

The score must:

- 

Have a clearly documented methodology.

- 

Identify the metrics used.

- 

Identify the weighting of those metrics.

- 

Be reproducible.

- 

Respect active filters.

- 

Respect permissions.

- 

Avoid implying that accessibility can be perfectly represented by a
single number.

If the available data is insufficient to calculate a meaningful score,
ART shall display:

> 

**Accessibility Health Score unavailable**

rather than inventing or estimating a value.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Health Components

If a composite score is implemented, the Dashboard shall expose the
underlying components.

For example:

    Accessibility Health

    Overall Health
    ──────────────
    78

    Contributing Indicators
    ├── High-Severity Findings
    ├── Finding Recurrence
    ├── Resolution Rate
    ├── Finding Aging
    ├── Testing Coverage
    └── Recent Trend

Users must be able to understand why an indicator changed.

Do not provide a score without access to its underlying contributing
information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Health Trends

Accessibility Health should support trend analysis over time.

Users should be able to identify:

- 

Improving trends.

- 

Declining trends.

- 

Stable trends.

- 

Significant changes.

- 

Changes in individual contributing indicators.

Trend calculations shall use the same date methodology defined by the
metrics engine.

A trend shall not be labeled "improving" merely because the number of
findings decreased.

For example, reduced testing activity could produce fewer findings
without representing an actual improvement.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Recurrence

The **Finding Recurrence** section shall identify accessibility issues
that appear repeatedly across reports, audits, Projects, Workspaces, or
Products.

Recurrence analysis should help users identify:

- 

Persistent issues.

- 

Repeated issues.

- 

Recurring Categories.

- 

Recurring Issue Types.

- 

Recurring WCAG Success Criteria.

- 

Recurring Accessibility Standards.

- 

Recurring Products.

- 

Recurring Projects.

- 

Recurring components or locations where the underlying data supports
such analysis.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Finding Identity and Recurrence

ART shall use the most reliable available information to determine
whether findings represent the same underlying issue.

Potential matching information may include:

- 

Stable finding ID.

- 

Finding title.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Category.

- 

Success Criterion.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

Product.

- 

Page or screen.

- 

Component.

- 

Location.

- 

Description.

- 

Other stable identifying information.

Do not assume that two findings are identical merely because they have
the same title.

Conversely, do not treat every repeated finding as a completely
unrelated issue when sufficient identifying information indicates
continuity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Confidence

Where recurrence is inferred rather than explicitly established through
a stable finding identifier, ART should identify the result as a
**potential recurrence** rather than a confirmed recurrence.

For example:

> 

**Potential recurring issue**

rather than:

> 

**Confirmed recurring issue**

unless the underlying data provides sufficient evidence.

This distinction is important to prevent users from interpreting
heuristic matching as definitive.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Metrics

Provide recurrence metrics such as:

- 

Number of recurring findings.

- 

Percentage of findings that recur.

- 

Number of reports containing recurring findings.

- 

Recurrence by Product.

- 

Recurrence by Project.

- 

Recurrence by Workspace.

- 

Recurrence by Category.

- 

Recurrence by Severity.

- 

Recurrence by Issue Type.

- 

Recurrence by Success Criterion.

- 

Recurrence over time.

Where appropriate, also provide:

- 

Number of recurrence events.

- 

First occurrence.

- 

Most recent occurrence.

- 

Number of reporting periods affected.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Trend

The Dashboard shall support identifying whether recurrence is:

- 

Increasing.

- 

Decreasing.

- 

Stable.

A decrease in recurrence should not automatically be labeled an
improvement unless sufficient testing activity exists to support that
conclusion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Persistent Finding Identification

Where reliable data exists, identify findings that remain present across
consecutive audit or testing cycles.

For example:

    Audit 1 → Finding present
    Audit 2 → Finding present
    Audit 3 → Finding present
    Audit 4 → Finding present

may be identified as a persistent issue.

The Dashboard should provide the number of consecutive reporting cycles
when that information is available.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recurrence Drill-Down

Users shall be able to drill from a recurrence metric into the
underlying reports.

For example:

    Recurring Issue
        ↓
    Product
        ↓
    Project
        ↓
    Reports
        ↓
    Finding occurrences

The drill-down must preserve:

- 

Recurrence context.

- 

Active filters.

- 

Organization.

- 

Product.

- 

Date range.

- 

Applicable permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Comparisons

The **Product Comparisons** section shall provide detailed comparative
analytics across Products associated with the selected Organization.

Support comparisons of:

- 

Total findings.

- 

Findings by Severity.

- 

Findings by Category.

- 

Findings by Issue Type.

- 

Findings by WCAG Success Criterion.

- 

Findings by Accessibility Standard.

- 

Findings per Report.

- 

Findings per testing target.

- 

Recurring findings.

- 

Resolution rate.

- 

Finding aging.

- 

Testing activity.

- 

Number of reports.

- 

Number of unique testers.

- 

Accessibility Health indicators.

Only metrics supported by reliable source data shall be displayed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Comparison Filters

Product comparisons shall support applicable filters including:

- 

Date range.

- 

Severity.

- 

Category.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

WCAG Version.

- 

WCAG Level.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report.

- 

Tester.

Filters shall update all dependent statistics consistently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Comparison Tables

Provide an accessible table representation for Product comparisons.

Example:

    | Product | Reports | Findings | High Severity | Recurring | Testers |
    |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | Product A | 12 | 148 | 24 | 17 | 5 |
    | Product B | 8 | 91 | 11 | 8 | 3 |
    | Product C | 15 | 173 | 31 | 22 | 7 |

The exact columns may vary based on the available metrics.

Users must be able to access equivalent information without relying on
visual charts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Category Analytics

Organization Statistics shall provide detailed analytics by
**Category**.

Users shall be able to determine:

- 

Number of findings by Category.

- 

Percentage of findings by Category.

- 

Category trends over time.

- 

Category by Product.

- 

Category by Project.

- 

Category by Workspace.

- 

Category by Report.

- 

Category by Severity.

- 

Category by Accessibility Standard.

- 

Category by WCAG Success Criterion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Category Analytics by Report, Workspace, Product, and Time Period

The Organization Statistics Dashboard shall specifically support
analysis of the **number and percentage of issues by Category** across:

- 

Report.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Organization.

- 

Selected time period.

For example:

    Category: Keyboard Accessibility

    Organization:
    42 findings — 18.4%

    Product A:
    21 findings — 22.1%

    Product B:
    14 findings — 15.7%

    Product C:
    7 findings — 12.3%

The denominator for each percentage must be clearly defined.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Issue Type Analytics

Provide equivalent analytics for **Issue Type** where ART's reporting
model supports Issue Types.

Support:

- 

Number of issues by Issue Type.

- 

Percentage by Issue Type.

- 

Trends.

- 

Issue Type by Product.

- 

Issue Type by Project.

- 

Issue Type by Workspace.

- 

Issue Type by Report.

- 

Issue Type by Severity.

- 

Issue Type by Category.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### WCAG Success Criterion Analytics

Where reports contain WCAG Success Criterion information, Organization
Statistics shall support analysis by:

- 

Success Criterion.

- 

WCAG Version.

- 

Conformance Level.

- 

Principle.

- 

Number of findings.

- 

Percentage of findings.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report.

- 

Time period.

- 

Severity.

For example:

> 

**1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)**\
38 findings — 14.7% of findings in the selected scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Standard Analytics

Organization Statistics shall support standards beyond WCAG.

Where reports contain applicable accessibility standards, users should
be able to analyze:

- 

Findings by Accessibility Standard.

- 

Findings by standard version.

- 

Findings by criterion.

- 

Findings by Product.

- 

Findings by Project.

- 

Findings by Workspace.

- 

Findings by Report.

- 

Findings by time period.

The implementation shall not assume that every accessibility standard
uses WCAG-style Success Criterion identifiers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Conformance-Level Analytics

Where applicable, provide statistics by conformance level.

For WCAG data this may include:

- 

Level A.

- 

Level AA.

- 

Level AAA.

Where another standard uses a different conformance model, ART shall use
the terminology appropriate to that standard.

Do not force non-WCAG standards into WCAG-specific terminology.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Standard Comparison

Users should be able to compare accessibility findings across standards
when multiple standards are represented in an organization.

For example:

    WCAG 2.2
    Section 508
    EN 301 549

Comparisons shall clearly identify the standard associated with each
result.

Do not assume that criteria across different standards are equivalent
unless ART has an authoritative mapping.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report-Level Analytics

Organization Statistics shall support report-level aggregation while
preserving the distinction between:

- 

Report metrics.

- 

Organization metrics.

Report-level metrics may include:

- 

Findings.

- 

Severity.

- 

Categories.

- 

Issue Types.

- 

Accessibility Standards.

- 

Success Criteria.

- 

Tester.

- 

Product.

- 

Date.

These metrics can then be aggregated into Organization Statistics.

The same metric definitions should be reused to prevent discrepancies
between Report Analytics and Organization Statistics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Workspace Analytics

Where Reports belong to Project Workspaces, Organization Statistics
shall support aggregation by Workspace.

Track, where available:

- 

Reports.

- 

Findings.

- 

Findings by Severity.

- 

Findings by Category.

- 

Findings by Issue Type.

- 

Unique testers.

- 

Products tested.

- 

Testing activity.

- 

Recurring findings.

- 

Resolution information.

Workspace statistics must respect Workspace permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Project Analytics

Where Reports belong to Projects, provide corresponding Project-level
analytics.

Support:

- 

Reports.

- 

Findings.

- 

Severity.

- 

Categories.

- 

Issue Types.

- 

Products.

- 

Testers.

- 

Testing activity.

- 

Recurrence.

- 

Resolution.

- 

Trends.

Project analytics must respect Project and Workspace permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Analytics by Product, Project, and Report

The Tester analytics section shall allow users to determine the number
of unique testers associated with:

- 

Each Product.

- 

Each Project.

- 

Each Workspace.

- 

Each Report.

- 

Each time period.

Where appropriate, also show:

- 

Tester count over time.

- 

Reports tested.

- 

Products tested.

- 

Projects tested.

Individual tester names should only be displayed when permitted and when
the source data provides them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Coverage

Where appropriate, provide metrics showing testing coverage by unique
tester.

For example:

> 

**5 unique testers contributed to 12 reports across 3 Products.**

This is intended to describe testing coverage and participation.

It shall not be presented as a productivity or performance ranking.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Testing Coverage

Organization Statistics should provide a high-level view of testing
coverage.

Potential metrics include:

- 

Reports tested.

- 

Products tested.

- 

Projects tested.

- 

Workspaces tested.

- 

Pages tested.

- 

Screens tested.

- 

Components tested.

- 

Testing targets tested.

- 

Unique testers.

- 

Testing activity over time.

The Dashboard shall clearly distinguish between **testing coverage** and
**finding volume**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Cross-Tabulation

The metrics engine shall support cross-tabulation of dimensions where
meaningful.

Examples:

    Category × Product

    Severity × Product

    Category × Severity

    Issue Type × Product

    Success Criterion × Product

    Category × Time Period

    Severity × Time Period

    Tester × Product

    Findings × Report

    Findings × Workspace

The implementation should provide reusable aggregation capabilities
rather than creating a separate hard-coded calculation for every
possible combination.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Analytics Filtering Consistency

When users apply a filter, all dependent metrics must update
consistently.

For example, selecting:

    Product: Customer Portal
    Date Range: January–June 2026
    Severity: High

shall update:

- 

Finding counts.

- 

Category percentages.

- 

Issue Type percentages.

- 

Recurrence.

- 

Accessibility Health indicators.

- 

Tester counts where applicable.

- 

Product comparisons where applicable.

The Dashboard must clearly indicate which metrics are affected by the
current filter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### . Filter Scope Communication

Every analytics view should make the active scope understandable.

Users should be able to determine:

> 

Organization: Acme Corporation\
Product: Customer Portal\
Date: Jan 1–Jun 30, 2026\
Severity: High

without having to inspect multiple controls or infer the scope from a
chart.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Reset Filters

Provide an accessible **Reset Filters** action.

The action shall:

- 

Restore the default filter state.

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Have a meaningful accessible name.

- 

Announce the resulting state when necessary.

- 

Not unexpectedly move focus.

If no filters are active, the Reset Filters action may be disabled.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Saved Analytics Filter State

When users save an Organization Statistics view, the saved configuration
may include filter state.

Saved filters shall include only supported values and shall not preserve
references to resources the user can no longer access.

If a saved view references a deleted Product, Project, Workspace, or
Report, ART shall clearly indicate that the resource is unavailable
rather than silently substituting another resource.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation Requirements for Part 7

Verify that:

1.  

Organization Benchmarking uses clearly defined internal comparisons.

2.  

Benchmarking does not imply unsupported judgments about accessibility
quality.

3.  

Testing activity is considered when interpreting comparisons.

4.  

Accessibility Health uses multiple meaningful indicators.

5.  

Any Accessibility Health Score has a transparent methodology.

6.  

Users can inspect the components behind Accessibility Health.

7.  

Finding Recurrence distinguishes confirmed recurrence from inferred
recurrence where necessary.

8.  

Persistent findings can be identified when reliable data exists.

9.  

Recurrence can be drilled down to the underlying reports and findings.

10. 

Product comparisons support meaningful organization-level comparisons.

11. 

Category analytics work by Report, Workspace, Product, Project, and time
period.

12. 

Category percentages use clearly defined denominators.

13. 

Issue Type analytics follow the same principles.

14. 

WCAG Success Criterion analytics are available when the required data
exists.

15. 

Accessibility Standards beyond WCAG are supported.

16. 

Non-WCAG standards are not incorrectly forced into WCAG terminology.

17. 

Report, Project, and Workspace analytics use the same authoritative
metric definitions.

18. 

Unique tester counts are calculated correctly.

19. 

Tester analytics do not become employee-performance rankings.

20. 

Cross-tabulated analytics do not double-count findings unexpectedly.

21. 

Filters update dependent metrics consistently.

22. 

Active metric scope is clearly communicated.

23. 

Saved views preserve supported filter state without bypassing
permissions.

24. 

All charts and comparative visualizations have equivalent accessible
data representations.

25. 

Existing ART functionality remains unaffected when Organization
Statistics is disabled.

:::

### Part 8 — Documentation, Accessibility, Testing, Security, Migration, and Acceptance Criteria

#### User Guide Requirements

Update the ART User Guide to document the complete **Organization
Statistics** feature.

Documentation shall explain:

- 

What Organization Statistics are.

- 

How to enable Organization Statistics.

- 

How to access Organization Statistics.

- 

How the Organization menu works.

- 

How Organization Statistics relate to Reports, Projects, Workspaces, and
Products.

- 

How Organization/Client metadata determines organization grouping.

- 

How Product metadata affects Product analytics.

- 

How Tester/Tester Name data affects tester analytics.

- 

How filters work.

- 

How saved views work.

- 

How shared views work.

- 

How permissions affect statistics.

- 

How exports work.

- 

How benchmarking works.

- 

How Accessibility Health works.

- 

How Finding Recurrence works.

- 

How Product Comparisons work.

- 

How Category and Issue Type analytics work.

- 

How historical statistics are calculated.

- 

Known limitations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization/Client Metadata Documentation

The User Guide shall explicitly state that **Organization Statistics can
only be accurately provided when the Organization/Client field in the
Report Metadata section is consistently and accurately populated.**

Include guidance such as:

> 

**Important:** Organization Statistics are derived from the
Organization/Client value stored in each report's metadata. For accurate
organization-level statistics, consistently enter the same organization
name in the Organization/Client field for every applicable report.

The documentation shall explain that inconsistent values such as:

    Acme Corporation
    Acme Corp.
    ACME
    Acme Corporation, Inc.

may be interpreted as different organizations unless ART provides an
authorized mechanism for associating them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Metadata Documentation

The User Guide shall explain that Product analytics depend on the
optional **Product** field in report metadata.

Document that:

- 

Reports without a Product value may still contribute to
Organization-level statistics.

- 

Reports without a Product value cannot reliably contribute to
Product-specific statistics.

- 

Product names should be entered consistently.

- 

Changing a Product value can affect Product statistics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Metadata Documentation

The User Guide shall explain that Tester analytics depend on available
Tester/Tester Name information.

Document that:

- 

Tester statistics are optional.

- 

Reports without tester information cannot contribute to tester-specific
analytics.

- 

ART attempts to identify unique testers using available identifiers.

- 

Tester analytics describe testing activity and coverage.

- 

Tester analytics are not intended to evaluate employee performance.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Data Quality Documentation

Document the relationship between metadata quality and Organization
Statistics.

Explain that incomplete metadata can result in:

- 

Incomplete organization statistics.

- 

Incomplete Product statistics.

- 

Incomplete tester statistics.

- 

Incomplete benchmarking.

- 

Incomplete trend analysis.

The documentation should encourage users to establish consistent
metadata practices before relying on Organization Statistics for
organizational decision-making.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stand-Alone Report Documentation

Document that Organization Statistics do not require Project Workspaces.

Stand-alone reports can contribute to Organization Statistics when:

- 

Organization/Client is populated.

- 

The report contains the required metric data.

- 

The report is within the user's authorized dataset.

Explain that a report does not need to belong to a Workspace or Project
to participate in organization-level analytics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Project Workspace Documentation

Document how Reports inside Project Workspaces contribute to
Organization Statistics.

Explain the relationship:

    Organization
        ↓
    Project
        ↓
    Workspace
        ↓
    Report

and that stand-alone Reports may also contribute:

    Organization
        ↓
    Report

Both structures must be supported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation of Permissions

Document how Organization Statistics interact with:

- 

Organization permissions.

- 

Project permissions.

- 

Workspace permissions.

- 

Report permissions.

- 

Product permissions.

- 

Collaboration permissions.

Clearly explain that viewing organization-level statistics does not
automatically grant access to the underlying Reports, Projects,
Workspaces, or Products.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation of Statistical Limitations

The User Guide shall explain that Organization Statistics are
**descriptive analytics derived from ART data**.

ART shall not imply that its statistics establish:

- 

Causation.

- 

Statistical significance.

- 

Organizational accessibility compliance.

- 

Legal compliance.

- 

Accessibility quality beyond what the underlying metrics support.

Where appropriate, documentation should encourage users to interpret
metrics in context.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation of Accessibility Health

If an Accessibility Health Score is implemented, document:

- 

Its calculation.

- 

Its inputs.

- 

Its weighting.

- 

Its limitations.

- 

How insufficient data affects the score.

Explicitly state that the score is a **summary indicator**, not an
accessibility certification or compliance determination.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation of Finding Recurrence

Document how ART identifies recurring findings.

Clearly distinguish between:

- 

Confirmed recurrence.

- 

Potential recurrence.

- 

Persistent findings.

Explain what data ART uses to identify recurrence and the limitations of
heuristic matching.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation of Benchmarking

Document that Organization Benchmarking is primarily intended for
comparisons **within the same organization**.

Explain:

- 

What is being compared.

- 

How comparison periods are selected.

- 

How findings are normalized where applicable.

- 

How testing coverage affects interpretation.

- 

That lower finding counts do not necessarily indicate better
accessibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Documentation of Historical Data

The User Guide shall clearly explain how historical statistics are
calculated.

If ART does not maintain historical snapshots, document that:

> 

Historical statistics may reflect the current state of report data
rather than an exact historical snapshot of the data as it existed at
that time.

Do not imply historical accuracy that the underlying data cannot
support.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### . In-App Help

Where ART already supports contextual help, provide help links or
accessible descriptions for Organization Statistics controls.

Examples:

- 

Organization Statistics.

- 

Organization/Client.

- 

Product.

- 

Tester.

- 

Finding Recurrence.

- 

Accessibility Health.

- 

Benchmarking.

- 

Data Quality.

- 

Filters.

Help text should be concise and should not overwhelm the Dashboard.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Conformance

The entire Organization Statistics feature shall be implemented to meet
the applicable ART accessibility requirements.

At minimum, verify:

- 

Keyboard accessibility.

- 

Screen-reader accessibility.

- 

Focus management.

- 

Logical reading order.

- 

Logical tab order.

- 

Accessible names.

- 

Accessible descriptions.

- 

Accessible state changes.

- 

Accessible tables.

- 

Accessible charts.

- 

Accessible tabs.

- 

Accessible filters.

- 

Accessible dialogs.

- 

Accessible menus.

- 

Accessible error messages.

- 

Accessible loading states.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tablist and Tabpanel Accessibility

The statistical sections shall use a fully accessible
**tablist/tab/tabpanel** implementation.

The implementation shall follow the applicable WAI-ARIA pattern.

Tabs shall:

- 

Have appropriate roles.

- 

Have unique accessible names.

- 

Have correct `aria-selected` state.

- 

Have appropriate `aria-controls` relationships.

- 

Have appropriate tabpanel relationships.

- 

Have logical keyboard navigation.

- 

Clearly communicate the active tab.

- 

Preserve focus appropriately.

- 

Support screen readers.

- 

Not create duplicate accessible names.

The tab sequence should be predictable and should not require users to
traverse every statistic within every tab before reaching the next
section.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tab Keyboard Interaction

The Organization Statistics tablist shall support appropriate keyboard
interaction.

At minimum, verify:

- 

Arrow-key navigation where appropriate.

- 

Home/End behavior where appropriate.

- 

Enter/Space behavior where appropriate.

- 

Correct focus behavior.

- 

Correct selection state.

- 

Correct panel visibility.

Follow ART's established keyboard interaction conventions where they
already exist.

Do not introduce a custom interaction model unnecessarily.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dynamic Dashboard Updates

When metrics change because of:

- 

Filter changes.

- 

Organization changes.

- 

Product changes.

- 

Date changes.

- 

Report updates.

ART shall update the relevant statistics without unnecessarily moving
focus.

Screen-reader users shall receive appropriate status information when
necessary.

Do not announce every individual chart value or table cell during a
routine update.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Filter Controls

All filters shall have:

- 

Visible labels where appropriate.

- 

Programmatically associated labels.

- 

Accessible descriptions when needed.

- 

Correct states.

- 

Keyboard operation.

- 

Predictable focus behavior.

Examples include:

- 

Organization.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report.

- 

Date range.

- 

Severity.

- 

Category.

- 

Issue Type.

- 

Accessibility Standard.

- 

WCAG Version.

- 

Tester.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Filter Change Announcements

When a filter changes, ART should provide an appropriate accessible
status indicating that the results have been updated.

For example:

> 

**Organization Statistics updated. Product filter: Customer Portal. 148
findings found.**

The announcement should be concise.

Do not force screen-reader users to listen to a large amount of
regenerated Dashboard content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility of Charts

All charts shall have:

- 

Accessible names.

- 

Accessible descriptions where necessary.

- 

Equivalent tabular data.

- 

Keyboard access where interactive.

- 

Meaningful labels.

- 

Accessible legends.

- 

Accessible data values.

Charts shall not rely on:

- 

Color alone.

- 

Position alone.

- 

Hover alone.

- 

Animation alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility of Data Tables

All Organization Statistics tables shall:

- 

Use semantic table structures where appropriate.

- 

Have correct headers.

- 

Expose sorting state.

- 

Expose filtering state.

- 

Support keyboard navigation.

- 

Maintain logical reading order.

- 

Provide accessible empty states.

- 

Provide accessible loading states.

- 

Avoid unnecessary horizontal scrolling where possible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility of Drill-Down

Drill-down controls shall:

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Have meaningful accessible names.

- 

Identify the destination or action.

- 

Preserve focus appropriately.

- 

Announce context changes when necessary.

For example:

> 

**View 24 recurring findings for Customer Portal**

is preferable to:

> 

**View**

when additional context is required to understand the action.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility of Exports

Validate the accessibility of all supported Organization Statistics
export formats.

Where ART supports:

- 

HTML.

- 

Word.

- 

PDF.

- 

CSV.

- 

Excel.

- 

JSON.

verify that the exported data remains understandable and usable with
appropriate assistive technologies.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Security and Privacy

Organization Statistics shall follow ART's existing security and privacy
architecture.

Do not expose organization-level data to unauthorized users.

The implementation shall prevent:

- 

Cross-organization data leakage.

- 

Cross-project data leakage.

- 

Cross-workspace data leakage.

- 

Cross-report data leakage.

- 

Unauthorized tester information.

- 

Unauthorized Product information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Aggregation Privacy

Permission filtering must occur before aggregation so that users cannot
infer unauthorized information from totals.

For example, a user must not be able to determine that:

> 

Product C contains exactly 17 findings

merely because Product C is excluded from a table but included
indirectly in an organization-level total.

The implementation shall consider aggregation-based information
disclosure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Isolation

When a user switches between organizations, ART must completely refresh
the applicable Organization Statistics context.

No stale information from the previous organization shall remain
visible.

This includes:

- 

Charts.

- 

Tables.

- 

Summary cards.

- 

Filters.

- 

Saved views.

- 

Drill-down state.

- 

Cached data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Secure Exports

Organization Statistics exports shall respect the same authorization
rules as the Dashboard.

A user must not be able to export data they cannot view.

Export endpoints and generation logic must enforce permissions
independently of the UI.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sensitive Tester Data

Tester names and other potentially identifying information shall be
treated as potentially sensitive data.

Individual tester information shall only be displayed or exported when:

- 

The source report contains it.

- 

The user has appropriate permissions.

- 

The applicable Organization configuration allows it.

Aggregate tester counts should remain available where individual
identities are not appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No External Analytics by Default

Organization Statistics shall not transmit report data, findings, tester
information, or organization information to third-party analytics
services by default.

Any future external analytics integration must be:

- 

Explicitly enabled.

- 

Clearly documented.

- 

Permission-aware.

- 

Privacy-conscious.

- 

Consistent with ART's local-first architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Migration of Existing Reports

Existing ART reports shall remain functional after this feature is
introduced.

Migration shall:

- 

Preserve existing metadata.

- 

Preserve existing findings.

- 

Preserve existing templates.

- 

Preserve existing reports.

- 

Preserve existing Projects and Workspaces.

- 

Preserve existing exports.

- 

Preserve existing settings.

No destructive migration shall be performed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Backward Compatibility

Reports created before Organization Statistics existed shall remain
valid.

If they contain:

    Organization/Client
    Product
    Tester

ART shall use those values where applicable.

If they do not contain these values, they shall remain usable without
requiring users to retroactively populate them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Feature Disablement

When **Organization Statistics** is disabled in Application Settings:

- 

Organization Statistics shall not appear on the Dashboard.

- 

The Organization menu shall not appear unless another Organization
feature independently requires it.

- 

Organization Statistics commands shall not appear in Command Search.

- 

Organization Statistics toolbar options shall not appear.

- 

Metrics calculations shall not unnecessarily run.

- 

Existing Reports shall continue functioning.

- 

Existing Report Analytics shall continue functioning.

- 

No source data shall be deleted.

Re-enabling Organization Statistics shall restore access to the feature.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Feature Re-Enablement

When Organization Statistics is re-enabled:

- 

Existing eligible reports shall be available for aggregation.

- 

Organization/Client values shall be recognized.

- 

Product values shall be recognized.

- 

Tester values shall be recognized.

- 

Existing organization metrics should be rebuilt or refreshed as
necessary.

Users should not have to recreate Reports merely because Organization
Statistics was temporarily disabled.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Testing

The implementation shall include regression testing for existing ART
functionality.

At minimum verify:

- 

Report creation.

- 

Report editing.

- 

Report saving.

- 

Report loading.

- 

Report importing.

- 

Report exporting.

- 

Templates.

- 

Project Workspaces.

- 

Collaboration.

- 

Report permissions.

- 

Organization metadata.

- 

Product metadata.

- 

Tester metadata.

- 

Report Analytics.

- 

Dashboard functionality.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Menu navigation.

- 

Keyboard shortcuts.

#### Automated Testing

Organization grouping.

Organization filtering.

Product filtering.

Project filtering.

Workspace filtering.

Report filtering.

Tester counting.

Permission filtering.

Export generation.

Saved views.

Shared views.

Metadata changes.

Import behavior.

Disable/re-enable behavior.

#### Accessibility Testing

Perform accessibility testing using keyboard-only interaction and

At minimum, test with the accessibility testing technologies supported
by ART's existing testing process.

Verify:

- 

Keyboard-only operation.

Screen-reader navigation.

Tablist/tabpanel behavior.

Tables.

Charts.

Filters.

Menus.

Dialogs.

Loading states.

Error states.

Dynamic updates.

Drill-down navigation.

Exported reports.

#### Screen Reader Testing

Screen-reader testing shall verify that users can:

1.  

Open Organization Statistics.

2.  

Identify the selected Organization.

3.  

Navigate the statistical tabs.

4.  

Identify the active tab.

5.  

Navigate filters.

6.  

Change filters.

7.  

Understand updated results.

8.  

Navigate charts through their accessible alternatives.

9.  

Navigate tables.

10. 

Drill into underlying Reports.

11. 

Return to the previous analytics context.

12. 

Export statistics.

13.

#### Keyboard-Only Acceptance Test

The complete Organization Statistics workflow shall be operable without
a mouse.

A keyboard-only user shall be able to:

1.  

Open Organization Statistics.

2.  

Select an Organization.

3.  

Navigate the tablist.

4.  

Apply filters.

5.  

Review metrics.

6.  

Navigate accessible chart alternatives.

7.  

Sort tables.

8.  

Drill down.

9.  

Return to the previous context.

10. 

Save a personal view.

11. 

Access shared views when authorized.

12. 

Export statistics.

13. 

Close dialogs.

14. 

Return to the Report or Workspace from which the statistics were opened.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Data Accuracy Acceptance Test

Create a controlled test dataset containing:

- 

Multiple Organizations.

- 

Multiple Products.

- 

Multiple Projects.

- 

Multiple Workspaces.

- 

Multiple Reports.

- 

Multiple Testers.

- 

Multiple Categories.

- 

Multiple Issue Types.

- 

Multiple Severities.

- 

Multiple WCAG Success Criteria.

- 

Multiple Accessibility Standards.

- 

Recurring findings.

- 

Missing metadata.

- 

Inconsistent metadata.

- 

Reports with no Organization/Client.

- 

Reports with no Product.

- 

Reports with no Tester.

Verify that every Organization Statistics calculation matches the
expected result.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Cross-Organization Acceptance Test

Verify that:

    Organization A

never appears in:

    Organization B

statistics unless an explicitly authorized cross-organization
aggregation feature exists.

Test:

- 

Dashboard.

- 

Filters.

- 

Drill-down.

- 

Saved views.

- 

Shared views.

- 

Exports.

- 

Command Palette.

- 

API/service layer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Acceptance Test

Create test users representing:

- 

Organization Administrator.

- 

Organization Contributor.

- 

Organization Viewer.

- 

Workspace Administrator.

- 

Workspace Contributor.

- 

Workspace Viewer.

- 

Report Editor.

- 

Report Viewer.

- 

User with access to only selected Reports.

Verify that every user sees only statistics derived from resources they
are authorized to access.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Metadata Quality Acceptance Test

Create reports with:

    Organization/Client: Acme Corporation

and:

    Organization/Client: Acme Corp.

Verify that ART does not silently assume these values represent the same
organization unless an explicit normalization or canonicalization
mechanism exists.

Verify that the Dashboard communicates the resulting data-quality
limitation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Acceptance Test

Verify that reports containing:

    Organization/Client: Acme Corporation
    Product: Customer Portal

contribute to:

- 

Acme Corporation statistics.

- 

Customer Portal statistics.

Verify that reports with no Product value contribute to
organization-level statistics but are excluded from Product-specific
statistics where Product is required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester Acceptance Test

Create reports with:

    Tester: Jane Smith

and multiple reports containing the same tester.

Verify that:

- 

Jane Smith is counted once as a unique tester within the appropriate
scope.

- 

Tester participation can be analyzed by Product, Project, Workspace, and
Report where supported.

- 

Tester analytics do not create performance rankings.

- 

Missing tester data is communicated appropriately.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Acceptance Criteria

Epic 42 shall not be considered complete until:

- 

Existing ART functionality continues to work.

- 

Organization Statistics can be disabled without breaking ART.

- 

Existing Reports remain usable.

- 

Existing Templates remain usable.

- 

Existing Projects and Workspaces remain usable.

- 

Existing collaboration functionality remains usable.

- 

Existing Report Analytics remain usable.

- 

Existing exports remain usable.

- 

Existing keyboard shortcuts remain functional.

- 

Existing accessibility behavior does not regress.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Epic Acceptance Criteria

Epic 42 shall be considered complete only when all applicable
requirements in this epic have been implemented, tested, documented, and
validated.

The final implementation must provide:

- 

Optional Organization Statistics.

- 

Application-level enable/disable configuration.

- 

Organization menu integration.

- 

Accessible tablist/tabpanel Dashboard architecture.

- 

Organization/Client-based organization grouping.

- 

Product analytics.

- 

Project analytics.

- 

Workspace analytics.

- 

Report analytics.

- 

Tester analytics.

- 

Category analytics.

- 

Issue Type analytics.

- 

WCAG Success Criterion analytics.

- 

Accessibility Standard analytics.

- 

Finding Recurrence.

- 

Product Comparisons.

- 

Accessibility Health.

- 

Organization Benchmarking.

- 

Testing Coverage analytics.

- 

Time-based analytics.

- 

Permission-aware aggregation.

- 

Data-quality indicators.

- 

Accessible charts and tables.

- 

Accessible filters.

- 

Drill-down capabilities.

- 

Export capabilities.

- 

Saved views.

- 

Personal and shared views where supported.

- 

Local-first compatibility.

- 

Collaboration compatibility.

- 

User Guide documentation.

- 

Automated testing.

- 

Accessibility testing.

- 

Security and privacy validation.

- 

Regression testing.

Most importantly, the implementation must **not modify or corrupt the
underlying Report, Project, Workspace, Product, Tester, Template, or
finding data merely to support Organization Statistics**.

## Epic 43 — Usability Reports

### Part 1 — Usability Report Type and Report Builder Configuration

#### Purpose

Add **Usability Report** as a new Report Type in the ART Report Builder.

Usability Reports are intended to complement Audit Logs by providing a
flexible reporting format for documenting usability issues that affect
users but may fall outside typical accessibility standards, WCAG Success
Criteria, or other accessibility requirements.

A Usability Report is **not** intended to be a traditional usability
research-study report.

It is a configurable ART report format for documenting usability issues.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Type

Add the following option to the Report Builder's Report Type selection:

> 

**Usability Report**

When **Usability Report** is selected:

- The Report Builder shall use the same general report-building
  architecture as the **Executive Summary** report type.

- The user shall be able to configure the report's layout.

- The user shall be able to configure the report's fields.

- The user shall be able to create as many or as few fields as needed.

- ART shall not impose a predefined set of Usability Report fields.

- ART shall not automatically add fields to a new Usability Report.

- Existing Report Types shall remain unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No Default Usability Report Fields

There shall be **no default field configuration** for Usability Reports.

When a user creates a new Usability Report, the report shall not
automatically contain fields such as:

- Issue Title.

- Location.

- Issue Description.

- Impact on Users.

- How to Reproduce.

- Comments.

- Tester Name.

- Severity.

- Category.

- Recommendation.

Instead, the user shall decide which fields are appropriate for their
particular Usability Report.

For example, one user may configure:

    Issue Title

    Location

    Issue Description

    Impact on Users

    How to Reproduce

    Usability Heuristics

    Tester Name

    Comments

while another user may configure:

    Issue

    Recommendation

    Severity

    Usability Heuristics

    Tester

    Status

ART shall support both configurations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Executive Summary Layout and Field Configuration Parity

When **Usability Report** is selected as the Report Type, it shall
provide the same **Layout** and **Field Configuration** capabilities
available to the **Executive Summary** Report Type.

This includes all applicable existing functionality for:

- Adding fields.

- Removing fields.

- Reordering fields.

- Configuring field labels.

- Selecting field types.

- Configuring required/optional behavior where supported.

- Configuring dropdown values.

- Configuring multi-value fields where supported.

- Configuring default values where supported.

- Configuring layout options.

- Configuring sections where supported.

- Configuring other existing Executive Summary layout options.

Do not create a separate Usability Report configuration system.

Reuse the existing Executive Summary implementation and extend it only
where necessary to support the Usability Heuristics field type.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Usability Report-Specific Field Type

The only additional field type introduced specifically for Usability
Reports shall be:

> 

**Usability Heuristics**

This field type shall appear in the Field Type selection when
**Usability Report** is the selected Report Type.

The new field type shall not unnecessarily appear for unrelated Report
Types.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Usability Heuristics Field Configuration

When a user adds a field and selects:

> 

**Field Type → Usability Heuristics**

ART shall create a configurable Usability Heuristics field for the
report.

The field shall allow the user to select one or more usability
heuristics from an available list.

The implementation should support multiple selected heuristics where the
existing field architecture supports multi-value fields.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Usability Heuristic Options

The Usability Heuristics field shall provide recognized usability
heuristics as selectable options.

The initial available options shall include the commonly recognized
**Nielsen usability heuristics**:

- Visibility of system status.

- Match between system and the real world.

- User control and freedom.

- Consistency and standards.

- Error prevention.

- Recognition rather than recall.

- Flexibility and efficiency of use.

- Aesthetic and minimalist design.

- Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors.

- Help and documentation.

The exact displayed labels should be concise while remaining
understandable and identifiable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Usability Heuristic Dropdown in the Report Editor

When a Usability Heuristics field has been configured for a Usability
Report, the Report Editor shall display the corresponding **Usability
Heuristic** selection control.

The control shall:

- Use the configured field label.

- Provide the available usability heuristics as options.

- Support the configured selection behavior.

- Support keyboard operation.

- Support screen readers.

- Preserve the user's selected value(s).

- Display the selected value(s) when the report is viewed.

- Preserve the selected value(s) during saving, loading, importing, and
  exporting where supported.

If the user has not configured a Usability Heuristics field, the Report
Editor shall **not** display a Usability Heuristic selection control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Configurable Heuristic Options

Where the existing Field Configuration architecture supports
configurable dropdown options, the Usability Heuristics field should
allow the available heuristic options to be customized.

This would allow organizations to use:

- Nielsen's heuristics.

- Organization-specific heuristics.

- Other recognized usability frameworks.

- Custom usability principles.

Do not require every organization to use Nielsen's heuristics.

However, the initial available options should include Nielsen's
heuristics so users can immediately create a useful usability report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No Analytics

When **Usability Report** is selected as the Report Type, the report
shall **not include an Analytics section**.

The Report Builder shall not display an Analytics configuration option
for Usability Reports if Analytics is incompatible with this Report
Type.

A Usability Report shall therefore consist of the configured report
content and layout without an Analytics section.

This requirement applies specifically to the Report Builder/report
itself.

It does not prevent future organization-level analytics from aggregating
Usability Report data through the separate **Organization Statistics**
functionality established by Epic 42.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Optional Table of Contents

When **Usability Report** is selected as the Report Type, the report
may include an optional **Table of Contents**.

When enabled, the Table of Contents shall display accessible links pointing
to each section of the report. Activating a section link from the Table of
Contents shall move keyboard focus directly to that section heading in the
report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Layout

Usability Reports shall support the same Layout functionality available
to Executive Summary reports.

Do not introduce a separate Usability Report layout system.

If Executive Summary supports configurable:

- Sections.

- Field placement.

- Field ordering.

- Layout arrangements.

- Content organization.

- Other existing layout options.

those capabilities shall also be available to Usability Reports.

The user shall have control over how their Usability Report is
organized.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Editor Behavior

When the user selects:

> 

**Report Type → Usability Report**

the Report Builder shall update the available configuration options
appropriately.

The user shall see:

- Executive Summary-compatible Layout options.

- Executive Summary-compatible Field Configuration options.

- The additional **Usability Heuristics** field type.

- Table of Contents configuration options.

The user shall not see:

- Analytics configuration.

- Automatically generated usability fields.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Switching Report Types

If the user changes an existing report from another Report Type to
**Usability Report**, ART shall handle incompatible configuration
elements appropriately.

For example, if the existing report contains:

- Analytics configuration.

- Table of Contents configuration.

- Report-Type-specific fields.

ART shall not silently corrupt or discard the user's data.

Before removing incompatible configuration where necessary, ART should:

- Preserve the underlying data where possible.

- Warn the user when a configuration element cannot be retained.

- Clearly identify what will change.

- Avoid destructive behavior without user confirmation.

Similarly, changing a Usability Report to another Report Type must not
unexpectedly delete configured fields or report content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Viewer

The Report Viewer shall render a Usability Report according to its
configured Layout and Fields.

The Viewer shall:

- Display only configured fields.

- Preserve configured field order.

- Preserve configured labels.

- Display selected usability heuristics where configured.

- Not display Analytics.

- Display an optional Table of Contents with accessible section focus links when configured.

- Preserve the configured layout.

- Preserve existing Report Viewer accessibility behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Templates

Usability Reports shall integrate with ART's existing Report Template
functionality.

Users shall be able to create templates containing:

- Usability Report as the Report Type.

- Configured fields.

- Usability Heuristics fields.

- Configured heuristic options where supported.

- Configured layout.

- Other Executive Summary-compatible configuration options.

Templates shall not introduce automatic/default Usability Report fields.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stand-Alone and Workspace Reports

Usability Reports shall be usable both:

- As stand-alone reports.

- Within Project Workspaces.

The Report Type and configuration behavior shall be the same in both
contexts.

Workspace-based Usability Reports shall continue to respect existing:

- Workspace permissions.

- Collaboration functionality.

- Sharing.

- Working Views.

- Templates.

- Comments.

- Report permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Relationship to Audit Logs

Usability Reports shall complement Audit Logs.

An Audit Log may contain findings such as:

> 

**WCAG 1.4.3 — Contrast (Minimum)**

while a Usability Report may contain:

> 

**Checkout workflow is unnecessarily complex**

The usability issue does not need to correspond to a WCAG Success
Criterion.

A usability issue may optionally be related to an accessibility finding
when both apply, but the two report types shall remain distinct.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Examples of Appropriate Usability Report Issues

Usability Reports may be used to document issues such as:

- Navigation labels are inconsistent.

- Users cannot easily determine where they are in a workflow.

- A frequently used function is difficult to discover.

- A checkout workflow requires unnecessary steps.

- Error messages do not provide useful recovery instructions.

- Users are unsure what action will occur when activating a control.

- Terminology changes between screens.

- Important functionality is buried in an unexpected location.

- The interface requires users to remember information unnecessarily.

- A workflow is unnecessarily inefficient.

These issues may have significant effects on users even when they do not
represent accessibility violations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility and Usability

ART shall maintain a clear distinction between usability and
accessibility.

A usability issue:

> 

**Users have difficulty understanding the checkout process.**

shall not automatically be labeled as an accessibility violation.

An accessibility issue:

> 

**The checkout form's error messages are not programmatically associated
with their fields.**

shall not automatically be classified as a usability issue.

However, both may be documented when both are applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Validation

Verify that:

- **Usability Report** is available as a Report Type.

- Usability Reports use the same Layout functionality as Executive
  Summary reports.

- Usability Reports use the same Field Configuration functionality as
  Executive Summary reports.

- There are **no default Usability Report fields**.

- A newly created Usability Report can contain zero configured fields
  until the user adds fields.

- Users can configure whatever fields they need.

- Users can add, remove, reorder, and configure fields using the
  existing configuration system.

- **Usability Heuristics** is available as a field type for Usability
  Reports.

- Usability Heuristics does not unnecessarily appear as a field type for
  unrelated Report Types.

- Selecting Usability Heuristics adds the appropriate Usability
  Heuristic control to the Report Editor.

- The heuristic control contains the available usability heuristics.

- Multiple heuristics can be selected when configured for
  multi-selection.

- Nielsen's usability heuristics are available.

- Heuristic options can be customized where supported.

- Usability Reports contain **no Analytics section**.

- Usability Reports contain an optional **Table of Contents** with accessible section focus links when configured.

- Usability Reports retain Executive Summary-compatible layout
  functionality.

- Usability Reports retain Executive Summary-compatible field
  configuration functionality.

- Usability Reports work as stand-alone reports.

- Usability Reports work inside Project Workspaces.

- Usability Report templates work correctly.

- Usability Reports render correctly in the Report Viewer.

- Selected usability heuristics are preserved through save/load.

- Selected usability heuristics are preserved through supported
  import/export operations.

- Keyboard users can configure and use Usability Reports.
