- Screen-reader users can identify and operate all Usability Report
  controls.

- Existing Audit Logs are unaffected.

- Existing Executive Summaries are unaffected.

- Existing Report Types are unaffected.

- Existing Analytics functionality is unaffected for Report Types that
  support Analytics.

- Existing Table of Contents functionality is unaffected for Report
  Types that support it.

- Existing collaboration functionality is unaffected.

#### Implementation Constraint

Do **not** build a separate Usability Report editor.

Do **not** create a separate Usability Report field configuration
architecture.

Do **not** create default Usability Report fields.

Instead:

1.  Reuse the existing **Executive Summary Report Type architecture**.

2.  Reuse its **Layout** capabilities.

3.  Reuse its **Field Configuration** capabilities.

4.  Add **Usability Report** as a supported Report Type.

5.  Add **Usability Heuristics** as the only Usability Report-specific
    field type.

6.  Suppress Analytics for Usability Reports.

7.  Allow an optional Table of Contents for Usability Reports with accessible section focus links.

8.  Allow users to configure the fields they actually need.

The result should feel like a natural extension of ART's existing Report
Builder rather than a separate reporting system.

### Part 2 — Usability Heuristics, Report Data, Templates, Viewer, and Integration

#### Usability Heuristics Field Behavior

The **Usability Heuristics** field type shall behave consistently with
ART's existing configurable field types.

When a user adds a **Usability Heuristics** field to a Usability Report,
the user shall be able to configure the field using the same applicable
options available to other field types.

The field shall support, where applicable:

- 

A configurable field label.

- 

Field ordering.

- 

Required/optional configuration.

- 

Single-select or multi-select behavior.

- 

Configurable heuristic options.

- 

Preservation of selected values.

- 

Editing of selected values.

- 

Removal of the field from the report configuration.

Do not create a separate configuration interface for the Usability
Heuristics field. Reuse the existing Field Configuration architecture.

#### Usability Heuristic Selection

When a Usability Heuristics field is present in the Report Editor, ART
shall display the corresponding usability heuristic selection control.

The control shall:

- 

Use the configured field label.

- 

Display the configured usability heuristic options.

- 

Support the configured single-select or multi-select behavior.

- 

Allow the user to select the applicable heuristic or heuristics.

- 

Preserve the selected value or values.

- 

Allow the user to change the selection.

- 

Be fully keyboard accessible.

- 

Be fully accessible to screen-reader users.

For example:

    Usability Heuristic(s)

    [Consistency and standards
     Recognition rather than recall]

The exact presentation shall follow ART's existing accessible
field-control patterns.

If the field is configured for single selection, only one heuristic may
be selected.

If the field is configured for multiple selection, multiple heuristics
may be selected.

#### Usability Heuristic Options

The initial Usability Heuristics options shall include the commonly
recognized Nielsen usability heuristics:

- 

Visibility of system status.

- 

Match between the system and the real world.

- 

User control and freedom.

- 

Consistency and standards.

- 

Error prevention.

- 

Recognition rather than recall.

- 

Flexibility and efficiency of use.

- 

Aesthetic and minimalist design.

- 

Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors.

- 

Help and documentation.

The options shall be presented as selectable values rather than
hard-coded report content.

The user shall not be required to use all of the available heuristics.

#### Configurable Heuristic Options

Where the existing Field Configuration architecture supports
configurable dropdown or multi-select options, users shall be able to
customize the Usability Heuristics options.

This shall allow organizations to use:

- 

Nielsen's usability heuristics.

- 

Organization-specific usability heuristics.

- 

Custom usability principles.

- 

Other recognized usability methodologies.

For example:

    Visibility of system status
    Consistency and standards
    Recognition rather than recall
    Task efficiency
    Content clarity
    Workflow consistency
    Organization-specific heuristic

ART shall not require every organization to use the same usability
methodology.

The implementation shall not hard-code Nielsen's heuristics in a manner
that prevents customization where customization is supported by the
existing field architecture.

#### Usability Heuristic Definitions

Where ART provides field help, descriptions, tooltips, or other
explanatory information, the Usability Heuristics options may include
accessible definitions or descriptions.

Any such explanatory information shall:

- 

Be available to keyboard users.

- 

Be accessible to screen-reader users.

- 

Not interfere with the accessible name of the control.

- 

Not interfere with keyboard navigation.

- 

Not replace the selected value.

- 

Not alter the configured report output unless explicitly configured to
do so.

#### No Automatically Added Usability Heuristic Field

Selecting **Usability Report** as the Report Type shall **not
automatically add a Usability Heuristics field**.

The user must explicitly add the field through Field Configuration if
they want to use usability heuristics.

For example:

    Report Type: Usability Report

    Configured Fields:
    - Issue Title
    - Location
    - Issue Description
    - Recommendation

shall remain a valid Usability Report.

Likewise:

    Report Type: Usability Report

    Configured Fields:
    - Finding
    - Usability Heuristics
    - Tester Name
    - Comments

shall also be valid.

#### Usability Report Data Model

Usability Reports shall use ART's existing report data architecture.

Do not create a separate storage system solely for Usability Reports.

The report data shall preserve:

- 

Report Type.

- 

Configured fields.

- 

Field types.

- 

Field labels.

- 

Field order.

- 

Field values.

- 

Layout configuration.

- 

Report metadata.

- 

Organization/Client information where provided.

- 

Product information where provided.

- 

Project information where applicable.

- 

Workspace information where applicable.

- 

Tester information where provided.

- 

Usability Heuristic selections where configured.

The data model must support different Usability Reports having different
field configurations.

For example, both of the following must be valid:

    Usability Report A

    Issue
    Location
    Description
    Usability Heuristic
    Tester

and:

    Usability Report B

    Finding
    Severity
    Recommendation
    Status
    Comments

ART shall not assume that a particular field exists merely because it is
commonly useful for usability testing.

#### Report Metadata

Usability Reports shall use ART's existing report metadata architecture.

Where applicable, metadata may include:

- 

Organization/Client.

- 

Product.

- 

Product Version.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Tester/Tester Name.

- 

Report Date.

- 

Other existing metadata.

Metadata shall remain separate from configurable report fields where
that distinction already exists in ART.

The absence of a particular configurable field shall not prevent a
Usability Report from being created, saved, viewed, or exported.

#### Organization/Client Integration

The existing **Organization/Client** metadata field shall be supported
for Usability Reports.

When Organization/Client is populated, the value may be used by the
**Organization Statistics** functionality established by Epic 42.

Organization Statistics shall use the explicitly provided
Organization/Client value when grouping Usability Report data.

ART shall not attempt to infer an organization from:

- 

Report title.

- 

Product name.

- 

Project name.

- 

Workspace name.

- 

Tester name.

The Organization/Client metadata value shall be the authoritative source
for organizational aggregation.

The ART documentation shall continue to explain that Organization
Statistics are only accurate when the Organization/Client field is
consistently and accurately populated.

#### Product Integration

The optional **Product** field established for report metrics shall be
supported for Usability Reports.

When Product information is provided, Usability Report data may be
aggregated by:

- 

Product.

- 

Organization.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Report.

- 

Time period.

If Product information is not provided, the report shall remain
completely valid.

ART shall not invent or infer a Product value.

#### Tester Integration

Where **Tester/Tester Name** information is provided, ART may use it for
Organization Statistics and other applicable reporting.

Potential statistics include:

- 

Number of unique testers.

- 

Usability Reports contributed to by each tester.

- 

Products tested by each tester.

- 

Projects tested by each tester.

- 

Workspaces tested by each tester.

- 

Usability findings associated with each tester.

Tester statistics shall describe testing activity and coverage.

They shall not be presented as employee performance evaluations,
productivity rankings, or quality rankings.

#### Report Templates

Usability Reports shall integrate with ART's existing Report Template
functionality.

A Usability Report template shall preserve the configured:

- 

Report Type.

- 

Layout.

- 

Fields.

- 

Field order.

- 

Field labels.

- 

Field types.

- 

Usability Heuristics fields.

- 

Configured heuristic options where supported.

- 

Required/optional settings where supported.

- 

Other Executive Summary-compatible configuration.

A Usability Report template shall **not** introduce fields that were not
configured by the template author.

#### Creating a Usability Report from a Template

When a user creates a Usability Report from a template:

1.  

ART shall create the report using the Usability Report Report Type.

2.  

The template's configured Layout shall be applied.

3.  

The template's configured fields shall be created.

4.  

Any configured Usability Heuristics field shall be created.

5.  

The configured heuristic options shall be available.

6.  

No Analytics section shall be created.

7.  

Table of Contents shall be created only when explicitly enabled in template or layout options.

8.  

No additional default fields shall be added.

9.  

The user shall be able to enter and edit the configured report data
according to their permissions.

#### Editing an Existing Usability Report

When an existing Usability Report is opened for editing:

- 

The Report Type shall remain Usability Report.

- 

The configured Layout shall be preserved.

- 

The configured fields shall be preserved.

- 

Field order shall be preserved.

- 

Field labels shall be preserved.

- 

Existing field values shall be preserved.

- 

Selected Usability Heuristics shall be preserved.

- 

Report metadata shall be preserved.

- 

Organization/Client shall be preserved.

- 

Product shall be preserved where provided.

- 

Tester information shall be preserved where provided.

Opening or editing a report shall not automatically add fields.

#### Adding or Removing Fields After Data Entry

If a user modifies Field Configuration after data has already been
entered, ART shall handle existing data safely.

Adding a field shall not modify existing fields or their values.

Reordering fields shall not modify their stored values.

Changing a field label shall not change the underlying field value.

If removing a configured field could result in loss of data associated
with that field, ART shall:

- 

Warn the user.

- 

Clearly identify the potentially affected data.

- 

Require appropriate confirmation before destructive behavior.

The implementation shall follow existing ART behavior for field removal
wherever possible.

#### Report Viewer

The Report Viewer shall render Usability Reports according to their
configured Layout and Fields.

The Viewer shall:

- 

Display the configured report title.

- 

Display configured sections.

- 

Display configured fields.

- 

Preserve configured field order.

- 

Preserve configured field labels.

- 

Display configured field values.

- 

Display selected Usability Heuristics.

- 

Preserve multi-value selections.

- 

Display applicable metadata according to existing Report Viewer
behavior.

- 

Respect existing permissions and sharing behavior.

The Report Viewer shall **not** display:

- 

Analytics.

- 

A Table of Contents.

- 

Fields that were not configured for the report.

#### Usability Heuristics in the Report Viewer

When a Usability Heuristics field has been configured and populated, the
Report Viewer shall display the selected heuristic value or values using
ART's existing field-rendering conventions.

For example:

    Applicable Heuristics

    Consistency and standards
    Recognition rather than recall

If the user configured the field label as:

> 

**Applicable Heuristics**

the Report Viewer shall display **Applicable Heuristics**.

It shall not replace the configured label with a hard-coded label such
as **Usability Heuristics**.

#### Exported Usability Reports

Usability Reports shall use ART's existing export architecture.

Where the selected export format supports the applicable report
configuration, the exported report shall preserve:

- 

Report title.

- 

Configured Layout.

- 

Configured fields.

- 

Field labels.

- 

Field values.

- 

Usability Heuristic selections.

- 

Report metadata.

- 

Organization/Client.

- 

Product.

- 

Tester information.

- 

Other configured content.

Exports shall not automatically add:

- 

Analytics.

- 

Table of Contents.

- 

Default usability fields.

- 

Fields that were not configured.

The exported report shall reflect the actual configuration of the
Usability Report.

#### Word, PDF, HTML, and Other Exports

Where ART supports Microsoft Word, PDF, HTML, or other report exports,
Usability Reports shall use the existing export mechanisms.

The exported report should preserve the configured structure and content
as closely as the target format permits.

For example, if the user configures:

    Issue Title
    Location
    Issue Description
    Usability Heuristics
    Recommendation

the exported report shall contain those fields in the configured order.

It shall not automatically add:

    Tester Name
    Severity
    Category
    Impact on Users

unless those fields were actually configured.

#### Search and Filtering

Usability Reports shall integrate with ART's existing report search and
filtering capabilities where applicable.

Where supported by the underlying field architecture, users should be
able to search or filter Usability Reports by:

- 

Report Type.

- 

Field values.

- 

Usability Heuristic.

- 

Organization/Client.

- 

Product.

- 

Project.

- 

Workspace.

- 

Tester.

- 

Date.

- 

Other configured metadata.

The implementation must account for the fact that Usability Reports can
have completely different field configurations.

ART shall not assume that every Usability Report contains the same
fields.

#### Organization Statistics Integration

Usability Report data shall be available to the optional **Organization
Statistics** framework when sufficient information exists.

Potential metrics may include:

- 

Total Usability Reports.

- 

Usability Reports by Product.

- 

Usability Reports by Project.

- 

Usability Reports by Workspace.

- 

Usability Reports by time period.

- 

Usability issues by Usability Heuristic.

- 

Usability issues by Category, when a Category field is configured.

- 

Usability issues by Severity, when a Severity field is configured.

- 

Unique testers, when Tester Name information is available.

- 

Recurring usability issues where sufficient information exists.

ART shall not assume that any optional field exists.

If a particular Usability Report does not contain a Category field, for
example, ART shall not fabricate a Category value for Organization
Statistics.

Organization Statistics shall clearly distinguish between:

- 

Data that exists.

- 

Data that is not available.

- 

Data that is not configured.

- 

Data that cannot be reliably aggregated.

#### Heuristic Analytics

When Organization Statistics are enabled, ART may aggregate Usability
Heuristic data across applicable Usability Reports.

Potential metrics include:

- 

Number of reports containing each heuristic.

- 

Number of findings associated with each heuristic.

- 

Percentage of findings associated with each heuristic.

- 

Heuristic trends over time.

- 

Heuristics by Product.

- 

Heuristics by Project.

- 

Heuristics by Workspace.

- 

Heuristics by Organization.

Because a single finding may have multiple heuristics, ART shall clearly
distinguish between:

> 

**Number of findings**

and:

> 

**Number of heuristic associations**

Percentages shall clearly identify the denominator being used.

#### No Analytics Inside Individual Usability Reports

The Organization Statistics integration shall **not** cause an Analytics
section to appear inside an individual Usability Report.

These are separate concepts.

**Individual Usability Report:**

- 

Configured report content.

- 

Configured Layout.

- 

Configured fields.

- 

No Analytics.

- 

Optional Table of Contents with accessible section focus links.

**Organization Statistics:**

- 

Optional organization-level aggregation.

- 

May analyze data from Usability Reports.

- 

Exists independently of the individual Usability Report.

This distinction shall be maintained throughout ART.

#### Workspace Integration

Usability Reports created within Project Workspaces shall use the
existing Workspace architecture.

They shall respect:

- 

Workspace permissions.

- 

Report permissions.

- 

Collaboration permissions.

- 

Sharing permissions.

- 

Working Views.

- 

Comments.

- 

Templates.

- 

Workspace organization.

- 

Existing collaboration functionality.

Usability Reports shall not introduce a separate permission model.

#### Stand-Alone Report Integration

A stand-alone Usability Report shall not require:

- 

An Organization.

- 

A Product.

- 

A Project.

- 

A Workspace.

- 

An Audit Log.

Users shall be able to create and use a Usability Report with only the
fields and metadata they choose to provide.

If organizational or product information is omitted, the report shall
remain valid. The missing information shall simply be unavailable for
corresponding organization or product-level analytics.

#### Accessibility Requirements

The Usability Report functionality itself shall meet ART's existing
accessibility requirements.

All controls shall be accessible using:

- 

Keyboard.

- 

Screen reader.

- 

Mouse.

- 

Other supported input methods.

The Usability Heuristics field shall have:

- 

An accessible label.

- 

A programmatically determinable role.

- 

Correct accessible states and values.

- 

Keyboard interaction.

- 

Meaningful screen-reader announcements.

- 

Accessible instructions where provided.

- 

Accessible error handling.

If multiple selection is supported, the selected/unselected state of
each option shall be programmatically determinable.

The Report Viewer and supported exports shall preserve accessible
structure and semantics appropriate to the output format.

#### Validation

Verify that:

- Executive Summary Layout functionality is available to Usability
  Reports.
- Executive Summary Field Configuration functionality is available to
  Usability Reports.
- No default Usability Report fields are automatically created.
- A user can create a Usability Report containing only the fields they
  choose.
- The Usability Heuristics field type can be added.
- The Usability Heuristics field can be configured.
- The Usability Heuristics control appears in the Report Editor only
  when the corresponding field has been configured.
- Configured heuristic values are available for selection.
- Multiple heuristics can be selected when multi-select is configured.
- Custom heuristic options work where supported.
- Selected heuristic values are saved.
- Selected heuristic values are restored when the report is reopened.
- Selected heuristic values appear correctly in the Report Viewer.
- Selected heuristic values appear correctly in supported exports.
- Adding fields does not alter existing fields.
- Removing fields does not silently destroy unrelated data.
- Reordering fields preserves their values.
- Changing a field label preserves its underlying data.
- Templates preserve Usability Report configuration.
- No Analytics section appears in a Usability Report.
- An optional Table of Contents appears in a Usability Report when configured, providing accessible section focus links.
- Organization Statistics can use Usability Report data without adding
  Analytics to the individual report.
- Stand-alone Usability Reports work.
- Workspace Usability Reports work.
- Existing permissions remain enforced.
- Existing collaboration functionality remains enforced.
- Keyboard navigation works throughout the Report Builder.
- Screen readers can identify and operate all Usability Report controls.
- Existing Audit Logs and Executive Summaries continue to work without
  regression.

### Part 3 — Commands, Menus, Permissions, Collaboration, and Documentation

#### Report Type Commands and Actions

Usability Report functionality shall use ART's existing command and
action architecture wherever possible.

Commands and actions related to Usability Reports shall be available
through the appropriate existing ART mechanisms, including:

- 

Menu bar.

- 

Menus.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Command Palette.

- 

Context menus where appropriate.

- 

Existing keyboard shortcuts where applicable.

Do not add unnecessary persistent controls to the primary Report Builder
interface.

The addition of Usability Reports must not unnecessarily increase visual
clutter.

#### Report Type Selection

The existing **Report Type** control shall allow users to select:

> 

**Usability Report**

When selected, ART shall update the Report Builder configuration options
to reflect the Usability Report requirements.

The transition shall occur without requiring the user to navigate to a
separate Usability Report editor.

#### Report Builder Configuration Behavior

When **Usability Report** is selected:

The Report Builder shall provide:

- 

Executive Summary-compatible Layout configuration.

- 

Executive Summary-compatible Field Configuration.

- 

The Usability Heuristics field type.

The Report Builder shall not provide:

- 

Analytics configuration.

- 

Table of Contents configuration.

- 

Automatically generated usability fields.

All other applicable Report Builder functionality shall remain
available.

#### Keyboard Accessibility

All Usability Report functionality shall be accessible using the
keyboard.

Users shall be able to:

- 

Select Usability Report as the Report Type.

- 

Configure Layout.

- 

Open Field Configuration.

- 

Add fields.

- 

Remove fields.

- 

Reorder fields.

- 

Change field types.

- 

Configure Usability Heuristics.

- 

Enter report data.

- 

Select usability heuristics.

- 

Save the report.

- 

Cancel changes.

- 

Open an existing Usability Report.

- 

View a Usability Report.

- 

Use applicable commands.

Keyboard focus shall:

- 

Follow a logical sequence.

- 

Remain predictable when controls are dynamically added or removed.

- 

Move appropriately when a new field is created.

- 

Not become trapped in dynamically generated controls.

- 

Not unexpectedly return to the beginning of the page.

Existing ART keyboard shortcuts shall continue to function.

#### Screen Reader Accessibility

Usability Report functionality shall be fully compatible with supported
screen readers.

Screen-reader users shall be able to determine:

- 

Which Report Type is selected.

- 

Which fields are configured.

- 

The label of each configured field.

- 

The field type.

- 

Required/optional state where applicable.

- 

The available Usability Heuristics options.

- 

Which heuristic values are selected.

- 

Validation errors.

- 

Save status.

- 

Other relevant dynamic changes.

Dynamic changes to Field Configuration shall be announced appropriately
where an announcement is necessary for understanding the change.

For example, when a user adds a Usability Heuristics field, the newly
created field should become discoverable without requiring the user to
manually search through the page.

#### Dynamic Usability Heuristic Control

When a Usability Heuristics field is added to the report configuration,
the corresponding control shall be dynamically added to the Report
Editor.

The implementation shall ensure that:

- 

The new control has a programmatically associated label.

- 

The control appears in the correct visual position.

- 

The control appears in the correct keyboard navigation order.

- 

Screen-reader users can discover the new control.

- 

Focus behavior is predictable.

- 

Existing controls are not displaced from the logical interaction
sequence.

If ART's existing dynamic-field behavior already provides these
capabilities, reuse that implementation.

#### Field Configuration and Focus

When a user adds a Usability Heuristics field through Field
Configuration, focus behavior shall follow the same conventions used by
other configurable field types.

When a field is removed:

- 

Focus shall move to an appropriate nearby control.

- 

Focus shall not be lost.

- 

Focus shall not unexpectedly move to the beginning of the page.

When fields are reordered:

- 

Keyboard users shall be able to determine the resulting order.

- 

Screen readers shall encounter the fields in the same logical order as
sighted users.

#### Permissions

Usability Reports shall use ART's existing permissions architecture.

Do not create a separate Usability Report permission system.

Permissions shall control access to:

- 

Creating Usability Reports.

- 

Viewing Usability Reports.

- 

Editing Usability Reports.

- 

Deleting Usability Reports.

- 

Sharing Usability Reports.

- 

Configuring Usability Report fields.

- 

Editing report metadata.

- 

Exporting Usability Reports.

The exact permissions shall follow the existing Report and Workspace
permission models.

#### Stand-Alone Report Permissions

For stand-alone Usability Reports, permissions shall be applied at the
report level according to ART's existing permission framework.

A user may have permission to:

- 

Read a report.

- 

Edit a report.

- 

Configure its fields.

- 

Share the report.

- 

Export the report.

Permissions shall be independently enforceable where the existing
architecture supports modular report permissions.

#### Workspace Usability Report Permissions

Usability Reports inside a Project Workspace shall inherit the
applicable Workspace and Report permissions.

Workspace permissions shall not automatically grant users permissions
beyond what the existing collaboration framework allows.

For example, a user with read-only access to a Workspace shall not gain
editing access to a Usability Report merely because it is a Usability
Report.

#### Collaboration

Usability Reports shall participate in ART's existing collaboration
framework.

Where collaboration is enabled, users shall be able to collaborate on
Usability Reports according to their permissions.

Existing collaboration capabilities may include:

- 

Shared editing.

- 

Comments.

- 

Sharing.

- 

Working Views.

- 

Workspace collaboration.

- 

Report-level collaboration.

- 

Appropriate presence or synchronization functionality where already
supported.

Usability Reports shall not introduce a separate collaboration
mechanism.

#### Working Views

Usability Reports shall support ART's existing Working View
functionality where applicable.

Working Views shall respect the user's permissions.

For example:

- 

An editor may create an editable Working View.

- 

A contributor may create a Working View within their permissions.

- 

A viewer may create a read-only Working View where the existing Working
View architecture permits it.

A Working View shall not change the underlying Usability Report
configuration unless the user has the necessary permissions.

#### Comments

Where ART supports comments on reports or report fields, Usability
Reports shall use the existing commenting functionality.

Comments shall remain distinct from the configured report fields.

A user shall not be required to add a Comments field simply to
participate in collaboration comments.

If a user wants comments to be part of the actual report content, they
may explicitly add a configurable field such as:

> 

Comments

This distinction shall be maintained between:

- 

**Report content fields.**

- 

**Collaboration comments.**

#### Sharing

Usability Reports shall use ART's existing sharing architecture.

Users shall be able to share Usability Reports according to their
existing permissions.

Sharing shall not automatically expose:

- 

Other reports.

- 

Other Workspace content.

- 

Organization Statistics.

- 

Private Working Views.

- 

Personal plugins.

- 

Other private resources.

Sharing a Usability Report shall only grant the access permitted by
ART's existing sharing model.

#### Plugins and Packages

Usability Reports shall be compatible with ART's existing plugin and
package architecture.

A plugin may provide functionality related to Usability Reports, but the
plugin's availability shall follow the existing plugin permission and
sharing model.

A user may have:

- 

A personal Usability Report plugin.

- 

An organization-provided plugin.

- 

A Workspace-provided plugin.

- 

A shared plugin.

The Usability Report feature itself shall not require any plugin.

#### Organization Statistics

If Organization Statistics are enabled in Application Settings,
Usability Reports may contribute data to the Organization Statistics
system.

The Organization Statistics system shall respect:

- 

Organization/Client metadata.

- 

Product metadata.

- 

Project information.

- 

Workspace information.

- 

Report information.

- 

Tester information.

- 

Available configured fields.

Usability Reports shall not display organization-level analytics within
the individual report.

#### Organization Statistics Data Availability

Because Usability Reports are fully configurable, ART must account for
different reports having different fields.

For example:

**Report A**

    Issue
    Severity
    Usability Heuristic
    Tester

**Report B**

    Problem
    Recommendation
    Usability Heuristic

**Report C**

    Finding
    Category
    Status

The Organization Statistics system shall aggregate only data that is
actually available.

It shall not assume that all Usability Reports contain:

- 

Severity.

- 

Category.

- 

Status.

- 

Tester.

- 

Recommendation.

- 

Impact.

- 

Location.

- 

Any other specific field.

#### Organization Statistics Accuracy

The ART User Guide and related documentation shall explain that
organizational analytics depend on the quality and consistency of report
metadata and configured fields.

In particular, accurate organization-level aggregation requires users to
consistently populate:

> 

**Organization/Client**

in the report metadata.

If Organization/Client values are:

- 

Missing.

- 

Inconsistent.

- 

Misspelled.

- 

Abbreviated differently.

- 

Changed between reports.

ART may be unable to accurately group the reports into a single
organization.

The system shall not silently assume that similar-looking organization
names represent the same organization unless ART's Organization
management architecture explicitly provides that capability.

#### Product Statistics

Where Product information is provided, Organization Statistics may
aggregate Usability Report data by Product.

Potential statistics include:

- 

Usability Reports by Product.

- 

Usability findings by Product.

- 

Heuristics by Product.

- 

Categories by Product where Category exists.

- 

Severity by Product where Severity exists.

- 

Tester coverage by Product.

- 

Trends by Product.

If Product is not provided, the report shall not be assigned to an
invented or inferred Product.

#### Tester Statistics

Where Tester/Tester Name information is available, Organization
Statistics may track unique testers.

Potential dimensions include:

- 

Unique testers in the organization.

- 

Unique testers by Product.

- 

Unique testers by Project.

- 

Unique testers by Workspace.

- 

Unique testers by Report.

- 

Usability Reports by tester.

- 

Testing activity over time.

These statistics shall be informational and descriptive.

ART shall not present them as:

- 

Employee rankings.

- 

Productivity scores.

- 

Performance evaluations.

- 

Quality rankings.

#### Data Relationships

Where sufficient information exists, ART should be able to analyze
Usability Report data across multiple dimensions.

For example:

> 

Organization → Product → Project → Workspace → Report → Usability
Heuristic

or:

> 

Organization → Product → Time Period → Category

or:

> 

Organization → Tester → Product → Report

The implementation shall use the existing Organization Statistics
architecture rather than creating a separate Usability Analytics
architecture.

#### Report Duplication and Templates

Duplicating an existing Usability Report shall preserve the report's
configured:

- 

Report Type.

- 

Layout.

- 

Fields.

- 

Field configuration.

- 

Usability Heuristic field configuration.

- 

Selected values where appropriate according to existing duplication
behavior.

- 

Other supported report configuration.

The duplication process shall follow ART's existing rules regarding
whether entered report content is copied or whether only the report
structure is copied.

Templates shall remain the preferred mechanism for creating standardized
report structures.

#### Import

Where ART supports report import, imported Usability Reports shall:

- 

Preserve the Usability Report Report Type.

- 

Preserve configured fields where supported.

- 

Preserve field values.

- 

Preserve Usability Heuristic selections.

- 

Preserve metadata where supported.

- 

Preserve Organization/Client where provided.

- 

Preserve Product where provided.

Import functionality shall validate incompatible or malformed Usability
Report data using ART's existing validation architecture.

#### Export and Accessibility

Supported exports shall preserve the semantic relationship between:

- 

Field labels.

- 

Field values.

- 

Usability Heuristic selections.

Where the target format supports accessible structure, exported reports
shall use appropriate semantic structure.

For example, a field label should not be exported merely as visual
styling if the format supports an appropriate semantic relationship
between the label and its value.

#### Documentation

Update the ART User Guide to document:

- 

How to select Usability Report as a Report Type.

- 

How Usability Reports differ from Audit Logs.

- 

How Usability Reports differ from Executive Summaries.

- 

How Layout configuration works.

- 

How Field Configuration works.

- 

That Usability Reports have **no default fields**.

- 

How to add fields.

- 

How to configure fields.

- 

How to configure the Usability Heuristics field.

- 

How to select individual or multiple heuristics.

- 

How to customize heuristic options where supported.

- 

How Usability Reports work as stand-alone reports.

- 

How Usability Reports work within Project Workspaces.

- 

How Usability Reports interact with collaboration.

- 

How Usability Reports contribute to Organization Statistics.

- 

Why Organization/Client metadata must be consistently populated.

- 

How Product and Tester information affect organizational statistics.

#### Documentation — Important Clarification

The documentation shall explicitly state:

> 

**Usability Reports are completely configurable. ART does not require or
automatically provide a predefined set of usability report fields. Users
configure the fields appropriate to their testing methodology and
reporting needs.**

The documentation shall also explicitly state:

> 

**The Usability Heuristics field is an optional field type available
when Usability Report is selected as the Report Type. Adding a Usability
Heuristics field is optional.**

#### Regression Requirements

Implementation shall not regress existing functionality for:

- Audit Logs.
- Executive Summaries.
- Other Report Types.
- Report Builder.
- Field Configuration.
- Layout Configuration.
- Report Templates.
- Report Viewer.
- Report exports.
- Organization Statistics.
- Collaboration.
- Working Views.
- Permissions.
- Plugins.
- Packages.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Screen-reader functionality.

#### Acceptance Criteria

The Epic shall be considered complete when:

- Usability Report is available as a Report Type.
- Usability Reports use Executive Summary-compatible Layout
  functionality.
- Usability Reports use Executive Summary-compatible Field Configuration
  functionality.
- No default fields are automatically added.
- Users can configure any fields they need.
- Usability Heuristics is available as an optional field type.
- A Usability Heuristics field creates the corresponding selection
  control in the Report Editor.
- Nielsen's usability heuristics are initially available.
- Heuristic options can be customized where supported.
- Single- and multi-select behavior works according to configuration.
- Usability Reports do not contain Analytics.
- Usability Reports support an optional Table of Contents with accessible links that move focus to report sections.
- Usability Reports work as stand-alone reports.
- Usability Reports work within Project Workspaces.
- Usability Reports participate in existing permissions and
  collaboration.
- Usability Reports participate in existing templates.
- Usability Reports participate in existing import/export functionality.
- Usability Reports participate in Organization Statistics without
  adding analytics to the individual report.
- Organization/Client metadata is used for organization-level
  aggregation.
- Product information is used for product-level aggregation when
  available.
- Tester information can contribute to unique tester statistics when
  available.
- Missing optional fields do not invalidate a Usability Report.
- Missing optional fields are not fabricated for statistical purposes.
- All Usability Report functionality is keyboard accessible.
- All Usability Report functionality is screen-reader accessible.
- Existing ART functionality remains unchanged unless explicitly
  required by this Epic.

### Part 4 — Testing, Validation, Error Handling, and Implementation Requirements

#### Report Builder Testing

Verify the complete Usability Report workflow from the Report Builder.

Test the following sequence:

1.  Open the Report Builder.
2.  Select **Usability Report** as the Report Type.
3.  Confirm that the Report Builder changes to the Usability Report
    configuration.
4.  Confirm that no default fields are automatically added.
5.  Open Layout Configuration.
6.  Verify that the same applicable Layout options available to
    Executive Summary reports are available.
7.  Open Field Configuration.
8.  Verify that the same applicable Field Configuration options
    available to Executive Summary reports are available.
9.  Add a standard field.
10. Add a **Usability Heuristics** field.
11. Configure the Usability Heuristics field.
12. Save the configuration.
13. Return to the Report Editor.
14. Verify that the configured fields appear in the configured order.
15. Verify that the Usability Heuristics control is present.
16. Enter report information.
17. Select one or more usability heuristics.
18. Save the report.
19. Reopen the report.
20. Verify that all configured fields and values are preserved.

#### No Default Fields Testing

Create a brand-new Usability Report without adding any fields.

Verify that:

- No fields are automatically added.
- No Issue Title field is automatically added.
- No Location field is automatically added.
- No Issue Description field is automatically added.
- No Severity field is automatically added.
- No Category field is automatically added.
- No Tester Name field is automatically added.
- No Comments field is automatically added.
- No Usability Heuristics field is automatically added.
- No other usability-specific fields are automatically added.

The user must be able to determine the complete structure of the report
through Field Configuration.

#### Executive Summary Parity Testing

Compare an Executive Summary and a Usability Report side by side.

Verify that Usability Report provides the same applicable:

- Layout capabilities.
- Field Configuration capabilities.
- Field types.
- Field configuration controls.
- Field ordering capabilities.
- Field labeling capabilities.
- Required/optional behavior.
- Dropdown configuration.
- Multi-value configuration.
- Other existing Executive Summary configuration capabilities.

Then verify that the Usability Report additionally provides:

> 

**Usability Heuristics**

as a field type.

Do not introduce unrelated Usability Report-specific configuration
controls.

#### Analytics Suppression Testing

Select **Usability Report** as the Report Type.

Verify that:

- Analytics configuration is unavailable.
- No Analytics section is generated.
- No Analytics fields are generated.
- No Analytics configuration is saved to the report.
- No Analytics section appears in the Report Viewer.
- No Analytics section appears in supported exports.

Then switch to a Report Type that supports Analytics.

Verify that Analytics functionality continues to work normally.

#### Table of Contents Testing

Select **Usability Report** as the Report Type and enable Table of Contents in layout configuration.

Verify that:

- Table of Contents configuration is available.
- The Table of Contents renders accessible links pointing to each section of the report.
- Activating a section link from the Table of Contents moves keyboard focus directly to that section heading.
- When disabled, no Table of Contents appears in the Report Viewer.

Then switch to a Report Type that supports a Table of Contents.

Verify that existing Table of Contents functionality remains unchanged.

#### Usability Heuristics Testing

Add a Usability Heuristics field.

Verify that:

- The field can be added.
- The field can be removed.
- The field can be reordered.
- The field label can be configured.
- The field can be configured as required/optional where supported.
- Available heuristic values are displayed.
- Nielsen's initial heuristic options are available.
- Single selection works when configured.
- Multiple selection works when configured.
- Selected values are saved.
- Selected values are restored.
- Selected values can be edited.
- Selected values are displayed correctly in the Report Viewer.

#### Heuristic Configuration Testing

Where configurable field options are supported, modify the available
heuristic values.

For example, remove:

> 

Aesthetic and minimalist design

and add:

> 

Organization-specific workflow efficiency

Verify that the Report Editor uses the updated list.

Verify that the customized values are preserved when:

- Saving the report.
- Closing and reopening the report.
- Saving the template.
- Creating a report from the template.

#### Dynamic Field Testing

Add multiple fields dynamically.

Verify that:

- Each field is inserted correctly.
- Each field receives the correct label.
- Each field receives the correct field type.
- Each field appears in the correct order.
- The Usability Heuristics control appears when appropriate.
- No duplicate controls are created.
- Existing controls remain functional.
- Focus remains predictable.

Remove fields dynamically.

Verify that:

- The correct field is removed.
- Other fields remain unchanged.
- Focus moves to an appropriate control.
- No orphaned controls remain.
- No stale field values appear.

#### Field Reordering Testing

Create a report with several fields:

    Issue
    Location
    Description
    Usability Heuristic
    Recommendation
    Tester
    Comments

Reorder them several times.

Verify that:

- The visual order changes correctly.
- The keyboard navigation order follows the configured order.
- The screen-reader reading order follows the configured order.
- The Report Viewer uses the configured order.
- Supported exports use the configured order.
- Field values remain associated with the correct fields.

#### Field Label Testing

Change:

> 

Usability Heuristics

to:

> 

Applicable Heuristics

Verify that:

- The Report Editor uses the new label.
- The accessible name uses the new label.
- The Report Viewer uses the new label.
- Supported exports use the new label.
- The underlying field type remains Usability Heuristics.
- Existing selected values are preserved.

#### Required Field Testing

Where required/optional field configuration is supported:

Configure a Usability Heuristics field as required.

Attempt to save the report without selecting a heuristic.

Verify that:

- The save operation is prevented when appropriate.
- An accessible validation message is provided.
- The error is associated with the correct field.
- Keyboard users can reach the field.
- Screen-reader users are informed of the error.
- Focus moves appropriately according to ART's existing validation
  behavior.

Then select a valid heuristic and verify that the report can be saved.

#### Stand-Alone Report Testing

Create a Usability Report outside of a Workspace.

Verify that it can be:

- Created.
- Configured.
- Saved.
- Edited.
- Viewed.
- Duplicated where supported.
- Exported where supported.
- Deleted according to permissions.

Verify that no Workspace is required.

#### Workspace Report Testing

Create a Usability Report inside a Project Workspace.

Verify that:

- The report can be created.
- Workspace permissions are enforced.
- Report permissions are enforced.
- Collaboration functionality remains available where permitted.
- Comments remain available where permitted.
- Working Views remain available where permitted.
- Sharing remains available where permitted.
- Templates remain available where permitted.

Verify that Workspace functionality does not require a separate
Usability Report implementation.

#### Organization Metadata Testing

Create several Usability Reports using different Organization/Client
values.

For example:

    Organization/Client:
    Acme Corporation

and:

    Organization/Client:
    Acme Corporation

and:

    Organization/Client:
    Other Organization

Verify that Organization Statistics correctly groups the applicable
reports according to the provided metadata.

Then create a report with no Organization/Client value.

Verify that:

- The report remains valid.
- It is not incorrectly assigned to an organization.
- Organization-level statistics do not fabricate an organization value.

#### Product Metadata Testing

Create Usability Reports with:

- Product A.
- Product B.
- No Product.

Verify that Product-level statistics correctly distinguish the available
Product values.

Verify that reports without Product information remain valid.

#### Tester Testing

Create Usability Reports with multiple Tester/Tester Name values.

Verify that ART can identify:

- Unique testers.
- Reports associated with each tester.
- Products associated with each tester.
- Projects associated with each tester where applicable.
- Workspaces associated with each tester where applicable.

Verify that missing Tester information does not prevent a report from
being created or saved.

#### Organization Statistics Testing

When Organization Statistics are enabled:

Verify that Usability Reports can contribute applicable data to the
Organization Statistics dashboard.

Test available dimensions including:

- Organization.
- Product.
- Project.
- Workspace.
- Report.
- Time period.
- Tester.
- Usability Heuristic.
- Category when configured.
- Severity when configured.

Verify that statistics correctly distinguish between:

- Data that exists.
- Data that is missing.
- Data that is not configured.
- Data that cannot be reliably aggregated.

Do not display fabricated zero values when a field is simply not present
in the underlying reports.

#### Cross-Report Field Variability Testing

Create multiple Usability Reports with different field configurations.

For example:

**Report A**

    Issue
    Usability Heuristic
    Tester

**Report B**

    Issue
    Severity
    Category

**Report C**

    Finding
    Recommendation
    Usability Heuristic
    Status

Verify that ART can aggregate available data without assuming that all
reports have identical fields.

For example, Category statistics should be based only on reports where
Category data actually exists.

#### Import Testing

Where report import is supported:

Import a Usability Report containing:

- Configured fields.
- Usability Heuristic values.
- Metadata.
- Organization/Client.
- Product.
- Tester information.

Verify that all supported data is preserved.

Test invalid or incomplete imported data.

Verify that ART handles validation gracefully without corrupting the
report.

#### Export Testing

Export Usability Reports using each supported export format.

Verify that:

- The report is identified as a Usability Report where appropriate.
- Configured fields are preserved.
- Field order is preserved.
- Field labels are preserved.
- Usability Heuristic values are preserved.
- Metadata is preserved where supported.
- Analytics are not added.
- An optional Table of Contents with accessible section focus links is included when configured.
- Unconfigured fields are not added.

#### Report Viewer Testing

Verify that the Report Viewer correctly renders Usability Reports
containing:

- No fields.
- One field.
- Multiple fields.
- A Usability Heuristics field.
- Multiple selected heuristics.
- Long field values.
- Multi-line field values.
- Customized field labels.
- Custom heuristic values.

Verify that the Viewer does not display functionality that belongs to
other Report Types.

#### Accessibility Testing

Perform accessibility testing of the complete Usability Report workflow.

Test using keyboard-only interaction.

Verify:

- Logical focus order.
- Visible focus.
- No keyboard traps.
- Predictable dynamic focus.
- Accessible field configuration.
- Accessible dropdowns.
- Accessible multi-select controls.
- Accessible validation.
- Accessible save/cancel behavior.
- Accessible Report Viewer.

Test with supported screen readers, including the screen readers already
supported by ART's accessibility testing strategy.

Verify that screen readers can determine:

- Report Type.
- Field labels.
- Field types where exposed.
- Required state.
- Selected Usability Heuristics.
- Validation errors.
- Dynamic field additions.
- Dynamic field removals.
- Save status where applicable.

#### Regression Testing

Regression testing shall verify that adding Usability Reports does not
modify existing behavior for:

- Audit Logs.
- Executive Summaries.
- Other Report Types.
- Report Builder.
- Field Configuration.
- Layout Configuration.
- Templates.
- Report Viewer.
- Export functionality.
- Organization Statistics.
- Collaboration.
- Working Views.
- Permissions.
- Plugins.
- Packages.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Menu Bar.
- Keyboard shortcuts.

#### Implementation Requirements

The implementation shall prioritize reuse of existing ART architecture.

Do not create:

- A separate Usability Report editor.
- A separate Usability Report Field Configuration system.
- A separate Usability Report Layout system.
- A separate Usability Report permission model.
- A separate Usability Report collaboration system.
- A separate Usability Report storage architecture.
- A separate Usability Report analytics architecture.

Instead, extend existing systems to recognize the new Report Type.

The primary implementation should be conceptually:

    Existing Report Builder
            |
            +-- Executive Summary
            |
            +-- Audit Log
            |
            +-- Other Report Types
            |
            +-- Usability Report
                    |
                    +-- Executive Summary Layout capabilities
                    +-- Executive Summary Field Configuration capabilities
                    +-- Usability Heuristics field type
                    +-- No Analytics
                    +-- Optional Table of Contents with accessible section focus links

#### Code Quality

The implementation shall:

- Reuse existing components.
- Reuse existing validation.
- Reuse existing field rendering.
- Reuse existing field persistence.
- Reuse existing Layout functionality.
- Reuse existing Report Viewer functionality.
- Reuse existing export functionality.
- Reuse existing permissions.
- Reuse existing collaboration.
- Reuse existing Organization Statistics infrastructure.

Avoid duplicated logic.

If existing functionality must be refactored to support Usability
Reports, refactor it in a backward-compatible manner rather than
creating duplicate implementations.

#### Final Acceptance Criteria

Epic 43 shall be considered complete only when all of the following are
true:

- **Usability Report** is available as a Report Type.
- Usability Reports use the same applicable Layout capabilities as
  Executive Summary reports.
- Usability Reports use the same applicable Field Configuration
  capabilities as Executive Summary reports.
- Usability Reports have **no default fields**.
- Users can configure exactly the fields they need.
- **Usability Heuristics** is available as an optional field type.
- The Usability Heuristics field dynamically creates its corresponding
  report-editor control.
- Nielsen's heuristics are initially available.
- Heuristic options can be customized where supported.
- Single- and multi-selection work appropriately.
- No Analytics are included in individual Usability Reports.
- An optional Table of Contents can be included in Usability Reports, featuring accessible links that move focus to each section of the report when activated.
- Organization Statistics can analyze Usability Report data
  independently of the individual report.
- Organization/Client metadata is used for organizational aggregation.
- Product metadata is used for Product aggregation when available.
- Tester information can contribute to unique tester statistics when
  available.
- Reports with different field configurations can coexist and be
  analyzed without fabricated data.
- Stand-alone Usability Reports work.
- Workspace Usability Reports work.
- Existing collaboration and permission systems are respected.
- Templates work.
- Import/export works where supported.
- Report Viewer works.
- Keyboard accessibility works.
- Screen-reader accessibility works.
- Existing Report Types and functionality do not regress.

**The core design principle for this Epic is:**

> 

**Usability Report is a flexible Report Builder Report Type—not a
predefined usability-reporting template. It inherits the existing
Executive Summary Layout and Field Configuration capabilities and adds
the optional Usability Heuristics field type and optional Table of Contents
with accessible section focus links, while excluding Analytics.**

## Epic 44 — Shared Progress Logs

#### Purpose

Enhance ART's existing **Progress Log** functionality so that Progress
Logs can be shared, collaborated on, and associated with reports,
projects, and Workspaces.

A Shared Progress Log shall provide a central place for authorized users
to document and track the progress of an accessibility audit, usability
evaluation, project, or other testing activity over time.

The feature shall complement, rather than replace:

-Audit Logs.

- Usability Reports.
- Executive Summaries.
- Organization Statistics.
- Project Workspaces.
- Collaboration.
- Working Views.
- Dashboard Notifications.

A Progress Log records **what is happening during a project or testing
effort**. It is not intended to duplicate the detailed findings
contained within an Audit Log or Usability Report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Collaboration Models

Shared Progress Logs shall support two collaboration models:

1.  **Local/File-Based Collaboration**

    - Users shall be able to share Progress Logs through ART
      project/workspace export and import.
    - Shared Progress Log data shall be included in the exported
      project/workspace package.
    - Users shall be able to import an updated project/workspace package
      and merge changes.
    - Local/file-based collaboration shall not require an ART server,
      user account, or network connection.

2.  **Server-Based Collaboration**

    - When ART is connected to a supported collaboration server, Shared
      Progress Logs may support persistent multi-user synchronization.
    - Server-based collaboration shall support shared user accounts,
      permissions, synchronization, notifications, and other
      collaborative capabilities defined by this epic.
    - Server-based collaboration shall be optional and shall not
      eliminate ART's ability to operate locally.

#### Existing Progress Log Functionality

Preserve all existing Progress Log functionality unless explicitly
modified by this Epic.

Existing capabilities such as:

- Creating Progress Log entries.
- Editing entries.
- Deleting entries.
- Viewing entries.
- Adding Evaluation Items.
- Editing Evaluation Items.
- Removing Evaluation Items.
- Saving Progress Log information.
- Exporting Progress Log information where currently supported.

shall continue to function.

Do not replace the existing Progress Log implementation with a separate
system.

Extend the existing architecture to support sharing and collaboration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Progress Log

Add support for a **Shared Progress Log**.

A Shared Progress Log shall allow multiple authorized users to access
and contribute to the same Progress Log.

The Progress Log shall maintain a shared source of truth so that
authorized users see the same underlying Progress Log data.

A Shared Progress Log may be associated with:

- A stand-alone report.
- Multiple reports.
- A Project Workspace.
- A project.
- An audit.
- A usability evaluation.
- Another ART project or testing activity where the existing
  architecture supports the relationship.

The Progress Log shall not require a Workspace unless the user chooses
to associate it with one.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Stand-Alone Progress Logs

Progress Logs shall continue to work outside of Project Workspaces.

A stand-alone Progress Log may be:

- Private to one user.
- Shared with selected users.
- Associated with a specific report.
- Used independently of a report.
- Exported where supported.

A user shall not be required to create a Workspace simply to use a
Progress Log.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Workspace Progress Logs

A Progress Log associated with a Project Workspace shall participate in
the existing Workspace architecture.

Workspace Progress Logs shall respect:

- Workspace permissions.
- Report permissions.
- Collaboration permissions.
- Sharing permissions.
- Working Views.
- Comments.
- Existing Workspace membership.

Do not create a separate permission system specifically for Progress
Logs.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Persistent Object Identification

Every Progress Log, task, comment, assignment, status, and other
collaborative object shall have a stable unique identifier.

Identifiers shall remain associated with the object when the
project/workspace is exported, imported, copied, synchronized, or
merged.

These identifiers shall provide the foundation for both file-based merge
operations and future server-based synchronization.

#### Report Association

A Progress Log shall be capable of being associated with a report.

Applicable report types may include:

- Audit Log.
- Executive Summary.
- Usability Report.
- Other supported ART report types.

The Progress Log association shall not change the Report Type or report
configuration.

For example:

    Project Workspace
        |
        +-- Audit Log
        +-- Usability Report
        +-- Executive Summary
        +-- Shared Progress Log

The Progress Log records project/testing activity while the reports
contain the substantive findings and reporting content.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Multiple Report Association

Where appropriate, a single Progress Log may be associated with multiple
reports belonging to the same project or Workspace.

For example:

    Shared Progress Log
        |
        +-- Audit Log — Website
        +-- Audit Log — Mobile App
        +-- Usability Report — Website
        +-- Executive Summary

The user shall not be required to maintain separate Progress Logs merely
because multiple reports are part of the same project.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Progress Log Ownership

Each Progress Log shall have an owner or controlling user according to
ART's existing ownership architecture.

The owner shall be able to manage the Progress Log according to their
permissions, including where supported:

- Sharing.
- Removing access.
- Editing Progress Log configuration.
- Managing associated reports.
- Deleting the Progress Log.
- Managing collaborators.

If a Progress Log belongs to a Workspace, Workspace administrators or
owners shall have the appropriate management capabilities according to
the existing Workspace permission model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Model

#### Modular Permissions

Progress Log permissions shall follow the modular permission model
established by the Collaboration Framework.

Permissions shall be independently assignable where supported.

Potential permission capabilities include:

- **Read**
- **Comment**
- **Status Update**
- **Edit**
- **Task Management**
- **Share**
- **Manage Access**
- **Delete Progress Log**

The implementation shall distinguish between permissions that allow a
user to **participate in progress tracking** and permissions that allow
a user to **manage the Progress Log itself**.

A user who can read a Progress Log shall not automatically be able to
modify it.

A user who can update task status shall not automatically be able to
reassign tasks.

A user who can contribute to tasks shall not automatically receive
administrative control over sharing or permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Update Permission

Provide a dedicated **Status Update** permission.

This permission shall allow a user to:

- View the Shared Progress Log.
- View task assignments.
- Update the status of tasks assigned to them.
- Comment on tasks assigned to them.
- Use @mentions in comments according to the existing mention
  functionality.

A user with **Status Update** permission shall not automatically be able
to:

- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Edit task content.
- Delete tasks.
- Modify Progress Log configuration.
- Manage sharing.
- Manage permissions.
- Create, edit, or delete status options.

Those capabilities require additional permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### @Mentions and Notifications

@mentions shall be supported within task comments.

In local/file-based collaboration, @mentions shall be stored as part of
the project/workspace data but shall not require ART to send email.

When server-based collaboration is enabled, an @mention shall be capable
of generating an appropriate notification and email to the mentioned
team member.

#### Task Management Permissions

Shared Progress Logs shall distinguish between **Status Update** and
broader **Task Management** permissions.

Users with appropriate administrator, creator, editor, or
task-management permissions may:

- Create tasks.
- Edit tasks.
- Delete tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Change task descriptions.
- Change task metadata.
- Modify task configuration.
- Update task status where their permissions allow.
- Manage status options where their permissions allow.

The exact permission names shall integrate with ART's existing
Collaboration Framework rather than creating unnecessary parallel
permission concepts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Contributor Permissions

A contributor may be granted permission to:

- View the Progress Log.
- Add entries.
- Edit their own entries where permitted.
- Edit shared entries where permitted.
- Add Evaluation Items where permitted.
- Update Evaluation Item progress where permitted.
- Comment where permitted.
- Update statuses of tasks assigned to them if Status Update permission
  is granted.

The exact capabilities shall depend on the permissions granted to that
user.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Viewer Permissions

A viewer shall be able to view the Progress Log according to the
existing sharing model.

A viewer shall not be able to modify shared Progress Log data unless an
additional permission has explicitly been granted.

A viewer may optionally be able to create a personal Working View of the
Progress Log according to the existing Working View architecture.

A personal Working View shall not modify the shared underlying Progress
Log.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sharing and Team Members

#### Sharing a Progress Log

The process of sharing a Progress Log shall require an authorized user
to provide the information necessary to identify and notify each shared
member.

At minimum, the sharing interface shall collect:

- Team member name.
- Team member email address.
- Permission level.

The email address shall be associated with the corresponding shared
member and used for Progress Log notifications, including @mention
notifications.

The sharing interface shall provide accessible validation for missing or
invalid information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Managing Shared Members

Authorized Progress Log administrators, creators, editors, or users with
the appropriate **Manage Access** permission shall be able to:

- Add a shared member.
- Remove a shared member.
- Change a member's permission.
- Update a member's name.
- Update a member's email address.
- View the current shared members.
- Determine each member's permission level.

If a team member's email address changes, future notifications shall use
the updated address.

Existing comments and historical entries shall retain their original
attribution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tasks and Assignments

#### Assigned Tasks

Each Progress Log task shall expose its current assignment information.

For example:

    Task: Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow
    Assigned to: Jane Smith
    Status: In Progress

Team members shall be able to identify:

- Tasks assigned to themselves.
- Tasks assigned to other team members.
- Tasks that have not yet been assigned, where applicable.
- The current status of each task.
- Comments associated with the task.

Assignment information shall be available to screen-reader users and
shall not rely solely on visual presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Assignment and Reassignment

Shared Progress Log administrators, creators, editors, and users with
appropriate **Task Management/Edit** permissions shall be able to assign
Progress Log tasks to specific shared team members.

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Assign a task.
- Reassign a task.
- Change the assignee.
- Remove an assignee where appropriate.
- View the current assignee.
- Determine which tasks are assigned to themselves.
- Determine which tasks are assigned to other team members.

A user with only **Status Update** permission shall not be able to
assign or reassign tasks.

Assignment changes shall be persisted and synchronized to all authorized
users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Visibility

Team members shall be able to see which tasks are assigned to them and
which tasks are assigned to other team members, subject to their
Progress Log permissions.

The interface should provide an accessible way to distinguish:

- My Tasks.
- Tasks assigned to others.
- Unassigned Tasks.

This may be implemented through filtering, grouping, a Working View, or
another existing ART pattern rather than adding unnecessary permanent UI
controls.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Modification

Users with appropriate permissions shall be able to modify tasks.

Depending on permission level, this may include:

- Task name.
- Task description.
- Assignment.
- Status.
- Other configured task properties.
- Comments.

A user with only Status Update permission shall not be able to modify
task content unless another permission explicitly grants that
capability.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Status

#### Status Control

The mechanism for changing the status of a Progress Log task shall be an
accessible dropdown/select control.

The control shall:

- Have a programmatically associated accessible name.
- Expose the current status.
- Provide all available status options.
- Be keyboard accessible.
- Work with screen readers.
- Have a visible focus indicator.
- Preserve the selected value.
- Provide appropriate accessible feedback when the value changes.

Example:

    Status
    [In Progress ▼]

The status shall not be communicated solely through color.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Predefined Status Options

ART shall provide an initial set of predefined Progress Log task
statuses.

The initial status set should include useful general-purpose states such
as:

- Not Started.
- In Progress.
- Blocked.
- Completed.
- On Hold.
- Needs Review.
- Cancelled.

The status system shall be extensible.

Users shall not be restricted to the initial predefined options.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Custom Status Options

Authorized users shall be able to add additional status options.

For example:

- Ready for Review.
- Awaiting Client Response.
- Pending Retest.
- Retest Complete.
- Needs Clarification.

The ability to create, edit, or delete status options shall be
permission-controlled.

Users with only **Status Update** permission shall not automatically be
able to modify status options.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Option Management

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Add a status option.
- Rename a status option.
- Delete a status option where permitted.
- Reorder status options where supported.

Status-option management commands shall be available through:

- Menu bar menus.
- Global Context Menu.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Persistence

Task status shall be stored as part of the Shared Progress Log's
persistent data.

When a permitted user changes:

    Not Started

to:

    In Progress

the new value shall persist.

The status shall remain available:

- After the Progress Log is closed.
- After the browser is closed.
- After the user signs out and returns.
- Across supported sessions.
- On other supported devices when synchronization is available.
- For all users who have permission to view the Shared Progress Log.

The status shall not exist only as temporary UI state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Status Synchronization

When a task status is changed by an authorized user, the updated status
shall synchronize through the Collaboration Framework.

All authorized members shall ultimately see the same status value.

The implementation shall prevent stale local values from silently
overwriting newer shared status values.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Option Persistence

When a status option itself is modified, the updated status definition
shall persist.

For example:

    Pending Retest

may be renamed to:

    Ready for Retest

The updated status option shall persist across sessions and synchronize
to all authorized members.

If a status option is deleted, ART shall safely handle existing tasks
that previously used that status.

Do not silently lose task status information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Deletion

If an authorized user deletes a status option that is currently used by
tasks, ART shall not silently destroy the status history.

Before deletion, ART shall provide an appropriate accessible warning
and, where appropriate, require the user to:

- Reassign affected tasks to another status.
- Retain the status as an archived option.
- Confirm another safe handling method.

The implementation shall prevent orphaned tasks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status History

Where the existing Progress Log architecture supports history/audit
information, ART should preserve significant status changes.

Where status history is implemented, it should identify:

- Previous status.
- New status.
- User who made the change.
- Date/time of change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Comments and @Mentions

#### Comments on Assigned Tasks

Users with **Status Update** permission shall be able to comment on
tasks assigned to them.

Comments shall remain associated with the specific task.

For example:

    Task:
    Keyboard Testing — Checkout

    Status:
    In Progress

    Comment:
    Keyboard testing is complete through payment selection.
    The final confirmation workflow still needs testing.

The comment shall remain associated with that task even if the task is
subsequently reassigned.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### @Mention Support

Comments on Shared Progress Log tasks shall support **@mentions**.

A team member shall be able to mention another shared member by typing
an @ symbol and selecting the appropriate person.

For example:

    @Jane Smith

The mention system shall only expose people who are shared members of
the Progress Log or otherwise authorized to participate in the relevant
conversation.

Users shall not be able to use the Progress Log's @mention mechanism to
arbitrarily expose unrelated users or email addresses.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible @Mention Selection

The @mention mechanism shall be fully accessible.

When a user begins typing an @mention:

- Available shared members shall be presented.
- The suggestion list shall be keyboard accessible.
- Screen readers shall announce available suggestions appropriately.
- Users shall be able to navigate suggestions using the keyboard.
- Users shall be able to select a person without using a mouse.
- The selected person's identity shall be programmatically represented
  in the comment.

The implementation shall follow appropriate accessible
autocomplete/listbox patterns.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Mention Notifications

When a user is @mentioned in a Progress Log task comment, ART shall send
an email notification to the mentioned user.

The email shall identify:

- That the user was mentioned.
- Organization, if applicable.
- Project.
- Workspace, if applicable.
- Associated report, if applicable.
- Specific Progress Log.
- Specific task.
- Person who made the mention.
- Specific comment containing the @mention.

The notification should provide a direct way to navigate to the relevant
Progress Log/task when technically possible.

For example:

    You were mentioned in a Shared Progress Log

    Project: Website Accessibility Audit
    Workspace: Acme Accessibility Project
    Report: Main Website Audit
    Task: Keyboard Testing — Checkout
    Comment by: Alex Johnson

    "@Jane Smith — Can you verify the keyboard behavior
    on the final confirmation screen?"

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Security

Users who no longer have access to the Progress Log shall not receive
new notifications that expose private Progress Log information.

The notification system shall correctly handle:

- Multiple people mentioned in one comment.
- A person mentioning themselves.
- Removed team members.
- Invalid email addresses.
- Updated email addresses.
- Users whose permissions have changed.

ART shall avoid unnecessary duplicate notifications when the same person
is mentioned multiple times in a single comment.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Notifications

#### Shared Progress Log Notifications

All relevant Shared Progress Log activity shall be displayed in the
**Notifications** section of each user's ART Dashboard.

Dashboard Notifications shall provide a second notification channel in
addition to email notifications.

Notifications shall be personalized according to:

- The user's relationship to the Progress Log.
- Their permissions.
- Their relationship to the affected task.
- Whether they are the assignee.
- Whether they are mentioned.
- Whether they are directly affected by a change.

Users shall not receive irrelevant notifications for every change
occurring within every Shared Progress Log to which they have access.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Assignment Notifications

When a task is assigned to a team member, that team member shall receive
a Dashboard Notification.

Example:

> 

**Task Assigned**\
You were assigned the task **Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow** in
the **Website Accessibility Audit** Progress Log.

The notification should identify, where applicable:

- Organization.
- Project.
- Workspace.
- Report.
- Progress Log.
- Task.
- Person who assigned the task.
- Date/time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Reassignment Notifications

When a task is reassigned from one team member to another:

- The new assignee shall receive a notification.
- The previous assignee should receive a notification informing them
  that the task was reassigned, where appropriate.
- Users who are not affected by the reassignment should not receive
  unnecessary notifications.

Example:

> 

**Task Reassigned**\
The task **Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow** was reassigned to you
by Alex Johnson.
