------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Modification Notifications

Relevant team members shall receive Dashboard Notifications when
significant changes are made to tasks they are responsible for or
otherwise directly involved with.

Potential notification events include:

- Task assigned.
- Task reassigned.
- Task name changed.
- Task description changed.
- Task status changed.
- Task deleted.
- Task due date changed, if due dates are supported.
- Task priority changed, if priorities are supported.
- Comment added to an assigned task.
- User @mentioned in a task comment.

Notifications shall be permission-aware.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Change Notifications

When the status of a task changes, the appropriate affected team members
shall receive a Dashboard Notification.

Example:

> 

**Task Status Updated**\
**Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow** changed from **In Progress** to
**Completed**.

The notification should identify:

- Task.
- Previous status.
- New status.
- Person who changed the status.
- Progress Log.
- Associated report/project/workspace where applicable.
- Date/time.

A user should not receive notifications for every status change in a
Progress Log if they have no relevant relationship to the task.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Comment Notifications

Relevant users shall receive Dashboard Notifications when a new comment
is added to a task they are assigned to or otherwise directly involved
with.

The notification should identify:

- Task.
- Comment author.
- Comment.
- Progress Log.
- Associated report/project/workspace where applicable.
- Date/time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### @Mention Dashboard Notifications

An @mention shall generate a Dashboard Notification for the mentioned
user.

The notification shall identify:

- Person who mentioned them.
- Project.
- Workspace, where applicable.
- Report, where applicable.
- Progress Log.
- Task.
- Comment containing the mention.
- Date/time.

The @mention shall continue to generate the required email notification.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Recipient Rules

The primary recipient of task-specific notifications should be
determined by the user's relationship to the task.

EventAppropriate recipient

Task assignedNew assignee

Task reassignedNew assignee and, where appropriate, previous assignee

Status changedAssigned user and other directly relevant collaborators

Comment addedAssigned user and users participating in the task

@mentionMentioned user

Task deletedAssigned user and directly affected collaborators

Task modifiedUsers with an appropriate relationship to the task

The implementation shall avoid generating excessive notification noise.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Grouping

Where multiple changes occur within a short period, ART may group
related notifications where doing so improves usability.

For example:

> 

**3 updates to Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow**

- Task reassigned to Jane Smith.
- Status changed to In Progress.
- Alex Johnson added a comment.

Grouping must not obscure important information.

Users shall still be able to determine what changed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Navigation

Notifications associated with Shared Progress Logs shall be actionable
where possible.

Selecting a notification should take the user directly to the relevant:

- Project.
- Workspace.
- Report.
- Progress Log.
- Task.
- Comment.

The destination shall respect the user's current permissions.

If the user no longer has access to the associated Progress Log, ART
shall not expose its content through the notification.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Read/Unread State

Shared Progress Log notifications shall participate in the existing ART
Dashboard Notifications architecture.

Notifications shall support the existing:

- Read/unread state.
- Notification history.
- Dismissal behavior.
- Navigation behavior.

If ART supports notification counts/badges, Shared Progress Log
notifications shall contribute appropriately.

Users shall be able to distinguish unread notifications from previously
viewed notifications without relying solely on color.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Email and Dashboard Notification Relationship

Dashboard Notifications and email notifications shall work together
without unnecessarily duplicating information.

For example:

- An **@mention** shall generate the required email notification and
  Dashboard Notification.
- A **task assignment** shall generate a Dashboard Notification and may
  generate an email notification according to the user's notification
  preferences.
- A **status change** shall generate a Dashboard Notification according
  to the notification rules.

ART should eventually provide notification preferences allowing users to
control which eligible events generate email notifications, while
Dashboard Notifications remain available according to the application's
notification architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Persistence and Synchronization

Dashboard Notifications generated by Shared Progress Log activity shall
persist appropriately and synchronize across supported sessions/devices.

If a user views a notification on one supported device, its read/unread
state should synchronize where the existing notification architecture
supports synchronization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Accessibility

The Notifications section shall remain fully accessible.

Users shall be able to:

- Navigate notifications using the keyboard.
- Determine whether a notification is read or unread.
- Determine the type of event.
- Determine the affected Progress Log/task.
- Open the associated task.
- Dismiss notifications where supported.
- Navigate between notifications predictably.

Screen readers shall receive meaningful notification information.

For example:

> 

"Task status updated. Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow. Status
changed from In Progress to Completed. Updated by Alex Johnson. Website
Accessibility Audit Progress Log."

Dynamic notifications shall use appropriate accessible announcements
without unexpectedly moving keyboard focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Privacy

Dashboard Notifications shall be filtered according to the user's
permissions.

A user shall not receive a notification containing information about a
Shared Progress Log that they cannot currently access.

If a user's access is removed:

- Existing notification history shall be handled according to ART's
  privacy model.
- New notifications shall not expose the removed Progress Log.
- Selecting an inaccessible notification shall not bypass permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Collaboration and Synchronization

#### Simultaneous Editing

Shared Progress Logs shall support simultaneous editing when ART's
Collaboration Framework supports synchronous collaboration.

If two or more authorized users are editing the same Progress Log at the
same time:

- Changes shall be synchronized.
- Users shall not unknowingly overwrite each other's changes.
- The application shall provide appropriate conflict handling.
- Shared state shall remain consistent.

Do not implement simplistic last-write-wins behavior if doing so could
silently destroy another user's changes.

Use the synchronization architecture established by the Collaboration
Framework.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Asynchronous Collaboration

Shared Progress Logs shall support asynchronous collaboration.

A user may:

1.  Open a shared Progress Log.
2.  Add or modify entries in accordance with their permission level.
3.  Change permitted task statuses.
4.  Add permitted comments.
5.  Save changes.
6.  Leave the Progress Log.
7.  Another authorized user later opens it.
8.  The second user sees the updated shared state.

Users do not need to be online simultaneously to contribute.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Synchronization Status

When a Shared Progress Log is being synchronized, the interface shall
provide an accessible indication of the current state where appropriate.

Potential states include:

- Saved.
- Saving.
- Synchronizing.
- Offline.
- Changes Pending.
- Conflict Requiring Attention.

Status information shall be available to screen-reader users as well as
sighted users.

Do not rely solely on color, animation, or visual indicators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Offline Behavior

Shared Progress Logs shall respect ART's local-first architecture.

If offline editing is supported:

- Users should be able to make permitted changes while offline.

- Changes should be retained locally.

- Changes should synchronize when connectivity is restored.

- Conflicts should be handled through the Collaboration Framework.

- Users should be informed if synchronization cannot be completed.

Offline behavior must not silently discard Progress Log changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Evaluation Items

#### Existing Evaluation Items

Shared Progress Logs shall support the existing **Evaluation Item**
functionality.

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Add Evaluation Items.
- Edit Evaluation Items.
- Remove Evaluation Items.
- Update Evaluation Item information.
- Track progress.
- View Evaluation Items created by other collaborators.

All actions shall be subject to permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Evaluation Item Collaboration

When multiple users have permission to edit Evaluation Items, changes
shall be reflected in the shared Progress Log.

Another authorized collaborator shall see the updated state rather than
maintaining a separate conflicting copy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Evaluation Item Keyboard Behavior

Preserve the existing accessible keyboard behavior for Evaluation Items.

In particular:

- The **Add Evaluation Item** button follows the final Evaluation Item.

- A newly added Evaluation Item appears immediately above the Add
  Evaluation Item button.

- Focus moves to the new Evaluation Item Name field.

- The new Evaluation Item participates in normal tab order.

- The Add Evaluation Item button precedes Done.

- Keyboard navigation remains sequential and predictable.

Shared functionality must not regress this behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Working Views

#### Personal Working Views

Shared Progress Logs shall support ART's existing Working View
architecture.

Working Views shall remain primarily individual to each user.

A user may create a personal Working View of a Shared Progress Log
according to their permissions.

For example:

    My Evaluation Items
    In Progress
    High Priority

without changing what other collaborators see.

A user with read-only access may create a read-only Working View where
the existing Working View architecture permits it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Shared Working Views

A user with appropriate permissions may create a **shared Working View**
for collaborators.

Shared Working Views may be useful for:

- 

Team leads.

- 

Workspace administrators.

- 

Project owners.

- 

Audit leads.

Shared Working Views shall be optional.

Individual users shall not be forced to use a shared Working View.

Personal Working Views shall remain independent from shared Working
Views.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Commands and UI Integration

#### Command Architecture

Shared Progress Log commands shall use ART's existing command
architecture.

Do not add a large collection of permanent buttons to the primary UI.

Applicable commands shall be available through:

- 

Menu bar.

- 

Menus.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Command Palette.

- 

Global Context Menu.

- 

Existing keyboard shortcuts where applicable.

If Collaboration is enabled, appropriate Progress Log collaboration
commands may also appear under the existing **Collaboration** menu.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Commands

Commands shall include, where applicable:

- 

Add Task.

- 

Edit Task.

- 

Delete Task.

- 

Assign Task.

- 

Reassign Task.

- 

Change Status.

- 

Add Comment.

- 

Edit Comment.

- 

Delete Comment.

- 

Mention Team Member.

Commands shall only be available or enabled when the user has the
required permission.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Commands

Commands shall include:

- 

Add Status.

- 

Edit Status.

- 

Delete Status.

- 

Reorder Status Options where supported.

These commands shall be available through:

- 

Menu bar menus.

- 

Global Context Menu.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Command Palette where applicable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Context-Sensitive Commands

The Global Context Menu shall expose relevant actions based on the
user's current location and selection.

For example, when a user is focused on a task assigned to themselves, a
user with Status Update permission may see:

- 

Change Status.

- 

Add Comment.

- 

Mention Team Member.

An administrator/editor may see:

- 

Edit Task.

- 

Assign Task.

- 

Reassign Task.

- 

Change Status.

- 

Add Comment.

- 

Delete Task.

Unauthorized commands shall not be presented as available actions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Enforcement

Permissions must be enforced at the underlying application/data level as
well as through the UI.

Do not merely hide an unauthorized command while leaving it executable
through:

- 

Keyboard shortcuts.

- 

Command Search.

- 

Command Palette.

- 

Global Context Menu.

- 

Direct interaction.

- 

API calls or other programmatic mechanisms.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard Accessibility

All Shared Progress Log functionality shall be available without
requiring a mouse.

Users shall be able to:

- 

Create tasks.

- 

Edit tasks.

- 

Assign tasks.

- 

Reassign tasks.

- 

Open the status dropdown.

- 

Select a status.

- 

Add a status option where permitted.

- 

Edit a status option where permitted.

- 

Delete a status option where permitted.

- 

Add comments.

- 

@mention team members.

- 

Navigate mention suggestions.

- 

Save changes.

- 

Navigate Dashboard Notifications.

- 

Open notifications and navigate to their associated tasks.

Existing keyboard navigation and shortcuts shall remain functional.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Screen Reader Accessibility

Shared Progress Logs shall be fully compatible with supported screen
readers.

Screen-reader users shall be able to determine:

- 

Progress Log name.

- 

Sharing state.

- 

User permissions.

- 

Task name.

- 

Task assignment.

- 

Task status.

- 

Available status options.

- 

Comments.

- 

Comment author.

- 

@mentions\.

- 

Synchronization status.

- 

Validation messages.

- 

Dashboard Notifications.

- 

Notification read/unread state.

- 

Notification type.

- 

Notification destination.

Dynamic collaboration updates shall not unexpectedly steal keyboard
focus.

Live updates should use appropriate announcements without creating
excessive or repetitive speech.

Users shall be able to continue editing without unexpected focus
movement.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Task Assignment

Task assignment controls shall:

- 

Have accessible labels.

- 

Identify the current assignee.

- 

Provide accessible selection of shared members.

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Work with screen readers.

- 

Clearly distinguish available members.

- 

Not expose unauthorized people.

When a task is reassigned, the change shall be communicated
appropriately to the user making the change and, where applicable, to
the new assignee.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Status Management

Status-management controls shall:

- 

Use semantic controls.

- 

Have accessible names.

- 

Expose current values.

- 

Expose available options.

- 

Work with keyboard navigation.

- 

Work with screen readers.

- 

Provide accessible validation.

- 

Preserve visible focus.

- 

Provide appropriate feedback after changes.

Status shall never depend solely on color, icons, or visual styling.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Comments

The comment interface shall:

- 

Have an accessible label.

- 

Be keyboard accessible.

- 

Support multiline comments where appropriate.

- 

Preserve comment structure.

- 

Identify comment authors.

- 

Expose timestamps where provided.

- 

Support accessible @mention selection.

- 

Announce validation or submission results.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessible Dashboard Notifications

The Notifications section shall:

- 

Use appropriate semantic structure.

- 

Provide a logical keyboard navigation order.

- 

Expose notification state programmatically.

- 

Provide meaningful accessible names.

- 

Identify the affected task and Progress Log.

- 

Expose notification actions.

- 

Preserve visible focus.

- 

Avoid unexpected focus movement when notifications are dynamically
added.

Unread state shall not be conveyed by color alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data Model and Persistence

#### Shared Progress Log Data Model

Extend ART's existing Progress Log data model rather than creating a
completely separate Progress Log architecture.

The data model shall support:

- 

Progress Log ID.

- 

Owner/creator.

- 

Sharing state.

- 

Shared members.

- 

Member names.

- 

Member email addresses.

- 

Member permissions.

- 

Entries.

- 

Tasks/Evaluation Items.

- 

Task assignment.

- 

Task status.

- 

Status-option definitions.

- 

Comments.

- 

@mentions\.

- 

Associated reports.

- 

Associated Project Workspace.

- 

Project information where applicable.

- 

Organization information where applicable.

- 

Product information where applicable.

- 

Created/modified metadata.

- 

Synchronization information where required.

The exact implementation shall conform to ART's existing architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Persistent Task Assignment

Task assignments shall be stored as persistent data.

The assignment shall remain available:

- 

Across sessions.

- 

After reopening ART.

- 

After reopening the Progress Log.

- 

On supported synchronized devices.

- 

To all authorized users.

Changing an assignee shall update the shared source of truth.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Persistent Task Status

Task status shall be stored as persistent shared data.

A status change shall not be lost when:

- 

The Progress Log closes.

- 

The browser closes.

- 

The user navigates away.

- 

The user signs out.

- 

Another collaborator opens the Progress Log.

- 

Another authorized device synchronizes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Persistent Status Definitions

Status options shall be stored as persistent configuration.

Each status should have a stable internal identity rather than relying
solely on its visible text.

For example:

    Internal status:
    status-123

    Visible label:
    Pending Retest

may later become:

    Internal status:
    status-123

    Visible label:
    Ready for Retest

Existing tasks using that status should continue to reference the same
underlying status.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Comments and Mentions Data

Comments shall preserve:

- 

Comment ID.

- 

Task association.

- 

Author.

- 

Comment content.

- 

Creation date/time.

- 

Modification information where supported.

- 

Mentioned members.

Mentions should reference the shared member's stable identity rather
than relying solely on their display name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Notification Data

Dashboard Notifications shall maintain sufficient information to
identify:

- 

Notification type.

- 

Source Progress Log.

- 

Source task.

- 

Source report/project/workspace.

- 

Source user.

- 

Date/time.

- 

Read/unread state.

- 

Navigation destination where applicable.

Notification data shall not bypass the user's current permissions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Reports, Projects, Products, and Organizations

#### Associated Reports

A Shared Progress Log shall maintain relationships to associated reports
without duplicating report data.

For example:

    Shared Progress Log
            |
            +-- Audit Log
            +-- Usability Report
            +-- Executive Summary

Deleting or modifying a Progress Log association shall not delete the
associated report.

Deleting a report shall not silently delete the entire Progress Log
unless the user explicitly confirms an appropriate destructive action
and the relationship requires it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Progress Log and Organization Integration

Shared Progress Logs shall integrate with ART's Organization
architecture where applicable.

Where an associated report or Workspace contains Organization/Client
information, the Progress Log may be associated with that organization.

Organization-level statistics may use applicable Progress Log data where
Epic 42 supports it.

ART shall not infer an organization solely from a Progress Log title or
user name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Product Integration

Where Product information is available through the associated report,
Workspace, or project architecture, Progress Log data may be associated
with that Product.

Product-level statistics may include:

- 

Progress Logs.

- 

Tasks.

- 

Completed tasks.

- 

Task status.

- 

Testing activity.

- 

Evaluation Items.

Statistics shall only be generated from data that actually exists.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tester and Contributor Activity

Where user attribution is available, ART may use Progress Log data to
provide descriptive organization/project statistics.

Potential metrics include:

- 

Number of contributors.

- 

Number of assigned tasks.

- 

Number of completed tasks.

- 

Number of active contributors.

- 

Progress over time.

These metrics shall be descriptive and shall not be presented as
employee performance scores.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Organization Statistics

Shared Progress Log information may contribute to Organization
Statistics when:

- 

Organization Statistics are enabled.

- 

The Progress Log has sufficient organization metadata.

- 

The user has appropriate access.

- 

The relevant data is available.

Potential statistics include:

- 

Total Progress Logs.

- 

Tasks by status.

- 

Tasks completed over time.

- 

Tasks by Product.

- 

Tasks by Project.

- 

Tasks by Workspace.

- 

Tasks by tester/contributor.

- 

Evaluation Items by status.

- 

Progress trends.

Organization Statistics shall respect all applicable permissions.

A user shall not gain access to organization-level information simply
because they have access to an individual Progress Log.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### No Automatic Analytics in Progress Logs

Progress Logs shall not automatically gain an Analytics section merely
because their data contributes to Organization Statistics.

The distinction shall remain:

**Progress Log:**

- 

Project/testing progress.

- 

Tasks.

- 

Assignments.

- 

Statuses.

- 

Comments.

- 

Collaboration.

**Organization Statistics:**

- 

Aggregated organizational/project data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Security and Privacy

#### Progress Log Access Without Report Access

Where permissions are modular, access to a Progress Log shall not
automatically grant access to every associated report.

For example:

    Progress Log: Edit
    Audit Log: Read

or:

    Progress Log: Status Update
    Audit Log: No Access

The Progress Log permission model shall respect the existing modular
Collaboration Framework.

ART shall not unintentionally expose report content because a user has
access to a Progress Log.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Report Access Without Progress Log Access

Having access to an associated report shall not automatically grant
access to a private Progress Log unless the sharing configuration
explicitly permits it.

This distinction is important when Progress Logs contain internal
project notes or collaboration information.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Sharing Privacy

Sharing a Progress Log shall expose only the information necessary for
the recipient's permission level.

ART shall protect:

- 

Member email addresses.

- 

Private comments.

- 

Private Progress Logs.

- 

Report content.

- 

Organization information.

- 

Other collaboration data.

Email addresses should not be displayed to all shared members unless the
existing product design explicitly requires this.

The mention-selection interface may display names while internally
associating the selected member with their email address.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Templates and Import/Export

#### Templates

Where ART supports Progress Log templates, templates shall preserve
appropriate Progress Log configuration.

Templates may include:

- 

Task structure.

- 

Evaluation Items.

- 

Status configuration.

- 

Initial status options.

- 

Layout.

- 

Other supported configuration.

Templates shall not contain private user-specific sharing information
unless the existing architecture explicitly supports reusable member
configurations.

Sharing and email addresses should normally be established when the
actual Progress Log is shared.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Import and Export

Where Progress Log import/export is supported, the implementation shall
preserve applicable:

- 

Tasks.

- 

Evaluation Items.

- 

Assignments where appropriate.

- 

Statuses.

- 

Status definitions.

- 

Comments where supported.

- 

Metadata.

- 

Associated report references where supported.

Private collaboration information should not be unintentionally exported
where the export format or permissions do not permit it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Exported Progress Logs

A Shared Progress Log export should clearly identify task information,
including where applicable:

- 

Task.

- 

Assignee.

- 

Status.

- 

Comments.

- 

Dates.

- 

Related report.

- 

Other configured information.

The exported data should not misrepresent a user's permissions or
status.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data Integrity

#### Concurrent Changes

Shared Progress Logs shall maintain data integrity when multiple users:

- 

Add tasks.

- 

Edit tasks.

- 

Assign tasks.

- 

Reassign tasks.

- 

Change status.

- 

Add comments.

- 

Mention users.

- 

Add or modify status options.

The implementation shall avoid:

- 

Duplicate tasks caused by synchronization.

- 

Lost status changes.

- 

Orphaned assignments.

- 

Orphaned statuses.

- 

Comments attached to incorrect tasks.

- 

Mentions attached to the wrong users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Assignment History

Where supported by the existing architecture, task assignment changes
should preserve historical information such as:

- 

Previous assignee.

- 

New assignee.

- 

User who made the reassignment.

- 

Date/time.

This allows collaborators to understand how responsibility changed over
time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Testing and Validation

#### Sharing Testing

Verify that an authorized user can share a Progress Log by providing:

- 

Name.

- 

Email address.

- 

Permission level.

Verify that:

- 

Required fields are validated.

- 

Invalid email addresses are handled accessibly.

- 

The shared member receives the appropriate access.

- 

The shared member appears in the member list.

- 

Their permission is correctly displayed.

- 

Their email is securely stored.

- 

Their information can be updated by authorized administrators.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Permission Testing

Test every Progress Log permission level.

Verify that a user with **Read** can view but cannot modify shared data.

Verify that a user with **Status Update** can:

- 

View the Progress Log.

- 

View assignments.

- 

Change the status of tasks assigned to them.

- 

Comment on tasks assigned to them.

Verify that a Status Update user cannot:

- 

Change another user's task status.

- 

Assign a task.

- 

Reassign a task.

- 

Modify task content unless separately permitted.

- 

Delete a task.

- 

Manage status options.

- 

Manage sharing.

Verify that administrators/creators/editors with appropriate permissions
can:

- 

Create tasks.

- 

Edit tasks.

- 

Delete tasks.

- 

Assign tasks.

- 

Reassign tasks.

- 

Manage status options.

- 

Manage access.

Permission enforcement must work through every supported interaction
mechanism.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Task Assignment Testing

Create multiple shared members.

Create multiple tasks.

Assign different tasks to different members.

Verify that:

- 

Each task displays the correct assignee.

- 

Each member can identify their own assigned tasks.

- 

Members can see tasks assigned to other members.

- 

Authorized users can reassign tasks.

- 

Unauthorized users cannot reassign tasks.

- 

Assignment changes persist.

- 

Assignment changes synchronize.

- 

Assignment notifications appear in the appropriate Dashboard
Notifications section.

- 

Appropriate affected users receive notifications.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Testing

Verify that the initial predefined statuses are available.

Verify that users with Status Update permission can change the status of
their assigned tasks.

Verify that they cannot change statuses of tasks assigned to others.

Verify that authorized administrators/editors can change statuses where
permitted.

Verify that status changes:

- 

Persist.

- 

Synchronize.

- 

Remain after reopening the application.

- 

Remain after signing out and back in.

- 

Are visible to all authorized members.

- 

Generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Custom Status Testing

Verify that an authorized user can:

- 

Add a status.

- 

Rename a status.

- 

Delete a status where safe.

- 

Reorder a status where supported.

Verify that unauthorized users cannot perform those actions.

Verify that custom statuses persist across sessions.

Verify that all authorized members receive the updated status
configuration.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Status Deletion Testing

Attempt to delete a status currently used by tasks.

Verify that ART:

- 

Identifies affected tasks.

- 

Warns the user.

- 

Prevents accidental loss of status information.

- 

Provides an appropriate remediation mechanism.

Verify that no task becomes orphaned.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Simultaneous Editing Testing

Have two authorized users open the same Progress Log.

Test:

- 

Editing different tasks.

- 

Editing the same task.

- 

Changing status.

- 

Assigning tasks.

- 

Reassigning tasks.

- 

Adding comments.

- 

Adding status options.

Verify that changes synchronize correctly.

Verify that conflicting changes are handled safely.

Verify that one user's changes do not silently disappear.

Verify that appropriate Dashboard Notifications are generated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Asynchronous Testing

User A makes changes and leaves.

User B later opens the Progress Log.

Verify that User B sees:

- 

New tasks.

- 

Updated assignments.

- 

Updated statuses.

- 

New comments.

- 

Updated status options.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### @Mention Testing

Test mentioning one team member.

Verify that:

- 

The member appears in the suggestion list.

- 

The member can be selected using the keyboard.

- 

Screen readers can identify the suggestions.

- 

The mention is correctly inserted.

- 

The correct member receives an email.

- 

The correct member receives a Dashboard Notification.

- 

The email identifies the project/workspace/report.

- 

The email identifies the Progress Log.

- 

The email identifies the task.

- 

The email contains the relevant comment.

- 

The Dashboard Notification identifies the relevant task and comment.

- 

The notification does not expose unrelated private information.

Test multiple mentions in one comment.

Verify that each appropriate recipient receives the correct
notification.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Removed-Member Testing

Share a Progress Log with a user.

Mention that user.

Remove the user's access.

Attempt to mention the removed user again.

Verify that the removed user is no longer available as an authorized
mention target.

Verify that the removed user does not receive new private Progress Log
notifications through email or the Dashboard.

Historical comments shall retain appropriate historical attribution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Email Change Testing

Change a shared member's email address.

Create a new @mention.

Verify that the notification is sent to the updated email address.

Verify that historical comments remain associated with the correct user
identity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Dashboard Notification Testing

Verify that the following generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications:

- 

Task assignment.

- 

Task reassignment.

- 

Task status change.

- 

Relevant task modification.

- 

Relevant task deletion.

- 

Comment added to an assigned/relevant task.

- 

@mention\.

Verify that:

- 

Notifications appear in the correct user's Dashboard.

- 

Unrelated users do not receive unnecessary notifications.

- 

Notifications contain the appropriate contextual information.

- 

Notifications link to the relevant task where possible.

- 

Read/unread state works.

- 

Dismissal works where supported.

- 

Notification state persists.

- 

Notification state synchronizes where supported.

- 

Removed users do not receive private notifications.

- 

Notifications are accessible to keyboard and screen-reader users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Working View Testing

Create personal Working Views.

Verify that personal views:

- 

Remain specific to the user.

- 

Do not alter other users' views.

- 

Respect the user's permissions.

- 

Do not modify shared task data merely by filtering or sorting.

Create a shared Working View with appropriate permissions.

Verify that authorized users can access it.

Verify that users can still create personal Working Views independently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Accessibility Testing

Perform keyboard-only testing of the complete feature.

Verify:

- 

Logical focus order.

- 

Visible focus.

- 

No keyboard traps.

- 

Accessible menus.

- 

Accessible context menus.

- 

Accessible task assignment.

- 

Accessible status dropdown.

- 

Accessible comments.

- 

Accessible @mention autocomplete.

- 

Accessible validation.

- 

Accessible notification/status messages.

- 

Accessible Dashboard Notifications.

- 

Predictable dynamic focus.

Perform screen-reader testing.

Verify that users can determine:

- 

Progress Log name.

- 

Sharing state.

- 

Permission level.

- 

Task name.

- 

Assignee.

- 

Status.

- 

Comments.

- 

Comment author.

- 

@mentions\.

- 

Synchronization state.

- 

Dashboard Notification type.

- 

Dashboard Notification content.

- 

Dashboard Notification read/unread state.

- 

Dashboard Notification destination.

Dynamic synchronization must not unexpectedly move focus.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Regression Testing

Verify that existing functionality continues to work for:

- 

Progress Logs.

- 

Evaluation Items.

- 

Audit Logs.

- 

Usability Reports.

- 

Executive Summaries.

- 

Report Builder.

- 

Project Workspaces.

- 

Collaboration.

- 

Working Views.

- 

Permissions.

- 

Comments.

- 

Templates.

- 

Organization Statistics.

- 

Dashboard Notifications.

- 

Import/export.

Keyboard shortcuts.

Command Search.

Command Palette.

- 

Global Context Menu.

- 

Menu bar.

#### Documentation — Permission Explanation

**Status Update:** Allows a team member to update the status of tasks
assigned to them and comment on those assigned tasks. This permission

Progress Log.

#### Implementation Requirements

#### Reuse Existing Architecture

The implementation shall prioritize reuse of ART's existing
architecture.

Do not create:

- 

A separate Progress Log collaboration system.

- 

A separate permission architecture.

- 

A separate comment system.

- 

A separate Working View architecture.

- A separate Workspace system.

- A separate sharing system.

- A separate notification identity system.

- A separate report-association architecture.

Instead, extend the existing Collaboration Framework and Progress Log
architecture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Code Quality

The implementation shall:

- Reuse existing components.
- Reuse existing permission infrastructure.
- Reuse existing collaboration infrastructure.
- Reuse existing comments.
- Reuse existing Working Views.
- Reuse existing Workspace relationships.
- Reuse existing command architecture.
- Reuse existing accessibility patterns.
- Reuse existing notification infrastructure where available.
- Avoid duplicated logic.

If existing functionality must be refactored, refactor it in a
backward-compatible manner.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### UI Requirements

The Shared Progress Log feature shall not unnecessarily clutter ART's
interface.

Commands and actions shall primarily be available through:

- Menu bar.
- Menus.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Global Context Menu.

The interface shall not require a large permanent collection of buttons
for:

- Assigning.
- Reassigning.
- Status management.
- Comments.
- Sharing.
- Collaboration.
- Notifications.

Context-sensitive controls may be displayed where they improve
discoverability without creating unnecessary UI clutter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Final Acceptance Criteria

Epic 44 shall be considered complete only when all of the following are
true:

- Existing Progress Log functionality continues to work.
- Progress Logs can be used independently of Workspaces.
- Progress Logs can be associated with reports.
- A Progress Log can be associated with multiple reports where
  supported.
- Shared Progress Logs can be accessed by authorized users.
- Sharing requires the appropriate name and email information.
- Modular permissions are enforced.
- A dedicated **Status Update** permission exists.
- Status Update users can update statuses of tasks assigned to
  themselves.
- Status Update users can comment on tasks assigned to themselves.
- Status Update users cannot change statuses of tasks assigned to other
  users.
- Status Update users cannot assign or reassign tasks unless separately
  permitted.
- Authorized administrators/creators/editors can create and modify
  tasks.
- Authorized administrators/creators/editors can assign tasks.
- Authorized administrators/creators/editors can reassign tasks.
- Team members can identify tasks assigned to themselves.
- Team members can identify tasks assigned to others.
- Task assignments persist across sessions.
- Task assignments synchronize across authorized users.
- Task statuses use an accessible dropdown.
- Initial predefined statuses are available.
- Authorized users can add status options.
- Authorized users can edit status options.
- Authorized users can delete status options safely.
- Status options persist across sessions.
- Status-option changes synchronize to authorized users.
- Task status changes persist across sessions.
- Task status changes synchronize to authorized users.
- Existing tasks remain valid when status options are modified.
- Status history is preserved where supported.
- Task assignment history is preserved where supported.
- Task comments are associated with specific tasks.
- @mentions are supported in task comments.
- @mention selection is keyboard accessible.
- @mention selection is screen-reader accessible.
- Shared members receive email notifications when @mentioned.
- Shared members receive appropriate Dashboard Notifications when
  @mentioned.
- Task assignments generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.
- Task reassignments generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.
- Relevant task modifications generate appropriate Dashboard
  Notifications.
- Relevant status changes generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.
- Relevant task comments generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.
- Notifications identify the relevant Project, Workspace, Report,
  Progress Log, and Task where applicable.
- Notifications identify the relevant user who performed the action.
- Notifications identify the nature of the change.
- Notifications provide direct navigation to the affected task where
  possible.
- Notifications respect the user's permissions.
- Removed users cannot receive new notifications exposing private
  Progress Log information.
- Notification read/unread state works with the existing Dashboard
  notification system.
- Dashboard Notifications are keyboard accessible.
- Dashboard Notifications are screen-reader accessible.
- Dynamic notification updates do not unexpectedly steal focus.
- Notification behavior does not create excessive or unnecessary
  notification noise.
- Dashboard Notifications and email notifications work together
  appropriately.
- Personal Working Views remain primarily individual.
- Shared Working Views can be created by appropriately authorized users.
- Personal Working Views do not alter the shared Progress Log.
- Simultaneous editing works where supported.
- Asynchronous collaboration works.
- Offline changes are retained where offline editing is supported.
- Synchronization conflicts are handled safely.
- Progress Log commands are available through menus and the Global
  Context Menu.
- Appropriate commands are available through Command Search/Command
  Palette.
- Unauthorized commands cannot be executed through alternate interaction
  mechanisms.
- The interface does not become unnecessarily cluttered.
- Organization Statistics can use applicable Progress Log data without
  adding analytics to individual Progress Logs.
- Associated reports remain protected by their own permissions.
- Progress Log access does not unintentionally grant report access.
- Report access does not unintentionally grant private Progress Log
  access.
- Documentation is updated.
- Keyboard accessibility is preserved.
- Screen-reader accessibility is preserved.
- Existing ART functionality does not regress.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Core Design Principle

> 

**A Shared Progress Log is a collaborative task and progress-tracking
system built on ART's existing Progress Log and Collaboration Framework.
Users with appropriate permissions can assign and manage tasks, while
team members with the dedicated Status Update permission can update the
status of their assigned tasks and comment on them. Shared status,
assignment, comments, and @mentions remain persistent and synchronized
for authorized members. Relevant task activity is surfaced through each
user's ART Dashboard Notifications, while @mentions can additionally
generate email notifications. Personal Working Views remain individual
to each user, and the primary ART interface remains uncluttered by
making collaboration functionality available through menus, commands,
Command Search, Command Palette, and the Global Context Menu.**

### Part 2 — Shared Progress Logs

#### Workspace Progress Logs

A Progress Log associated with a Project Workspace shall participate in
the existing Workspace architecture.

Workspace Progress Logs shall respect:

- Workspace permissions.
- Report permissions.
- Collaboration permissions.
- Sharing permissions.
- Working Views.
- Comments.
- Existing Workspace membership.

Do not create a separate permission system specifically for Progress
Logs.

#### Report Association

A Progress Log shall be capable of being associated with a report.

Applicable report types may include:

- Audit Log.
- Executive Summary.
- Usability Report.
- Other supported ART report types.

The Progress Log association shall not change the Report Type or report
configuration.

For example:

    Project Workspace
        |
        +-- Audit Log
        +-- Usability Report
        +-- Executive Summary
        +-- Shared Progress Log

The Progress Log records project/testing activity while the reports
contain the substantive findings and reporting content.

#### Multiple Report Association

Where appropriate, a single Progress Log may be associated with multiple
reports belonging to the same project or Workspace.

For example:

    Shared Progress Log
        |
        +-- Audit Log — Website
        +-- Audit Log — Mobile App
        +-- Usability Report — Website
        +-- Executive Summary

The user shall not be required to maintain separate Progress Logs merely
because multiple reports are part of the same project.

#### Progress Log Ownership

Each Progress Log shall have an owner or controlling user according to
ART's existing ownership architecture.

The owner shall be able to manage the Progress Log according to their
permissions, including where supported:

- Sharing.
- Removing access.
- Editing Progress Log configuration.
- Managing associated reports.
- Deleting the Progress Log.
- Managing collaborators.

If a Progress Log belongs to a Workspace, Workspace administrators or
owners shall have the appropriate management capabilities according to
the existing Workspace permission model.

#### Permission Model

#### Modular Permissions

Progress Log permissions shall follow the modular permission model
established by the Collaboration Framework.

Permissions shall be independently assignable where supported.

Potential permission capabilities include:

- **Read**
- **Comment**
- **Status Update**
- **Edit**
- **Task Management**
- **Share**
- **Manage Access**
- **Delete Progress Log**

The implementation shall distinguish between permissions that allow a
user to **participate in progress tracking** and permissions that allow
a user to **manage the Progress Log itself**.

A user who can read a Progress Log shall not automatically be able to
modify it.

A user who can update task status shall not automatically be able to
reassign tasks.

A user who can contribute to tasks shall not automatically receive
administrative control over sharing or permissions.

#### Status Update Permission

Provide a dedicated **Status Update** permission.

This permission shall allow a user to:

- View the Shared Progress Log.
- View task assignments.
- Update the status of tasks assigned to them.
- Comment on tasks assigned to them.
- Use @mentions in comments according to the existing mention
  functionality.

A user with **Status Update** permission shall not automatically be able
to:

- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Edit task content.
- Delete tasks.
- Modify Progress Log configuration.
- Manage sharing.
- Manage permissions.
- Create, edit, or delete status options.

Those capabilities require additional permissions.

#### Task Management Permissions

Shared Progress Logs shall distinguish between **Status Update** and
broader **Task Management** permissions.

Users with appropriate administrator, creator, editor, or
task-management permissions may:

- Create tasks.
- Edit tasks.
- Delete tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Change task descriptions.
- Change task metadata.
- Modify task configuration.
- Update task status where their permissions allow.
- Manage status options where their permissions allow.

The exact permission names shall integrate with ART's existing
Collaboration Framework rather than creating unnecessary parallel
permission concepts.

#### Contributor Permissions

A contributor may be granted permission to:

- View the Progress Log.
- Add entries.
- Edit their own entries where permitted.
- Edit shared entries where permitted.
- Add Evaluation Items where permitted.
- Update Evaluation Item progress where permitted.
- Comment where permitted.
- Update statuses of tasks assigned to them if Status Update permission
  is granted.

The exact capabilities shall depend on the permissions granted to that
user.

#### Viewer Permissions

A viewer shall be able to view the Progress Log according to the
existing sharing model.

A viewer shall not be able to modify shared Progress Log data unless an
additional permission has explicitly been granted.

A viewer may optionally be able to create a personal Working View of the
Progress Log according to the existing Working View architecture.

A personal Working View shall not modify the shared underlying Progress
Log.

#### Sharing and Team Members

#### Sharing a Progress Log

The process of sharing a Progress Log shall require an authorized user
to provide the information necessary to identify and notify each shared
member.

At minimum, the sharing interface shall collect:

- Team member name.
- Team member email address.
- Permission level.

The email address shall be associated with the corresponding shared
member and used for Progress Log notifications, including @mention
notifications.

The sharing interface shall provide accessible validation for missing or
invalid information.

#### Managing Shared Members

Authorized Progress Log administrators, creators, editors, or users with
the appropriate **Manage Access** permission shall be able to:

- Add a shared member.
- Remove a shared member.
- Change a member's permission.
- Update a member's name.
- Update a member's email address.
- View the current shared members.
- Determine each member's permission level.

If a team member's email address changes, future notifications shall use
the updated address.

Existing comments and historical entries shall retain their original
attribution.

#### Tasks and Assignments

#### Assigned Tasks

Each Progress Log task shall expose its current assignment information.

For example:

    Task: Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow
    Assigned to: Jane Smith
    Status: In Progress

Team members shall be able to identify:

- Tasks assigned to themselves.
- Tasks assigned to other team members.
- Tasks that have not yet been assigned, where applicable.
- The current status of each task.
- Comments associated with the task.

Assignment information shall be available to screen-reader users and
shall not rely solely on visual presentation.

#### Task Assignment and Reassignment

Shared Progress Log administrators, creators, editors, and users with
appropriate **Task Management/Edit** permissions shall be able to assign
Progress Log tasks to specific shared team members.

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Assign a task.
- Reassign a task.
- Change the assignee.
- Remove an assignee where appropriate.
- View the current assignee.
- Determine which tasks are assigned to themselves.
- Determine which tasks are assigned to other team members.

A user with only **Status Update** permission shall not be able to
assign or reassign tasks.

Assignment changes shall be persisted and synchronized to all authorized
users.

#### Task Visibility

Team members shall be able to see which tasks are assigned to them and
which tasks are assigned to other team members, subject to their
Progress Log permissions.

The interface should provide an accessible way to distinguish:

- My Tasks.
- Tasks assigned to others.
- Unassigned Tasks.

This may be implemented through filtering, grouping, a Working View, or
another existing ART pattern rather than adding unnecessary permanent UI
controls.

#### Task Modification

Users with appropriate permissions shall be able to modify tasks.

Depending on permission level, this may include:

- Task name.
- Task description.
- Assignment.
- Status.
- Other configured task properties.
- Comments.

A user with only Status Update permission shall not be able to modify
task content unless another permission explicitly grants that
capability.

#### Task Status

#### Status Control

The mechanism for changing the status of a Progress Log task shall be an
accessible dropdown/select control.

The control shall:

- Have a programmatically associated accessible name.
- Expose the current status.
- Provide all available status options.
- Be keyboard accessible.
- Work with screen readers.
- Have a visible focus indicator.
- Preserve the selected value.
- Provide appropriate accessible feedback when the value changes.

Example:

    Status
    [In Progress ▼]

The status shall not be communicated solely through color.

#### Predefined Status Options

ART shall provide an initial set of predefined Progress Log task
statuses.

The initial status set should include useful general-purpose states such
as:

- Not Started.
- In Progress.
- Blocked.
- Completed.
- On Hold.
- Cancelled.

The status system shall be extensible.

Users shall not be restricted to the initial predefined options.

#### Custom Status Options

Authorized users shall be able to add additional status options.

For example:

- Ready for Review.
- Awaiting Client Response.
- Pending Retest.
- Retest Complete.
- Needs Clarification.

The ability to create, edit, or delete status options shall be
permission-controlled.

Users with only **Status Update** permission shall not automatically be
able to modify status options.

#### Status Option Management

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Add a status option.
- Rename a status option.
- Delete a status option where permitted.
- Reorder status options where supported.

Status-option management commands shall be available through:

- Menu bar menus.
- Global Context Menu.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette where applicable.

#### Status Persistence

Task status shall be stored as part of the Shared Progress Log's
persistent data.

When a permitted user changes:

    Not Started

to:

    In Progress

the new value shall persist.

The status shall remain available:

- After the Progress Log is closed.
- After the browser is closed.
- After the user signs out and returns.
- Across supported sessions.
- On other supported devices when synchronization is available.
- For all users who have permission to view the Shared Progress Log.

The status shall not exist only as temporary UI state.

#### Shared Status Synchronization

When a task status is changed by an authorized user, the updated status
shall synchronize through the Collaboration Framework.

All authorized members shall ultimately see the same status value.

The implementation shall prevent stale local values from silently
overwriting newer shared status values.

#### Status Option Persistence

When a status option itself is modified, the updated status definition
shall persist.

For example:

    Pending Retest

may be renamed to:

    Ready for Retest

The updated status option shall persist across sessions and synchronize
to all authorized members.

If a status option is deleted, ART shall safely handle existing tasks
that previously used that status.

Do not silently lose task status information.

#### Status Deletion

If an authorized user deletes a status option that is currently used by
tasks, ART shall not silently destroy the status history.

Before deletion, ART shall provide an appropriate accessible warning
and, where appropriate, require the user to:

- Reassign affected tasks to another status.
- Retain the status as an archived option.
- Confirm another safe handling method.

The implementation shall prevent orphaned tasks.

#### Status History

Where the existing Progress Log architecture supports history/audit
information, ART should preserve significant status changes.

Where status history is implemented, it should identify:

- Previous status.
- New status.
- User who made the change.
- Date/time of change.

### Part 3 — Shared Progress Logs

#### Comments and @Mentions

#### Comments on Assigned Tasks

Users with **Status Update** permission shall be able to comment on
tasks assigned to them.

Comments shall remain associated with the specific task.

For example:

    Task:
    Keyboard Testing — Checkout

    Status:
    In Progress

    Comment:
    Keyboard testing is complete through payment selection.
    The final confirmation workflow still needs testing.

The comment shall remain associated with that task even if the task is
subsequently reassigned.

#### @Mention Support

Comments on Shared Progress Log tasks shall support **@mentions**.

A team member shall be able to mention another shared member by typing
an @ symbol and selecting the appropriate person.

For example:

    @Jane Smith

The mention system shall only expose people who are shared members of
the Progress Log or otherwise authorized to participate in the relevant
conversation.

Users shall not be able to use the Progress Log's @mention mechanism to
arbitrarily expose unrelated users or email addresses.

#### Accessible @Mention Selection

The @mention mechanism shall be fully accessible.

When a user begins typing an @mention:

- Available shared members shall be presented.
- The suggestion list shall be keyboard accessible.
- Screen readers shall announce available suggestions appropriately.
- Users shall be able to navigate suggestions using the keyboard.
- Users shall be able to select a person without using a mouse.
- The selected person's identity shall be programmatically represented
  in the comment.

The implementation shall follow appropriate accessible
autocomplete/listbox patterns.

#### Mention Notifications

When a user is @mentioned in a Progress Log task comment, ART shall send
an email notification to the mentioned user.

The email shall identify:

- That the user was mentioned.
- Organization, if applicable.
- Project.
- Workspace, if applicable.
- Associated report, if applicable.
- Specific Progress Log.
- Specific task.
- Person who made the mention.
- Specific comment containing the @mention.

The notification should provide a direct way to navigate to the relevant
Progress Log/task when technically possible.

For example:

    You were mentioned in a Shared Progress Log

    Project: Website Accessibility Audit
    Workspace: Acme Accessibility Project
    Report: Main Website Audit
    Task: Keyboard Testing — Checkout

    Comment by: Alex Johnson

    "@Jane Smith — Can you verify the keyboard behavior
    on the final confirmation screen?"

#### Notification Security

Users who no longer have access to the Progress Log shall not receive
new notifications that expose private Progress Log information.

The notification system shall correctly handle:

- Multiple people mentioned in one comment.
- A person mentioning themselves.
- Removed team members.
- Invalid email addresses.
- Updated email addresses.
- Users whose permissions have changed.

ART shall avoid unnecessary duplicate notifications when the same person
is mentioned multiple times in a single comment.

#### Dashboard Notifications

#### Shared Progress Log Notifications

All relevant Shared Progress Log activity shall be displayed in the
**Notifications** section of each user's ART Dashboard.

Dashboard Notifications shall provide a second notification channel in
addition to email notifications.

Notifications shall be personalized according to:

- The user's relationship to the Progress Log.
- Their permissions.
- Their relationship to the affected task.
- Whether they are the assignee.
- Whether they are mentioned.
- Whether they are directly affected by a change.

Users shall not receive irrelevant notifications for every change
occurring within every Shared Progress Log to which they have access.

#### Task Assignment Notifications

When a task is assigned to a team member, that team member shall receive
a Dashboard Notification.

Example:

> 

**Task Assigned**\
You were assigned the task **Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow** in
the **Website Accessibility Audit** Progress Log.

The notification should identify, where applicable:

- Organization.
- Project.
- Workspace.
- Report.
- Progress Log.
- Task.
- Person who assigned the task.
- Date/time.

### Task Reassignment Notifications

When a task is reassigned from one team member to another:

- The new assignee shall receive a notification.
- The previous assignee should receive a notification informing them
  that the task was reassigned, where appropriate.
- Users who are not affected by the reassignment should not receive
  unnecessary notifications.

Example:

> 

**Task Reassigned**\
The task **Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow** was reassigned to you
by Alex Johnson.

#### Task Modification Notifications

Relevant team members shall receive Dashboard Notifications when
significant changes are made to tasks they are responsible for or
otherwise directly involved with.

Potential notification events include:

- Task assigned.
- Task reassigned.
- Task name changed.
- Task description changed.
- Task status changed.
- Task deleted.
- Task due date changed, if due dates are supported.
- Task priority changed, if priorities are supported.
- Comment added to an assigned task.
- User @mentioned in a task comment.

Notifications shall be permission-aware.

#### Status Change Notifications

When the status of a task changes, the appropriate affected team members
shall receive a Dashboard Notification.

Example:

> 

**Task Status Updated**\
**Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow** changed from **In Progress** to
**Completed**.

The notification should identify:

- Project/Workspace
- Task.
- Previous status.
- New status.
- Person who changed the status.
- Progress Log.
- Associated report/project/workspace where applicable.
- Date/time.

A user should not receive notifications for every status change in a
Progress Log if they have no relevant relationship to the task.

#### Comment Notifications

Relevant users shall receive Dashboard Notifications when a new comment
is added to a task they are assigned to or otherwise directly involved
with.

The notification should identify:

- Task.
- Comment author.
- Comment.
- Progress Log.
- Associated report/project/workspace where applicable.
- Date/time.

### @Mention Dashboard Notifications

An @mention shall generate a Dashboard Notification for the mentioned
user.

The notification shall identify:

- Person who mentioned them.
- Project.
- Workspace, where applicable.
- Report, where applicable.
- Progress Log.
- Task.
- Comment containing the mention.
- Date/time.

The @mention shall continue to generate the required email notification.

#### Notification Recipient Rules

The primary recipient of task-specific notifications should be
determined by the user's relationship to the task.

EventAppropriate recipient

Task assignedNew assignee

Task reassignedNew assignee and, where appropriate, previous assignee

Status changedAssigned user and other directly relevant collaborators

Comment addedAssigned user and users participating in the task

@mentionMentioned user

Task deletedAssigned user and directly affected collaborators

Task modifiedUsers with an appropriate relationship to the task

The implementation shall avoid generating excessive notification noise.

#### Notification Grouping

Where multiple changes occur within a short period, ART may group
related notifications where doing so improves usability.

For example:

> 

**3 updates to Keyboard Testing — Checkout Workflow**

- Task reassigned to Jane Smith.
- Status changed to In Progress.
- Alex Johnson added a comment.

Grouping must not obscure important information.

Users shall still be able to determine what changed.

#### Notification Navigation

Notifications associated with Shared Progress Logs shall be actionable
where possible.

Selecting a notification should take the user directly to the relevant:

- Project
- Workspace.
- Report.
- Progress Log.
- Task.
- Comment.

The destination shall respect the user's current permissions.

If the user no longer has access to the associated Progress Log, ART
shall not expose its content through the notification.

#### Notification Read/Unread State

Shared Progress Log notifications shall participate in the existing ART
Dashboard Notifications architecture.

Notifications shall support the existing:

- Read/unread state.
- Notification history.
- Dismissal behavior.
- Navigation behavior.

If ART supports notification counts/badges, Shared Progress Log
notifications shall contribute appropriately.

Users shall be able to distinguish unread notifications from previously
viewed notifications without relying solely on color.

#### Email and Dashboard Notification Relationship

Dashboard Notifications and email notifications shall work together
without unnecessarily duplicating information.

For example:

- An **@mention** shall generate the required Dashboard notification and
  may generate an email notification according to the user's
  notification preferences.
- A **task assignment** shall generate a Dashboard Notification and may
  generate an email notification according to the user's notification
  preferences.
- A **status change** shall generate a Dashboard Notification according
  to the notification rules.

ART should eventually provide notification preferences allowing users to
control which eligible events generate email notifications, while
Dashboard Notifications remain available according to the application's
notification architecture.

#### Notification Persistence and Synchronization

Dashboard Notifications generated by Shared Progress Log activity shall
persist appropriately and synchronize across supported sessions/devices.

If a user views a notification on one supported device, its read/unread
state should synchronize where the existing notification architecture
supports synchronization.

#### Collaboration and Synchronization

#### Simultaneous Editing

Shared Progress Logs shall support simultaneous editing when ART's
Collaboration Framework supports synchronous collaboration.

If two or more authorized users are editing the same Progress Log at the
same time:

- Changes shall be synchronized.
- Users shall not unknowingly overwrite each other's changes.
- The application shall provide appropriate conflict handling.
- Shared state shall remain consistent.

Do not implement simplistic last-write-wins behavior if doing so could
silently destroy another user's changes.

Use the synchronization architecture established by the Collaboration
Framework.

#### Asynchronous Collaboration

Shared Progress Logs shall support asynchronous collaboration.

A user may:

1.  Open a shared Progress Log.
2.  Add or modify entries.
3.  Change permitted task statuses.
4.  Add permitted comments.
5.  Save changes.
6.  Leave the Progress Log.
7.  Another authorized user later opens it.
8.  The second user sees the updated shared state.

Users do not need to be online simultaneously to contribute.

#### Synchronization Status

When a Shared Progress Log is being synchronized, the interface shall
provide an accessible indication of the current state where appropriate.

Potential states include:

- Saved.
- Saving.
- Synchronizing.
- Offline.
- Changes Pending.
- Conflict Requiring Attention.

Status information shall be available to screen-reader users as well as
sighted users.

Do not rely solely on color, animation, or visual indicators.

#### Offline Behavior

Shared Progress Logs shall respect ART's local-first architecture.

If offline editing is supported:

- Users should be able to make permitted changes while offline.
- Changes should be retained locally.
- Changes should synchronize when connectivity is restored.
- Conflicts should be handled through the Collaboration Framework.
- Users should be informed if synchronization cannot be completed.

Offline behavior must not silently discard Progress Log changes.

#### Evaluation Items

#### Existing Evaluation Items

Shared Progress Logs shall support the existing **Evaluation Item**
functionality.

Authorized users shall be able to:

- Add Evaluation Items.
- Edit Evaluation Items.
- Remove Evaluation Items.
- Update Evaluation Item information.
- Track progress.
- View Evaluation Items created by other collaborators.

All actions shall be subject to permissions.

#### Evaluation Item Collaboration

When multiple users have permission to edit Evaluation Items, changes
shall be reflected in the shared Progress Log.

Another authorized collaborator shall see the updated state rather than
maintaining a separate conflicting copy.

#### Evaluation Item Keyboard Behavior

Preserve the existing accessible keyboard behavior for Evaluation Items.

In particular:

- The **Add Evaluation Item** button follows the final Evaluation Item.
- A newly added Evaluation Item appears immediately above the Add
  Evaluation Item button.
- Focus moves to the new Evaluation Item Name field.
- The new Evaluation Item participates in normal tab order.
- The Add Evaluation Item button precedes Done.
- Keyboard navigation remains sequential and predictable.

Shared functionality must not regress this behavior.

#### Working Views

#### Personal Working Views

Shared Progress Logs shall support ART's existing Working View
architecture.

Working Views shall remain primarily individual to each user.

A user may create a personal Working View of a Shared Progress Log
according to their permissions.

For example:

    My Evaluation Items
    In Progress
    High Priority

without changing what other collaborators see.

A user with read-only access may create a read-only Working View where
the existing Working View architecture permits it.

#### Shared Working Views

A user with appropriate permissions may create a **shared Working View**
for collaborators.

Shared Working Views may be useful for:

- Team leads.
- Workspace administrators.
- Project owners.
- Audit leads.

Shared Working Views shall be optional.

Individual users shall not be forced to use a shared Working View.

Personal Working Views shall remain independent from shared Working
Views.

### Part 4 — Shared Progress Logs

#### Commands and UI Integration

#### Command Architecture

Shared Progress Log commands shall use ART's existing command
architecture.

Do not add a large collection of permanent buttons to the primary UI.

Applicable commands shall be available through:

- Menu bar.
- Menus.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Global Context Menu.\
  Existing keyboard shortcuts where applicable.

If Collaboration is enabled, appropriate Progress Log collaboration
commands may also appear under the existing **Collaboration** menu.

#### Task Commands

Commands shall include, where applicable:

- Add Task.
- Edit Task.
- Delete Task.
- Assign Task.
- Reassign Task.
- Change Status.
- Add Comment.
- Edit Comment.
- Delete Comment.
- Mention Team Member.

Commands shall only be available or enabled when the user has the
required permission.

#### Status Commands

Commands shall include:

- Add Status.
- Edit Status.
- Delete Status.
- Reorder Status Options where supported.

These commands shall be available through:

- Menu bar menus.
- Global Context Menu.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette where applicable.

#### Context-Sensitive Commands

The Global Context Menu shall expose relevant actions based on the
user's current location and selection.

For example, when a user is focused on a task assigned to themselves, a
user with Status Update permission may see:

- Change Status.
- Add Comment.
- Mention Team Member.

An administrator/editor may see:

- Edit Task.
- Assign Task.
- Reassign Task.
- Change Status.
- Add Comment.
- Delete Task.

Unauthorized commands shall not be presented as available actions.

#### Permission Enforcement

Permissions must be enforced at the underlying application/data level as
well as through the UI.

Do not merely hide an unauthorized command while leaving it executable
through:

- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Command Search.
- Command Palette.
- Global Context Menu.
- Direct interaction.
- API calls or other programmatic mechanisms.

#### Accessibility

#### Keyboard Accessibility

All Shared Progress Log functionality shall be available without
requiring a mouse.

Users shall be able to:

- Create tasks.
- Edit tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Open the status dropdown.
- Select a status.
- Add a status option where permitted.
- Edit a status option where permitted.
- Delete a status option where permitted.
- Add comments.
- @mention team members.
- Navigate mention suggestions.
- Save changes.
- Navigate Dashboard Notifications.
- Open notifications and navigate to their associated tasks.

Existing keyboard navigation and shortcuts shall remain functional.

#### Screen Reader Accessibility

Shared Progress Logs shall be fully compatible with supported screen
readers.

Screen-reader users shall be able to determine:

- Progress Log name.
- Sharing state.
- User permissions.
- Task name.
- Task assignment.
- Task status.
- Available status options.
- Comments.
- Comment author.
- @mentions\.
- Synchronization status.
- Validation messages.
- Dashboard Notifications.
- Notification read/unread state.
- Notification type.
- Notification destination.

Dynamic collaboration updates shall not unexpectedly steal keyboard
focus.

Live updates should use appropriate announcements without creating
excessive or repetitive speech.

Users shall be able to continue editing without unexpected focus
movement.

#### Accessible Task Assignment

Task assignment controls shall:

- Have accessible labels.
- Identify the current assignee.
- Provide accessible selection of shared members.
- Be keyboard accessible.
- Work with screen readers.
- Clearly distinguish available members.
- Not expose unauthorized people.

When a task is reassigned, the change shall be communicated
appropriately to the user making the change and, where applicable, to
the new assignee.

#### Accessible Status Management

Status-management controls shall:

- Use semantic controls.
- Have accessible names.
- Expose current values.
- Expose available options.
- Work with keyboard navigation.
- Work with screen readers.
- Provide accessible validation.
- Preserve visible focus.
- Provide appropriate feedback after changes.

Status shall never depend solely on color, icons, or visual styling.

#### Accessible Comments

The comment interface shall:

- Have an accessible label.
- Be keyboard accessible.
- Support multiline comments where appropriate.
- Preserve comment structure.
- Identify comment authors.
- Expose timestamps where provided.
- Support accessible @mention selection.
- Announce validation or submission results.

#### Accessible Dashboard Notifications

The Notifications section shall:

- Use appropriate semantic structure.
- Provide a logical keyboard navigation order.
- Expose notification state programmatically.
- Provide meaningful accessible names.
- Identify the affected task and Progress Log.
- Expose notification actions.
- Preserve visible focus.
- Avoid unexpected focus movement when notifications are dynamically
  added.

Unread state shall not be conveyed by color alone.

### Persistence

Shared Progress Log data shall persist locally when ART is operating
without a collaboration server.

When server-based collaboration is enabled, changes shall additionally
be synchronized through the configured collaboration service.

#### Data Model and Persistence

#### Shared Progress Log Data Model

Extend ART's existing Progress Log data model rather than creating a
completely separate Progress Log architecture.

The data model shall support:

- Progress Log ID.
- Owner/creator.
- Sharing state.
- Shared members.
- Member names.
- Member email addresses.
- Member permissions.
- Entries.
- Tasks/Evaluation Items.
- Task assignment.
- Task status.
- Status-option definitions.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- Associated reports.
- Associated Project Workspace.
- Project information where applicable.
- Organization information where applicable.
- Product information where applicable.
- Created/modified metadata.
- Synchronization information where required.

The exact implementation shall conform to ART's existing architecture.

Note that Shared Progress Logs are optional, the default is for Progress
Logs to be Personal (Not shared by default). Therefore ART's existing
infrastructure for individual Progress Logs shall not be removed or
superceded by Shared Progress Logs.

#### Persistent Task Assignment

Task assignments shall be stored as persistent data.

The assignment shall remain available:

- Across sessions.
- After reopening ART.
- After reopening the Progress Log.
- On supported synchronized devices.
- To all authorized users.

Changing an assignee shall update the shared source of truth.

#### Persistent Task Status

Task status shall be stored as persistent shared data.

A status change shall not be lost when:

- The Progress Log closes.
- The browser closes.
- The user navigates away.
- The user signs out.
- Another collaborator opens the Progress Log.
- Another authorized device synchronizes.

### Persistent Status Definitions
