Status options shall be stored as persistent configuration.

Each status should have a stable internal identity rather than relying
solely on its visible text.

For example:

    Internal status:
    status-123

    Visible label:
    Pending Retest

may later become:

    Internal status:
    status-123

    Visible label:
    Ready for Retest

Existing tasks using that status should continue to reference the same
underlying status.

#### Comments and Mentions Data

Comments shall preserve:

- Comment ID.
- Task association.
- Author.
- Comment content.
- Creation date/time.
- Modification information where supported.
- Mentioned members.

Mentions should reference the shared member's stable identity rather
than relying solely on their display name.

#### Notification Data

Dashboard Notifications shall maintain sufficient information to
identify:

- Notification type.
- Source Progress Log.
- Source task.
- Source report/project/workspace.
- Source user.
- Date/time.
- Read/unread state.
- Navigation destination where applicable.

Notification data shall not bypass the user's current permissions.

#### Reports, Projects, Products, and Organizations

#### Associated Reports

A Shared Progress Log shall maintain relationships to associated reports
without duplicating report data.

For example:

    Shared Progress Log
            |
            +-- Audit Log
            +-- Usability Report
            +-- Executive Summary

Deleting or modifying a Progress Log association shall not delete the
associated report.

Deleting a report shall not silently delete the entire Progress Log
unless the user explicitly confirms an appropriate destructive action
and the relationship requires it.

#### Progress Log and Organization Integration

Shared Progress Logs shall integrate with ART's Organization
architecture where applicable.

Where an associated report or Workspace contains Organization/Client
information, the Progress Log may be associated with that organization.

Organization-level statistics may use applicable Progress Log data where
Epic 42 supports it.

ART shall not infer an organization solely from a Progress Log title or
user name.

#### Product Integration

Where Product information is available through the associated report,
Workspace, or project architecture, Progress Log data may be associated
with that Product.

Product-level statistics may include:

- Progress Logs.
- Tasks.
- Completed tasks.
- Task status.
- Testing activity.
- Evaluation Items.

Statistics shall only be generated from data that actually exists.

#### Tester and Contributor Activity

Where user attribution is available, ART may use Progress Log data to
provide descriptive organization/project statistics.

Potential metrics include:

- Number of contributors.
- Number of assigned tasks.
- Number of completed tasks.
- Number of active contributors.
- Progress over time.

These metrics shall be descriptive and shall not be presented as
employee performance scores.

#### Organization Statistics

Shared Progress Log information may contribute to Organization
Statistics when:

- Organization Statistics are enabled.
- The Progress Log has sufficient organization metadata.
- The user has appropriate access.
- The relevant data is available.

Potential statistics include:

- Total Progress Logs.
- Tasks by status.
- Tasks completed over time.
- Tasks by Product.
- Tasks by Project.
- Tasks by Workspace.
- Tasks by tester/contributor.
- Evaluation Items by status.
- Progress trends.

Organization Statistics shall respect all applicable permissions.

A user shall not gain access to organization-level information simply
because they have access to an individual Progress Log.

#### No Automatic Analytics in Progress Logs

Progress Logs shall not automatically gain an Analytics section merely
because their data contributes to Organization Statistics.

The distinction shall remain:

**Progress Log:**

- Project/testing progress.
- Tasks.
- Assignments.
- Statuses.
- Comments.
- Collaboration.

**Organization Statistics:**

- Aggregated organizational/project data.

### Part 5 — Shared Progress Logs

#### Security and Privacy

#### Progress Log Access Without Report Access

Where permissions are modular, access to a Progress Log shall not
automatically grant access to every associated report.

For example:

    Progress Log: Edit
    Audit Log: Read

or:

    Progress Log: Status Update
    Audit Log: No Access

The Progress Log permission model shall respect the existing modular
Collaboration Framework.

ART shall not unintentionally expose report content because a user has
access to a Progress Log.

#### Report Access Without Progress Log Access

Having access to an associated report shall not automatically grant
access to a private Progress Log unless the sharing configuration
explicitly permits it.

This distinction is important when Progress Logs contain internal
project notes or collaboration information.

#### Sharing Privacy

Sharing a Progress Log shall expose only the information necessary for
the recipient's permission level.

ART shall protect:

- Member email addresses.
- Private comments.
- Private Progress Logs.
- Report content.
- Organization information.
- Other collaboration data.

Email addresses should not be displayed to all shared members unless the
existing product design explicitly requires this.

The mention-selection interface may display names while internally
associating the selected member with their email address.

#### Templates and Import/Export

#### Templates

Where ART supports Progress Log templates, templates shall preserve
appropriate Progress Log configuration.

Templates may include:

- Task structure.
- Evaluation Items.
- Status configuration.
- Initial status options.
- Layout.
- Other supported configuration.

Templates shall not contain private user-specific sharing information
unless the existing architecture explicitly supports reusable member
configurations.

Sharing and email addresses should normally be established when the
actual Progress Log is shared.

#### Import and Export

Where Progress Log import/export is supported, the implementation shall
preserve applicable:

- Tasks.
- Evaluation Items.
- Assignments where appropriate.
- Statuses.
- Status definitions.
- Comments where supported.
- Metadata.
- Associated report references where supported.

Private collaboration information should not be unintentionally exported
where the export format or permissions do not permit it.

#### Exported Progress Logs

A Shared Progress Log export should clearly identify task information,
including where applicable:

- Task.
- Assignee.
- Status.
- Comments.
- Dates.
- Related report.
- Other configured information.

The exported data should not misrepresent a user's permissions or
status.

#### Data Integrity

##### Concurrent Changes

Shared Progress Logs shall maintain data integrity when multiple users:

- Add tasks.
- Edit tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Change status.
- Add comments.
- Mention users.
- Add or modify status options.

The implementation shall avoid:

- Duplicate tasks caused by synchronization.
- Lost status changes.
- Orphaned assignments.
- Orphaned statuses.
- Comments attached to incorrect tasks.
- Mentions attached to the wrong users.

##### Assignment History

Where supported by the existing architecture, task assignment changes
should preserve historical information such as:

- Previous assignee.
- New assignee.
- User who made the reassignment.
- Date/time.

This allows collaborators to understand how responsibility changed over
time.

#### Testing and Validation

##### Sharing Testing

Verify that an authorized user can share a Progress Log by providing:

- Name.
- Email address.
- Permission level.

Verify that:

- Required fields are validated.
- Invalid email addresses are handled accessibly.
- The shared member receives the appropriate access.
- The shared member appears in the member list.
- Their permission is correctly displayed.
- Their email is securely stored.
- Their information can be updated by authorized administrators.

#### Permission Testing

Test every Progress Log permission level.

Verify that a user with **Read** can view but cannot modify shared data.

Verify that a user with **Status Update** can:

- View the Progress Log.
- View assignments.
- Change the status of their assigned tasks.
- Comment on their assigned tasks.

Verify that a Status Update user cannot:

- Change statuses of tasks assigned to other users.
- Assign a task.
- Reassign a task.
- Modify task content unless separately permitted.
- Delete a task.
- Manage status options.
- Manage sharing.

Verify that administrators/creators/editors with appropriate permissions
can:

- Create tasks.
- Edit tasks.
- Delete tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Manage status options.
- Manage access.

Permission enforcement must work through every supported interaction
mechanism.

#### Task Assignment Testing

Create multiple shared members.

Create multiple tasks.

Assign different tasks to different members.

Verify that:

- Each task displays the correct assignee.
- Each member can identify their own assigned tasks.
- Members can see tasks assigned to other members.
- Authorized users can reassign tasks.
- Unauthorized users cannot reassign tasks.
- Assignment changes persist.
- Assignment changes synchronize.
- Assignment notifications appear in the appropriate Dashboard
  Notifications section.
- Appropriate affected users receive notifications.

#### Status Testing

Verify that the initial predefined statuses are available.

Verify that users with Status Update permission can change the status of
their assigned tasks.

Verify that they cannot change statuses of tasks assigned to others.

Verify that authorized administrators/editors can change statuses where
permitted.

Verify that status changes:

- Persist.
- Synchronize.
- Remain after reopening the application.
- Remain after signing out and back in.
- Are visible to all authorized members.
- Generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.

### Custom Status Testing

Verify that an authorized user can:

- Add a status.
- Rename a status.
- Delete a status where safe.
- Reorder a status where supported.

Verify that unauthorized users cannot perform those actions.

Verify that custom statuses persist across sessions.

Verify that all authorized members receive the updated status
configuration.

#### Status Deletion Testing

Attempt to delete a status currently used by tasks.

Verify that ART:

- Identifies affected tasks.
- Warns the user.
- Prevents accidental loss of status information.
- Provides an appropriate remediation mechanism.

Verify that no task becomes orphaned.

#### Simultaneous Editing Testing

Have two authorized users open the same Progress Log.

Test:

- Editing different tasks.
- Editing the same task.
- Changing status.
- Assigning tasks.
- Reassigning tasks.
- Adding comments.
- Adding status options.

Verify that changes synchronize correctly.

Verify that conflicting changes are handled safely.

Verify that one user's changes do not silently disappear.

Verify that appropriate Dashboard Notifications are generated.

#### Asynchronous Testing

User A makes changes and leaves.

User B later opens the Progress Log.

Verify that User B sees:

- New tasks.
- Updated assignments.
- Updated statuses.
- New comments.
- Updated status options.

#### @Mention Testing

Test mentioning one team member.

Verify that:

-The member appears in the suggestion list.

- The member can be selected using the keyboard.
- Screen readers can identify the suggestions.
- The mention is correctly inserted.
- The correct member receives an email.
- The correct member receives a Dashboard Notification.
- The email identifies the project/workspace/report.
- The email identifies the Progress Log.
- The email identifies the task.
- The email contains the relevant comment.
- The Dashboard Notification identifies the relevant task and comment.
- The notification does not expose unrelated private information.

Test multiple mentions in one comment.

Verify that each appropriate recipient receives the correct
notification.

#### Removed-Member Testing

Share a Progress Log with a user.

Mention that user.

Remove the user's access.

Attempt to mention the removed user again.

Verify that the removed user is no longer available as an authorized
mention target.

Verify that the removed user does not receive new private Progress Log
notifications through email or the Dashboard.

Historical comments shall retain appropriate historical attribution.

#### Email Change Testing

Change a shared member's email address.

Create a new @mention.

Verify that the notification is sent to the updated email address.

Verify that historical comments remain associated with the correct user
identity.

#### Dashboard Notification Testing

Verify that the following generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications:

- Task assignment.
- Task reassignment.
- Task status change.
- Relevant task modification.
- Relevant task deletion.
- Comment added to an assigned/relevant task.
- @mention\.

Verify that:

- Notifications appear in the correct user's Dashboard.
- Unrelated users do not receive unnecessary notifications.
- Notifications contain the appropriate contextual information.
- Notifications link to the relevant task where possible.
- Read/unread state works.
- Dismissal works where supported.
- Notification state persists.
- Notification state synchronizes where supported.
- Removed users do not receive private notifications.
- Notifications are accessible to keyboard and screen-reader users.

#### Working View Testing

Create personal Working Views.

Verify that personal views:

- Remain specific to the user.
- Do not alter other users' views.
- Respect the user's permissions.
- Do not modify shared task data merely by filtering or sorting.

Create a shared Working View with appropriate permissions.

Verify that authorized users can access it.

Verify that users can still create personal Working Views independently.

#### Accessibility Testing

Perform keyboard-only testing of the complete feature.

Verify:

-Logical focus order.

- Visible focus.
- No keyboard traps.
- Accessible menus.
- Accessible context menus.
- Accessible task assignment.
- Accessible status dropdown.
- Accessible comments.
- Accessible @mention autocomplete.
- Accessible validation.
- Accessible notification/status messages.
- Accessible Dashboard Notifications.
- Dynamic notification updates do not unexpectedly steal focus.

Perform screen-reader testing.

Verify that users can determine:

- Progress Log name.
- Sharing state.
- Permission level.
- Task name.
- Assignee.
- Status.
- Comments.
- Comment author.
- @mentions\.
- Synchronization state.
- Dashboard Notification type.
- Dashboard Notification content.
- Dashboard Notification read/unread state.
- Dashboard Notification destination.

Dynamic synchronization must not unexpectedly move focus.

### Part 6 — Shared Progress Logs

#### Implementation Requirements

##### Preserve Existing Progress Log Functionality

Implement Shared Progress Logs by extending the existing Progress Log
functionality.

Do not unnecessarily replace or rewrite the existing Progress Log
system.

The implementation shall preserve existing functionality, including:

- Progress Log creation.
- Progress Log editing.
- Evaluation Items.
- Add Evaluation Item behavior.
- Existing keyboard navigation.
- Existing focus management.
- Existing Progress Log persistence.
- Existing Workspace integration.
- Existing Report integration.
- Existing menu and command functionality.

Where Shared Progress Logs introduce new capabilities, those
capabilities shall extend the existing architecture.

Do not create a separate, disconnected Progress Log system for shared
and non-shared Progress Logs.

##### Preserve Existing Keyboard Behavior

The Shared Progress Log implementation shall preserve existing keyboard
interactions.

In particular, when the Progress Log feature supports Evaluation Items:

- The existing **Add Evaluation Item** button shall continue to be used.
- Do not create a duplicate Add Evaluation Item button.
- The button shall remain immediately after the final Evaluation Item.
- The button shall remain immediately before the **Done** button.
- A newly created Evaluation Item shall be appended immediately above
  the Add Evaluation Item button.
- A newly created Evaluation Item shall appear on the next available
  row.
- Focus shall immediately move to the **Evaluation Item Name** field of
  the newly created item.
- The new item shall participate in the normal keyboard tab order.
- After the final **Remove Evaluation Item** button, focus shall move to
  **Add Evaluation Item**.
- After **Add Evaluation Item**, focus shall move to **Done**.

Shared collaboration functionality shall not alter this sequence.

##### Extend Existing Collaboration Infrastructure

Shared Progress Logs shall integrate with the Collaboration Framework
rather than implementing a separate sharing system.

Reuse the existing architecture for:

- User identity.
- Permissions.
- Sharing.
- Membership.
- Synchronization.
- Conflict resolution.
- Notifications.
- Working Views.
- Activity/history where supported.

Progress Log-specific logic should extend these shared systems.

##### Email Notification Infrastructure

Use ART's notification architecture for Shared Progress Log email
notifications.

Do not implement an unrelated, hard-coded email mechanism specifically
for @mentions.

The email system shall support:

- Recipient identification.
- Notification context.
- Multiple recipients where appropriate.
- Permission checks.
- Updated email addresses.
- Duplicate prevention.
- Notification preferences where supported.

The @mention system shall integrate with this infrastructure.

#### Recommended Architecture

##### Shared Progress Log Service

Implement Shared Progress Log functionality through a centralized
service or equivalent domain layer.

The service should manage:

- Shared members.
- Permission validation.
- Task assignment.
- Task reassignment.
- Task status changes.
- Status configuration.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- Notification generation.
- Synchronization requests.

UI components shall invoke the underlying service or command layer.

Do not duplicate business logic across:

- Menu commands.
- Context-menu commands.
- Buttons.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Dashboard actions.

All interaction methods shall invoke the same underlying operation.

##### Permission Validation

Every state-changing operation shall validate permissions before
modifying shared data.

For example:

``` text

changeTaskStatus()
    |
    +-- Validate Progress Log access
    |
    +-- Validate Status Update or equivalent permission
    |
    +-- Validate task assignment
    |
    +-- Update shared task status
    |
    +-- Persist
    |
    +-- Synchronize
    |
    +-- Generate relevant notifications
```

## Epic 45 — Assigned Tasks, Shared To-Do Lists, Personal To-Do Lists, and Task Reminders

### Overview

Extend ART with a unified, accessible task-management system for
organizing assigned work, shared tasks, and personal To-Do items.

This epic shall build on the existing:

-Shared Progress Logs.

- Collaboration Framework.
- Projects.
- Workspaces.
- Reports.
- Organization architecture.
- Dashboard.
- Notifications.
- History Framework.
- Permission system.
- Global Context Menu.
- Menu bar.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.
- Local-first storage architecture.

The goal is to provide users with one coherent task system that answers:

> 

**What work needs to be done, who is responsible for it, what is its
current status, what needs attention, and what have I completed?**

Do **not** create separate first-class Checklist and To-Do systems.
Tasks shall be the fundamental unit of work. Personal and shared To-Do
Lists shall provide different ways of organizing and viewing tasks.

### Local-First Task Management

The Tasks and To-Do functionality shall operate without requiring an ART
server.

Personal To-Do Lists, task status, priority, due dates, reminders,
comments/notes/instructions, completion state, and task history shall be
capable of being stored locally.

Tasks associated with projects, workspaces, reports, or Shared Progress
Logs shall be included in project/workspace export and import
operations.

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Do not modify unrelated ART functionality.

Preserve all existing:

- Accessibility behavior.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Menu commands.
- Global Context Menu functionality.
- History Framework behavior.
- Dashboard functionality.
- Notification functionality.
- Permission controls.
- Collaboration functionality.
- Local-first storage.
- Import/export functionality.

All new functionality shall be fully accessible using:

- Keyboard-only interaction.
- Screen readers.
- Browser zoom.
- Magnification.
- Other assistive technologies supported by ART.

### Unified Task Model

Tasks shall be the fundamental unit of work.

A task may be:

- Assigned to a specific team member.
- Part of a Shared To-Do List.
- Added to one or more users' Personal To-Do Lists.
- Created as a personal task.
- Associated with a project.
- Associated with a workspace.
- Associated with a product.
- Associated with a report.
- Associated with an organization.
- Associated with a Progress Log.

A task shall use stable internal identifiers.

Do not create duplicate task records merely because a task is displayed
in multiple locations.

### Task Types and Relationships

ART shall support at least the following task contexts.

#### Assigned Tasks

Assigned Tasks are tasks assigned by an authorized user to a specific
team member.

Examples include:

- Test keyboard navigation.
- Test a workflow with JAWS.
- Perform regression testing.
- Retest a finding.
- Review a report.
- Test a specific WCAG Success Criterion.
- Complete testing for a product or component.

#### Shared To-Do Tasks

Shared To-Do Lists contain tasks that authorized team members can view
and interact with according to their permissions.

A shared task may be assigned to a particular team member or remain
unassigned.

#### Personal To-Do Tasks

Personal To-Do Lists contain tasks that the current user wants to track
as part of their own work.

A Personal To-Do List may contain:

- User-created personal tasks.
- Assigned Tasks added by the user.
- Shared tasks added by the user.

Adding a task to a Personal To-Do List shall not create a duplicate
underlying task.

### Tasks Modal

ART shall provide an accessible multi-tab **Tasks & To-Do** modal
dialog.

The modal shall use a proper accessible:

- `tablist`.
- `tab`.
- `tabpanel`.

The tabs shall include:

1.  **Assigned Tasks**
2.  **Shared To-Do Lists/Tasks**, when available.
3.  **Personal To-Do List**
4.  **Completed Tasks**

The Shared To-Do Lists/Tasks tab shall only be presented when shared
To-Do Lists or shared tasks are available to the user.

### Assigned Tasks Tab

The Assigned Tasks tab shall display tasks assigned to the current user.

Users shall be able to:

- View assigned tasks.
- View task status.
- View priority.
- View due date/time.
- View assignment information.
- Add a task to their Personal To-Do List.
- Add comments, notes, or instructions.
- Change permitted status values.
- Set personal reminders.
- Navigate to associated project/workspace/report information.

Users shall only be able to modify tasks according to their permissions.

### Shared To-Do Lists/Tasks Tab

When available, this tab shall display Shared To-Do Lists and their
associated tasks.

Users shall be able to:

- View shared lists.
- View tasks.
- Identify assignees.
- View task status.
- View task priority.
- View due dates.
- Add eligible tasks to their Personal To-Do List.
- Add comments where permitted.
- Set personal reminders where permitted.
- Navigate to associated ART content.

Authorized users shall also be able to manage shared tasks according to
their permissions.

### Personal To-Do List Tab

The Personal To-Do List shall provide the user's consolidated work
queue.

It shall include:

- Personal tasks created by the user.
- Assigned tasks added by the user.
- Shared tasks added by the user.

The Personal To-Do List shall provide:

- Checkbox for quick completion.
- Status dropdown.
- Optional Comments, Notes, or Instructions text area.

Other actions shall be available through the command architecture rather
than through persistent buttons on each task.

### Completed Tasks Tab

Completed tasks shall automatically be removed from the active Personal
To-Do List and moved to the **Completed Tasks** tab.

This behavior shall keep the active To-Do List uncluttered.

The Completed Tasks tab shall contain completed Personal To-Do items and
applicable completed tasks associated with the user.

Completed tasks shall retain their relevant:

- Task information.
- Status.
- Priority.
- Comments, Notes, or Instructions.
- Due date/time.
- Completion information.
- Relevant relationships.
- Assigner/Originating list.

### Restoring Completed Tasks

Users shall be able to change the completion status of a completed task.

For example, a user may change:

> 

**Complete → In Progress**

or:

> 

**Complete → Not Started**

When a completed task is changed to an incomplete status:

1.  The task shall automatically be removed from the Completed Tasks
    tab.
2.  The task shall automatically return to the active Personal To-Do
    List.
3.  The task shall appear according to the currently selected/default
    sorting rules.
4.  Its existing task information shall be preserved.

The same underlying task shall be restored rather than creating a new
task.

### Task Checkbox

Each applicable task shall provide a traditional checkbox for users who
prefer a simple completed/not-completed interaction.

Checking the checkbox shall set the task's status to **Complete**.

When the checkbox is checked:

- The task shall move to Completed Tasks.
- The task shall no longer appear in the active Personal To-Do List.

Unchecking a completed task shall return it to an appropriate incomplete
status, such as **Not Started**, and move it back to the active Personal
To-Do List.

### Task Status Dropdown

Each task shall also provide an accessible Status dropdown.

The Status dropdown shall allow users to use detailed task states
instead of relying solely on a checkbox.

Default status options shall include:

- Not Started.
- In Progress.
- Blocked.
- Deferred.
- Not Applicable.
- Needs Review.
- Need Assistance.
- Complete.

The status system shall support configurable status options where
permitted.

### Status and Checkbox Synchronization

The checkbox and Status dropdown shall remain synchronized.

Examples:

User ActionResult

Check checkboxStatus becomes Complete

Select CompleteCheckbox becomes checked

Uncheck checkboxTask becomes incomplete and returns to To-Do

Select In ProgressCheckbox becomes unchecked

Select BlockedCheckbox becomes unchecked

Select DeferredCheckbox becomes unchecked and Deferred date/time is
requested

Select Not ApplicableCheckbox becomes unchecked unless configured
otherwise

Select Needs ReviewCheckbox becomes unchecked

Select Need AssistanceCheckbox becomes unchecked

Custom status options shall have an appropriate complete/incomplete
state.

### Deferred Status

When **Deferred** is selected, ART shall provide accessible date/time
controls.

The user shall specify when the task should become active again.

For example:

> 

Status: Deferred\
Resume: September 5, 2026 at 9:00 AM

ART shall retain the deferred date/time.

When the deferred time arrives:

- The task shall become eligible for a reminder/notification.
- The deferred state shall be clearly communicated.
- The task shall remain available to the user.
- Existing task history shall be preserved.

### Need Assistance Status

The **Need Assistance** status shall support collaborative workflows.

The user may:

1.  Select Need Assistance.
2.  Enter an explanation in the Comments, Notes, or Instructions text
    area.
3.  @mention one or more authorized team members.

The appropriate notification shall be generated.

The underlying task shall remain assigned to the original user unless an
authorized user explicitly reassigns it.

### Needs Review Status

The **Needs Review** status shall allow users to indicate that work
requires review without automatically changing the task assignment.

Where appropriate, authorized reviewers shall receive notifications.

Reviewers may add comments or change the task status according to their
permissions.

### Task Priority

Priority shall be a first-class task property.

Default priority options shall include:

- Critical.
- High.
- Normal.
- Low.

Priority shall be:

- Keyboard accessible.
- Screen-reader accessible.
- Programmatically determinable.
- Exposed through appropriate accessibility APIs.
- Available to assistive technologies without relying on color or visual
  position.

Priority shall never be communicated through color alone.

### Default Task Ordering

The active Personal To-Do List shall display tasks in **decreasing
priority order by default**.

The highest-priority tasks shall always appear first.

For example:

    Critical
    Critical
    High
    High
    Normal
    Normal
    Low
    Low

Within the same priority level, ART shall use a consistent secondary
ordering, such as due date/time or date added.

The default ordering shall remain predictable.

### Task Sorting

Users shall be able to change task ordering through commands.

Sorting commands shall be available through:

- Global Context Menu.
- Menu bar when the Tasks modal is open.
- Command Search/Command Palette where supported.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts where appropriate.

Sorting options shall include:

- Priority — highest first.\
  -Due Date/Time — earliest first.
- Date Added — oldest first.
- Date Added — newest first.

Sorting shall not modify the underlying task data.

The current sorting method and direction shall be programmatically
determinable.

The user's selected sorting preference should persist where appropriate.

### Task Information

A task may contain:

- Task name.
- Description.
- Assignee.
- Creator/Assigner.
- Organization.
- Project.
- Workspace.
- Product.
- Report.
- Status.
- Priority.
- Due date/time.
- Deferred date/time.
- Completion date/time.
- Comments, Notes, or Instructions.
- Personal reminder information.
- Shared relationships.
- Creation and modification timestamps.

### Comments, Notes, or Instructions

Each task shall provide **one optional text area** labeled:

> 

**Comments**

- Notes.
- Instructions.
- Progress notes.
- Assistance requests.
- Review notes.
- Completion notes.

All such information shall be entered through this single optional text
area.

The text area shall:

- Be optional.
- Have an accessible label.
- Support keyboard input.
- Support screen readers.
- Support dictation.
- Preserve entered content.
- Support @mentions.

### @Mentions

Users shall be able to @mention authorized team members directly within
the Comments text area.

The existing ART @mention mechanism shall be reused where possible.

When the user enters `@`, ART shall provide an accessible list of
eligible team members.

The @mention functionality shall:

- Support keyboard navigation.
- Support screen readers.
- Support dictation.
- Provide accessible autocomplete.
- Prevent unauthorized users from being mentioned.
- Preserve stable user identifiers.
- Generate appropriate Dashboard Notifications.
- Generate email notifications where applicable.

The notification shall identify the relevant:

- Organization.
- Project.
- Workspace.
- Product.
- Report.
- Task.
- Comment.
- Progress log entry (where appropriate).

### Personal and Shared Task Information

ART shall distinguish between:

- Shared task information.
- Personal To-Do information.

A user's personal action must not unintentionally modify shared task
data.

For example:

Removing a shared task from the Personal To-Do List shall **not delete
the shared task**.

Likewise, a personal reminder shall not modify another user's reminder.

### Personal Task References

When an Assigned Task or Shared Task is added to a Personal To-Do List,
ART shall create a personal relationship/reference rather than
duplicating the underlying task.

For example:

    Shared Task
        |
        +-- Assigned to: User A
        |
        +-- Personal To-Do: User A
        |
        +-- Personal To-Do: User B

The underlying shared task shall remain a single task.

### Personal To-Do State

ART shall distinguish between:

- **Task Status** — the status of the underlying task.
- **Personal To-Do State** — whether the task is included in the current
  user's Personal To-Do List.

This prevents personal organization actions from accidentally changing
shared task status.

### Due Dates

Tasks shall support optional due dates and times.

Users with appropriate permissions shall be able to:

- Set due date/time.
- Modify due date/time.
- Remove due date/time.
- View due date/time.
- Sort by due date/time.

Due dates shall be accessible and programmatically determinable.

Overdue information shall not rely solely on color.

### Task Reminders

Users shall be able to create personal reminders for applicable tasks.

A reminder shall support:

- Task reference.
- Reminder date/time.
- Optional due date/time relationship.
- Reminder state.
- Snooze state.
- User ownership.

Reminders shall be personal to the user.

One user's reminder shall not modify another user's reminder.

### Reminder Configuration

Users shall be able to configure reminder timing.

Reminders may be set:

- At a specific date/time.
- Before the task is due.
- At the task's due date/time.

The interface shall clearly communicate the selected reminder time.

### Reminder Alert Modal

When a reminder becomes due, ART shall display an accessible Reminder
Alert modal dialog.

The modal shall:

- Receive focus appropriately.
- Clearly identify the task.
- Identify the originating project/workspace/report.
- Identify the due date/time.
- Explain why the reminder is being displayed.
- Provide accessible actions.

Available actions shall include:

- Open Task.
- Mark Complete.
- Snooze.
- Dismiss (also dismissable using the Escape key).

### Reminder Snooze

Users shall be able to snooze reminders.

Default options shall include:

- 5 minutes.
- 15 minutes.
- 30 minutes.

Additional snooze options may be configurable.

Snoozing shall update only the current user's reminder.

### Reminder Focus Management

When the Reminder Alert opens:

1.  Focus shall move into the dialog.
2.  The task and reminder information shall be accessible to screen
    readers.
3.  Focus shall move to an appropriate action.
4.  Focus shall remain within the dialog while it is active.
5.  After dismissal, focus shall return to an appropriate originating
    control when practical.

Multiple simultaneous reminders should be presented through an
accessible consolidated reminder interface rather than repeatedly
stealing focus.

### Visual Reminder Alerts

Users shall be able to configure visual reminder behavior where
supported.

Possible options include:

- Modal alert.
- Dashboard notification.
- Application notification.
- Accessible e-mail notification.

Visual alerts shall not be the only notification mechanism.

### Auditory Reminder Alerts

Users shall be able to configure auditory reminder alerts.

The sound system shall:

- Support enable/disable.
- Respect system/browser restrictions.
- Provide configurable sounds where supported.
- Provide an accessible alternative when sound cannot be played.

Auditory alerts shall never be the sole means of communicating reminder
information.

### Optional Task Sound Effects

ART may support optional sound effects for specific task actions.

Possible actions include:

- Marking a Task completed.
- Task reopened.
- Task status changed.
- Task assigned.
- Task reassigned.
- Reminder triggered.
- Task marked Needs Review.
- Task marked Need Assistance.
- Task deleted.

Users shall be able to:

- Enable/disable task sounds.
- Configure sounds where supported.
- Preview sounds.
- Restore default sound settings.

Sound shall never be the only indication of a task action.

### Task Deletion

Users with appropriate permissions shall be able to delete tasks.

Delete commands shall be available through:

- Global Context Menu.
- Menu bar when the Tasks modal is open.
- Command Search/Command Palette where supported.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts where appropriate.

Do not place a permanent Delete button on every task.

### Accessible Delete Confirmation

Deleting a task shall require an accessible confirmation dialog.

The dialog shall clearly identify the task and communicate the
consequences.

Example:

> 

**Delete Task?**

Are you sure you want to delete "Test keyboard navigation"? This action
cannot be undone.

**Delete**\
**Cancel**

The dialog shall:

- Have an accessible name.
- Identify the task.
- Clearly communicate the action.
- Support keyboard interaction.
- Work with screen readers.
- Trap focus appropriately.
- Provide clearly labeled actions.
- Return focus appropriately after closing.

The destructive action should not receive focus by default unless there
is a compelling usability reason.

### Removing Tasks from Personal To-Do

Removing an item from the Personal To-Do List shall be different from
deleting the underlying task.

For example:

**Remove from Personal To-Do List**

> 

Removes the task from my personal work queue.

**Delete Task**

> 

Deletes the underlying task for authorized users.

ART shall clearly distinguish these operations.

### Menu Bar

When the Tasks modal is open, task-related commands shall be available
through the menu bar.

Commands shall be permission-aware.

Potential commands include:

- Create Task.

- Add to Personal To-Do.

- Remove from Personal To-Do.

- Change Status.

- Assign (based on user permissions).

- Reassign (based on user permissions).

- Set Priority.

- Set Due Date.

- Set Reminder.

- Sort.

- Delete Task (available from Assigned Tasks or Shared Tasks (based on
  permissions)).

- Undo.

- Redo.

### Global Context Menu

Applicable task actions shall be available through the Global Context
Menu.

Potential commands include:

- Add to Personal To-Do List.
- Remove from Personal To-Do List.
- Change Status.
- Assign (based on permissions).
- Reassign (based on permissions).
- Set Priority.
- Set Due Date.
- Set Reminder.
- Add/Edit Comments.
- Add @Mention.
- Defer Task.
- Request Assistance.
- Mark for Review.
- Open Task.
- Open Report.
- Open Workspace.
- Open Project.
- Delete Task.
- Edit Task Name.

The commands displayed shall depend on:

- Current task.
- Current context.
- User permissions.
- Feature availability.
- Task state.

### Customizable Keyboard Shortcuts

Task commands shall participate in ART's existing customizable keyboard
shortcut system.

Potential shortcuts include:

- Mark Complete.
- Mark Incomplete.
- Change Status.
- Add to Personal To-Do.
- Remove from Personal To-Do.
- Set Reminder.
- Set Due Date.
- Add/Edit Comments, Notes, or Instructions.
- Request Assistance.
- Mark Needs Review.
- Open Task.
- Delete Task.
- Undo.
- Redo.

Not every command requires a default shortcut.

### Minimal Interface Principle

The task interface shall remain intentionally uncluttered.

The persistent task controls shall primarily consist of:

- Checkbox.
- Status dropdown.
- Optional Comments text area.

Most other task actions shall be implemented as commands and exposed
through:

- Global Context Menu.
- Menu bar when the Tasks modal is open.
- Command Search/Command Palette where supported.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

Do not add rows of persistent action buttons to individual tasks unless
specifically required for accessibility or usability.

### Dashboard Integration

ART shall provide an optional **To-Do List** section on the Dashboard.

The section shall be enabled by default when task functionality is
enabled, subject to existing Dashboard configuration.

The Dashboard section may display:

- Highest-priority active tasks.
- Due tasks.
- Overdue tasks.
- Tasks needing assistance.
- Tasks needing review.
- Assigned Tasks
- Re-assigned tasks

Completed tasks shall not clutter the active Dashboard To-Do section.

The Dashboard shall provide a command or accessible navigation mechanism
for opening the full Tasks & To-Do modal.

### Notifications

Task-related events shall integrate with ART's existing Notifications
section.

Notifications may be generated for:

- Task assignment.
- Task reassignment.
- Status changes.
- Priority changes.
- Due date changes.
- @mentions\.
- Requests for assistance.
- Requests for review.
- Task comments.
- Reminder events.

Notifications shall respect permissions and user relationships.

### Task Assignment Permissions

ART shall respect its existing permission architecture.

Permission capabilities should include, where appropriate:

- View tasks.
- Create tasks.
- Update assigned tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Modify shared tasks.
- Delete tasks.
- Manage shared To-Do Lists.
- Manage task status options.

Users shall only be able to modify tasks according to their permissions.

### Assigned Task Updates

Users with permission to update assigned tasks shall be able to update
tasks assigned to them.

This may include:

- Status.
- Comments.
- Personal reminder.
- Personal To-Do inclusion.

Users shall not be able to reassign or delete tasks unless they have the
required permissions.

### Shared Task Management

Authorized Shared To-Do List administrators, creators, and editors shall
be able to:

- Create tasks.
- Modify tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Change task status.
- Change priority.
- Set due dates.
- Delete tasks.
- Manage shared lists.

Team members shall be able to see task assignments according to their
permissions.

### Status Option Management

Authorized users shall be able to manage task status options.

Commands shall be available through:

- Menu bar.
- Global Context Menu where applicable.
- Command Search.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts where appropriate.

Users may be able to:

- Add status options.
- Rename status options.
- Modify status behavior.
- Delete unused status options.

Status options currently used by tasks shall be protected against
destructive changes that would invalidate existing task data.

### Persistence

Task information shall persist across:

- Navigation.
- Browser refresh.
- Browser restart.
- Application restart.
- Sessions.
- Device restart.

Shared task information shall persist for all authorized members.

Personal information shall persist for the appropriate individual user.

### History Framework Integration

All task-related changes shall integrate with ART's existing **History
Framework**.

Actions performed from:

- Tasks & To-Do modal.
- Dashboard To-Do section.
- Global Context Menu.
- Menu bar.
- Keyboard shortcuts.

shall participate in Undo/Redo where the underlying action is
reversible.

### Undo and Redo

Users shall be able to undo and redo applicable task actions using ART's
existing:

- Undo keyboard shortcut.
- Redo keyboard shortcut.
- Menu commands.
- History Framework commands.

Applicable actions may include:

- Creating a task.
- Editing a task.
- Changing status.
- Checking/unchecking a task.
- Adding/removing a task from Personal To-Do.
- Changing priority.
- Changing due date.
- Setting/removing a reminder.
- Adding/editing task comments.
- Assigning a task.
- Reassigning a task.
- Deleting a task.

Undo/Redo shall not bypass permission controls.

The History Framework shall preserve the appropriate task state when an
action is undone or redone.

### Completed Task Undo/Redo

When a task is marked Complete and automatically moved to Completed
Tasks:

- Undo shall restore the task to its previous state and location.
- Redo shall reapply completion and move it back to Completed Tasks.

When an incomplete task is restored from Completed Tasks:

- Undo shall restore its previous completed state where appropriate.
- Redo shall reapply the status change.

The user should not have to manually move the task between panels when
Undo/Redo is used.

### Shared Data and History

For shared tasks, ART shall distinguish between:

- Local reversible actions.
- Changes made by other users.

Undo shall not silently overwrite another user's subsequent changes.

Any conflict between History Framework operations and collaborative
changes shall be handled by the Merge Conflict functionality established
in the subsequent collaboration epic.

### Import and Export

Where supported by ART's existing import/export architecture, task data
should be importable and exportable.

Export/import shall preserve, where technically possible:

- Task identity.
- Task name.
- Description.
- Assignment.
- Status.
- Priority.
- Due date/time.
- Organization.
- Project.
- Workspace.
- Product.
- Report.
- Comments.
- Relevant relationships.

Personal reminders and personal To-Do references should remain
user-specific unless the export format explicitly supports them.

### Organization Statistics Integration

Where Organization Statistics are enabled, task data may contribute to
organizational metrics.

Potential metrics include:

- Number of assigned tasks.
- Completed tasks.
- Outstanding tasks.
- Tasks by status.
- Tasks by priority.
- Tasks by tester.
- Tasks by product.
- Tasks by project.
- Tasks by workspace.
- Tasks by report.
- Tasks completed over time.
- Average task completion time where sufficient data exists.
- Tasks requiring assistance.
- Tasks requiring review.
- Overdue tasks.

Organizational statistics shall use the existing Organization/Client
association rules established by Organization Statistics.

### Accessibility Requirements

All task functionality shall comply with ART's accessibility
requirements.

Verify:

- Keyboard accessibility.
- Logical focus order.
- Visible focus.
- Screen-reader compatibility.
- Accessible tablist/tab/tabpanel implementation.
- Accessible modal dialogs.
- Accessible checkboxes.
- Accessible status dropdowns.
- Accessible autocomplete controls.
- Accessible text areas.
- Accessible context menus.
- Accessible menu bar commands.
- Accessible confirmation dialogs.
- Accessible notifications.
- Accessible reminder dialogs.
- Programmatically determinable task status.
- Programmatically determinable priority.
- Programmatically determinable sorting state.
- No reliance on color alone.
- No keyboard traps.
- Appropriate focus restoration.
- Programmatic label association with all controls and form elements.

### Dynamic Updates

When a task changes state, ART shall update the appropriate interface
without unnecessarily disrupting the user's focus.

For example, when a user checks a task:

1.  The status changes to Complete.
2.  The task is removed from the active To-Do list.
3.  The task appears in Completed Tasks.
4.  The appropriate update is announced to assistive technologies.
5.  Focus is restored or moved logically according to the interaction.

The application shall not unexpectedly move focus to unrelated controls.

### Data Relationships

Tasks shall reference existing ART entities rather than duplicating
their data.

A conceptual relationship may be:

    Organization
        |
        +-- Project
              |
              +-- Workspace
                    |
                    +-- Product
                          |
                          +-- Report
                                |
                                +-- Task
                                      |
                                      +-- Assigned User
                                      |
                                      +-- Personal To-Do References
                                      |
                                      +-- Reminder(s)
                                      |
                                      +-- Comments, Notes, or Instructions

### No Automatic Findings Creation

Completing a task shall not automatically create an accessibility
finding.

A task may lead to a finding, but creating the finding shall remain an
explicit user action.

Likewise:

- A To-Do item is not automatically a finding.
- A status change is not automatically a finding.
- A completed task is not automatically a finding.

### No Automatic Audit Compliance

Completing tasks shall not automatically indicate that an audit is
compliant or complete.

Task completion represents completion of the task only.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Shared Progress Logs can be created, edited, exported, imported, and
  merged without an ART server.
- Server-based collaboration is an optional enhancement rather than a
  prerequisite for Shared Progress Log functionality.

#### Task Management

- Users can create appropriate tasks.
- Authorized users can assign tasks.
- Authorized users can reassign tasks.
- Users can view tasks assigned to them.
- Users can add applicable tasks to Personal To-Do.
- Users can remove tasks from Personal To-Do without deleting the
  underlying task.
- Users can delete tasks when permitted.
- Deletion requires accessible confirmation.

#### Task Status

- Users can check and uncheck tasks.
- Users can use the Status dropdown.
- Checkbox and status remain synchronized.
- Completed tasks automatically move to Completed Tasks.
- Incomplete tasks automatically return to the active To-Do list.
- Deferred tasks support a date/time.
- Need Assistance and Needs Review states work appropriately.
- Custom statuses persist.

#### Priority and Sorting

- Task priority is programmatically determinable.
- Priority is available to screen readers.
- Highest-priority tasks appear first by default.
- Users can sort by priority.
- Users can sort by due date/time.
- Users can sort by date added.
- Sorting is accessible.
- Sorting state is programmatically determinable.

#### Comments and @Mentions

- Each task provides one optional Comments text area.
- Users can enter @mentions in the text area.
- @mentions are keyboard accessible.
- @mentions work with screen readers.
- Mentioned users receive appropriate notifications.
- Shared and personal information is handled according to permissions.

#### Reminders

- Users can create task reminders.
- Reminders are personal to the user.
- Reminder timing is configurable.
- Reminder alerts are accessible.
- Reminder dialogs receive focus appropriately.
- Snooze options include 5, 15, and 30 minutes.
- Visual alerts are configurable.
- Auditory alerts are configurable.
- Sound is never the only notification mechanism.
- Local task reminders shall operate without a server.

Server-based notifications and email reminders may be provided when ART
is connected to a collaboration service.

#### Sound Effects

- Users can enable/disable task sounds.
- Supported task actions can have optional sounds.
- Sounds can be previewed where supported.
- Sound settings persist.
- Sound never replaces accessible visual/programmatic information.

#### Completed Tasks

- Completed tasks automatically leave the active To-Do List.
- Completed tasks appear in the Completed Tasks tab.
- Users can change the completion status of completed tasks.
- Incomplete tasks automatically return to the active To-Do List.
- Task information is preserved during movement between panels.

#### Tasks Modal

- The Tasks & To-Do modal is fully accessible.
- Tabs use proper tablist/tab/tabpanel semantics.
- Assigned Tasks are available.
- Shared To-Do Lists/Tasks are available when applicable.
- Personal To-Do List is available.
- Completed Tasks is available.
- Tab navigation is keyboard accessible.
- Screen readers correctly announce tabs and panels.

#### Dashboard

- An optional To-Do section is available.
- The section can be enabled/disabled according to Dashboard settings.
- Active tasks are presented without unnecessary clutter.
- Completed tasks are excluded from the active To-Do section.
- Users can open the Tasks modal from the Dashboard.

#### Commands

- Task actions are available through the Global Context Menu.
- Task actions are available through the menu bar when the Tasks modal
  is open.
- Applicable actions are available through Command Search/Command
  Palette.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts can be assigned to appropriate
  commands.
- Commands respect permissions.
- The task interface is not cluttered with unnecessary persistent
  buttons.

#### History

- Task actions participate in the History Framework.
- Undo works from the Tasks modal.
- Redo works from the Tasks modal.
- Undo works from Dashboard task interactions.
- Redo works from Dashboard task interactions.
- Keyboard shortcuts work.
- Menu commands work.
- Undoing completion restores the task to the appropriate active state.
- Redoing completion returns it to Completed Tasks.

#### Persistence and Collaboration

- Task data persists across sessions.
- Shared task changes are visible to authorized users.
- Personal To-Do information remains user-specific.
- Personal reminders remain user-specific.
- Permissions are consistently enforced.
- Collaborative changes do not silently overwrite other users' work.

### Regression Testing

Verify that Epic 45 does not regress:

- Audit Logs.
- Executive Summaries.
- Usability Reports.
- Progress Logs.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Organization Statistics.
- Report Builder.
- Report Viewer.
- Dashboard.
- Notifications.
- History Framework.
- Existing keyboard shortcuts.
- Existing menu commands.
- Global Context Menu.
- Local-first storage.
- Import/export.
- Collaboration functionality.

### Non-Goals

This epic shall not:

- Create a separate Checklist system.
- Create a separate task-management application inside ART.
- Replace Shared Progress Logs.
- Replace Audit Logs.
- Replace Findings.
- Automatically create findings from tasks.
- Automatically declare an audit compliant when tasks are completed.
- Require Organization Statistics to be enabled.
- Require collaboration for personal tasks.
- Expose private task information to unauthorized users.
- Automatically delete shared tasks when users remove them from Personal
  To-Do Lists.

The result of this epic shall be a unified, accessible task-management
system in which **Assigned Tasks, Shared To-Do Lists, and Personal To-Do
Lists all use the same underlying task model**, while the Tasks & To-Do
modal and Dashboard provide clean, focused views of the work.

The interface shall remain intentionally uncluttered: **checkboxes and
Status dropdowns provide immediate task-state controls, while the Global
Context Menu, menu bar, Command Search, and customizable keyboard
shortcuts provide access to task-management commands.**

## Epic 46 — Collaboration Merge Conflicts and Conflict Resolution

### Overview

Extend ART's collaboration and shared-data architecture with a robust,
accessible **Merge Conflict Detection and Resolution Framework**.

This epic addresses situations where multiple users, devices, browser
sessions, or ART processes modify the same shared project, workspace,
report, task, progress log, or other collaborative data before those
changes can be synchronized.

### Purpose

The Merge Conflict system shall provide the foundation for resolving
conflicting changes made to ART project and workspace data.

The system shall support:

- File-based collaboration using exported/imported project or workspace
  packages.
- Future server-based synchronization.
- Offline work followed by synchronization.
- Concurrent changes by multiple users.
- Changes made on different devices.

The purpose of this epic is to ensure that:

- User changes are not silently lost.
- Conflicting changes are detected automatically.
- Users are clearly informed when conflicts occur.
- Users can review the competing versions.
- Users can choose how conflicts are resolved.
- Conflict resolution is fully accessible.
- Shared data remains consistent across sessions and users.
- The existing History Framework, Undo/Redo functionality,
  Notifications, Shared Progress Logs, Tasks, and collaboration
  permissions continue to work correctly.

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic.

Do not modify unrelated ART functionality.

Preserve all existing:

- Accessibility behavior
- Keyboard navigation
- Screen-reader support
- Focus management
- Menu commands
- Global Context Menu
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts
- History Framework
- Undo/Redo
- Notifications
- Permissions
- Local-first storage
- Import/Export
- Shared Progress Logs
- Tasks and To-Do Lists
- Organization Statistics
- Report Builder
- Report Viewer
- Audit Logs
- Executive Summaries
- Usability Reports

All conflict-resolution functionality shall be available using
keyboard-only interaction and shall be compatible with supported screen
readers and assistive technologies.

### Conflict Detection

ART shall detect conflicts when two or more versions of the same shared
data have been independently modified.

A conflict shall occur when:

1.  A user has a locally stored version of shared data.
2.  Another authorized user or session modifies the same underlying
    data.
3.  The local version is subsequently synchronized, saved, imported, or
    otherwise merged.
4.  ART determines that the changes cannot safely be combined
    automatically.

ART shall not silently overwrite either version.

### Types of Conflicts

The conflict framework shall support conflicts involving, where
applicable:

- Projects
- Workspaces
- Reports
- Report metadata
- Report content
- Report fields
- Audit Log entries
- Findings
- Executive Summary content
- Usability Report content
- Progress Logs
- Shared Progress Logs
- Progress Log tasks
- Task assignments
- Task status
- Task priority
- Task due dates
- Task comments
- Shared To-Do Lists
- Organization-related data
- Report metrics
- Organization Statistics source data
- Templates
- Configuration data
- Other shared entities introduced by future ART features

The architecture shall be extensible so new collaborative data types can
participate in conflict detection without requiring an entirely new
conflict-resolution system.

### Conflict Identity

Each collaborative entity shall have a stable identifier.

Where appropriate, ART shall track:

- Entity ID
- Entity type
- Parent entity
- Organization
- Project
- Workspace
- Report
- Version identifier
- Revision identifier
- Last-modified timestamp
- Last-modified user
- Change metadata

Conflict detection shall use stable identifiers rather than relying
solely on visible names.

### Change Tracking

ART shall maintain sufficient metadata to determine how
project/workspace data has changed.

Where appropriate, changes shall record:

- Object identifier
- Object type
- Field changed
- Previous value
- New value
- User or source of change when available
- Timestamp
- Project/workspace identifier
- Version information

Change metadata shall support both local file-based merging and future
server synchronization.

### Revision Tracking

ART shall maintain sufficient revision information to determine whether
two versions originated from the same previous state.

Where technically appropriate, revisions should include:

- Revision ID
- Parent revision ID
- Creation timestamp
- Modification timestamp
- User
- Change type
- Entity identifier

The implementation shall support branching histories when multiple users
independently modify the same data.

### Optimistic Collaboration Model

ART should use an optimistic collaboration model where practical.

Users shall be allowed to work without continuously locking shared
entities.

ART shall detect conflicts when changes are synchronized rather than
unnecessarily preventing simultaneous work.

### Automatic Merge

ART shall attempt to automatically merge non-conflicting changes
whenever safe.

For example:

    User A changes Task Priority → High

    User B changes Task Due Date → Friday

These changes affect different properties and should be eligible for
automatic merging.

The resulting task should contain:

    Priority → High
    Due Date → Friday

### Automatic Merge Safety

ART shall not automatically merge changes when doing so could cause data
loss or create an ambiguous result.

Examples include:

- Two users changing the same text content differently.
- Two users changing the same task status differently.
- One user deleting an entity while another modifies it.
- Two users modifying the same field configuration incompatibly.
- Two users changing the same assignment.
- Conflicting changes to ordered collections where the intended result
  cannot be determined safely.

When automatic merging is unsafe, ART shall create a conflict requiring
resolution.

### Three-Way Merge

Where appropriate, ART shall use a three-way merge model consisting of:

- Common/base version
- Current/local version
- Incoming/remote version

The merge engine shall automatically combine non-conflicting changes and
identify conflicting changes requiring user resolution.

### File-Based Collaboration

ART shall allow users to export a project/workspace, make changes
independently, and import another version of the same project/workspace.

When differences are detected, ART shall identify changes that can be
merged automatically and changes that require conflict resolution.

File-based collaboration shall not require a server.

### Conflict Resolution Modal

When a conflict requires user intervention, ART shall display an
accessible **Merge Conflict** modal dialog.

The dialog shall:

- Have an accessible name
- Clearly identify the conflicting entity
- Explain that conflicting changes were detected
- Identify the relevant project/workspace/report where applicable
- Identify the users associated with the conflicting versions
- Provide access to the competing versions
- Provide clear resolution choices
- Trap focus appropriately
- Restore focus appropriately when closed

### Conflict Modal Structure

The conflict dialog should provide an accessible tablist/tab/tabpanel
structure when multiple conflict categories or versions need to be
reviewed.

Potential panels include:

- **Conflict Summary**
- **My Version**
- **Other Version**
- **Merged Result**
- **Change Details**

Only panels applicable to the conflict need to be displayed.

### Conflict Summary

The Conflict Summary shall explain:

- What entity is affected
- What changed
- Who made each change
- When the changes occurred
- Whether automatic merging was attempted
- Why manual resolution is required

The summary shall use plain language.

### Version Comparison

Users shall be able to compare conflicting versions.

For example:

    Current Local Version
    Status: In Progress
    Priority: High
    Due Date: August 20

    Shared Version
    Status: Needs Review
    Priority: High
    Due Date: August 22

Differences shall be programmatically determinable.

Do not rely solely on:

- Color
- Bold text
- Icons
- Position
- Visual highlighting

to communicate differences.

### Text Conflicts

For conflicting text content, ART shall identify:

- Original content
- Local changes
- Shared changes

Where technically practical, ART should provide a structured difference
view showing additions, deletions, and modifications.

The difference information shall remain accessible to screen readers.

### Field-Level Conflicts

Where a conflict involves structured fields, ART should identify
conflicts at the field/property level.

For example:

    Field: Priority

    Original: Normal
    Your version: High
    Shared version: Critical

This allows the user to resolve only the conflicting property rather
than replacing an entire record unnecessarily.

### Resolution Options

The available resolution options shall depend on the conflict type.

Common options shall include:

- Keep My Version
- Keep Other Version
- Use Both Where Possible
- Resolve Manually
- Accept Merged Version
- Cancel

Destructive or potentially data-losing options shall be clearly
identified.

### Field-Level Resolution

When possible, users shall be able to resolve conflicts individually.

For example:

    Priority
        ○ Keep My Version: High
        ○ Keep Other Version: Critical

    Due Date
        ○ Keep My Version: August 20
        ○ Keep Other Version: August 22

    Status
        ○ Keep My Version: In Progress
        ○ Keep Other Version: Needs Review

The user shall then be able to create a final resolved version.

### Manual Merge

For complex conflicts, ART shall provide a manual merge workflow.

The user shall be able to select the desired value from each conflicting
version.

Where appropriate, the user shall also be able to enter a new value.

The final merged result shall be previewed before it is committed.

### Merged Result Preview

Before applying a manual merge, ART shall provide a **Merged Result**
view.

The preview shall clearly communicate:

- Which version was selected
- Which fields were merged
- Which fields were manually edited
- Any unresolved conflicts

The **Apply Merge** command shall remain unavailable until all required
conflicts have been resolved.

### Unresolved Conflicts

ART shall not allow an incomplete merge to be silently committed.

If required conflicts remain unresolved, the user shall receive an
accessible message explaining what remains unresolved.

### Canceling Conflict Resolution

If the user closes the conflict dialog without resolving the conflict:

- The conflicting versions shall remain preserved.
- No data shall be silently overwritten.
- ART shall retain sufficient information to allow the conflict to be
  resolved later.

### Conflict Notifications

When a conflict requires user intervention, ART shall create an
appropriate notification.

The notification shall identify:

- The affected project/workspace/report
- The entity
- The fact that a merge conflict requires attention

The notification shall provide a command to open the conflict-resolution
interface.

### Dashboard Notifications

Merge conflict notifications shall appear in the existing Dashboard
Notifications section.

Users shall be able to identify unresolved conflicts.

For example:

> 

**Merge conflict requires attention**\
Report: Accessibility Audit — Homepage\
Another user modified this report while you were working on it.

### Conflict Notification Persistence

Unresolved conflict notifications shall persist until:

- The conflict is resolved
- The conflict is otherwise dismissed according to the application's
  conflict policy

Dismissing a notification shall not delete or discard the underlying
conflict.

### Conflict Status

ART shall maintain a conflict state for affected entities.

Potential states include:

- No Conflict
- Conflict Detected
- Resolution Required
- Resolution In Progress
- Resolved
- Resolution Failed

The state shall be programmatically determinable.

### Conflict Indicators

ART may provide visual indicators for unresolved conflicts.

However, visual indicators shall never be the sole means of
communicating conflict status.

The conflict state shall also be available through:

- Accessible names
- Screen-reader announcements
- Text
- Notifications
- Programmatic state

### Permissions

Conflict resolution shall respect ART's permission architecture.

A user shall only be able to resolve conflicts for entities they are
authorized to modify.

A user who can view but not modify an entity shall not be given commands
that would modify the entity.

### Server Synchronization Compatibility

The merge architecture shall not be dependent on a specific server
implementation.

The same change and conflict model shall be capable of being used by a
future ART collaboration server or synchronization API.

### Shared Progress Logs

Merge conflict handling shall support Shared Progress Logs.

Potential conflicts include:

- Task status
- Task assignment
- Task reassignment
- Task priority
- Task due date
- Task comments
- Task modifications
- Shared To-Do List membership
- Status-option changes

### Task Assignment Conflicts

If two authorized users change the assignment of the same task
independently, ART shall detect the conflict when the changes cannot
safely be merged.

For example:

    Original:
    Assigned to: User A

    Local:
    Assigned to: User B

    Shared:
    Assigned to: User C

ART shall require an appropriate resolution.

### Task Status Conflicts

If two users change the same task's status independently, ART shall not
silently select one status.

The conflict interface shall identify:

- Previous status
- Local status
- Shared status

The authorized user shall select the appropriate result.

### Task Comments

Where users add comments independently to the same task, ART should
merge comments when their ordering can be safely preserved.

For example:

    User A comment
    User B comment

should generally not constitute a destructive conflict merely because
both users added comments.

Comments should retain:

- Author
- Timestamp
- Content
- @mentions

### @Mentions During Conflicts

@mentions shall remain associated with their original comments.

A merge operation shall not silently remove an @mention.

If a conflicting comment is discarded, ART shall clearly indicate that
the comment and associated @mentions are being discarded.

### Progress Log History

Progress Log task changes shall participate in the existing History
Framework.

Conflict resolution shall not destroy the historical record of the
conflicting changes.

### History Framework Integration

All applicable conflict-resolution actions shall participate in ART's
existing History Framework.

Users shall be able to use:

- Undo
- Redo
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Menu commands

where the action is safely reversible.

### Conflict Resolution and Undo

After resolving a conflict, Undo shall restore the previous state where
technically possible.

For example:

    Conflict detected
            ↓
    User resolves conflict
            ↓
    Merged version saved
            ↓
    Undo
            ↓
    Previous pre-resolution state restored

Undo shall not silently overwrite subsequent collaborative changes.

### Conflict Resolution and Redo

Redo shall reapply the conflict-resolution action when the underlying
state remains compatible.

If the state has changed because of another user's subsequent
modification, ART shall detect the resulting conflict rather than
blindly applying stale data.

### Concurrent Changes During Resolution

Another user may modify the affected entity while the
conflict-resolution dialog is open.

ART shall detect this condition.

The user shall be informed that the data changed while they were
resolving the conflict.

ART shall not silently apply a stale resolution over the newer version.

### Stale Resolution

If the underlying data changes while a conflict is being resolved:

1.  ART shall detect the new revision.
2.  The pending resolution shall be invalidated or recalculated.
3.  The user shall be informed.
4.  ART shall provide an updated conflict view.
5.  The user shall be allowed to resolve the new conflict.

### Conflict Locking

ART should avoid requiring exclusive locks merely to resolve conflicts.

If temporary locking is technically necessary, it shall:

- Be clearly communicated
- Be time-limited
- Be accessible
- Automatically expire when appropriate
- Not prevent other users from viewing the entity unnecessarily

### Conflict Resolution Commands

Applicable commands shall be available through:

- Menu bar
- Global Context Menu
- Command Search/Command Palette
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts where appropriate

Potential commands include:

- Review Conflict
- Keep My Version
- Keep Other Version
- Merge Versions
- Resolve Manually
- Apply Merge
- Cancel Resolution
- Retry Synchronization
- Undo
- Redo

### Global Context Menu

When an entity has an unresolved conflict, the Global Context Menu shall
provide appropriate commands.

For example:

- Review Conflict
- Resolve Conflict
- View Conflict Details
- Retry Synchronization

Commands shall only appear when applicable.

### Menu Bar

When conflict-resolution UI is open, the menu bar shall provide relevant
commands.

Commands shall be:

- Clearly labeled
- Keyboard accessible
- Permission-aware
- Consistent with the Global Context Menu

### Customizable Keyboard Shortcuts

Conflict-resolution commands shall participate in ART's customizable
keyboard shortcut system.

Potential shortcuts include:

- Open Conflict
- Keep My Version
- Keep Other Version
- Merge
- Apply Resolution
- Cancel Resolution
- Undo
- Redo

No shortcut shall be assigned if doing so could create an unsafe or
confusing workflow.

### Accessible Conflict Dialog

The conflict dialog shall comply with ART's modal-dialog accessibility
requirements.

Verify:

- Accessible dialog name
- Accessible description
- Correct role
- Focus moves into dialog
- Focus remains within dialog
- Logical tab order
- Visible focus
- Screen-reader announcements
- Escape behavior where appropriate
- Correct focus restoration
- No keyboard trap
- All controls have accessible names

### Accessible Difference Presentation

Differences between versions shall be accessible to screen readers.

For example, a screen reader should be able to communicate:

> 

Priority. Original value: Normal. Your value: High. Other user's value:
Critical.

rather than merely announcing that a visual element has changed color.

### Status Announcements

When a conflict is resolved, ART shall provide an accessible status
announcement.

For example:

> 

**Merge conflict resolved. The report was updated successfully.**

If resolution fails:

> 

**Merge conflict could not be resolved. The conflicting changes have
been preserved.**

### Focus Management

When a conflict is detected while the user is actively working:

- ART should avoid unexpectedly stealing focus unless immediate user
  attention is required.
- A notification should be generated.
- The user should be able to open the conflict-resolution dialog through
  an accessible command.

When the user explicitly opens the conflict dialog, focus shall move
into the dialog.

After resolution, focus shall return to the originating context where
practical.

### Synchronization Failures

A synchronization failure shall be distinguished from a merge conflict.

For example:

    Synchronization failure:
    Unable to communicate with the shared data source.

    Merge conflict:
    The shared data source was reached, but two incompatible versions exist.

Users shall receive different messages and appropriate recovery options.

### Retry Synchronization

Where a synchronization failure occurs, ART shall provide an accessible
**Retry Synchronization** command.

Retrying shall not overwrite local changes.

### Offline Changes

ART shall continue to support local-first workflows.

Users shall be able to continue working offline where existing ART
functionality supports offline operation.

When synchronization becomes available:

1.  ART shall compare revisions.
2.  Non-conflicting changes shall be merged.
3.  Conflicting changes shall enter the Merge Conflict workflow.
4.  No changes shall be silently discarded.

### Browser Sessions

Conflict detection shall account for multiple ART browser sessions where
shared synchronization is supported.

For example:

- Chrome window A modifies a report.
- Chrome window B modifies the same report.
- The changes are synchronized.
- ART detects whether the changes can be merged.

### Multiple Devices

Where shared synchronization supports multiple devices, the same
conflict model shall apply.

A change made from one device shall not silently overwrite a conflicting
change made from another device.

### Import Conflicts

If a user imports data containing entities that conflict with existing
data, ART shall use the same conflict-resolution architecture where
appropriate.

The import process shall clearly communicate:

- What conflicts were detected
- Which entities are affected
- Available resolution options

### Export/Import Safety

Exporting data shall never modify or resolve a conflict.

Importing data shall not silently overwrite conflicting entities.

### Conflict Data Preservation

When a conflict is detected, ART shall preserve enough information to
reconstruct the competing versions.

At minimum, where technically feasible:

- Original/base version
- Local version
- Shared version
- User
- Timestamp
- Revision information

shall be retained until the conflict is resolved or appropriately
discarded.

### Conflict Resolution Record

ART should maintain a historical record of resolved conflicts.

Where appropriate, the record should contain:

- Entity
- Conflict date/time
- Users involved
- Resolution method
- Fields affected
- Resulting revision

This record should participate in existing audit/history functionality
where applicable.

### Privacy and Security

Conflict information shall respect existing privacy and permissions.

Users shall not be shown:

- Unauthorized private data
- Private comments
- Restricted project information
- Restricted organization information

merely because that information exists in a conflicting revision.

### No Silent Data Loss

This is a fundamental requirement.

ART shall never silently discard a user's changes because of
synchronization or merging.

If a change cannot be safely preserved, ART shall:

1.  Detect the issue.
2.  Preserve the competing data where possible.
3.  Inform the user.
4.  Provide an accessible resolution workflow.

### Conflict Resolution for Deleted Entities

If one user deletes an entity while another user modifies it, ART shall
detect a delete/modify conflict.

For example:

    Original:
    Report exists.

    User A:
    Deletes Report.

    User B:
    Adds findings to Report.

ART shall not silently discard User B's changes.

The conflict workflow shall provide appropriate choices, such as:

- Keep Deleted Version
- Restore and Keep Changes
- Review and Merge

### Delete/Delete Conflicts

If two users delete the same entity, ART may automatically resolve the
conflict when the deletions are equivalent.

The event should still be represented appropriately in history where
required.

### Rename Conflicts

If two users rename the same entity differently, ART shall detect the
conflict.

For example:

    Local:
    Homepage Audit

    Shared:
    Homepage Accessibility Audit

The user shall be able to choose the desired name.

### Ordered Collection Conflicts

Where users independently reorder the same collection, ART shall attempt
to merge changes when the resulting order can be determined safely.

If it cannot safely determine the intended order, ART shall provide a
manual resolution workflow.

This may apply to:

- Report sections
- Report fields
- Progress Log tasks
- To-Do tasks
- Template sections
- Other ordered collections

### Configuration Conflicts

Conflicts involving shared configuration shall be handled separately
from content conflicts where appropriate.

Examples include:

- Field configuration
- Status options
- Report layout
- Shared templates
- Shared Progress Log configuration

### Organization Statistics Conflicts

Organization Statistics shall not be manually merged as though they were
ordinary user-entered content.

Where statistics are derived from source data, ART should regenerate the
statistics from the resolved underlying data.

This prevents stale calculated values from being treated as
authoritative.
