provide a migration strategy that preserves the user's ART identity
where possible.

Changing authentication methods shall not unintentionally orphan:

- Projects
- Reports
- Tasks
- Progress Logs
- Organization memberships
- Comments
- Assignments
- Notifications

### Authentication and Future Desktop Application

The authentication architecture shall be compatible with ART's long-term
goal of supporting both:

- Web-based ART
- Stand-alone downloadable/installable ART applications

The identity architecture shall allow authenticated users to access
authorized server-dependent features from supported ART clients.

### Authentication and Integrations

The authentication architecture shall support future integrations such
as:

- Jira
- GitHub Issues
- Microsoft Azure
- Google Workspace
- Other testing and project-management platforms

External integrations shall use appropriate authorization mechanisms and
shall not require ART users to provide passwords for external services.

### Acceptance Criteria

Epic 48 shall be considered complete when:

1.  ART can be used fully without logging in for fundamental local
    functionality.
2.  ART does not require users to create an ART password.
3.  A secure passwordless login workflow has been implemented.
4.  WebAuthn/FIDO2 passkey authentication has been implemented.
5.  Users can create ART accounts using a passkey.
6.  Users can sign in using a passkey.
7.  Users can register multiple passkeys.
8.  Users can remove and replace passkeys securely.
9.  Google authentication is supported.
10. Microsoft authentication is supported.
11. Amazon authentication is supported.
12. GitHub authentication is supported.
13. OAuth 2.0 and/or OpenID Connect has been evaluated and used where
    appropriate.
14. Authentication credentials are never stored in plain text.
15. Passkey private keys are never transmitted to or stored by ART.
16. OAuth tokens are handled securely.
17. Authentication secrets are not exposed in source code.
18. Users can log out securely.
19. Session expiration is handled securely.
20. Authentication failures are handled accessibly.
21. Local ART data remains available after login and logout.
22. Logging in does not automatically upload local projects without
    appropriate user awareness and authorization.
23. Server-dependent features require appropriate authentication.
24. Authentication does not grant unauthorized access to organizations,
    projects, workspaces, reports, or other data.
25. Stable ART user identities are implemented.
26. Authentication supports future organization membership and
    permissions.
27. Authentication supports future Shared Project Workspaces and
    collaboration.
28. Authentication supports future server-based synchronization.
29. An accessible account security interface has been implemented.
30. Users can manage registered passkeys.
31. Hardware security keys are supported where technically feasible.
32. Cross-device authentication is supported where technically feasible.
33. TOTP authenticator applications can be supported as an optional
    additional/recovery mechanism if enabled.
34. TOTP enrollment provides an accessible manual-entry alternative to
    QR-code scanning.
35. Secure recovery mechanisms are implemented.
36. Recovery codes are securely generated and managed where implemented.
37. Authentication workflows have been tested with multiple screen
    readers.
38. Authentication workflows have been tested using keyboard-only
    interaction.
39. Authentication workflows have been tested with refreshable braille
    displays where available.
40. Authentication workflows have been tested with multiple assistive
    technologies.
41. Each supported OAuth provider has undergone accessibility testing.
42. Passkey workflows have undergone accessibility testing.
43. Security testing has been performed.
44. Authentication rate limiting and abuse prevention are implemented
    where applicable.
45. Authentication documentation has been added to the user guide.
46. Developer security documentation has been added.
47. Authentication architecture documentation has been added.
48. Development, testing, and production authentication environments are
    appropriately separated.
49. Automated authentication tests have been implemented.
50. No known critical authentication vulnerabilities remain unresolved
    before production deployment.

### Deliverables

The completed epic shall produce:

- Secure passwordless authentication architecture
- WebAuthn/FIDO2 implementation
- Passkey registration
- Passkey authentication
- Multiple-passkey management
- Passkey removal and replacement
- Optional hardware security-key support
- Cross-device authentication where supported
- Accessible account creation
- Accessible passwordless login
- Google authentication
- Microsoft authentication
- Amazon authentication
- GitHub authentication
- Secure logout
- Session management
- Secure OAuth token handling
- ART user identity system
- Account profile
- Account security dashboard
- Authentication-provider management
- Optional TOTP authenticator-app support
- Recovery-code system where implemented
- Secure account recovery
- Authentication error handling
- Authentication-state management
- Local unauthenticated mode
- Server-dependent authenticated mode
- Authentication/authorization integration
- Security logging
- Authentication testing
- Accessibility testing
- User documentation
- Developer documentation
- Security documentation
- Authentication deployment documentation
- Provider configuration documentation

### Non-Goals

This epic does not require ART to:

- Require an account to use fundamental ART functionality.
- Require users to create passwords.
- Store passwords.
- Force users to use a particular identity provider.
- Force users to use a particular authenticator application.
- Require biometric authentication.
- Require a smartphone.
- Require a particular operating system.
- Automatically upload local user data when a user logs in.
- Implement every possible authentication provider.
- Replace an organization's existing identity-management system.
- Grant collaboration access merely because a user is authenticated.
- Claim security certification merely because authentication has been
  implemented.

### Future Extensions

The authentication architecture should provide a foundation for future
capabilities including:

- Enterprise SSO
- Microsoft Entra ID
- Google Workspace authentication
- SAML
- Additional OpenID Connect providers
- Additional OAuth providers
- Enterprise-managed passkeys
- Enterprise security keys
- Organization invitations
- Organization membership
- Role-based access control
- Shared Project Workspaces
- Shared Progress Logs
- Server-synchronized Tasks
- Centralized notifications
- Email notifications
- @mentions
- Organization Statistics
- Enterprise administration
- Self-hosted identity management
- Additional FIDO-compatible authentication mechanisms

### Long-Term Goal

The long-term goal of Epic 48 is to provide a secure, accessible,
passwordless authentication system that gives users a meaningful choice:

> **Use ART locally without an account, or sign in using a passkey,
> Google, Microsoft, Amazon, GitHub, or another supported authentication
> method when you want the additional capabilities provided by
> collaboration and server-based services.**

ART shall not make passwords a requirement for accessing collaborative
functionality.

Passkeys shall provide the preferred native ART authentication
experience, while external identity providers and optional authenticator
mechanisms provide additional flexibility.

The authentication system shall provide a secure foundation for ART's
transition from a primarily local web application into an optional
collaborative, hosted, self-hosted, and eventually desktop-capable
platform while preserving ART's local-first, accessibility-first,
privacy-conscious, and platform-agnostic principles.

## Epic 49 — ART Identity, Organization Folders, and File-Based Collaboration

### Epic Overview

Establish the foundational infrastructure required for **file-based
collaboration in ART** without requiring an ART server.

This epic introduces a shared-file collaboration model in which ART
users can collaborate by saving and opening `.art` files from a shared
or synchronized folder provided by an external storage system such as
Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, SharePoint, a network drive,
NAS, or another compatible shared/virtual drive system.

This epic also introduces a persistent **ART User Profile** and **ART
Identity** system that allows each local ART installation to identify
the person using it. The identity information shall support file-based
collaboration, shared reports, shared projects, shared tasks, shared
Progress Logs, revision history, change tracking, @mentions, and future
server-based collaboration.

ART shall remain fully usable without an account, server, shared folder,
or Internet connection. File-based collaboration shall be an optional
capability built on top of ART's existing local-first functionality.

### Goals

The goals of this epic are to:

- Introduce file-based collaboration as a first-class ART capability.
- Allow multiple ART users to collaborate on the same `.art` file
  without requiring an ART server.
- Allow collaboration through shared folders managed by external storage
  systems.
- Establish a persistent ART user identity that is independent of server
  authentication.
- Allow users to configure and edit their personal ART identity
  information.
- Provide reliable identification of users who create, modify, comment
  on, assign, or complete collaborative work.
- Establish document and revision metadata required for detecting
  changes and resolving merge conflicts.
- Integrate file-based collaboration with ART's existing Merge Changes
  functionality.
- Introduce shared ART Organization Folders.
- Allow projects, reports, tasks, Progress Logs, and related ART files
  to participate in the same shared-folder collaboration model.
- Support Organization Metrics based on the ART files contained within a
  configured Organization Folder.
- Introduce @mentions as part of the file-based collaboration
  infrastructure.
- Allow @mentions to work within a shared report, shared project, or
  shared ART Organization Folder.
- Establish an architecture that can later support server-based
  collaboration without requiring the file-based collaboration system to
  be redesigned.
- Preserve ART's local-first and offline capabilities.

### General Requirements

Implement only the functionality described in this epic and the
functionality necessary to support the file-based collaboration
architecture.

Do not require users to create an ART account to use fundamental ART
functionality.

Do not require an ART server for file-based collaboration.

Do not make ART dependent on a particular external storage provider.

The implementation shall be storage-provider agnostic and should work
with any storage system that makes `.art` files available to ART as
ordinary files.

Examples include:

- Google Drive
- Microsoft OneDrive
- Dropbox
- SharePoint-synchronized folders
- Network drives
- NAS storage
- USB or removable storage
- Other virtual or synchronized drives
- Locally shared folders

External storage providers shall remain responsible for file storage,
synchronization, and their own access-control mechanisms.

ART shall be responsible for document identity, revision tracking,
change detection, collaboration metadata, merging, conflict detection,
and collaboration-related application behavior.

### ART User Profile and Identity

Add a new **ART User Profile** configuration area within ART Settings.

The profile shall allow each user to personalize their local copy of ART
with information that can be used to identify them when working with
reports and collaborative content.

The profile shall include:

- Name
- Email Address
- Display Name
- Job Title
- ART Role

The user shall be able to edit or change any of these values at any
time.

### User Name

Provide a field for the user's name.

The name may represent the user's full professional name or another name
they use when working within ART.

### Email Address

Provide a field for the user's email address.

The email address shall be available for collaboration functionality
such as identifying users and supporting @mentions.

ART shall not expose the user's email address to other users merely
because it has been entered into the local profile.

Email addresses shall only be included in shared collaboration metadata
when required by the applicable collaboration functionality and when
appropriate to the user's configured sharing context.

### Display Name

Provide an optional Display Name field.

The Display Name may differ from the user's name.

For example:

- Name: `Jonathan Smith`
- Display Name: `Jon Smith`

When a Display Name is provided, ART should preferentially use it for
user-facing collaboration interfaces, comments, task assignments,
revision history, and @mentions.

If no Display Name is provided, ART shall use the user's configured
Name.

### Job Title

Provide an optional Job Title field.

Examples include:

- Digital Accessibility Analyst
- Accessibility Tester
- UX Researcher
- Accessibility Consultant
- QA Engineer
- Project Manager

The job title may be used in applicable collaboration and attribution
interfaces.

### ART Role

Provide an ART Role field that identifies the user's role within ART
collaboration.

The role shall be designed so it can support both file-based and future
server-based collaboration.

The implementation shall not assume that the user's ART Role is
equivalent to their job title.

For example:

- Job Title: Digital Accessibility Analyst
- ART Role: Tester

The role information shall be available to collaboration features that
need to distinguish between different types of participants.

### Persistent Local User Identifier

Each ART installation shall have a unique persistent local user
identifier.

The identifier shall:

- Be generated automatically.
- Persist across sessions.
- Not be based solely on the user's name.
- Not be based solely on the user's email address.
- Remain stable when the user changes their name, display name, job
  title, or role.
- Be usable for identifying revisions, comments, tasks, assignments, and
  other collaborative actions.

The identifier shall not be presented as the user's primary visible
identity.

The user's Display Name or Name shall be used for normal user-facing
interfaces.

### Identity and Authentication Separation

The local ART User Profile shall be separate from authentication.

A user shall be able to configure an ART User Profile without logging
into ART.

A user shall be able to use ART's fundamental functionality without
creating an account.

Authentication shall only be required for server-dependent functionality
when required by the applicable server or service.

This architecture shall remain compatible with the passwordless
authentication system defined by Epic 48.

When a user eventually signs into an ART server, their server identity
may be associated with their existing ART identity rather than creating
an unnecessary duplicate identity.

### Privacy of User Identity Information

ART shall clearly distinguish between:

- Information stored only in the user's local ART profile.
- Information embedded in `.art` files.
- Information shared with collaborators.
- Information transmitted to an ART server when server-based
  functionality is used.

Users shall not have their personal information unexpectedly exposed
through shared files.

ART shall minimize the amount of personally identifiable information
written into shared files.

Where possible, collaboration metadata should use the persistent ART
User ID for machine-readable identity and the user's configured Display
Name for human-readable attribution.

### File-Based Collaboration

Introduce **File-Based Collaboration** as an ART capability that does
not require an ART server.

Multiple users shall be able to collaborate by opening, modifying,
saving, and synchronizing `.art` files through a shared folder.

The shared storage provider shall handle synchronization of the physical
file.

ART shall handle the collaborative document state.

### Shared `.art` Files

An `.art` file used for collaboration shall contain sufficient metadata
to allow ART to determine:

- Document identity
- Current revision
- Parent revision
- Revision history, where retained
- Last modification information
- User attribution
- Collaboration metadata
- Change information necessary for merging

The `.art` file shall remain a valid ART document and shall continue to
work when copied, backed up, moved, or opened from another supported
location.

### Document Identity

Each collaborative `.art` document shall have a persistent unique
Document ID.

The Document ID shall remain unchanged when:

- The file is renamed.
- The file is moved.
- The file is copied within a collaboration environment.
- The file is opened by another ART user.

ART shall use the Document ID to distinguish the document from the
physical filename.

### Revision Identity

Each saved revision of a collaborative `.art` document shall have a
unique Revision ID.

Each revision should maintain a relationship to its parent revision.

This shall allow ART to determine the history and ancestry of changes.

### Revision Metadata

Revision metadata should include, when available:

- Revision ID
- Parent Revision ID
- Document ID
- User ID
- Display Name
- Timestamp
- Type of change
- Merge information
- Other metadata necessary for conflict detection and resolution

### File Change Detection

When an `.art` file is opened, ART shall determine whether the file has
changed since the user's previous working revision.

ART shall be able to detect that:

- The shared file is unchanged.
- The shared file contains newer changes.
- The user's local working copy is based on an older revision.
- The file contains changes that may be automatically merged.
- The file contains changes that require conflict resolution.

### Simultaneous Editing

Multiple users shall be permitted to have the same `.art` file open at
the same time.

ART shall not assume that only one person can edit a file at a time.

Each user's active editing session shall operate on that user's local
working state until changes are saved or synchronized.

ART shall protect against silently overwriting another user's changes.

### Saving a Stale Document

If a user attempts to save a document that is based on an older revision
than the currently synchronized shared file, ART shall not simply
overwrite the newer shared version.

Instead, ART shall:

1.  Detect that the shared file has changed.
2.  Preserve the user's current changes.
3.  Retrieve or use the newer shared revision.
4.  Determine the common ancestor revision.
5.  Compare the user's changes with the newer shared changes.
6.  Automatically merge non-conflicting changes where possible.
7.  Identify conflicting changes.
8.  Open the Merge Changes interface when conflicts require user
    intervention.
9.  Allow the user to resolve the conflicts.
10. Create a new merged revision.
11. Save the resulting revision safely.

### Three-Way Merge

File-based collaboration shall use a three-way merge model whenever
possible.

The merge operation shall compare:

- The common ancestor.
- The user's current working version.
- The newer shared version.

This shall allow ART to distinguish between:

- Changes made only by the current user.
- Changes made only by another user.
- Identical changes made by both users.
- Changes that affect different parts of the document.
- Changes that conflict with one another.

### Automatic Non-Conflicting Merging

When changes do not conflict, ART should merge them automatically.

For example, if User A modifies one finding and User B modifies a
different finding, ART should preserve both changes without requiring
manual conflict resolution.

### Conflict Detection

When two users modify the same underlying data in incompatible ways, ART
shall identify the changes as conflicts.

Examples may include:

- Two users changing the same field to different values.
- Two users modifying the same task status differently.
- Two users editing the same comment.
- Two users changing the assignment of the same task.
- Two users changing the same Progress Log information.
- Two users making incompatible structural changes.

### Merge Changes Modal

The existing Merge Changes functionality shall be integrated into the
file-based collaboration workflow.

When conflicts are detected, ART shall automatically open the Merge
Changes modal when appropriate.

The modal shall allow the user to:

- Review changes.
- Identify the user associated with each change.
- Compare conflicting values.
- Keep the current user's change.
- Keep the shared version.
- Resolve conflicts manually where supported.
- Accept non-conflicting changes.
- Cancel the merge.
- Return to the document without silently discarding changes.

The existing accessibility requirements for the Merge Changes interface
shall remain in effect.

### Refresh From Shared File

Provide an accessible command for:

> **Refresh from Shared File**

The command shall be available through appropriate command interfaces,
including applicable menus, the global context menu, and customizable
keyboard shortcuts.

When invoked, ART shall:

1.  Check whether the shared file has changed.
2.  Retrieve the newer revision when available.
3.  Compare the user's working version with the shared version.
4.  Automatically merge non-conflicting changes.
5.  Open Merge Changes when conflicts exist.
6.  Update the current document after the merge is resolved.

### Automatic External Change Notification

When ART detects that a newer version of the currently open shared
document is available, it should notify the user without automatically
replacing their current working state.

The notification should clearly state that:

- A newer version is available.
- The current user's unsaved work will be preserved.
- The user can refresh when ready.

Provide an accessible command to initiate synchronization.

### Collaboration Synchronization Model

File-based collaboration shall use a **save-and-refresh synchronization
model**.

Users may work simultaneously on their local copies of a report.

Other users' changes become available after the changes have been:

1.  Saved by the other user.
2.  Synchronized by the external storage provider.
3.  Retrieved by ART through a refresh or other supported
    synchronization check.

ART shall not claim to provide true real-time synchronization through
this mechanism.

The interface should describe this capability as file-based or
near-real-time collaboration rather than real-time collaboration.

### Version History

Collaborative `.art` files should maintain sufficient revision
information to support a useful version history.

Where supported, users should be able to view:

- Revision number or identifier
- Date and time
- User
- Summary of changes
- Merge events
- Previous revisions

The version history should allow users to understand how a document
reached its current state.

### File-Based Collaboration Scope

File-based collaboration shall support collaboration on:

- Individual reports
- Audit Logs
- Executive Summaries
- Usability Reports
- Shared Tasks
- Shared Progress Logs
- Project information
- Organization information
- Other ART documents that are explicitly designed to support
  collaboration

### Shared ART Organization Folders

Introduce the concept of an **ART Organization Folder**.

An ART Organization Folder shall be a user-selected parent folder that
contains an organization's ART projects, reports, tasks, Progress Logs,
and related ART files.

For example:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
├── Website/
├── Mobile/
├── Internal Applications/
├── Shared Tasks/
├── Progress Logs/
└── Projects/
```

The Organization Folder shall serve as the collaboration boundary for
file-based organization functionality.

### Configuring an Organization Folder

Provide an accessible interface for selecting an Organization Folder.

Users shall be able to:

- Select an existing folder.
- Change the selected folder.
- Remove the configured Organization Folder.
- Enable or disable recursive subfolder discovery.
- Refresh organization information.
- View the currently configured organization.

The user should be able to select a folder through the operating
system's supported file-selection mechanism.

### Organization Folder Name

ART should allow the user to provide an organization name independently
from the physical folder name.

For example:

``` text
Folder:
Acme Co A11y Audits

Organization:
Acme Corporation
```

### Organization Manifest

When appropriate, ART should create a small organization manifest file
in the root of an ART Organization Folder.

The manifest shall identify the folder as an ART Organization Folder
without storing unnecessary personal or confidential information.

The manifest may contain:

- Organization ID
- Organization Name
- ART Organization format/version
- Creation metadata
- Organization-level configuration
- Supported collaboration settings

The manifest shall not contain user passwords or authentication
credentials.

### Organization ID

Each ART Organization Folder shall have a persistent Organization ID.

The Organization ID shall remain stable when the organization folder is
renamed or moved.

The Organization ID shall allow ART to distinguish between two
organizations with similar names.

### Subfolder Discovery

When recursive discovery is enabled, ART shall be able to discover
supported ART content in subfolders beneath the configured Organization
Folder.

Users should be able to control whether subfolders are included.

ART shall not assume that every file within the folder is an ART
document.

Only supported ART file types and recognized ART collaboration metadata
shall be processed.

### External Folder Permissions

ART shall not attempt to duplicate the permission system provided by the
external storage platform.

Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, SharePoint, network administrators, or
other storage providers shall remain responsible for controlling
physical access to the shared folder and files.

ART shall respect the access available to the current user.

If the user cannot access a file through the storage system, ART shall
not attempt to bypass those permissions.

### ART Collaboration Permissions

ART may provide application-level permissions for supported
collaborative objects.

These permissions shall remain separate from the external storage
provider's permissions.

For example, a user may have access to a shared folder but have limited
ART permissions for a particular collaborative object.

The implementation shall preserve compatibility with future server-based
ART permissions.

### Shared Tasks

File-based collaboration shall support shared Tasks stored within shared
`.art` documents or other supported ART task files.

Users shall be able to collaborate on:

- Task creation
- Task assignments
- Task reassignment
- Task status
- Task priority
- Due dates
- Task comments
- Task completion
- Other supported task properties

Changes shall be persisted in the shared file and become available to
other users after synchronization.

### Shared Progress Logs

File-based collaboration shall support shared Progress Logs.

Multiple users shall be able to:

- View shared Progress Logs.
- Update permitted task information.
- Add comments.
- Update task status where permitted.
- Assign and reassign tasks where permitted.
- View task assignments.
- Synchronize changes through the shared `.art` file.
- Resolve conflicts when simultaneous edits affect the same information.

### Organization Metrics

Organization Metrics shall be capable of using the contents of a
configured ART Organization Folder as a source of information.

ART shall be able to calculate or update metrics based on supported ART
documents contained within the organization folder and its configured
subfolders.

Metrics may include information from:

- Audit Logs
- Executive Summaries
- Usability Reports
- Findings
- WCAG Success Criteria
- Accessibility Standards
- Severity
- Priority
- Status
- Tasks
- Shared Tasks
- Progress Logs
- Project completion
- Testing progress
- Remediation progress
- Other supported ART data

### Organization Metrics Refresh

Organization Metrics shall provide an accessible mechanism to refresh
the information gathered from the Organization Folder.

The metrics interface shall clearly indicate that file-based metrics
represent the most recently synchronized and accessible ART files.

ART shall not imply that unsaved work in another user's ART session has
been included in the metrics.

### Organization Metrics and Subfolders

When configured to include subfolders, Organization Metrics shall
aggregate information from supported ART files throughout the configured
Organization Folder hierarchy.

Users should be able to determine which projects, folders, or files
contributed to a metric where practical.

### File-Based Collaboration and @Mentions

Introduce @mentions as a core capability of the file-based collaboration
infrastructure.

Users shall be able to @mention another known ART collaborator in
supported comments, notes, and other collaboration text areas.

The @mention system shall work without requiring an ART server when the
relevant users and collaboration metadata are available through the
shared ART document, shared project, or shared Organization Folder.

### @Mention Scope

@mentions shall work within:

- The same shared report.
- The same shared project.
- Shared Tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- A shared ART Organization Folder.
- Other supported file-based collaborative content.

A user shall only be able to select or resolve collaborators that ART
can identify within the applicable collaboration context.

### @Mention Identity

ART shall use the configured Display Name when presenting a collaborator
in the @mention interface.

The system shall associate the mention with the collaborator's
persistent ART User ID.

Where appropriate, the associated email address may be retained as
collaboration metadata for notification purposes.

### @Mention Entry

Supported comment, note, instruction, and collaboration text areas shall
allow users to enter an @ symbol and begin typing a collaborator's name
or display name.

ART should provide an accessible suggestion list of matching
collaborators.

The suggestion list shall be keyboard accessible and compatible with
screen readers.

Users shall be able to select a collaborator without relying solely on
pointer interaction.

### @Mention Storage

Mentions shall be stored as structured collaboration information rather
than relying solely on plain text.

The stored mention should associate:

- Mentioned User ID
- Display Name
- Relevant collaboration object
- Comment or text entry
- Timestamp
- Author

This shall allow ART to preserve the meaning of a mention if a user's
display name later changes.

### @Mention Notifications in File-Based Collaboration

File-based @mentions shall not depend on an ART server to exist.

When possible, ART shall provide local or file-based notification
information through the shared ART collaboration environment.

Where an Internet-connected notification mechanism becomes available
through future server functionality, @mentions may also generate email
notifications according to the applicable server-based collaboration
rules.

The architecture shall allow the file-based and server-based
notification systems to coexist without requiring the file-based
collaboration model to be redesigned.

### Shared User Directory

A shared Organization Folder may maintain collaboration identity
information for users who participate in that organization.

This information shall allow ART to resolve:

- Display Name
- Name
- Email Address, where appropriate
- Persistent ART User ID
- Job Title
- ART Role

The implementation shall minimize unnecessary exposure of personal
information.

### Collaborator Discovery

When opening a shared report, project, task collection, or Progress Log,
ART shall be able to identify collaborators associated with the shared
document or Organization Folder.

Collaborator information shall be available to supported features such
as:

- @mentions
- Task assignments
- Task reassignment
- Progress Log assignments
- Revision attribution
- Comments
- Change history
- Merge Changes

### Shared Collaboration Metadata

ART may maintain collaboration metadata within shared `.art` files
and/or the configured Organization Folder.

The metadata shall be designed to remain portable.

The collaboration metadata shall not require an ART server.

### Collaboration Without Authentication

Users shall be able to participate in file-based collaboration without
logging into an ART server.

Their configured ART User Profile shall provide the identity information
required for local attribution and file-based collaboration.

Authentication shall only be required for functionality that
specifically requires a server or authenticated external service.

### Compatibility With Epic 48

This epic shall remain compatible with Epic 48's passwordless
authentication architecture.

If a user later signs into an ART server, the server identity may be
associated with the user's existing local ART identity.

ART shall avoid creating duplicate identities when a valid association
can be established.

### Desktop and Web Compatibility

The file-based collaboration architecture shall be designed to support
both:

- ART Web
- Future ART Desktop

The underlying document, identity, revision, change-set, merge, and
collaboration models shall not depend on a particular user interface.

The future desktop application should be able to work naturally with
shared folders and network locations.

The web application shall use browser-supported file access mechanisms
where available and shall not assume unrestricted access to the user's
file system.

### Data Integrity

ART shall prioritize data integrity when working with shared `.art`
files.

ART shall:

- Avoid silently overwriting newer revisions.
- Detect stale versions.
- Preserve user changes during merge operations.
- Provide safe recovery options.
- Validate `.art` files before processing them.
- Handle incomplete or unavailable files gracefully.
- Warn users when a file cannot be safely merged.
- Avoid silently discarding changes.

### File Locking

ART shall not depend exclusively on file locking provided by an external
storage system.

External storage providers may implement locking or synchronization
behavior differently.

ART shall therefore use revision information and conflict detection as
the primary protection against lost changes.

### Cloud Synchronization Delays

ART shall account for the possibility that external storage
synchronization may be delayed.

If a user saves a file and immediately attempts to refresh from another
device or user session, ART shall handle the possibility that the newest
revision is not yet available.

ART shall provide clear messaging rather than reporting that no changes
exist when the storage provider has not yet synchronized the latest
version.

### Offline Behavior

File-based collaboration shall not eliminate ART's offline capabilities.

A user shall be able to:

- Open local `.art` files.
- Edit reports.
- Create findings.
- Work on tasks.
- Use supported ART features.
- Save local changes.

When the user later has access to the shared collaboration location, ART
shall be able to synchronize the document and identify conflicts when
appropriate.

### Error Handling

ART shall provide accessible error messages when:

- The shared file cannot be accessed.
- The file is locked or temporarily unavailable.
- The file has been deleted.
- The file has been moved.
- The file is corrupted.
- The file is an unsupported version.
- The file has conflicting revisions.
- The storage provider has not synchronized the newest revision.
- The user does not have sufficient file access.
- A merge cannot be completed automatically.

Error messages shall explain what happened and provide an appropriate
recovery action where possible.

### Accessibility Requirements

All functionality introduced by this epic shall meet ART's existing
accessibility requirements.

This includes:

- User Profile modal
- Organization Folder configuration
- Organization Metrics
- Collaborator selection
- @mention suggestions
- Revision history
- Merge Changes
- Refresh commands
- Collaboration notifications
- Error messages
- Shared Task interfaces
- Shared Progress Log interfaces

All controls shall be keyboard accessible.

All dynamic updates shall be communicated appropriately to assistive
technologies.

All dialogs shall have logical focus management.

All interactive controls shall have accessible names, roles, states, and
values.

### Menu and Command Integration

File-based collaboration commands shall be available through appropriate
ART command interfaces.

Where applicable, provide commands through:

- File menu
- Organization menu
- Tasks menu
- Progress Log menu
- Global context menu
- Context menus for applicable objects
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts

Commands may include:

- Refresh from Shared File
- Check for Updates
- View Version History
- View Changes
- Merge Changes
- Configure Organization Folder
- Refresh Organization Metrics
- View Collaborators
- Add @Mention
- Manage Collaboration Settings

### Customizable Keyboard Shortcuts

All appropriate file-based collaboration commands shall be available to
ART's customizable keyboard shortcut system.

Users shall be able to configure shortcuts for frequently used commands
such as:

- Refresh from Shared File
- Check for Updates
- View Changes
- Merge Changes
- View Version History
- Open Organization Metrics
- Add @Mention

Existing keyboard shortcuts shall not be disrupted.

### History Framework Integration

Actions performed through file-based collaboration shall integrate with
ART's existing History Framework where technically appropriate.

The History Framework shall allow supported actions to be undone and
redone.

This shall include applicable actions involving:

- Report changes
- Task changes
- Status changes
- Assignments
- Comments
- Progress Logs
- Merge operations
- Other collaborative document changes

The implementation shall distinguish between local undo/redo operations
and the creation of a new shared revision.

Undoing a change shall not silently rewrite historical shared revisions.

### Revision and Undo/Redo Relationship

Undo and Redo shall operate on the user's current working state.

When a user saves an undo-generated state, ART shall create an
appropriate new revision rather than deleting the historical record of
the previous revision.

### Security Considerations

Never store:

- Passwords
- Authentication secrets
- OAuth client secrets
- Access tokens
- Refresh tokens

inside `.art` files or collaboration metadata.

Sensitive authentication information shall remain under the control of
the applicable authentication or storage provider.

File-based collaboration metadata shall contain only information
necessary for collaboration.

### Future Server Compatibility

The file-based collaboration architecture shall be designed so that a
future ART server can use the same conceptual model.

The server-based system should be able to support:

- Document IDs
- User IDs
- Organization IDs
- Revision IDs
- Change sets
- Merge operations
- Collaborators
- @mentions
- Tasks
- Progress Logs
- Organization Metrics

The future server shall enhance the collaboration experience rather than
invalidate the file-based collaboration model.

### Migration From File-Based to Server-Based Collaboration

When ART eventually supports server-based collaboration, users should be
able to import or associate existing file-based ART projects with an
authenticated organization or workspace.

Existing:

- Reports
- Revisions
- User attribution
- Tasks
- Progress Logs
- Collaboration metadata
- Organization information

should be preserved where technically possible.

### No Vendor Lock-In

File-based collaboration shall not require users to adopt a specific
storage provider.

ART shall not require Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, or another
provider solely to use this functionality.

Organizations shall be free to choose the storage infrastructure
appropriate to their security, privacy, accessibility, and operational
requirements.

### Validation

Verify that:

- A user can configure their ART User Profile.
- Profile information persists across sessions.
- Profile information can be edited later.
- A unique persistent ART User ID is generated.
- Users can create and use ART without logging in.
- A user can save an `.art` file to a shared folder.
- Another user can open the same `.art` file.
- The second user can see the first user's saved changes.
- The second user can make additional changes and save them.
- The first user can subsequently open or refresh the file and see the
  second user's changes.
- Two users can have the same `.art` file open simultaneously.
- Users can independently make changes while working.
- Saving detects when the shared file has been modified since the
  current user's working revision.
- ART does not silently overwrite newer shared changes.
- Non-conflicting changes are merged automatically.
- Conflicting changes are identified correctly.
- Merge Changes opens when manual conflict resolution is required.
- Users can resolve conflicts without losing unrelated changes.
- The resulting merged revision is saved correctly.
- A subsequent user can retrieve the merged revision.
- Revision history correctly identifies applicable users and changes.
- A configured Organization Folder can be selected and changed.
- Supported `.art` files in configured subfolders can be discovered.
- Organization Metrics can be calculated from discovered ART files.
- Organization Metrics can be refreshed.
- Shared Tasks can use the file-based collaboration model.
- Shared Progress Logs can use the file-based collaboration model.
- Task assignments and changes persist across synchronization.
- @mentions can be entered in supported collaboration fields.
- Collaborators can be selected through an accessible @mention
  interface.
- @mentions remain associated with the correct ART User ID.
- @mentions work within shared reports.
- @mentions work within shared projects.
- @mentions work within shared Tasks and Progress Logs.
- @mentions can operate within a shared Organization Folder.
- User identity information is not unnecessarily exposed.
- File-based collaboration works without an ART server.
- Local ART functionality continues to work without a shared folder.
- Offline editing remains functional.
- Cloud synchronization delays are handled safely.
- File locking does not cause silent data loss.
- Corrupt, unavailable, deleted, or unsupported files are handled
  accessibly.
- File-based collaboration commands are available through appropriate
  menus and context menus.
- Applicable commands can be assigned customizable keyboard shortcuts.
- Undo and Redo work correctly with supported collaboration-related
  actions.
- Existing Merge Changes functionality remains functional.
- Existing ART functionality does not regress.

### Definition of Done

This epic is complete when ART provides a functional, server-independent
foundation for file-based collaboration in which multiple users can
safely work with the same `.art` documents through a shared or
synchronized folder.

The implementation shall support persistent user identity, document
identity, revision tracking, change detection, automatic non-conflicting
merges, conflict detection, Merge Changes integration, shared
Organization Folders, Organization Metrics, Shared Tasks, Shared
Progress Logs, and @mentions.

The resulting architecture shall allow ART to provide meaningful
collaborative functionality without requiring users to create an ART
account or use an ART server.

The implementation shall also provide a clear architectural foundation
for future server-based collaboration, authentication, real-time
synchronization, organizational administration, and enterprise
functionality without requiring the file-based collaboration model to be
discarded or fundamentally redesigned.

## Epic 50 — Authenticated Users, Organization Membership, Roles, Authorization, and Multi-Device Identity

### Epic Overview

Implement the authenticated-user, organization, authorization, and
multi-device identity infrastructure required to support ART's
server-dependent collaboration, organization management, shared
workspaces, shared projects, shared reports, shared tasks, shared
Progress Logs, Organization Metrics, notifications, @mentions, and other
multi-user capabilities.

This epic completes the foundational pieces that were intentionally
deferred in **Epic 42, Parts 5, 7, and 8** because ART did not yet have
authenticated users, organization membership, roles, or an authorization
policy service.

This epic also establishes a secure mechanism for recognizing the same
ART user across multiple devices and multiple ART installations,
including:

- ART web applications
- ART desktop applications
- Different browsers
- Different computers
- Different operating systems
- Different ART installations
- Online/server-connected environments
- Offline/file-based collaboration environments

The implementation shall build upon:

- **Epic 48 — Secure Login, Passwordless Authentication, and User
  Sign-Up**
- **Epic 49 — File-Based Collaboration, User Identity, and Organization
  Folders**

ART shall continue to support its local-first, no-login operating model.

A user shall **not** be required to authenticate simply to use ART's
fundamental local functionality.

Authentication, organization membership, and authorization shall become
necessary only when a user accesses functionality that requires a known
authenticated identity, organization membership, server-side
collaboration, protected organizational resources, or other
server-dependent capabilities.

### Goals

This epic shall:

- Establish authenticated ART user identities.
- Connect authenticated identities to ART's persistent User ID.
- Establish organizations as first-class ART entities.
- Allow users to belong to one or more organizations.
- Establish organization membership records.
- Establish organization roles.
- Establish resource-level authorization.
- Create a centralized Authorization Policy Service.
- Provide a consistent mechanism for determining whether a user may
  perform an action.
- Support organization administrators and delegated administrative
  roles.
- Support workspace, project, report, task, Progress Log, and
  collaboration permissions.
- Provide a foundation for server-based collaboration.
- Preserve compatibility with file-based collaboration.
- Provide a secure mechanism for linking multiple ART installations to
  the same user identity.
- Allow a user to establish their ART identity on additional devices.
- Allow file-based ART installations to recognize a previously
  established user identity.
- Support secure device-to-device identity linking without requiring a
  server.
- Prevent unauthorized users from impersonating another ART user.
- Provide secure recovery and unlinking mechanisms.
- Provide an architecture suitable for future enterprise deployments.
- Provide auditable identity, authorization, membership, and
  device-linking events.

### Relationship to Epic 48

Epic 48 establishes ART's authentication and passwordless sign-in
system.

Epic 50 shall consume the authenticated identity established by Epic 48
rather than creating a separate authentication mechanism.

Epic 48 remains responsible for:

- Account creation
- Sign-up
- Passwordless authentication
- OAuth/OIDC provider authentication
- Authentication sessions
- Authentication security
- Account recovery
- Authentication lifecycle

Epic 50 is responsible for:

- User identity within ART
- Organization membership
- Roles
- Permissions
- Authorization
- Device identity
- Multi-device identity linking
- File-based identity verification
- Resource ownership and access

Authentication answers:

> Who is this user?

Authorization answers:

> What is this user allowed to do?

Device identity answers:

> Is this ART installation an authorized installation belonging to this
> user?

### Relationship to Epic 49

Epic 49 establishes:

- Local ART identity
- ART User ID
- File-based collaboration
- Organization Folders
- Organization IDs
- Document IDs
- Revision IDs
- Collaborators
- File-based @mentions
- User profile information

Epic 50 shall provide authenticated organization identity, server-side
authorization, and multi-device identity without invalidating Epic 49.

File-based collaboration shall continue to function without
authentication.

### Local-First Operation

ART shall remain fully usable without authentication.

Unauthenticated users shall retain access to fundamental capabilities
such as:

- Creating reports
- Editing reports
- Saving `.art` files
- Opening `.art` files
- Importing and exporting supported formats
- Using the WCAG Lookup Tool
- Configuring report templates
- Performing accessibility testing
- Using local Tasks and To Do functionality
- Using local Progress Logs
- Using other features that do not require server access

ART shall clearly communicate when a feature requires authentication.

The application shall not unnecessarily block local functionality merely
because the user is not signed in.

### Authenticated ART User

An authenticated ART User shall have a server-recognized identity.

The authenticated identity shall include, at minimum:

- User ID
- Email address
- Display name
- Account status
- Authentication provider information
- Account creation timestamp
- Last authentication timestamp
- Associated ART User ID

Additional profile information may include:

- Name
- Job title
- ART role
- Accessibility preferences
- Notification preferences
- Other non-sensitive profile information

### Persistent ART User ID

Each ART user shall have a persistent, globally unique ART User ID.

The ART User ID shall not depend solely on:

- Name
- Display name
- Email address
- Authentication provider
- Device
- Browser
- Operating system

Changing a user's:

- Name
- Display name
- Email address
- Job title
- Authentication provider

shall not create a new ART identity.

### Identity Association

When an authenticated user signs in from an ART installation that
already contains a local ART User ID, ART should associate the local
identity with the authenticated account when the identity can be safely
established.

The association shall require appropriate safeguards against accidental
identity collisions.

ART shall not automatically merge two identities merely because they
have the same:

- Name
- Display name
- Email address

### Multi-Device Identity

ART shall provide a secure mechanism for associating multiple ART
installations with the same ART User identity.

A single user may have:

- ART on a desktop computer
- ART on a laptop
- ART in a browser
- ART in another browser
- ART on a second operating system
- ART on a future mobile or tablet application
- Multiple desktop installations

All authorized installations shall be capable of being recognized as
belonging to the same ART user.

### Device Identity

Each ART installation capable of being linked to an account shall have a
unique device/installation identity.

The device identity shall be generated securely and shall not simply
consist of:

- Computer name
- Browser name
- Operating system
- IP address
- MAC address
- User-selected device name

The device identity should use cryptographic keys where technically
practical.

### Cryptographic Device Identity

When a device is registered with an ART identity, ART should generate a
device-specific cryptographic key pair.

The private key shall remain protected on the device.

The corresponding public key may be associated with the user's ART
account or file-based identity.

The private key shall never be uploaded to the server.

### Personal Identity Token / Linking Passphrase

In the ART Settings area established by Epic 49, provide a section for
**Identity and Device Linking**.

This area shall allow the user to establish a personal identity-linking
credential.

The interface may provide a field such as:

> Personal ART Identity Code

or

> Device Linking Passphrase

The user may enter a unique value of their choosing, or ART may generate
a high-entropy value for them.

However, this value shall **not be treated as the user's sole permanent
authentication credential**.

It shall instead be used as part of a secure device-linking process.

### Security Requirement for the Personal Token

ART shall not store the user's personal identity token/passphrase in
plain text.

The system shall not transmit the raw token unnecessarily.

Where a server is involved, the token shall be processed using an
appropriate cryptographic construction.

The implementation should preferably use the token to unlock or
authorize a cryptographic device-linking operation rather than using the
token directly as a long-term password.

### Recommended Token Model

The preferred architecture is:

1.  The user's primary ART installation establishes the user's
    authenticated identity.
2.  ART generates or protects a cryptographic identity key.
3.  The user initiates **Link Another Device**.
4.  ART generates a temporary, short-lived device-linking code or
    pairing mechanism.
5.  The second ART installation receives the code or pairing
    information.
6.  The user confirms the pairing.
7.  The second device generates its own device key pair.
8.  ART associates the new device public key with the same ART User ID.
9.  The temporary pairing credential expires.
10. Future authentication uses the registered device/authenticator
    rather than repeatedly transmitting the permanent personal token.

This approach is preferable to using a manually chosen passphrase as the
sole identity authenticator.

NIST's current authentication guidance specifically supports binding
multiple authenticators to the same subscriber account and describes
cross-endpoint authenticator binding.

### User-Selected Passphrase Support

If ART supports a user-selected identity passphrase, the interface shall
clearly explain that:

- It should be unique to ART.
- It should not be reused as another account password.
- It should not be shared with other people.
- It should not be used as the only protection for highly sensitive
  server operations.
- Losing it may require account/device recovery.
- A randomly generated value may provide stronger security.

A passphrase is a memorized secret, not equivalent to possession of a
cryptographic device key.

### Server-Based Device Linking

When a server is available, a user shall be able to link another ART
installation to their authenticated account.

The preferred workflow shall be:

1.  User authenticates to ART on an existing trusted device.
2.  User opens **Settings → Identity and Device Linking**.
3.  User selects **Link Another Device**.
4.  ART generates a temporary device-linking code or equivalent secure
    pairing mechanism.
5.  User opens ART on the new device.
6.  User selects **Link to Existing ART Account**.
7.  User enters the temporary linking code or uses another supported
    pairing mechanism.
8.  ART verifies the request.
9.  The new device generates its own cryptographic device identity.
10. The new device is associated with the same ART User ID.
11. The user receives confirmation that the device has been linked.

### Device-Linking Expiration

Temporary linking codes shall:

- Expire automatically.
- Be usable only for their intended linking operation.
- Not function as permanent login credentials.
- Be invalidated after successful use.
- Be invalidated when canceled.
- Have sufficient randomness to prevent guessing.

### Device Linking Without a Server

ART shall also support device identity linking through the file-based
collaboration infrastructure established by Epic 49.

This allows users to establish a relationship between ART installations
even when no server is available.

The file-based process shall not pretend to provide the same security
properties as an authenticated server.

Instead, it shall establish a cryptographically verifiable relationship
between ART identities and devices.

### File-Based Identity Handshake

When two ART installations exchange a shared `.art` file, the file may
contain appropriate identity metadata.

The metadata may include:

- ART User ID
- Device ID
- Public identity key
- Public device key
- Display name
- Organization ID where applicable
- Identity metadata version
- Signature information
- Revision information

Private keys and secrets shall never be stored in the `.art` file.

### File-Based Identity Verification

When a user opens a `.art` file containing a previously encountered ART
identity, ART shall compare the identity information with locally known
identities.

ART may determine that:

- The identity is known and trusted.
- The identity is known but the device is new.
- The identity is unknown.
- The identity has changed unexpectedly.
- The identity cannot be verified.

### File-Based "Handshake"

ART shall provide a secure file-based identity handshake mechanism.

For example:

1.  User A has an established ART identity.
2.  User A opens a shared `.art` file.
3.  User B opens the same file on another device.
4.  ART detects User B's identity information.
5.  ART compares the cryptographic identity metadata.
6.  ART determines whether the identity matches a previously trusted ART
    identity.
7.  If appropriate, ART associates the new device with the same user
    identity.
8.  The identity relationship is recorded in the local ART identity
    store.

The handshake shall require appropriate user confirmation when the
identity cannot be safely verified automatically.

### Trust Confirmation

When ART encounters a new device claiming to belong to an existing ART
User ID, the user shall receive a clear confirmation request.

For example:

> A new ART device is attempting to use the identity "Jane Smith." Do
> you recognize and trust this device?

The user shall be able to:

- Trust
- Reject
- Cancel
- View identity details

### Identity Mismatch

If an ART file contains an identity that conflicts with the locally
known identity, ART shall not silently overwrite the existing identity.

Instead, ART shall provide an appropriate warning.

For example:

> This report contains changes associated with an ART identity that does
> not match the identity currently associated with this device.

The user shall be able to investigate the identity before accepting
changes.

### Identity Conflict Protection

The identity system shall prevent an attacker from simply changing:

- Name
- Email
- User ID
- Device ID

inside a file and thereby impersonating another user.

Identity information shall be protected using cryptographic signatures
or another appropriate integrity mechanism.

### Multiple Devices Per User

A user may register multiple devices.

The system shall maintain a device registry containing, as appropriate:

- Device ID
- User ID
- Device name
- Platform
- ART version
- First registration date
- Last activity
- Device status
- Public key
- Trust status

### Device Management

Authenticated users shall be able to view their registered devices.

The interface should allow users to:

- View devices
- Rename devices
- View device type
- View last-used information
- Revoke a device
- Re-link a device when appropriate

### Device Revocation

Users shall be able to revoke a device.

Revoking a device shall:

- Prevent future server authentication using that device identity.
- Invalidate applicable device credentials.
- Remove its trusted status.
- Preserve the user's account.
- Preserve other registered devices.

### Lost or Stolen Device

A user shall be able to revoke a lost or stolen device without deleting
their ART account.

Server-connected ART installations shall recognize the revocation.

File-based ART installations shall recognize the revocation when they
next receive updated identity information where technically possible.

### Device Re-Registration

After a device is revoked, the user may re-register it through an
appropriate authenticated process.

A revoked device shall not automatically regain trust merely because the
same computer or browser is used again.

### Device Names

Users should be able to assign human-readable device names.

Examples:

- Work Desktop
- Home Laptop
- Surface Laptop
- Testing Mac
- ART Development PC

Device names shall not be used as authentication credentials.

### Cross-Browser Identity

ART shall support linking separate browser installations.

For example:

- Chrome on Desktop
- Edge on Desktop
- Firefox on Desktop

may all be associated with the same ART User account.

Browser-specific storage shall not be assumed to represent the user's
permanent identity.

### Web and Desktop Identity

A user's web-based ART installation and desktop ART installation shall
be capable of representing the same ART User identity.

The implementation shall not require the web and desktop applications to
use identical storage mechanisms.

### Device Linking and Passwordless Authentication

Device linking shall work with Epic 48's passwordless authentication
model.

The system should favor:

- Passkeys
- Hardware-backed authenticators
- Secure device keys
- OAuth/OIDC authentication
- Temporary device-binding codes

over requiring users to repeatedly type a permanent secret.

### Personal Token as Recovery/Pairing Mechanism

If the personal identity token is retained as part of the design, it may
serve as:

- A device-linking secret
- A local identity-unlock mechanism
- A recovery mechanism where appropriate

It shall not automatically grant full server access without the
appropriate authentication and authorization checks.

### No Plaintext Authentication Secrets

ART shall never store:

- Passwords
- Authentication secrets
- Personal identity tokens
- Device private keys

in plaintext.

Appropriate secure storage mechanisms shall be used.

### Organization Entity

Organizations shall be first-class server-side entities.

An organization shall have:

- Organization ID
- Organization name
- Organization status
- Creation timestamp
- Owner or initial administrator
- Organization configuration
- Membership records
- Role definitions or assigned roles
- Authorization policies
- Applicable subscription or service information when required in the
  future

### Organization Creation

An authenticated user shall be able to create an organization when
permitted.

The user creating an organization shall become its initial organization
administrator/owner.

The exact role name may evolve, but the initial creator shall receive
sufficient privileges to administer the organization.

### Organization Membership

Users shall be able to belong to organizations.

A membership shall associate:

- User ID
- Organization ID
- Organization role(s)
- Membership status
- Membership creation timestamp
- Membership modification timestamp
- Invited-by information where applicable

### Membership Status

Organization memberships shall support statuses such as:

- Invited
- Pending
- Active
- Suspended
- Removed

Inactive memberships shall not provide normal access to organization
resources.

### Multiple Organizations

A user shall be able to belong to multiple organizations.

The user shall be able to select the organization in which they are
currently working.

ART shall never assume that membership in one organization grants access
to another organization.

### Organization Context

When an authenticated user performs an organization-scoped action, ART
shall establish the applicable organization context.

Authorization shall always evaluate access within the correct
organization.

### Organization Switching

Users who belong to multiple organizations shall be able to switch
organization context through an accessible interface.

Switching organizations shall update available:

- Workspaces
- Projects
- Reports
- Tasks
- Progress Logs
- Organization Metrics
- Members
- Administration options

### Organization Isolation

Organization data shall be logically isolated.

A user who belongs to Organization A shall not be able to access
Organization B's protected resources unless independently authorized
through Organization B.

This isolation shall apply to:

- Reports
- Projects
- Workspaces
- Tasks
- Progress Logs
- Organization Metrics
- Members
- Collaboration data
- Attachments
- Settings
- Other organization-owned resources

### Organization Roles

ART shall support organization roles.

At minimum, the authorization architecture shall support:

- Organization Owner
- Organization Administrator
- Editor
- Member
- Viewer

The implementation shall allow additional roles to be introduced without
redesigning the authorization system.

### Role Characteristics

Roles shall represent permission bundles rather than hard-coded
application behavior.

**Organization Owner**

May generally:

- Manage the organization
- Manage administrators
- Manage organization settings
- Manage members
- Manage roles
- Manage authorization policies
- Access organization resources

**Organization Administrator**

May generally:

- Manage members
- Assign supported roles
- Manage organization resources
- Configure applicable organization settings
- Manage collaboration resources where permitted

**Editor**

May generally:

- Create and modify permitted organization resources
- Edit reports and projects
- Manage permitted tasks
- Participate in collaboration

**Member**

May generally:

- Access resources granted to members
- Perform assigned work
- Update permitted tasks
- Add permitted comments
- Participate in collaboration

**Viewer**

May generally:

- View resources to which they have access
- Review reports and project information
- Have limited or no modification privileges

These are baseline roles only. The Authorization Policy Service shall
determine actual permissions.

### Custom Roles

The authorization architecture shall support future custom organization
roles.

Examples include:

- Accessibility Tester
- Project Manager
- QA Tester
- Reviewer
- Report Author
- Client
- Auditor
- Read-Only Stakeholder

Custom roles shall be composed of defined permissions rather than
arbitrary application logic.

### Role Assignment

Authorized users shall be able to assign roles to organization members.

ART shall:

- Verify the acting user's permission.
- Verify that the target user belongs to the organization.
- Record the role change.
- Apply the authorization change.
- Record an audit event.

### Preventing Privilege Escalation

Users shall not be able to grant themselves permissions.

A user shall not be able to assign a role that exceeds their authority
unless explicitly permitted by policy.

### Role Removal

Authorized users shall be able to remove or change roles.

ART shall prevent an organization from accidentally losing its final
required administrative authority.

### Authorization Policy Service

Create a centralized **Authorization Policy Service**.

The Authorization Policy Service shall be the authoritative mechanism
for determining whether an authenticated user may perform a protected
action.

Application components shall not independently implement conflicting
authorization rules.

### Authorization Decision

The Authorization Policy Service shall evaluate:

- Authenticated User ID
- Organization ID
- Membership status
- Organization role
- Resource type
- Resource ID
- Resource ownership
- Resource membership
- Requested action
- Applicable policy
- Resource-specific permissions
- Security context

The service shall return an authorization decision such as:

- Allowed
- Denied

Where useful, it may also return a machine-readable reason code.

### Permission Model

Permissions should follow an action-oriented model.

Examples include:

- `organization.view`
- `organization.manage`
- `organization.members.view`
- `organization.members.invite`
- `organization.members.remove`
- `organization.roles.view`
- `organization.roles.assign`
- `organization.roles.manage`
- `workspace.view`
- `workspace.create`
- `workspace.edit`
- `workspace.delete`
- `project.view`
- `project.create`
- `project.edit`
- `project.delete`
- `report.view`
- `report.create`
- `report.edit`
- `report.delete`
- `report.share`
- `task.view`
- `task.create`
- `task.edit`
- `task.assign`
- `task.reassign`
- `task.comment`
- `progress_log.view`
- `progress_log.create`
- `progress_log.edit`
- `progress_log.assign`
- `metrics.view`
- `metrics.manage`

The final permission catalog shall be extensible.

### Resource-Based Authorization

Authorization shall support resource-level permissions.

A user may have permission to edit one project but only view another.

The architecture shall support:

- Organization-level access
- Workspace-level access
- Project-level access
- Report-level access
- Task-level access
- Progress Log-level access

### Ownership

Supported resources may have an owner.

Ownership shall not automatically override organization-level security
policies.

The Authorization Policy Service shall determine whether ownership
grants the applicable permission.

### Shared Resources

Resources may be explicitly shared with users or groups.

The authorization system shall support resource sharing without
requiring access for every organization member.

### Invitations

Authorized organization administrators shall be able to invite users to
an organization.

An invitation shall contain:

- Organization
- Invited email address
- Inviting user
- Intended role
- Invitation status
- Expiration
- Creation timestamp

Invitations shall not automatically grant access until accepted.

### Invitation Security

Organization invitations shall:

- Use secure, unpredictable identifiers.
- Expire after a defined period.
- Be invalidated when canceled.
- Avoid unnecessary disclosure of organization information.
- Be associated with the intended organization.
- Require appropriate authentication before membership is established.

### Accepting an Invitation

A user receiving an organization invitation shall be able to:

1.  Authenticate or create an ART account.
2.  Review the organization.
3.  Review the offered role.
4.  Accept or decline.
5.  Become a member after successful acceptance.

### Existing Authenticated Users

If the invited email address already corresponds to an ART account, the
invitation shall associate with that existing account rather than
creating a duplicate account.

### Account Deactivation

Authorized administrators shall be able to suspend or deactivate
organization access without necessarily deleting the user's ART account.

### Account Deletion

Account deletion shall be handled separately from organization
membership removal.

The implementation shall account for:

- Ownership
- Authored content
- Audit history
- Device registrations
- Organization memberships
- Other dependencies

### Authorization API

The Authorization Policy Service shall expose a well-defined internal
API.

The API shall support questions such as:

- Can this user view this resource?
- Can this user edit this resource?
- Can this user delete this resource?
- Can this user assign this task?
- Can this user invite a member?
- Can this user change this role?
- Can this user manage this organization?

### Server-Side Enforcement

Authorization shall be enforced on the server.

Client-side UI hiding shall never be considered sufficient
authorization.

### Defense in Depth

ART shall use multiple protection layers:

- Authentication
- Organization membership validation
- Authorization policy evaluation
- Resource ownership/sharing checks
- Server-side enforcement
- Input validation
- Audit logging
- Secure session handling
- Appropriate rate limiting

### Permission-Aware User Interface

The ART interface shall adapt appropriately to the authenticated user's
permissions.

Permission-sensitive commands shall be handled consistently across:

- Menubar
- Context menus
- Global context menu
- Toolbar commands
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Command palette

A user shall not be able to bypass authorization by invoking an
alternate command path.

### Authorization Failure

Unauthorized actions shall:

- Clearly indicate that access is denied.
- Avoid exposing sensitive information.
- Explain the reason when appropriate.
- Provide a recovery option when possible.

### Default Deny

The Authorization Policy Service shall follow a **default-deny**
principle.

If authorization cannot be established, access shall be denied.

### Least Privilege

ART shall follow least-privilege principles.

Users should receive only the permissions necessary for their
responsibilities.

### Separation of Duties

The authorization architecture shall support separation of duties for
workflows where appropriate.

### Audit Logging

Authorization-sensitive actions shall be auditable.

Events shall include:

- Organization creation
- Invitation creation
- Invitation acceptance
- Membership activation
- Membership suspension
- Membership removal
- Role assignment
- Role changes
- Role removal
- Policy changes
- Ownership changes
- Device linking
- Device unlinking
- Device revocation
- Identity association
- Other security-sensitive administrative actions

Audit records should include:

- Actor
- Organization
- Action
- Target
- Timestamp
- Result
- Relevant metadata

### Device-Linking Audit Events

The following should be auditable:

- Device registration
- Device linking
- Device unlinking
- Device revocation
- Identity association
- Identity conflict
- Trust acceptance
- Trust rejection
- Device recovery

Sensitive authentication secrets shall not be written into audit logs.

### Authorization Policy Changes

Only authorized users shall change authorization policies.

Policy changes shall be auditable.

The system shall avoid partially applied policy changes.

### File-Based Collaboration Relationship

File-based collaboration from Epic 49 shall remain available without
server authentication.

When an authenticated user opens a file-based collaborative document
associated with an organization, ART may associate the authenticated
identity with the existing local ART identity.

Server authorization shall not invalidate file-based collaboration.

### File-Based and Server-Based Permissions

The system shall distinguish between:

- File-system permissions
- File-based ART collaboration metadata
- Server-side ART organization permissions

Opening a file shall not automatically grant server organization
permissions.

Server membership shall not automatically grant access to arbitrary
files.

### File-Based Device Linking

The file-based collaboration system shall provide a way to associate
multiple devices with the same ART User ID.

For example:

- Device A establishes User A's identity.
- Device B opens a trusted `.art` file containing User A's signed
  identity information.
- Device B initiates a device-linking operation.
- User A confirms the identity relationship.
- Device B generates its own device identity.
- Device B becomes an authorized installation associated with User A.

### Offline Identity Limitations

ART shall clearly distinguish between:

**Cryptographically verified identity**

and

**Server-authenticated identity**

A file-based handshake may establish that two installations possess
credentials associated with the same ART identity, but it cannot
independently guarantee that the human operating the device is the
legitimate account owner.

Therefore, file-based identity linking shall use appropriate trust
confirmation.

### File-Based Identity Trust

The user shall be able to decide whether a new identity/device should be
trusted.

ART shall avoid silently trusting a newly encountered device merely
because it claims the same name or email address.

### File-Based Identity Metadata Integrity

Identity metadata inside `.art` files shall be protected against
unauthorized modification.

Where practical, ART shall use digital signatures.

### Migration From File-Based Identity

When a user signs into an ART server for the first time, ART should
provide a safe mechanism to associate the authenticated account with the
local ART User ID.

The process shall clearly communicate what identity is being associated.

### Organization Association for Existing Files

When a shared `.art` file is associated with an organization, ART may
allow an authorized user to associate the document with the
authenticated organization.

### Server-Dependent Features

The following may require authentication and organization authorization:

- Server-based collaboration
- Shared server workspaces
- Organization administration
- Member management
- Shared projects
- Shared reports
- Server-based Tasks
- Server-based Progress Logs
- Organization Metrics
- Server-based notifications
- Server-based @mentions
- Enterprise integrations

### Session Management

Authenticated sessions shall use Epic 48's secure session architecture.

ART shall:

- Detect expired sessions.
- Handle revoked sessions.
- Prevent unauthorized session reuse.
- Prompt for reauthentication when required.
- Preserve unsaved local work.

### Authorization Cache

If authorization information is cached client-side, it shall have
appropriate expiration and invalidation behavior.

Security-sensitive changes shall take effect promptly.

### Permission Revocation

When permission is removed, ART shall prevent continued access as soon
as reasonably possible.

### Multi-Device Session Management

Each linked device shall have its own device/session credentials.

Revoking one device shall not automatically revoke all other trusted
devices unless the user chooses to do so.

ART should provide a **Sign Out All Devices** or equivalent security
command.

### Emergency Account Protection

Authenticated users should have a way to:

- Revoke all devices
- Revoke selected devices
- End active sessions
- Regenerate device credentials
- Review recent devices

### Organization Metrics

Organization Metrics shall only include information the authenticated
user is authorized to access.

A user shall not be able to infer protected information through metrics.

### Integration With Tasks

The authorization system shall support:

- View task
- Create task
- Edit task
- Assign task
- Reassign task
- Change status
- Change priority
- Comment
- Delete task

### Integration With Shared Progress Logs

The authorization system shall support:

- View Progress Log
- Edit Progress Log
- Add comments
- Update assigned task status
- Assign tasks
- Reassign tasks
- Modify tasks
- Manage Progress Log membership

### Integration With Reports

The authorization system shall support:

- View reports
- Create reports
- Edit reports
- Delete reports
- Share reports
- Export reports
- Manage report permissions

### Integration With Projects and Workspaces

The authorization system shall support:

- Workspace membership
- Project membership
- Project roles
- Workspace roles
- Project-level permissions
- Workspace-level permissions

### Integration With @Mentions

Server-based @mentions shall resolve against authenticated organization
