members where applicable.

File-based @mentions shall continue to work within:

- Shared reports
- Shared projects
- Shared organization folders
- Other file-based collaboration contexts

ART shall associate @mentions with the appropriate ART User ID whenever
the identity can be safely established.

### @Mention Identity Resolution

ART shall not resolve an @mention solely from a display name.

Where possible, identity resolution shall use:

- ART User ID
- Organization membership
- Email address
- Trusted device identity
- Cryptographically protected identity metadata

### Notifications

Notifications shall be authorization-aware.

ART shall not deliver protected information to users who no longer have
access to the associated organization or resource.

This applies to:

- @mentions
- Task assignments
- Progress Log updates
- Project updates
- Report changes
- Collaboration notifications

### Future Enterprise Identity Integration

The architecture should allow future support for:

- Microsoft Entra ID
- Google Workspace
- Other OIDC providers
- SAML-based enterprise identity providers

External providers shall authenticate users; ART shall remain
responsible for ART-specific organization membership and authorization.

### Future SCIM Support

The architecture should allow future implementation of SCIM or
equivalent provisioning for:

- User provisioning
- User deprovisioning
- Group synchronization
- Role/group mapping

### API and Database Architecture

Implement persistent server-side storage for:

- Users
- Organizations
- Memberships
- Roles
- Permissions
- Policies
- Invitations
- Device registrations
- Device public keys
- Identity associations
- Resource ownership
- Resource sharing
- Audit events
- Other authorization metadata

### Database Integrity

Database constraints shall ensure that:

- Memberships reference valid users.
- Memberships reference valid organizations.
- Role assignments reference valid roles.
- Resource permissions reference valid resources.
- Device registrations reference valid users.
- Revoked devices cannot remain active.
- Deleted organizations do not leave orphaned authorization records.

### Authorization Policy Versioning

The Authorization Policy Service should support policy versioning so
that future permission changes do not make historical authorization
records ambiguous.

### Policy Testing

Automated tests shall cover:

- Allowed actions
- Denied actions
- Organization isolation
- Role inheritance
- Resource permissions
- Membership status
- Suspended users
- Removed users
- Invitation expiration
- Permission revocation
- Cross-organization access
- Direct API access
- Privilege escalation

### Device Identity Testing

Automated and functional tests shall cover:

- First device registration
- Second-device registration
- Multiple devices
- Multiple browsers
- Web-to-desktop linking
- Desktop-to-web linking
- Cross-platform linking
- Device revocation
- Device re-registration
- Lost-device scenarios
- Identity mismatch
- File-based identity handshake
- File-based identity conflict
- Cryptographic signature validation
- Invalid identity metadata
- Tampered `.art` files
- Expired pairing codes
- Reused pairing codes
- Unauthorized device-link attempts

### Security Testing

Perform testing for:

- Authentication bypass
- Authorization bypass
- Privilege escalation
- Horizontal privilege escalation
- Vertical privilege escalation
- Cross-organization access
- IDOR-style resource access
- Session misuse
- Device impersonation
- Device credential theft
- Token guessing
- Token replay
- Pairing-code replay
- Identity spoofing
- File identity tampering
- Malicious `.art` files
- Unauthorized device registration
- Unauthorized device revocation
- API authorization failures

### Accessibility Testing

Test all identity, device-linking, and authorization interfaces with:

- JAWS
- NVDA
- Narrator
- VoiceOver
- TalkBack
- ChromeVox where applicable
- Braille displays
- Keyboard-only interaction
- Zoom and magnification
- High contrast
- Other supported ART visual settings

### Identity Interface Accessibility

The following shall be accessible:

- Identity settings
- Device-linking controls
- Identity token/passphrase fields
- Pairing-code fields
- Device lists
- Device revocation commands
- Identity confirmation dialogs
- Trust dialogs
- Organization switcher
- Member management
- Role management
- Invitation dialogs
- Permission management
- Authorization errors

### Error and Edge-Case Testing

Test situations including:

- Session expiration
- User removal
- Role changes
- Organization suspension
- Resource deletion
- Cross-organization access
- Expired invitations
- Multiple organizations
- Organization switching
- Network failure
- Authorization service failure
- Device loss
- Device theft
- Device revocation
- Identity mismatch
- File tampering
- Offline device linking
- Simultaneous device registration

### Authorization Service Failure

If the Authorization Policy Service is unavailable, ART shall fail
securely.

Protected server-side operations shall not automatically be permitted.

Local functionality that does not require server authorization shall
remain available.

### Availability and Resilience

The authorization infrastructure should support:

- Health monitoring
- Logging
- Error reporting
- Appropriate caching
- Recovery
- Service restart
- Database backup
- Database restoration

### Administration Interface

Provide an accessible organization administration area for authorized
users.

The administration area should provide:

- Organization information
- Members
- Invitations
- Roles
- Permissions
- Policies
- Devices where applicable
- Audit events

### Organization Member Management

Authorized administrators shall be able to:

- View members
- Invite members
- Resend invitations
- Cancel invitations
- Change roles
- Suspend members
- Remove members
- View membership status

### Role Management Interface

If custom roles are implemented, authorized administrators shall be able
to:

- Create roles
- Edit roles
- Duplicate roles
- Assign permissions
- Remove permissions
- Delete unused roles

### Permission Management Interface

The permission-management interface shall provide understandable
descriptions of permissions.

Internal permission identifiers may be available for administrators or
developers but shall not be the only explanation.

### Device Management Interface

Provide an accessible interface where users can:

- View linked devices
- Name devices
- View device type
- View platform
- View last-used information
- Link another device
- Revoke a device
- Revoke all devices
- Review trust status

### Identity Settings in ART

The Settings area introduced by Epic 49 shall contain an **Identity and
Device Linking** section.

It shall allow users to manage:

- Name
- Email address
- Display name
- Job title
- Role
- ART User ID
- Identity-linking settings
- Linked devices
- Device names
- Device trust
- Device revocation

### Identity Token Interface

If the personal identity token/passphrase is exposed to users, the
interface shall include:

- A clearly labeled textbox.
- Instructions explaining its purpose.
- Appropriate masking/unmasking behavior.
- Accessible error messages.
- A secure save/change operation.
- A way to generate a secure random token.
- A warning against reuse as another password.
- Appropriate recovery guidance.

The interface shall not expose the token unnecessarily.

### Token Change

When a user changes their identity-linking token/passphrase, ART shall
not silently invalidate every existing trusted device unless required by
the security model.

Instead, the system shall distinguish between:

- Changing a pairing/recovery secret
- Revoking a device
- Revoking all devices
- Changing the authenticated account

### Identity Recovery

ART shall provide a secure identity recovery process.

A forgotten identity-linking token shall not automatically result in
account loss.

Recovery shall use the secure authentication mechanisms established by
Epic 48.

### No Knowledge-Based Recovery

ART shall not rely on insecure security questions or other easily
guessed knowledge-based authentication for identity recovery.

NIST's current guidance explicitly rejects knowledge-based
authentication as an acceptable authentication mechanism.

### Privacy

ART shall minimize collection of device information.

The system should not collect unnecessary:

- Hardware identifiers
- MAC addresses
- IP history
- Browser fingerprinting data
- Other persistent tracking information

Device identification should rely on ART-generated cryptographic
identifiers where practical.

### Data Protection

Sensitive user and organization data shall be protected using
appropriate security practices.

Authentication credentials, device private keys, and identity secrets
shall never be stored in plaintext.

### API Authorization

Every protected API endpoint shall perform appropriate authorization
checks.

Client-side restrictions shall never replace server-side authorization.

### Authorization Middleware

Where practical, authorization checks should be implemented through
reusable middleware or policy enforcement components.

### Permission Consistency

The same permission shall produce the same authorization result
regardless of whether the action originates from:

- Report Viewer
- Report Builder
- Context menu
- Keyboard shortcut
- Command palette
- API request
- Other interface

### Backward Compatibility

Existing local ART functionality shall continue to work.

Existing `.art` files shall remain usable.

Existing file-based collaboration shall remain functional.

Existing local user profiles shall remain usable.

Users shall not be forced to migrate to server accounts simply to
continue using ART.

### Migration Strategy

The implementation shall provide a migration strategy for existing local
ART identities.

Where appropriate:

1.  Detect the existing local identity.
2.  Authenticate the user.
3.  Confirm the identity association.
4.  Associate the authenticated account with the existing ART User ID.
5.  Preserve existing collaboration attribution.
6.  Continue using the existing identity.

### Multi-Device Migration

Existing users shall be able to link additional devices without creating
duplicate ART identities.

### Definition of Done

Epic 50 is complete when ART has a functional identity, authorization,
organization, and multi-device foundation providing:

- Authenticated users
- Persistent ART User IDs
- Organizations
- Organization membership
- Organization invitations
- Organization roles
- Role assignment
- Permission definitions
- Resource-level authorization
- Centralized Authorization Policy Service
- Server-side authorization enforcement
- Organization isolation
- Permission-aware user interfaces
- Authorization-aware APIs
- Audit logging
- Permission revocation
- Secure organization membership
- Secure multi-device identity
- Device registration
- Device linking
- Device revocation
- Device management
- Secure identity-linking credentials
- File-based identity handshake
- File-based identity verification
- Identity conflict detection
- Cryptographically protected identity metadata
- Integration with Epic 48 authentication
- Integration with Epic 49 file-based identity and collaboration
- Integration foundations for shared workspaces
- Integration foundations for projects
- Integration foundations for reports
- Integration foundations for Tasks
- Integration foundations for Progress Logs
- Integration foundations for Organization Metrics
- Integration foundations for @mentions
- Integration foundations for notifications

ART shall maintain its fundamental no-login, local-first functionality
while providing a secure authenticated model for server-dependent
features.

Most importantly:

**Authentication establishes who the user is.**

**The ART User ID establishes the user's persistent ART identity.**

**Device identity establishes which ART installations belong to that
user.**

**Organization membership establishes where the user belongs.**

**Roles and permissions establish what the user may do.**

**The Authorization Policy Service provides the authoritative decision
about whether an action is permitted.**

**Cryptographic identity and device-linking mechanisms establish trusted
relationships between multiple ART installations.**

**File-based identity handshakes allow ART to recognize and verify
related user/device identities even when no server is available, while
clearly distinguishing that trust relationship from server-authenticated
identity.**

This architecture shall provide the foundation for ART's future
collaborative, organizational, enterprise, multi-device, server-based,
and file-based capabilities without compromising ART's local-first
design.

## Epic 51 — Storage Provider Architecture

### Epic Overview

Design and implement a provider-independent storage architecture that
allows ART to work with multiple file-storage and collaboration
providers without making ART dependent on any single cloud service,
server, or storage platform.

The storage architecture shall provide a common interface for accessing,
creating, opening, saving, updating, moving, renaming, deleting, and
monitoring ART files regardless of where those files are stored.

The architecture shall support ART's existing local-first and file-based
collaboration model while providing a foundation for future integrations
with Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, network/shared folders,
and an optional ART server.

ART shall remain fully functional without connecting to any external
storage provider or ART server.

### Goals

The storage provider architecture shall:

- Establish a common, provider-independent storage interface.
- Preserve ART's local-first functionality.
- Support `.art` files as the primary portable ART report/project file
  format.
- Allow users to work with files stored locally or through supported
  external storage providers.
- Support file-based collaboration without requiring an ART server.
- Provide the foundation for Google Drive integration.
- Provide the foundation for OneDrive integration.
- Provide the foundation for Dropbox integration.
- Provide the foundation for network/shared-folder storage.
- Provide the foundation for future ART server integration.
- Allow additional storage providers to be implemented without
  redesigning ART's core reporting and collaboration functionality.
- Preserve existing merge-conflict functionality.
- Provide consistent accessibility and keyboard interaction regardless
  of the selected storage provider.
- Keep provider-specific authentication, permissions, APIs, and
  implementation details isolated from ART's core application logic.

### Relationship to Existing ART Architecture

The storage provider architecture shall build upon the file-based
collaboration model established in Epic 49.

ART shall treat a stored `.art` file as the primary artifact being
synchronized or shared.

The storage provider shall be responsible for locating and transferring
the file, while ART remains responsible for:

- Interpreting the `.art` file.
- Loading report/project data.
- Tracking changes.
- Detecting changes between versions.
- Identifying merge conflicts.
- Presenting merge conflicts to users.
- Applying user-selected merge decisions.
- Maintaining the History Framework.
- Preserving report, project, task, and collaboration data.

Storage providers shall not implement ART-specific merge logic.

### Local-First Operation

ART shall remain fully usable without an external storage provider.

Users shall be able to:

- Create reports.
- Create projects.
- Edit reports.
- Configure report layouts and fields.
- Save `.art` files locally.
- Open `.art` files locally.
- Export reports.
- Import reports.
- Use the History Framework.
- Use Tasks and To Do Lists.
- Use Shared Progress Logs when supported through file-based
  collaboration.
- Use file-based collaboration.
- Resolve merge conflicts.

No user shall be required to create an ART account or connect an
external storage provider merely to use ART's fundamental capabilities.

### Storage Provider Abstraction

Implement a common storage-provider interface between ART's core
application and external storage systems.

Conceptually, ART shall interact with a storage provider through
operations such as:

- Connect.
- Disconnect.
- Authenticate.
- Browse.
- Search.
- Create folder.
- Create file.
- Open file.
- Save file.
- Save a new version.
- Rename file.
- Move file.
- Copy file.
- Delete file.
- Restore file when supported.
- Determine whether a file has changed.
- Retrieve file metadata.
- Retrieve version metadata when supported.
- Refresh file state.
- Detect synchronization conflicts.
- Report storage errors.
- Report authentication errors.
- Report permission errors.
- Report unavailable/offline states.

The exact implementation shall vary by provider, but the interface
exposed to ART's core application shall remain consistent.

### Provider Independence

ART's core application shall not contain provider-specific logic such
as:

- Google Drive API calls.
- Microsoft Graph API calls.
- Dropbox API calls.
- Provider-specific authentication flows.
- Provider-specific folder structures.
- Provider-specific error handling embedded throughout the application.

Provider-specific functionality shall be isolated into dedicated
storage-provider implementations.

Conceptually:

``` text
ART Core
    |
    +-- Storage Provider Interface
            |
            +-- Local File Provider
            +-- Google Drive Provider
            +-- OneDrive Provider
            +-- Dropbox Provider
            +-- Network Folder Provider
            +-- ART Server Provider
```

This architecture shall allow additional providers to be added without
requiring major changes to ART's report, project, task, collaboration,
or merge-conflict systems.

### Local File Provider

Implement a local-file storage provider as the baseline implementation.

The local provider shall support:

- Opening `.art` files.
- Saving `.art` files.
- Creating new `.art` files.
- Selecting local folders.
- Renaming files.
- Moving files when supported by the operating system.
- Deleting files through appropriate user-controlled commands.
- Detecting when an opened file has changed outside ART.
- Reloading or comparing changed files.
- Invoking ART's merge-conflict functionality when appropriate.

The local provider shall serve as the reference implementation for the
storage-provider interface.

### Shared and Network Folder Support

ART shall support storage locations that appear to the operating system
as accessible folders.

This shall include, where supported by the operating system:

- Local folders.
- Network folders.
- Shared folders.
- Synchronized cloud-drive folders.
- External drives.
- Removable storage.

ART shall not need to know whether a folder is backed by Google Drive,
OneDrive, Dropbox, a network server, or another file-synchronization
system when the operating system exposes the location as a normal
filesystem.

### File-Based Collaboration

The storage architecture shall support the file-based collaboration
model established in Epic 49.

For example:

``` text
User A
   |
   | Save .art
   v
Shared Folder
   |
   | Synchronization
   v
User B
   |
   | Open .art
   v
ART
```

Multiple users shall be able to work with the same `.art` file through a
shared or synchronized storage location.

ART shall detect when a previously opened file has changed since the
user's last known version.

When appropriate, ART shall:

1.  Detect that the external file changed.
2.  Preserve the user's current work.
3.  Compare the current version with the newly available version.
4.  Identify non-conflicting changes.
5.  Automatically incorporate compatible changes.
6.  Identify conflicting changes.
7.  Open the Merge Changes interface when conflicts require user
    intervention.
8.  Allow the user to choose which changes to keep.
9.  Save the resulting merged version back to the storage provider.

### Synchronization Model

The storage architecture shall use a version-aware, file-based
synchronization model rather than assuming that the storage provider
provides real-time ART collaboration.

Users shall understand that file-based collaboration may be:

- Asynchronous.
- Near-real-time when the storage provider synchronizes quickly.
- Manual when the user must refresh or reopen a file.
- Offline until the storage provider becomes available.

ART shall not represent file-based collaboration as real-time server
collaboration unless the selected provider actually supports the
necessary behavior.

### Change Detection

ART shall detect when the file currently being edited has been modified
externally.

Where available, ART may use file metadata such as:

- Modification time.
- File size.
- File identifier.
- Version identifier.
- Provider revision identifier.
- Content hash.
- Provider-specific change tokens.

ART shall use appropriate safeguards to avoid incorrectly assuming that
a file has changed.

### Merge Conflict Integration

The storage provider architecture shall integrate with ART's existing
merge-conflict functionality.

The storage provider shall provide ART with the appropriate versions or
file contents required for comparison.

ART's existing merge framework shall determine:

- What changed.
- Which changes are compatible.
- Which changes conflict.
- Which version contains each change.
- What user decisions are required.

The storage provider shall not independently decide which user's ART
content should win.

### User Experience

ART shall provide a consistent user experience regardless of the
selected storage provider.

Users shall be able to determine:

- Where the current file is stored.
- Which storage provider is being used.
- Whether the file is available.
- Whether the file has changed externally.
- Whether the current copy is synchronized.
- Whether a conflict has been detected.
- Whether a save operation succeeded or failed.
- Whether authentication is required.
- Whether access to the file has been denied.
- Whether the provider is temporarily unavailable.

Status information shall be accessible to screen readers and other
assistive technologies.

### Storage Location Selection

ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for selecting a storage
location.

The user shall be able to choose among available storage providers and
locations.

The interface shall not require users to understand provider-specific
technical terminology.

Where possible, ART shall present familiar concepts such as:

- Local Computer.
- Shared Folder.
- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Network Folder.
- ART Server.

Provider-specific names shall remain recognizable to users.

### Settings and Storage Preferences

ART shall provide accessible storage settings allowing users to:

- View connected storage providers.
- Connect a provider.
- Disconnect a provider.
- Select a default storage provider when appropriate.
- Select a default storage location when appropriate.
- Change the default storage location.
- View the current storage location.
- Manage provider connections.

Storage preferences shall be specific to the user's local copy of ART
unless synchronization of settings is explicitly supported by an
authenticated ART server.

### Authentication Separation

Storage-provider authentication shall remain separate from ART's own
authentication system.

Connecting Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, or another provider shall
not automatically imply that the user is logged into an ART server.

Likewise, an ART account shall not automatically grant ART access to a
user's external storage provider.

Each provider shall use its own appropriate authentication mechanism.

### OAuth and Provider Authentication

Where a storage provider supports OAuth or an equivalent secure
authorization mechanism, ART shall use the provider's recommended
authorization mechanism.

ART shall:

- Avoid requesting unnecessary permissions.
- Request the minimum permissions required for the selected
  functionality.
- Avoid storing provider passwords.
- Protect provider access tokens.
- Provide a mechanism for disconnecting or revoking a provider
  connection.
- Handle expired or revoked tokens.
- Provide accessible authentication error messages.
- Never expose authentication credentials in the user interface.

Provider-specific credentials and tokens shall not be committed to
source control.

### Google Drive Provider Foundation

The architecture shall specifically support a future Google Drive
provider.

The Google Drive implementation shall be capable of supporting:

- Connecting a user's Google account.
- Selecting an ART folder.
- Browsing folders.
- Creating `.art` files.
- Opening `.art` files.
- Saving `.art` files.
- Detecting changes.
- Retrieving relevant file metadata.
- Handling provider permissions.
- Handling authentication expiration.
- Disconnecting the Google Drive account.

The implementation shall use the minimum appropriate Google Drive
permissions.

ART shall not require unrestricted access to a user's entire Google
Drive when narrower permissions are sufficient.

### OneDrive Provider Foundation

The architecture shall support a future Microsoft OneDrive provider.

The provider shall be designed to use the appropriate Microsoft
authentication and storage APIs without requiring changes to ART's core
storage interface.

### Dropbox Provider Foundation

The architecture shall support a future Dropbox provider.

The provider shall be designed to use Dropbox's supported authentication
and file APIs without requiring changes to ART's core storage interface.

### ART Server Provider

The storage architecture shall reserve a provider implementation for a
future ART server.

The ART server provider shall eventually support server-based
functionality such as:

- Authenticated collaboration.
- Organizations.
- Shared workspaces.
- Server-side synchronization.
- Notifications.
- @mentions\.
- Server-side tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Organization Metrics.
- Device synchronization.
- Centralized authorization.

The ART server provider shall not be required for basic file-based
collaboration.

### File-Based Collaboration and @Mentions

The storage architecture shall support the @mentions functionality
introduced in Epic 49.

When collaboration data containing an @mention is stored inside a shared
`.art` file, ART shall preserve:

- The author of the comment.
- The mentioned user.
- The comment containing the @mention.
- The associated task, report, project, workspace, or other ART object.
- Relevant timestamps.
- User identity information necessary to resolve the mention.

File-based @mentions shall function within the appropriate shared scope,
including:

- The same shared report.
- The same shared project.
- A shared organization folder.
- Other supported shared ART resources.

Server-based notifications may provide additional functionality when an
ART server is available, but basic file-based @mention information shall
remain part of the shared ART data when appropriate.

### User Identity in File-Based Collaboration

File-based collaboration shall use the user identity information
established in Epic 49 and Epic 50.

ART shall associate changes with the appropriate user identity when
possible.

The identity information associated with file-based changes shall allow
collaborators to distinguish between users working on the same shared
report or project.

ART shall not assume that two different ART installations represent
different users merely because they are running on different devices.

Device and identity association shall follow the user identity and
device-linking mechanisms established by Epic 50.

### File Ownership and Permissions

ART shall distinguish between:

- ART-level permissions.
- Storage-provider permissions.
- Operating-system permissions.
- File-level permissions.
- Organization permissions.

ART shall not claim that a user has permission to modify a file when the
underlying storage provider or filesystem denies that operation.

Provider permissions shall be respected.

### Shared Organization Folders

The storage architecture shall support the organization-folder model
established in Epic 49.

A shared parent folder may contain:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
    |
    +-- Project A/
    |      +-- Report 1.art
    |      +-- Report 2.art
    |
    +-- Project B/
    |      +-- Report 3.art
    |
    +-- Progress Logs/
    |
    +-- Tasks/
    |
    +-- Organization Metrics/
```

Where the underlying storage provider supports inherited folder
permissions, ART shall work with those inherited permissions rather than
attempting to recreate them internally.

ART shall be able to identify the shared organization folder when the
storage provider exposes sufficient metadata.

### Organization Metrics

The storage architecture shall provide a foundation for Organization
Metrics to operate against shared organization folders.

Where supported, ART shall be able to identify relevant `.art` files
within a configured organization folder and its supported subfolders.

Organization Metrics shall be able to use the contents of those files as
data sources.

ART shall not assume that every file in a shared folder is an ART file.

Only compatible ART files and supported data sources shall be processed.

### Tasks and Shared To Do Lists

The storage architecture shall support file-based sharing of:

- Assigned tasks.
- Shared tasks.
- Shared To Do Lists.
- Personal task information when intentionally shared.
- Task assignments.
- Task status.
- Task priority.
- Due dates.
- Comments/notes/instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Relevant task history.

Changes shall be preserved in the `.art` file and made available to
collaborators when the file is synchronized.

### Shared Progress Logs

The storage architecture shall support file-based sharing of Progress
Logs.

Shared Progress Log data shall include, where applicable:

- Tasks.
- Assignments.
- Status.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- User identity.
- Progress information.
- Relevant history.

Merge handling shall preserve compatible changes and identify conflicts
requiring user intervention.

### Report Types

The storage architecture shall support all ART report types, including:

- Audit Logs.
- Executive Summaries.
- Usability Reports.
- Other report types introduced by ART.

The storage provider shall not need to understand the internal structure
of individual report types.

### History Framework

Storage operations and synchronization-related actions shall integrate
with ART's History Framework where appropriate.

The History Framework shall allow users to undo and redo applicable
actions associated with:

- File changes.
- Merge decisions.
- Storage-related edits.
- Task changes.
- Progress Log changes.
- Report changes.

The provider itself shall not be responsible for implementing ART's
Undo/Redo functionality.

### Offline Behavior

ART shall provide useful behavior when a storage provider becomes
unavailable.

If a file is already open, ART shall preserve the user's local working
state.

ART shall avoid silently discarding unsaved changes because a provider
becomes unavailable.

Users shall receive accessible information when:

- A save cannot be completed.
- A provider becomes unavailable.
- Authentication expires.
- A file cannot be retrieved.
- A file is locked or inaccessible.
- A synchronization operation cannot complete.

Where possible, ART shall allow the user to retain or export their
current work locally.

### Error Handling

Storage-provider errors shall be translated into understandable ART
messages.

Errors shall distinguish among conditions such as:

- Authentication failure.
- Authorization failure.
- File not found.
- Folder not found.
- Provider unavailable.
- Network unavailable.
- File changed externally.
- Merge conflict.
- Save failure.
- Storage quota exceeded.
- File type unsupported.
- File locked.
- Invalid or corrupted ART file.

Error messages shall identify the appropriate user action when possible.

### Accessibility

All storage-provider functionality shall meet ART's accessibility
requirements.

This includes:

- Provider selection.
- Authentication workflows.
- Folder browsing.
- File browsing.
- File creation.
- File opening.
- File saving.
- Synchronization status.
- Conflict notifications.
- Merge workflows.
- Error messages.
- Settings.
- Provider connection management.

All controls shall be keyboard accessible.

All important state changes shall be programmatically exposed to
assistive technologies.

Screen readers shall receive meaningful announcements for storage and
synchronization events.

### Keyboard Commands and Context Menus

Storage-related commands shall be available through ART's existing
command architecture.

Where applicable, commands shall be available through:

- Menubar menus.
- Global context menus.
- Context menus within file and folder interfaces.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

Commands may include:

- Open.
- Save.
- Save As.
- Refresh.
- Sync or Refresh from Provider.
- Connect Provider.
- Disconnect Provider.
- Choose Storage Location.
- Rename.
- Move.
- Copy.
- Delete.
- Resolve Conflict.
- View File Information.

Keyboard shortcuts shall remain customizable.

### Security

The storage provider architecture shall follow security principles
established by Epics 47–50.

ART shall:

- Follow least-privilege principles.
- Avoid storing provider passwords.
- Protect OAuth tokens.
- Protect authentication credentials.
- Avoid exposing sensitive information through logs.
- Validate files before processing them.
- Validate provider responses.
- Protect against malicious or malformed `.art` files.
- Prevent unauthorized access to locally stored credentials.
- Avoid unnecessary provider permissions.

Provider integrations shall be reviewed for security before being
enabled for production use.

### Data Integrity

ART shall protect the integrity of `.art` files during storage
operations.

ART shall avoid:

- Partial writes where possible.
- Silent overwriting of newer versions.
- Data loss during synchronization.
- Corruption caused by interrupted saves.
- Loss of metadata during provider transfers.

Where practical, saving shall use a safe-write process that minimizes
the possibility of leaving a corrupted `.art` file.

### Version and Revision Metadata

Where a provider exposes version or revision information, ART should
preserve and use that information to improve synchronization.

ART shall not assume that timestamps alone are sufficient to identify
all changes when a stronger provider-specific revision identifier is
available.

Provider-specific revision information shall remain abstracted behind
the storage-provider interface.

### Extensibility

Adding a new storage provider shall require implementing the common
provider interface rather than modifying ART's core reporting
architecture.

The architecture shall make it possible to add future providers such as:

- Additional cloud storage platforms.
- Enterprise document-management systems.
- Network storage systems.
- Private cloud storage.
- Self-hosted storage systems.
- ART Server.

### Testing

Each storage provider shall be tested independently and through ART's
complete workflows.

Testing shall include:

- Connecting.
- Disconnecting.
- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- File creation.
- File opening.
- File saving.
- Save As.
- Rename.
- Move.
- Copy.
- Delete.
- File browsing.
- Folder browsing.
- External file changes.
- Synchronization.
- Merge conflicts.
- Concurrent editing.
- Offline operation.
- Recovery from failed saves.
- Authentication expiration.
- Provider permission changes.
- File deletion by another user.
- File renaming by another user.
- Folder permission changes.
- Large files.
- Corrupted files.
- Unsupported files.
- Network interruptions.

### Accessibility Testing

Storage-provider functionality shall be tested with multiple assistive
technologies and accessibility configurations, including:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only operation.
- Low-vision and magnification configurations.
- High-contrast configurations.
- Other assistive technologies as appropriate.

Testing shall cover complete workflows rather than isolated controls.

### Provider-Specific Testing

Each provider implementation shall be tested using real provider
accounts and supported environments where possible.

Google Drive testing shall include:

- Personal Google accounts.
- Shared folders.
- Shared files.
- Permission changes.
- File synchronization.
- OAuth authorization.
- OAuth revocation.
- File deletion.
- File renaming.
- Concurrent editing.

Equivalent provider-specific tests shall be developed for OneDrive,
Dropbox, and future providers.

### Automated Testing

Where practical, automated tests shall validate the storage-provider
interface.

The automated test suite should verify that every provider correctly
implements required operations and returns standardized ART storage
states and errors.

Provider-specific tests shall supplement, not replace, end-to-end
testing.

### Migration and Backward Compatibility

The storage-provider architecture shall preserve compatibility with
existing `.art` files.

Existing ART users shall not lose access to previously created reports
or projects because of the new storage architecture.

Existing local files shall continue to open normally.

Existing import and export functionality shall remain available.

### Documentation

ART shall provide documentation explaining:

- Local storage.
- File-based collaboration.
- Shared folders.
- Storage providers.
- Connecting storage providers.
- Disconnecting providers.
- Synchronization.
- Merge conflicts.
- Offline behavior.
- File permissions.
- Provider permissions.
- Security considerations.

Documentation shall clearly explain the difference between:

- Local ART.
- File-based collaboration.
- Cloud storage.
- Server-based collaboration.

### Definition of Done

Epic 51 shall be considered complete when:

- A provider-independent storage interface has been implemented.
- Local file storage implements the interface.
- ART's core application is not dependent on a specific storage
  provider.
- `.art` files remain portable.
- File-based collaboration continues to function without an ART server.
- External file changes can be detected.
- Existing merge-conflict functionality integrates with the storage
  architecture.
- Storage errors are handled consistently.
- Authentication and provider credentials are handled securely.
- Storage-related functionality is keyboard accessible.
- Storage-related functionality is accessible to screen readers and
  other assistive technologies.
- Storage commands integrate with ART's command architecture.
- The History Framework continues to work appropriately.
- Tasks and Shared Progress Logs can participate in file-based
  collaboration.
- @mentions are preserved within shared ART files where applicable.
- Organization-folder and Organization Metrics functionality can use the
  storage architecture.
- The architecture is ready for Google Drive integration.
- The architecture is ready for OneDrive integration.
- The architecture is ready for Dropbox integration.
- The architecture is ready for future ART Server integration.
- Automated and end-to-end testing has been implemented for the
  storage-provider architecture.
- Documentation has been created.
- No existing ART functionality has regressed.

## Epic 52 — Google Drive Storage Integration

### Epic Overview

Implement Google Drive as the first external cloud-storage provider
using the provider-independent Storage Provider Architecture established
in Epic 51.

ART shall allow users to optionally connect Google Drive and work with
`.art` files stored in Google Drive without requiring an ART server.

Google Drive integration shall support ART's file-based collaboration
model, allowing multiple users to share `.art` files through Google
Drive or shared Google Drive folders while ART detects external changes
and uses its existing Merge Changes functionality when conflicts occur.

ART shall remain fully functional without Google Drive, without an ART
account, and without an ART server.

### Goals

The Google Drive integration shall:

- Allow users to optionally connect Google Drive to ART.
- Use Google's supported OAuth authentication mechanism.
- Request only the minimum permissions required.
- Never store a Google password in ART.
- Protect OAuth tokens and other credentials.
- Allow users to browse Google Drive files and folders.
- Allow users to select an ART storage folder.
- Open `.art` files directly from Google Drive.
- Save `.art` files directly to Google Drive.
- Create new `.art` files in Google Drive.
- Save modified `.art` files back to Google Drive.
- Detect changes made by other users.
- Support asynchronous file-based collaboration.
- Support synchronized/shared Google Drive folders.
- Integrate with ART's existing Merge Changes functionality.
- Preserve user identity information within shared ART files.
- Support file-based @mentions where applicable.
- Support shared projects, reports, tasks, Progress Logs, and other
  supported ART data.
- Preserve local-first operation when Google Drive is unavailable or
  disconnected.
- Provide accessible status information and controls.
- Provide a foundation for future OneDrive, Dropbox, and other provider
  integrations.

### Relationship to Epic 51

Epic 52 shall implement the Google Drive-specific provider using the
provider-independent architecture established in Epic 51.

The Google Drive provider shall not bypass the Storage Provider
Interface.

Conceptually:

``` text
ART Core
    |
    +-- Storage Provider Interface
            |
            +-- Local File Provider
            |
            +-- Google Drive Provider
```

ART's core reporting, project, task, collaboration, and merge-conflict
functionality shall remain independent of Google Drive.

### Google Drive Connection

ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for connecting a Google Drive
account.

The user shall be able to:

- Connect Google Drive.
- View the currently connected Google account when supported.
- Disconnect Google Drive.
- Reconnect Google Drive.
- Change the Google account used by ART.
- View the current connection status.

Connecting Google Drive shall be optional.

### Google OAuth Authentication

Google Drive authentication shall use Google's supported OAuth
authorization process.

ART shall:

- Redirect or otherwise invoke the appropriate Google authentication
  workflow.
- Allow the user to select the Google account they want to use.
- Clearly communicate the permissions being requested.
- Request only the minimum required scopes.
- Never request the user's Google password.
- Never store the user's Google password.
- Securely store or protect OAuth tokens as appropriate for the
  platform.
- Handle expired tokens.
- Handle revoked authorization.
- Handle denied authorization.
- Provide an accessible way to retry authorization.
- Provide accessible authentication error messages.

ART shall not embed or hard-code user credentials.

### Google Drive Permissions

The integration shall follow the principle of least privilege.

ART shall request only the permissions necessary to perform the
functions the user has selected.

Where possible, ART shall prefer access limited to files or folders that
the user explicitly selects rather than unrestricted access to the
user's entire Google Drive.

The implementation shall document the Google Drive scopes being
requested and why each scope is required.

### Google Drive Storage Selection

After connecting Google Drive, ART shall provide an accessible mechanism
for selecting a Google Drive folder to use for ART files.

The user shall be able to:

- Browse folders.
- Open folders.
- Select a folder.
- Create an ART folder.
- Change the selected ART folder.
- View the current selected folder.
- Return to the root or other accessible locations.
- Cancel folder selection.

The folder-selection interface shall support keyboard navigation and
screen readers.

### ART Folder

ART should provide an option to create a dedicated folder for ART files,
such as:

``` text
ART/
```

or a user-defined folder name.

Users shall also be able to select an existing folder.

ART shall not require users to create a dedicated folder if they prefer
to use an existing Google Drive folder.

### Google Drive File Browser

ART shall provide an accessible file browser for supported Google Drive
locations.

The file browser shall allow users to:

- Browse folders.
- Open folders.
- View `.art` files.
- Open `.art` files.
- Create new `.art` files.
- Rename files where permitted.
- Move files where permitted.
- Copy files where supported.
- Delete files where permitted.
- Refresh the folder contents.
- View relevant file information.

The interface shall clearly distinguish `.art` files from unsupported
file types.

### Opening an ART File

When the user opens an `.art` file from Google Drive, ART shall:

1.  Retrieve the file.
2.  Validate that it is a supported ART file.
3.  Load the report/project data.
4.  Record the relevant file and revision information.
5.  Begin monitoring the file for external changes where supported.
6.  Display the appropriate storage and synchronization status.

The user shall be informed when the file is being loaded or when an
error prevents it from being opened.

### Saving an ART File

When the user saves an `.art` file stored in Google Drive, ART shall:

1.  Determine whether the remote file has changed since the user's
    current version was retrieved.
2.  Preserve the user's current work.
3.  Retrieve the latest remote version when necessary.
4.  Compare the relevant versions.
5.  Automatically incorporate compatible changes.
6.  Identify conflicts.
7.  Open the Merge Changes interface when user intervention is required.
8.  Save the resulting version to Google Drive.
9.  Update the local revision information.

ART shall not silently overwrite a newer remote version when doing so
could cause another user's work to be lost.

### Save As

ART shall support saving an existing report/project as a new `.art` file
in Google Drive.

The user shall be able to:

- Choose a Google Drive folder.
- Specify the new filename.
- Confirm the save.
- Cancel the operation.

If the destination file already exists, ART shall provide an accessible
confirmation or conflict workflow rather than silently overwriting it.

### External Change Detection

ART shall detect when a file opened from Google Drive has changed since
it was last retrieved or saved.

Where Google Drive provides revision identifiers or other reliable
metadata, ART shall use those mechanisms rather than relying solely on
timestamps.

ART shall distinguish between:

- No remote change.
- Remote change with no local unsaved changes.
- Remote change with local unsaved changes.
- Remote change resulting in compatible changes.
- Remote change resulting in merge conflicts.

### Automatic Synchronization of Compatible Changes

When a remote `.art` file has changed and the user's local changes do
not conflict with the remote changes, ART should automatically merge the
compatible changes where technically and safely possible.

The user shall be informed that remote changes were incorporated.

ART shall preserve appropriate History Framework information so that
supported changes can be undone when appropriate.

### Merge Conflicts

When Google Drive contains changes that conflict with the user's local
changes, ART shall use the existing Merge Changes functionality.

The Merge Changes interface shall:

- Identify the conflicting changes.
- Identify the users associated with the changes when identity
  information is available.
- Clearly distinguish local and remote changes.
- Allow the user to choose which changes to keep.
- Allow supported changes to be combined.
- Preserve non-conflicting changes.
- Provide accessible descriptions of the conflict.
- Support keyboard operation.
- Work with screen readers.
- Preserve the user's ability to cancel or defer conflict resolution
  where appropriate.

The Google Drive provider shall not implement separate merge logic.

### File-Based Collaboration

Google Drive shall serve as a storage and synchronization mechanism for
ART's file-based collaboration model.

Multiple users shall be able to collaborate through shared Google Drive
folders.

For example:

``` text
Shared Google Drive Folder
        |
        +-- Audit Project.art
        |
        +-- Progress Log.art
        |
        +-- Tasks.art
        |
        +-- Other Reports.art
```

Users shall be able to open and modify shared `.art` files according to
their Google Drive permissions.

### Asynchronous Collaboration

Google Drive collaboration shall primarily support asynchronous
file-based collaboration.

For example:

``` text
User A
  |
  | Opens report
  | Makes changes
  | Saves
  v
Google Drive
  |
  | Synchronizes
  v
User B
  |
  | Opens/refreshes report
  | Detects changes
  v
ART
```

ART shall not claim to provide real-time collaborative editing merely
because the file is stored in Google Drive.

### Concurrent Editing

When two or more users have the same `.art` file open simultaneously,
each user's local copy shall remain independent until changes are saved
or synchronized.

ART shall detect remote changes when the user:

- Saves.
- Refreshes.
- Reopens the file.
- Performs another supported synchronization operation.

When conflicts occur, the Merge Changes interface shall be presented to
the appropriate user.

### File Version Information

Where Google Drive exposes revision information, ART shall record
sufficient information to determine which remote version the user last
accessed.

ART should use revision information to improve:

- Change detection.
- Conflict detection.
- Synchronization reliability.
- Recovery from failed saves.

Provider-specific revision identifiers shall remain isolated within the
Google Drive provider implementation.

### Google Drive Shared Folders

ART shall support `.art` files stored in Google Drive folders shared
with other users.

The integration shall respect Google Drive's existing sharing
permissions.

ART shall not attempt to duplicate Google Drive permissions internally.

If a user has:

- View-only access, ART shall not present editing functionality as
  available.
- Comment access where applicable, ART shall respect the limitations of
  that permission.
- Edit access, ART may allow supported ART editing operations.
- No access, ART shall report that the file is unavailable.

### Google Shared Drives

Where technically supported by the selected Google Drive API and account
type, ART should support Google Shared Drives.

The implementation shall account for differences between:

- Personal Google Drive.
- Shared folders.
- Google Shared Drives.

Provider limitations shall be communicated clearly to users.

### Google Drive Folder Permissions

ART shall respect inherited permissions from Google Drive folders.

For example:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
    |
    +-- Project A/
    |
    +-- Project B/
    |
    +-- Progress Logs/
    |
    +-- Tasks/
```

If the Google Drive folder structure provides inherited access, ART
shall use the permissions supplied by Google Drive rather than creating
a conflicting internal permission model.

### Organization Folders

Google Drive shall support the organization-folder model introduced by
Epic 49.

An organization may configure a shared parent folder such as:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
```

Subfolders may contain:

- Projects.
- Reports.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Other shared ART files.
- Organization Metrics data.

ART shall be able to work with this structure when the user has
sufficient Google Drive access.

### Organization Metrics

Where supported, ART shall allow Organization Metrics to use `.art`
files stored in a configured Google Drive organization folder.

ART shall:

- Identify supported ART files.
- Process supported data.
- Ignore unsupported files.
- Respect Google Drive access permissions.
- Update metrics when relevant ART files change.
- Avoid modifying source files merely to calculate metrics.

Metrics synchronization shall remain subject to Google Drive
synchronization behavior.

### Tasks and To Do Lists

Google Drive storage shall support file-based task collaboration.

Shared `.art` data may contain:

- Assigned tasks.
- Shared tasks.
- Task status.
- Task priority.
- Due dates.
- Comments/notes/instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Task history.
- Assignment information.

Changes shall synchronize through the `.art` file.

### Shared Progress Logs

Google Drive shall support file-based Shared Progress Logs.

Shared Progress Log data may include:

- Tasks.
- Assignments.
- Status.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- User identity.
- Progress information.
- History.

Changes shall be preserved in the `.art` file and merged when
compatible.

### @Mentions

The Google Drive integration shall preserve @mentions contained within
shared ART files.

A user shall be able to mention another collaborator using the existing
ART @mention functionality.

The stored collaboration data shall preserve sufficient information to
identify:

- The user creating the mention.
- The mentioned user.
- The associated comment.
- The associated task/report/project/workspace.
- The relevant date/time.

When an ART server is unavailable, Google Drive file-based collaboration
shall preserve the @mention data inside the shared ART file.

Server-based notification delivery may be implemented separately when an
ART server is available.

### User Identity

Google Drive collaboration shall use the ART user identity information
established by Epics 49 and 50.

Where possible, changes shall identify the ART user responsible for the
change.

ART shall not rely solely on a Google account's display name to identify
an ART user.

The ART identity associated with a change shall remain distinguishable
from the storage-provider account used to access the file.

### Device Linking

Google Drive file-based collaboration shall work with the device-linking
functionality established in Epic 50.

A user's multiple ART installations may be associated with the same ART
identity.

For example:

``` text
User A
  |
  +-- ART Web
  |
  +-- ART Desktop
  |
  +-- ART on Device 2
  |
  +-- ART on Device 3
```

The storage provider shall not be responsible for determining ART
identity.

ART shall use its own identity and device-linking mechanisms.

### File Ownership

ART shall distinguish between the owner of a Google Drive file and the
ART user who created or modified content within the file.

Google Drive ownership shall remain controlled by Google Drive.

ART collaboration metadata shall identify ART users independently where
appropriate.

### Offline Operation

ART shall remain usable when Google Drive is temporarily unavailable.

If the user's current `.art` file has already been loaded:

- The user shall be able to continue working locally.
- Unsaved changes shall be preserved.
- ART shall not silently discard work.
- The user shall receive an accessible indication that Google Drive is
  unavailable.
- The user should be able to save/export a local copy when possible.

When Google Drive becomes available again, ART shall allow the user to
refresh or synchronize the file.

### Failed Saves

If ART cannot save changes to Google Drive, it shall:

- Preserve the user's current work.
- Clearly identify that the save failed.
- Explain the likely reason when known.
- Provide an opportunity to retry.
- Provide an option to save/export a local copy where appropriate.
- Avoid falsely indicating that the remote file was updated.

### Authentication Expiration

When the Google OAuth authorization expires or is revoked, ART shall:

- Detect the authentication failure.
- Preserve unsaved work.
- Inform the user.
- Provide an accessible option to reconnect.
- Avoid repeatedly displaying authentication errors unnecessarily.

### Disconnecting Google Drive

Users shall be able to disconnect Google Drive from ART.

Disconnecting shall:

- Remove the local connection to the provider.
- Prevent future Google Drive operations until the user reconnects.
- Preserve local `.art` files.
- Not delete Google Drive files.
- Not delete the user's Google Drive account.
- Not remove Google Drive permissions unless the user explicitly chooses
  an appropriate revocation option.

### Security

The Google Drive integration shall comply with the security requirements
established in Epics 47–51.

ART shall:

- Use secure OAuth authorization.
- Request minimum necessary permissions.
- Protect OAuth tokens.
- Avoid storing Google passwords.
- Avoid logging sensitive credentials.
- Validate downloaded files.
- Validate Google Drive API responses.
- Protect against malicious or malformed `.art` files.
- Avoid unnecessary access to unrelated Google Drive content.
- Respect Google Drive permissions.
- Handle revoked credentials securely.

### Data Privacy

ART shall clearly communicate what Google Drive data it accesses.

ART shall not access unrelated Google Drive files merely because Google
Drive is connected.

Where possible, users shall be able to limit ART's access to designated
ART folders or files.

### Accessibility

All Google Drive functionality shall conform to ART's accessibility
requirements.

This includes:

- Connecting Google Drive.
- OAuth authentication.
- Account selection.
- Folder selection.
- File browsing.
- File opening.
- File saving.
- Save As.
- Refreshing.
- Synchronization.
- Conflict detection.
- Merge Changes.
- Error handling.
- Disconnecting Google Drive.

All functionality shall be accessible using the keyboard.

All important status changes shall be programmatically exposed.

### Screen Reader Support

Google Drive integration shall be tested with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.

Screen readers shall receive meaningful information about:

- Current storage provider.
- Current file.
- Current folder.
- Synchronization state.
- External changes.
- Save status.
- Authentication status.
- Errors.
- Merge conflicts.

### Low-Vision and Visual Accessibility

Google Drive integration shall be tested using:

- Browser zoom.
- Operating-system magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- ART visual settings.
- Different screen sizes.
- Different display scaling levels.

The interface shall remain usable without relying solely on color,
spatial position, or visual indicators.

### Keyboard Commands

Google Drive-related commands shall integrate with ART's command
architecture.

Commands shall be available through appropriate:

- Menubar menus.
- Global context menus.
- File/folder context menus.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

Potential commands include:

- Connect Google Drive.
- Disconnect Google Drive.
- Open from Google Drive.
- Save to Google Drive.
- Save As to Google Drive.
- Refresh from Google Drive.
- Synchronize.
- Resolve Merge Conflicts.
- Select Google Drive Folder.
- View File Information.

### Context Menu Integration

Where appropriate, users shall be able to access Google Drive commands
from context menus.

Context menus shall expose only commands appropriate to the selected
object and the user's permissions.

Disabled commands shall communicate why they are unavailable where
appropriate.

### History Framework

Google Drive-related ART changes shall integrate with ART's History
Framework where appropriate.

The History Framework shall support Undo/Redo for applicable ART content
changes resulting from synchronization or merge operations.

Provider connection and authentication actions shall not necessarily be
treated as ordinary document edits unless explicitly designed to be
reversible.

### Notifications

ART shall provide accessible notifications for important Google Drive
events, including:

- File changed externally.
- Remote changes successfully synchronized.
- Merge conflict detected.
- Save successful.
- Save failed.
- Google Drive unavailable.
- Authentication expired.
- Permission denied.
- File deleted.
- File moved.
- File renamed.

Notifications shall not rely exclusively on transient visual messages.

### Error Handling

Google Drive errors shall be translated into understandable ART
messages.

The system shall distinguish among:

- Authentication failure.
- Authorization failure.
- File not found.
- Folder not found.
- Permission denied.
- Google Drive unavailable.
- Network failure.
- Quota limitations.
- File changed externally.
- Merge conflict.
- Save failure.
- Unsupported file.
- Corrupted ART file.
- Revoked authorization.

### File Integrity

ART shall protect `.art` file integrity during Google Drive operations.

The integration shall avoid:

- Partial writes.
- Silent overwriting.
- Corrupted saves.
- Lost changes.
- Incorrect revision tracking.
- Loss of ART metadata.

Where possible, ART shall use a safe-write process.

### Large Files

The Google Drive provider shall support `.art` files of realistic
production sizes.

Testing shall identify:

- Maximum practical file size.
- Upload/download performance.
- Timeout behavior.
- Interrupted transfers.
- Recovery behavior.

ART shall provide useful feedback when large files require additional
processing time.

### Network Interruptions

ART shall gracefully handle interruptions during:

- Authentication.
- File download.
- File upload.
- Save.
- Refresh.
- Synchronization.
- Merge preparation.

The user's work shall not be silently lost because of a network
interruption.

### Concurrent Editing Testing

The integration shall be tested with at least two users.

Testing shall include:

1.  User A opens a report.
2.  User B opens the same report.
3.  User A makes a change.
4.  User A saves.
5.  User B refreshes.
6.  User B sees User A's change.
7.  User B makes another change.
8.  User B saves.
9.  User A refreshes.
10. User A sees User B's change.

Additional testing shall verify conflicting edits.

### Merge Conflict Testing

Testing shall include:

1.  User A opens a report.
2.  User B opens the same report.
3.  User A changes one value.
4.  User B changes the same value differently.
5.  User A saves.
6.  User B saves or refreshes.
7.  ART detects the conflict.
8.  The Merge Changes modal opens.
9.  User B chooses the desired version.
10. ART creates the merged result.
11. The merged result is saved.
12. User A subsequently opens or refreshes the file.
13. User A sees the merged result.

### File-Based Collaboration Testing

Testing shall verify:

- Multiple users.
- Multiple devices.
- Shared folders.
- Asynchronous collaboration.
- Concurrent editing.
- Compatible changes.
- Conflicting changes.
- Merge resolution.
- User identity.
- Task assignments.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- @mentions\.
- Organization folders.
- Organization Metrics.

### Google Drive Permission Testing

Test scenarios shall include:

- File owner.
- Editor.
- Viewer.
- Shared-folder member.
- Removed user.
- Permission changed while a file is open.
- File moved.
- File deleted.
- Folder access revoked.
- Shared Drive access where supported.

ART shall accurately respond to the permissions returned by Google
Drive.

### Automated Testing

Automated tests shall validate the Google Drive provider implementation
against the common Storage Provider Interface.

Testing shall verify:

- Authentication state handling.
- Provider connection state.
- File operations.
- Folder operations.
- Metadata retrieval.
- Change detection.
- Error translation.
- Revision handling.
- Save behavior.
- Conflict detection.

Provider integration tests shall supplement end-to-end testing.

### Accessibility Testing

Complete Google Drive workflows shall be tested with multiple assistive
technologies and users with diverse disabilities.

Testing shall include:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only users.
- Low-vision users.
- Screen magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- Other assistive technologies as appropriate.

Testing shall include actual end-to-end workflows rather than isolated
controls.

### Documentation

ART documentation shall explain:

- How to connect Google Drive.
- What permissions ART requests.
- How to select an ART folder.
- How to open `.art` files from Google Drive.
- How to save `.art` files.
- How synchronization works.
- How file-based collaboration works.
- How merge conflicts work.
- How to disconnect Google Drive.
- What happens when Google Drive is unavailable.
- How Google Drive permissions affect ART.
- How Google Drive collaboration differs from server-based
  collaboration.
- Security and privacy considerations.

Documentation shall clearly state that Google Drive storage does not
provide ART's full real-time server collaboration capabilities.

### Backward Compatibility

The Google Drive integration shall not alter the `.art` file format in a
way that prevents existing ART files from opening.

Existing local files shall continue to work.

Existing import/export functionality shall remain available.

Users shall be able to move `.art` files between local storage and
Google Drive without losing supported ART data.

### Future Provider Compatibility

The implementation shall not introduce Google Drive-specific assumptions
into ART's core architecture that would prevent future providers from
being implemented.

The same Storage Provider Interface shall remain usable for:

- Microsoft OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Network storage.
- Other cloud-storage providers.
- ART Server.

### Definition of Done

Epic 52 shall be considered complete when:

- Google Drive is implemented as a Storage Provider using the Epic 51
  architecture.
- Users can optionally connect Google Drive.
- Google OAuth authentication is implemented securely.
- ART does not store Google passwords.
- Minimum necessary Google Drive permissions are requested.
- Users can browse Google Drive folders.
- Users can select an ART storage folder.
- Users can create `.art` files in Google Drive.
- Users can open `.art` files from Google Drive.
- Users can save `.art` files to Google Drive.
- Save As functionality works with Google Drive.
- External changes can be detected.
- Compatible changes can be synchronized.
- Merge conflicts invoke ART's existing Merge Changes functionality.
- Concurrent editing has been tested.
- File-based collaboration works through Google Drive.
- Shared folders work appropriately.
- Google Drive permissions are respected.
- User identity information is preserved.
- Device-linked ART identities work with file-based collaboration.
- Tasks can be shared through `.art` files.
- Shared Progress Logs can be shared through `.art` files.
- @mentions are preserved within shared `.art` files.
- Organization folders can be used where permissions permit.
- Organization Metrics can use supported `.art` files where implemented.
- Offline behavior protects user work.
- Failed saves do not silently discard changes.
- OAuth expiration and revocation are handled correctly.
- Users can disconnect Google Drive.
- All Google Drive commands integrate with ART's command architecture.
- Keyboard shortcuts remain customizable.
- Google Drive workflows are accessible to keyboard users.
- Google Drive workflows are accessible to screen readers.
- Google Drive workflows have been tested with JAWS, NVDA, Narrator,
  VoiceOver, TalkBack, ChromeVox, and braille displays.
- Low-vision and visual accessibility testing has been completed.
- Automated provider tests have been implemented.
- End-to-end collaboration testing has been completed.
- Security and privacy requirements have been reviewed.
- Documentation has been completed.
- Existing ART functionality has not regressed.
- The implementation does not prevent future OneDrive, Dropbox, or ART
  Server providers from using the Storage Provider Interface.

## Epic 53 — Microsoft OneDrive Storage Integration

### Epic Overview

Implement Microsoft OneDrive as the second external cloud-storage
provider using the provider-independent Storage Provider Architecture
established in Epic 51.

ART shall allow users to optionally connect Microsoft OneDrive and work
with `.art` files stored in OneDrive without requiring an ART server.

OneDrive integration shall support ART's file-based collaboration model,
allowing multiple users to share `.art` files through OneDrive or shared
folders while ART detects external changes and uses its existing Merge
Changes functionality when conflicts occur.

ART shall remain fully functional without OneDrive, without an ART
account, and without an ART server.

### Goals

The OneDrive integration shall:

- Allow users to optionally connect Microsoft OneDrive to ART.
- Use Microsoft's supported OAuth authentication mechanism.
- Support Microsoft account authentication.
- Support Microsoft 365 organizational accounts where technically
  appropriate.
- Request only the minimum permissions required.
- Never store a Microsoft password in ART.
- Protect OAuth tokens and other credentials.
- Allow users to browse OneDrive files and folders.
- Allow users to select an ART storage folder.
- Open `.art` files directly from OneDrive.
- Save `.art` files directly to OneDrive.
- Create new `.art` files in OneDrive.
- Save modified `.art` files back to OneDrive.
- Detect changes made by other users.
- Support asynchronous file-based collaboration.
- Support synchronized/shared OneDrive folders.
- Integrate with ART's existing Merge Changes functionality.
- Preserve user identity information within shared ART files.
- Support file-based @mentions where applicable.
- Support shared projects, reports, tasks, Progress Logs, and other
  supported ART data.
- Preserve local-first operation when OneDrive is unavailable or
  disconnected.
- Provide accessible status information and controls.
- Provide a foundation for future Microsoft 365 and enterprise
  integrations.

### Relationship to Epic 51

Epic 53 shall implement the Microsoft OneDrive-specific provider using
the provider-independent architecture established in Epic 51.

The OneDrive provider shall not bypass the Storage Provider Interface.

Conceptually:

``` text
ART Core
    |
    +-- Storage Provider Interface
            |
            +-- Local File Provider
            +-- Google Drive Provider
            +-- OneDrive Provider
```

ART's core reporting, project, task, collaboration, and merge-conflict
functionality shall remain independent of Microsoft OneDrive.

### Microsoft Authentication

ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for connecting a Microsoft
account to OneDrive.

The user shall be able to:

- Connect OneDrive.
- View the currently connected Microsoft account when supported.
- Disconnect OneDrive.
- Reconnect OneDrive.
- Change the Microsoft account used by ART.
- View the current connection status.

Connecting OneDrive shall be optional.

### OAuth Authentication

The OneDrive integration shall use Microsoft's supported OAuth
authorization process and Microsoft identity platform.

ART shall:

- Invoke the appropriate Microsoft authentication workflow.
- Allow the user to select the Microsoft account they want to use.
- Clearly communicate the permissions being requested.
- Request only the minimum required permissions.
- Never request the user's Microsoft password.
- Never store the user's Microsoft password.
- Securely store or protect OAuth tokens as appropriate for the
  platform.
- Handle expired tokens.
- Handle revoked authorization.
- Handle denied authorization.
- Provide an accessible mechanism to retry authorization.
- Provide accessible authentication error messages.

ART shall not embed or hard-code user credentials.

### Microsoft Account Types

Where supported by the Microsoft APIs and ART's implementation, the
integration should accommodate:

- Personal Microsoft accounts.
- Microsoft 365 accounts.
- Organizational Microsoft accounts.
- Education accounts.

The interface shall clearly identify account or organizational
restrictions when applicable.

If an organization has disabled third-party application access, ART
shall provide an understandable message explaining that organizational
authorization is required.

### OneDrive Permissions

The integration shall follow the principle of least privilege.

ART shall request only the permissions necessary to perform the
functions the user has selected.

ART shall respect permissions established by Microsoft OneDrive and
Microsoft 365 administrators.

ART shall not attempt to bypass organizational restrictions.

### OneDrive Storage Selection

After connecting OneDrive, ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for
selecting a OneDrive folder to use for ART files.

The user shall be able to:

- Browse folders.
- Open folders.
- Select a folder.
- Create an ART folder.
- Change the selected ART folder.
- View the current selected folder.
- Return to the root or another available location.
- Cancel folder selection.

The folder-selection interface shall support keyboard navigation and
screen readers.

### ART Folder

ART should provide an option to create a dedicated folder for ART files,
such as:

``` text
ART/
```

or a user-defined folder name.

Users shall also be able to select an existing OneDrive folder.

ART shall not require users to create a dedicated folder if they prefer
to use an existing OneDrive folder.

### OneDrive File Browser

ART shall provide an accessible file browser for supported OneDrive
locations.

The file browser shall allow users to:

- Browse folders.
- Open folders.
- View `.art` files.
- Open `.art` files.
- Create new `.art` files.
- Rename files where permitted.
- Move files where permitted.
- Copy files where supported.
- Delete files where permitted.
- Refresh folder contents.
- View relevant file information.

The interface shall clearly distinguish `.art` files from unsupported
file types.

### Opening an ART File

When the user opens an `.art` file from OneDrive, ART shall:

1.  Retrieve the file.
2.  Validate that it is a supported ART file.
3.  Load the report/project data.
4.  Record relevant file and revision information.
5.  Begin monitoring for external changes where supported.
6.  Display the appropriate storage and synchronization status.

The user shall receive accessible feedback while the file is being
loaded.

### Saving an ART File

When the user saves an `.art` file stored in OneDrive, ART shall:

1.  Determine whether the remote file has changed since the user's
    current version was retrieved.
2.  Preserve the user's current work.
3.  Retrieve the latest remote version when necessary.
4.  Compare the relevant versions.
5.  Automatically incorporate compatible changes.
6.  Identify conflicting changes.
7.  Open the Merge Changes interface when user intervention is required.
8.  Save the resulting version to OneDrive.
9.  Update local revision information.

ART shall not silently overwrite a newer remote version when doing so
could cause another user's work to be lost.

### Save As

ART shall support saving an existing report/project as a new `.art` file
in OneDrive.

The user shall be able to:

- Select a OneDrive folder.
- Specify a filename.
- Confirm the save.
- Cancel the operation.

If the destination file already exists, ART shall provide an accessible
confirmation or conflict workflow rather than silently overwriting it.

### External Change Detection

ART shall detect when a OneDrive `.art` file has changed since it was
last retrieved or saved.

Where Microsoft Graph provides reliable revision or change information,
ART shall use that information rather than relying solely on timestamps.

ART shall distinguish between:

- No remote change.
- Remote change with no local unsaved changes.
- Remote change with local unsaved changes.
- Remote change containing compatible changes.
- Remote change containing conflicting changes.

### Automatic Synchronization of Compatible Changes

When a remote `.art` file has changed and the user's local changes do
not conflict with the remote changes, ART should automatically merge
compatible changes where technically and safely possible.

The user shall be informed that remote changes were incorporated.

ART shall preserve appropriate History Framework information so
supported changes can be undone where appropriate.

### Merge Conflicts

When OneDrive contains changes that conflict with the user's local
changes, ART shall use the existing Merge Changes functionality.

The Merge Changes interface shall:

- Identify conflicting changes.
- Identify the users associated with changes when identity information
  is available.
- Clearly distinguish local and remote changes.
- Allow the user to choose which changes to keep.
- Allow supported changes to be combined.
- Preserve non-conflicting changes.
- Provide accessible descriptions of conflicts.
- Support keyboard operation.
- Work with screen readers.
- Allow the user to cancel or defer conflict resolution where
  appropriate.

The OneDrive provider shall not implement separate merge logic.

### File-Based Collaboration

OneDrive shall serve as a storage and synchronization mechanism for
ART's file-based collaboration model.

Multiple users shall be able to collaborate through shared OneDrive
folders.

For example:

``` text
Shared OneDrive Folder
        |
        +-- Audit Project.art
        |
        +-- Progress Log.art
        |
        +-- Tasks.art
        |
        +-- Other Reports.art
```

Users shall be able to open and modify shared `.art` files according to
their OneDrive permissions.

### Asynchronous Collaboration

OneDrive collaboration shall primarily support asynchronous file-based
collaboration.

For example:

``` text
User A
  |
  | Opens report
  | Makes changes
  | Saves
  v
OneDrive
  |
  | Synchronizes
  v
User B
  |
  | Opens/refreshes report
  | Detects changes
  v
ART
```

ART shall not claim to provide real-time collaborative editing merely
because a file is stored in OneDrive.

### Concurrent Editing

When two or more users have the same `.art` file open simultaneously,
each user's local copy shall remain independent until changes are saved
or synchronized.

ART shall detect remote changes when the user:

- Saves.
- Refreshes.
- Reopens the file.
- Performs another supported synchronization operation.

When conflicts occur, the Merge Changes interface shall be presented to
the appropriate user.

### File Revision Information

Where Microsoft Graph exposes file revision information, ART shall
record sufficient information to determine which remote version the user
last accessed.

ART should use revision information to improve:

- Change detection.
- Conflict detection.
- Synchronization reliability.
- Recovery from failed saves.

Provider-specific revision identifiers shall remain isolated within the
OneDrive provider implementation.

### OneDrive Shared Folders

ART shall support `.art` files stored in OneDrive folders shared with
other users.

The integration shall respect OneDrive's existing sharing permissions.

ART shall not duplicate OneDrive permissions internally.

If a user has:

- View-only access, ART shall not present editing functionality as
  available.
- Edit access, ART may allow supported ART editing operations.
- No access, ART shall report that the file is unavailable.

### Microsoft 365 and SharePoint-Backed Storage

Where OneDrive and Microsoft Graph expose SharePoint-backed document
