libraries through the same supported storage APIs, the architecture
should be designed so that future SharePoint support can be added
without redesigning ART's storage architecture.

This epic does not require full SharePoint integration unless it is
necessary to implement the OneDrive provider.

Any Microsoft 365 or SharePoint limitations shall be documented.

### Shared Organizational Folders

OneDrive shall support the organization-folder model established in Epic
49.

An organization may configure a shared parent folder such as:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
    |
    +-- Project A/
    |
    +-- Project B/
    |
    +-- Progress Logs/
    |
    +-- Tasks/
    |
    +-- Organization Metrics/
```

Where Microsoft permissions provide inherited access, ART shall respect
those permissions.

### Organization Metrics

Where supported, ART shall allow Organization Metrics to use `.art`
files stored in a configured OneDrive organization folder.

ART shall:

- Identify supported ART files.
- Process supported data.
- Ignore unsupported files.
- Respect OneDrive permissions.
- Update metrics when relevant ART files change.
- Avoid modifying source files merely to calculate metrics.

Metrics synchronization shall remain subject to OneDrive synchronization
behavior.

### Tasks and To Do Lists

OneDrive storage shall support file-based task collaboration.

Shared `.art` data may contain:

- Assigned tasks.
- Shared tasks.
- Task status.
- Task priority.
- Due dates.
- Comments/notes/instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Task history.
- Assignment information.

Changes shall synchronize through the `.art` file.

### Shared Progress Logs

OneDrive shall support file-based Shared Progress Logs.

Shared Progress Log data may include:

- Tasks.
- Assignments.
- Status.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- User identity.
- Progress information.
- History.

Changes shall be preserved in the `.art` file and merged when
compatible.

### @Mentions

The OneDrive integration shall preserve @mentions contained within
shared ART files.

A user shall be able to mention another collaborator using ART's
existing @mention functionality.

The stored collaboration data shall preserve sufficient information to
identify:

- The user creating the mention.
- The mentioned user.
- The associated comment.
- The associated task, report, project, or workspace.
- Relevant date/time information.

When an ART server is unavailable, file-based @mention data shall remain
within the shared `.art` file.

Server-based email or dashboard notifications may be implemented
separately when an ART server is available.

### User Identity

OneDrive collaboration shall use ART user identity information
established by Epics 49 and 50.

Where possible, changes shall identify the ART user responsible for the
change.

ART shall not rely solely on a Microsoft account display name to
identify an ART user.

The ART identity associated with a change shall remain distinguishable
from the Microsoft account used to access the storage provider.

### Device Linking

OneDrive file-based collaboration shall work with the device-linking
functionality established in Epic 50.

A user's multiple ART installations may be associated with the same ART
identity.

For example:

``` text
User A
  |
  +-- ART Web
  |
  +-- ART Desktop
  |
  +-- ART on Device 2
  |
  +-- ART on Device 3
```

The storage provider shall not be responsible for determining ART
identity.

ART shall use its own identity and device-linking mechanisms.

### File Ownership

ART shall distinguish between:

- The Microsoft account that owns a OneDrive file.
- The Microsoft 365 organization that controls a file.
- The ART user who created or modified content within the file.

OneDrive ownership and permissions shall remain controlled by Microsoft.

ART collaboration metadata shall identify ART users independently where
appropriate.

### Offline Operation

ART shall remain usable when OneDrive is temporarily unavailable.

If the user's current `.art` file has already been loaded:

- The user shall be able to continue working locally.
- Unsaved changes shall be preserved.
- ART shall not silently discard work.
- The user shall receive an accessible indication that OneDrive is
  unavailable.
- The user should be able to save/export a local copy when possible.

When OneDrive becomes available again, ART shall allow the user to
refresh or synchronize the file.

### Failed Saves

If ART cannot save changes to OneDrive, it shall:

- Preserve the user's current work.
- Clearly identify that the save failed.
- Explain the likely reason when known.
- Provide an opportunity to retry.
- Provide an option to save/export a local copy where appropriate.
- Avoid falsely indicating that the remote file was updated.

### Authentication Expiration

When Microsoft OAuth authorization expires or is revoked, ART shall:

- Detect the authentication failure.
- Preserve unsaved work.
- Inform the user.
- Provide an accessible option to reconnect.
- Avoid repeatedly displaying authentication errors unnecessarily.

### Disconnecting OneDrive

Users shall be able to disconnect OneDrive from ART.

Disconnecting shall:

- Remove the local connection to the provider.
- Prevent future OneDrive operations until the user reconnects.
- Preserve local `.art` files.
- Not delete OneDrive files.
- Not delete the user's Microsoft account.
- Not modify OneDrive permissions unless the user explicitly chooses an
  appropriate revocation option.

### Security

The OneDrive integration shall comply with the security requirements
established in Epics 47–52.

ART shall:

- Use secure OAuth authorization.
- Request minimum necessary permissions.
- Protect OAuth tokens.
- Avoid storing Microsoft passwords.
- Avoid logging sensitive credentials.
- Validate downloaded files.
- Validate Microsoft Graph responses.
- Protect against malicious or malformed `.art` files.
- Avoid unnecessary access to unrelated OneDrive content.
- Respect Microsoft and OneDrive permissions.
- Handle revoked credentials securely.
- Respect organizational security policies.

### Data Privacy

ART shall clearly communicate what OneDrive data it accesses.

ART shall not access unrelated OneDrive files merely because OneDrive is
connected.

Where possible, users shall be able to limit ART's access to designated
ART folders or files.

### Organizational Restrictions

Some Microsoft 365 organizations may restrict:

- OAuth applications.
- Third-party applications.
- External sharing.
- File downloads.
- File uploads.
- Access to certain OneDrive resources.

ART shall detect relevant restrictions where possible and provide
understandable error messages.

ART shall not attempt to circumvent organizational security controls.

### Accessibility

All OneDrive functionality shall conform to ART's accessibility
requirements.

This includes:

- Connecting OneDrive.
- OAuth authentication.
- Account selection.
- Folder selection.
- File browsing.
- File opening.
- File saving.
- Save As.
- Refreshing.
- Synchronization.
- Conflict detection.
- Merge Changes.
- Error handling.
- Disconnecting OneDrive.

All functionality shall be accessible using the keyboard.

All important status changes shall be programmatically exposed.

### Screen Reader Support

OneDrive integration shall be tested with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.

Screen readers shall receive meaningful information about:

- Current storage provider.
- Current account.
- Current file.
- Current folder.
- Synchronization state.
- External changes.
- Save status.
- Authentication status.
- Errors.
- Merge conflicts.

### Low-Vision and Visual Accessibility

OneDrive integration shall be tested using:

- Browser zoom.
- Operating-system magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- ART visual settings.
- Different display sizes.
- Different display scaling levels.

The interface shall not rely solely on color, spatial position, or
visual indicators.

### Keyboard Commands

OneDrive-related commands shall integrate with ART's command
architecture.

Commands shall be available through appropriate:

- Menubar menus.
- Global context menus.
- File/folder context menus.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

Potential commands include:

- Connect OneDrive.
- Disconnect OneDrive.
- Open from OneDrive.
- Save to OneDrive.
- Save As to OneDrive.
- Refresh from OneDrive.
- Synchronize.
- Resolve Merge Conflicts.
- Select OneDrive Folder.
- View File Information.

### Context Menu Integration

Where appropriate, users shall be able to access OneDrive commands from
context menus.

Context menus shall expose only commands appropriate to the selected
object and the user's permissions.

Disabled commands shall communicate why they are unavailable where
appropriate.

### History Framework

OneDrive-related ART content changes shall integrate with ART's History
Framework where appropriate.

The History Framework shall support Undo/Redo for applicable ART content
changes resulting from synchronization or merge operations.

Provider connection and authentication actions shall not necessarily be
treated as ordinary document edits unless explicitly designed to be
reversible.

### Notifications

ART shall provide accessible notifications for important OneDrive
events, including:

- File changed externally.
- Remote changes successfully synchronized.
- Merge conflict detected.
- Save successful.
- Save failed.
- OneDrive unavailable.
- Authentication expired.
- Permission denied.
- File deleted.
- File moved.
- File renamed.
- Organization access denied.

Notifications shall not rely exclusively on transient visual messages.

### Error Handling

OneDrive errors shall be translated into understandable ART messages.

The system shall distinguish among:

- Authentication failure.
- Authorization failure.
- File not found.
- Folder not found.
- Permission denied.
- OneDrive unavailable.
- Network failure.
- Storage limitations.
- File changed externally.
- Merge conflict.
- Save failure.
- Unsupported file.
- Corrupted ART file.
- Revoked authorization.
- Organization policy restriction.

### File Integrity

ART shall protect `.art` file integrity during OneDrive operations.

The integration shall avoid:

- Partial writes.
- Silent overwriting.
- Corrupted saves.
- Lost changes.
- Incorrect revision tracking.
- Loss of ART metadata.

Where possible, ART shall use a safe-write process.

### Large Files

The OneDrive provider shall support `.art` files of realistic production
sizes.

Testing shall identify:

- Maximum practical file size.
- Upload/download performance.
- Timeout behavior.
- Interrupted transfers.
- Recovery behavior.

ART shall provide useful feedback when large files require additional
processing time.

### Network Interruptions

ART shall gracefully handle interruptions during:

- Authentication.
- File download.
- File upload.
- Save.
- Refresh.
- Synchronization.
- Merge preparation.

The user's work shall not be silently lost because of a network
interruption.

### Concurrent Editing Testing

The integration shall be tested with at least two users.

Testing shall include:

1.  User A opens a report.
2.  User B opens the same report.
3.  User A makes a change.
4.  User A saves.
5.  User B refreshes.
6.  User B sees User A's change.
7.  User B makes another change.
8.  User B saves.
9.  User A refreshes.
10. User A sees User B's change.

Additional testing shall verify conflicting edits.

### Merge Conflict Testing

Testing shall include:

1.  User A opens a report.
2.  User B opens the same report.
3.  User A changes one value.
4.  User B changes the same value differently.
5.  User A saves.
6.  User B saves or refreshes.
7.  ART detects the conflict.
8.  The Merge Changes modal opens.
9.  User B chooses the desired version.
10. ART creates the merged result.
11. The merged result is saved.
12. User A subsequently opens or refreshes the file.
13. User A sees the merged result.

### File-Based Collaboration Testing

Testing shall verify:

- Multiple users.
- Multiple devices.
- Shared folders.
- Asynchronous collaboration.
- Concurrent editing.
- Compatible changes.
- Conflicting changes.
- Merge resolution.
- User identity.
- Device linking.
- Task assignments.
- Shared To Do Lists.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- @mentions\.
- Organization folders.
- Organization Metrics.

### OneDrive Permission Testing

Test scenarios shall include:

- File owner.
- Editor.
- Viewer.
- Shared-folder member.
- Removed user.
- Permission changed while a file is open.
- File moved.
- File deleted.
- Folder access revoked.
- Organizational policy restrictions.
- Microsoft 365 account restrictions.
- Personal Microsoft account.
- Organizational Microsoft account.

ART shall accurately respond to the permissions returned by Microsoft.

### Microsoft 365 Organizational Testing

Where access is available, testing should include representative
organizational environments.

Testing should verify:

- Administrator-controlled application permissions.
- OAuth approval workflows.
- Restricted third-party applications.
- Shared folders.
- Organizational file ownership.
- User removal.
- Account deactivation.
- Permission changes.
- External sharing restrictions.

### Automated Testing

Automated tests shall validate the OneDrive provider implementation
against the common Storage Provider Interface.

Testing shall verify:

- Authentication state handling.
- Provider connection state.
- File operations.
- Folder operations.
- Metadata retrieval.
- Change detection.
- Error translation.
- Revision handling.
- Save behavior.
- Conflict detection.

Provider integration tests shall supplement end-to-end testing.

### Accessibility Testing

Complete OneDrive workflows shall be tested with multiple assistive
technologies and users with diverse disabilities.

Testing shall include:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only users.
- Low-vision users.
- Screen magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- Other assistive technologies as appropriate.

Testing shall include actual end-to-end workflows rather than isolated
controls.

### Documentation

ART documentation shall explain:

- How to connect OneDrive.
- What Microsoft permissions ART requests.
- How to select an ART folder.
- How to open `.art` files from OneDrive.
- How to save `.art` files.
- How synchronization works.
- How file-based collaboration works.
- How merge conflicts work.
- How to disconnect OneDrive.
- What happens when OneDrive is unavailable.
- How OneDrive permissions affect ART.
- How organizational policies can affect ART.
- How OneDrive collaboration differs from server-based collaboration.
- Security and privacy considerations.

Documentation shall clearly state that OneDrive storage does not provide
ART's full real-time server collaboration capabilities.

### Backward Compatibility

The OneDrive integration shall not alter the `.art` file format in a way
that prevents existing ART files from opening.

Existing local files shall continue to work.

Existing import/export functionality shall remain available.

Users shall be able to move `.art` files between local storage, Google
Drive, and OneDrive without losing supported ART data.

### Future Provider Compatibility

The implementation shall not introduce OneDrive-specific assumptions
into ART's core architecture that would prevent future providers from
being implemented.

The same Storage Provider Interface shall remain usable for:

- Dropbox.
- Network storage.
- Additional cloud-storage providers.
- SharePoint.
- Private cloud storage.
- ART Server.

### Definition of Done

Epic 53 shall be considered complete when:

- Microsoft OneDrive is implemented as a Storage Provider using the Epic
  51 architecture.
- Users can optionally connect OneDrive.
- Microsoft OAuth authentication is implemented securely.
- ART does not store Microsoft passwords.
- Minimum necessary Microsoft permissions are requested.
- Users can browse OneDrive folders.
- Users can select an ART storage folder.
- Users can create `.art` files in OneDrive.
- Users can open `.art` files from OneDrive.
- Users can save `.art` files to OneDrive.
- Save As functionality works with OneDrive.
- External changes can be detected.
- Compatible changes can be synchronized.
- Merge conflicts invoke ART's existing Merge Changes functionality.
- Concurrent editing has been tested.
- File-based collaboration works through OneDrive.
- Shared folders work appropriately.
- OneDrive permissions are respected.
- Microsoft 365 organizational restrictions are handled appropriately.
- User identity information is preserved.
- Device-linked ART identities work with file-based collaboration.
- Tasks can be shared through `.art` files.
- Shared To Do Lists can be shared through `.art` files.
- Shared Progress Logs can be shared through `.art` files.
- @mentions are preserved within shared `.art` files.
- Organization folders can be used where permissions permit.
- Organization Metrics can use supported `.art` files where implemented.
- Offline behavior protects user work.
- Failed saves do not silently discard changes.
- OAuth expiration and revocation are handled correctly.
- Users can disconnect OneDrive.
- All OneDrive commands integrate with ART's command architecture.
- Keyboard shortcuts remain customizable.
- OneDrive workflows are accessible to keyboard users.
- OneDrive workflows are accessible to screen readers.
- OneDrive workflows have been tested with JAWS, NVDA, Narrator,
  VoiceOver, TalkBack, ChromeVox, and braille displays.
- Low-vision and visual accessibility testing has been completed.
- Automated provider tests have been implemented.
- End-to-end collaboration testing has been completed.
- Security and privacy requirements have been reviewed.
- Documentation has been completed.
- Existing ART functionality has not regressed.
- The implementation does not prevent future Dropbox, SharePoint,
  network-storage, or ART Server providers from using the Storage
  Provider Interface.

## Epic 54 — Dropbox Storage Integration

### Epic Overview

Implement Dropbox as the third external cloud-storage provider using the
provider-independent Storage Provider Architecture established in Epic
51.

ART shall allow users to optionally connect Dropbox and work with `.art`
files stored in Dropbox without requiring an ART server.

Dropbox integration shall support ART's file-based collaboration model,
allowing multiple users to share `.art` files through Dropbox or shared
folders while ART detects external changes and uses its existing Merge
Changes functionality when conflicts occur.

ART shall remain fully functional without Dropbox, without an ART
account, and without an ART server.

### Goals

The Dropbox integration shall:

- Allow users to optionally connect Dropbox to ART.
- Use Dropbox's supported OAuth authentication mechanism.
- Request only the minimum permissions required.
- Never store a Dropbox password in ART.
- Protect OAuth tokens and other credentials.
- Allow users to browse Dropbox files and folders.
- Allow users to select an ART storage folder.
- Open `.art` files directly from Dropbox.
- Save `.art` files directly to Dropbox.
- Create new `.art` files in Dropbox.
- Save modified `.art` files back to Dropbox.
- Detect changes made by other users.
- Support asynchronous file-based collaboration.
- Support synchronized/shared Dropbox folders.
- Integrate with ART's existing Merge Changes functionality.
- Preserve user identity information within shared ART files.
- Support file-based @mentions where applicable.
- Support shared projects, reports, tasks, To Do Lists, Progress Logs,
  and other supported ART data.
- Preserve local-first operation when Dropbox is unavailable or
  disconnected.
- Provide accessible status information and controls.
- Maintain compatibility with the provider-independent storage
  architecture.
- Provide a foundation for additional storage providers and future ART
  Server integration.

### Relationship to Epic 51

Epic 54 shall implement the Dropbox-specific provider using the
provider-independent architecture established in Epic 51.

The Dropbox provider shall not bypass the Storage Provider Interface.

Conceptually:

``` text
ART Core
    |
    +-- Storage Provider Interface
            |
            +-- Local File Provider
            +-- Google Drive Provider
            +-- OneDrive Provider
            +-- Dropbox Provider
```

ART's core reporting, project, task, collaboration, and merge-conflict
functionality shall remain independent of Dropbox.

### Dropbox Connection

ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for connecting a Dropbox
account.

The user shall be able to:

- Connect Dropbox.
- View the currently connected Dropbox account when supported.
- Disconnect Dropbox.
- Reconnect Dropbox.
- Change the Dropbox account used by ART.
- View the current connection status.

Connecting Dropbox shall be optional.

### OAuth Authentication

The Dropbox integration shall use Dropbox's supported OAuth
authorization process.

ART shall:

- Invoke the appropriate Dropbox authentication workflow.
- Allow the user to authorize the Dropbox account they want to use.
- Clearly communicate the permissions being requested.
- Request only the minimum required permissions.
- Never request the user's Dropbox password.
- Never store the user's Dropbox password.
- Securely store or protect OAuth tokens as appropriate for the
  platform.
- Handle expired tokens.
- Handle revoked authorization.
- Handle denied authorization.
- Provide an accessible mechanism to retry authorization.
- Provide accessible authentication error messages.

ART shall not embed or hard-code user credentials.

### Dropbox Permissions

The integration shall follow the principle of least privilege.

ART shall request only the permissions necessary to perform the
functions the user has selected.

Where Dropbox provides a choice between application-specific folders and
broader Dropbox access, ART should use the narrowest appropriate access
model.

ART shall respect permissions established by Dropbox.

ART shall not attempt to bypass Dropbox access controls.

### Dropbox Storage Selection

After connecting Dropbox, ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for
selecting a Dropbox folder to use for ART files.

The user shall be able to:

- Browse folders.
- Open folders.
- Select a folder.
- Create an ART folder.
- Change the selected ART folder.
- View the current selected folder.
- Return to the root or another available location.
- Cancel folder selection.

The folder-selection interface shall support keyboard navigation and
screen readers.

### ART Folder

ART should provide an option to create a dedicated folder for ART files,
such as:

``` text
ART/
```

or a user-defined folder name.

Users shall also be able to select an existing Dropbox folder.

ART shall not require users to create a dedicated folder if they prefer
to use an existing Dropbox folder.

### Dropbox File Browser

ART shall provide an accessible file browser for supported Dropbox
locations.

The file browser shall allow users to:

- Browse folders.
- Open folders.
- View `.art` files.
- Open `.art` files.
- Create new `.art` files.
- Rename files where permitted.
- Move files where permitted.
- Copy files where supported.
- Delete files where permitted.
- Refresh folder contents.
- View relevant file information.

The interface shall clearly distinguish `.art` files from unsupported
file types.

### Opening an ART File

When the user opens an `.art` file from Dropbox, ART shall:

1.  Retrieve the file.
2.  Validate that it is a supported ART file.
3.  Load the report/project data.
4.  Record relevant file and revision information.
5.  Begin monitoring for external changes where supported.
6.  Display the appropriate storage and synchronization status.

The user shall receive accessible feedback while the file is being
loaded.

### Saving an ART File

When the user saves an `.art` file stored in Dropbox, ART shall:

1.  Determine whether the remote file has changed since the user's
    current version was retrieved.
2.  Preserve the user's current work.
3.  Retrieve the latest remote version when necessary.
4.  Compare the relevant versions.
5.  Automatically incorporate compatible changes.
6.  Identify conflicting changes.
7.  Open the Merge Changes interface when user intervention is required.
8.  Save the resulting version to Dropbox.
9.  Update local revision information.

ART shall not silently overwrite a newer remote version when doing so
could cause another user's work to be lost.

### Save As

ART shall support saving an existing report/project as a new `.art` file
in Dropbox.

The user shall be able to:

- Select a Dropbox folder.
- Specify a filename.
- Confirm the save.
- Cancel the operation.

If the destination file already exists, ART shall provide an accessible
confirmation or conflict workflow rather than silently overwriting it.

### External Change Detection

ART shall detect when a Dropbox `.art` file has changed since it was
last retrieved or saved.

Where Dropbox provides reliable revision identifiers or file metadata,
ART shall use that information rather than relying solely on timestamps.

ART shall distinguish between:

- No remote change.
- Remote change with no local unsaved changes.
- Remote change with local unsaved changes.
- Remote change containing compatible changes.
- Remote change containing conflicting changes.

### Automatic Synchronization of Compatible Changes

When a remote `.art` file has changed and the user's local changes do
not conflict with the remote changes, ART should automatically merge
compatible changes where technically and safely possible.

The user shall be informed that remote changes were incorporated.

ART shall preserve appropriate History Framework information so
supported changes can be undone where appropriate.

### Merge Conflicts

When Dropbox contains changes that conflict with the user's local
changes, ART shall use the existing Merge Changes functionality.

The Merge Changes interface shall:

- Identify conflicting changes.
- Identify the users associated with changes when identity information
  is available.
- Clearly distinguish local and remote changes.
- Allow the user to choose which changes to keep.
- Allow supported changes to be combined.
- Preserve non-conflicting changes.
- Provide accessible descriptions of conflicts.
- Support keyboard operation.
- Work with screen readers.
- Allow the user to cancel or defer conflict resolution where
  appropriate.

The Dropbox provider shall not implement separate merge logic.

### File-Based Collaboration

Dropbox shall serve as a storage and synchronization mechanism for ART's
file-based collaboration model.

Multiple users shall be able to collaborate through shared Dropbox
folders.

For example:

``` text
Shared Dropbox Folder
        |
        +-- Audit Project.art
        |
        +-- Progress Log.art
        |
        +-- Tasks.art
        |
        +-- Other Reports.art
```

Users shall be able to open and modify shared `.art` files according to
their Dropbox permissions.

### Asynchronous Collaboration

Dropbox collaboration shall primarily support asynchronous file-based
collaboration.

For example:

``` text
User A
  |
  | Opens report
  | Makes changes
  | Saves
  v
Dropbox
  |
  | Synchronizes
  v
User B
  |
  | Opens/refreshes report
  | Detects changes
  v
ART
```

ART shall not claim to provide real-time collaborative editing merely
because a file is stored in Dropbox.

### Concurrent Editing

When two or more users have the same `.art` file open simultaneously,
each user's local copy shall remain independent until changes are saved
or synchronized.

ART shall detect remote changes when the user:

- Saves.
- Refreshes.
- Reopens the file.
- Performs another supported synchronization operation.

When conflicts occur, the Merge Changes interface shall be presented to
the appropriate user.

### File Revision Information

Where Dropbox exposes revision information, ART shall record sufficient
information to determine which remote version the user last accessed.

ART should use revision information to improve:

- Change detection.
- Conflict detection.
- Synchronization reliability.
- Recovery from failed saves.

Provider-specific revision identifiers shall remain isolated within the
Dropbox provider implementation.

### Dropbox Shared Folders

ART shall support `.art` files stored in Dropbox folders shared with
other users.

The integration shall respect Dropbox's existing sharing permissions.

ART shall not duplicate Dropbox permissions internally.

If a user has:

- View-only access, ART shall not present editing functionality as
  available.
- Edit access, ART may allow supported ART editing operations.
- No access, ART shall report that the file is unavailable.

### Shared Team and Organizational Storage

Where supported by Dropbox account and folder capabilities, ART shall
work with shared organizational folders.

An organization may configure a shared parent folder such as:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
    |
    +-- Project A/
    |
    +-- Project B/
    |
    +-- Progress Logs/
    |
    +-- Tasks/
    |
    +-- Organization Metrics/
```

ART shall respect the permissions provided by Dropbox.

ART shall not attempt to recreate Dropbox's folder-sharing or
organizational permission model internally.

### Organization Metrics

Where supported, ART shall allow Organization Metrics to use `.art`
files stored in a configured Dropbox organization folder.

ART shall:

- Identify supported ART files.
- Process supported data.
- Ignore unsupported files.
- Respect Dropbox permissions.
- Update metrics when relevant ART files change.
- Avoid modifying source files merely to calculate metrics.

Metrics synchronization shall remain subject to Dropbox synchronization
behavior.

### Tasks and To Do Lists

Dropbox storage shall support file-based task collaboration.

Shared `.art` data may contain:

- Assigned tasks.
- Shared tasks.
- Personal To Do items when intentionally included in a shared artifact.
- Task status.
- Task priority.
- Due dates.
- Comments/notes/instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Task history.
- Assignment information.

Changes shall synchronize through the `.art` file.

### Shared Progress Logs

Dropbox shall support file-based Shared Progress Logs.

Shared Progress Log data may include:

- Tasks.
- Assignments.
- Status.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- User identity.
- Progress information.
- History.

Changes shall be preserved in the `.art` file and merged when
compatible.

### @Mentions

The Dropbox integration shall preserve @mentions contained within shared
ART files.

A user shall be able to mention another collaborator using ART's
existing @mention functionality.

The stored collaboration data shall preserve sufficient information to
identify:

- The user creating the mention.
- The mentioned user.
- The associated comment.
- The associated task, report, project, workspace, or shared
  organization folder.
- Relevant date/time information.

When an ART server is unavailable, file-based @mention data shall remain
within the shared `.art` file.

Server-based email or dashboard notifications may be implemented
separately when an ART server is available.

### User Identity

Dropbox collaboration shall use ART user identity information
established by Epics 49 and 50.

Where possible, changes shall identify the ART user responsible for the
change.

ART shall not rely solely on a Dropbox account display name to identify
an ART user.

The ART identity associated with a change shall remain distinguishable
from the Dropbox account used to access the storage provider.

### Device Linking

Dropbox file-based collaboration shall work with the device-linking
functionality established in Epic 50.

A user's multiple ART installations may be associated with the same ART
identity.

For example:

``` text
User A
  |
  +-- ART Web
  |
  +-- ART Desktop
  |
  +-- ART on Device 2
  |
  +-- ART on Device 3
```

The storage provider shall not be responsible for determining ART
identity.

ART shall use its own identity and device-linking mechanisms.

### File Ownership

ART shall distinguish between:

- The Dropbox account that owns a file.
- The Dropbox organization or team controlling access to a file.
- The ART user who created or modified content within the file.

Dropbox ownership and permissions shall remain controlled by Dropbox.

ART collaboration metadata shall identify ART users independently where
appropriate.

### Offline Operation

ART shall remain usable when Dropbox is temporarily unavailable.

If the user's current `.art` file has already been loaded:

- The user shall be able to continue working locally.
- Unsaved changes shall be preserved.
- ART shall not silently discard work.
- The user shall receive an accessible indication that Dropbox is
  unavailable.
- The user should be able to save/export a local copy when possible.

When Dropbox becomes available again, ART shall allow the user to
refresh or synchronize the file.

### Failed Saves

If ART cannot save changes to Dropbox, it shall:

- Preserve the user's current work.
- Clearly identify that the save failed.
- Explain the likely reason when known.
- Provide an opportunity to retry.
- Provide an option to save/export a local copy where appropriate.
- Avoid falsely indicating that the remote file was updated.

### Authentication Expiration

When Dropbox OAuth authorization expires or is revoked, ART shall:

- Detect the authentication failure.
- Preserve unsaved work.
- Inform the user.
- Provide an accessible option to reconnect.
- Avoid repeatedly displaying authentication errors unnecessarily.

### Disconnecting Dropbox

Users shall be able to disconnect Dropbox from ART.

Disconnecting shall:

- Remove the local connection to the provider.
- Prevent future Dropbox operations until the user reconnects.
- Preserve local `.art` files.
- Not delete Dropbox files.
- Not delete the user's Dropbox account.
- Not modify Dropbox permissions unless the user explicitly chooses an
  appropriate revocation option.

### Security

The Dropbox integration shall comply with the security requirements
established in Epics 47–53.

ART shall:

- Use secure OAuth authorization.
- Request minimum necessary permissions.
- Protect OAuth tokens.
- Avoid storing Dropbox passwords.
- Avoid logging sensitive credentials.
- Validate downloaded files.
- Validate Dropbox API responses.
- Protect against malicious or malformed `.art` files.
- Avoid unnecessary access to unrelated Dropbox content.
- Respect Dropbox permissions.
- Handle revoked credentials securely.

### Data Privacy

ART shall clearly communicate what Dropbox data it accesses.

ART shall not access unrelated Dropbox files merely because Dropbox is
connected.

Where possible, users shall be able to limit ART's access to designated
ART folders or files.

### Accessibility

All Dropbox functionality shall conform to ART's accessibility
requirements.

This includes:

- Connecting Dropbox.
- OAuth authentication.
- Account authorization.
- Folder selection.
- File browsing.
- File opening.
- File saving.
- Save As.
- Refreshing.
- Synchronization.
- Conflict detection.
- Merge Changes.
- Error handling.
- Disconnecting Dropbox.

All functionality shall be accessible using the keyboard.

All important status changes shall be programmatically exposed.

### Screen Reader Support

Dropbox integration shall be tested with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.

Screen readers shall receive meaningful information about:

- Current storage provider.
- Current account.
- Current file.
- Current folder.
- Synchronization state.
- External changes.
- Save status.
- Authentication status.
- Errors.
- Merge conflicts.

### Low-Vision and Visual Accessibility

Dropbox integration shall be tested using:

- Browser zoom.
- Operating-system magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- ART visual settings.
- Different display sizes.
- Different display scaling levels.

The interface shall not rely solely on color, spatial position, or
visual indicators.

### Keyboard Commands

Dropbox-related commands shall integrate with ART's command
architecture.

Commands shall be available through appropriate:

- Menubar menus.
- Global context menus.
- File/folder context menus.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

Potential commands include:

- Connect Dropbox.
- Disconnect Dropbox.
- Open from Dropbox.
- Save to Dropbox.
- Save As to Dropbox.
- Refresh from Dropbox.
- Synchronize.
- Resolve Merge Conflicts.
- Select Dropbox Folder.
- View File Information.

### Context Menu Integration

Where appropriate, users shall be able to access Dropbox commands from
context menus.

Context menus shall expose only commands appropriate to the selected
object and the user's permissions.

Disabled commands shall communicate why they are unavailable where
appropriate.

### History Framework

Dropbox-related ART content changes shall integrate with ART's History
Framework where appropriate.

The History Framework shall support Undo/Redo for applicable ART content
changes resulting from synchronization or merge operations.

Provider connection and authentication actions shall not necessarily be
treated as ordinary document edits unless explicitly designed to be
reversible.

### Notifications

ART shall provide accessible notifications for important Dropbox events,
including:

- File changed externally.
- Remote changes successfully synchronized.
- Merge conflict detected.
- Save successful.
- Save failed.
- Dropbox unavailable.
- Authentication expired.
- Permission denied.
- File deleted.
- File moved.
- File renamed.
- Shared-folder access changed.

Notifications shall not rely exclusively on transient visual messages.

### Error Handling

Dropbox errors shall be translated into understandable ART messages.

The system shall distinguish among:

- Authentication failure.
- Authorization failure.
- File not found.
- Folder not found.
- Permission denied.
- Dropbox unavailable.
- Network failure.
- Storage limitations.
- File changed externally.
- Merge conflict.
- Save failure.
- Unsupported file.
- Corrupted ART file.
- Revoked authorization.
- Shared-folder access restriction.

### File Integrity

ART shall protect `.art` file integrity during Dropbox operations.

The integration shall avoid:

- Partial writes.
- Silent overwriting.
- Corrupted saves.
- Lost changes.
- Incorrect revision tracking.
- Loss of ART metadata.

Where possible, ART shall use a safe-write process.

### Large Files

The Dropbox provider shall support `.art` files of realistic production
sizes.

Testing shall identify:

- Maximum practical file size.
- Upload/download performance.
- Timeout behavior.
- Interrupted transfers.
- Recovery behavior.

ART shall provide useful feedback when large files require additional
processing time.

### Network Interruptions

ART shall gracefully handle interruptions during:

- Authentication.
- File download.
- File upload.
- Save.
- Refresh.
- Synchronization.
- Merge preparation.

The user's work shall not be silently lost because of a network
interruption.

### Concurrent Editing Testing

The integration shall be tested with at least two users.

Testing shall include:

1.  User A opens a report.
2.  User B opens the same report.
3.  User A makes a change.
4.  User A saves.
5.  User B refreshes.
6.  User B sees User A's change.
7.  User B makes another change.
8.  User B saves.
9.  User A refreshes.
10. User A sees User B's change.

Additional testing shall verify conflicting edits.

### Merge Conflict Testing

Testing shall include:

1.  User A opens a report.
2.  User B opens the same report.
3.  User A changes one value.
4.  User B changes the same value differently.
5.  User A saves.
6.  User B saves or refreshes.
7.  ART detects the conflict.
8.  The Merge Changes modal opens.
9.  User B chooses the desired version.
10. ART creates the merged result.
11. The merged result is saved.
12. User A subsequently opens or refreshes the file.
13. User A sees the merged result.

### File-Based Collaboration Testing

Testing shall verify:

- Multiple users.
- Multiple devices.
- Shared folders.
- Asynchronous collaboration.
- Concurrent editing.
- Compatible changes.
- Conflicting changes.
- Merge resolution.
- User identity.
- Device linking.
- Task assignments.
- Shared To Do Lists.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- @mentions\.
- Organization folders.
- Organization Metrics.

### Dropbox Permission Testing

Test scenarios shall include:

- File owner.
- Editor.
- Viewer.
- Shared-folder member.
- Removed user.
- Permission changed while a file is open.
- File moved.
- File deleted.
- Folder access revoked.
- Shared-folder access changed.
- Team or organization access restrictions where applicable.

ART shall accurately respond to the permissions returned by Dropbox.

### Shared-Folder Testing

Testing shall verify:

- A user creates a shared Dropbox folder.
- The folder is shared with another user.
- Both users can access the folder.
- User A creates an `.art` file.
- User B opens the file.
- User B modifies and saves the file.
- User A refreshes or reopens the file.
- User A sees User B's changes.
- Conflicting changes invoke Merge Changes.
- Permissions remain controlled by Dropbox.

### Automated Testing

Automated tests shall validate the Dropbox provider implementation
against the common Storage Provider Interface.

Testing shall verify:

- Authentication state handling.
- Provider connection state.
- File operations.
- Folder operations.
- Metadata retrieval.
- Change detection.
- Error translation.
- Revision handling.
- Save behavior.
- Conflict detection.

Provider integration tests shall supplement end-to-end testing.

### Accessibility Testing

Complete Dropbox workflows shall be tested with multiple assistive
technologies and users with diverse disabilities.

Testing shall include:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only users.
- Low-vision users.
- Screen magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- Other assistive technologies as appropriate.

Testing shall include actual end-to-end workflows rather than isolated
controls.

### Documentation

ART documentation shall explain:

- How to connect Dropbox.
- What permissions ART requests.
- How to select an ART folder.
- How to open `.art` files from Dropbox.
- How to save `.art` files.
- How synchronization works.
- How file-based collaboration works.
- How merge conflicts work.
- How to disconnect Dropbox.
- What happens when Dropbox is unavailable.
- How Dropbox permissions affect ART.
- How shared-folder permissions affect ART.
- How Dropbox collaboration differs from server-based collaboration.
- Security and privacy considerations.

Documentation shall clearly state that Dropbox storage does not provide
ART's full real-time server collaboration capabilities.

### Backward Compatibility

The Dropbox integration shall not alter the `.art` file format in a way
that prevents existing ART files from opening.

Existing local files shall continue to work.

Existing import and export functionality shall remain available.

Users shall be able to move `.art` files between local storage, Google
Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox without losing supported ART data.

### Future Provider Compatibility

The implementation shall not introduce Dropbox-specific assumptions into
ART's core architecture that would prevent future providers from being
implemented.

The same Storage Provider Interface shall remain usable for:

- Network storage.
- Additional cloud-storage providers.
- SharePoint.
- Private cloud storage.
- Enterprise document-management systems.
- ART Server.

### Definition of Done

Epic 54 shall be considered complete when:

- Dropbox is implemented as a Storage Provider using the Epic 51
  architecture.
- Users can optionally connect Dropbox.
- Dropbox OAuth authentication is implemented securely.
- ART does not store Dropbox passwords.
- Minimum necessary Dropbox permissions are requested.
- Users can browse Dropbox folders.
- Users can select an ART storage folder.
- Users can create `.art` files in Dropbox.
- Users can open `.art` files from Dropbox.
- Users can save `.art` files to Dropbox.
- Save As functionality works with Dropbox.
- External changes can be detected.
- Compatible changes can be synchronized.
- Merge conflicts invoke ART's existing Merge Changes functionality.
- Concurrent editing has been tested.
- File-based collaboration works through Dropbox.
- Shared folders work appropriately.
- Dropbox permissions are respected.
- User identity information is preserved.
- Device-linked ART identities work with file-based collaboration.
- Tasks can be shared through `.art` files.
- Shared To Do Lists can be shared through `.art` files.
- Shared Progress Logs can be shared through `.art` files.
- @mentions are preserved within shared `.art` files.
- Organization folders can be used where permissions permit.
- Organization Metrics can use supported `.art` files where implemented.
- Offline behavior protects user work.
- Failed saves do not silently discard changes.
- OAuth expiration and revocation are handled correctly.
- Users can disconnect Dropbox.
- All Dropbox commands integrate with ART's command architecture.
- Keyboard shortcuts remain customizable.
- Dropbox workflows are accessible to keyboard users.
- Dropbox workflows are accessible to screen readers.
- Dropbox workflows have been tested with JAWS, NVDA, Narrator,
  VoiceOver, TalkBack, ChromeVox, and braille displays.
- Low-vision and visual accessibility testing has been completed.
- Automated provider tests have been implemented.
- End-to-end collaboration testing has been completed.
- Security and privacy requirements have been reviewed.
- Documentation has been completed.
- Existing ART functionality has not regressed.
- The implementation does not prevent future network-storage, additional
  cloud-storage, enterprise-storage, or ART Server providers from using
  the Storage Provider Interface.

## Epic 55 — Storage Provider Management, Synchronization, and Offline Resilience

### Epic Overview

Implement a unified storage-provider management and synchronization
experience across all ART storage providers.

Epics 51–54 established the provider-independent Storage Provider
Architecture and individual providers for local storage, Google Drive,
Microsoft OneDrive, and Dropbox.

This epic shall provide the common user-facing infrastructure required
to manage those providers consistently and safely.

The goal is to ensure that users can move between local files and
supported cloud-storage providers without losing work, while maintaining
ART's local-first philosophy and file-based collaboration capabilities.

ART shall continue to function fully without any external storage
provider or ART server.

### Goals

This epic shall:

- Provide a consistent storage-provider management experience.
- Allow users to select their preferred storage provider.
- Allow users to switch between storage providers.
- Display the current storage provider and synchronization state.
- Provide accessible synchronization controls.
- Provide reliable external-change detection.
- Provide safe conflict handling.
- Protect against accidental data loss.
- Support offline work.
- Support recovery from failed synchronization.
- Preserve `.art` file integrity.
- Maintain compatibility between local and cloud storage.
- Provide a common framework for future storage providers.
- Support file-based collaboration without requiring an ART server.
- Clearly distinguish file synchronization from real-time server
  collaboration.

### Storage Provider Architecture

ART shall use the common Storage Provider Interface established in Epic
51.

The architecture shall support:

``` text
ART Core
    |
    +-- Storage Provider Interface
            |
            +-- Local File Provider
            +-- Google Drive Provider
            +-- OneDrive Provider
            +-- Dropbox Provider
            +-- Future Providers
            +-- ART Server Provider
```

Provider-specific implementation details shall remain isolated from
ART's core application logic.

### Supported Providers

The storage-provider management interface shall support, at minimum:

- Local file storage.
- Google Drive.
- Microsoft OneDrive.
- Dropbox.

The architecture shall also accommodate future providers without
requiring major changes to ART's core reporting functionality.

Potential future providers include:

- Network drives.
- SharePoint.
- Private cloud storage.
- Enterprise document-management systems.
- ART Server.

### Provider Selection

ART shall provide an accessible mechanism for selecting a storage
provider.

Users shall be able to choose among available providers such as:

- Local Computer.
- Google Drive.
- Microsoft OneDrive.
- Dropbox.

Unavailable providers shall be clearly identified.

The provider-selection interface shall communicate:

- Provider name.
- Connection status.
- Availability.
- Whether authentication is required.
- Whether the provider supports file-based collaboration.
- Whether the provider requires an internet connection.

### Current Storage Provider

ART shall clearly communicate which provider is currently being used for
the active report/project.

The current provider shall be available through appropriate:

- Application status information.
- File menus.
- Settings.
- Accessible programmatic information.

Screen readers shall be able to determine the current storage provider.

### Provider Connection Status

ART shall expose a meaningful provider connection state.

Possible states include:

- Not connected.
- Connecting.
- Connected.
- Authentication required.
- Authentication expired.
- Offline.
- Synchronization required.
- Synchronizing.
- Synchronization complete.
- Synchronization failed.
- Permission denied.
- Provider unavailable.

Status changes shall be exposed programmatically.

### Synchronization Status

ART shall provide an accessible indication of whether the current `.art`
file is synchronized with its remote storage location.

Possible states include:

- Up to date.
- Local changes pending.
- Remote changes available.
- Synchronizing.
- Conflict detected.
- Save failed.
- Offline.
- Unknown status.

The synchronization status shall not rely solely on color.

### Manual Synchronization

ART shall provide a command to manually synchronize the active file.

The command shall be available through:

- Menubar commands.
- Global context menu commands.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts where appropriate.

The user shall be able to initiate synchronization without needing to
close and reopen the report.

### Refresh

ART shall provide a separate Refresh command when appropriate.

Refresh shall retrieve the current remote version or metadata and
determine whether changes are available.

Refresh shall not silently overwrite local changes.

If local changes exist, ART shall preserve them and invoke the
appropriate synchronization or merge process.

### Synchronization Workflow

The general synchronization process shall be:

``` text
Local ART File
      |
      v
Check Remote Version
      |
      +---- No Remote Changes ----> Continue Working
      |
      +---- Remote Changes -------> Compare Versions
                                      |
                                      +-- Compatible
                                      |      |
                                      |      v
                                      |   Merge Automatically
                                      |
                                      +-- Conflicting
                                             |
                                             v
                                      Merge Changes Modal
```

### Local Changes Only

If the user has local changes and the remote file has not changed, ART
shall save the local changes normally.

### Remote Changes Only

If the remote file has changed and the user has no conflicting local
changes, ART shall retrieve the remote changes.

ART shall clearly indicate that remote changes were incorporated.

### Local and Remote Changes

If both local and remote changes exist, ART shall compare the changes.

Compatible changes should be merged automatically.

Conflicting changes shall be presented through ART's existing Merge
Changes functionality.

### Conflict Prevention

ART shall take reasonable measures to prevent accidental overwriting of
newer remote content.

Before replacing a remote file, ART shall determine whether the remote
version has changed since the user's current version was loaded.

If the remote version has changed, ART shall not simply overwrite it.

### Merge Changes Integration

The existing Merge Changes implementation shall remain the authoritative
mechanism for resolving ART content conflicts.

Storage providers shall not create independent merge implementations.

The common synchronization framework shall provide the Merge Changes
system with:

- Local version.
- Remote version.
- Relevant revision information.
- User identity information where available.
- Change metadata.
- Conflict information.

### Merge Conflict Modal

When a conflict requires user intervention, the Merge Changes modal
shall:

- Open automatically when appropriate.
- Clearly announce that a conflict exists.
- Identify the affected report/project.
- Identify local and remote versions.
- Identify the users responsible for changes where available.
- Present conflicting changes in an understandable format.
- Allow users to choose which changes to retain.
- Allow compatible changes to be combined.
- Preserve non-conflicting changes.
- Allow the user to cancel or defer the operation where supported.
- Maintain keyboard accessibility.
- Support screen readers.
- Provide meaningful focus management.

### File Revision Tracking

ART shall maintain sufficient information to determine which version of
a remote `.art` file was last retrieved.

Where supported, providers should use:

- Revision IDs.
- Version IDs.
- ETags.
- Change tokens.
- Provider-specific file metadata.

Provider-specific values shall remain isolated within the storage
provider implementation.

### File Metadata

ART shall maintain appropriate metadata associated with a stored `.art`
file, including where available:

- Provider.
- File identifier.
- Folder identifier.
- Revision identifier.
- Last synchronization time.
- Last known remote modification time.
- Local modification state.
- Synchronization state.

Sensitive provider credentials shall not be stored as ordinary document
metadata.

### Local File Metadata

Local `.art` files shall remain usable independently of any connected
storage provider.

If an `.art` file is copied to another location, ART shall not require
access to the original storage provider merely to open the file.

### Copying Between Providers

ART shall support copying or saving a report/project from one provider
to another.

Examples include:

``` text
Local File
    ↓
Google Drive
```

``` text
Google Drive
    ↓
OneDrive
```

``` text
OneDrive
    ↓
Dropbox
```

``` text
Dropbox
    ↓
Local Computer
```

The operation shall preserve supported ART data.

### Move Between Providers

Where technically appropriate, ART may provide a Move operation between
storage providers.

A move shall not delete the original file until ART can verify that the
destination was successfully created.

If the destination operation fails, the original file shall remain
intact.

### Save a Local Copy

Users shall always have an accessible way to save/export a local copy of
the current `.art` file.

This shall be especially important when:

- A provider is unavailable.
- Authentication has expired.
- Synchronization fails.
- A merge conflict cannot currently be resolved.
- The user wants an independent backup.

### Backup

ART should provide an accessible mechanism for creating backups of
`.art` files.

Backup functionality should allow users to:

- Create a manual backup.
- Choose a destination.
- Preserve the original file.
- Include relevant ART metadata.
- Verify that the backup was successfully created.

### Automatic Backup

Where technically feasible, ART may provide optional automatic backup
functionality.

Users shall be able to configure:

- Whether automatic backups are enabled.
- Backup frequency.
- Backup location.
- Maximum number of retained backups.

Automatic backups shall not silently consume excessive storage.

### Offline Mode

ART shall support a robust offline mode.

When no network connection is available, users shall still be able to:

- Open previously available `.art` files.
- Edit reports.
- Create reports.
- Edit tasks.
- Update Progress Logs.
- Add comments.
- Use the History Framework.
- Save local copies.
- Continue other fundamental ART functions that do not require a server
  or external provider.

### Offline Indicators

When ART is offline, the application shall clearly communicate this
state.

The indication shall be:

- Visible.
- Accessible to screen readers.
- Keyboard accessible where interaction is required.
- Understandable without relying on color.

### Offline Changes

Changes made while offline shall be preserved locally.

ART shall not discard offline changes merely because synchronization is
unavailable.

### Reconnection

When connectivity is restored, ART shall not automatically overwrite
remote data.

Instead, ART shall:

1.  Detect the remote state.
2.  Compare it with the local state.
3.  Determine whether changes occurred remotely.
4.  Merge compatible changes.
5.  Invoke Merge Changes for conflicts.
6.  Save the resulting version when authorized.

### Network Interruption During Save

If network connectivity is interrupted during a save:

- The current local work shall remain intact.
- ART shall report that the remote save did not complete.
- ART shall not report the save as successful.
- ART shall provide a retry mechanism.
- ART shall provide a local-save/export option where appropriate.

### Provider Unavailability

If a storage provider becomes unavailable, ART shall:

- Preserve local work.
- Inform the user.
- Identify the provider as unavailable.
- Allow continued local editing where possible.
- Provide a retry option.
- Avoid repeated disruptive notifications.

### Authentication Failure

If synchronization fails because authentication has expired:

- ART shall preserve the user's work.
- ART shall identify that authentication is required.
- ART shall provide an accessible reconnect command.
- ART shall not expose credentials.
- ART shall not silently discard changes.

### Permission Changes

If a user's provider permissions change while ART is being used, ART
shall detect the failure where possible.

Examples include:

- Edit permission removed.
- Folder access revoked.
- File ownership changed.
- File moved.
- File deleted.
- Organization access revoked.

ART shall provide an understandable error message and preserve local
work.

### Deleted Remote Files

If an `.art` file is deleted remotely while the user has a local copy
open, ART shall not automatically delete the local copy.

ART shall inform the user that the remote file is no longer available.

The user shall have the option to:

- Save a new copy.
- Choose another location.
- Restore/re-upload the file where permitted.
- Cancel.

### Moved Remote Files

If a remote file is moved to another folder, ART should detect the
change where the provider supports reliable file identifiers.

ART shall continue to reference the file rather than assuming the
original folder remains unchanged.

### Renamed Remote Files

If a remote file is renamed, ART should update its displayed filename
after synchronization where supported.

The underlying file identity shall remain stable.

### Duplicate Files

ART shall handle duplicate `.art` files safely.

Users shall be able to distinguish among files using information such
as:

- Filename.
- Location.
- Provider.
- Last modified date.
- Last modified user where available.

ART shall not assume that two files with the same filename are the same
file.

### Stale File Detection

ART shall detect when a local copy has become significantly out of date
relative to the remote file.

The user shall receive an appropriate notification.

### File Locking

Where a storage provider supports file locking or check-out mechanisms,
ART may use those mechanisms.

However, ART shall not depend on provider-specific locking for
correctness.

The Merge Changes system shall remain the primary mechanism for handling
concurrent edits.

### Server-Free Collaboration

The synchronization framework shall explicitly support collaboration
without an ART server.

Shared `.art` files stored in:

- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Other supported file providers.

shall be capable of asynchronous collaboration.

Users shall be able to:

- Edit.
- Save.
- Reopen.
- Refresh.
- Synchronize.
- Detect changes.
- Resolve conflicts.

### Server-Based Collaboration

The architecture shall remain compatible with future server-based
collaboration.

When an ART server is eventually available, it may provide:

- Real-time synchronization.
- Real-time presence.
- Server-side notifications.
- Centralized permissions.
- Centralized organization management.
- Server-side @mention notifications.
- Server-side audit history.
- Real-time task updates.

The existence of those capabilities shall not change the fundamental
local/file-based operation of ART.

### File-Based vs. Server-Based Collaboration

ART shall clearly distinguish the two collaboration models.

#### File-Based Collaboration

File-based collaboration shall:

- Use `.art` files.
- Depend on shared storage.
- Primarily support asynchronous collaboration.
- Detect changes when files are saved, refreshed, or reopened.
- Use Merge Changes for conflicts.
- Not provide guaranteed real-time synchronization.

#### Server-Based Collaboration

Server-based collaboration may:

- Synchronize changes in real time.
- Maintain centralized user identities.
- Provide centralized permissions.
- Deliver notifications.
- Support real-time presence.
- Coordinate concurrent editing.

### User Notifications

The synchronization framework shall provide accessible notifications for
important events.

Notifications may include:

- Remote changes detected.
- Changes synchronized.
- Merge conflict detected.
- Merge completed.
- Save successful.
- Save failed.
- Provider unavailable.
- Authentication required.
- Permission denied.
- Remote file deleted.
- Remote file moved.
- Offline mode activated.
- Connection restored.

### Notification Persistence

Important synchronization notifications shall be available through ART's
Notifications section where appropriate.

Transient notifications shall not be the sole method of communicating
important state changes.

### Notification Accessibility

Notifications shall:

- Be programmatically exposed.
- Be understandable to screen readers.
- Avoid unexpected focus movement unless user attention is required.
- Use appropriate live-region behavior where applicable.
- Provide sufficient information to understand the event.

### Tasks and To Do Lists

Synchronization shall support the task and To Do functionality
established in previous epics.

Changes to tasks shall synchronize as part of the `.art` file.

This includes:

- Task creation.
- Task deletion.
- Task assignment.
- Task reassignment.
- Task priority.
- Task status.
- Due dates.
- Reminders where stored in the shared artifact.
- Comments/notes/instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Completion state.

### Shared Progress Logs

Synchronization shall support Shared Progress Logs, including:

- Task assignments.
- Status updates.
- Comments.
- @mentions\.
- Progress information.
- History.

Conflicting Progress Log changes shall use the same Merge Changes
infrastructure.

### Organization Metrics

Synchronization shall support organization metrics based on supported
shared `.art` files.

Where an organization folder contains multiple ART projects and reports,
ART may recalculate metrics when relevant files change.

The system shall avoid treating unsupported or corrupted files as valid
ART source data.

### @Mentions

File-based @mentions shall remain functional across supported storage
providers.

A mention shall preserve:

- Mentioning user.
- Mentioned user.
- Associated project/workspace/report.
- Associated task.
- Associated comment.
- Timestamp.
- Relevant identity information.

When server-based notification delivery is unavailable, the mention
shall remain stored in the shared `.art` file.

### Device Synchronization

Users who use ART on multiple devices shall be able to synchronize their
work through shared storage.

For example:

``` text
User A

Desktop ART
    |
    | Save
    v
Google Drive
    |
    | Open
    v
Laptop ART
```

Device linking and identity recognition shall use the mechanisms
established by Epic 50.

### Identity Conflicts

If ART detects that the same device appears to be associated with
conflicting ART identities, it shall not silently select one identity.

The user shall receive an accessible identity-conflict workflow.

The workflow shall allow the user to:

- Confirm the correct identity.
- Reconnect the device.
- Cancel.
- Preserve existing local work.

### History Framework

All supported synchronization and merge operations shall integrate with
ART's History Framework.

Where appropriate, users shall be able to:

- Undo a synchronization-related change.
- Redo a synchronization-related change.
- Undo a merge decision.
- Redo a merge decision.

History shall not expose sensitive provider credentials.

### Command Integration

Synchronization commands shall be available through:

- Menubar menus.
- Global context menus.
- File context menus.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

Commands shall include, where applicable:

- Refresh.
- Synchronize.
- Save.
- Save As.
- Save Local Copy.
- Create Backup.
- Connect Provider.
- Disconnect Provider.
- Resolve Merge Conflicts.
- View Synchronization Status.

### Keyboard Accessibility

All storage and synchronization commands shall be usable from the
keyboard.

Keyboard shortcuts shall remain customizable through ART's keyboard
shortcut system.

No critical synchronization function shall require mouse interaction.

### Screen Reader Accessibility

Storage-provider status and synchronization state shall be
programmatically available.

Screen readers shall be able to determine:

- Provider.
- File.
- Folder.
- Synchronization state.
- Pending local changes.
- Pending remote changes.
- Conflict state.
- Authentication state.
- Permission state.

### Low-Vision Accessibility

The synchronization interface shall support:

- Zoom.
- Magnification.
- High contrast.
- User-configured visual settings.
- Reflow where applicable.

Important synchronization information shall remain available without
relying exclusively on visual styling.

### Braille Accessibility

Synchronization status and conflict information shall be exposed through
accessibility APIs so that supported braille displays can present
meaningful information.

### Testing Matrix

The synchronization framework shall be tested across:

| Storage Provider | Local | External Changes | Conflicts | Offline | Multi-Device       |
|------------------|-------|------------------|-----------|---------|--------------------|
| Local Files      | Yes   | N/A              | Yes       | Yes     | Via shared storage |
| Google Drive     | Yes   | Yes              | Yes       | Yes     | Yes                |
| OneDrive         | Yes   | Yes              | Yes       | Yes     | Yes                |
| Dropbox          | Yes   | Yes              | Yes       | Yes     | Yes                |

### Multi-User Testing

Testing shall include at least two users working with the same `.art`
file.

Testing shall include:

- Sequential editing.
- Concurrent editing.
- Compatible changes.
- Conflicting changes.
- Repeated synchronization.
- Multiple save operations.
- Refresh operations.
- Reopening files.
- File-based @mentions.
- Task assignments.
- Shared Progress Logs.

### Multi-Device Testing

Testing shall include:

- Same user on two devices.
- Same user on three or more devices.
- Different ART versions where supported.
- Web ART.
- Desktop ART.
- Offline edits.
- Reconnection.
- Conflicting device changes.

### Data-Loss Testing

Testing shall deliberately simulate:

- Network interruption.
- Provider outage.
- Authentication expiration.
- Permission removal.
- File deletion.
- File movement.
- Simultaneous edits.
- Failed uploads.
- Failed downloads.
- Browser crashes.
- Application crashes.

The system shall demonstrate that user work is preserved.

### Accessibility Testing

The complete synchronization workflow shall be tested with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only operation.
- Low-vision users.
- Screen magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- Other relevant assistive technologies.

Testing shall include actual end-to-end synchronization and
conflict-resolution workflows.

### Performance

The synchronization framework shall avoid unnecessary network requests.

ART shall:

- Avoid repeatedly downloading unchanged files.
- Use provider revision information where available.
- Avoid blocking the user interface unnecessarily.
- Provide progress information for long operations.
- Handle large `.art` files efficiently.

### Security

The synchronization framework shall comply with the security
requirements established by previous security and authentication epics.

ART shall:

- Protect authentication tokens.
- Avoid exposing credentials.
- Validate remote files.
- Validate file contents before loading.
- Prevent malicious provider responses from compromising ART.
- Avoid unauthorized provider access.
- Respect provider permissions.
- Protect sensitive collaboration metadata.
- Avoid leaking user identity information unnecessarily.

### Privacy

ART shall minimize information transmitted to external providers.

Provider-specific APIs shall receive only information necessary to
perform the requested operation.

ART shall not upload unrelated local files or application data.

### Error Recovery

The synchronization framework shall provide recovery mechanisms for
failed operations.

Where an operation fails, ART shall preserve sufficient state to safely
retry.

The user shall not need to restart ART merely because synchronization
failed.

### Documentation

ART documentation shall explain:

- Storage providers.
- Provider connection.
- Provider selection.
- Synchronization.
- Refresh.
- Offline mode.
- Conflict detection.
- Merge Changes.
- File-based collaboration.
- Server-based collaboration.
- Backups.
- Local copies.
- Provider permissions.
- Authentication.
- Multi-device workflows.
- Data-loss protection.

Documentation shall clearly explain that cloud storage does not equal
real-time collaboration.

### Backward Compatibility

The synchronization framework shall remain compatible with existing
`.art` files.

Existing local files shall continue to open.

Existing import/export functionality shall continue to work.

Files shall remain portable between supported providers.

### Future Storage Providers

The synchronization framework shall provide a stable foundation for
additional providers.

Future providers shall be able to implement the common Storage Provider
Interface without modifying ART's core report model.

Potential providers include:

- SharePoint.
- Network drives.
- WebDAV.
- SFTP-backed storage.
- Enterprise document-management systems.
- Private cloud storage.
- ART Server.

### Definition of Done

Epic 55 shall be considered complete when:

- A unified storage-provider management experience exists.
- Local storage remains fully supported.
- Google Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox use the common provider
  architecture.
- Users can view the current provider.
- Users can view synchronization status.
- Manual synchronization is available.
- Refresh functionality is available.
- External changes are detected.
- Compatible changes are synchronized safely.
- Conflicting changes invoke the existing Merge Changes functionality.
- ART does not silently overwrite newer remote content.
- Local changes are preserved during synchronization failures.
- Offline editing works.
- Reconnection works.
- Failed saves can be retried.
- Users can save a local copy when necessary.
- Backup functionality is available where implemented.
- Files can be copied between supported providers.
- Provider permissions are respected.
- Deleted and moved remote files are handled safely.
- Multi-user collaboration has been tested.
- Multi-device collaboration has been tested.
- File-based collaboration works without an ART server.
- Tasks synchronize correctly.
- Shared Progress Logs synchronize correctly.
- @mentions are preserved.
- Organization-folder scenarios have been tested.
- Organization Metrics can use supported shared ART data where
  implemented.
- Device identity conflicts are handled safely.
- History Framework integration works for supported synchronization and
  merge operations.
- Menubar commands are available.
- Global context-menu commands are available.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts are available.
- Screen-reader accessibility has been verified.
- Keyboard-only accessibility has been verified.
- Low-vision accessibility has been verified.
- Braille accessibility has been verified.
- JAWS testing has been completed.
- NVDA testing has been completed.
- Narrator testing has been completed.
- VoiceOver testing has been completed.
- TalkBack testing has been completed.
- ChromeVox testing has been completed.
- Braille-display testing has been completed.
- Data-loss scenarios have been tested.
- Network interruption scenarios have been tested.
- Provider outage scenarios have been tested.
- Authentication-expiration scenarios have been tested.
- Permission-change scenarios have been tested.
- Concurrent editing has been tested.
- Merge conflicts have been tested.
- Documentation has been completed.
- Existing ART functionality has not regressed.
- The architecture remains suitable for future storage providers and ART
  Server integration.

## Epic 56 — External Platform Integrations

### Epic Overview

Implement a provider-independent integration framework that allows ART
to connect with external project-management, issue-tracking,
development, collaboration, and productivity platforms.

ART shall support integrations with platforms commonly used by
accessibility, software-development, quality-assurance,
project-management, and enterprise teams, including:

- Jira.
- GitHub Issues.
- Microsoft Azure DevOps.
- Microsoft Azure.
- Google Workspace.
- Other compatible platforms added in the future.

These integrations shall allow users to move relevant information
between ART and external systems without requiring users to duplicate
the same information manually.

ART shall remain fully functional without any external integration.

External integrations shall be optional and shall not become
prerequisites for ART's fundamental reporting, auditing,
task-management, or collaboration capabilities.

### Goals

This epic shall:

- Establish a common External Integration Architecture.
- Allow users to connect supported external platforms.
- Use secure, supported authentication mechanisms.
- Prefer OAuth or equivalent delegated authorization where available.
- Avoid storing external service passwords.
- Request only the permissions required for the selected integration.
- Allow users to disconnect integrations.
- Allow users to configure which ART data is shared with external
  systems.
- Support importing relevant information from external systems.
- Support exporting or synchronizing relevant ART information to
  external systems.
- Preserve ART as the authoritative accessibility-reporting application.
- Avoid forcing users to maintain duplicate information unnecessarily.
- Provide accessible integration-management interfaces.
- Support customizable keyboard commands.
- Support global context-menu commands.
- Provide clear synchronization status.
- Handle conflicts and errors safely.
- Preserve user privacy and security.
- Provide a foundation for future integrations.

### Relationship to the Storage Provider Architecture

External platform integrations shall be architecturally separate from
the Storage Provider Architecture established in Epic 51.

Storage providers are responsible for storing and synchronizing ART
files.

External integrations are responsible for communicating with external
systems.

Conceptually:

``` text
ART Core
    |
    +-- Storage Provider Interface
    |       |
    |       +-- Local Files
    |       +-- Google Drive
    |       +-- OneDrive
    |       +-- Dropbox
    |
    +-- External Integration Interface
            |
            +-- Jira
            +-- GitHub Issues
            +-- Azure DevOps
            +-- Google Workspace
            +-- Future Integrations
```

An external integration shall not replace ART's local or file-based
storage capabilities.

### Integration Architecture

ART shall provide a common integration interface.

Each integration should provide standardized capabilities such as:

- Authentication.
- Connection status.
- Account identification.
- Permission management.
- Project/workspace selection.
- Import.
- Export.
- Synchronization.
- Error handling.
- Disconnect.
- Configuration.

Platform-specific functionality shall remain isolated within the
individual integration provider.

### Integration Management

ART shall provide an accessible Integration Management interface.

Users shall be able to:

- View available integrations.
- Connect an integration.
- View connected integrations.
- View the account associated with an integration.
- Configure an integration.
- Disconnect an integration.
- Reauthorize an integration.
- View requested permissions.
- View synchronization status.
- View integration errors.
- Test an integration connection.

### Settings Integration

Integration management shall be available through ART Settings.

The interface shall provide a clear distinction between:

- Storage providers.
- External service integrations.
- Authentication providers.
- ART account settings.

Users shall not be required to connect an external platform simply to
use ART.

### Authentication

Integrations shall use secure delegated authentication whenever
supported by the external platform.

ART shall:

- Prefer OAuth or equivalent secure authorization.
- Never request external service passwords unnecessarily.
- Never store external service passwords.
- Protect access tokens.
- Protect refresh tokens.
- Handle token expiration.
- Handle revoked authorization.
- Handle denied authorization.
- Provide an accessible reconnect workflow.
- Request only necessary permissions.

### Least Privilege

Each integration shall request the minimum permissions required for the
features the user chooses to enable.

ART shall not request broad access merely because a platform supports
additional functionality.

Where a platform supports granular permissions, ART should use them.

### Integration Scope

Users shall be able to determine, where technically possible, which ART
information is shared with an external service.

Potential scope options may include:

- Current report.
- Current project.
- Selected findings.
- Selected tasks.
- Selected Progress Log entries.
