- Selected organization.
- Selected workspace.
- Entire integration workspace.

### Jira Integration

ART shall provide an optional Jira integration.

The Jira integration shall support relevant accessibility-reporting
workflows.

Potential functionality shall include:

- Connect Jira.
- Select Jira organization/site.
- Select project.
- Import Jira issues.
- Create Jira issues from ART findings.
- Update existing Jira issues.
- Link ART findings to Jira issues.
- Link ART tasks to Jira issues.
- Synchronize issue status where appropriate.
- Synchronize priority where appropriate.
- Synchronize assignees where appropriate.
- Synchronize comments where explicitly enabled.
- Open the corresponding Jira issue from ART.

### Jira Issue Creation

Users shall be able to create a Jira issue from an ART finding.

The user shall be able to review information before creating the issue.

Potential fields include:

- Summary.
- Description.
- Accessibility issue.
- WCAG Success Criterion.
- Severity.
- Priority.
- Environment.
- Steps to reproduce.
- Expected result.
- Actual result.
- Suggested remediation.
- ART report/project.
- Assignee.
- Labels.

The user shall be able to choose which fields are transmitted.

### Jira Issue Linking

ART shall maintain a relationship between an ART finding and its
corresponding Jira issue.

The relationship should include sufficient information to identify the
external issue without unnecessarily storing sensitive authentication
information.

ART shall allow users to:

- Open the Jira issue.
- View synchronization status.
- Refresh issue information.
- Remove the link.
- Re-link to another issue where permitted.

### GitHub Issues Integration

ART shall provide an optional GitHub Issues integration.

Potential functionality shall include:

- Connect GitHub.
- Select an account or organization.
- Select a repository.
- Import GitHub Issues.
- Create GitHub Issues from ART findings.
- Update GitHub Issues.
- Link ART findings to GitHub Issues.
- Link ART tasks to GitHub Issues.
- Synchronize supported status information.
- Synchronize supported labels.
- Synchronize supported assignees.
- Open the corresponding GitHub Issue.

### GitHub Issue Creation

Users shall be able to create a GitHub Issue from an ART finding.

The user shall be able to review the information before submission.

ART should provide a configurable mapping between ART fields and GitHub
Issue fields.

### Azure DevOps Integration

ART shall provide an optional Microsoft Azure DevOps integration.

Potential functionality shall include:

- Connect Azure DevOps.
- Select organization.
- Select project.
- Select team.
- Import work items.
- Create work items from ART findings.
- Update work items.
- Link ART findings to work items.
- Link ART tasks to work items.
- Synchronize supported statuses.
- Synchronize priorities.
- Synchronize assignments.
- Open the corresponding Azure DevOps work item.

### Azure DevOps Work Item Types

ART should support commonly used work-item types where available,
including:

- Bug.
- Task.
- Issue.
- User Story.
- Other organization-defined work-item types where practical.

The user shall be able to select the appropriate type before creating an
item.

### Google Workspace Integration

ART shall provide an optional Google Workspace integration.

Potential functionality shall include integration with:

- Google Drive.
- Google Docs.
- Google Sheets.
- Google Calendar where appropriate.
- Google account identity.

Google Workspace functionality shall remain separate from Google Drive
storage functionality.

### Google Docs Integration

Where technically appropriate, ART may provide functionality to:

- Export report content to Google Docs.
- Open an associated Google Doc.
- Link a Google Doc to an ART report.
- Import supported content from Google Docs.

ART shall not require Google Docs merely to create or edit an ART
report.

### Google Sheets Integration

ART may provide functionality to:

- Export structured report data to Google Sheets.
- Export audit findings.
- Export task information.
- Export metrics.
- Link a spreadsheet to an ART project.

The integration shall avoid silently overwriting existing spreadsheets.

### Integration Data Mapping

ART shall provide a configurable mapping system where external platforms
have different data models.

For example:

``` text
ART Finding
    |
    +-- Summary ----------> Jira Summary
    +-- Description ------> Jira Description
    +-- Priority ---------> Jira Priority
    +-- Status -----------> Jira Status
    +-- Assignee ----------> Jira Assignee
    +-- WCAG Criterion ----> Jira Label/Custom Field
```

Mappings shall be configurable where technically appropriate.

### Custom Fields

Where supported by the external platform, ART should allow users to map
ART fields to custom external fields.

The user shall not be required to modify ART's internal data model
merely because an external system contains custom fields.

### Synchronization Direction

Each integration shall clearly communicate whether a particular field
supports:

- ART → External platform.
- External platform → ART.
- Bidirectional synchronization.
- One-time import.
- One-time export.

ART shall not imply bidirectional synchronization when only one
direction is supported.

### Synchronization Conflicts

When ART and an external platform both contain changes to the same
synchronized data, ART shall detect conflicts where practical.

The integration shall not silently overwrite user changes.

Depending on the data type, ART may:

- Prefer the most recent version when explicitly configured.
- Ask the user which version to keep.
- Preserve both versions.
- Invoke ART's existing Merge Changes functionality where the data model
  supports it.

### External System as Source of Truth

Users shall be able to configure, where appropriate, whether:

- ART is authoritative.
- The external system is authoritative.
- Synchronization is bidirectional.

The default shall favor safety and avoid destructive overwrites.

### Integration Status

ART shall provide accessible status information for each integration.

Possible states include:

- Not connected.
- Connected.
- Authentication required.
- Synchronization required.
- Synchronizing.
- Synchronized.
- Synchronization failed.
- Permission denied.
- Service unavailable.
- Configuration incomplete.

### Integration Notifications

ART shall provide notifications for important integration events,
including:

- Connection successful.
- Authentication expired.
- Authentication revoked.
- Synchronization successful.
- Synchronization failed.
- External item created.
- External item updated.
- Conflict detected.
- Permission denied.
- External service unavailable.

Important notifications should also appear in ART's Notifications
section where appropriate.

### Tasks and To Do Lists

External integrations shall support ART's task architecture where
applicable.

Users may be able to create external issues/tasks from ART tasks.

For example:

``` text
ART Task
    |
    +-- Create Jira Issue
    |
    +-- Create GitHub Issue
    |
    +-- Create Azure DevOps Work Item
```

ART shall preserve the relationship between the ART task and the
external task.

### Shared Tasks

Where an ART task is part of a shared project, Progress Log, or shared
To Do List, users with appropriate permissions shall be able to create
or link external work items.

Integration actions shall respect ART permissions established by Epics
48–50 and subsequent authorization functionality.

### @Mentions

Where an external platform supports mentions, ART should provide
appropriate mapping between ART @mentions and external mentions.

ART shall not automatically expose a user's email address to an external
service merely because the user was mentioned.

The user shall be informed when an @mention will be transmitted
externally.

### Comments

Where supported, ART may synchronize comments with external
issue-tracking systems.

Users shall be able to determine whether comments are:

- ART-only.
- External-only.
- Synchronized.

Private ART comments shall not be transmitted without explicit
permission.

### Accessibility Findings

ART shall be able to associate accessibility findings with external
issues.

The integration should preserve important accessibility information such
as:

- WCAG Success Criterion.
- Accessibility Standard.
- Severity.
- Priority.
- Description.
- Steps to reproduce.
- Expected result.
- Actual result.
- Suggested remediation.
- Testing environment.

### Report Links

Where supported, external issues should contain a reference to the
associated ART report or project.

The link shall only be included when it can be safely and meaningfully
accessed by the intended users.

ART shall not expose private local file paths or sensitive information
unnecessarily.

### Local-Only Reports

Reports stored only on the user's local computer shall remain usable
without any external integration.

Users shall not be required to upload a report to a server simply to
create an external issue if the integration can safely transmit the
selected information directly.

### File-Based Collaboration

External integrations shall remain compatible with ART's file-based
collaboration architecture.

For example:

``` text
Shared .art File
      |
      +-- Finding
      |
      +-- Jira Link
      |
      +-- Task
      |
      +-- GitHub Issue Link
```

Integration metadata may be stored within the `.art` file when
appropriate.

Sensitive OAuth credentials shall never be stored in shared `.art`
files.

### Shared Files and Credentials

A shared `.art` file shall never contain:

- OAuth access tokens.
- OAuth refresh tokens.
- Passwords.
- API secrets.
- Private authentication credentials.

If a second user opens a shared report, that user shall not inherit
another user's external-service credentials.

Each user shall authenticate independently when required.

### User Identity

External integrations shall use ART user identity information
established by Epics 49 and 50.

ART shall distinguish between:

- ART identity.
- External service identity.
- External account.
- External organization membership.

The system shall not assume that matching display names represent the
same person.

### Device Linking

External integrations shall work with ART's device-linking
functionality.

Users who use ART on multiple devices shall be able to authenticate the
external integration separately as necessary.

Provider tokens shall not be copied through shared `.art` files.

### Security

All external integrations shall comply with ART's security architecture.

ART shall:

- Use secure authentication.
- Protect OAuth tokens.
- Avoid storing passwords.
- Avoid exposing credentials in logs.
- Validate external API responses.
- Validate imported data.
- Protect against malicious external content.
- Use HTTPS for network communication.
- Apply least-privilege permissions.
- Respect external service authorization.
- Provide secure token revocation/disconnection.
- Avoid transmitting unnecessary information.

### Privacy

ART shall clearly communicate what data is shared with each external
platform.

Before sending data to an external service, ART shall provide enough
information for the user to understand:

- What information will be transmitted.
- Which external service will receive it.
- Which account/project/repository will receive it.
- Whether the operation is one-time or ongoing.
- Whether future synchronization will occur.

### Enterprise Privacy

Organizations may prohibit certain integrations.

ART shall support organizational restrictions where server-based
organizational policies are available.

For file-based use, users shall still be able to use ART without
integrations.

### Accessibility

All integration functionality shall meet ART's accessibility
requirements.

This includes:

- Integration management.
- Authentication.
- Account selection.
- Project selection.
- Repository selection.
- Field mapping.
- Import.
- Export.
- Synchronization.
- Conflict resolution.
- Error handling.
- Disconnecting integrations.

### Screen Reader Testing

Integrations shall be tested with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.

Screen readers shall receive meaningful information about:

- Integration name.
- Connection status.
- Account.
- Organization.
- Project.
- Repository.
- Synchronization state.
- Errors.
- Conflicts.

### Low-Vision Testing

Integration workflows shall be tested using:

- Browser zoom.
- Operating-system magnification.
- High contrast.
- ART visual settings.
- Different screen sizes.
- Different display scaling.

### Keyboard Accessibility

All integration workflows shall be fully keyboard accessible.

Commands shall be available through:

- Menubar menus.
- Global context menus.
- Context menus appropriate to the selected object.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.

### Command Architecture

Potential commands shall include:

- Connect Integration.
- Disconnect Integration.
- Configure Integration.
- Import.
- Export.
- Synchronize.
- Refresh.
- Create External Issue.
- Link External Issue.
- Unlink External Issue.
- Open External Issue.
- View Integration Status.

### Context Menu

Integration commands shall be available through the global context menu
where appropriate.

For example, when an accessibility finding is selected:

``` text
Context Menu
    |
    +-- Create Jira Issue
    +-- Create GitHub Issue
    +-- Create Azure DevOps Work Item
    +-- Link External Issue
    +-- Open Linked Issue
```

Only commands appropriate to the selected object and user's permissions
shall be displayed.

### History Framework

Applicable integration actions shall integrate with ART's History
Framework.

Where an operation changes ART data, users should be able to undo and
redo the change where technically appropriate.

External actions that cannot be safely reversed shall clearly
communicate that limitation.

For example, deleting an external Jira issue shall not be performed
merely because the user undoes creation of the ART-to-Jira relationship.

### Import

ART shall provide controlled import functionality.

Imported data shall be:

- Validated.
- Sanitized.
- Mapped to ART's data model.
- Presented for user confirmation where appropriate.

ART shall not blindly execute instructions contained within imported
external data.

### Export

ART shall provide controlled export/synchronization functionality.

Users shall be able to review important information before transmitting
it externally.

### Duplicate Prevention

ART shall avoid accidentally creating duplicate external issues.

Where supported, ART shall retain a stable relationship between the ART
object and the external issue.

Before creating a new issue, ART should check whether an existing linked
issue already exists.

### External Deletion

If an externally linked issue is deleted:

- ART shall preserve the ART finding/task.
- ART shall identify that the external item is unavailable.
- ART shall not delete the ART object automatically.
- The user shall be able to create a replacement external issue if
  desired.

### External Status Changes

When an external issue's status changes, ART may synchronize that state
when configured.

The synchronization shall not unexpectedly change an ART task's status
unless the user has enabled that behavior.

### External Priority Changes

External priority changes may be synchronized with ART priority where
configured.

ART shall preserve its own priority model.

Mappings shall be configurable where external priority schemes differ.

### External Assignees

Where external users can be mapped to ART users, ART may synchronize
assignments.

The mapping shall not assume that identical names represent the same
person.

Where no reliable mapping exists, ART shall inform the user rather than
assigning the task incorrectly.

### Integration Configuration

Each integration shall provide a configuration interface appropriate to
its capabilities.

Configuration may include:

- Account.
- Organization.
- Project.
- Repository.
- Team.
- Default issue type.
- Default priority.
- Field mappings.
- Synchronization direction.
- Synchronization frequency.
- Comment synchronization.
- Assignment synchronization.

### Default Settings

Users shall be able to establish default integration settings where
supported.

Defaults shall not override explicit choices made during an individual
operation unless the user has configured that behavior.

### Multiple Accounts

Where technically supported, ART should allow users to connect more than
one account for the same integration provider.

For example:

``` text
Jira
    |
    +-- Personal/Organization Account A
    +-- Organization Account B
```

Users shall be able to identify which account is being used for each
operation.

### Multiple Projects and Repositories

Users shall be able to connect ART to multiple external projects or
repositories where supported.

ART shall clearly identify the destination before creating or
synchronizing external items.

### Integration Logs

ART may provide a user-accessible integration history.

The history may include:

- Date/time.
- Integration.
- Operation.
- Result.
- External object.
- Error information.

Logs shall not contain passwords, OAuth tokens, or other secrets.

### Error Handling

ART shall provide understandable error messages for:

- Authentication failure.
- Authorization failure.
- Permission denied.
- Project unavailable.
- Repository unavailable.
- External item unavailable.
- Invalid mapping.
- Synchronization failure.
- Network failure.
- Rate limiting.
- External service outage.
- Invalid external data.
- Duplicate issue.
- Conflict.

### Rate Limiting

ART shall handle external API rate limits gracefully.

When rate limited, ART shall:

- Avoid unnecessary repeated requests.
- Inform the user when appropriate.
- Retry according to provider-supported guidance.
- Preserve unsynchronized work.
- Avoid blocking unrelated ART functionality.

### External Service Outages

If an external platform is unavailable:

- ART shall remain usable.
- Existing ART data shall remain available.
- Pending integration operations shall be preserved where possible.
- ART shall provide an accessible status message.
- Users shall be able to retry later.

### Offline Operation

External integrations shall not prevent offline use of ART.

When offline:

- Core ART functionality shall remain available.
- Existing integration links shall remain visible.
- External synchronization shall be deferred.
- Pending operations shall be handled safely.
- The user shall be informed when synchronization cannot occur.

### Testing

Each integration shall receive:

- Unit testing.
- Integration testing.
- Accessibility testing.
- Security testing.
- Error-handling testing.
- End-to-end testing.
- Offline testing.
- Authentication testing.
- Permission testing.
- Synchronization testing.

### Jira Testing

Jira testing shall include:

- Authentication.
- Project selection.
- Issue creation.
- Issue linking.
- Issue updates.
- Status mapping.
- Priority mapping.
- Assignment mapping.
- Comment handling.
- Permission changes.
- Token expiration.
- API errors.
- Rate limiting.

### GitHub Testing

GitHub testing shall include:

- Authentication.
- Repository selection.
- Issue creation.
- Issue linking.
- Issue updates.
- Labels.
- Assignees.
- Comments where supported.
- Repository permission changes.
- Token expiration.
- API errors.
- Rate limiting.

### Azure DevOps Testing

Azure DevOps testing shall include:

- Authentication.
- Organization selection.
- Project selection.
- Work-item creation.
- Work-item linking.
- Work-item updates.
- Status mapping.
- Priority mapping.
- Assignment mapping.
- Permission changes.
- Token expiration.
- API errors.
- Rate limiting.

### Google Workspace Testing

Google Workspace testing shall include:

- Authentication.
- Drive integration.
- Docs integration where implemented.
- Sheets integration where implemented.
- Permission changes.
- Account changes.
- Token expiration.
- API errors.
- Rate limiting.

### Cross-Integration Testing

Testing shall verify that users can use multiple integrations within the
same ART installation.

For example:

``` text
ART Finding
    |
    +-- Jira Issue
    +-- GitHub Issue
    +-- Azure DevOps Work Item
```

ART shall preserve these relationships independently.

### File-Based Collaboration Testing

Testing shall verify that shared `.art` files containing external
integration metadata can be opened by multiple users.

Testing shall verify:

- External links are preserved.
- Credentials are not stored in the file.
- Users authenticate independently.
- Users without integration access can still open the report.
- Missing integrations do not prevent core report functionality.
- External identifiers remain valid where possible.

### Multi-Device Testing

Integration functionality shall be tested across:

- ART Web.
- ART Desktop.
- Multiple computers.
- Multiple browsers where applicable.

Users shall not be required to share OAuth credentials between devices.

### Accessibility Testing

End-to-end integration workflows shall be tested with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- TalkBack.
- ChromeVox.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only operation.
- Low-vision users.
- Screen magnification.
- High-contrast settings.
- Other relevant assistive technologies.

### Documentation

ART documentation shall explain:

- Available integrations.
- How to connect integrations.
- Authentication.
- Permissions.
- Data sharing.
- Import.
- Export.
- Synchronization.
- Field mapping.
- Conflict handling.
- Disconnecting integrations.
- Security.
- Privacy.
- Offline behavior.
- File-based collaboration.
- Server-based collaboration.

Documentation shall clearly state that integrations are optional.

### Backward Compatibility

External integrations shall not modify existing `.art` files in a way
that prevents them from being opened by versions of ART that do not
support the integration.

Integration metadata shall be designed for graceful degradation.

A user without a particular integration shall still be able to open and
edit the report.

### Future Integrations

The External Integration Interface shall be designed to accommodate
future platforms.

Potential future integrations include:

- ServiceNow.
- Trello.
- Asana.
- Monday.com.
- Linear.
- ClickUp.
- Slack.
- Microsoft Teams.
- Notion.
- GitLab.
- Bitbucket.
- Other issue-tracking systems.
- Other project-management systems.
- Other accessibility-testing platforms.

Future integrations shall not require redesigning ART's core reporting
architecture.

### Definition of Done

Epic 56 shall be considered complete when:

- A provider-independent External Integration Architecture exists.
- Integration management is available through ART Settings.
- Users can connect and disconnect supported integrations.
- Secure delegated authentication is implemented.
- OAuth tokens are protected.
- External passwords are never stored by ART.
- Least-privilege permissions are requested.
- Jira integration is implemented.
- GitHub Issues integration is implemented.
- Azure DevOps integration is implemented.
- Google Workspace integration is implemented to the agreed supported
  scope.
- Users can create or link external issues from ART findings where
  supported.
- External issue relationships are preserved.
- Appropriate data mappings are implemented.
- Synchronization direction is clearly communicated.
- Synchronization conflicts are handled safely.
- External deletions do not automatically delete ART data.
- External permissions are respected.
- Multiple external accounts can be supported where technically
  appropriate.
- Integration credentials are never stored in shared `.art` files.
- File-based collaboration remains functional.
- Shared reports remain usable by users who do not have the relevant
  external integration.
- Tasks can be linked to external work items where supported.
- Accessibility findings can be linked to external issues.
- @mention behavior is handled safely.
- Integration commands are available through appropriate menubar
  commands.
- Integration commands are available through appropriate context menus.
- Integration commands can use customizable keyboard shortcuts.
- Applicable ART changes integrate with the History Framework.
- Offline ART functionality remains fully usable.
- External service outages do not prevent core ART functionality.
- Rate limiting is handled safely.
- Authentication expiration is handled safely.
- Permission changes are handled safely.
- External data is validated and sanitized.
- Security testing has been completed.
- Privacy considerations have been reviewed.
- Jira end-to-end testing has been completed.
- GitHub Issues end-to-end testing has been completed.
- Azure DevOps end-to-end testing has been completed.
- Google Workspace end-to-end testing has been completed.
- Multi-user testing has been completed.
- Multi-device testing has been completed.
- File-based collaboration testing has been completed.
- JAWS testing has been completed.
- NVDA testing has been completed.
- Narrator testing has been completed.
- VoiceOver testing has been completed.
- TalkBack testing has been completed.
- ChromeVox testing has been completed.
- Braille-display testing has been completed.
- Low-vision testing has been completed.
- Keyboard-only testing has been completed.
- Documentation has been completed.
- Existing ART functionality has not regressed.
- The architecture supports future external integrations without major
  changes to ART's core reporting functionality.

## Epic 57 — ART Desktop Application and Cross-Platform Packaging

### Epic Overview

Extend ART beyond its existing web application by creating a
full-featured, standalone, downloadable, installable desktop application
while preserving the existing web application.

The ART desktop application shall provide complete functional,
usability, accessibility, security, privacy, performance, and
user-experience parity with the web application.

Creating the desktop application shall **not intentionally remove,
reduce, simplify, disable, or sacrifice any functionality available in
the web application**.

The desktop application shall instead provide an additional way to use
ART, while taking advantage of capabilities available in a native
desktop environment.

The desktop application shall initially target Windows and shall be
architected to support future macOS and Linux versions without requiring
a rewrite of ART's core application.

The preferred desktop technology is **Electron**, subject to final
technical and accessibility validation.

### Core Principle

The ART desktop application shall follow this principle:

> **Desktop ART = Full Web ART + Native Desktop Advantages**

The desktop application shall not become a reduced-feature version of
ART.

The desktop application shall provide the same ART experience,
functionality, navigation, commands, workflows, accessibility features,
collaboration capabilities, data-management capabilities, and
customization options available in the web application, while adding
desktop-specific conveniences where they provide meaningful value.

### Goals

This epic shall:

- Create a standalone ART desktop application.
- Preserve the existing ART web application.
- Provide complete functional parity between web and desktop ART.
- Use Electron as the preferred desktop framework.
- Share ART's core application logic between web and desktop.
- Avoid maintaining two independent implementations of ART
  functionality.
- Provide an official ART desktop download through the ART website.
- Allow users to download ART without visiting GitHub.
- Provide a standard Windows installation workflow.
- Allow users to launch ART as a standard Windows application.
- Support `.art` file associations.
- Support opening `.art` files directly from the operating system.
- Support local-first operation.
- Support file-based collaboration.
- Support cloud/shared storage.
- Support server-based collaboration when available.
- Support authentication.
- Support device linking.
- Support authorization.
- Support external integrations.
- Support all existing ART reporting functionality.
- Preserve all existing accessibility functionality.
- Preserve customizable keyboard shortcuts.
- Preserve customizable working views.
- Preserve the menu bar.
- Preserve global and contextual menus.
- Preserve search functionality.
- Preserve Tasks and To Do functionality.
- Preserve Shared Progress Logs.
- Preserve Notifications.
- Preserve History Framework functionality.
- Preserve Undo/Redo.
- Provide native desktop capabilities where appropriate.
- Provide a simple desktop update workflow.
- Automate desktop releases through GitHub Actions.
- Keep web and desktop releases synchronized to the same source version.
- Minimize manual release work for the ART maintainer.
- Provide a foundation for future macOS and Linux applications.

### Desktop Technology

Electron shall be the preferred technology for the ART desktop
application.

Electron is appropriate because ART is already a web application and
Electron can package the existing web application environment into a
desktop application while providing access to native operating-system
capabilities.

The final implementation shall validate Electron against ART's
accessibility, security, performance, and maintainability requirements
before the desktop application is considered production-ready.

### Shared Application Architecture

ART shall use a shared application architecture.

The preferred architecture shall be:

``` text
                    ART Core
                       |
          +------------+------------+
          |                         |
      Web Application          Electron Desktop
          |                         |
       Browser                  Chromium
                                    |
                              Desktop APIs
```

ART's core functionality shall be shared between the web and desktop
applications wherever practical.

The project shall avoid implementing the same business logic separately
for web and desktop.

### Shared Core Functionality

The shared ART core shall include, where applicable:

- Report model.
- Report creation.
- Report editing.
- Report viewing.
- Report management.
- Report tracking.
- WCAG Lookup.
- Accessibility standards.
- Findings.
- Tasks.
- To Do Lists.
- Shared Tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Notifications.
- User profiles.
- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- Device linking.
- Organization functionality.
- Organization Metrics.
- File-based collaboration.
- Server-based collaboration.
- Merge Changes.
- History Framework.
- Undo/Redo.
- Storage Providers.
- External Integrations.
- Import.
- Export.
- Search.
- Settings.
- Accessibility settings.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Customizable working views.

### Web Application Preservation

The existing ART web application shall remain fully functional.

The creation of the desktop application shall not require removing or
reducing functionality from the web application.

Both applications shall continue to use the same ART data model and
shared application logic wherever practical.

### Full Feature Parity Requirement

The desktop application shall provide functional parity with the web
application.

The desktop application shall preserve, at minimum:

- Dashboard.
- Report Builder.
- Report Viewer.
- Report creation.
- Report editing.
- Report management.
- Report tracking.
- Report templates.
- WCAG Lookup Tool.
- Accessibility Standards Lookup.
- Findings.
- Tasks.
- To Do Lists.
- Shared Tasks.
- Assigned Tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Notifications.
- Organization Metrics.
- Collaboration.
- File-based collaboration.
- Server-based collaboration when available.
- Merge Changes.
- Import.
- Export.
- Report generation.
- Report outputs.
- Search.
- Settings.
- User profiles.
- Authentication.
- Device linking.
- Authorization.
- Storage providers.
- External integrations.
- Menu bar.
- Global context menu.
- Context-sensitive menus.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.
- Customizable working views.
- Application panes.
- Navigation.
- Accessible live status messages.
- Accessibility settings.
- History Framework.
- Undo.
- Redo.
- Task reminders.
- @mentions\.
- Comments/Notes/Instructions.
- Priority.
- Status.
- Due dates.
- Completed Tasks.
- Report/file actions.
- All other functionality available in the web application.

### No Feature Sacrifice

Creating the desktop application shall not result in intentional loss
of:

- Functionality.
- Usability.
- Accessibility.
- Performance.
- Security.
- Privacy.
- Convenience.
- Customization.
- Keyboard accessibility.
- Screen-reader accessibility.
- Collaboration capabilities.
- File-based workflows.
- Server-based workflows.
- Reporting capabilities.
- Export capabilities.
- Import capabilities.
- Navigation.
- Search.
- User interaction.

If a feature is available in the web application and technically
applicable to the desktop environment, it shall also be available in the
desktop application.

### Desktop Enhancement Principle

The desktop application may provide additional functionality that is
difficult, inconvenient, or impossible to provide through a browser.

Potential desktop enhancements include:

- Native file associations.
- Native Open dialogs.
- Native Save dialogs.
- Native folder selection.
- Native desktop notifications.
- Improved local filesystem access.
- Secure operating-system credential storage.
- Crash recovery.
- Automatic updates.
- Native application menus.
- Native clipboard integration.
- Native printing.
- Native operating-system integration.
- Improved offline functionality.
- Background synchronization where appropriate.
- Other desktop-specific capabilities.

Desktop-specific functionality shall complement ART rather than replace
existing web functionality.

### Windows as Initial Desktop Platform

Windows shall be the initial desktop platform.

The Windows version shall support appropriate currently supported
Windows versions.

The application shall behave as a standard Windows desktop application.

### Future macOS Support

The architecture shall support future macOS development without
requiring a rewrite of ART's core functionality.

### Future Linux Support

The architecture shall similarly support future Linux development.

Linux packaging may be implemented in a later epic or release.

### Official Website Distribution

ART shall provide an official desktop download experience through the
ART website.

Users shall **not be required to visit GitHub to download ART**.

The ART website shall provide a clearly labeled download link such as:

> Download ART for Windows

The link shall download the official ART Windows installation package.

### Windows Installer

The Windows desktop application shall be distributed using a standard
installation package, such as:

``` text
ART-Setup.exe
```

The installer shall launch a standard Windows installation
wizard/workflow.

The expected user workflow shall be:

1.  User visits the ART website.
2.  User activates **Download ART for Windows**.
3.  The ART installer downloads.
4.  User opens the installer.
5.  The standard Windows installation workflow begins.
6.  User completes installation.
7.  ART becomes available as a standard Windows application.

### Application Launch

After installation, users shall be able to launch ART through standard
Windows mechanisms, including:

- Start Menu.
- Desktop shortcut, where provided.
- `.art` file association.
- Installed ART executable.
- Windows Search.
- Other standard application-launch mechanisms.

The installed application shall provide an executable such as:

``` text
ART.exe
```

### GitHub as Release Infrastructure

GitHub may remain the underlying source-code, build, release, and
distribution infrastructure.

However, users shall not be required to interact with GitHub to install
ART.

GitHub may be used for:

- Source code.
- Issue tracking.
- Release management.
- Build automation.
- GitHub Actions.
- Release artifacts.
- Development.
- Automated testing.

### Automated Release Pipeline

ART shall use an automated CI/CD pipeline to minimize manual release
work.

A release from the ART repository shall be capable of automatically:

1.  Validate the source code.
2.  Run automated tests.
3.  Build the web application.
4.  Build the Electron desktop application.
5.  Generate the Windows installer.
6.  Assign the same release version to web and desktop builds.
7.  Publish the desktop installer.
8.  Deploy the web application.
9.  Publish/update desktop update metadata.
10. Record the release information.

### Single-Source Release

The web and desktop applications shall be built from the same
source-code commit for each production release.

For example:

``` text
Git Commit
    |
    |-- Version 1.2.0
    |
    +----> Web ART 1.2.0
    |
    +----> Desktop ART 1.2.0
```

This shall ensure that the web and desktop applications remain
synchronized to the same application version and source revision.

### Web/Desktop Synchronization

The web and desktop applications shall remain synchronized at the
application-release level.

A production release shall use:

- The same ART version.
- The same release commit.
- The same ART data model.
- The same core business logic.
- The same accessibility requirements.
- The same feature set.

The desktop application shall not independently drift into a different
feature set.

### Important Synchronization Limitation

Web and desktop applications shall be synchronized through the release
pipeline, but desktop users shall retain control over when an available
update is installed.

A new web deployment shall not forcibly interrupt a user's active
desktop application.

Instead:

``` text
Same GitHub Release
       |
       +----> Web updated automatically
       |
       +----> Desktop installer/update published automatically
                          |
                          ▼
                   User chooses when
                   to install update
```

### Desktop Update Architecture

The desktop application shall provide a secure automatic update
mechanism.

The update system shall:

- Check for available updates.
- Verify update authenticity.
- Verify package integrity.
- Download updates securely.
- Preserve user data.
- Preserve settings.
- Provide accessible status information.
- Avoid silently installing unexpected updates.
- Recover safely from failed updates.

### Check for Updates

The Help menu shall contain:

> Check for Updates

This command shall be accessible through:

- Help menu.
- Appropriate context/menu commands where applicable.
- A customizable keyboard shortcut where appropriate.

### Simple Update Workflow

The normal desktop update workflow shall require no more than one or two
user actions after the user chooses to check for updates.

The intended workflow shall be:

1.  User opens **Help → Check for Updates**.

2.  ART checks for an available update.

3.  If no update exists, ART informs the user.

4.  If an update exists, ART presents an accessible update dialog.

5.  The dialog provides:

    - **Update Now**
    - **Cancel**

6.  If the user activates **Update Now**, ART downloads and installs the
    update.

7.  If the user activates **Cancel**, ART remains at the current
    version.

### Update Dialog

The update dialog shall clearly communicate:

- Current ART version.
- Available ART version.
- Whether the update is recommended or security-related.
- Approximate update size where available.
- Update status.
- Available actions.

The dialog shall be fully keyboard accessible and screen-reader
accessible.

### Automatic Update Check

ART may optionally check for updates automatically.

Automatic checking shall:

- Respect user preferences.
- Not interfere with active work.
- Not interrupt users unexpectedly.
- Provide an accessible notification when an update is available.
- Allow the user to initiate the update.

### Security-Critical Updates

Security-critical updates may receive special treatment.

ART may notify users more prominently when an update addresses a
critical security issue.

The update shall still use secure update mechanisms.

### Update Failure

If an update fails:

- The existing ART installation shall remain usable where possible.
- User data shall remain intact.
- ART shall communicate the failure.
- ART shall provide a retry option.
- ART shall provide a recovery mechanism.
- ART shall not silently delete the existing installation.

### Interrupted Update

If an update is interrupted because of:

- Network failure.
- Computer shutdown.
- User cancellation.
- Installer failure.

ART shall recover safely.

The application shall not leave the user with a broken installation
whenever technically avoidable.

### Update Rollback

Where technically supported, ART shall provide rollback/recovery if a
newly installed update cannot launch successfully.

### Release Automation

The ART maintainer should not need to manually build the desktop
application every time the web application is updated.

The preferred release process shall be:

``` text
Developer/Maintainer
        |
        | Pushes release to GitHub
        ▼
GitHub Actions
        |
        +--> Automated tests
        |
        +--> Build Web ART
        |
        +--> Build Electron ART
        |
        +--> Build ART-Setup.exe
        |
        +--> Publish release
        |
        +--> Deploy Web ART
        |
        +--> Publish desktop update metadata
```

### Release Failure Handling

If the desktop build fails:

- The release pipeline shall identify the failure.
- The web deployment shall not be falsely represented as having a
  matching desktop release.
- The release shall not be marked as fully successful.
- The maintainer shall receive an actionable error.
- Previously released desktop versions shall remain available.

If the web build fails, the same principle shall apply.

### Release Validation

A production release shall not be considered complete until the
automated pipeline confirms that the required web and desktop artifacts
were successfully produced.

### Release Versioning

Web and desktop releases shall use the same ART version number.

For example:

``` text
ART Web:      1.5.0
ART Desktop:  1.5.0
```

Where appropriate, the desktop build shall also retain the source commit
identifier.

### Installation

The installer shall provide an accessible installation workflow.

The installer shall:

- Clearly identify ART.
- Explain what is being installed.
- Provide accessible controls.
- Support keyboard navigation.
- Work with screen readers.
- Avoid unnecessary bundled software.
- Request only necessary privileges.

### Uninstallation

Users shall be able to uninstall ART using standard Windows mechanisms.

Uninstallation shall not silently delete user-created reports.

### User Data Preservation

Uninstalling ART shall not automatically delete:

- `.art` reports.
- Templates.
- Backups.
- Exported reports.
- User settings.

If application data can be removed, the user shall be clearly informed.

### `.art` File Association

ART shall register the `.art` file extension.

Users shall be able to:

- Double-click `.art` files.
- Open `.art` files through Open With.
- Associate `.art` files with ART.
- Change the association through Windows.

### Opening `.art` Files

When a user opens an `.art` file:

1.  ART launches if necessary.
2.  ART loads the file.
3.  ART validates the file.
4.  ART identifies the report/project.
5.  ART restores the appropriate working state.
6.  ART checks for synchronization changes.
7.  ART checks for merge conflicts.
8.  ART displays appropriate notifications.
9.  ART opens the Merge Changes interface when required.

### Local-First Operation

The desktop application shall remain fully usable without an ART server.

Users shall be able to:

- Create reports.
- Edit reports.
- Save reports.
- Open reports.
- Import reports.
- Export reports.
- Use Tasks.
- Use Progress Logs.
- Use History.
- Use Undo/Redo.
- Use WCAG Lookup.
- Use accessibility settings.
- Work with `.art` files.
- Perform other fundamental ART functions.

### File-Based Collaboration

The desktop application shall fully support ART's file-based
collaboration infrastructure.

Users shall be able to store `.art` files in:

- Local folders.
- Shared network folders.
- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Other supported storage providers.

ART shall:

- Detect changes.
- Compare versions.
- Merge compatible changes.
- Detect conflicts.
- Preserve changes.
- Present Merge Changes when required.
- Avoid silently overwriting newer work.

### Cloud Storage

The desktop application shall support the Storage Provider Architecture.

Supported providers shall include, where implemented:

- Local Files.
- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.

### Offline Operation

The desktop application shall remain fully functional for
non-server-dependent features while offline.

### Reconnection

When connectivity returns, ART shall safely synchronize applicable data
and detect conflicts.

### Authentication

The desktop application shall support ART's authentication architecture.

Supported authentication providers shall include, where implemented:

- Google.
- Microsoft.
- Amazon.
- GitHub.

Passwordless authentication shall be preferred.

External provider passwords shall never be stored by ART.

### Device Linking

The desktop application shall support the device-linking architecture
established by Epic 50.

Users shall be able to associate multiple ART installations with the
same ART identity.

### User Profile

The desktop application shall support:

- Name.
- Email.
- Display name.
- Job title.
- Role.
- Other supported profile information.

### Authorization

The desktop application shall enforce ART authorization policies.

Authorization shall apply to:

- Reports.
- Projects.
- Organizations.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Shared content.
- External integrations.
- Server-dependent functionality.

### Security

The desktop application shall:

- Validate files.
- Sanitize imported content.
- Protect credentials.
- Protect tokens.
- Avoid plain-text secrets.
- Use secure network connections.
- Validate external data.
- Request minimal privileges.
- Protect against malicious files.
- Avoid executing arbitrary report content.

### Operating-System Credential Storage

Sensitive credentials/tokens should use secure operating-system
credential storage.

For Windows, this may include:

- Windows Credential Manager.
- Equivalent secure credential APIs.

Future platforms shall use their equivalent secure credential
mechanisms.

### Application Sandboxing

Where supported, Electron shall use appropriate application isolation
and sandboxing capabilities.

ART shall request only the permissions it requires.

### Performance

The desktop application shall remain responsive when:

- Opening reports.
- Saving reports.
- Searching.
- Filtering.
- Loading large projects.
- Viewing Tasks.
- Viewing Progress Logs.
- Running WCAG searches.
- Exporting reports.
- Synchronizing.
- Running integrations.

### Large Reports

The desktop application shall be tested with large reports containing:

- Large numbers of findings.
- Large numbers of tasks.
- Large Progress Logs.
- Large WCAG references.
- Large exports.
- Multiple integrations.

### Dashboard

The desktop dashboard shall provide the same functionality as the web
dashboard.

This includes, where implemented:

- Notifications.
- Tasks.
- To Do Lists.
- Progress information.
- Organization Metrics.
- Shared activity.
- Reminders.
- Collaboration information.
- Other dashboard functionality.

### Tasks

The desktop application shall provide full Tasks functionality.

Users shall be able to:

- Create tasks.
- Edit tasks.
- Delete tasks.
- Assign tasks.
- Reassign tasks.
- Set priority.
- Set status.
- Set due date/time.
- Set reminders.
- Add comments/notes/instructions.
- Use @mentions.
- Complete tasks.
- Restore tasks.
- Sort tasks.
- Filter tasks.
- Use context menus.
- Use keyboard shortcuts.

### Completed Tasks

Completed tasks shall automatically move to the Completed Tasks panel.

Changing their status back to an active status shall return them to the
active To Do list.

### Shared Progress Logs

The desktop application shall fully support Shared Progress Logs.

### Notifications

The desktop application shall support the ART Notifications system.

Notifications may include:

- Task assignments.
- Reassignments.
- @mentions\.
- Progress Log changes.
- Merge conflicts.
- Synchronization events.
- Integration events.
- Authentication events.
- Reminders.
- Update notifications.

### Desktop Notifications

Where appropriate, ART may use native Windows notifications.

Native notifications shall not replace ART's accessible Notifications
interface.

### Task Reminders

Task reminders shall support:

- Visual alerts.
- Auditory alerts.
- Focus-grabbing modal alerts where appropriate.
- Snooze.
- 5-minute snooze.
- 15-minute snooze.
- 30-minute snooze.
- User-configurable snooze intervals.

### Sound Effects

Optional task/action sound effects shall be supported where appropriate.

Sound shall never be the only indication of an important event.

### WCAG Lookup

The desktop WCAG Lookup Tool shall provide the same capabilities as the
web version.

### Report Creation and Editing

The desktop application shall provide full Report Builder and Report
Viewer functionality.

### Import and Export

All supported import/export formats shall remain available.

### External Integrations

The desktop application shall support the External Integration
Architecture established by Epic 56.

This includes supported:

- Jira.
- GitHub Issues.
- Azure DevOps.
- Google Workspace.

### Integration Credentials

External integration credentials shall never be stored in shared `.art`
files.

Each user shall authenticate independently where required.

### Menu Bar

The desktop application shall provide an accessible application menubar.

Menus shall include appropriate commands for:

- File.
- Edit.
- View.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Reports.
- Accessibility.
- Storage.
- Integrations.
- Help.
- Settings.

### Help Menu

The Help menu shall contain:

- Check for Updates.
- About ART.
- ART documentation.
- Accessibility information.
- Other applicable help commands.

### Global Context Menu

The desktop application shall preserve ART's global context-menu
architecture.

Commands shall be:

- Context-sensitive.
- Permission-aware.
- Keyboard accessible.
- Screen-reader accessible.

### Keyboard Shortcuts

All existing customizable keyboard shortcuts shall be preserved.

Users shall be able to:

- View shortcuts.
- Search shortcuts.
- Customize shortcuts.
- Restore defaults.
- Detect conflicts.
- Disable optional shortcuts.

### Customizable Working Views

The desktop application shall preserve customizable working views.

Users shall be able to configure visible application panels and views.

### Accessibility

Accessibility shall be a release requirement.

The desktop application shall expose appropriate:

- Names.
- Roles.
- States.
- Properties.
- Relationships.
- Values.

### Screen Readers

Windows desktop testing shall include:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.

Future platform testing shall include appropriate platform screen
readers.

### Braille

ART shall be tested with supported braille displays through the relevant
screen readers and accessibility APIs.

### Keyboard-Only Operation

Every desktop feature shall be operable using the keyboard.

### Low-Vision Testing

Testing shall include:

- Zoom.
- Magnification.
- Display scaling.
- High contrast.
- ART visual settings.
- Different screen resolutions.
- Different window sizes.

### Focus Management

Modal dialogs shall:

- Move focus appropriately.
- Trap focus where required.
- Return focus appropriately.
- Expose meaningful titles and instructions.

### Live Status Messages

The desktop application shall preserve ART's accessible live status
messaging.

Important operations shall communicate their status to assistive
technologies.

### History Framework

The desktop application shall use the existing ART History Framework.

Users shall be able to:

- Undo.
- Redo.
- Use keyboard shortcuts.
- Use menu commands.

Applicable Tasks, dashboard, collaboration, and other changes shall
participate in History where appropriate.

### Crash Recovery

ART shall attempt to recover unsaved work after a crash.

### Auto-Save and Recovery Copies

ART may maintain recovery copies without silently overwriting the user's
intentionally saved `.art` file.

### Recovery Workflow

Users shall be able to:

- Recover work.
- Discard recovery data.
- Save recovered work.
- Compare versions where appropriate.

### Version Compatibility

ART shall detect `.art` file compatibility.

If migration is required:

- The user shall be informed.
- The original shall be preserved where practical.
- Migration shall be recoverable.

### Distribution Security

Official installers shall be digitally signed where practical.

ART shall provide a trustworthy release mechanism.

### Code Signing

Windows desktop releases should be digitally signed.

The project shall establish an appropriate certificate and signing
process.

### Release Artifacts

Each production release shall produce, where applicable:

- Web deployment artifact.
- Windows installer.
- Version information.
- Release notes.
- Update metadata.
- Checksums or equivalent integrity information.

### Release Notes

Desktop updates shall provide accessible release notes.

Release notes should identify:

- New functionality.
- Bug fixes.
- Accessibility improvements.
- Security fixes.
- Compatibility changes.
- Known issues.

### Accessibility of the Installer

The installer itself shall be tested for accessibility.

Users shall be able to install ART using:

- Keyboard.
- Screen reader.
- Magnification.
- High contrast.

### Accessibility of the Updater

The update workflow shall also be accessible.

The user shall be able to:

- Check for updates.
- Read update information.
- Activate Update Now.
- Activate Cancel.
- Monitor update progress.
- Understand failures.

### Testing

The desktop application shall receive complete end-to-end testing.

Testing shall include:

- Unit testing.
- Integration testing.
- Functional testing.
- Regression testing.
- Security testing.
- Performance testing.
- Accessibility testing.
- Installation testing.
- Update testing.
- Collaboration testing.
- File-based collaboration testing.
- External integration testing.
- Multi-device testing.

### Web/Desktop Feature-Parity Testing

Every major web feature shall be tested against its desktop equivalent.

The test matrix shall identify:

| Feature | Web | Desktop | Equivalent | Additional Desktop Capability |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| Dashboard | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| Report Builder | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| Report Viewer | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| Tasks | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| Progress Logs | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| WCAG Lookup | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| Collaboration | Required | Required | Yes | As applicable |
| Import/Export | Required | Required | Yes | Native file access |
| Keyboard Shortcuts | Required | Required | Yes | Native desktop commands |
| Settings | Required | Required | Yes | OS integration |
| Integrations | Required | Required | Yes | Secure credential storage |

No major feature shall be intentionally omitted from the desktop
application.

### Collaboration Testing

Testing shall include:

- Sequential editing.
- Concurrent editing.
- Multiple users.
- Multiple devices.
- Shared folders.
- Cloud storage.
- Network folders.
- Remote changes.
- Local changes.
- Merge conflicts.
- Merge resolution.
- Reopening after merge.
- Shared Tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- @mentions\.
- Notifications.

### Multi-Device Testing

Testing shall verify that the same ART user can work across:

- Desktop ART.
- Web ART.
- Multiple computers.
- Multiple ART installations.

### Security Testing

Testing shall include:

- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- Credential storage.
- Token storage.
- File validation.
- Network security.
- Update security.
- Package integrity.
- Dependency security.
- Sandboxing.
- Permission handling.

### Update Testing

Update testing shall include:

- No update available.
- Update available.
- Update Now.
- Cancel.
- Successful update.
- Failed update.
- Interrupted update.
- Network interruption.
- Invalid update package.
- Rollback/recovery.
- Preservation of user data.
- Preservation of settings.
- Version synchronization.

### Automated Release Testing

GitHub Actions shall verify before publishing a release that:

- The web build succeeds.
- The desktop build succeeds.
- The Windows installer is generated.
- Automated tests pass.
- Version numbers match.
- Release artifacts are valid.
- Update metadata is valid.
- Deployment succeeds.

### Documentation

Documentation shall explain:

- Downloading ART.
- Installing ART.
- Launching ART.
- Updating ART.
- Checking for updates.
- Uninstalling ART.
- `.art` file associations.
- File-based collaboration.
- Cloud storage.
- Authentication.
- Device linking.
- External integrations.
- Accessibility settings.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Working views.
- Backup/recovery.
- Troubleshooting.

### Future Platforms

The desktop architecture shall remain suitable for future:

- macOS.
- Linux.

Mobile applications are not required by this epic, but the shared ART
core should avoid unnecessarily preventing future mobile development.

### Definition of Done

Epic 57 shall be considered complete when:

- A production-capable ART desktop application exists.
- Electron has been validated as the desktop framework.
- Windows is supported.
- The existing web application remains fully functional.
- Web and desktop share ART's core application architecture.
- The desktop application provides functional parity with the web
  application.
- No major existing web functionality has been intentionally removed
  from the desktop version.
- The desktop application provides additional native desktop
  capabilities where appropriate.
- The ART website provides a direct desktop download link.
- Users do not need to visit GitHub to download ART.
- The Windows installer uses a standard installation workflow.
- ART installs as a standard Windows application.
- ART provides an `ART.exe` executable.
- ART can be launched through the Windows Start Menu.
- `.art` files can be associated with ART.
- Double-clicking an `.art` file opens ART.
- Local-first functionality works without a server.
- File-based collaboration works.
- Cloud storage providers work to their supported scope.
- Server-based functionality works when available.
- Authentication works.
- Passwordless authentication works where implemented.
- Device linking works.
- Authorization works.
- User profiles work.
- Tasks work.
- To Do Lists work.
- Shared Tasks work.
- Shared Progress Logs work.
- Notifications work.
- Task reminders work.
- @mentions work.
- Completed Tasks work.
- WCAG Lookup works.
- Report creation works.
- Report editing works.
- Report viewing works.
- Report management works.
- Report tracking works.
- Import works.
- Export works.
- External integrations work to their supported scope.
- Menu bar functionality works.
- Context menus work.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts work.
- Customizable working views work.
- Search works.
- Accessibility settings work.
- Accessible live status messages work.
- History Framework integration works.
- Undo/Redo works.
- Crash recovery works.
- Desktop notifications work where implemented.
- Native desktop capabilities work where implemented.
- The Help menu contains Check for Updates.
- The update workflow supports Check for Updates.
- The update workflow provides Update Now.
- The update workflow provides Cancel.
- Normal updates require no more than one or two user actions after
  checking for updates.
- Updates preserve user data.
- Updates preserve settings.
- Failed updates do not leave the installation unusable where
  technically avoidable.
- Updates use secure package verification.
- Desktop releases can be automatically built by GitHub Actions.
- Web and desktop builds originate from the same release commit.
- Web and desktop releases use the same ART version.
- GitHub Actions can automatically build both web and desktop artifacts
  from the same release.
- The web application can be automatically deployed through the same
  release pipeline.
- The desktop installer/update artifact can be automatically published
  through the same release pipeline.
- Desktop update metadata can be automatically generated or updated.
- The maintainer does not need to manually rebuild the desktop
  application for each normal web release.
- A failed desktop build prevents the release from being incorrectly
  represented as a synchronized production release.
- A failed web build is similarly reported.
- Official installers are digitally signed where practical.
- Credentials are protected.
- Sensitive credentials are never stored in `.art` files.
- Security testing is complete.
- Accessibility testing is complete.
- JAWS testing is complete.
- NVDA testing is complete.
- Narrator testing is complete.
- Braille-display testing is complete.
- Keyboard-only testing is complete.
- Low-vision testing is complete.
- Screen-magnification testing is complete.
- Installer accessibility testing is complete.
- Updater accessibility testing is complete.
- Installation testing is complete.
- Update testing is complete.
- Feature-parity testing is complete.
- Multi-device testing is complete.
- File-based collaboration testing is complete.
- Merge-conflict testing is complete.
- External integration testing is complete.
- Documentation is complete.
- The desktop application does not require an ART server for fundamental
  ART functionality.
- Existing ART functionality has not regressed.
- The architecture supports future macOS and Linux applications.

## Epic 58 — ART Privacy, Data Governance, and User Data Control

### Epic Overview

Establish a comprehensive privacy, data-governance, and
user-data-control framework for the Accessibility Reporting Tool (ART).

ART shall be designed and implemented according to **privacy-by-design,
data minimization, user control, transparency, and least-data-necessary
principles**.

Privacy shall be treated as a first-class architectural requirement
rather than merely as documentation or a privacy policy added after
development.

ART shall clearly distinguish between:

- Data stored locally on a user's device.
- Data stored in `.art` files.
- Data stored in shared folders.
- Data transmitted between ART users.
- Data stored on ART-controlled servers.
- Data stored by self-hosted ART installations.
- Data transmitted to third-party services.
- Data processed by authentication providers.
- Data processed by external integrations.
- Technical information required to operate the service.
- Optional telemetry or analytics, if ever implemented.

### Privacy-by-Design Principle

ART shall follow the principle:

> **Collect, process, transmit, and retain only the minimum information
> necessary to provide the functionality the user has explicitly chosen
> to use.**

ART shall not collect or transmit information merely because it
technically can.

### Local-First Privacy

ART shall preserve its local-first architecture.

Users shall be able to use ART without:

- Creating an account.
- Signing in.
- Providing an email address.
- Providing their name.
- Connecting to an ART server.
- Uploading reports to ART-controlled infrastructure.

Fundamental ART functionality shall remain available without
authentication.

### No-Account Usage

Users who do not sign in shall retain access to ART's fundamental
capabilities.

These capabilities shall include, where applicable:

- Creating reports.
- Editing reports.
- Viewing reports.
- Saving reports.
- Opening reports.
- Importing reports.
- Exporting reports.
- Using report templates.
- Using the WCAG Lookup Tool.
- Using accessibility standards information.
- Using Tasks and To Do Lists.
- Using Progress Logs.
- Using History.
- Using Undo/Redo.
- Using accessibility settings.
- Customizing keyboard shortcuts.
- Customizing working views.
- Using local `.art` files.
- Using other functionality that does not inherently require server
  services.

### Authentication Privacy

Authentication shall only be required for functionality that genuinely
requires an authenticated identity.

Examples may include:

- Server-based collaboration.
- Organization membership.
- Server-hosted projects.
- Server-hosted reports.
- Server synchronization.
- Organization Metrics requiring centralized data.
- Server-based Tasks.
- Server-based Progress Logs.
- Other server-dependent functionality.

### Passwordless Authentication

ART shall prefer passwordless authentication.

Where OAuth or other external authentication providers are used, ART
shall minimize the personal information obtained from those providers.

ART shall not store external provider passwords.

### Authentication Providers

Where implemented, ART may support:

- Google.
- Microsoft.
- Amazon.
- GitHub.
- Other appropriate identity providers.

ART shall clearly explain what information is received from the selected
authentication provider.

### Authentication Data Minimization

ART shall request only the identity information required to establish
and maintain an ART account.

Where possible, this shall be limited to information such as:

- Provider identifier.
- Email address.
- Display name.
- Authentication metadata required for account management.

ART shall not request unrelated profile information without a legitimate
purpose.

### User Profile Privacy

ART may allow users to provide:

- Name.
- Email address.
- Display name.
- Job title.
- Role.

Users shall be informed why each piece of information is used.

For example, profile information may support:

- Task assignments.
- @mentions\.
- Collaboration.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Organization membership.
- User identification.
- Audit history.

### Optional Profile Information

Where profile information is not technically required, it should remain
optional.

ART shall not require users to provide unnecessary personal information
merely to use fundamental functionality.

### User Identity in File-Based Collaboration

ART's file-based collaboration architecture shall minimize personal
information stored inside `.art` files.

Where identity information is required for:

- Change attribution.
- Merge resolution.
- @mentions\.
- Task assignments.
- Progress Logs.

ART shall store only the minimum information necessary.

### File-Based Identity

Users shall be able to configure their ART identity locally.

The identity information may include:

- Name.
- Email.
- Display name.
- Job title.
- Role.

The user shall be able to edit this information later.

### Personal Identity Tokens

Where Epic 50 provides a personal identity/device-linking token, the
token shall be treated as sensitive information.

ART shall:

- Protect the token.
- Avoid exposing it unnecessarily.
- Avoid storing it in plain text where technically avoidable.
- Avoid placing it in publicly shared report content.
- Avoid including it in exports unless explicitly required.
- Avoid transmitting it to third parties unnecessarily.

### Device Linking Privacy

ART shall clearly distinguish between:

- User identity.
- Device identity.
- Authentication credentials.
- Device-linking tokens.
- Report ownership.
- Organization membership.

Device linking shall not expose unnecessary device information to other
users.

### `.art` File Privacy

ART shall treat `.art` files as potentially sensitive user data.

An `.art` file may contain:

- Accessibility findings.
- Report content.
- URLs.
- Testing notes.
- Tasks.
- Comments.
- Progress Logs.
- User identities.
- Organization information.
- Change history.
- Collaboration metadata.

ART shall not transmit `.art` files to ART-controlled servers unless the
user has explicitly chosen functionality requiring such transmission.

### Metadata Minimization

ART shall minimize metadata stored in `.art` files.

Metadata shall only be retained when necessary for:

- Report functionality.
- Versioning.
- Collaboration.
- Merge operations.
- Attribution.
- History.
- Integrity.
- Recovery.

### Sensitive Metadata

ART shall identify metadata that could reveal:

- User identities.
- Email addresses.
- Organization membership.
- Internal project names.
- Internal URLs.
- Internal system information.
- File paths.
- Device information.

Such information shall not be unnecessarily exposed.

### File Export Privacy

When exporting reports, ART shall ensure that hidden metadata is not
unintentionally included.

Exports shall not unnecessarily include:

- Internal user identifiers.
- Authentication tokens.
- Device identifiers.
- Internal file paths.
- Private collaboration metadata.
- Unused personal information.

### Export Privacy Options

Where technically appropriate, users shall have options to control
whether certain metadata is included in exports.

### Shared Folder Privacy

ART shall clearly communicate that when users save `.art` files to:

- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Network folders.
- Other shared storage.

The privacy and security of those files are also affected by the
permissions and policies of the storage provider.

### Shared Folder Permissions

ART shall not falsely represent a shared folder as secure simply because
ART is using it.

Users shall be informed that:

> **Access to a shared ART file is ultimately governed by the
> permissions of the storage system containing that file.**

### File-Based Collaboration Privacy

File-based collaboration shall minimize unnecessary personal information
shared between users.

Change attribution shall provide enough information for users to
understand:

- Who made a change.
- What was changed.
- When it was changed.

It shall not expose unrelated personal information.

### @Mentions Privacy

ART shall support @mentions within appropriate collaboration scopes.

@mentions shall be limited to users who are appropriately visible within
the relevant:

- Shared report.
- Shared project.
- Shared organization folder.
- Organization.
- Collaboration environment.

ART shall not expose a user's profile information to unrelated users
merely because @mentions exist.

### Task Privacy

Tasks may contain sensitive information.

ART shall protect:

- Task names.
- Descriptions.
- Comments/Notes/Instructions.
- Assignees.
- Priorities.
- Due dates.
- Status.
- Reminders.
- @mentions\.

### Task Visibility

Task visibility shall respect:

- Report permissions.
- Project permissions.
- Organization permissions.
- User roles.
- Collaboration permissions.

### Progress Log Privacy

Progress Logs may contain sensitive testing information.

ART shall ensure that shared Progress Logs are only available to
appropriately authorized users.

### Comments/Notes/Instructions Privacy

ART shall treat the combined Task Comments/Notes/Instructions field as
user-generated content.

The field may contain:

- Personal information.
- Testing information.
- Internal business information.
- Accessibility findings.
- Instructions.
- References to other users.

ART shall not transmit or expose this content unnecessarily.

### Organization Privacy

ART shall protect organization information.

Organizations may contain:

- Organization names.
- Users.
- Roles.
- Projects.
- Reports.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Metrics.
- Permissions.
- Internal URLs.
- Internal testing information.

### Organization Data Ownership

ART shall clearly define how organizational data is owned and
controlled.

The system shall distinguish between:

- Individual user data.
- Organization-owned data.
- Shared project data.
- Shared report data.
- Personal Tasks.
- Shared Tasks.
- Organization Metrics.

### Organization Administrators

Organization administrators shall have clearly defined access to
organization data.

Administrator access shall not automatically provide unrestricted access
to unrelated personal data unless explicitly required and documented.

### User Departure

ART shall define what happens when a user:

- Leaves an organization.
- Is removed from an organization.
- Deactivates an account.
- Deletes an account.
- Loses access to an organization.

Organization-owned data shall remain available to the organization where
appropriate.

Personal information shall be handled according to ART's documented
privacy and retention policies.

### Account Deletion

Users shall have a clearly documented process for requesting account
deletion.

Where technically applicable, account deletion shall:

- Delete the user's account.
- Remove unnecessary personal information.
- Revoke authentication sessions.
- Revoke device connections.
- Revoke applicable tokens.
- Remove unnecessary profile information.
- Preserve organization-owned content where required.
- Preserve required audit information where legally or operationally
  necessary.

### Data Deletion

ART shall provide mechanisms to delete user-controlled data.

Deletion shall address:

- Reports.
- Projects.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Personal settings.
- Account information.
- Local application data.

### Deletion Confirmation

Destructive privacy actions shall provide accessible confirmation
workflows.

Users shall be clearly informed when deletion is:

- Immediate.
- Reversible.
- Irreversible.
- Subject to retention requirements.

### Data Export

Users shall be able to export their data where technically applicable.

Data export shall support, where appropriate:

- Reports.
- Projects.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- User settings.
- Profile information.
- Collaboration data.

### Data Portability

ART shall favor open or documented formats for user-owned data.

The `.art` format shall remain documented sufficiently to support
long-term data portability.

### Backup Privacy

ART shall document how backups are handled.

For server-hosted ART, backups shall:

- Be protected.
- Follow retention policies.
- Be encrypted where appropriate.
- Not remain indefinitely without justification.

### Backup Deletion

When user data is deleted, ART shall document when corresponding backup
copies are expected to expire or be permanently deleted.

### Server-Hosted Data

When ART is deployed as a SaaS service, ART shall clearly communicate:

- Where data is stored.
- What data is stored.
- Why it is stored.
- Who can access it.
- How long it is retained.
- How it is protected.
- How it is deleted.

### Self-Hosted ART

ART shall support organizations that choose to self-host.

Self-hosted organizations shall have greater control over:

- Data storage.
- Data retention.
- Backups.
- Access controls.
- Network configuration.
- Logging.
- Infrastructure.
- Data deletion.

### Self-Hosted Privacy Responsibilities

ART documentation shall clearly distinguish between:

- Privacy responsibilities of the ART software.
- Privacy responsibilities of the organization operating the ART server.
- Privacy responsibilities of hosting providers.
- Privacy responsibilities of third-party services.

### Third-Party Services

ART shall maintain a documented inventory of third-party services.

This shall include, where applicable:

- Authentication providers.
- Cloud storage providers.
- Jira.
- GitHub Issues.
- Azure DevOps.
- Google Workspace.
- Analytics services.
- Error-reporting services.
- Hosting providers.
- Email providers.
- Notification providers.

### Third-Party Data Sharing

ART shall clearly identify what information is transmitted to each
third-party service.

ART shall not transmit unrelated user information to a third party.

### OAuth Privacy

When using OAuth:

- ART shall request the minimum required scopes.
- ART shall not request unnecessary permissions.
- ART shall clearly identify the provider being used.
- ART shall explain what information is obtained.
- ART shall provide appropriate authentication and authorization
  controls.

### Integration Privacy

Each external integration shall document:

- Data transmitted.
- Data received.
- Authentication information.
- Required permissions.
- User controls.
- Data retention considerations.

### Google Workspace Privacy

If Google Workspace integration is implemented, ART shall clearly
communicate what Google data is accessed.

ART shall request only the scopes required for the selected
functionality.

### Microsoft Privacy

If Microsoft services are integrated, ART shall similarly minimize
requested permissions and data access.

### GitHub Privacy

If GitHub integration is implemented, ART shall only access
repositories, issues, or other GitHub resources necessary for the
selected ART functionality.

### Jira Privacy

If Jira integration is implemented, ART shall only access Jira data
necessary for the selected integration.

### Azure DevOps Privacy

If Azure DevOps integration is implemented, ART shall minimize
permissions and data access.

### Analytics and Telemetry

ART shall not implement analytics or telemetry merely because it is
convenient.

If analytics or telemetry is introduced, ART shall:

- Clearly document it.
- Minimize collected information.
- Avoid collecting report contents.
- Avoid collecting unnecessary personal information.
- Provide appropriate user controls.
- Provide an option to disable nonessential telemetry where practical.

### No Unnecessary Report Telemetry

ART shall not transmit report content, findings, testing notes, Tasks,
Progress Logs, or other user-created report information for analytics
purposes without explicit justification and appropriate user controls.

### Error Reporting

If ART uses automated error reporting:

- Error reports shall minimize personal information.
- Report contents shall not be included unnecessarily.
- File paths shall be sanitized where possible.
- User identifiers shall be minimized.
- Authentication tokens shall never be included.
- Sensitive information shall be filtered.

### Browser Storage Privacy

ART shall document its use of:

- Local Storage.
- IndexedDB.
- Cookies.
- Cache.
- Service Workers.
- Other browser storage mechanisms.

ART shall minimize sensitive information stored in browser-accessible
storage.

### Desktop Storage Privacy

The desktop application shall document where it stores:

- User settings.
- Reports.
- Cache data.
- Recovery data.
- Authentication information.
- Update information.
- Logs.

### Secure Credential Storage

Sensitive credentials shall not be stored in plain text.

Where available, ART shall use:

- Windows Credential Manager.
- macOS Keychain.
- Linux Secret Service or equivalent.
- Secure browser credential mechanisms.

### Logging Privacy

ART logs shall avoid unnecessary personal information.

Logs shall not contain:

- Passwords.
- OAuth secrets.
- Access tokens.
- Personal identity tokens.
- Authentication credentials.

### Log Retention

ART shall define appropriate retention periods for logs.

Logs shall not be retained indefinitely without a legitimate purpose.

### Audit Logs

Audit logs may contain information about:

- User actions.
- Changes.
- Authentication events.
- Administrative actions.
- Collaboration.
