- ART has a documented and repeatable process for determining whether a
  release is ready for production.

## Epic 60 — Advanced Collaboration & Synchronization

### Epic Overview

Implement and complete ART's advanced collaboration and synchronization
infrastructure so that multiple users can safely work with the same
projects, reports, Tasks, Progress Logs, and organization data using
either:

- File-based collaboration through shared folders and virtual/cloud
  storage.
- Server-based real-time collaboration when ART is connected to a
  server.
- A combination of local-first and server-based workflows.

The collaboration architecture shall support both **asynchronous** and
**near-real-time/synchronous** collaboration while preserving ART's
local-first design, accessibility, privacy, security, data integrity,
and existing functionality.

The implementation shall build upon the authenticated-user,
organization, role, authorization, identity, device-linking, `.art`
file, History Framework, Tasks, Progress Logs, and merge-conflict
functionality established by earlier epics.

### Core Collaboration Principle

ART shall allow users to collaborate without requiring a centralized
server whenever file-based collaboration is sufficient.

A server shall provide additional capabilities rather than being a
mandatory requirement for fundamental ART functionality.

The collaboration architecture shall therefore support:

1.  Local-only use.
2.  File-based asynchronous collaboration.
3.  File-based concurrent collaboration with conflict detection and
    resolution.
4.  Server-assisted synchronization.
5.  Server-based near-real-time collaboration where supported.

### Collaboration Architecture

Design collaboration as a layered architecture:

``` text
ART Application
    |
    +-- Local Data Layer
    |
    +-- .art File Layer
    |
    +-- File-Based Collaboration Layer
    |
    +-- Synchronization / Merge Layer
    |
    +-- Identity & Device Layer
    |
    +-- Authorization Layer
    |
    +-- Optional Server Collaboration Layer
    |
    +-- Optional Integration Layer
```

The architecture shall prevent server-dependent functionality from
unnecessarily coupling ART's fundamental local functionality to a
server.

### Local-First Compatibility

ART shall remain fully usable without a server.

Users shall be able to:

- Create reports.
- Edit reports.
- Save reports.
- Open reports.
- Import/export reports.
- Manage Tasks.
- Manage Progress Logs.
- Use the WCAG Lookup Tool.
- Use templates.
- Use accessibility settings.
- Use keyboard shortcuts.
- Use customizable working views.
- Use the History Framework.
- Perform other fundamental ART functions.

A server shall only be required for functionality that genuinely
requires centralized or real-time services.

### File-Based Collaboration

Implement collaboration through `.art` files stored in locations such
as:

- Local folders.
- Shared network folders.
- Google Drive.
- Microsoft OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Other supported synchronization/storage systems.

ART shall not require direct API access to these services merely to
support basic file-based collaboration.

### Shared Folder Model

Users shall be able to place ART projects/reports in a shared folder.

For example:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
    Project A/
        Report 1.art
        Report 2.art
    Project B/
        Report 3.art
    Tasks/
    Progress Logs/
```

ART shall treat the shared file system as the collaboration medium.

### File-Based Collaboration Without a Server

Users shall be able to collaborate without an ART server.

Example workflow:

1.  User A creates a report.
2.  User A saves the `.art` file in a shared folder.
3.  User B opens the `.art` file.
4.  User B modifies the report.
5.  User B saves the file.
6.  User A opens or refreshes the report.
7.  ART detects that the external version has changed.
8.  ART incorporates User B's non-conflicting changes.
9.  If conflicts exist, ART presents the Merge Changes interface.
10. The user resolves the conflicts.
11. The resolved report is saved.
12. Other collaborators can subsequently see the merged result.

### Asynchronous Collaboration

ART shall support asynchronous collaboration in which users do not need
to be online simultaneously.

Users shall be able to:

- Work independently.
- Save changes.
- Close ART.
- Return later.
- Open updated files.
- Detect changes made by other users.
- Merge changes.
- Continue working.

### Concurrent Collaboration

ART shall support situations where two or more users have the same
`.art` file open simultaneously.

The system shall detect when the underlying file has changed since the
user's working copy was loaded or last synchronized.

### External Change Detection

ART shall detect relevant changes when:

- Opening a file.
- Refreshing a report.
- Saving a report.
- Returning to an active report.
- Synchronizing the file.
- Receiving a file-system change notification where supported.

### Change Detection

ART shall maintain sufficient metadata to determine:

- Which version was originally opened.
- Which version the user last synchronized.
- Which changes were made locally.
- Which changes originated from another user.
- Which changes have already been merged.
- Whether a conflict exists.

### Collaboration Metadata

Where appropriate, collaboration metadata shall include:

- User identifier.
- Display name.
- Timestamp.
- Device identifier.
- Change identifier.
- Parent version.
- Revision/version identifier.
- Change type.
- Object affected.

Sensitive information shall not be unnecessarily embedded in `.art`
files.

### Change Attribution

Changes shall be attributable to the appropriate ART user when identity
information is available.

Examples include:

- User A added a finding.
- User B modified a Task.
- User A changed a Progress Log entry.
- User B changed a report field.

### Identity Integration

Use the user identity infrastructure established by earlier epics.

Collaboration shall integrate with:

- User name.
- Email address.
- Display name.
- Job title.
- Role.
- Organization membership.
- User identifier.
- Device identity.

### Device Integration

A user's multiple ART installations shall be capable of being recognized
as belonging to the same user when the user has established the
appropriate identity/device relationship.

This shall work with:

- Web ART.
- Desktop ART.
- Multiple computers.
- Multiple supported browsers.
- Multiple ART installations.

### Device Identity Security

Device-linking information shall not expose sensitive credentials.

Do not place:

- Passwords.
- OAuth client secrets.
- Authentication secrets.
- Server credentials.

inside `.art` files.

### Versioning

ART shall maintain sufficient version information to determine
relationships between document versions.

Each saved collaborative state should have a unique version/revision
identifier.

### Revision History

Where appropriate, ART shall maintain a history of collaborative
revisions.

Revision information may include:

- Revision ID.
- User.
- Timestamp.
- Parent revision.
- Summary of changes.

### History Framework Integration

Collaboration shall integrate with ART's existing History Framework.

Appropriate collaborative actions shall be represented as reversible
operations where technically and logically appropriate.

### Undo/Redo

Users shall be able to use ART's existing:

- Undo keyboard shortcut.
- Redo keyboard shortcut.
- Undo menu command.
- Redo menu command.

for applicable collaboration-related actions.

### Merge Architecture

Implement merge functionality as a reusable service rather than
embedding merge logic separately into each feature.

The merge system shall be capable of processing changes to:

- Reports.
- Findings.
- WCAG Success Criteria.
- Accessibility Standards.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Project information.
- Templates where applicable.
- Other structured ART data.

### Object-Level Merging

Where practical, merge changes at the smallest meaningful data level.

For example, if:

- User A modifies Finding 1.
- User B modifies Finding 2.

ART should preserve both changes rather than treating the entire report
as conflicted.

### Field-Level Merging

Where practical, identify conflicts at the field level.

For example:

``` text
Finding 12
    Description
        User A: modified
        User B: unchanged

    Recommendation
        User A: unchanged
        User B: modified
```

Both changes should be preserved automatically where no conflict exists.

### Conflict Definition

A merge conflict shall occur when two users make incompatible changes to
the same logical data.

Examples include:

- Both users modify the same field differently.
- One user deletes an object while another modifies it.
- Two users perform incompatible structural changes.
- Two users change a Task's status differently.
- Two users modify the same Progress Log entry.

### Conflict Detection

Conflict detection shall:

- Detect conflicting changes reliably.
- Preserve both versions until resolution.
- Avoid silent data loss.
- Identify affected objects.
- Identify users where possible.
- Identify the conflicting values.
- Identify relevant timestamps/version information.

### Merge Changes Modal

When a conflict requires user intervention, ART shall automatically open
the existing Merge Changes modal where appropriate.

The modal shall:

- Clearly identify that a conflict exists.
- Identify the affected item.
- Identify the users involved.
- Identify the local change.
- Identify the incoming change.
- Provide available resolution choices.
- Preserve non-conflicting changes.
- Provide accessible status information.

### Merge Resolution Choices

Where technically appropriate, provide options such as:

- Keep my change.
- Keep incoming change.
- Keep both.
- Edit/resolve manually.
- Skip this conflict.
- Cancel merge.

The available options shall depend on the data type and conflict.

### Merge Conflict Accessibility

The Merge Changes interface shall be fully accessible.

Verify:

- Keyboard-only operation.
- Logical focus order.
- Focus placement when the modal opens.
- Focus trapping.
- Accessible modal name.
- Accessible headings.
- Accessible descriptions.
- Meaningful control names.
- Screen-reader announcements.
- Live status messages.
- Accessible comparison of changes.

### Screen Reader Conflict Information

Assistive Technology users shall be able to determine:

- What changed.
- Who changed it.
- What the current value is.
- What the incoming value is.
- Which option is selected.
- What will happen when the resolution is activated.

### Non-Conflicting Changes

ART shall automatically preserve non-conflicting changes whenever
possible.

Users should not be required to manually resolve changes that can safely
be merged.

### Conflict Resolution Safety

Before applying a merge, ART shall preserve sufficient information to
recover from an incorrect resolution.

Where appropriate:

- Create a recoverable history entry.
- Support Undo.
- Preserve the previous revision.
- Prevent accidental destruction of unrelated changes.

### Merge Validation

After a merge is completed, ART shall validate:

- Data structure.
- Required fields.
- Relationships.
- References.
- Permissions.
- Task relationships.
- Progress Log relationships.
- Report integrity.

### Failed Merge Recovery

If a merge fails, ART shall:

- Preserve the user's original data.
- Preserve the incoming data.
- Explain the failure.
- Avoid silently discarding changes.
- Provide an appropriate recovery mechanism.

### File Save Safety

ART shall use safe save behavior for collaborative `.art` files.

Where technically feasible:

1.  Write to a temporary file.
2.  Validate the resulting file.
3.  Replace the previous version atomically.
4.  Preserve a recovery copy where appropriate.

### Simultaneous Save Protection

ART shall detect situations in which the underlying file has changed
since the current user loaded or synchronized it.

ART shall not silently overwrite another user's newer changes.

### Stale Version Detection

If User A attempts to save a version based on an outdated file, ART
shall:

- Detect the stale version.
- Preserve the current external version.
- Preserve User A's local changes.
- Initiate synchronization/merge processing.
- Prevent silent data loss.

### File Synchronization Delays

Account for cloud-storage synchronization delays.

ART shall not assume that a file-system timestamp changing necessarily
means the final synchronized file is immediately available.

Where appropriate, ART shall:

- Retry reading the file.
- Verify file integrity.
- Detect incomplete files.
- Delay merge processing until a valid version is available.

### File Locking

Where file locking is available through the operating system or storage
provider, ART may use it as an optimization.

File locking shall not be the sole mechanism for preventing data loss
because many cloud synchronization systems do not provide reliable
application-level locking.

### Collaboration Status

ART shall provide accessible status information indicating states such
as:

- Local changes.
- Saved locally.
- Saving.
- Synchronizing.
- External changes detected.
- Merge required.
- Merge in progress.
- Merge completed.
- Synchronization failed.
- File unavailable.

### Live Status Messages

Dynamic collaboration status shall be communicated through accessible
live regions/status messaging where appropriate.

Messages shall not unnecessarily interrupt users.

### Collaboration Notifications

Users may receive notifications when:

- Another user changes a shared report.
- A merge is required.
- A Task is assigned.
- A user is mentioned.
- A shared Progress Log changes.
- A synchronization problem occurs.

Notification behavior shall respect user settings and accessibility
preferences.

### @Mentions Integration

Integrate @mentions into the collaboration infrastructure.

@mentions shall work within:

- Shared reports.
- Shared projects.
- Shared organization folders.
- Shared Tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Other supported collaborative content.

### @Mention Identity Resolution

ART shall resolve @mentions against the appropriate user identity.

Where an organization context exists, the available users should be
limited to users the current user is authorized to reference.

### @Mention Notifications

Where supported, an @mention may generate a notification for the
mentioned user.

The notification shall:

- Identify the user who mentioned them.
- Identify the relevant report/project/task/progress log.
- Provide an appropriate navigation target.
- Respect notification settings.

### @Mention File-Based Collaboration

@mentions shall continue to function in file-based collaboration even
when no ART server is available.

When notification delivery requires a server, ART may defer notification
functionality while preserving the underlying mention information.

### File-Based Mention Resolution

For file-based collaboration, ART shall preserve enough information to
recognize mentions between users who share the same project, report, or
organization context.

### Shared Projects

Implement collaboration at the project level where supported.

Users shall be able to share projects through:

- Shared folders.
- Server-based collaboration.

### Shared Project Structure

Project collaboration shall preserve:

- Project metadata.
- Reports.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- User information.
- Relevant collaboration metadata.

### Shared Organization Folders

Where configured, an organization may designate a shared parent folder.

Example:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
```

Subfolders may contain:

``` text
Acme Co A11y Audits/
    Client A/
    Client B/
    Internal Audits/
    Projects/
    Reports/
    Progress Logs/
    Tasks/
```

### Permission Inheritance

Where the underlying storage system supports inherited permissions, ART
shall respect those permissions.

ART shall not attempt to bypass the permissions established by the
storage provider.

### Organization Folder Discovery

Where supported, ART may allow users to designate an organization folder
as an ART collaboration location.

ART shall not assume that every folder is an organization folder.

### Organization Metrics Integration

Organization Metrics may use the contents of an authorized shared
organization folder as a data source.

Metrics shall only include data the user is authorized to access.

### Metrics Synchronization

When reports are added, modified, removed, or moved within a shared
organization folder, metrics should update when ART next evaluates the
available data.

### Shared Tasks

Tasks stored in shared collaborative locations shall support:

- Assignment.
- Status.
- Priority.
- Due dates.
- Reminders where supported.
- Comments/Notes/Instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Completion.
- Reopening.
- Collaboration.
- Merge processing.

### Shared Progress Logs

Shared Progress Logs shall support:

- Multiple contributors.
- Change attribution.
- File-based synchronization.
- Server synchronization where available.
- Merge conflict detection.
- Accessible conflict resolution.

### Server-Based Collaboration

When ART is connected to an ART collaboration server, provide additional
synchronization capabilities.

Server-based collaboration may provide:

- Centralized synchronization.
- Real-time or near-real-time updates.
- User presence.
- Notifications.
- Centralized organization data.
- Server-side conflict coordination.
- Centralized permissions.
- Shared project management.

### Server Independence

Server-based collaboration shall not replace or unnecessarily duplicate
the local-first data model.

The application should remain resilient when temporarily disconnected.

### Offline Server Collaboration

If the user loses server connectivity, ART shall:

- Continue allowing supported local work.
- Preserve local changes.
- Indicate offline state.
- Synchronize when connectivity returns.
- Detect conflicts created during the offline period.

### Reconnection

When server connectivity returns, ART shall:

1.  Authenticate the user.
2.  Verify authorization.
3.  Determine the current server revision.
4.  Compare local changes.
5.  Synchronize non-conflicting changes.
6.  Identify conflicts.
7.  Present the Merge Changes interface where necessary.

### Real-Time Collaboration

If supported by the server architecture, ART may provide near-real-time
updates.

Real-time collaboration shall not compromise:

- Accessibility.
- Performance.
- Privacy.
- Security.
- Data integrity.

### Real-Time Change Notifications

When another user changes a collaborative resource, ART may notify the
current user without requiring a manual refresh.

Users shall be able to understand:

- Who made the change.
- What changed.
- Whether their current work is affected.

### Real-Time Conflict Handling

If a user is actively editing a resource that another user changes, ART
shall not unexpectedly overwrite the user's local work.

The system shall preserve local edits and determine whether the changes
can be automatically merged.

### Collaboration Presence

If user presence is implemented, it shall be optional and accessible.

Users may be shown:

- Who is viewing a report.
- Who is editing a report.
- Who recently changed the report.

Presence information shall not reveal unnecessary personal information.

### Collaboration Privacy

Collaboration shall follow the privacy requirements established by Epic
58.

ART shall minimize the information shared between collaborators.

### Sensitive Information

Collaboration metadata shall not unnecessarily expose:

- Personal information.
- Authentication information.
- Private organizational information.
- Server credentials.
- OAuth secrets.

### Authorization Integration

Every server-based collaboration operation shall respect ART's
authorization system.

Users shall only be able to:

- View authorized resources.
- Modify authorized resources.
- Share authorized resources.
- Assign authorized Tasks.
- View authorized Progress Logs.
- Resolve authorized merge conflicts.

### File-Based Authorization

For file-based collaboration, ART shall respect the permissions imposed
by the storage system.

ART shall not attempt to circumvent operating-system, network, or
cloud-storage permissions.

### Security Validation

Collaboration shall protect against:

- Unauthorized modification.
- Malicious `.art` files.
- Tampered collaboration metadata.
- Forged user identity information.
- Replay of invalid revisions.
- Corrupted synchronization data.
- Unauthorized server requests.

### File Trust

ART shall not automatically trust user identity information contained in
an `.art` file as proof of server authorization.

Identity metadata inside files shall be treated as collaboration
attribution information unless cryptographically verified through an
appropriate trust mechanism.

### Cryptographic Integrity

Where appropriate, ART may use cryptographic hashes or signatures to
verify:

- File integrity.
- Revision relationships.
- Change packages.
- Server responses.

Cryptographic mechanisms shall not expose private credentials.

### Collaboration Audit Trail

Where appropriate, ART shall preserve an audit trail of significant
collaborative actions.

Examples include:

- User created report.
- User modified finding.
- User assigned Task.
- User completed Task.
- User modified Progress Log.
- User resolved merge conflict.

### Audit Trail Accessibility

Collaborative history and audit information shall be accessible to
keyboard and screen-reader users.

### Collaboration Performance

Collaboration shall remain responsive with:

- Small reports.
- Large reports.
- Large projects.
- Many Tasks.
- Large Progress Logs.
- Many collaborators.
- Large shared folders.

### Large Shared Folder Handling

ART shall avoid unnecessarily loading every file in a large shared
folder into memory.

Where possible, use:

- Incremental discovery.
- Lazy loading.
- Caching.
- Background processing.

### Synchronization Efficiency

ART shall avoid repeatedly transferring or processing unchanged data.

Where appropriate, synchronization should use:

- Revision identifiers.
- Change sets.
- Hashes.
- Incremental updates.

### Conflict Scalability

The merge system shall remain usable when a large number of conflicts
exist.

Provide appropriate:

- Grouping.
- Filtering.
- Navigation.
- Conflict counts.
- Resolution progress.

### Merge Progress

When a merge involves substantial data, provide accessible progress
information.

### Cancellation

Where technically safe, long-running synchronization or merge operations
should support cancellation.

Cancellation shall leave the user's data in a recoverable state.

### Error Handling

Collaboration errors shall provide actionable information.

Examples:

- Shared file unavailable.
- Permission denied.
- File changed externally.
- File corrupted.
- Synchronization delayed.
- Merge required.
- Server unavailable.
- Authentication expired.
- Authorization denied.

### Error Recovery

Users shall be able to recover from collaboration failures without
losing local work.

### Collaboration Logging

Technical collaboration errors may be logged for diagnostics, but logs
shall not contain unnecessary sensitive information.

### Import/Export Compatibility

Collaboration metadata shall not interfere with standard report
import/export functionality.

Exported reports intended for distribution shall not unnecessarily
expose internal collaboration metadata.

### Report Distribution

Provide a distinction between:

- Collaborative working files.
- Final/distributed reports.

Users shall not accidentally expose internal collaboration information
simply by exporting a report.

### Version Migration

When `.art` file formats change, ART shall migrate collaborative files
safely.

Migration shall preserve:

- Report content.
- Collaboration metadata where supported.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- User attribution.
- Version relationships where possible.

### Backward Compatibility

Where supported, newer ART versions shall safely identify older `.art`
files.

If a file cannot safely be opened or migrated, ART shall explain why and
avoid destructive conversion.

### Collaboration Recovery Files

Where appropriate, ART may maintain temporary recovery versions during:

- Synchronization.
- Merge operations.
- Large saves.
- Conflict resolution.

Recovery files shall not unnecessarily expose sensitive information.

### Testing Requirements

Test collaboration using at least:

- One user.
- Two users.
- Multiple users.
- Multiple devices.
- Web ART.
- Desktop ART.
- Shared folders.
- Network folders.
- Cloud-synchronized folders.
- Server-based collaboration.

### File-Based Test Scenarios

Test:

- User A saves.
- User B opens.
- User B changes.
- User B saves.
- User A opens.
- User A sees User B's changes.

### Concurrent Test Scenarios

Test:

- User A and User B open the same report.
- User A changes one field.
- User B changes another field.
- Both save.
- Both changes are preserved.

### Conflict Test Scenarios

Test:

- Both users modify the same field.
- One user deletes an item while another edits it.
- Both change Task status.
- Both change Progress Log content.
- Multiple conflicts occur simultaneously.

### Merge Test Scenarios

Verify:

- Automatic non-conflicting merge.
- Manual conflict resolution.
- Keep local.
- Keep incoming.
- Keep both.
- Cancel.
- Undo.
- Redo.
- Reopen after merge.

### Cloud Storage Testing

Test file-based collaboration using:

- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.

Where actual provider behavior varies, document provider-specific
limitations.

### Server Testing

Test:

- Online.
- Offline.
- Reconnection.
- Multiple concurrent users.
- Server errors.
- Authentication expiration.
- Authorization changes.
- Synchronization delays.

### Identity Testing

Verify:

- Correct user attribution.
- Multiple devices for one user.
- Multiple users on one device where supported.
- Identity changes.
- Organization membership changes.

### @Mention Testing

Test:

- Mentions in shared reports.
- Mentions in Tasks.
- Mentions in Progress Logs.
- File-based mentions.
- Server-based mentions.
- Invalid mentions.
- Removed users.
- Cross-device mentions.
- Notification behavior.

### Accessibility Testing

Collaboration functionality shall be tested with:

- Keyboard-only operation.
- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- ChromeVox.
- TalkBack.
- Braille displays.
- Low-vision settings.

### Regression Testing

Collaboration changes shall not regress:

- Local report editing.
- Report saving.
- Import/export.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- History.
- Undo/Redo.
- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- Organizations.
- Metrics.
- Accessibility.

### Automated Testing

Create automated tests for:

- Version comparison.
- Change detection.
- Merge logic.
- Conflict detection.
- Conflict resolution.
- Revision handling.
- File integrity.
- Synchronization.
- Authorization.
- Identity attribution.

### End-to-End Testing

Create end-to-end tests representing realistic collaboration workflows.

### Data Integrity Testing

After every synchronization/merge operation, verify:

- No data loss.
- No duplicate records unless intended.
- No broken relationships.
- No invalid references.
- No corrupted report structure.

### Security Testing

Test malicious or unexpected collaboration input, including:

- Modified revision metadata.
- Invalid user identifiers.
- Tampered files.
- Invalid change sets.
- Unauthorized server requests.
- Malicious file content.

### Performance Testing

Measure:

- File load time.
- Save time.
- Merge time.
- Synchronization time.
- Memory usage.
- CPU usage.

Test increasingly large datasets.

### Documentation

Document:

- Collaboration architecture.
- File format/versioning.
- Merge strategy.
- Conflict resolution.
- Identity attribution.
- File-based collaboration.
- Server collaboration.
- Offline behavior.
- Recovery behavior.
- Security considerations.
- Privacy considerations.
- Known storage-provider limitations.

### User Documentation

Help documentation shall explain:

- How file-based collaboration works.
- How to use shared folders.
- How to resolve conflicts.
- How server collaboration differs.
- What happens when another user changes a report.
- How synchronization works.
- How @mentions work.
- How identity is associated with changes.
- How to recover from synchronization problems.

### Definition of Done

Epic 60 shall be considered complete when:

- ART has a documented collaboration architecture.
- Local-first operation remains intact.
- File-based collaboration is implemented.
- Asynchronous collaboration is implemented.
- Concurrent collaboration is implemented.
- External change detection is implemented.
- Version tracking is implemented.
- Revision tracking is implemented.
- Change attribution is implemented.
- User identity integration is implemented.
- Device identity integration is implemented.
- Object-level merging is implemented where practical.
- Field-level merging is implemented where practical.
- Conflict detection is implemented.
- Conflict resolution is implemented.
- The existing Merge Changes modal is integrated.
- Non-conflicting changes merge automatically where safe.
- Conflicting changes are presented for user resolution.
- Merge operations are recoverable.
- Merge operations integrate with the History Framework.
- Undo/Redo works for applicable collaboration operations.
- Safe file saving is implemented.
- Stale-version detection is implemented.
- Cloud synchronization delays are handled safely.
- File locking is treated as an optimization rather than the sole
  protection mechanism.
- Accessible collaboration status messages are implemented.
- Accessible collaboration notifications are implemented.
- @mentions are integrated into collaboration.
- File-based @mentions are supported.
- Server-based @mentions are supported where applicable.
- Shared projects are supported.
- Shared Tasks are supported.
- Shared Progress Logs are supported.
- Shared organization folders are supported where applicable.
- Organization Metrics can use authorized shared-folder data where
  applicable.
- Server-based synchronization is implemented where server
  infrastructure exists.
- Offline server collaboration is supported.
- Reconnection/synchronization is supported.
- Real-time or near-real-time collaboration is supported where the
  server architecture provides it.
- Authorization is enforced for server-based collaboration.
- File-system permissions are respected for file-based collaboration.
- Collaboration metadata does not expose sensitive credentials.
- Collaboration does not compromise privacy.
- Collaboration does not compromise accessibility.
- Collaboration does not compromise data integrity.
- Collaboration does not silently overwrite another user's work.
- Collaboration errors are recoverable.
- Large collaborative datasets are handled efficiently.
- Automated collaboration tests exist.
- Merge/conflict tests exist.
- Accessibility testing exists.
- Security testing exists.
- Performance testing exists.
- End-to-end collaboration testing exists.
- Documentation exists for both users and developers.
- Web and desktop applications support the same collaboration model to
  the extent technically appropriate.
- Existing ART functionality remains intact and regression testing
  passes.

## Epic 61 — Web/Desktop Feature Parity & Native Desktop Application

### Epic Overview

Implement ART as a fully supported desktop application while maintaining
complete functional, accessibility, usability, security, privacy, and
user-experience parity with the web application.

The desktop application shall provide the same core ART experience as
the web application while taking advantage of capabilities available in
a native desktop environment.

The desktop application shall not be a reduced, simplified, or
feature-limited version of ART.

The goal is:

> **The desktop application shall provide all functionality available in
> the web application, plus additional conveniences and capabilities
> made possible by the desktop environment.**

### Desktop Application Technology

Use **Electron** as the preferred desktop application framework unless
technical evaluation demonstrates that another framework provides
substantially better accessibility, security, performance,
maintainability, or cross-platform support.

The implementation shall reuse as much of ART's existing web application
code as practical.

Where possible:

- Share application logic.
- Share UI components.
- Share accessibility implementations.
- Share data models.
- Share business logic.
- Share validation.
- Share keyboard shortcut infrastructure.
- Share History Framework functionality.
- Share collaboration functionality.
- Share import/export functionality.
- Share report-generation functionality.

Avoid maintaining separate implementations of the same functionality
unless platform-specific behavior requires it.

### Web/Desktop Architecture

Design ART so that the web and desktop applications use a common
application core.

``` text
                    ART Core
                       |
          +------------+------------+
          |                         |
     Web Application          Desktop Application
          |                         |
     Browser APIs              Native APIs
          |                         |
          +------------+------------+
                       |
              Shared ART Features
```

### Functional Parity

The desktop application shall provide all functionality available in the
web application, including:

- Dashboard.
- Projects.
- Reports.
- Report Builder.
- Report Viewer.
- Audit Logs.
- Executive Summary reports.
- Usability Reports.
- WCAG Lookup Tool.
- Accessibility Standards Lookup.
- Templates.
- Findings.
- Tasks.
- Shared Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Organization Metrics.
- Organizations.
- Collaboration.
- File-based collaboration.
- Server-based collaboration.
- Merge Changes.
- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- User profiles.
- Device identity.
- Import/export.
- `.art` files.
- History.
- Undo/Redo.
- Settings.
- Accessibility settings.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts.
- Customizable working views.
- Context menus.
- Menu bar.
- Search.
- Notifications.
- Reminders.
- @mentions\.
- Report management.
- Report tracking.
- Report generation.
- Report output.
- All other functionality implemented in ART.

### No Feature Regression

Creating the desktop application shall not remove, weaken, or simplify
existing web functionality.

Do not intentionally create:

- Desktop-only reduced feature sets.
- Desktop-only simplified workflows.
- Desktop-only accessibility compromises.
- Desktop-only navigation differences that make equivalent workflows
  harder.
- Desktop-only limitations on report types.
- Desktop-only limitations on collaboration.

### User Experience Parity

Equivalent functionality shall have a consistent user experience between
web and desktop versions.

Where platform conventions require differences, those differences shall:

- Be intentional.
- Be documented.
- Improve usability.
- Preserve accessibility.
- Not remove functionality.

### Navigation Parity

Maintain equivalent application navigation between:

- Web ART.
- Desktop ART.

The desktop application may additionally use:

- Native application menus.
- Native keyboard commands.
- Native window controls.
- Multiple windows where appropriate.
- Native dialogs where appropriate.

### Dashboard

The desktop application shall provide the same dashboard functionality
as the web application.

The dashboard shall preserve:

- Project access.
- Report access.
- Task access.
- Progress information.
- Organization information.
- Search.
- Customizable views.
- Accessibility settings.
- User preferences.

### Application Panes

Desktop ART shall support the same application panes/navigation
structures as the web application.

Where desktop window size permits, additional pane-management
capabilities may be provided.

### Customizable Working Views

Preserve customizable working views across platforms.

Users shall be able to configure:

- Visible panes.
- Panel arrangement.
- Sidebar visibility.
- Task views.
- Report views.
- Dashboard views.
- Other supported workspace/view settings.

Where appropriate, preferences should persist between sessions.

### Keyboard Shortcuts

The desktop application shall support all ART keyboard shortcuts.

This includes:

- Existing shortcuts.
- User-defined shortcuts.
- Customizable shortcut mappings.
- Context-sensitive shortcuts.
- Menu-command shortcuts.

### User-Defined Keyboard Shortcuts

Users shall be able to customize keyboard shortcuts in the same manner
as the web application.

Shortcut customization shall:

- Remain accessible.
- Detect conflicts.
- Clearly identify conflicting commands.
- Allow users to restore defaults.
- Persist between sessions.
- Avoid breaking essential application functionality.

### Native Keyboard Shortcuts

Where appropriate, desktop ART may additionally support
platform-standard keyboard commands.

Do not allow native operating-system shortcuts to unintentionally
override critical ART accessibility shortcuts.

### Menu Bar

Provide a standard desktop menu bar.

At minimum, where applicable, provide:

- File.
- Edit.
- View.
- Tasks.
- Project.
- Report.
- Tools.
- Help.

Menu structure shall remain logically consistent with the web
application's command structure.

### Menu Accessibility

The menu bar shall be fully accessible using:

- Keyboard.
- Screen readers.
- Switch devices where applicable.
- Other supported assistive technologies.

### Context Menus

Preserve ART's context-menu architecture.

Context menus shall provide appropriate commands for:

- Reports.
- Findings.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- Projects.
- Collaboration.
- Files.
- Other applicable objects.

### Global Commands

Common commands shall be available consistently through:

- Context menus.
- Menu bar.
- Keyboard shortcuts.

Where appropriate, actions may remain hidden from the primary interface
to reduce visual clutter while remaining discoverable through these
command mechanisms.

### Desktop File Integration

Desktop ART shall provide enhanced file-system integration.

Users shall be able to:

- Open `.art` files.
- Save `.art` files.
- Save As.
- Import files.
- Export reports.
- Open files from the operating system.
- Use standard file-selection dialogs.
- Drag and drop supported files where accessible.
- Associate `.art` files with ART where supported.

### `.art` File Association

The desktop installer shall optionally associate `.art` files with ART.

When a user activates an `.art` file through the operating system,
desktop ART should automatically open the file.

### Standard File Dialogs

Use accessible operating-system file dialogs where practical.

Users shall be able to:

- Browse folders.
- Select files.
- Create folders where supported.
- Save files.
- Rename files where supported.

### Drag and Drop

Where supported, allow users to drag `.art` files into the application.

Drag-and-drop functionality shall never be the only method available.

### Desktop Notifications

Where appropriate, ART may use native desktop notifications for:

- Task reminders.
- @mentions\.
- Collaboration updates.
- Merge conflicts.
- Synchronization events.
- Other user-requested notifications.

All notifications shall remain accessible.

### Notification Preferences

Users shall be able to configure notification behavior.

Settings may include:

- Enable/disable desktop notifications.
- Enable/disable auditory notifications.
- Enable/disable visual notifications.
- Notification categories.
- Reminder behavior.

### Task Reminders

Desktop ART shall support the same task reminder functionality as the
web application.

When a reminder is due, the application may use:

- Native notification.
- Accessible modal.
- Visual alert.
- Auditory alert.

The user shall be able to configure the available alert methods.

### Reminder Modal

The reminder modal shall remain accessible.

It shall support:

- Keyboard operation.
- Screen readers.
- Focus management.
- Snooze.
- Dismiss.
- Open task.
- Appropriate task navigation.

### Auditory Alerts

Where supported, desktop ART may provide configurable sounds for:

- Task reminders.
- Successful saves.
- Synchronization completion.
- Merge conflicts.
- Errors.
- Other task actions.

Sounds shall always be optional.

### Custom Task Sounds

If custom sound effects are supported, users shall be able to:

- Enable/disable them.
- Select available sounds.
- Restore defaults.

Custom sounds shall not interfere with assistive technology speech.

### Native Window Management

Desktop ART shall support standard operating-system window behavior,
including where applicable:

- Minimize.
- Maximize.
- Restore.
- Resize.
- Move.
- Close.
- Full screen.

### Multiple Windows

Evaluate support for multiple ART windows where it provides meaningful
value.

Potential uses include:

- Comparing reports.
- Viewing a report while editing another.
- Viewing Tasks while working on a report.
- Viewing Progress Logs alongside reports.

Multiple-window functionality shall not create accessibility or
data-integrity problems.

### Multi-Monitor Support

Where technically practical, desktop ART should support multi-monitor
workflows.

Users may be able to:

- Place ART windows on different monitors.
- Open additional ART windows.
- Maintain useful window positions.

### Window State Persistence

Where appropriate, persist:

- Window size.
- Window position.
- Pane configuration.
- View configuration.

Avoid restoring windows to invalid displays or inaccessible positions.

### Clipboard Integration

Desktop ART shall provide appropriate operating-system clipboard
integration.

Support:

- Copy.
- Cut.
- Paste.
- Copy report information.
- Copy findings.
- Copy Tasks.
- Copy relevant text.

Clipboard operations shall preserve accessibility and data integrity.

### Native Printing

Where applicable, desktop ART may support native printing functionality.

Printing shall not replace report export functionality.

### Offline Functionality

Desktop ART shall preserve ART's local-first capabilities when
disconnected from the Internet.

Users shall be able to continue supported local work without server
connectivity.

### Offline Collaboration

Desktop ART shall support Epic 60's file-based collaboration
architecture.

Users shall be able to collaborate through `.art` files stored in:

- Local folders.
- Network folders.
- Shared folders.
- Cloud-synchronized folders.

### Server Collaboration

When configured for server-based collaboration, desktop ART shall
support the same collaboration functionality as the web application.

### Synchronization

Desktop ART shall support:

- Synchronization.
- External file change detection.
- Revision tracking.
- Merge processing.
- Conflict detection.
- Conflict resolution.
- Offline changes.
- Reconnection.

### Merge Changes

The desktop application shall use the same Merge Changes architecture
established by Epic 60.

Do not create a separate desktop-only merge implementation unless
technically necessary.

### Merge Conflict Notifications

Where appropriate, desktop ART may provide a native notification
indicating that a merge conflict requires attention.

Activating the notification shall open the appropriate accessible Merge
Changes interface.

### Authentication

Desktop ART shall support the authentication architecture established in
Epic 48 and subsequent identity/authorization epics.

Support, where applicable:

- Passwordless authentication.
- OAuth.
- Google.
- Microsoft.
- Amazon.
- GitHub.
- Account recovery.
- Device linking.

### Local-Only Use

Users shall be able to use desktop ART without logging in for
fundamental functionality.

Login shall remain required only for functionality that requires
authenticated identity or server-based services.

### Authorization

Desktop ART shall enforce the same authorization rules as the web
application when accessing server-based resources.

### User Profile

Desktop ART shall provide access to the same user profile information as
web ART.

Where applicable:

- Name.
- Email.
- Display name.
- Job title.
- Role.
- Organization membership.
- Device information.

### Device Identity

Desktop ART shall integrate with the multi-device identity model.

Users shall be able to associate desktop installations with their ART
identity where supported.

### Secure Local Storage

Sensitive authentication information shall not be stored in plain text.

Use appropriate operating-system secure credential storage where
available.

Examples include:

- Windows Credential Manager.
- macOS Keychain.
- Linux Secret Service or equivalent.

### OAuth Security

OAuth credentials/tokens shall be stored using secure mechanisms.

Do not expose:

- Client secrets.
- Access tokens.
- Refresh tokens.

through normal application storage or `.art` files.

### Desktop Security

The desktop application shall follow secure
Electron/application-development practices.

Where applicable:

- Disable unnecessary Node.js integration.
- Use context isolation.
- Use secure preload scripts.
- Validate IPC communication.
- Restrict navigation.
- Prevent unauthorized remote code execution.
- Avoid loading untrusted remote content with elevated privileges.
- Keep dependencies updated.

### Content Security

Implement an appropriate Content Security Policy where applicable.

### Dependency Security

Monitor desktop dependencies for:

- Known vulnerabilities.
- Unsupported versions.
- Deprecated components.

### Automatic Updates

Provide an accessible **Check for Updates** command in the Help menu.

### Update Workflow

The preferred user experience shall be:

1.  User selects **Help → Check for Updates**.

2.  ART determines whether an update is available.

3.  If no update is available, ART provides an accessible status
    message.

4.  If an update is available, ART presents an accessible update dialog.

5.  The user chooses:

    - **Update Now**
    - **Cancel**

6.  If Update Now is selected, ART downloads/applies the update.

7.  ART restarts when necessary.

8.  The updated application opens normally.

### Update Accessibility

The update process shall support:

- Keyboard operation.
- Screen readers.
- Focus management.
- Accessible status messages.
- Progress information.
- Error recovery.

### Automatic Update Architecture

Design the release process so that the same source-code release can
produce both:

- Web application updates.
- Desktop application updates.

### GitHub-Based Release Pipeline

Where technically practical, pushing a release to the GitHub repository
should automatically trigger the appropriate build/deployment pipeline.

The pipeline should be capable of:

1.  Building the web application.
2.  Deploying the web application.
3.  Building the desktop application.
4.  Packaging desktop installers.
5.  Publishing desktop update artifacts.
6.  Updating the desktop application's update metadata.

### Single Source of Truth

Web and desktop applications should be built from the same
version-controlled source whenever practical.

Avoid maintaining separate feature branches or duplicated
implementations solely for web and desktop.

### Version Synchronization

Web and desktop versions shall use a consistent versioning strategy.

A release should identify:

- ART version.
- Build version where applicable.
- Release date.
- Relevant release notes.

### Release Notes

Desktop ART shall provide accessible release notes for updates.

### Installer

Create standard operating-system installers.

The Windows release shall provide a standard installer package that
users can download from the ART website.

### Website Download

The ART website shall provide an accessible link to download the desktop
application.

The user should not be required to visit GitHub to obtain ART.

The website may host or redirect to the official release artifact, but
the user experience shall be:

``` text
ART Website
    ↓
Download ART
    ↓
ART Installer
    ↓
Standard OS Installation Workflow
    ↓
ART Installed
    ↓
ART .exe / Shortcut
```

### Windows Installation

The Windows version shall support a conventional installation workflow.

Users shall be able to:

1.  Activate the ART download link.
2.  Download the installer.
3.  Open the installer.
4.  Follow the standard installation wizard.
5.  Complete installation.
6.  Launch ART from the Start Menu, desktop shortcut, or `.exe`.

### Windows Executable

The installed application shall provide a standard Windows executable.

The application should be launchable through:

- Start Menu.
- Desktop shortcut where selected.
- `.exe` executable.
- `.art` file association where configured.

### Installer Accessibility

The installer workflow shall be accessible to the extent supported by
the operating system and installer technology.

Verify:

- Keyboard navigation.
- Screen-reader compatibility.
- Accessible labels.
- Focus order.
- Status messages.
- Error messages.

### Installer Options

Where appropriate, allow users to choose:

- Installation location.
- Start Menu shortcut.
- Desktop shortcut.
- File associations.

Avoid unnecessary installation choices that make the process confusing.

### Uninstallation

Provide a standard operating-system uninstall workflow.

Uninstalling ART shall not unexpectedly delete user-created report
files.

### User Data During Uninstallation

Clearly distinguish:

- Application files.
- User settings.
- Local ART data.
- `.art` files.
- Exported reports.

Users shall be informed before deleting persistent application data.

### Desktop Data Storage

Preserve ART's local-first storage model.

Use appropriate application data locations rather than storing user data
inside the application installation directory.

### Portable Data

`.art` files shall remain portable between:

- Web ART.
- Desktop ART.
- Different desktop installations.

### Cross-Platform Desktop Support

Design the desktop application to support multiple operating systems
where practical.

Initially prioritize the platform with the greatest expected user need.

Potential platforms include:

- Windows.
- macOS.
- Linux.

### Platform-Specific Accessibility

Verify desktop accessibility independently on each supported operating
system.

### Native Integrations

Where appropriate, desktop ART may provide capabilities unavailable to
browser-based ART, such as:

- Native file associations.
- Native notifications.
- Native menus.
- Native clipboard integration.
- Native printing.
- Native window management.
- Native filesystem access.
- OS credential storage.

These capabilities shall add value without changing ART's fundamental
workflows.

### Search

Desktop ART shall provide the same search capabilities as web ART.

Search shall support applicable:

- Reports.
- Projects.
- Findings.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- WCAG criteria.
- Accessibility standards.
- Other searchable ART content.

### Accessible Search

Search interfaces shall preserve:

- Accessible labels.
- Keyboard access.
- Screen-reader announcements.
- Search result navigation.
- Result counts where applicable.

### Live Status Messages

Desktop ART shall preserve ART's accessible live status message
architecture.

Status information shall communicate important events such as:

- Saved.
- Saving.
- Synchronizing.
- Merge required.
- Merge completed.
- Update available.
- Update completed.
- Error.
- Task reminder.

### Accessibility Settings

All web accessibility settings shall be available in desktop ART where
technically applicable.

Examples include:

- Zoom.
- Text sizing.
- Contrast.
- Visual settings.
- Motion preferences.
- Focus indicators.
- Other ART accessibility settings.

### Assistive Technology Compatibility

Desktop ART shall be tested with supported desktop Assistive
Technologies.

At minimum, test as appropriate with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- Braille displays.
- Keyboard-only operation.
- Magnification tools.

### Screen Reader Behavior

Equivalent web and desktop workflows should produce equivalent
meaningful announcements.

Do not introduce unnecessary desktop-specific verbosity.

### Focus Management

Desktop ART shall preserve predictable focus behavior.

Focus shall not:

- Disappear.
- Move unexpectedly.
- Become trapped unintentionally.
- Move outside the active modal.
- Reset unnecessarily.

### Native Dialog Accessibility

Any native dialogs introduced by the desktop application shall be tested
for:

- Keyboard accessibility.
- Screen-reader compatibility.
- Focus behavior.
- Accessible names.
- Accessible descriptions.

### Performance

The desktop application shall provide performance at least comparable to
the web application for equivalent workflows.

Where possible, desktop ART should improve:

- Startup performance.
- File loading.
- Large report handling.
- Search.
- Rendering.
- Exporting.

### Memory Usage

Monitor desktop memory usage.

Avoid unnecessary long-term memory growth.

### CPU Usage

Avoid unnecessary background processing when ART is idle.

### Startup

Optimize application startup while preserving reliable initialization.

### Large Reports

Test desktop ART with large:

- Reports.
- Projects.
- Findings.
- Task lists.
- Progress Logs.
- Shared data sets.

### Large Files

Verify that large `.art` files can be opened, edited, saved, and
synchronized without unnecessary performance degradation.

### Crash Recovery

Provide recovery mechanisms for unexpected application termination.

Where practical:

- Detect unsaved changes.
- Preserve recovery data.
- Offer recovery on restart.
- Avoid data loss.

### Application Crash Handling

Application errors shall:

- Fail safely.
- Preserve user data where possible.
- Provide accessible error information.
- Provide recovery options.

### Error Reporting

If diagnostic/error reporting is implemented, it shall:

- Be privacy-conscious.
- Avoid sensitive report content.
- Avoid transmitting user data without consent.
- Respect privacy settings.

### Logging

Desktop logs shall not contain:

- Passwords.
- OAuth secrets.
- Access tokens.
- Sensitive report content.
- Unnecessary personal information.

### Import/Export

Desktop ART shall provide identical import/export capabilities to web
ART.

Support all existing report formats.

### Report Generation

Desktop ART shall generate equivalent reports to web ART.

Verify:

- Content.
- Formatting.
- Hyperlinks.
- Accessibility.
- Metadata.
- File integrity.

### Report Output Parity

Equivalent inputs shall produce equivalent outputs between web and
desktop ART.

### Printing and Export

Desktop-specific printing functionality may be added without changing
existing export behavior.

### Templates

Desktop ART shall support all existing templates.

Template management shall remain compatible between web and desktop
versions.

### History Framework

Desktop ART shall use the same History Framework.

Users shall be able to:

- Undo.
- Redo.
- Navigate history where supported.
- Recover from applicable actions.

### Cross-Platform History

History behavior shall remain consistent between web and desktop where
the same `.art` data is used.

### Task Management

Desktop ART shall provide the complete Tasks/To Do functionality.

This includes:

- Personal Tasks.
- Shared Tasks.
- Assigned Tasks.
- Task status.
- Checkboxes.
- Priority.
- Due dates.
- Reminders.
- Comments/Notes/Instructions.
- @mentions\.
- Completed Tasks.
- Task deletion.
- Context menus.
- Keyboard shortcuts.

### Progress Logs

Desktop ART shall provide complete Progress Log functionality.

### Organization Metrics

Desktop ART shall provide the same Organization Metrics functionality
when the required data and permissions are available.

### Collaboration

Desktop ART shall support Epic 60's collaboration infrastructure.

This includes:

- File-based collaboration.
- Server collaboration.
- Synchronization.
- Merge conflicts.
- Conflict resolution.
- @mentions\.
- Shared projects.
- Shared Tasks.
- Shared Progress Logs.
- Organization folders.

### Server Independence

Desktop ART shall remain useful without a server.

Server-dependent capabilities shall clearly identify when connectivity
is required.

### Connectivity Status

Provide accessible information about:

- Online.
- Offline.
- Connecting.
- Synchronizing.
- Authentication required.
- Server unavailable.

### Desktop Settings

Desktop settings shall integrate with existing ART settings.

Where appropriate, provide additional desktop-specific settings such as:

- Start behavior.
- Notification preferences.
- Update preferences.
- File associations.
- Native notification settings.
- Window behavior.

### Settings Synchronization

User preferences that are safe and appropriate to synchronize may be
synchronized between devices.

Sensitive information shall not be synchronized through unsafe
mechanisms.

### Privacy

Desktop ART shall preserve the privacy requirements established by Epic
58.

The desktop application shall not introduce unnecessary:

- Telemetry.
- Tracking.
- Analytics.
- Data transmission.

### Server-Dependent Functionality

Clearly distinguish:

**Local functionality**

from:

**Server-dependent functionality.**

Users shall be able to understand what will continue to work when
offline.

### Documentation

Document:

- Desktop installation.
- System requirements.
- Supported operating systems.
- Updating.
- Uninstallation.
- File associations.
- Opening `.art` files.
- Desktop collaboration.
- Offline functionality.
- Server functionality.
- Accessibility features.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Native features.
- Troubleshooting.

### Developer Documentation

Document:

- Desktop architecture.
- Electron configuration.
- IPC architecture.
- Security model.
- Build process.
- Installer creation.
- Code signing.
- Update mechanism.
- Release process.
- Platform-specific code.
- Shared web/desktop code.
- Testing requirements.

### Automated Testing

Create automated tests covering:

- Shared application logic.
- Desktop initialization.
- File opening.
- File saving.
- `.art` association.
- Import/export.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Menu commands.
- Context menus.
- Tasks.
- Progress Logs.
- History.
- Undo/Redo.
- Collaboration.
- Synchronization.
- Merge conflicts.
- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- Settings.
- Update detection.

### Desktop Integration Testing

Test:

- Installer.
- Uninstaller.
- Application launch.
- `.art` file association.
- Native dialogs.
- Native notifications.
- File-system integration.
- Clipboard.
- Window management.

### Accessibility Testing

Perform accessibility testing of:

- Application UI.
- Menus.
- Context menus.
- Dialogs.
- Notifications.
- Native integrations.
- Installer.
- Update workflow.

### Screen Reader Testing

Test with:

- JAWS.
- NVDA.
- Narrator.
- VoiceOver.
- Braille displays.

### Keyboard Testing

Verify that the complete application can be operated using only the
keyboard.

### Web/Desktop Comparison Testing

For equivalent workflows, compare:

- Navigation.
- Focus.
- Keyboard shortcuts.
- Screen-reader output.
- Functionality.
- Data.
- Report output.
- Collaboration behavior.

### Regression Testing

Desktop development shall not regress the web application.

Web regression tests shall continue to pass after desktop-related
changes.

### End-to-End Testing

Create end-to-end workflows such as:

``` text
Install ART
    ↓
Launch ART
    ↓
Create Project
    ↓
Create Report
    ↓
Enter Findings
    ↓
Save .art File
    ↓
Close ART

    ↓

Save

Export Report

```

Also test:

``` text
    ↓
Open Shared .art File

User B Modifies Report
    ↓
User B Saves
    ↓
User A Reopens/Refreshes
    ↓
External Change Detected

Automatic Merge
    ↓
Conflict Detected
    ↓
Merge Changes Modal
    ↓
Resolve Conflict
    ↓
Save
```

### Update Testing

Verify:

- Update available.
- No update available.
- Update Now.
- Cancel.
- Download failure.
- Interrupted update.
- Restart.
- Recovery after failed update.
- Version verification.

### Release Testing

Before publishing a desktop release, verify:

- Installer integrity.
- Application startup.
- Core functionality.
- Accessibility.
- Security.
- Collaboration.
- Import/export.
- Updates.
- Web compatibility.

### Definition of Done

Epic 61 shall be considered complete when:

- A supported desktop version of ART exists.
- Electron is used unless a documented technical evaluation determines
  otherwise.
- Desktop ART shares the maximum practical amount of application logic
  with web ART.
- Desktop ART provides functional parity with web ART.
- No fundamental web functionality is removed from the desktop
  application.
- Dashboard functionality is available.
- Report creation is available.
- Report editing is available.
- Report management is available.
- Report tracking is available.
- All supported report types are available.
- All supported report outputs are available.
- WCAG Lookup functionality is available.
- Accessibility Standards functionality is available.
- Tasks are available.
- Shared Tasks are available.
- Progress Logs are available.
- Organization Metrics are available where applicable.
- Collaboration is available.
- File-based collaboration is available.
- Server-based collaboration is available where applicable.
- Merge Changes is available.
- @mentions are available.
- Authentication is available where required.
- Authorization is enforced where required.
- User profiles are available.
- Device identity is supported.
- Import/export is available.
- `.art` files can be opened and saved.
- `.art` files can be associated with the desktop application.
- Customizable keyboard shortcuts are available.
- Customizable working views are available.
- Context menus are available.
- Menu bar commands are available.
- Search functionality is available.
- Accessible live status messages are available.
- Accessibility settings are available.
- Undo/Redo uses the existing History Framework.
- Offline local functionality remains available.
- Native desktop conveniences are implemented where appropriate.
- Native notifications are available where appropriate.
- Task reminders are available.
- Configurable auditory alerts are available where appropriate.
- Standard operating-system installation is supported.
- The ART website provides an accessible desktop download link.
- Users do not need to visit GitHub to download ART.
- Windows users can install ART through a standard installation wizard.
- Windows users can launch ART through a standard `.exe`.
- Start Menu integration is supported.
- Desktop shortcuts are supported where selected.
- Uninstallation uses the standard operating-system workflow.
- User data is not unintentionally deleted during uninstall.
- Check for Updates is available through the Help menu.
- Available updates can be installed through an accessible Update
  Now/Cancel workflow.
- The desktop release process is integrated with the GitHub-based
  development/release pipeline.
- Web and desktop releases use a consistent versioning strategy.
- Desktop update artifacts are automatically produced where practical.
- Web and desktop builds remain synchronized.
- Secure local credential storage is implemented.
- OAuth credentials are not stored in plain text.
- Electron security best practices are implemented.
- Desktop application dependencies are monitored for vulnerabilities.
- Crash recovery is implemented where practical.
- Desktop logs do not expose sensitive information.
- Desktop privacy controls comply with Epic 58.
- Automated desktop tests exist.
- Web/desktop parity tests exist.
- Accessibility testing has been completed.
- Screen-reader testing has been completed.
- Keyboard-only testing has been completed.
- Installer testing has been completed.
- Update testing has been completed.
- Collaboration testing has been completed.
- Merge-conflict testing has been completed.
- End-to-end testing has been completed.
- Existing web application functionality continues to pass regression
  testing.

The desktop application shall ultimately provide **more choice and
convenience, not fewer capabilities**.

A user should be able to choose between web ART and desktop ART based on
preference and environment without having to sacrifice functionality,
accessibility, security, privacy, usability, performance, collaboration,
reporting, or productivity.

## Epic 62 — Advanced Integrations & Platform Expansion

### Epic Overview

Expand ART's interoperability with external development,
project-management, productivity, accessibility-testing, and
organizational platforms.

The goal of this epic is to allow ART to integrate with the tools
organizations already use without making those integrations mandatory
for users who prefer ART's local-first, standalone functionality.

Integrations shall extend ART's capabilities while preserving:

- Accessibility.
- Privacy.
- Security.
- Local-first functionality.
- Offline functionality where applicable.
- Existing ART workflows.
- Existing import/export capabilities.
- Web/desktop feature parity.
- User choice.
- Data ownership.

ART shall remain fully usable without any external integration.

### Integration Principles

All integrations shall follow these principles:

- Integrations are optional unless explicitly required by a specific
  workflow.
- ART's fundamental functionality shall never depend on an external
  integration.
- Users shall control whether an integration is enabled.
- Organizations shall control which integrations are available where
  appropriate.
- Integration credentials shall never be stored in plain text.
- OAuth shall be preferred where supported.
- API tokens and secrets shall be stored securely.
- Integrations shall use the minimum permissions necessary.
- Users shall be able to disconnect integrations.
- Disconnecting an integration shall not unexpectedly delete ART data.
- External services shall not gain access to ART data beyond what the
  user or organization authorizes.
- Integration failures shall not corrupt ART data.
- Integration outages shall not prevent normal local ART use.
- Accessibility shall be preserved throughout integration workflows.

### Integration Architecture

Create a modular integration architecture so new integrations can be
added without significantly modifying ART's core functionality.

Use an abstraction similar to:

``` text
ART Core
   |
   +-- Integration Framework
          |
          +-- Jira
          +-- GitHub Issues
          +-- Microsoft Azure
          +-- Google Workspace
          +-- Other Project Management Platforms
          +-- Other Testing Platforms
          +-- Future Integrations
```

### Integration Management

Provide an accessible integration-management interface within ART
Settings.

Users shall be able to:

- View available integrations.
- Connect an integration.
- Disconnect an integration.
- Reauthorize an integration.
- View connection status.
- View required permissions.
- View authorized account information.
- Test a connection.
- Manage integration preferences.

### Integration Accessibility

The integration-management interface shall be fully accessible.

Verify:

- Keyboard navigation.
- Screen-reader compatibility.
- Accessible names.
- Accessible descriptions.
- Focus management.
- Error messages.
- Status messages.
- Confirmation messages.
- Authentication workflows.

### Integration Authentication

Use secure authentication mechanisms.

Where supported, prefer:

- OAuth 2.0.
- OpenID Connect where appropriate.
- Provider-supported secure authentication.

Avoid requiring users to manually enter passwords into ART for external
services.

### Credential Security

Never store:

- Passwords.
- OAuth client secrets.
- Access tokens.
- Refresh tokens.
- API keys.

in plain text.

Use secure storage appropriate to the environment.

For desktop ART, use operating-system secure credential storage where
available.

For server-based ART, use secure server-side secret management.

### Minimum Permissions

Request only the permissions required for the selected integration.

Clearly communicate requested permissions before authorization.

### Integration Revocation

Users shall be able to revoke an integration from ART.

Users should also be able to revoke ART's access from the external
service where supported.

### Integration Failure Handling

If an external service becomes unavailable:

- ART shall remain usable.
- ART shall clearly communicate the integration problem.
- Unsynchronized data shall not be silently discarded.
- Users shall be informed when synchronization resumes.
- Retry behavior shall be safe.
- Duplicate records shall be avoided where practical.

### Synchronization

Where an integration supports synchronization, define clearly:

- What data is synchronized.
- Which system is authoritative for each data element.
- When synchronization occurs.
- Whether synchronization is automatic or manual.
- How conflicts are handled.
- How deleted records are handled.

### Integration Conflicts

Integration conflicts shall not overwrite ART data without appropriate
safeguards.

Where conflicts occur, provide an accessible conflict-resolution
workflow.

Where practical, allow users to:

- Keep ART version.
- Keep external version.
- Merge information.
- Cancel.
- Review differences.

### Integration Audit Trail

Where appropriate, record integration-related actions in ART's History
Framework.

Examples include:

- Connected integration.
- Disconnected integration.
- Imported issue.
- Exported finding.
- Synchronized task.
- Updated external issue.
- Resolved integration conflict.

Do not store sensitive credentials in the History Framework.

### Jira Integration

Implement integration with Jira.

[Jira](https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The integration should support applicable workflows such as:

- Creating Jira issues from ART findings.
- Updating Jira issues from ART.
- Linking ART findings to Jira issues.
- Importing applicable Jira issue information.
- Synchronizing task status where appropriate.
- Synchronizing priority where appropriate.
- Synchronizing assignees where appropriate.
- Synchronizing due dates where appropriate.
- Viewing linked Jira issue information from ART.

### Jira Finding Export

Allow users to create a Jira issue from an ART finding.

Where supported, include:

- Finding title.
- Description.
- Severity/priority.
- WCAG Success Criterion.
- Accessibility Standard.
- Steps to reproduce.
- Expected behavior.
- Actual behavior.
- Suggested remediation.
- ART report/project reference.

Do not export information the user has not authorized.

### Jira Linking

An ART finding shall be capable of maintaining a reference to its
associated Jira issue.

The user should be able to navigate between the ART finding and the Jira
issue.

### Jira Synchronization

Where synchronization is enabled, define appropriate mappings between:

- ART status.
- Jira status.
- ART priority.
- Jira priority.
- ART assignee.
- Jira assignee.
- ART due date.
- Jira due date.

### GitHub Issues Integration

Implement integration with GitHub Issues.

[GitHub](https://github.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Support applicable workflows such as:

- Creating GitHub Issues from ART findings.
- Linking ART findings to GitHub Issues.
- Updating linked issues.
- Importing issue information.
- Synchronizing applicable statuses.
- Synchronizing priorities where supported.
- Synchronizing assignees where supported.
- Viewing issue status from ART.

### GitHub Issue Creation

Allow an ART finding to be converted into a GitHub Issue.

Where appropriate, include:

- Finding title.
- Description.
- Reproduction steps.
- Expected behavior.
- Actual behavior.
- WCAG Success Criterion.
- Accessibility Standard.
- Severity/priority.
- Remediation information.

### GitHub Repository Selection

Where authorized, users shall be able to select:

- Organization.
- Repository.
- Issue destination.

### Microsoft Azure Integration

Support integration with applicable Microsoft Azure services,
particularly Azure DevOps.

The integration should support applicable workflows including:

- Work items.
- Bugs.
- Tasks.
- User stories.
- Links to ART findings.
- Status synchronization.
- Assignment synchronization.
- Priority synchronization.

### Azure DevOps Work Items

Allow ART findings to be exported to appropriate Azure DevOps work-item
types.

Where supported, preserve relevant ART information.

### Azure Authentication

Use Microsoft's supported secure authentication mechanisms.

Do not require users to provide their Microsoft account password
directly to ART.

### Google Workspace Integration

Support applicable Google Workspace functionality.

Potential integrations include:

- Google Drive.
- Google Sheets.
- Google Docs.

- Selecting Google Drive locations.

file-based collaboration model.

### Google Sheets

Where appropriate, support exporting or synchronizing applicable ART

Potential uses include:

- Task information.
- Project metrics.

### Google Docs

Where appropriate, support exporting applicable ART reports to Google
Docs.

### Google Workspace Permissions

Respect Google Workspace permissions.

ART shall not bypass Google Drive, Sheets, or Docs access controls.

### Microsoft 365 Integration

Evaluate support for applicable Microsoft 365 services.

Potential integrations include:

- OneDrive.
- SharePoint.
- Microsoft Teams.
- Microsoft Word.
- Microsoft Excel.

Where practical, support these services using Microsoft-supported
authentication and APIs.

### OneDrive

Support applicable workflows involving:

- `.art` files.
- Shared folders.
- Report exports.
- File-based collaboration.

### SharePoint

Where authorized, support:

- Shared ART files.
- Organization repositories.
- Report storage.
- Document workflows.

### Microsoft Teams

Evaluate integration capabilities such as:

- Sharing ART reports.
- Sharing findings.
- Linking tasks.
- Notifications.
- Collaboration links.

### Microsoft Word

Preserve ART's existing Word export functionality while evaluating
enhanced integration with Microsoft Word/365 workflows.

### Microsoft Excel

Where applicable, provide export or synchronization of:

### Cloud Storage Integration

Support common cloud-storage workflows without making cloud storage
mandatory.

Potential providers include:

- Google Drive.
- OneDrive.
- Dropbox.
- Box.
- Other compatible storage platforms.

### File-Based Collaboration Integration

External cloud-storage providers shall work with ART's file-based
collaboration architecture established in Epic 60.

The external storage provider shall act as the storage/transport
mechanism while ART remains responsible for:

- `.art` file structure.
- Version information.
- Change detection.
- Merge processing.
- Conflict resolution.
- User identity information.
- Collaboration metadata.

### Shared Folder Workflows

ART shall support shared-folder workflows such as:

``` text
Shared Organization Folder
        |
        +-- Project A
        |     +-- Report 1.art
        |     +-- Report 2.art
        |
        +-- Project B
        |     +-- Report 3.art
        |
        +-- Shared Tasks
        |
        +-- Progress Logs
        |
        +-- Metrics
```

### External File Change Detection

When a `.art` file changes outside ART, detect the change when
practical.

Possible triggers include:

- Opening the file.
- Refreshing.
- Saving.
- Returning to the application.
- File-system notification.

### Integration With File-Based Collaboration

Cloud integrations shall not create a second, incompatible collaboration
system.

Instead, they shall extend the existing `.art` file-based collaboration
architecture.

### Dropbox Integration

Evaluate and implement Dropbox integration where technically practical.

Support applicable:

- Shared folders.
- `.art` files.
- Import/export.
- File change detection.
- File-based collaboration.

### Box Integration

Evaluate support for Box for organizations that use Box as their
document-management platform.

### Other Cloud Providers

Design the integration architecture so additional cloud-storage
providers can be added without redesigning ART's core file system.

### Project Management Platform Expansion

Design the integration framework to support additional
project-management platforms.

Potential future integrations include:

- Asana.
- Trello.
- Monday.com.
- Linear.
- ClickUp.
- Other widely used project-management platforms.

Only implement platforms that provide meaningful value and appropriate
API access.

### Testing Platform Integrations

Evaluate integrations with accessibility and testing platforms where
APIs permit useful integration.

Potential functionality includes:

- Importing test results.
- Linking findings.
- Exporting findings.
- Linking test cases.
- Synchronizing issue status.

### Accessibility Testing Tools

Evaluate integrations with tools such as:

- axe.
- WAVE.
- Lighthouse.
- Other automated accessibility testing platforms.

Do not represent automated testing results as equivalent to human
accessibility testing.

### Imported Automated Findings

Where automated findings are imported, clearly distinguish:

- Automated finding.
- Manual finding.
- User-verified finding.
- False positive.
- Needs review.

### Integration Data Mapping

Create standardized mappings between ART data and external systems.

Potential mappings include:

| ART Data | External Data      |
|----------|--------------------|
| Finding  | Issue/Bug          |
| Task     | Task               |
| Priority | Priority           |
| Status   | Status             |
| Assignee | Assignee           |
| Due Date | Due Date           |
| Comment  | Comment            |
| Project  | Project/Repository |
| Report   | Document/File      |
| User     | Account/User       |

### Status Mapping

Provide configurable mappings when external systems use different status
models.

For example:

``` text
ART:
Needs Review

Jira:
In Review

GitHub:
Open

Azure:
Active
```

### Priority Mapping

Preserve ART priority information when the external platform supports
equivalent priority values.

Priority shall remain available programmatically within ART.

### User Mapping

Where appropriate, map ART users to external-service accounts.

Do not assume that matching display names means matching users.

Use provider account identifiers where appropriate.

### @Mentions Integration

Preserve ART's @mentions functionality when interacting with external
systems where supported.

For example:

- ART comment → external issue comment.
- External issue comment → ART comment.

Where external systems do not support equivalent mention functionality,
preserve the ART mention internally rather than silently losing the
information.

### Comments

Where supported, synchronize task/finding comments between ART and
external systems.

Comments shall remain distinguishable from:

- System-generated messages.
- Synchronization messages.
- User notes.

### Attachments

Evaluate support for attachments.

Where supported:

- Preserve file references.
- Respect external permissions.
- Avoid duplicating large files unnecessarily.
- Clearly identify externally hosted files.

### Links

External links shall:

- Have meaningful accessible names.
- Open in the expected destination.
- Clearly communicate when opening a new browser window/tab where
  applicable.
- Remain usable by keyboard and screen readers.

### Integration Context Menus
